pra | ye | dvitā | divaḥ | yaṃjaṃti | ātāḥ | susaṃmṛṣṭāsaḥ | vṛṣabhasya | mūrāḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां बृहंतो महांतो युजाना रथे युज्यमाना हरयोऽश्वाः सधमादः सह मादयंतः संतोऽर्वाक् अस्मदभिमुखमा वहंतु । वृषभस्य कामानां वर्षितुरिंद्रस्य मूराः शत्रोणां मारकाः सुसंमृष्टास इंद्रस्य हस्ताभ्यां पृष्ठभागे सुष्टु संस्पृष्टा दिवो नभसः सकाशादागच्छंतो येऽश्वा आताः । अभिमुख्यन गम्यंते प्राणिभिस्तत्तत्कार्यं प्रतीत्याता दिशः । सर्वा दिशो द्विता द्वैधं यथा भवति तथा प्र ऋंजंति । प्रकर्षण साधयंति ॥ युजानाः । युजिर् योगे युजिबुधिदृशः किच्च । उ. २.९०. । इत्यानच् । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । सधमादः । मदी हर्ष इत्यस्माण्यंतात् क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । द्विता । द्विशब्दात्संख्याया विधार्थे धेति धाप्रत्ययः । धकारस्य तकारश्चांदसः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । दिवः । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । आताः । आत सातत्यगमन इत्यस्मात्कर्मणि घञ् । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तः ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, may the great (बृहंतः (bṛhaṃtaḥ)) horses, yoked to the chariot, delighting together (सधमादः (sadhamādaḥ)), bring you hither, toward us. Those horses are the slayers (मूराः (mūrāḥ)) of the enemies of Indra, the "bull", the showerer of desires. They are well rubbed (सुसंमृष्टासः (susaṃmṛṣṭāsaḥ)) on the back by Indra's two hands, and they come from heaven, from the sky. They are ātāḥ: the directions are called ātāḥ because creatures go toward them for their various tasks. These horses accomplish (प्र ऋंजंति (pra ṛṃjaṃti): they bring to completion eminently) all the directions in a twofold manner (द्विता (dvitā)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • त्वा (tvā)—you
  • बृहंतः (bṛhaṃtaḥ)—of great form
  • युजानाः (yujānāḥ)—yoked to the chariot
  • हरयः (harayaḥ)—horses
  • सधमादः (sadhamādaḥ)—rejoicing together
  • अर्वाक् (arvāk)—toward us
  • आ वहंतु (ā vahaṃtu)—let them bring
  • वृषभस्य (vṛṣabhasya)—of Indra, the showerer of desires
  • मूराः (mūrāḥ)—destroyers (of enemies)
  • सुसंमृष्टासः (susaṃmṛṣṭāsaḥ)—(lovingly) patted on the back
  • दिवः (divaḥ)—from the atmosphere
  • ये (ye)—which, those very horses
  • आताः (ātāḥ)—in all directions
  • द्विता (dvitā)—doubled
  • प्र ऋंजंति (pra ṛṃjaṃti)—(exceedingly) shine
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may the great horses, yoked to the chariot, rejoicing together, bring you toward us. Those same horses of Indra, the showerer of desires, destroyers of enemies, patted on the back, shine doubled in all the directions.

p. 59

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May your mighty horses, Indra, harnessed (in your car), and alike exhilarated (by the beverage) bring you to our presence, for they are the destroyers (of the foes) of the showerer (of benefits), and kindly rubbed by his hand they traverse, going quickly, the regions of the sky, making them as it were twofold.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Mūrāḥ: for the word mūra the meaning "foolish" (mūḍha), i.e. ignorant, is generally well known; mūra is popularly an ignorant person and amūra a knowing one. In the present Ṛk, however, Sāyaṇa explains the word as a destroying power. The scholar Monier Wiliam, explaining this word, cites this very Ṛk and in his dictionary gives the meaning "Rushing, impetuous"; he also records Sāyaṇa's opinion "destroyer" (māraka). Besides, it also means "firm, secure, well established". The word is also used in the sense of "root, base" (A. Ve. 1-28-3).NOTE

Ātāḥ: since it is the means by which birds and others move here and there, ātā is a synonym for the side of a direction. In many places it also means the door of a shutter.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इंद्र॒ पिब॒ वृष॑धूतस्य॒ वृष्ण॒ आ यं ते॑ श्ये॒न उ॑श॒ते ज॒भार॑ ।
यस्य॒ मदे॑ च्या॒वय॑सि॒ प्र कृ॒ष्टीर्यस्य॒ मदे॒ अप॑ गो॒त्रा ॒॑ ववर्थ ॥ ७ ॥

iṃdra piba vṛṣadhūtasya vṛṣṇa ā yaṃ te śyena uśate jabhāra |
yasya made cyāvayasi pra kṛṣṭīryasya made apa gotrā
vavartha ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

इंद्र । पिब । वृषधूतस्य । वृष्णः ! आ । यं । ते । श्येनः । उशते । जभार ।
यस्य । मदे । च्यवयसि । प्र । कृष्टीः । यस्य । मदे । अप । गोत्रा । ववर्थ ॥ ७ ॥

iṃdra | piba | vṛṣadhūtasya | vṛṣṇaḥ ! ā | yaṃ | te | śyenaḥ | uśate | jabhāra |
yasya | made | cyavayasi | pra | kṛṣṭīḥ | yasya | made | apa | gotrā | vavartha ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र वृषधूतस्य ग्रावभिरभिषुतं वृष्णोऽभिमतफलसेचकं सोमं पिब । श्येनः शंसनीयगतिश्चंदोरूपः सुपर्ण उशते सोमं कामयमानाय

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, drink the Soma that is pressed with the stones (ग्रावभिरभिषुतं (grāvabhirabhiṣutaṃ)) and is the sprinkler (वृष्णः (vṛṣṇaḥ)) of the desired fruit. The Śyena, the hawk of praiseworthy flight, who has the form of a metre, brought (जभार (jabhāra): आजहार (ājahāra)) to you, who desire Soma, that Soma.

p. 60

ते तुभ्यं यं सोममा जभार । आजहार । यस्य सोमस्य मदे हर्ष संजाते सति कृष्टीः । आकर्षंति वशीकुर्वंति कर्मणा सर्वानिति कृस्टयो मनुष्याः । तान् सपत्नभूतान्मनुष्यान् प्र च्यावयसि । प्रकर्षण पातयसि । यस्य सोमस्य मदे संजाते सति गोत्रा । गामुदकं रश्मिभिरावृतं वर्षास्वतुषु त्रायंते पालयंतीति गोत्रा मुघाः । तानह ववर्थ । अपवृणेषि ॥ वृषधूतस्य । धूञ् कंपन इत्यस्य निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदस्वरः । शैनः । श्येज् गतौ । श्यास्ताहृञ्विभ्य इनच् । उ २.४६. । इतीनच् प्रत्ययः । श्यायत इति शैनः । चित्तादंतोदात्तः । जभार । हरतेर्लिटि णलि रूपं । हृग्रहोर्भश्चंदसीति भकारः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । लित्स्वरः । मदे । मदी हर्षे । मदोऽनुपसर्ग इत्यप्रत्ययः । तस्य पित्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । गोत्रा । त्रैज् पालन इत्यस्यातोऽनुपसर्गे क इति कः । सुपो डादेशः । एकादेशस्वरः । ववर्थ । वृञ् वरण इत्यस्य लिट थल्यतो भारद्वाजस्येतीट् प्रतिषेधः । गुणः लित्स्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

When joy is born from that Soma, you make fall, you cast down eminently, the kṛṣṭayaḥ, human beings who are your rivals (kṛṣṭayaḥ are people who draw all, bring all under control, by their action). When joy is born from that Soma, you uncover (अप ववर्थ (apa vavartha): अपवृणेषि (apavṛṇeṣi)) the gotrās, the clouds, which in the rainy seasons protect (त्रायंते पालयंतीति (trāyaṃte pālayaṃtīti)) the water enveloped in rays (go means water).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • यं (yaṃ)—which Soma
  • श्येनः (śyenaḥ)—the Śyena bird in the form of a metre
  • उशते (uśate)—to you who desired it
  • ते (te)—for you
  • आ जभार (ā jabhāra)—brought (and)
  • यस्य (yasya)—by drinking which Soma juice
  • मदे (made)—becoming exhilarated
  • कृष्टीः (kṛṣṭīḥ)—men (who are enemies)
  • प्रच्यावयसि (pracyāvayasi)—you beat down and drive away (and)
  • यस्य (yasya)—by drinking which Soma juice
  • मदे (made)—becoming exhilarated
  • गोत्रा (gotrā)—the clouds
  • अप ववर्थ (apa vavartha)—you split open; such
  • वृषधूतस्य (vṛṣadhūtasya)—pressed by the pressing stones
  • वृष्णः (vṛṣṇaḥ)—the Soma that grants desires
  • पिब (piba)—drink
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink that pressed Soma juice, the granter of desires, which the Śyena bird in the form of a metre brought for you who desired it; by drinking which, rejoicing, you beat down the enemies; and by drinking which Soma, exhilarated, you split open the clouds for the sake of rain.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Drink, Indra, of the bountiful (libation) expressed by the beneficent (stones); that which the falcon has borne to you desiring it, in whose exhilaration you cast down (opposing) men, in whose exhilaration you have set open the clouds.

p. 61

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Śyena: the occasion on which the Śyena bird, of the nature of the Gāyatrī, brought the Soma was told earlier, and it will be told later when the greatness of the Gāyatrī is described.

Kṛṣṭīḥ: the special meanings of the words kṛṣṭi and carṣaṇi were explained earlier. The uses of the words pañcakṛṣṭayaḥ and pañcajanāḥ, which signify identity, were also explained.

Gotrā: the word gotra generally means a cowshed that protects cows; this is well known, and the same meaning is indicated in the Nirukta (Ni. 1-2). In the present Ṛk gotra is explained as "cloud". Since the word go is a synonym of water, and since the cloud holds back and protects the water, gotra also means "cloud". The special meaning of this word will be explained when Indra's valour is described with the word गोत्रभित् (gotrabhit).

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिंद्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सात् ।
शृ॒ण्वंत॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्तु॒ घ्नंतं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ ॑ धॆनानां ॥ ८ ॥

śunaṃ huvema maghavānamiṃdramasminbhare nṛtamaṃ vājasāt |
śṛṇvaṃtamugramūtaye samattu ghnaṃtaṃ vṛtrāṇi saṃjitaṃ
dhènānāṃ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शुनं । हुवेम । मघवानं । इंद्रं । अस्मिन् । भरे । नृतमं । वाजसात् ।
शृण्वंतं । उग्रं । ऊतये । समत्सु । घ्नंतं । वृत्राणि । संजितं । धनानां ॥

śunaṃ | huvema | maghavānaṃ | iṃdraṃ | asmin | bhare | nṛtamaṃ | vājasāt |
śṛṇvaṃtaṃ | ugraṃ | ūtaye | samatsu | ghnaṃtaṃ | vṛtrāṇi | saṃjitaṃ | dhanānāṃ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः। अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन् संग्रामे शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृद्धं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं मघवानं धनवंतं आत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा तृण्यंतमस्माभिः क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्यंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, vājasāt: the one in whom there is the gain (सातिः (sātiḥ)) of food (वाज (vāja)). Bhara is battle, since in it warriors bear (बिभ्रति (bibhrati)) the goddess of victory. In this battle we call you, who are śuna, swollen, grown through enthusiasm; or else śuna is a name for happiness, so "making happiness"; who are wealthy (मघवानं (maghavānaṃ)), and therefore Indra endowed with unsurpassed lordship, the supreme leader (नृतमं (nṛtamaṃ)) of the whole world. We Kuśikas call you for the sacrifice. We call you who hear the praise made by us, fierce (उग्रं (ugraṃ)), a terror to enemies, in the battles (समत्सु (samatsu))…

p. 62

वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संजितं सम्यग्नेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्चि गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । ह्वयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते शपो लुकि कृते च लिजि रूपं । निघातः । भरे । बृञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । वाजसात् । षणु दाने । भावे क्तिन् । जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं । बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । समत्तु । अद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति योद्धाणामायूंशीति समदः संग्रामाः ! कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घ्नंतं । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेरिति घत्वं । संजितं । जि जये । क्विप् !'

Gist of the bhāṣya

…who destroy (घ्नंतं (ghnaṃtaṃ)) all the Rākṣasas, who are called by the name Vṛtra; who is the good leader and conqueror (संजितं (saṃjitaṃ)) of the wealth belonging to the enemies. We call you for protection (ऊतये (ūtaye)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • वाजसात् (vājasāt)—proceeding for the sake of food
  • भरे (bhare)—in the battle
  • शुनं (śunaṃ)—who grow through enthusiasm, or who produce happiness
  • मघवानं (maghavānaṃ)—wealthy
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—endowed with unsurpassed lordship
  • नृतमं (nṛtamaṃ)—the leader; you
  • हुवेम (huvema)—we invoke and call (likewise)
  • शृण्वंतं (śṛṇvaṃtaṃ)—who listen (to our praises)
  • उग्रं (ugraṃ)—fearsome to enemies
  • समत्तु (samattu)—in battles
  • वृत्राणि (vṛtrāṇi)—the Asuras beginning with Vṛtra
  • घ्नंतं (ghnaṃtaṃ)—who injure and destroy
  • धनानां (dhanānāṃ)—the wealth (of enemies)
  • संचितं (saṃcitaṃ)—who gather and give (to us); you
  • ऊतये (ūtaye)—for protection
  • हवेम (havema)—(we invoke and call)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in the battle waged for the sake of food, you who produce happiness, are wealthy, are endowed with unsurpassed lordship, are the leader, listen to our praises, are fearsome to enemies, injure and destroy Vṛtra and the other Asuras in battles, and gather the wealth of the enemies and give it to us—you we invoke and call for protection.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terri-ble in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The special topics of this Ṛk have already been explained earlier.

Sūkta 44 (Maṇḍala 3)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अयं ते अस्त्विति पंचर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं बार्हतमैंद्रं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । आयं ते पंच बार्हतं त्विति ॥ महाव्रते बार्हत्यां तृचाशीताविदं सूक्तं । ऐ. आ ५२ ॥ षोडशिशस्त्रेयं ते अस्तु हर्यत इत्याद्यस्तृचो विनियुक्तः ! सूत्रितं च । आयं ते अस्तु हर्यत इत्यौष्टिहबार्हतौ तृचौ । आ. ६.२ । इति !! अनुवादवु — आयं ते अस्तु ऎंब ई सूक्तवु नाल्कनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि आरनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि ऐदु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ विश्वामित्रनु ऋषियु, इंद्रनु देवतॆयु, बृहती छंदस्सु- अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—आयं ते पंच बार्हतं तु ऎंदु हेळिरुवुदु. महाव्रत दल्लि बृहती छंदस्सिन तृच (मूरु ऋक्कु) क्कागि ई सूक्तद विनियोगविरुवुदॆंदु ऐतरेयारण्य कदल्लियू (ऐ. आ. ५-२) षोडशियॆंब यागदल्लि शस्त्रमंत्रपठनकालदल्लि आयं ते अस्तु हर्यतः ऎंब ई सूक्तद मॊदलनॆय मूरु ऋक्कुगळ विनियोगविरुवुदॆंदु अश्वलायनश्रौत सूत्रद—आयं ते अस्तु हर्यत इत्यौष्ठिहबार्हत् तृचौ ऎंब सूत्रदिंदलू विवृत वागिरुवुदु (आ. ६-२). ॥ ओं ॥ सूक्त—४४ मंडल—३ ॥ अनुवाक—४ ॥ सूक्त—४४ ॥ अष्टक—३ ॥ अध्याय—३ ॥ वर्ग—८ ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—५ ॥ ॥ ऋषिः—विश्वामित्रः ॥ ॥ देवता—इंद्रः ॥ ॥ छंदः—बृहती ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अयं ते अस्तु (ayaṃ te astu), of five Ṛks, is the sixth sūkta; its seer is Viśvāmitra, it is Bārhata in metre and addressed to Indra. On it the Anukramaṇikā says आयं ते पंच बार्हतं त्विति (āyaṃ te paṃca bārhataṃ tviti). In the Mahāvrata this sūkta is used for the Bṛhatī tṛca: महाव्रते बार्हत्यां तृचाशीताविदं सूक्तं (mahāvrate bārhatyāṃ tṛcāśītāvidaṃ sūktaṃ) (Ai. Ā. 52). In the Ṣoḍaśin śastra the first tṛca of it, beginning अयं ते अस्तु हर्यतः (ayaṃ te astu haryataḥ), is applied; and it is given in the sūtra: आयं ते अस्तु हर्यत इत्यौष्टिहबार्हतौ तृचौ (āyaṃ te astu haryata ityauṣṭihabārhatau tṛcau) (Ā. 6-2).

The Anuvāda adds the particulars: Maṇḍala 3, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 44; Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 3, Varga 8; number of Ṛks in the sūkta 5; seer Viśvāmitra; deity Indra; metre Bṛhatī. It gives the Aitareya Āraṇyaka reference as Ai. Ā. 5-2 and the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra reference as 6-2.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒यं ते॑ अस्तु हर्य॒तः सोम॒ आ हरि॑भिः सु॒तः ।
जु॒षा॒ण इं॑द्र॒ हरि॑भिर्न॒ आ ग॒ह्या ति॑ष्ठ॒ हरि॑तं॒ रथं॑ ॥ १ ॥

ayaṃ te astu haryataḥ soma ā haribhiḥ sutaḥ |
juṣāṇa iṃdra haribhirna ā gahyā tiṣṭha haritaṃ rathaṃ ‖ 1 ‖

p. 64

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अयं । ते । अस्तु । हर्यतः । सोमः । आ । हरिभिः । सुतः ।
जुषाणः । इंद्र । हरिभिः । नः । आ । गहि । आ । तिष्ठ । हरितं । रथं ॥ १ ॥

ayaṃ | te | astu | haryataḥ | somaḥ | ā | haribhiḥ | sutaḥ |
juṣāṇaḥ | iṃdra | haribhiḥ | naḥ | ā | gahi | ā | tiṣṭha | haritaṃ | rathaṃ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र हरिभिः । हरंति सोमरसानेभिरिति हरयो ग्रावाणः । तैरा सुतः सर्वतोऽभिषुतो हर्यतः कमनीयो जषाणः प्रीतिविषयोऽयं सोमस्ते तुभ्यमस्तु । त्वं हरिभिरश्वैर्युक्तं हरितं हरिद्वर्णं रथमा तिष्ठ । अधितिष्य । ततो नोऽस्मानभिलक्ष्या गहि । आगच्छ ॥ हर्यतः । हर्य गतिकांतोरित्यस्मादृमृदृशीत्यादिनातच् प्रत्ययः । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । हरितं । हृञ् हरणे । दृश्याभ्यामितन् । उ. ३-९३ । इतीतन्न प्रत्ययः ! नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । रथं । रमु क्रीडायां । हनिकुषिनीत्यादिना क्फन्न प्रत्ययः । कित्वादनुनासिकलोपः । नित्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the harayaḥ are the pressing-stones, so called because they carry off (हरंति (haraṃti)) the Soma juice. This Soma, pressed all round by them, desirable and an object of delight, is for you. Mount the green-hued chariot yoked with tawny horses (हरिभिः (haribhiḥ)), and then come towards us.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • हरिभिः (haribhiḥ)—by the pressing-stones
  • आ सुतः (ā sutaḥ)—fully pressed
  • हर्यतः (haryataḥ)—attractive
  • जुषाणः (juṣāṇaḥ)—dear, an object of delight
  • आयं सोमः (āyaṃ somaḥ)—this Soma juice
  • ते (te)—directed to you
  • अस्तु (astu)—is ready
  • हरिभिः (haribhiḥ)—joined with horses
  • हरितं (haritaṃ)—of green colour
  • रथं (rathaṃ)—in the chariot
  • आ तिष्ठ (ā tiṣṭha)—mount and sit
  • नः (naḥ)—towards us
  • आ गहि (ā gahi)—be gracious to come
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, this Soma juice, fully pressed by the pressing-stones, attractive and dear, is ready for you. Mount and sit in the green-coloured chariot yoked with horses, and be gracious to come towards us.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May this desirable and gratifying Soma expressed by the stones, be, Indra, for you : ascend the verdant chariot, and with your tawny (steeds) come to us.

p. 65

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

ह॒र्यन्नु॒षस॑मर्चयः॒ सूर्यं॑ ह॒र्यन्न॑रोचयः ।
वि॒द्वांश्चि॑कि॒त्वान्ह॑र्यश्व वर्धस॒ इंद्र॒ विश्वा॑ अ॒भि श्रियः॑ ॥ २ ॥

haryannuṣasamarcayaḥ sūryaṃ haryannarocayaḥ |
vidvāṃścikitvānharyaśva vardhasa iṃdra viśvā abhi śriyaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

हर्यन् । उषसं । अर्चयः । सूर्यं । हर्यन् । आरोचयः ।
विद्वान् । चिकित्वान् । हरिअश्व । वर्धसे । इंद्र । विश्वाः । अभि । श्रियः ॥ २ ॥

haryan | uṣasaṃ | arcayaḥ | sūryaṃ | haryan | ārocayaḥ |
vidvān | cikitvān | hariaśva | vardhase | iṃdra | viśvāḥ | abhi | śriyaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र हर्यन् सोमं कामयमानस्त्वमुषसमुषःकालमर्चयः । पूजयसि । तथा हर्यन्नुदिते सूर्यॆ सोमं कामयमानस्त्वं सूर्यमरोचयः । दीपयसि । हे हर्यश्वेंद्र विद्यानेतत्सर्वं जानानश्चि कित्वानस्मदभिलषितफलविषयज्ञानवांस्तं विश्वाः सर्वाः श्रियो नः संपदोऽभि वर्धसे । अभिमतफलप्रदानेनाभितो वर्धयसि ॥ चिकित्वान् । कित ज्ञान इत्यस्य क्वसौ रूपं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । वर्धसे । वृधु वर्धन इत्य स्यांतर्भावितण्यर्थस्य लटि रूपं । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, desiring (हर्यन् (haryan)) Soma, you honour the Dawn, the time of dawn. Likewise, desiring Soma when the sun has risen, you make the sun shine. O Indra, lord of tawny horses, knowing all this and aware of the fruit we desire, you increase all our prosperity on every side by granting the desired fruit.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra, you
  • हर्यन् (haryan)—desiring the drinking of Soma
  • उषसं (uṣasaṃ)—the time of dawn
  • अर्चयः (arcayaḥ)—you honour
  • हर्यन् (haryan)—desiring the Soma (offered after sunrise)
  • सूरं (sūraṃ)—the sun
  • अरोचयः (arocayaḥ)—you make shine
  • हरश्व (haraśva)—O Indra, possessing horses named Hari
  • विद्वान् (vidvān)—knowing everything
  • चिकित्वान् (cikitvān)—knowing our desired ends
  • विश्वाः श्रियः (viśvāḥ śriyaḥ)—all riches
  • अभि वर्धसे (abhi vardhase)—you cause to increase among us
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, desiring the drinking of the Soma offered before sunrise, you honour the time of dawn. Then, desiring the Soma offered afterwards, you make the sun shine. O Indra, possessor of the horses named Hari, being all-knowing and knowing our desired ends, you cause all riches to increase among us.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Desiring (the Soma), you honour the dawn ; desiring the Soma, you have lighted up the sun ; knowing and discriminating (all our wishes), lord of the tawny steeds, you augment upon us all (sorts of) prosperity.

p. 66

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As the words of the Supreme Person say, उत्तीदेयुरिमे लोकाः न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहं (uttīdeyurime lokāḥ na kuryāṃ karma cedahaṃ)NOTE—"if I did not perform action, all the worlds would perish"—so, if Indra, the lord of the universe, were not constantly engaged in action useful for the conduct of the world, the ruin of the world would be certain. He is the cause of the appearance of Dawn and of the rising of the sun. As described in स्वराजः, महतः, ते (svarājaḥ, mahataḥ, te) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-1), he alone is lord of the whole universe and holds sovereign rank. Even so, because the performance of sacrifice nourishes the world and is the cause of the growth of prosperity of the whole world, of gods, men and others, it is said that Indra honoured Dawn and the Sun, the primary causes of that sacrifice. The purport of the present Ṛk is that, though himself the lord, he worshipped his own creation, which nourishes the world.

The two epithets विद्वान् (vidvān) and चिकित्वान् (cikitvān) are also noteworthy here. Indra is all-knowing and knows the intention of the sacrificer. Therefore, being the cause of the appearance of Dawn so as to suit the mutual dealings of gods and men, he worshipped that Dawn of great form. In this sūkta, from beginning to end, a spiritual principle lies hidden. The epithet हरस्व (harasva) and descriptions such as सूर‍्यं अरोचयः (sūryaṃ arocayaḥ) and उषसं अर्चयः (uṣasaṃ arcayaḥ) indicate this hidden meaning. Although an explanation of these is quite necessary, there is no room here for a detailed one, because of limits of space. It will be explained later as occasion arises.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

द्यामिंद्रो॒ हरि॑धायसं पृथि॒वीं हरि॑वर्पसं ।
अधा॑रयुद्ध॒रितो॒र्भूरि॒ भोज॑नं॒ ययो॑रं॒तर्हरि॒श्चर॑त् ॥३॥

dyāmiṃdro haridhāyasaṃ pṛthivīṃ harivarpasaṃ |
adhārayuddharitorbhūri bhojanaṃ yayoraṃtarhariścarat ‖3‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

द्यां । इंद्रः । हरिधायसं । सृथिवीं । हरिवर्पसं ।
अधारयत् । हरितोः । भूरि । भोजनं । ययोः । अंतः । हरिः । चरत् ॥ ३ ॥

dyāṃ | iṃdraḥ | haridhāyasaṃ | sṛthivīṃ | harivarpasaṃ |
adhārayat | haritoḥ | bhūri | bhojanaṃ | yayoḥ | aṃtaḥ | hariḥ | carat ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सोऽयमिंद्रो हरिधायसं । हरितो हरितवर्णा धायसो धारका रत्नयो यस्याः सा । तां द्यामधारयत् । तथा हरिवर्पसनोषधीभिर्हरितवर्णां

Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra upheld the heaven that is हरिधायसं (haridhāyasaṃ): the green-hued supporters (dhāyasaḥ) of which are रत्नयो (ratnayo)NOTE. Likewise he upheld the earth, हरिवर्पसं (harivarpasaṃ), green with plants.

p. 67

पृथिवीमधारयत् । हरितोर्हरिद्दर्णयोर्ययोर्द्यावापृथिव्योर्मध्यॆ स्वकीययोरश्वयोर्भूरि प्रभूतं भोजनं । भुज्यत इति भोजनं यवसादि । लभ्यते । ययोश्च व्यावापृथिव्योरः तर्मध्यॆ हरिरिंद्रश्चरत् । चरति । ते द्यावापृथिव्यानिंद्रोऽधारयदित्यर्थ: ॥ हरिधायसं । डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोरित्यस्माद्वहिहाथाञ्छंदसीत्यसुन् । णुदित्यनुवृत्तेरातो युक् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । पृथिवीं । प्रथेः शिवन् संप्रसारणं चेति पिवन्त्ययः । षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्चति जीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तः । हरिवर्पसं । वृज् संभक्तौ । वृजशीङ्ब्यां रूपस्वांगयोरित्यसुन्त्ययः। पुगागमश्च । संभज्यते तदिति वर्पो रूपं। बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । हरितोः । हृञ् हरण इत्यस्मात् हृस्यरुहि युषिभ्य इतिः । उ. १-९९ । इतीतिप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । भोजनं । भुज पालनाभ्यवहारयोरित्यस्मात्कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति कर्मणि ल्युट् । लित्स्वरः । अंतः । स्वरादिष्टंतोदात्तत्वेन पठितत्पादंतोदात्त, । चरत् । चरतिर्गत्यर्थः । लेटि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Between the two, heaven and earth, of green hue, his own two horses have abundant भोजनं (bhojanaṃ) (food), such as fodder, which is obtained; and between those same heaven and earth Hari, Indra, moves. The meaning is that Indra upheld those two, heaven and earth.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • ययोः (yayoḥ)—of which heaven and earth
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—throughout the middle
  • हरिः (hariḥ)—Indra
  • हरितोः (haritoḥ)—to his horses of green-tawny hue
  • भूरि (bhūri)—abundant
  • भोजनं (bhojanaṃ)—food such as fodder
  • (he has) made; and ययोः अंतः (yayoḥ aṃtaḥ)—throughout the middle of which heaven and earth
  • चरत् (carat)—he travels, such
  • हरिधायसं (haridhāyasaṃ)—endowed with golden rays
  • द्यां (dyāṃ)—the world of heaven
  • हरिवर्पसं (harivarpasaṃ)—adorned with crops and emeralds
  • पृथिवीं (pṛthivīṃ)—the earth
  • आधारयत् (ādhārayat)—has lifted and held up (established)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

He has lifted and held up the heaven endowed with golden rays and the earth adorned with crops and emeralds: the heaven and earth between which Indra has abundantly provided fodder and other food for his horses of green-tawny hue, and throughout the middle of which he travels. (He has created them.)

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra has upheld the yellow-rayed heaven , the verdant tinted earth ; there is abundant pasture (for his steeds) in the two azure spheres of heaven and earth, between which Hari travels.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The greatness of Indra is described by saying that he is the cause of the mutual growth of prosperity of heaven and earth. The description हरिधायसं द्यां हरिवर्पसं पृथिवीं (haridhāyasaṃ dyāṃ harivarpasaṃ pṛthivīṃ) is poetic

p. 68

and describes a principle of beauty; it is not merely a description of material wealth. The sky with its golden rays and the earth full of crops and emeralds, describing the beauty of the universe, make known the greatness of Indra, the primary cause of that beauty. Indra is the cause of the origin, the maintenance and the growth of heaven and earth.

Although हरिधायसं (haridhāyasaṃ) means "endowed with golden rays", wherever the words धायसे (dhāyase) and धायसा (dhāyasā) occur (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-95-1) the explanation is "supporting". The rays of the Sun support the universe. So the purport is "the rays of the Sun, which support the universe", and the meaning is the world of heaven endowed with such rays. Here the word हरि (hari) means golden. In the epithet हरिवर्पसं (harivarpasaṃ) the word हरि (hari) means emerald, and वर्पस् (varpas) means a radiant form. The earth has the epithet हरिवर्पसं (harivarpasaṃ) because it is endowed with world-attracting crops and emeralds. Indra has established heaven and earth, which are such nourishers of the world and endowed with world-attracting radiance.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

ज॒ज्ञा॒नो हरि॑तो॒ वृषा॒ विश्व॒मा भा॑ति रोच॒नं ।
हर्य॑श्वो॒ हरि॑तं धत्त॒ आयु॑ध॒मा वज्रं॑ बा॒ह्वोर्हरिं॑॥ ४ ॥

jajñāno harito vṛṣā viśvamā bhāti rocanaṃ |
haryaśvo haritaṃ dhatta āyudhamā vajraṃ bāhvorhariṃ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

जज्ञानः । हरितः । वृषा । विश्वं । आ । भाति । रोचनं ।
हरिऽश्वः । हरितं । धत्ते । आयुधं । आ । वज्रं । बाह्वोः । हरिं ॥ ४ ॥

jajñānaḥ | haritaḥ | vṛṣā | viśvaṃ | ā | bhāti | rocanaṃ |
hari 'śvaḥ | haritaṃ | dhatte | āyudhaṃ | ā | vajraṃ | bāhvoḥ | hariṃ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

वृषा कामानां वर्षको हरितो हरिद्वर्णोपेतो जज्ञानो जात इंद्रो विश्वं सर्वं रोचनं दीप्यमानं लोकमा भाति । सर्वतः प्रकाशयति । तथा हर्यश्व इंद्रो हरितं हरिद्वर्णोपेतमायुधं धत्ते । बाह्वोर्धत्ते । तथा हरिं शत्रूणां प्राणहारकं वज्रं बाह्वोराधत्ते ॥ जज्ञानः । जनी प्रादुर्भाव इत्यस्य लिटः कानच् । गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । भाति । भा दीप्ता वित्यस्यांतर्भावितण्यर्थस्य लटि रूपं । रोचनं । रुच दीप्तावित्यस्मादनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेरिति युच् । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । बाह्वोः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्नादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the showerer of desires, of green-tawny hue, being born, illumines on every side the whole shining world. Likewise Indra, lord of tawny horses, holds in his arms the weapon of tawny hue; and he holds in his arms the thunderbolt, हरिं (hariṃ), the taker of the lives of enemies.

p. 69

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • वृषा (vṛṣā)—showerer of desires
  • हरितः (haritaḥ)—of golden form; Indra
  • बज्ञानः (bajñānaḥ)—as soon as born
  • विश्वं (viśvaṃ)—the entire
  • रोचनं (rocanaṃ)—attractive world
  • अ भाति (a bhāti)—he causes to shine
  • हरश्वः (haraśvaḥ)—Indra, possessing horses named Hari
  • हरितं (haritaṃ)—golden
  • आयुधं (āyudhaṃ)—weapon
  • धत्ते (dhatte)—holds
  • हरिं (hariṃ)—that takes away (the lives of enemies)
  • वज्रं (vajraṃ)—the thunderbolt weapon
  • बाह्वोः (bāhvoḥ)—in his arms
  • (अधत्ते) ((adhatte))—holds
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the showerer of desires, of golden form, causes the entire attractive world to shine as soon as he is born. Indra, possessor of the horses named Hari, holds a golden weapon. He holds in his arms the thunderbolt that takes away the lives of enemies.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The azure-coloured showerer (of benefits), illumes, as soon as born, the whole luminous region ; the lord of the tawny steeds holds in his hands the yellow weapon, the destroying thunderbolt.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the greatness of Indra, the cause of the world's prosperity, is described, descriptions such as आयुधं धत्ते (āyudhaṃ dhatte) come along with it. Indra is a protector, and likewise a destroyer (of enemies). In the description that he makes the world attractive and radiant (विश्वं रोचनं आ भाति (viśvaṃ rocanaṃ ā bhāti)) and also lifts and holds a destructive weapon, the two forms of Indra are understood. The descriptions of Indra's thunderbolt, Viṣṇu's discus and Īśvara's trident are all of this kind. They are a harmony of protection and chastisement for the world, a harmony of truth and beauty. In their description a hidden spiritual principle is indicated. This principle of harmony will be discussed later, when the great nature of Indra's thunderbolt is explained.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इंद्रो॑ ह॒र्यंत॒मर्जु॑नं॒ वज्रं॑ शु॒क्रैर॒भीवृ॑तं ।
आपा॑वृणो॒द्धरि॑भि॒रद्रि॑भिः सु॒तमुद्गा हरि॑भिराजत ॥ ५ ॥

iṃdro haryaṃtamarjunaṃ vajraṃ śukrairabhīvṛtaṃ |
āpāvṛṇoddharibhiradribhiḥ sutamudgā haribhirājata ‖ 5 ‖

p. 70

Ṛk 5 (continued)

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

इंद्रः । हर्यंतं । अर्जुनं । वज्रं । शुक्रैः । अभिवृतं ।
अप । अवृणोत् । हरिभिः । अद्रिभिः । सुतं । उत् । गाः । हरिभिः । आजत ॥ ५ ॥

iṃdraḥ | haryaṃtaṃ | arjunaṃ | vajraṃ | śukraiḥ | abhivṛtaṃ |
apa | avṛṇot | haribhiḥ | adribhiḥ | sutaṃ | ut | gāḥ | haribhiḥ | ājata ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सोऽयमिंद्रो हर्यंतं कमनीयमर्जुनं शुभ्रं । शुभ्रत्वमुपपादयति । शुक्रैः शुभैः क्षीरादिभिरभिवृतं व्याप्तं वज्रं वेगवंतं हरिभिः । हरंत्येभिः सोमरसानिति हरयः। तैरद्रिभिग्रावभिः सुतमभिषुतं सोममपावृणोत् । आवरणरहितमकरोत् । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । पूषा राजानमाघृणिरपगूळ्हं गुहा हितं अविंदत् । ऋग्वे. १-२३-१४ । इति । तथा गाः पणिभिरपहृता गा हरिभिरश्वैरुपेतः स इंद्र उदाजत । विलान्नि रगमयत् ॥ अर्जुनं । अर्ज षर्ज आर्जन इत्यस्मादर्जॆर्णिलुक्चेत्युनन् । नित्स्वरः । अभिवृतं । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । आजत । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः । लजि व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra has uncovered the desirable (हर्यंतं (haryaṃtaṃ)) bright (अर्जुनं (arjunaṃ)) Soma. Sāyaṇa justifies the brightness: it is overlaid (अभिवृतं (abhivṛtaṃ)) with shining milk and the like; the vajra is swift. The हरिभिः (haribhiḥ) are the stones by which the Soma juices are carried off (हरंत्येभिः (haraṃtyebhiḥ)); with these pressing stones he made the pressed Soma free of covering. The mantra text is cited: "Pūṣan found the king, hidden, placed in the cave" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-14). Likewise Indra, accompanied by his tawny horses, drove out the cows carried off by the Paṇis, making them come out of the cave. The grammatical remainder is omitted.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • हर्यंतं (haryaṃtaṃ)—attractive
  • अर्जुनं (arjunaṃ)—bright
  • शुक्रैः (śukraiḥ)—with pure milk and the like
  • अभिवृतं (abhivṛtaṃ)—overlaid
  • वज्रं (vajraṃ)—swift-flowing
  • हरिभिः (haribhiḥ)—pressing out the juice
  • अद्रिभिः (adribhiḥ)—with stones
  • सुतं (sutaṃ)—crushed and pressed, the Soma juice
  • अपावृणोत् (apāvṛṇot)—released from concealment and made to appear shining
  • गाः (gāḥ)—the cows (carried off by the Paṇis)
  • हरिभिः (haribhiḥ)—Indra, furnished with horses
  • उत् अजत (ut ajata)—made them come out of the cave
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra uncovered the Soma juice, which is attractive, bright, overlaid with pure milk and the like, swift-flowing, and crushed and pressed by the pressing stones, releasing it from concealment and making it appear shining. Indra, furnished with horses, made the cows carried off by the Paṇis come out of the cave.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra has uncovered the desirable white-coloured, fast-flowing Soma, effused by the expressing stones, and overlaid with the shining (milk and other liquids), in like manner as when, borne by his tawny steeds, he rescued the cattle ### Printed p. 71

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this mantra the words arjuna, vajra and the rest are all epithets of the Soma juice. Arjuna is taken to mean bright; it is formed from the root raṃj, "to shine". In the Nirukta the word arjuna is read among the names of dawn (Ni. 1-8) and among the names of form (Ni. 3-7). The Nirukta author quotes अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः (ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1) and explains kṛṣṇa as night and arjuna as the day of white colour. Also in भद्रा वस्त्राण्यर्जुना वसाना (bhadrā vastrāṇyarjunā vasānā) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-9-2) it indicates the bright colour of cloth. Thus the word serves not only where a merely physical matter is expressed but also where a spiritual principle is expressed. For example, the two names Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna may be said to reflect two principles of the Lord, the hidden and the manifest. All principles perceptible to the outer eye are indicated by the word arjuna; and Ṛgvedic passages describing the hidden principle, such as महत्तन्नाम गुह्यं (mahattannāma guhyaṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-55-1) and एकस्यदृशे न रूपं (ekasyadṛśe na rūpaṃ) (1-164-44), suggest the meaning of the Bhagavadgītā phrase गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं (guhyādguhyataraṃ). So the uses of kṛṣṇa and arjuna in the senses of hidden (secret) and perceptible (bright) convey a spiritual principle. Vajra: explained as विवर्जयति प्राणान् (vivarjayati prāṇān), the thunderbolt having a destructive power. Its particulars were given earlier. In the present Ṛk it is used in the sense "swift-going". Adribhiḥ: आद्रिरादृणात्येतेन । अपि वा अत्तेः सात् (ādrirādṛṇātyetena | api vā atteḥ sāt). The word adri is formed either from the root dṛ meaning "to split" or from the root ad meaning "to eat". It is used in many places as a synonym both for the stones that press Soma and for Indra's vajra. Its particulars are given in the Special Topics of Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-149-1, in the 11th volume of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā. ### Printed p. 72 ## Sūkta 45 (Maṇḍala 3)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

आ मंद्रॆरिति पंचर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं बार्हतमैंद्रं ; आ मंद्रॆरित्यनुक्रमणिका । पूर्वसूक्ते बार्हतं त्वित्युक्तत्वादस्यापि बार्हतत्वं ॥ विशेषविनियोगस्तु यत्र श्रुत्या न सूत्रितः । स्मार्तं तत्र विजानीयादृग्विधानादि शास्त्रतः ॥ अनुवादवु—आ मंद्रॆः ऎंब ई सूक्तवु नाल्कनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि एळनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि ऐदु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ विश्वामित्रनु ऋषियु, इंद्रनु देवतॆयु, बृहती छंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि आ मंद्रॆः ऎंदु मॊदलागि हेळिरुवुदु. हिंदिन सूक्तदल्लि हेळिरुवंतॆ बृहतीछंदस्सिन शस्त्रमंत्रगळिगागि ई सूक्तद विनियोगविरुवुदु. याव सूक्त अथवा मंत्रगळिगॆ शौतसूत्रादिगळल्लि विनियोगवु हेळल्पट्टिरुवुदिल्लवो अवुगळिगॆ स्मार्तप्रयोग गदल्लियू, शौनकोक्तवाद ऋग्विधानवॆंब ग्रंथदल्लि हेळिरुवंतॆयू, इतर शास्त्रगळल्लि हेळिरु वंतॆयू विनियोगविरुवुदॆंदु भाविसबेकु. ॥ ओं ॥ सूक्त—४५ मंडल—३ ॥ अनुवाक—४ ॥ सूक्त—४५ ॥ अष्टक—३ ॥ अध्याय—३ ॥ वर्ग—९ ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—५ ॥ । ऋषिः— विश्वामित्र । । देवता— इंद्र । । छंदः— बृहती ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta आ मंद्रैः (ā maṃdraiḥ) has five Ṛks and is the seventh sūkta; seer Viśvāmitra, deity Indra; the Anukramaṇikā begins "ā mandraiḥ". Since the previous sūkta was said to be Bārhata, this one too is Bārhata. Where no specific use is given by Śruti-sūtra, one should know it from the Smārta rule, the Ṛgvidhāna and other śāstras.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This sūkta, आ मंद्रैः (ā maṃdraiḥ), is the seventh in the fourth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Viśvāmitra is the seer, Indra the deity, Bṛhatī the metre. Its use is for the śastra mantras of Bṛhatī metre, as stated for the previous sūkta. For any sūkta or mantras whose use is not stated in the Śrauta-sūtras and the like, the use is to be understood as in the Smārta practice, in the Ṛgvidhāna attributed to Śaunaka, and in other śāstras.

Particulars

Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 45; Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 3; Varga 9. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Viśvāmitra. Deity: Indra. Metre: Bṛhatī. #### Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

आ मं॒द्रैरिं॑द्र॒ हरि॑भिर्या॒हि म॒यूर॑रोमभिः ।
मा त्वा॒ के चि॒न्नि य॑म॒न्विं न पा॒शिनोऽति॒ धन्वे॑व॒ ता इ॑हि ॥ १ ॥

ā maṃdrairiṃdra haribhiryāhi mayūraromabhiḥ |
mā tvā ke cinni yamanviṃ na pāśino 'ti dhanveva tā ihi ‖ 1 ‖

p. 73

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

आ । मंद्रैः । इंद्र । हरिभिः । याहि । मयूररोमभिः ।
मा । त्वा । के । चित् । नि । यमन् । विं । न । पाशिनः । अति । धन्वइव । तान् । इहि॥१॥

ā | maṃdraiḥ | iṃdra | haribhiḥ | yāhi | mayūraromabhiḥ |
mā | tvā | ke | cit | ni | yaman | viṃ | na | pāśinaḥ | ati | dhanvaiva | tān | ihi‖1‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र मंद्रैर्मादयितृभिर्मयूररोमभिर्मयूररोमसदृशरोमयुक्तैर्हरिभिरश्चैरुपेतस्त्वमा याहि । यज्ञं प्रत्यागच्छ । केचिदपि जनास्त्वा त्वां मा नि यमन् । मा नियच्छंतु । गमनप्रतिबंधं मा कुर्वंत्वित्यभिप्रायः । प्रतिबंधे दृष्टांतः । विं न । यथा पाशिनः पाशहस्ता व्याधा विं गच्छंतं दक्षिणं नियच्छंति तद्वन्मा नियच्छंतु । किंच धन्वेव । यथा पांथा धन्व मरुदेशं शीघ्रमतिगच्छंति । तद्वद्दमनप्रतिबंधकानतीत्य शीघ्रमिहि । आगच्छ ॥ मंद्रॆः । मदि स्तुत्यादिश्वित्यस्य स्थायितंचीत्यादिना रक्षृत्ययः । इदित्तान्नुम् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मयूररोमभिः । मयूररोमवद्रोमाणि येषामिति सप्तम्युपमानपूर्वपदस्य बहुव्रीहिरुत्तरपदलोपश्च । पा. २-२-२४-१२ । इति समास उत्तरपदलोपश्च । मयूरशब्दो मीनातेरूरन् । उ. १-६८ । इत्यूरन्प्रत्ययांतः । मीनाति सर्पानिति मयूरो बर्हि । नित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते मादीनां । फि. ३-४ । इति सूत्रेण मध्योदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । यमन् यम उपरम इत्यस्य लेट्यडागमे रूपं । इहि । इण् गतावित्यस्य लोटि रूपं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, come to the sacrifice with your delighting horses, whose hair is like peacock hair. Let no persons restrain you." The example of restraint: as fowlers with snares in hand restrain a bird flying straight, let them not restrain you. Further, धन्वेव (dhanveva): as travellers quickly cross a desert, so pass beyond those who would hold you back and come quickly. Mayūra is derived from मीनाति सर्पानिति (mīnāti sarpāniti) ("he injures snakes"), the peacock. The grammatical remainder is omitted.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • मंद्रैः (maṃdraiḥ)—radiant
  • मयूररोमभिः (mayūraromabhiḥ)—having hair attractive like peacock feathers
  • हरिभिः (haribhiḥ)—you, joined with the horses
  • आ याहि (ā yāhi)—come to the sacrificial place
  • पाशिनः (pāśinaḥ)—fowlers holding a net
  • विं न (viṃ na)—as they stop a bird
  • के चित् (ke cit)—let no one (on the way)
  • त्वा (tvā)—you
  • मा नि यमन् (mā ni yaman)—stop
  • धन्वेव (dhanveva)—as travellers walk quickly to cross the obstacle of a desert
  • तान् (tān)—(you also) the obstacles (on the way)
  • अति (ati)—having crossed
  • इहि (ihi)—come quickly
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, come to our sacrificial place with horses that are radiant and have hair attractive like peacock feathers. As fowlers holding a net stop a bird ### Printed p. 74 so let no one on the way stop you. As travellers walk quickly and cross a desert, so do you also cross the obstacles that may arise on the way and come quickly.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Come, Indra, with your exulting peacock-haired steeds; let no persons detain you as (fowlers) throwing snares catch a bird : pass them by (quickly) as (travellers cross) a desert.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In describing Indra's unobstructed power, his swiftness is compared to the unobstructed flight of a bird. There is another comparison, धन्वेव (dhanveva). The word dhanva is read in the Nirukta among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 1-2) and among the names of motion (Ni. 4-2). Here it means motion; Indra's speed is compared to the swiftness of travellers in a desert. In places such as धन्वचरो न वंसगस्तृषाणश्चकमानः (dhanvacaro na vaṃsagastṛṣāṇaścakamānaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-36-1), dhanvacara is explained as a man who moves swiftly in a desert. Sāyaṇa sometimes explains it as a man who moves carrying a bow. Here the speed of motion and unobstructed power are indicated. #### Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

वृ॒त्र॒खा॒दो व॑लंरु॒जः पु॒रां द॒र्मो अ॒पाम॒जः ।
स्थात्ता॒ रथ॑स्य॒ हर्यो॑रभिस्व॒र इंद्रो॑ दृ॒ळ्हा चि॑दारु॒जः ॥ २ ॥

vṛtrakhādo valaṃrujaḥ purāṃ darmo apāmajaḥ |

वृत्रखादः । वलंरुज: । पुरां । दर्मः । अपां । अज: ।
स्थाता । रथस्य । हर्योः । अभिस्वरे । इंद्रः । दृळ्हा । चित् । आरुज: ॥ २ ॥

vṛtrakhādaḥ | valaṃruja: | purāṃ | darmaḥ | apāṃ | aja: |
sthātā | rathasya | haryoḥ | abhisvare | iṃdraḥ | dṛḷhā | cit | āruja: ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सोऽयमिंद्रो वृत्रखादः । वृत्रं खादति हिनस्तीति वृत्रखादः । वलंरुज: । वृणोश्याकाशमिति वलो मेघः । तस्य भंजकः । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । बिभेद वलं ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra is vṛtrakhāda: he devours (injures) Vṛtra. Valaṃruja: vala is the cloud, since it covers the sky (the verb is vṛṇoti); he is its breaker. So the mantra text: "he split Vala" ### Printed p. 75

ऋग्वे ३-३४-१० । इति । ततोऽपामजो मेघभेदनद्वारापां प्रेरकः पुरां शत्रुसंबंधिनां पुराणां दर्मो दारकः । तथा हर्योरश्वयोरभिस्वरेऽस्मदाभिमुख्येन प्रेरणे निमित्तभूते सति रथस्य स्थाता रथमधिष्ठाता । तथा दृळ्हा चित् दृढानामतिबलवतां शत्रूणामस्यारुजः समंताद्वंजको भवति ॥ वृत्रखादः । खादृ भक्षण इत्यस्मात्मर्मण्यण् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । वलंरुजः । रुजो भंगे। कर्मण्युपपदे मूलविभुजादित्वात्कृत्ययः । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमिति द्वितीयाया आलुक् । थाधादिस्वरः। आरुजः । रुजो भंग इत्यस्मादिगुपधलक्षणः कः । समासे थाधादिस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-34-10). Hence he is apāmaja, the impeller of the waters by splitting the cloud; darma, the tearer of the cities of the enemy. When his two horses are urged towards us (abhisvara), he is the stander on the chariot, its mounter. And he is the breaker on all sides of firm, very mighty enemies. The grammatical remainder is omitted.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

  • वलंरुजः (valaṃrujaḥ)—splitter of the cloud
  • अपामजः (apāmajaḥ)—sender down of water in the form of rain
  • पुरां (purāṃ)—of enemy cities
  • दर्मः (darmaḥ)—destroyer
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • हर्योः (haryoḥ)—his horses
  • अभिस्वरे (abhisvare)—to urge to run towards us

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, splitter of the cloud, sender down of water in the form of rain, destroyer of enemy cities, sits in his chariot to urge his horses to run towards us, and has the power to destroy even the exceedingly mighty enemies.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The devourer of Vritra, the fracturer of the cloud, the sender of the waters, the demolisher of cities. Indra, the destroyer of powerful enemies, has mounted his chariot to urge his horses to our presence.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The matters of Vala and Vṛtra were explained in detail earlier. Some hold that Vala and Vṛtra were brothers; they may also be understood as persons reflecting darkness. In the present Ṛk too, from वृणोतीति वलः (vṛṇotīti valaḥ) ("it covers the atmosphere"), the word vala is a synonym for cloud. Abhisvare: the word abhisvara is used in different senses. Its particular meaning was given earlier in the Special Topics of Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-21. "अभिस्वर्तारो अर्कं न (abhisvartāro arkaṃ na)

p. 76

The word अभिस्वर (abhisvara) is a synonym for the worshippers in passages such as सुष्टुभः (suṣṭubhaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-78-4): those who all around (अभितः (abhitaḥ)) make the sound of praise in order to impel the gods. In the present context, as it is explained in passages such as चतुष्पादेति द्विपदामभिस्वरे संपश्यन् पंक्तिरुपतिष्ठमानः (catuṣpādeti dvipadāmabhisvare saṃpaśyan paṃktirupatiṣṭhamānaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-117-8), the word अभिस्वर (abhisvara) can be taken to mean "approach"; the purport is "go towards". The purport is: to impel the horses to run towards us. The technical usages such as अभिस्वरंति (abhisvaraṃti) were also explained earlier.

gaṃbhīrān | udadhīn iva | kratuṃ | puṣyasi | gāḥ iva |
pra | sugopāḥ | yavasaṃ | dhenavaḥ | yathā | hradaṃ | kulyāḥ iva | āśaśa ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र त्वं गंभीरान्महावकाशानुदधीन् समुद्रानुदकैर्यथा पोषयसि तद्वत्कृतुं यज्ञस्य कर्तारमिमं यजमानमभिपुतफलप्रदानेन पुष्यसि । पोषयसि । अत्र दृष्टांतः । यथा सुगोपाः सविचीनो गोपालो यवसेन गा: पोषयति तद्वत्।यथा धेनवो यवसं तृणादिकं प्राप्नुवंति तद्वत्त्वं सोमान् प्राप्नोषि । ते च सोमाः कुल्या इव कृत्रिमसरितो ह्रदं महाजलाशयं यथा प्राप्नुवंति तद्वत्वामाशत । व्याप्नुवंति ॥ गंभीरान् । गाध्य प्रतिष्ठालिप्सयोग्रंथे चेत्यस्माद्गंभीरगभीरावित्यनेन सूत्रेण इरच् प्रत्ययः । नुमागमोपधाह्रस्वभकाराः सर्वे निपात्यंते । चित्तादंतोदात्तः । उदधीनिव । उदकशब्द उपपदे दधातेरधिकरणेऽर्थे कर्मण्यधिकरणे चेति किप्रत्ययः । उदकशब्दस्य पेषंवासवाहनधिषु च । पा. ६-३-५८ । इत्युदभावः । कृत्स्वरः । इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः । पुष्यसि । पुष पुष्टावित्यस्यांतर्णितण्यर्थस्य लटि रूपं । निघातः । सुगोपाः । गोपायतेः क्विपि रूपं । यथा । यथेति पादांते : फि ४-१७ । इति निघातः । आतत । अशू व्याप्तानित्यस्माल्लजि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, as you nourish with waters the deep oceans of great extent, so you nourish this sacrificer, the doer (क्रतुं (kratuṃ)) of the sacrifice, by granting the fruit he desires. An illustration is given here: as a good herdsman, one who watches well, nourishes the cows with fodder; as cows obtain fodder, grass and the like, so you obtain the Soma-juices. And those Soma-juices reach you, as artificial channels reach a lake, a great reservoir of water. They pervade you."

p. 77

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • गंभीरान् (gaṃbhīrān)—very deep
  • उदधीन् इव (udadhīn iva)—(as you fill) the oceans (with waters)
  • सुगोपाः (sugopāḥ)—an excellent herdsman
  • गाः इव (gāḥ iva)—as (he) nourishes the cows
  • क्रतुं (kratuṃ)—the sacrificer
  • पुष्यसि (puṣyasi)—you nourish (with the granting of what he desires)
  • यथा (yathā)—in the way in which
  • धेनवः (dhenavaḥ)—cows
  • यवसं (yavasaṃ)—obtain fodder and the like (so you too obtain the Soma)
  • कुल्याः इव (kulyāḥ iva)—as small rivers
  • ह्रदं (hradaṃ)—reach a lake
  • प्र आशत (pra āśata)—(those Soma-juices) reach your belly
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as you fill the very deep oceans with waters, and as an excellent herdsman nourishes the cows, so you nourish the sacrificer with the granting of what he desires. As cows abundantly obtain fodder and the like, so you too obtain the Soma. As small rivers reach a lake, so those streams of Soma-juice reach your belly.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

You cherish the celebrator of the pious rite as (you fill) the deep seas (with water) ; or as a careful herdsman (cherishes) the cows ; (you imbibe the Soma) as cows (obtain) fodder, (and the juices flow into you) as rivulets flow into a lake.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here the nature of the wealth that Indra provides for a sacrificer who performs good rites is described. Two aspects of this bestowal of wealth are given by way of comparison. This wealth is deep like the ocean. And the regard that Indra shows towards the sacrificer in this bestowal: both of these are possible only for an excellent sacrificer. In this Ṛk the word क्रतु (kratu) is a synonym for the sacrificer.

In the Ṛk-saṃhitā the word क्रतु (kratu) for the most part denotes the rite (karma); in some places it also denotes the aim of the rite. The deeper sense of this word has been explained in detail in the 13th part of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā. Here, since it is a synonym for the sacrificer, it is used in a special sense. This word denotes both the sacrificer's aim and his power of action.

In the Saṃhitā and also in the Upaniṣads the two words क्रतु (kratu) and दक्ष (dakṣa) denote the person's power of will and power of action; or they may denote both the inner power and the outward action.

p. 78

The Ṛk-saṃhitā explains in detail that if a person's wish or resolve is pure, then his practical capacity to obtain the human aim also grows. इंद्रः सुतेषु सोमेषु क्रतुं पुनीत उक्थं (iṃdraḥ suteṣu someṣu kratuṃ punīta ukthaṃ) विदे वृधस्य दक्षसो महान्हि षः (vide vṛdhasya dakṣaso mahānhi ṣaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-13-1) Here, in वृधस्य दक्षसः विदे (vṛdhasya dakṣasaḥ vide), it is stated that in order to acquire strength that makes one grow, Indra purifies the sacrificer (his resolve), as in क्रतुं पुनीते (kratuṃ punīte). Even when the person's spiritual aim is explained, it is set out in sentences such as ओं क्रतो स्मर (oṃ krato smara) (Īśa. 17) NOTE and क्रतुमयःपुरुषः (kratumayaḥpuruṣaḥ) (Chā. U. 3-14-2). In such contexts Śaṅkarācārya has explained the word क्रतु (kratu) as resolution, or as the person's duty; the purport is resolve, and the power of action that accomplishes the resolve. According to this resolve and power the aim is accomplished. The nature of क्रतु (kratu) is stated thus: यथाक्रतुरस्मिल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत (yathākraturasmilloke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati sa kratuṃ kurvīta) and so on. In the present Ṛk too the nature of the wealth that comes to such a person made of क्रतु (kratu) is described.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

-हे इंद्र नोऽस्माकं तुजं शत्रूणां बाधकं रयिं धनेनोपलक्षितं पुत्रमा भर । संपादय । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अंशं न ! यथा पिता प्रतिजानते व्यवहारज्ञाय पुत्राय स्वकीयस्य धनस्य भागं ददाति तद्वत् । किंच पक्वं फलं प्रति वृक्षमंकीवांकुशी यथा धूनोति तथा त्वं संपारणमस्मदच्छायाः सम्यक् पूरकं वसु धनं धूनुहि । चालय । प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः " प्रतिजानते । ज्ञा अवबोधन इत्यस्य

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, bring to us तुजं (tujaṃ), the harasser of enemies, रयिं (rayiṃ), that is, a son marked by wealth; provide him. An illustration: अंशं न (aṃśaṃ na), as a father gives a share of his own wealth to a son who knows how to manage affairs (प्रतिजानते (pratijānate)). Further: as a man with a hook (अंकी (aṃkī)) shakes a tree for the ripe fruit, so you shake down for us the wealth that is संपारणं (saṃpāraṇaṃ), that fully satisfies our wishes; that is, give it."

p. 79

शतरि रूपं । प्रादिसमास- । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । धूनुहि । धूञ् कंपन इत्यस्य लोटि रूपं । संपारणं । प्प पालनपूरणयोरित्यस्य ण्यंतस्य करणे ल्युट् । समासे कृत्स्वर ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This block contains only Sāyaṇa's grammatical notes on the words of the Ṛk.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • प्रतिजानते (pratijānate)—to a son who has acquired knowledge of practical affairs
  • अंशं न (aṃśaṃ na)—as a father gives a share of wealth
  • नः (naḥ)—to me
  • तुजं (tujaṃ)—harmful to enemies
  • रयिं (rayiṃ)—wealth in the form of a son
  • आ भर (ā bhara)—provide
  • सक्वं (sakvaṃ)—ripe
  • फलं (phalaṃ)—for the fruit
  • अंकी (aṃkī)—a hook
  • वृक्षं इव (vṛkṣaṃ iva)—as it shakes the tree (and provides the fruit)
  • संपारणं (saṃpāraṇaṃ)—that gives us satisfaction
  • वसु (vasu)—wealth
  • धनुहि (dhanuhi)—make it move (make it reach us)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as a father gives a share of wealth to a son who has acquired knowledge of practical affairs, provide us with a son who harasses enemies. As a hook shakes the tree for the ripe fruit and provides the fruit, set in motion the wealth that gives us satisfaction and provide it to us.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Grant us riches, securing (us against foes), (as a father bestows) his portion on (a son) arrived at maturity; send down upon us, Indra, wealth adequate (to our desires), as a crook brings down the ripe fruit from a tree.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk too there is a description of the wealth that comes to a person who knows the duty of sacrifice. The word तुजं (tujaṃ) is used in the sense of harming. In the Nirukta this word is listed among the names of the thunderbolt. It is also used in the sense of giving: तुजतिः दानकर्मा (tujatiḥ dānakarmā). In Ṛks such as भूं चिद्दि तुजशो मर्त्यस्य (bhūṃ ciddi tujaśo martyasya) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-8) the generosity of the patron is described as "giver of much". In the present Ṛk too, when it says तुजं रयिं आ भर (tujaṃ rayiṃ ā bhara), it may be explained either as "provide the wealth of a son who harasses enemies" or as "give a generous son".

संपारणं (saṃpāraṇaṃ) is formed from the root पृ पालनतरणयोः (pṛ pālanataraṇayoḥ), "to protect" or "to carry across". It may mean wealth that protects from poverty, or that carries one across poverty and brings one to the end. In sum the purport is: what gives satisfaction.

p. 80

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स्व॒युरिं॑द्र स्व॒राळ॑सि॒ स्मद्दि॑ष्टिः॒ स्वय॑शस्तरः ।
स ना॑वृधा॒न ओज॑सा पुरुष्टुत॒ भवा॑ नः सु॒श्रव॑स्तमः ॥ ५ ॥

svayuriṃdra svarāḷasi smaddiṣṭiḥ svayaśastaraḥ |
sa nāvṛdhāna ojasā puruṣṭuta bhavā naḥ suśravastamaḥ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

स्वयुः। इंद्र । स्वराट् । असि । स्मर्त्‌दिष्टिः । स्वयशःतरः !
सः । ववृधानः । ओजसा । पुरुस्तुत । भव । नः । सुश्रवःतमः ॥ ५ ॥

svayuḥ| iṃdra | svarāṭ | asi | smartdiṣṭiḥ | svayaśaḥtaraḥ !
saḥ | vavṛdhānaḥ | ojasā | purustuta | bhava | naḥ | suśravaḥtamaḥ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र स्वयुर्धनवानसि । तथा स्वराट् स्वर्गस्य राजासि । स्मद्दिष्टिर्भद्रवाक्यः स्वयशस्तरोऽतिशयेन प्रभूतकीर्तिरसि । हे पुरुष्टुत बहुभिराहूतेंद्र स त्वमोजसा बलेन वावृधानः वर्धमानः सन् नोऽस्मदर्थं सुश्रवस्तमोऽतिशयेन शोभनान्नोपेतो भव ॥ स्वयुः स्वशब्दान्मत्त्वर्थियो युः। स्वराट् । राज्य दीप्ता । क्विप् । व्रश्चादिना षत्वं । स्मद्दिष्टिः । स्सत् सुमदित्यर्थे । उकारलोपश्कांदसः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । पुरुष्टुत । संहितायां स्तुतस्तोमयोश्चंदसीति षत्वं । भव । भवतेर्लोटि रूपं । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिज इति संहितायां दीर्घः । सुश्रवस्तमः । श्रवः शब्दोऽसुनंतः । बहुव्रीहावाद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छंदसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं। तदंतादतिशायने तमप् । तस्य पित्तादनुदात्तत्वे बहुव्रीहिस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, you are स्वयुः (svayuḥ), possessed of wealth; likewise स्वराट् (svarāṭ), king of heaven. You are स्मद्दिष्टिः (smaddiṣṭiḥ), of auspicious speech, and स्वयशस्तरः (svayaśastaraḥ), of exceedingly great fame. O पुरुष्टुत (puruṣṭuta), Indra called upon by many, you, growing in strength (ओजसा (ojasā)), be for us सुश्रवस्तमः (suśravastamaḥ), most excellently endowed with good food." The rest of the block is grammatical.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • स्वयुः (svayuḥ)—(you) are possessed of wealth
  • स्वराट् (svarāṭ)—lord of all heaven
  • स्मद्दिष्टिः (smaddiṣṭiḥ)—of auspicious speech
  • स्वयशस्तरः (svayaśastaraḥ)—exceedingly famous
  • असि (asi)—you are
  • पुरुष्टुत (puruṣṭuta)—O Indra, praised by many
  • सः (saḥ)—you, of such greatness
  • ओजसा (ojasā)—with strength
  • वावृधानः (vāvṛdhānaḥ)—growing
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • सुश्रवस्तमः (suśravastamaḥ)—become an excellent giver of food
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are possessed of wealth, lord of all heaven, of auspicious speech and exceedingly famous. O Indra, praised by many, you who have such greatness, growing in strength, become for us an excellent giver of food.

p. 81

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

You are possessed of opulence, Indra; you are the lord of heaven, auspicious and renowend: may you who are adored of many, increasing in vigour, be to us a most (bountiful bestower) of food.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here Indra's independence and sovereignty are described. The words स्वायुः (svāyuḥ) and स्वराट् (svarāṭ) also indicate independence.

स्वयुः (svayuḥ)—This word is used in two places. In पशुर्नैति स्वयुरगोपाः (paśurnaiti svayuragopāḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-4-7) it is explained as "one who moves about independently like an animal". In the present Ṛk it is explained as "one possessed of wealth". The purport lies in being without dependence on others and without subordination.

स्वराट् (svarāṭ)—It means one who is lord of himself. It can be taken as "self-luminous by his own greatness" or as "sovereign". This sovereignty is full of spiritual and moral principle. स्वराट् (svarāṭ) also means one who is lord over himself. Considered from that point of view, it also means that a person who is lord over himself is fit to be lord of the world. This very point is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: the purport is that one who is to be lord of the world must have complete self-restraint, and must have self-independence without being subject to outward powers. In this word स्वराट् (svarāṭ) a harmony of spiritual and Vedic practice is seen; the presence of a harmony of these two practices is the chief mark of Vedic culture. Besides this, the commentators have explained the word स्वराट् (svarāṭ) as "king of heaven". In accordance with the śruti sentence स एक राजो जगतः (sa eka rājo jagataḥ), the meaning that Indra himself is king of this world and of heaven is described in many places in the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda.

As described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, the word स्वराट् (svarāṭ) must combine both aspects, lord of oneself and lord of the world. The purport is that one who is not self-restrained cannot be a sovereign. In the present Ṛk the two words स्वयुः (svayuḥ) and स्वराट् (svarāṭ) indicate these two special qualities of Indra. The meaning of the word स्वराट् (svarāṭ) can be stated from many points of view.

स्मद्दिष्टिः (smaddiṣṭiḥ)—It was stated earlier that the word स्मत् (smat) has the meanings beautiful, auspicious, propitious. दिष्टि (diṣṭi) is explained here as speech. The meaning is: one with auspicious speech. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-3-69 NOTE and similar places it means "of pleasing sight".

p. 82

Sūkta 46 (Maṇḍala 3)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

युध्मस्य त इति पंचर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रमैंद्रं । युद्धस्येत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ दशरात्रे चतुर्थेऽहनि निष्केवल्ये युध्मस्य त इति सूक्तं निविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । कुह श्रुत इंद्रो युध्मस्य त इति निष्केवल्यं । आ. ७-११ । इति ॥ ऋषभनाम्मेकाहेऽपि निष्केवल्यइदं सूक्तं निविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । युध्मस्य त इति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-७ इति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning युध्मस्य ते (yudhmasya te) is a group of five ṛks, the eighth hymn. It is by Viśvāmitra and addressed to Indra (the Anukramaṇikā: युद्धस्य (yuddhasya)). Use: on the fourth day of the Daśarātra, at the Niṣkevalya, the hymn युध्मस्य ते (yudhmasya te) serves as the nivid-hymn. The sūtra is: कुह श्रुत इंद्रो युध्मस्य त इति निष्केवल्यं (kuha śruta iṃdro yudhmasya ta iti niṣkevalyaṃ) (Ā. 7-11). In the one-day rite called Ṛṣabha as well, this hymn is the nivid-hymn at the Niṣkevalya. The sūtra is: युध्मस्य त इति मध्यंदिनः (yudhmasya ta iti madhyaṃdinaḥ) (Ā. 9-7).

Anuvāda

This hymn, "Yudhmasya te", is the eighth hymn in the fourth anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Its seer is Viśvāmitra, its deity Indra, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā begins with "Yudhmasya". When the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras are recited on the fourth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, the ṛks of this hymn are used for the nivid mantras; this is stated by the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra, in the sūtra "Kuha śruta Indro yudhmasya ta iti niṣkevalyam" (Ā. 7-11). It is likewise explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra, "Yudhmasya ta iti madhyandinaḥ" (Ā. 9-7), that in the one-day sacrifice called Ṛṣabhanāman the ṛks of this hymn are used for the nivid mantras of the Niṣkevalya śastra.

Particulars

Hymn 46. Maṇḍala 3, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 46. Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 3, Varga 10. Number of the book (Ṛks) in the hymn: 5. Seer: Viśvāmitra. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

p. 83

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यु॒ध्मस्य॑ ते वृष॒भस्य॑ स्व॒राज॑ उ॒ग्रस्य॒ यूनः॒ स्थवि॑रस्य॒ फृष्टेः॑ ।
अजू॑र्यतो व॒ज्रिणो॑ वी॒र्या॒३॒॑णींद्र॑ श्रु॒तस्य॑ मह॒तो ॒॑ महानि ॥ १ ॥

yudhmasya te vṛṣabhasya svarāja ugrasya yūnaḥ sthavirasya phṛṣṭeḥ |
ajūryato vajriṇo vīryāṇīṃdra śrutasya mahato
mahāni ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

युध्मस्य । ते । वृषभस्य । स्वराजः । उग्रस्य । यूनः । स्थविरस्य । फृष्टेः ।
अजूर्यतः । वज्रिणः । वीर्याणि । इंद्र । श्रुतस्य । महतः । महानि ॥ १ ॥

yudhmasya | te | vṛṣabhasya | svarājaḥ | ugrasya | yūnaḥ | sthavirasya | phṛṣṭeḥ |
ajūryataḥ | vajriṇaḥ | vīryāṇi | iṃdra | śrutasya | mahataḥ | mahāni ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र युध्मस्य योधनशीलस्य वृषभस्याभिमतफलसेचकस्य स्वराजो धनाधिपतेरुग्रस्य समर्थस्य यूनो नित्यतरुणस्य स्थविरस्य चिरंतनस्य घृष्टेः शत्रूणां संघर्षकस्याजूर्यतो जरारहितस्य वज्रिणः श्रुतस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रसिद्धस्य अत एव महतस्ते तव वीर्याणि महानि । महांति खलु ॥ युध्मस्य । युध संप्रहारे । इषियुधींधिदसीत्यादिना मक्प्रत्ययः । यूनः । यौतेः कनिन्युवृषीत्यादिना कनिन्। श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धित इति संप्रसारणं । नित्स्वरः । स्थविरस्य । अजिरशिशिरशिथिलेत्यादिना किरन्प्रत्ययांतो । निपातितः । घृष्टेः । घृषु संघर्षे । कृविघृष्टिच्छवीत्यादिना क्विन्प्रत्ययांतो निपात्यते । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, your heroic deeds are great: you are युध्मस्य (yudhmasya), given to fighting; वृषभस्य (vṛṣabhasya), the sprinkler of the desired fruit; स्वराजः (svarājaḥ), lord of wealth; उग्रस्य (ugrasya), capable; यूनः (yūnaḥ), ever young; स्थविरस्य (sthavirasya), ancient; घृष्टेः (ghṛṣṭeḥ), the grinder-down of enemies; अजूर्यतः (ajūryataḥ), free of old age; वज्रिणः (vajriṇaḥ), bearer of the thunderbolt; श्रुतस्य (śrutasya), famed in the three worlds. Therefore, being great, your heroic deeds are great; for they are indeed mighty. The remainder of the block gives derivations and accent notes on yudhmasya, yūnaḥ, sthavirasya and ghṛṣṭeḥ.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • युद्धस्य (yuddhasya)—of the excellent warrior
  • वृषभस्य (vṛṣabhasya)—of the showerer of desires
  • स्वराजः (svarājaḥ)—of the lord of all wealth
  • उग्रस्य (ugrasya)—of the fearsome
  • यूनः (yūnaḥ)—of the young
  • स्थविरस्य (sthavirasya)—(at the same time) of the aged (the ancient)
  • फृष्टैः (phṛṣṭaiḥ)—of him who crushes enemies
  • अजूरतः (ajūrataḥ)—of him free from old age (decrepitude)
  • वज्रिणः (vajriṇaḥ)—of the holder of the thunderbolt
  • श्रुतस्य (śrutasya)—of him famed in the three worlds
  • महतः (mahataḥ)—of him who is therefore endowed with greatness
  • ते (te)—your
  • वीर्याणि (vīryāṇi)—deeds of valour
  • महानि (mahāni)—are most wonderful
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, excellent warrior, showerer of desires, lord of all wealth, young and ancient, crusher of enemies, free from old age, holder of the thunderbolt: for that very reason you are endowed with greatness, and your deeds of valour are most wonderful.

p. 84

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Vast are the energies of you, Indra, the warrior, (the showerer of benefits), the lord of wealth, the fierce; you are (both) young and old; the overcomer of foes, the undecaying, the wielder of the thunderbolt; and you are mighty and renowned.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ते वीर्याणि महानि (te vīryāṇi mahāni)—In praising your heroic deeds as most wonderful, the verse also describes together with them the great qualities needed for such deeds. Earlier, "अहन्नहिमन्वपस्तर्द प्र वक्षणा अभिनत्पर्वतानां ; आत्सूरं जनयन्दामुषासं (ahannahimanvapastarda pra vakṣaṇā abhinatparvatānāṃ ; ātsūraṃ janayandāmuṣāsaṃ)" (Indra split the cloud, made a way for the streams flowing in the mountains, and created the sun, the dawn and the firmament for their light), and so on, describing Indra's valour, the glory of Indra was described with "इंद्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्रवोचं (iṃdrasya nu vīryāṇi pravocaṃ)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32). The fighting capacity, fierceness and self-rule useful for such great deeds are described in the present ṛk.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

म॒हा अ॑सि महिष॒ वृष्ट्ये॑भिर्धन॒स्पृदु॑ग्र॒ सह॑मानो अ॒न्यान् ।
एको॒ विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य॒ राजा॒ स यो॒धया॑ च क्ष॒यया॑ च॒ ॑ जनान् ॥ २ ॥

mahā asi mahiṣa vṛṣṭyebhirdhanaspṛdugra sahamāno anyān |
eko viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā sa yodhayā ca kṣayayā ca
janān ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

महान् । असि । महिष । वृष्ण्येभिः । धनस्पृत् । उग्र । सहमानः । अन्यान् ।
एकः । विश्वस्य । भुवनस्य । राजा । सः । योधय । च । क्षयय । च । जनान् ॥ २ ॥

mahān | asi | mahiṣa | vṛṣṇyebhiḥ | dhanaspṛt | ugra | sahamānaḥ | anyān |
ekaḥ | viśvasya | bhuvanasya | rājā | saḥ | yodhaya | ca | kṣayaya | ca | janān ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे महिष महनीय उग्र इंद्र त्वं महानसि । धनस्पृत् धनानि दानभोगत्यागैः पारं नयंस्त्वं वृष्ट्येभिर्वीरैरन्यान् । शत्रून्सहमानोऽभिभवन्वर्तसे । तथा विश्वस्य सर्वस्य भुवनस्यैकोऽसहायो राजा स त्वं योधय च । ससत्नान् प्रहर । जनान् क्षयय च । निवासय । बाधकान्हत्वा साधुजनान् स्वस्थाने स्थापयेत्यभिप्रायः ॥ महिष । मह पूजायां । अविमहोष्टिषच् । उ. १-४६ । इति टिषच्-

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mahiṣa (worshipful), fierce Indra, you are great. As धनस्पृत् (dhanaspṛt) you carry riches across (to the far shore) by giving, enjoying and relinquishing them. With वृष्ट्येभिः (vṛṣṭyebhiḥ), with heroes, you overpower other enemies. You are the sole, unaided king of the whole world. Such as you, fight, and make the people dwell: slay the obstructors and settle good people in their own place, is the intention. The derivation of महिष (mahiṣa) is from mah, "to worship", with the suffix ṭiṣac (Uṇ. Sū. 1-46).

p. 85

प्रत्ययः । आमंत्रितत्वान्निघातः । वृष्ट्येभिः । वृष्टि भवानि भवे छंदसीति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तः । योधय । युध संप्रहार इत्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लोटि रूपं । चादिषु चेति न निघातः । णित्स्वरः । क्षयय । क्षिनिवासगत्योरित्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लोटि रूपं । अत्रापि पूर्ववदनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This block continues with grammatical remarks (suffix, accent) on mahiṣa, vṛṣṭyebhiḥ, yodhaya and kṣayaya.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • महिष (mahiṣa)—venerable one
  • उग्र (ugra)—fierce Indra
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • महान् असि (mahān asi)—you are of great form
  • धनस्पृत् (dhanaspṛt)—you show wealth its uses such as giving
  • वृष्ट्येभिः (vṛṣṭyebhiḥ)—by your valorous powers
  • अन्यान् (anyān)—enemies
  • सहमानः (sahamānaḥ)—you are the defeater
  • विश्वस्य (viśvasya)—of all
  • भुवनस्य (bhuvanasya)—the world
  • एकः (ekaḥ)—alone
  • राजा (rājā)—you are lord
  • सः (saḥ)—such as you
  • योधय च (yodhaya ca)—fight (our enemies and defeat them)
  • जनान् (janān)—the people who perform sacrifice
  • क्षयय चॆ (kṣayaya cè)—make them possessors of dwellings
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshipful and fearsome Indra, you are of great form. You show wealth its uses such as giving, and you defeat enemies by your valorous powers. You alone are lord of the whole world. Such as you, fight our enemies and defeat them, and give houses and other dwellings to the human sacrificers and protect them.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Adorable and powerful Indra, you are great and magnificent, over-coming adversaries by your prowess ; you alone are lord of all the world ; war (upon our enemies), and give safe dwellings to men.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

महिष (mahiṣa)—The word mahiṣa is read among the names for "great" in the Nirukta (Ni. 3-3). It means venerable, or else the accomplisher of great deeds. The Nirukta-author quotes the ṛk "अपामुपस्थे महिषा... (apāmupasthe mahiṣā...)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4) and there explains this word as "deep". The intention here is that Indra's personal power is deep. In this power there is a blending of both beauty and terror(?). NOTEFor that reason the epithet उग्र (ugra) is fitting. Hence, without giving here the meaning "sprinkler" for the word वृष्णेभिः (vṛṣṇebhiḥ), it is shown that it is used in the sense of "power": वृष्णेभिः (vṛṣṇebhiḥ) means "by powers that accomplish great deeds".

p. 86

As described in the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa, Indra, once consecrated, obtained the rank of self-rule. The description "भुवनस्य एकः राजाः (bhuvanasya ekaḥ rājāḥ)" shows the point that there is no other lord of the world than him. Or else this description also shows that there is no other illuminator of the world than Indra, who is of the nature of the sun.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

प्र मात्रा॑भी रिरिचे॒ रोच॑मानः॒ प्र दे॒वेभि॑र्वि॒श्वतो॒ ॑ अप्र॑तीतः ।
प्र म॒ज्मना॑ दि॒व इंद्रः॑ पृथि॒व्याः प्रोरोर्म॒हो अं॒तरि॑क्षादृजी॒षी ॥ ३ ॥

pra mātrābhī ririce rocamānaḥ pra devebhirviśvato
apratītaḥ |
pra majmanā diva iṃdraḥ pṛthivyāḥ prorormaho aṃtarikṣādṛjīṣī ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

प्र । मात्राभिः । रिरिचे । रोचमानः । प्र । देवेभिः । विश्वतः । अप्रतिइत ।
प्र । मज्मना । दिवः । इंद्रः । पृथिव्याः । प्र । उरोः । महः । अंतरिक्षात् । ऋजीषी॥

pra | mātrābhiḥ | ririce | rocamānaḥ | pra | devebhiḥ | viśvataḥ | apratiita |
pra | majmanā | divaḥ | iṃdraḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | pra | uroḥ | mahaḥ | aṃtarikṣāt | ṛjīṣī‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

रोचमानो दीप्यमानो विश्वतः सर्वैरप्रतीत एतावदस्य सामर्थ्यमित्यपरिच्छिद्यमान यजीषी सोमवानिंद्रो मात्राभिः । मीयंते परिच्चिद्यंत इति मात्राः शिलोच्चयाः । तेभ्योऽपि प्र रिरिचे । प्रकर्षण महत्तयातिरिक्कोऽभूत् । तथा देवेभिर्देवेभ्योऽपि मज्जना । मज्जयति शत्रोन्मुखसागर इति मज्ज बलं । तेन बलेन प्ररिरिचे । तथा दिवः पृथिव्या द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां च प्ररिरिचे । तथोरोर्विस्तीर्णान्महो महतोंतरिक्षादपि प्ररिरिचे॥ मात्राभिः माज् माने शब्द चेत्यस्मात् हुयामाश्रुभसिभ्यस्त्रन्निति त्रन्प्रत्ययः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । ढ्रलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽण इति संहितायां दीर्घः । रोचमानः । रुच दीप्तावित्यस्मात् शानचि रूपं । तस्य लसार्वधातुकस्वरे धातुस्वरः । अप्रतीतः। इण् गतौ । कर्मणि क्तः। प्रादिसमासः । नञा समासे तस्य स्वरः । मज्जना । टुमस्टो शुद्धौ । औणादिको मनिच्प्रत्ययः । झलां झश् झशीति जत्त्वं । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । पृथिव्याः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, shining, not fully known by all ("this much is his power"), the Soma-possessor, has surpassed the मात्राः (mātrāḥ). These are things that are measured and bounded, namely rock-heaps (शिलोच्चयाः (śiloccayāḥ)); he has exceeded even these, becoming greatly excessive. Likewise he has surpassed even the gods by मज्जना (majjanā), that is by strength: majja is strength, because it plunges (मज्जयति (majjayati)) into the face of the sea of enemies. By that strength he has surpassed; so too heaven and earth, and the vast, great firmament. The rest of the block gives derivations and accent notes (mātrābhiḥ, rocamānaḥ, apratītaḥ, majjanā, pṛthivyāḥ). NOTE

p. 87

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • रोचमानः (rocamānaḥ)—shining
  • विश्वतः (viśvataḥ)—by all people (by anyone)
  • अप्रतीतः (apratītaḥ)—one who cannot be measured
  • ऋजीषीः (ṛjīṣīḥ)—Soma-possessing
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • मात्राभिः (mātrābhiḥ)—than all beings
  • प्र रिरिचे (pra ririce)—has grown with greater measure
  • मज्मना (majmanā)—by power
  • देवेभिः (devebhiḥ)—than the gods
  • प्र (pra)—he is greater
  • दिवः (divaḥ)—than the heavenly world
  • पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ)—than the earth
  • प्र रिरिचे (pra ririce)—he is greater
  • उरोः (uroḥ)—than the wide
  • महः (mahaḥ)—and great
  • अंतरिक्षात् (aṃtarikṣāt)—than the firmament
  • प्र (रिरिचे) (pra (ririce))—he is exceedingly greater
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, shining, immeasurable by anyone, and Soma-possessing, has grown with greater measure than all beings. In power he is greater than the gods. He is exceedingly greater than the firmament, which is wider and greater than the earth.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The resplendent and every way unlimited Indra, drinking the spiritless Soma juice, far surpasses the elements, (far exceeds) the gods in power; he is more vast than heaven and earth, or the widespread spacious firmament.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Indra's immeasurable nature is described here. The meaning is that he is greater than all things that are bounded, that is, that come within man's measure; in other words he is not an object that comes within man's measure. मात्राभिः (mātrābhiḥ)—As explained earlier in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-38-3, here too it is explained: "मीयंते मांतीति वा मात्रा: शिलोच्चयाः (mīyaṃte māṃtīti vā mātrā: śiloccayāḥ)". It is formed from the root mā, meaning "to measure". Although it applies to all things possessing limit, here it is explained as lofty rock-heaps. When describing the nature of all the elements such as earth, the Upaniṣads use this word thus: "पृथिवी च पृथिवीमात्रा चापश्चापोमात्राच तेजश्चतेजोमात्रा च वायुश्च नायुमात्रा च आकाशश्चाकाशमात्रा ॥ (pṛthivī ca pṛthivīmātrā cāpaścāpomātrāca tejaścatejomātrā ca vāyuśca nāyumātrā ca ākāśaścākāśamātrā ‖)" (Praśne. 4-8). NOTE In the quoted sentence the word mātrā has the technical meaning tanmātra ("subtle element"). Here there is no room for a philosophical discussion; in sum, they may be called things confined to the limits of man. The intention is that Indra has grown beyond all these.

p. 88

ऋजीषी (ṛjīṣī)—This epithet is because he is accompanied by Soma. It is used chiefly in describing the nature of Indra and the Maruts. In such contexts as "अमत्रेभिर्यजीषिणिमिंद्रं (amatrebhiryajīṣiṇimiṃdraṃ)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-42-2) NOTE the word ṛjīṣa is explained as power; it is explained as "of Indra, who has obtained power that obstructs enemies". But in many contexts this epithet is well known precisely because he is accompanied by Soma. As in "अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयान् (aṇoraṇīyān mahato mahīyān)", here too Indra's greatness is described by "उरोः महः अंतरिक्षात् प्र रिरिचे (uroḥ mahaḥ aṃtarikṣāt pra ririce)". Since Indra reflects all principles such as Vāyu and Āditya, it may be said that the supreme principle described in the Upaniṣads is at times regarded in the Saṃhitā in the form of Indra. This point will be explained later in the description of the spiritual nature of Indra and the other deities.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

उ॒रुं ग॑भी॒रं ज॒नुषा॒भ्यु१॒ं॑ग्रं वि॒श्वव्य॑चसमव॒तं म॑ती॒नां ।
इंद्रं॒ सोमा॑सः प्र॒दिवि॑ सु॒तासः॑ समु॒द्रं न स्र॒वत॒ आ वि॑शंति ॥

uruṃ gabhīraṃ januṣābhyuṃgraṃ viśvavyacasamavataṃ matīnāṃ |
iṃdraṃ somāsaḥ pradivi sutāsaḥ samudraṃ na sravata ā viśaṃti ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

उरुं । गभीरं । जनुषा । अभि । उग्रं । विश्वव्यचसं । अवतं । मतीनां ।
इंद्रं । सोमासः । प्रदिवि । सुतासः । समुद्रं । न । स्रवतः । आ । विशंति ॥ ४ ॥

uruṃ | gabhīraṃ | januṣā | abhi | ugraṃ | viśvavyacasaṃ | avataṃ | matīnāṃ |
iṃdraṃ | somāsaḥ | pradivi | sutāsaḥ | samudraṃ | na | sravataḥ | ā | viśaṃti ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

उरुं महांतं आत एव गभीरं महावकाशं जनुषा जन्मना स्वभावत एवोग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं । गभीरत्वमेवोच्यते । विश्वव्यचसं विश्वव्याप्तं मतीनां स्तुतीनां स्तोत्कणां वावतं रक्षकं तादृशनिंद्रं प्रदिवि पूर्वष्टहःसु सुतासो ग्रावभिरभिषुताः सोमासः सोमा अभि आभिमुख्येना विशंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । समुद्रं न । यथा स्रवतः स्रवंत्यो नद्यः समुद्रमाविशंति तद्वत् ॥ जनुषा । जनी प्रादुर्भाव इत्यस्माज्जनेरुसिरित्युसिप्रत्ययः । विश्वव्यचसं ! व्यच वाजीकरण इत्यस्मादसुन् । व्यचेः कुटादित्वमनसीति वक्तव्यमिश्यत्रानसीति पर्युदासात् जित्वाभावः । बहुन्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदस्यांतोदात्तत्वं । अवतु । अव रक्षणादिषु । औणादिकोऽतच् प्रत्ययः । चित्वादंतोदात्तः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is उरुं (uruṃ), great, and therefore गभीरं (gabhīraṃ), of great expanse; जनुषा (januṣā), by birth, by nature, fierce, terrifying to enemies. (Only depth is meant.) He is विश्वव्यचसं (viśvavyacasaṃ), all-pervading, and the protector (अवतं (avataṃ)) of the praises, or of the praisers. To such an Indra the Somas, pressed with the stones in प्रदिवि (pradivi), the earlier days, enter from the front. The illustration: समुद्रं न (samudraṃ na), as flowing rivers enter the ocean, so they. The rest of the block gives derivations and accent notes (januṣā, viśvavyacasam, avatam).

p. 89

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • उरुं (uruṃ)—one of vast form
  • गभीरं (gabhīraṃ)—one with an unfathomable belly
  • जनुषा (januṣā)—naturally (from birth itself)
  • उग्रं (ugraṃ)—terrible to enemies
  • विश्वव्यचसं (viśvavyacasaṃ)—all-pervading
  • मतीनां (matīnāṃ)—to the praises
  • अवतं (avataṃ)—the protector
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—Indra (accusative)
  • प्रदिवि (pradivi)—on former days
  • सुतासः (sutāsaḥ)—pressed
  • सोमासः (somāsaḥ)—the Soma juices
  • स्रवतः (sravataḥ)—flowing rivers
  • समुद्रं न (samudraṃ na)—as they enter the deep sea
  • अभि (abhi)—towards Indra's belly
  • आ विशंति (ā viśaṃti)—enter, flowing
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As long-flowing rivers enter the unfathomable sea, the Soma juices pressed on former days enter Indra, who is of vast form, who has an unfathomable belly, who is naturally terrible to enemies, all-pervading, and the protector of the praises.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The Soma juices daily poured out enter into the vast and profound Indra, fierce from his birth, all-pervading, the protector of the pious (worshippers), as rivers flow into the sea.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As described in the previous Ṛk, here too Indra's all-pervasiveness is described. In such contexts सोमासः (somāsaḥ) cannot be given merely the sacrificial-procedure meaning "Soma juice"; moreover the simile स्रवतः समुद्रं न (sravataḥ samudraṃ na) conveys an extraordinary meaning in such contexts. What is Indra's belly? How does a flow of Soma run there? One must examine what common quality there is between this vast form and the form described by the epithet विश्वव्यचसं (viśvavyacasaṃ). Examining the extraordinary qualities of Indra described earlier and those to be described later, it must be decided further on whether the principle of Indra is identical with the principle of the Supreme Brahman described in the Upaniṣads and the like, or whether, as modern scholars hold, Indra is a deity subject to a lower principle.
