yaṃ | somaṃ | iṃdra | pradhivīdyāvā | garbhaṃ | na | mātā | bibhṛtaḥ | tvāyā |
taṃ | te | hinvaṃti | taṃ | ūṃ iti | te | mṛjaṃti | adhvaryavaḥ | vṛṣabha | pātavai |
ūṃ iti ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र पृथिवीद्यावा द्यावापृथिव्य त्वाया त्वत्कामनया यं सोमं बिभृतोऽंतर्धारयतः । अत्र दृष्टांतः । गर्भ० न । यथा माता गर्भ० बिभर्ति तद्वत् हे वृषभ कामानां वर्षक हे इंद्र अध्वर्यवोऽध्वरं यजमानायेच्छंतस्ते त्वदर्थ० तं सोमं हिन्वंति । प्रेरयंति । किंच ते तव पातवै पानाय तं सोमं मृजंति । शोधयंति । उ प्रसिद्धौ ॥ पृथिवीद्यावा । दिवो द्यावेति द्यावादेशः । आद्युदात्तः । नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादावपृथिवीरुद्रपूषमंथिष्यत्र पर्युदासाद्देवताद्वंद्व चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । कृतसमासस्य विपर्यासश्चांदसः । बिभृतः । डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोरित्यस्माल्लट भृञामिदित्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । अजादिप्रत्ययपरत्वाभावादत्राभ्यस्तानामादिरिति स्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरः । त्वाया । त्वामिच्छतीत्यर्थे सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । पूर्वपददकारस्याकारश्चांदसः। अ प्रत्ययादिति भावेऽप्रत्ययः । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः सवर्णदीर्घः । एकादेशस्वरः । अध्वर्यवः । अध्वरमिच्छंतः । सुपः क्यच् । कव्यध्वरपृतनस्यर्चि लोप इत्याकारलोपः । क्याच्छंदसीत्युप्रत्ययः। प्रत्ययस्वरः । पातवै । पा पाने। तुमर्थे तवैप्रत्ययः । अंतश्च तवै युगपदिति धात्वंतस्य प्रत्ययस्य चोदात्तत्वं । उञ् इति प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, the Heaven and Earth, out of desire for you (त्वाया (tvāyā), "wishing you"), hold within themselves the Soma." Here is the example: गर्भ० न (garbha0 na)—as a mother carries the embryo. "O Indra, showerer (वृषभ (vṛṣabha)) of desires, the Adhvaryus, desiring the sacrifice for the sacrificer, impel (हिन्वंति (hinvaṃti), "send forth") that Soma for you. Moreover they purify (मृजंति (mṛjaṃti)) that Soma for your drinking (पातवै (pātavai))." उ (u) is a particle of well-known (emphatic) sense.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • माता (mātā)—the mother
  • गर्भं न (garbhaṃ na)—as she carefully protects and bears her child in the womb with affection
  • पृथिवीद्यावा (pṛthivīdyāvā)—Heaven and Earth both
  • त्वाया (tvāyā)—with reference to you
  • यं सोमं (yaṃ somaṃ)—which Soma
  • बिभृतः (bibhṛtaḥ)—they hold
  • तं (taṃ)—that same Soma
  • वृषभ (vṛṣabha)—O Indra, showerer of desires
  • अध्वरवः (adhvaravaḥ)—the Adhvaryus NOTE
  • ते (te)—for you
  • हिन्वंति (hinvaṃti)—press and hold
  • ते (te)—your
  • पातनै (pātanai)—for drinking NOTE
  • तं (taṃ)—that Soma
  • मृजंति (mṛjaṃti)—they purify

p. 91

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, showerer of desires, as a mother carefully protects and bears her child in her womb, so Heaven and Earth both hold for you the Soma; in the same way the Adhvaryus hold Soma for you. For your drinking they purify that same Soma.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Which Soma, Indra, the heaven and earth contain for you, as a mother contains the embryo; showerer (of benefits), the priests pour it out for you they purify it for your drinking.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As indicated in the previous Ṛk, it is understood that here too the word सोम (soma) must have a special meaning. As described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (11-5-9-10-11), it can be understood as a special radiance that gives beauty to creative power; or it may be a special essence that is the cause of that radiance. The god Soma is also of the form of Āditya, lord of radiance (Śa. Brā. 11-5-9). In the contexts where it is said that Soma is offered to Soma himself, the same kind of special meaning must be given. There is a hidden meaning in the statement that Heaven and Earth hold Soma for the increase of Indra: just as Heaven and Earth, fundamental to the world's functioning, are the cause of the increase of Indra's radiance, so the Adhvaryus too are the cause. This purport is stated on the basis of the above-cited passage of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.

Sūkta 47 (Maṇḍala 3)

The forty-seventh sūkta.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

मरुत्वानिति पंचर्चं नवमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । मरुत्वानित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ दशरात्रे चतुर्थेऽहनि मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं निविद्धानीयं । सूत्रितं च । श्रुधी हवमिंद्र मरुत्वा इंद्रेति मरुत्वतीयं । आ. ७-११ । इति ॥ ऋषभनाम्न्यकाहेऽपि मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र एतन्निविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । मरुत्वा इंद्र युध्मस्य त इति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-७ । इति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning मरुत्वान् (marutvān) has five Ṛks; it is the ninth sūkta (of the anuvāka), by Viśvāmitra, in the Triṣṭubh metre, addressed to Indra; the Anukramaṇikā says "मरुत्वान् (marutvān)". In the Daśarātra, on the fourth day, this sūkta is used at the Marutvatīya śastra as the one carrying the nivid. The sūtra says: श्रुधी हवमिंद्र मरुत्वा इंद्रेति मरुत्वतीयं (śrudhī havamiṃdra marutvā iṃdreti marutvatīyaṃ) (Ā. 7-11). In the one-day rite named Ṛṣabha also, this is the nivid-bearing sūkta at the Marutvatīya śastra; the sūtra says: मरुत्वा इंद्र युध्मस्य त इति मध्यंदिनः (marutvā iṃdra yudhmasya ta iti madhyaṃdinaḥ) (Ā. 9-7).

p. 92

अनुवादवु— मरुत्वान् ऎंब ई सूक्तवु नाल्कनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि ऒंभत्तनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि ऐदु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ विश्वामित्रनु ऋषियु, इंद्रनु देवतॆयु, त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि मरुत्वान् ऎंदु मॊदलागि हेळिरुवुदु दशरात्रवॆंब यागद नाल्कनॆय दिवस मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रमंत्रपठनकालदल्लि ई सूक्तवन्नु निविन्मंत्रगळिगागि उपयोगि सबेकॆंदु अश्वलायनशौतसूत्रद—श्रुधी हवमिंद्र मरुत्वा इंद्रेति मरुत्वतीयं ऎंब सूत्रदिंदलू (आ. ७-११), ऒंदु दिवसमात्र माडल्पडुव ऋषभनाम्मियॆंब यागदल्लि मरु त्वतीयशस्त्रमंत्रगळन्नु पठिसुवाग निविन्मंत्रगळिगागि ई सूक्तद विनियोगविरुवुदॆंदु आश्वलायन शौतसूत्रद—मरुत्वा इंद्र युध्मस्य त इति मध्यंदिनः ऎंब सूत्रदिंदलू (आ. ९-७) विवृतवागिरुवुदु. ॥ ओं ॥ सूक्त—४७ मंडल—३ ॥ अनुवाक—४ ॥ सूक्त—४७ ॥ अष्टक—३ ॥ अध्याय—३ ॥ वर्ग—११ ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—५ ॥ , ऋषिः— विश्वामित्रः । देवता— इंद्रः । । छंदः — त्रिष्टुप् ।

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning "Marutvān" is the ninth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka and has five Ṛks. Viśvāmitra is its seer, Indra the deity, Triṣṭubh the metre. The Anukramaṇikā begins with "Marutvān". It is to be used for the nivid mantras at the time of reciting the Marutvatīya śastra mantras on the fourth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, as stated by the Āśvalāyana-Śrautasūtra "श्रुधी हवमिंद्र मरुत्वा इंद्रेति मरुत्वतीयं (śrudhī havamiṃdra marutvā iṃdreti marutvatīyaṃ)" (Ā. 7-11); and in the sacrifice called Ṛṣabhanāmnī, performed in a single day, the use of this sūkta for the nivid mantras while reciting the Marutvatīya śastra mantras is explained by the Āśvalāyana-Śrautasūtra "मरुत्वा इंद्र युध्मस्य त इति मध्यंदिनः (marutvā iṃdra yudhmasya ta iti madhyaṃdinaḥ)" (Ā. 9-7). Particulars: Sūkta 47; Maṇḍala 3, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 47; Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 3, Varga 11; number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5; Ṛṣi: Viśvāmitra; Devatā: Indra; Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

म॒रुत्वा॑ इंद्र वृष॒भो रणा॑य॒ सिबा॒ सोम॑नुस्व॒धं ॑ मदा॑य ।
आ सिं॑चस्व ज॒ठरे॒ मध्व॑ ऊ॒र्मिं त्वं राजा॑सि प्र॒दिवः॑ सु॒तानां॑॥

marutvā iṃdra vṛṣabho raṇāya sibā somanusvadhaṃ
madāya |
ā siṃcasva jaṭhare madhva ūrmiṃ tvaṃ rājāsi pradivaḥ sutānāṃ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

मरुत्वान् । इंद्र । वृषभः । रणाय । पिज । सोमं । अनुस्वधं । मदाय ।
आ । सिंचस्व । जठरे । मध्वः । उर्मिं । त्वं । राजा । असि । प्रदिवः । सुतानां ॥ १ ॥

marutvān | iṃdra | vṛṣabhaḥ | raṇāya | pija | somaṃ | anusvadhaṃ | madāya |
ā | siṃcasva | jaṭhare | madhvaḥ | urmiṃ | tvaṃ | rājā | asi | pradivaḥ | sutānāṃ ‖ 1 ‖

p. 93

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र यो वृषभोऽपां वर्षिता मरुत्वान् । मरुतो देवविशस्तद्वान् । स त्वमनुष्वधं स्वधया सवनीयपुरोडाशादिरूपेणान्नेनानुगतं सोमं रणाय रमणीयसंग्रामार्थं मदाय तं सोमं पिब । किंच मध्यो मदकॆरस्य सोमस्त्योर्मि संघातं बहुरसं जठरे । जग्धमन्नमस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति जठरमुदरं । तस्मिन्नुदर आ सिंचस्व । सर्वतः क्षारय । यतस्त्वं प्रदिवः पूर्वेष्वहःसु सुतानामभिषुतानां सोमानां राजासीशितासि । न केवलमधुनातनानामिति भावः । उक्तमर्थं यास्को ब्रवीति । मरुत्वानिंद मरुद्भिस्तद्वान् वृषभो वर्षितापां रणाय रमणीयाय संग्रामाय पिब सोममनुष्वधमन्वन्नं मदाय मदनीयाय जैत्रायासिंच स्वजठरे मधुन ऊर्मि० । मधु सोममित्यौपमिकं माद्यतेरिदमपीतरन्मध्वतस्मादेव । त्वं राजासि पूर्वेष्वस्यहःसु सुतानां । नि. ४-८ । इति ॥ अनुस्वधं । स्वधामनुगम्य वर्तमानं । अत्यादयः क्रांताद्यर्थे द्वितीययेति समासः । संहितायां पूर्वपदात् । पा. ८-३-१०६ । इति षत्वं । निरुदकादित्वादंतोदात्तत्वं । ऊर्मि० । अर्तॆरुच्चेति मिप्रत्ययः धातोरू इत्यादेशो रपरः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, you who are the showerer (वृषभ (vṛṣabha)) of waters and मरुत्वान् (marutvān)—possessed of the Maruts, the divine clan—drink that Soma, which is accompanied (अनुस्वधं (anusvadhaṃ)) by स्वधा (svadhā), that is, by food in the form of the puroḍāśa and the like of the pressing, for the delightful (रणाय (raṇāya)) battle and for exhilaration (मदाय (madāya)). Moreover, pour the wave (ऊर्मिं (ūrmiṃ), the collected mass, abundant juice) of the intoxicating sweet Soma into your belly (जठरे (jaṭhare); the belly is so called because the food eaten stays in it); pour it in all around. For you are the lord of the Somas pressed on former days (प्रदिवः (pradivaḥ))—not only of the present ones." Yāska states the same meaning: मरुत्वानिंद मरुद्भिस्तद्वान् वृषभो वर्षितापां रणाय रमणीयाय संग्रामाय पिब सोममनुष्वधमन्वन्नं मदाय मदनीयाय जैत्रायासिंच स्वजठरे मधुन ऊर्मि० । मधु सोममित्यौपमिकं माद्यतेरिदमपीतरन्मध्वतस्मादेव । त्वं राजासि पूर्वेष्वस्यहःसु सुतानां । (marutvāniṃda marudbhistadvān vṛṣabho varṣitāpāṃ raṇāya ramaṇīyāya saṃgrāmāya piba somamanuṣvadhamanvannaṃ madāya madanīyāya jaitrāyāsiṃca svajaṭhare madhuna ūrmi0 | madhu somamityaupamikaṃ mādyateridamapītaranmadhvatasmādeva | tvaṃ rājāsi pūrveṣvasyahaḥsu sutānāṃ |) (Ni. 4-8).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ)—you who pour down rain
  • मरुत्वान् (marutvān)—who are accompanied by the Maruts
  • अनुष्वधं (anuṣvadhaṃ)—accompanied by food in the form of svadhā
  • सोमं (somaṃ)—the Soma
  • रणाय (raṇāya)—in battle
  • मदाय (madāya)—for increasing your valour
  • पिब (piba)—drink
  • मध्वः (madhvaḥ)—of the intoxicating Soma
  • ऊर्मि (ūrmi)—the essence in the form of a wave
  • जठरे (jaṭhare)—in your belly
  • आ सिंचस्व (ā siṃcasva)—pour fully
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • प्रदिवः (pradivaḥ)—on former days
  • सुतानां (sutānāṃ)—of all the pressed Somas
  • राजा (rājā)—as lord
  • असि (asi)—you are
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who pour down rain and are accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma accompanied by food in the form of svadhā, in battle, to increase your valour. Pour fully into your belly the Soma essence, which is intoxicating and in the form of a wave. You are the lord of all the Somas pressed on former days.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra, attended by the Maruts, the showerer (of benefits), drink the Soma offered after the other presentations, for your exhilaration for battle ; take into your belly the (full) wave of the inebriating (Soma), for you are lord of libations from the days of old.

p. 94

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अनुष्पधं (anuṣpadhaṃ)—two words, अनु (anu) + स्वधा (svadhā), are joined: drinking of Soma after the offering of food in the form of svadhā. The scholar Monier Williams, giving the meaning of the word अनुष्पधं (anuṣpadhaṃ), says "According one's own will ; voluntary ;" that is, acting by one's own impulse without the prompting of others, and he refers to the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā; but nowhere in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā has Sāyaṇa given this meaning. ऊर्मि (ūrmi)—ऊर्मिरूर्णोतेः (ūrmirūrṇoteḥ): it is the view of the Nirukta author that it is derived from the root ऊर्ण (ūrṇa), meaning to cover, conceal, envelop (Ni. 5-23). (The Uṇādi sūtra आर्तॆरच्च (ārtèracca) is recited.) Just as it is used in the sense of wave (billow), the word is also used in the sense of mass of water, collection of water. Here it indicates the abundance of the Soma juice. रणाय (raṇāya)—On the basis of the original meaning "delightful", the word रण (raṇa) is a synonym of battle. When the gods gather together and fight, there is a joyful cry that victory is assured; so (रणयंति (raṇayaṃti)) the word indicates that the battlefield too is delightful.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒जोषा॑ इंद्र॒ सग॑णो म॒रुद्भिः॒ सोमं॑ पिब वृतह्र॒ा शू॑र ॒ विद्वान् ।
ज॒हि शत्रू॒रप॒ मृधो॑ नुद॒स्वाथाभ॑यं कृणुहि वि॒श्वतो॑ नः

sajoṣā iṃdra sagaṇo marudbhiḥ somaṃ piba vṛtahrā śūra
vidvān |
jahi śatrūrapa mṛdho nudasvāthābhayaṃ kṛṇuhi viśvato naḥ

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सजोषाः । इंद्र । सगणः । मरुत्भिः । सोमं । पिब । वृत्रहा । शूर । विद्वान् ।
जहि । शत्रून् । अप । मृधः । नुदस्व । अथ । अभयं । कृणुहि । विश्वतः । नः । ॥ २ ॥

sajoṣāḥ | iṃdra | sagaṇaḥ | marutbhiḥ | somaṃ | piba | vṛtrahā | śūra | vidvān |
jahi | śatrūn | apa | mṛdhaḥ | nudasva | atha | abhayaṃ | kṛṇuhi | viśvataḥ | naḥ | ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सजोषा इंद्रेति मरुत्वतीयग्रहस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । सजोषा इंद्र सगणो मरुद्भिरिति भक्षयित्वैतत्पात्रं । आ. ५-१४ । इति ॥ हे शूर बलवन् हे इंद्र सजोषाः संगतो देवैर्मरुद्भिः सगणो मरुद्भिरेव वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य हंता विद्वान्कर्मविषयाभिज्ञस्त्वं सोमं पिब । ततो नः

Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse सजोषा इंद्र (sajoṣā iṃdra) is the yājyā of the Marutvatīya graha. The sūtra says: सजोषा इंद्र सगणो मरुद्भिरिति भक्षयित्वैतत्पात्रं (sajoṣā iṃdra sagaṇo marudbhiriti bhakṣayitvaitatpātraṃ) (Ā. 5-14). "O mighty hero (शूर (śūra)) Indra, you who are united (सजोषाः (sajoṣāḥ)) with the gods the Maruts, accompanied by your troop (सगणः (sagaṇaḥ)) by the Maruts alone, the slayer of Vṛtra, knowing (विद्वान् (vidvān)) the subject of the rites—drink the Soma. Then for us …" (the block breaks off here; the next window continues).

p. 95

Ṛk 2 (continued)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

शत्रून् जहि । मृधो हिंसकान् शत्रूनप नुदस्व । यद्वा मृधः। हिंस्यंतेऽत्र प्राणिन इति मृधः संग्रामाः । तत्र वर्तमानान् शत्रूनसनुदस्व । अथानंतरं नोऽस्माकं विश्वतः सर्वतोऽभयं कृणुहि । कुरु । सर्वतो भयरहितानस्मान्कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥ वृत्रहा । हंतेब्रह्मभ्रूणवृत्तेषु क्विप् । अभयं । इंभी भय इत्यस्मादेरच् । नञा समासे तस्य स्वरः । विश्वतः । पंचम्यास्तसिल् । लित्स्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues: "Slay the enemies. मृधः (mṛdhaḥ) are harmful enemies; drive them away." Or else मृधः (mṛdhaḥ) means battles, because living beings are injured in them ("they are harmed here"); drive away the enemies who stand in those battles. Then, afterwards, make us fearless on every side. The meaning is "make us free from fear everywhere."

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • शूर (śūra)—valorous
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ)—with the Maruts
  • सगणः (sagaṇaḥ)—united (with them)
  • सजोषाः (sajoṣāḥ)—having equal affection (for them)
  • वृत्रहा (vṛtrahā)—slayer of Vṛtra
  • विद्वान् (vidvān)—wise; you who are such
  • सोमं (somaṃ)—the Soma juice
  • पिब (piba)—drink
  • शत्र्यन् (śatryan)—our enemies
  • जहि (jahi)—defeat
  • मृधः (mṛdhaḥ)—the enemies in battle
  • आप नुदस्व (āpa nudasva)—destroy
  • अथ (atha)—afterwards
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • विश्वतः (viśvataḥ)—from all sides
  • अभयं (abhayaṃ)—freedom from fear
  • कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi)—bring about
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valorous Indra, you who are united with the Maruts, who have equal affection for them, who are the slayer of Vṛtra and are wise, drink the Soma juice. Defeat our enemies. Destroy the enemies who are intent on battle, and afterwards make us free from fear on every side.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra, hero, rejoicing with and accompanied by the host of Maruts, drink the Soma, for you are the slayer of Vritra, the sage; subdue our enemies, drive away the malevolent, make us safe on every side from peril.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk beginning सजोषा इंद्र (sajoṣā iṃdra) is to be used as the yājyā mantra for the Marutvatīya graha is explained by the Āśvalāyana sūtra सजोषा इंद्र सगणो मरुद्भिरिति भक्षयॆत्वैतत्पात्रं (sajoṣā iṃdra sagaṇo marudbhiriti bhakṣayètvaitatpātraṃ) (Ā. 5-14).

मृधः (mṛdhaḥ)—The word मृध (mṛdha) is read among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Its use is mostly in the sense of war. But in some contexts it is also understood as the enemy who is the cause of war. The Nirukta-kāra cites the Ṛk वि न इंद्र मृधो जहि नीचा यच्छ पृतन्यतः । (vi na iṃdra mṛdho jahi nīcā yaccha pṛtanyataḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-152-5)

p. 96

and shows that there it has the meaning "enemies who wage war" (Ni. 7-2). In the present Ṛk too the word stands as a synonym of "enemy".

उ॒त ऋ॒तुभि॑र्ऋतुपाः पाहि॒ सोम॒मिंद्र॑ दे॒वेभिः॒ सखि॑भिः ॒ ॑ सुतं नः ।
या अभ॑जो म॒रुतो॒ ये त्वान्वह॑न्वृ॒त्रमद॑धु॒स्तुभ्य॒मोजः॑॥

उत । ऋतुभिः । ऋतुपाः । पाहि । सोमं । इंद्र । देवेभिः । सखिभिः । सुतं ।

naḥ |

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

उत अपि च हे ऋतुपाः कालनिर्वाहकतया ऋतूनां पातः । ऋतुषु सोमं पिबतीति वा ऋतुपाः । यद्वा ऋतुभिर्मरुद्भिः सह सोमं पिबतीति ऋतुपाः । तादृश हे इंद्र सखिभिः समानख्यानैर्यतुभिर्मरुद्भिर्देवेभिर्देवैः सहितस्त्वं नः संबंधिनं सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पाहि । पिब । किंच यान्मरुत आभजो युद्धसहायार्थमसेवथा ये च मरुतस्त्वा त्वां युद्धे स्वामिनमन्वभजंत । ततस्त्वं वृत्रमहन् । हतवानसि । ते मरुतस्तुभ्यं त्वदर्थमोजो युद्धे शत्रुहननादिरूपं पराक्रममदधुः । अकुर्वन् ॥ अभजः । भज सेवायामित्यस्य लजि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । अहन् । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य लजि सिपो हल्ड्या दिना लोपः । पादादित्पादनिघातः । अदधुः । दधातेर्लजि झेः सिजभ्यस्तेति जुस् । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Moreover, O Ṛtupā": he who protects the seasons by regulating time; or he who drinks Soma in the seasons; or else he who drinks Soma together with the Ṛtus, that is, the Maruts. Such an Indra, being accompanied by his friends, the Maruts, who bear the same name as the Ṛtus, and by the gods, is to drink our pressed Soma. Further: the Maruts whom you resorted to for help in battle, and the Maruts who resorted to you as their lord in battle: thereupon you slew Vṛtra. Those Maruts placed in you ओजः (ojaḥ), vigour that takes the form of slaying enemies in battle; they produced it for you.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

  • ऋतुसाः (ṛtusāḥ)—one who drinks Soma together with the Maruts (or: one who drinks Soma at the fixed times)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • सखिभिः (sakhibhiḥ)—your friends

p. 97

  • ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ)—with the Maruts
  • देवेभिः (devebhiḥ)—and with the gods; you who are united with them
  • नः (naḥ)—by us
  • सुतं (sutaṃ)—pressed
  • सोमं (somaṃ)—the Soma
  • पाहि (pāhi)—drink
  • यान् (yān)—which Maruts
  • आभजः (ābhajaḥ)—you have served
  • ये (ye)—which Maruts
  • त्वा (tvā)—you
  • अनु (anu)—served (and for that very reason)
  • वृत्रं (vṛtraṃ)—Vṛtra
  • अहन् (ahan)—you have slain (those same Maruts)
  • तुभ्यं (tubhyaṃ)—to you
  • ओजः (ojaḥ)—the strength that destroys enemies
  • आदधुः (ādadhuḥ)—produced
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who drink Soma according to the regulation of time, together with your friends the Maruts and with the gods, drink the Soma pressed by us. Because you served the Maruts, and because the Maruts served you, you became able to slay Vṛtra; those same Maruts produced in you the strength that destroys enemies.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Drinker of the Soma in season, drink with your divine friends the Maruts, the Soma that is presented by us; those Maruts whose aid you have enjoyed (in battle), and who, following you, have given you the strength whereby you have slain Vritra.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The words ऋतुपाः (ṛtupāḥ) and ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ) must be explained according to the context. For the word ऋतु (ṛtu) the meaning "fixed state" or "regulation of time" is current. From the offering of oblations duly, in accordance with such a fixed ṛtu-dharma, the word ऋत्विक् (ṛtvik) is formed. Or, according to some, the word ऋतु (ṛtu) means a vessel in which oblations are offered. As indicated in "को अग्निमाट्टे हविषा धृतेन सुचा यजाता ऋतुभिर्घ्रवेभिः (ko agnimāṭṭe haviṣā dhṛtena sucā yajātā ṛtubhirghravebhiḥ)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-18), सुक् (suk), ऋतु (ṛtu) and ध्रुव (dhruva) are all three vessels for offering oblations. In places such as इंद्र सोमं पिब ऋतुना (iṃdra somaṃ piba ṛtunā) (1-15-1) and मरुतः पिब ऋतुना (marutaḥ piba ṛtunā) (1-15-2), one view is that the word ऋतु (ṛtu) means a vessel. But Sāyaṇa has explained ऋतु (ṛtu) in these contexts as the deity Ṛtu, and the Saṃhitā too shows the meaning "deity". Even in the Ṛk 1-84-18 cited above Sāyaṇa has not taken it to mean a vessel; he has given it as the seasons beginning with spring.

If the word ऋतु (ṛtu) is a synonym of "deity", then ऋत्विक् (ṛtvik) means a worshipper of the deity. In the present Ṛk, ऋतुपाः (ṛtupāḥ) can be explained as the Indra who drinks Soma in the seasons,

p. 98

and ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ) as the Indra who is united with the deities named Ṛtu. Sāyaṇa has explained them as the Marut deities. When one says ऋतुभिः देवेभिः (ṛtubhiḥ devebhiḥ), if ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ) is made an adjective of देवेभिः (devebhiḥ), it can also mean "with the deities named Ṛtu".

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रे याज्या ये त्वाहिहत्य इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्निति याज्या । आ. ५-१४ । इति ॥ हे मघवन्निंद्र ये मरुतोऽहिहत्ये वृत्रहननरूपे कर्मणि त्वा त्वामवर्धन् प्रहर भगवो जहि वीरयस्वेति बलदानेनावीवृधन् । हे हरिवोऽश्ववन्निंद्र ये च शांबरे शंबरवधसंबंधिनि युद्धे त्वामवीवृधन् । इंद्रः शंबरमवधीदित्यस्मिन्नर्थे मंत्रवर्णः । यः शंबरं पर्वतेषु क्षियंतं चत्वारिंश्यां शरद्यन्वविंदत् । ओजायमानं यो अहिं जघान । ऋग्वे २-१२-११ । इति । तथा ये मरुतो गविष्टौ पणिनामकैरसुरैः सह गवार्थे युद्धे च त्वामवीवृधन् । विप्रा

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Ṛk ये त्वाहिहत्ये (ye tvāhihatye) is the yājyā in the Marutvatīya śastra. It is prescribed by the sūtra ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्निति याज्या (ye tvāhihatye maghavannavardhanniti yājyā) (Ā. 5-14). O Maghavan Indra, the Maruts who in the work of slaying Ahi (Vṛtra) strengthened you by giving you strength, with words such as "strike, blessed one, slay, show your valour"; and, O Harivān (possessor of horses) Indra, those who strengthened you in the battle connected with the slaying of Śambara. That Indra slew Śambara is stated by a mantra passage: यः शंबरं पर्वतेषु क्षियंतं चत्वारिंश्यां शरद्यन्वविंदत् । ओजायमानं यो अहिं जघान । (yaḥ śaṃbaraṃ parvateṣu kṣiyaṃtaṃ catvāriṃśyāṃ śaradyanvaviṃdat | ojāyamānaṃ yo ahiṃ jaghāna |) (Ṛgve. 2-12-11)NOTE. Likewise the Maruts who strengthened you in the battle for cattle, गविष्टौ (gaviṣṭau), against the asuras named Paṇis; and the wise

p. 99

Maruts who now delight you: together with such Maruts, in company, drink this Soma.

मेधाविनो ये च मरुतो नूनमिदानीं त्वामनुमदंति मादयंति तादृशैस्त्यर्मरुद्धिः सगणः सन् इमं सोमं पिब ॥ अहिहत्ये । हंतेर्भावे हनस्त चेति क्यप् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । अवर्धन् । वृधु वृद्धावित्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लजि रूपं । छंदस्युभयथेति झीरार्धधातुकत्वाणेर्लोपः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । शांबरे । शंबरस्येदमित्यर्थे तस्येदमित्यण्प्रत्ययः । गविष्टौ । इषु इच्छायां । भावे क्तिन् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । अनुमदंति । मदि स्तुत्यादिश्वित्यस्य लटि व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । आगमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वान्नुमभावः । झीर्लसार्वधातुकस्वरे कृते धातुस्वरः । तिजं चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Gist for the portion of this block that stands in this window is given in the preceding paragraph, which completes the sentence ("the wise Maruts who now delight you … drink this Soma"); the remainder of the block is grammatical.

  • हरिवः (harivaḥ)—possessor of horses
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • ये (ye)—which Maruts
  • अहिहत्ये (ahihatye)—in the work consisting of the slaying of Vṛtra
  • त्वा (tvā)—you
  • अवर्धन् (avardhan)—made to grow
  • ये (ye)—which Maruts
  • शांबरे (śāṃbare)—in the battle fought with Śambara, gave strength
  • ये (ye)—which Maruts
  • गविष्टौ (gaviṣṭau)—helped in the recovery of the stolen cattle (and)
  • विप्राः (viprāḥ)—wise

  • नूनं (nūnaṃ)—now
  • अनुमदंति (anumadaṃti)—are gratifying to you
  • मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ)—with (such) Maruts
  • सगणः (sagaṇaḥ)—united together
  • सोमं (somaṃ)—this Soma
  • पिब (piba)—drink
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wealthy and possessed of horses, the Maruts who strengthened you in the work of slaying Vṛtra, who gave you strength in the battle fought with Śambara, who helped you in the recovery of the stolen cattle, and who, being wise, are now gratifying to you: united with such Maruts, drink this Soma.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

They who encouraged you Maghavan, to slay Ahi, who (aided you) in the conflict with Shambara, and in the recovery of the cattle, and who, possessed of wisdom, contribute verily to your exhilaration, with them, the troop of the Maruts, Indra, drink the Soma.

p. 100

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk beginning ये त्वाहिहत्ये (ye tvāhihatye) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the time of reciting the Marutvatīya śastra is explained by the sūktaNOTE of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्धन्निति याज्या (ye tvāhihatye maghavannavardhanniti yājyā) (Ā. 5-14).

The friendship between Indra and the Maruts, and the nature of the help that the Maruts gave Indra in many situations, have been explained fully before. Of these, three situations are indicated here.

The name of Śambara is usually joined with the asuras Śuṣṇa, Pipru and Varcin. In some Ṛks he is called a dāsa (6-26-5). It is said that for King Divodāsa, a close friend of Indra, Indra overthrew all the countless forts of the enemy Śambara and gave Divodāsa his property. These matters too have been told before. It is also said that this asura hid himself in the hills and mountains and caused great harm to Atithigva and Divodāsa, and so Indra destroyed him and gave both of them his protection. Like Ahi and Vṛtra, Śambara too can be said to be a person who represents a dense darkness.

"Sambara, meaning among other things the cloud, seems to be some mythical beings connected with the powers of darkness". Oldenberg.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

म॒रुत्वं॑तं वृष॒भं ना॑वृधा॒नमक॑वारिं दि॒व्यं शा॒समिंद्रं॑ ।
वि॒श्वा॒साह॒मव॑से॒ नूत॑नायो॒ग्रं स॑हो॒दामि॒ह तं हु॑वेम ॥

marutvaṃtaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ nāvṛdhānamakavāriṃ divyaṃ śāsamiṃdraṃ |
viśvāsāhamavase nūtanāyograṃ sahodāmiha taṃ huvema ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

मरुत्वंतं । वृषभं । ववृधानं । अकवअरिं । दिव्यं । शासं । इंद्रं ।
विश्वसहं । अवसे । नूतनाय । उग्रं । सहःदां । इह । तं । हुवेम ॥ ५ ॥

marutvaṃtaṃ | vṛṣabhaṃ | vavṛdhānaṃ | akavaariṃ | divyaṃ | śāsaṃ | iṃdraṃ |
viśvasahaṃ | avase | nūtanāya | ugraṃ | sahaḥdāṃ | iha | taṃ | huvema ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र मरुत्वंतं मरुद्भिस्तद्वंतं वृषभं मेघभेदनद्वारापांं वर्षक ववृधानं वृत्रहननादिकर्मसूत्साहेन वर्धमानमकवारिं प्रभूतशत्रु कं यद्वा

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, मरुत्वंतं (marutvaṃtaṃ)", accompanied by the Maruts; वृषभं (vṛṣabhaṃ), the rainer of waters by splitting the cloud; ववृधानं (vavṛdhānaṃ), growing through zeal in works such as the slaying of Vṛtra; akavāri, one who has many enemiesNOTE; "or else" — the block breaks off here and the next window continues it.

p. 101

अकुत्सि तारिं । तथा च मंत्रः । स्वरिरमत्तो ववक्षे रणाय । ऋग्वे. १-६१-९ । इति । दिव्यं दिवि स्वर्गलोके वर्तमानं शासं हितोपदेशाहितपरिहाराभ्यां शासितारं विश्वासाहं विश्वस्य प्रतिपक्षस्य सर्वस्याभिभवितारमुग्रं शत्रुषूद्रूर्णं सहोदां युद्धसहकारिणां मरुतां बलप्रदं तं तादृशसामर्थ्यपेतमिंद्रं नूतनाय नवतरायावसे रक्षणायेह कर्मणि हुवेम । त्वामाह्वयेम ॥ नूतनाय । नवतरायावतसे रक्षणायेह कर्मणि हुवेम । त्वामाह्वयेम ॥ नूतनाय । नवशब्दस्य नू इत्यादेशः । त्वप्तनखःश्च प्रत्यया वक्तव्या इति तनप्रत्ययः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The block opens by completing the explanation of अकवारिं (akavāriṃ) begun on the previous page.NOTE A mantra is cited in support: स्वरिरमत्तो ववक्षे रणाय (svariramatto vavakṣe raṇāya) (Ṛgve. 1-61-9).NOTE Then he glosses the remaining words. दिव्यं (divyaṃ): dwelling in heaven. शासं (śāsaṃ): the ruler who governs by beneficial instruction and by warding off harm. विश्वासाहं (viśvāsāhaṃ): the overcomer of every adversary. उग्रं (ugraṃ): formidable against enemies. सहोदां (sahodāṃ): the giver of strength to the Maruts, his allies in battle. Indra, so endowed, we call to this rite for new, that is, fresher protection (नूतनाय (nūtanāya), अवसे (avase), हुवेम (huvema): "we invoke you"). The rest of the block is grammar on नूतनाय (nūtanāya).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मरुत्वंतं (marutvaṃtaṃ)—one accompanied by the Maruts
  • वृषभं (vṛṣabhaṃ)—one who sends down rain
  • ववृधानं (vavṛdhānaṃ)—one who grows (with zeal)
  • अकवारिं (akavāriṃ)—one who has abundant enemies
  • दिव्यं (divyaṃ)—one who dwells in the world of the gods
  • शासं (śāsaṃ)—the instructor
  • विश्वासाहं (viśvāsāhaṃ)—one who defeats all enemies
  • उग्रं (ugraṃ)—the terrible one
  • सहोदां (sahodāṃ)—the giver of strength to the Maruts, his companions
  • तं इंद्रं (taṃ iṃdraṃ)—that Indra
  • नूतनाय (nūtanāya)—new
  • अवसे (avase)—for protection
  • इह (iha)—in this sacrificial rite
  • हुवेम (huvema)—we call with prayer
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts, sends down rain, grows with zeal, has abundant enemies, dwells in the world of the gods, is the instructor, defeats all enemies, is terrible, and gives strength to his companions the Maruts: him we call with prayer in this sacrificial rite for fresh protection.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

We inovke to this sacrifice for present protection Indra, the chief of the Maruts, the showerer (of benefits) ; augmenting (in glory), overcoming many foes, divine regulator (of good and ill), the subduer of all (enemies), the fierce the bestower of strength.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Akavārim: this word has been explained as "one with abundant enemies". The word kava is formed from the root ku, which gives the sense "contemptible"; kava therefore means what is small, despised, blameworthy. From this root both forms, kava and kavāri, are formed.

p. 102

The word kuvāriNOTE in general means a man who is extremely selfish, miserly, performs no sacrifice and leads a contemptible life. In the present ṛk, where akavārim stands, the word kava means a small, despised person, and the compound is kava-ari: a petty enemy. One who is not a kavāri is an akavāri, that is, an enemy of great power; or an abundant number may also be indicated by it. It is an epithet showing Indra's greatness: one who can face such enemies.

Sūkta 48 (Maṇḍala 3)

सद्यो हेति पंचर्चं दशमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । सद्यो हेत्यनुक्रमणिका । अग्निष्टोमे माध्यंदिनसवने मैत्रावरुणशस्त्रे सद्यो ह जात इत्येतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । सद्योह जात एवा त्वामिंद्र । आ. ५. १६ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽप्यहनि मैत्रावरुणशस्त्रेऽहरहः शस्यसंज्ञमेतत्तूक्तं॥ सूत्रितं च । सद्यो ह जात इत्यहरहःशस्यं मैत्रावरुणः । आ. ७ ४ । इति ॥ अहर्गणे द्वितीयादिष्वहःसु माध्यंदिनसवनेऽस्मिन् शस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । अहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव । आ. ७. १ । इति सूत्रितं ॥ साद्यस्क्र एकाहे मरुत्वतीये शस्त्रे सद्यो ह जात इत्याद्या सूक्तमुखीया । सूत्रितं च । सद्यो ह जातो वृषभः कनीनस्त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्र । आ. ९. ५ । इति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the tenth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, सद्यो ह (sadyo ha), of five ṛks; the seer is Viśvāmitra, the deity Indra, the metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā begins सद्यो ह (sadyo ha). Uses: in the Agniṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, this sūkta (सद्यो ह जात (sadyo ha jāta)) belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, and the sūtra says सद्यो ह जात एवा त्वामिंद्र (sadyo ha jāta evā tvāmiṃdra) (Ā. Sū. 5.16).NOTE On the Cāturviṃśika day, in the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, this sūkta is the one called ahar-ahaḥ-śasya; the sūtra says सद्यो ह जात इत्यहरहःशस्यं मैत्रावरुणः (sadyo ha jāta ityaharahaḥśasyaṃ maitrāvaruṇaḥ) (Ā. Sū. 7.4). In an ahargaṇa, from the second day onward, at the midday pressing, it is used in this śastra; the sūtra: अहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव (aharahaḥ śasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭeva) (Ā. Sū. 7.1). In the one-day sādyaskra rite, in the Marutvatīya śastra, its first ṛk सद्यो ह जात (sadyo ha jāta) is the sūktamukhīya (opening verse); the sūtra: सद्यो ह जातो वृषभः कनीनस्त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्र । (sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīnastvaṃ sadyo apibo jāta iṃdra |) (Ā. Sū. 9.5).

Anuvāda (Kannada): This sūkta सद्यो ह (sadyo ha) is the tenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka and has five ṛks. Its seer is Viśvāmitra, deity Indra, metre Triṣṭubh. It is stated in the Anukramaṇikā as beginning with सद्यो ह (sadyo ha). Its use for the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra mantras at the midday pressing of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra सद्यो ह जात एवा त्वामिंद्र (sadyo ha jāta evā tvāmiṃdra) (Ā. 5-6). Its use for the recitation called ahar-ahaḥ-śastra, when the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra mantras are recited on the twenty-fourth (Cāturviṃśaka) day, is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra सद्यो ह जात इत्यहरहः शस्यं मैत्रावरुणः (sadyo ha jāta ityaharahaḥ śasyaṃ maitrāvaruṇaḥ) (Ā. 7-4). Its use for reciting the śastra mantras at the midday pressing, from the second day onward of the sacrifice called ahargaṇa, is set out by the sūtra अहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव (aharahaḥ śasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭeva)

p. 103

(Ā. 7-1). Its use for the first ṛk of this sūkta, in reciting the Marutvatīya śastra mantras in the one-day sacrifice called sādyaskra, is set out by the sūtra सद्यो ह जातो वृषभ, कनीनस्त्वं सद्यो अपिबो जात इंद्र (sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabha, kanīnastvaṃ sadyo apibo jāta iṃdra) (Ā. 9-5).

Om. Sūkta 48. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 48. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 3; Varga 12. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Viśvāmitra. Devatā: Indra. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒द्यो ह॑ जा॒तो वृ॑ष॒भः क॒नीनः॒ प्रभ॑र्तुमाव॒दंध॑सः सु॒तस्य॑ ।
सा॒धोः पि॑ब प्रतिका॒मं यथा॑ ते॒ रसा॑शिरः प्रथ॒मं ॒॑ सोम्यस्य ॥ १ ॥

sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīnaḥ prabhartumāvadaṃdhasaḥ sutasya |
sādhoḥ piba pratikāmaṃ yathā te rasāśiraḥ prathamaṃ
somyasya ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सद्यः । ह । जातः । वृषभः । कनीनः। प्रभर्तुं । आवत् । अंधसः । सुतस्य ।
साधोः । पिब । प्रतिकामं । यथा । ते । रसआशिरः । प.थमं । सोम्यस्य ॥ १ ॥

sadyaḥ | ha | jātaḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | kanīnaḥ| prabhartuṃ | āvat | aṃdhasaḥ | sutasya |
sādhoḥ | piba | pratikāmaṃ | yathā | te | rasaāśiraḥ | pa.thamaṃ | somyasya ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

वृषभो वृष्टिद्वारापां वर्षिता सद्यस्तदानीमेव जात उत्पन्नः कनीनः कमनीय इंद्रः सुतस्याभिषुतस्यांधसो हविर्लक्षणस्यान्नस्य सोमस्य प्रभर्तुं

Gist of the bhāṣya

वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ): he who rains down through the clouds' bursting; सद्यः (sadyaḥ): at that very moment; जातः (jātaḥ): born; कनीनः (kanīnaḥ): the desirable Indra. सुतस्य (sutasya): of the pressed अंधसः (aṃdhasaḥ), the food in the form of oblation, Soma; प्रभर्तुं (prabhartuṃ) (the block breaks off here and continues on the next page).

p. 104

प्रकर्षण भर्तारं संग्रहीतारं यजमानमावत् । रक्षतु । ह प्रसिद्धौ । किंच तादृशस्त्वं प्रतिकामं कामे कामे सोमपानेच्छायां सत्यां ते तव यथा कामस्य पूर्तिर्भवति तथा साधो रसात्मना संसिद्धं रसाशिरो गॊपयोमिश्रणोपेतं सोम्यस्य सोममयं रसं प्रथमं सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पुरस्तात्पिब ॥ प्रतिकामं । कामं कामं प्रति । वीप्सायामव्ययाभावः । समासस्वरः । यथा । अपादांतत्वादेव लित्स्वरः । रसाशिरः । आज्‌पूर्वात् श्रीणातेः क्विप्यपस्पृधेथामित्यादिनाशिर् इत्यादेशः। बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । सोम्यस्य । सोमशब्दान्मयडर्थे मये चेति यप्रत्ययः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

प्रभर्तुं (prabhartuṃ): the bearer, the gatherer in abundance, the sacrificer; may Indra protect him (आवत् (āvat)). ह (ha) (both) are well-known particles. Further, O Indra, being such, whenever the desire to drink Soma arises (प्रतिकामं (pratikāmaṃ)), as your desire may be fulfilled, drink first, before all the gods, the Soma juice (सोम्यस्य (somyasya), made of Soma), perfected as juice (साधोः (sādhoḥ)) and रसाशिरः (rasāśiraḥ), that is, mixed with cow's milk. The rest is grammar on प्रतिकामं (pratikāmaṃ), यथा (yathā), रसाशिरः (rasāśiraḥ) and सोम्यस्य (somyasya).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ)—the sender-down of rain
  • सद्यो ह जातः (sadyo ha jātaḥ)—as soon as born
  • कनीनः (kanīnaḥ)—Indra, who has an attractive form
  • सुतस्य (sutasya)—pressed
  • अंधसः (aṃdhasaḥ)—the food in the form of Soma
  • प्रभर्तुं (prabhartuṃ)—the sacrificer who holds it in abundance
  • आवत् (āvat)—may he protect (O Indra)
  • प्रतिकामं (pratikāmaṃ)—whenever you have the wish
  • ते (te)—to you
  • यथा (yathā)—so as to be satisfied
  • साधोः (sādhoḥ)—juicy
  • रसाशिरः (rasāśiraḥ)—mixed with milk
  • सोम्यस्य (somyasya)—Soma juice
  • प्रथमं (prathamaṃ)—before all the gods
  • पिब (piba)—drink
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, the sender-down of rain, who is of a charming form as soon as he is born, protect the sacrificer who devoutly holds the pressed Soma. O Indra, whenever you wish, drink, so as to be satisfied, the juicy, milk-mixed Soma juice before all the gods.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May the showerer (of rain), who, as soon as born, is the object of affection, protect the offerer of the effused libation: drink at will, Indra, before (the other gods), of the pure Soma juice mixed with milk.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्रतिकामं यथा ते (pratikāmaṃ yathā te)—कामे कामे सोमपानेच्छायां सत्यां ते तव यथा कामस्य पूर्तिर्भवति तथा (पिब) (kāme kāme somapānecchāyāṃ satyāṃ te tava yathā kāmasya pūrtirbhavati tathā (piba)). O Indra, whenever the wish to drink Soma arises in you, that is, whenever you like, drink Soma juice as much as will satisfy you: so the seer prays.

p. 105

रसाशिरः (rasāśiraḥ)—rasa here means liquid milk. The meaning is Soma juice mixed with such milk, or gavāśira.

प्रथमं सोम्यस्य (prathamaṃ somyasya)—सोममयं रसं प्रथमं सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पुरस्तात्पिब (somamayaṃ rasaṃ prathamaṃ sarvebhyo devebhyaḥ purastātpiba). The meaning: drink the Soma, strained and prepared as juice, before the other gods drink it, that is, you first of all.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यज्ञाय॑था॒स्तदह॑रस्य॒ कामें॒ 5 शोः पी॒यूष॑मपिबो
गिरि॒ष्ठां ।

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र त्वं यद्यस्मिन्नहनि जायथा अजायथाः तदहस्तस्मिन्नेवाहन्यस्य सोमस्य कामे पिसासायां सत्यां गिरिष्ठां गिरिस्थां पर्वतोस्कोच्चस्थाने वर्तमानमंशोः सोमलताखंडविशिष्टस्य ऋजीषस्य पीयूषमभिनवं रसमपिबः । पीतवानसि । उत्पत्तिक्षण एव सोमपाने कारणं दर्शयति । ते तव जनित्री माता योषा युवतिरदितिर्महो महतः पितुर्जनकस्य कश्यपस्य दमे सूतिकागृहेऽग्रे स्तन्यदानात् प्राक् तं तादृषं सोमं पर्यासिंचत् । तवास्यॆ परितोऽक्षारयत् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, on the day on which you were born, on that very day, when the desire for this Soma arose, you drank the nectar, the fresh juice, of the अंशोः (aṃśoḥ), which is distinguished by pieces of the Soma plant, of the ṛjīṣa, गिरिष्ठां (giriṣṭhāṃ) (गिरिस्थां (giristhāṃ)), standing on the high place of a mountain.NOTE He shows the reason for drinking Soma at the very moment of birth: your mother (जनित्री (janitrī)), the young woman (योषा (yoṣā)) Aditi, in the lying-in chamber of your great father, your begetter Kaśyapa (महः पितुः दमे (mahaḥ pituḥ dame)), before giving the breast (अग्रे (agre)), poured that Soma around you (पर्यासिंचत् (paryāsiṃcat)), that is, made it flow all around your mouth.

p. 106

जायथाः । जनी प्रादुर्भाव इत्यस्य लजि बहुलं छंदसीत्यडभावः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । जनित्री । जनिता मंत्र इति निपातनाण्णेर्लोपः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The block contains only grammatical notes, on जायथाः (jāyathāḥ) and जनित्री (janitrī).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • (O Indra) यत् (yat)—when
  • जायथाः (jāyathāḥ)—you were born
  • तदहः (tadahaḥ)—that very day
  • अस्य (asya)—of this Soma juice
  • कामे (kāme)—when the desire to drink arose
  • गिरिष्ठां (giriṣṭhāṃ)—that was at the high place of the mountain
  • अंशोः (aṃśoḥ)—of the piece of Soma plant
  • पीयूषं (pīyūṣaṃ)—the juice
  • आपिबः (āpibaḥ)—you drank
  • ते (te)—your
  • जनित्री (janitrī)—mother
  • योषा (yoṣā)—and young woman, Aditi
  • महः (mahaḥ)—great-souled
  • पितुः (pituḥ)—your father, Kaśyapa's
  • दमे (dame)—in the lying-in chamber
  • अग्रे (agre)—before (giving you) the breast
  • तं (taṃ)—that Soma
  • परि आसिंचत् (pari āsiṃcat)—she made you drink fully
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as soon as you were born, when the desire to drink Soma juice arose, you drank the juice of the piece of Soma plant that was at the high place of the mountain. Your mother, the young Aditi, in the lying-in chamber of the great-souled Kaśyapa, your begetter, made you drink that Soma fully before giving you the breast.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

On the day on which you were born, you drank at will the mountain-abiding nectar of this Soma plant. for your youthful parent mother (Aditi), in the dwelling of your great sire (Kashyapa), gave it to you before she gave the breast.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The first half of this ṛk explains that Indra felt the wish to drink Soma on the very day he was born and drank that nectar-like Soma juice. The second half describes how Indra's mother, a young woman, in her husband's house, as soon as Indra was born, made him drink Soma juice before nursing him at the breast. This indicates that Indra's desire to drink Soma has been great from the beginning. Here, although there is no statement of who Indra's mother is or who his father is, the commentator says that the mother of Indra is Aditi, the mother of the gods, and the father is Kaśyapa. Although this explanation agrees with the descriptions given in the Purāṇas and similar works, it cannot be said to accord with Vedic literature. For the position and status of Indra stated in the Purāṇas and similar works, and the position and status of Indra stated in the Ṛgveda

p. 107

(continuing the Special Topics of the preceding Ṛk)

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

…the status and rank of Indra in the Purāṇas and the like also differ greatly from those stated for Indra in the Ṛgveda. In the Purāṇas and the like Indra's rank is not of the highest. It says that there are deities above him, that Indra is an ordinary deity, and that he is lord of heaven alone. In the Vedas, however, Indra's position is said to be one of sovereignty: Indra alone is the best among all the deities. It was he who created earth and the atmosphere. In many places it is said that heaven and earth, the sun and moon, all other living beings and the whole creation are obedient to Indra's command, that Indra alone is the sole lord of the whole universe, and that he is the best of all the deities. Therefore there is room to say that the Indra of the Ṛgveda is the very principle of the Supreme Brahman stated in the Vedānta texts. In the Ṛgveda there are not as many hymns addressed to any other deity as to Indra. About 250 hymns, and some portions of hymns, praise Indra. Indra is also praised together with certain other deities. Taken all together, about 300 hymns are in his honour, which means about a quarter of the Ṛgveda. Indra's greatness and his deeds of daring are described more especially than those of all the other deities.

Moreover, it is said both in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā and in the Yajurveda that Indra is a son of Aditi, the mother of the gods:

अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्वंस्परि । (aṣṭau putrāso aditerye jātāstanvaṃspari |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8)

अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेः । ये जातास्तन्वःपरि । देवाउप प्रैत्सप्तभिः । परामार्तांडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उप प्रैत्तूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्युवे तत् । परामार्तांडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंशुश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग् श्चेत्येते ॥ (aṣṭau putrāso aditeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥpari | devāupa praitsaptabhiḥ | parāmārtāṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upa praittūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyuve tat | parāmārtāṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃśuśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāg ścetyete ‖) (Tai. Ā. 1-13-2, 3)

As stated here, Aditi has eight children, and their names are given as Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Āryamā, Aṃśu, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān. Since it is clearly stated that Indra is one of these eight, there is no doubt whatever that Aditi, the mother of the gods, is Indra's mother. As for his father being Kaśyapa, that is only a statement of the Purāṇas; there is no support for it in the Ṛgveda.

गिरिस्थां अंशोः पीयूषं (giristhāṃ aṃśoḥ pīyūṣaṃ)—here the use of the word गिरिस्थां (giristhāṃ) indicates Soma plants grown on mountains. Although the Soma plant also grows on plains and on river banks, the one grown on mountains is famed as the best. Moreover, the higher it grows the better it is, and it is famed as having more juice and being more pleasant to the taste. Among the mountains where the Soma plant grows, the mountain named Mūjavat is famed, and is mentioned in many places in the Ṛgveda.

p. 108

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

उ॒प॒स्थाय॑ मा॒तर॒मन्न॑मैट्ट ति॒ग्मम॑पश्यद॒भि सोम॒मूधः॑ ।
प्र॒या॒वय॑न्नचर॒द्गत्सो॑ अ॒न्यान्म॒हानि॑ चक्रे पुरु॒धप्र॑तीकः ॥ ३ ॥

upasthāya mātaramannamaiṭṭa tigmamapaśyadabhi somamūdhaḥ |
prayāvayannacaradgatso anyānmahāni cakre purudhapratīkaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

उपस्थाय । मातरं । अन्नं । ऐट्ट । तिग्मं । अपश्यत् । अभि । सोमं । ऊधः ।
प्रयवयन् । अचरत् । गृत्सः । अन्यान् । महानि । चक्रे । पुरुध्रप्रतीकः ॥ ३ ॥

upasthāya | mātaraṃ | annaṃ | aiṭṭa | tigmaṃ | apaśyat | abhi | somaṃ | ūdhaḥ |
prayavayan | acarat | gṛtsaḥ | anyān | mahāni | cakre | purudhrapratīkaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

स इंद्रो मातरमुपस्थाय प्रार्थयित्वान्नमैट्ट । तामन्नमयाचत । ईळिरध्येषणाकर्मति यास्कः । ततस्तस्या ऊध ऊधसि क्षीररूपेण स्थितं तिग्मं दीप्तं सोममभ्य पश्यत् । सर्वतोऽदर्शत् । गृत्सः । अभिकांक्ष्यते सर्वैर्देवैः शत्रुहननार्थमिति गृत्स इंद्रः । अन्यान्सपत्नान्वयवयन् स्वस्वस्थानात्पकर्षणोच्चालयन्नचरत् । सर्वत्र चरति । किंच पुरुधप्रतीकस्तेजोयोगाद्बहुधा विक्षिप्तांगो महानि महांति वृत्रहननादीनि कर्माणि चक्रे ॥ उपस्थाय । तिष्ठतेर्लपि घुमास्थेतीत्वे प्राप्ने न ल्यपीति प्रतिषेधः । लित्स्वरः । ऐट्ट । ईळिर्याच्छार्थः । तस्माल्लजि रूपं । आडजादीनामित्याडागमः । ष्टुत्वं । निघातः । तिग्मं । तिज निशाने । अस्माद्युजिरुचितिजां कुश्चति मक्प्रत्ययः कवर्गादेशश्च । प्रयवयन् । यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोरित्यस्यण्यंतस्य शतरि रूपं । लित्स्वरः । गृत्सः । गृधु अभिकांक्षायां । गृधिपण्योर्दका चेति सप्रत्ययो दकारश्चांतादेशः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । पुरुधप्रतीकः । पुरुशब्द इह संख्यावाची । संख्याया विधार्थे धेति धाप्रत्ययः । ह्रस्वश्छांदसः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this Indra, approaching his mother, asked her for food (ऐट्ट (aiṭṭa)): he begged her for food. Yāska says that ईळि (īḷi) denotes the act of requesting. Then, in her udder, he saw all around the bright (तिग्मं (tigmaṃ)) Soma standing there in the form of milk. गृत्सः (gṛtsaḥ) is Indra, because he is desired by all the gods for the slaying of enemies. Driving the others, his rivals, away, dislodging them from their several places, he moved about everywhere. Further, being पुरुधप्रतीकः (purudhapratīkaḥ), with his limbs spread out in many ways through union with radiance, he performed great deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra. (The rest of the block is grammatical.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • मातरं (mātaraṃ)—his mother
  • उपस्थाय (upasthāya)—having approached
  • अन्नं (annaṃ)—food
  • ऐट्ट (aiṭṭa)—he begged
  • ऊधः (ūdhaḥ)—that which is in her breast in the form of milk
  • तिग्मं (tigmaṃ)—bright
  • सोमं (somaṃ)—Soma
  • अभि अपश्यत् (abhi apaśyat)—he looked at fully
  • गृत्सः (gṛtsaḥ)—Indra, who is desired by the gods
  • अन्यान् (anyān)—enemies
  • प्रयवयन् (prayavayan)—driving them out of their several places
  • अचरत् (acarat)—moves about everywhere
  • पुरुधप्रतीकः (purudhapratīkaḥ)—spread everywhere in his form of radiance
  • महानि (mahāni)—very great deeds
  • चक्रे (cakre)—he performed

p. 109

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra approached his mother and begged her for food. He looked fully at the bright Soma that was in her breast in the form of milk. Indra, who is desired by the gods, moves about everywhere driving the enemies out of their several places. Spread everywhere in his form of radiance, he performed very great deeds.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Approaching his mother he asked for food, and beheld the acrid Soma upon her bosom : eager he proceeds, dislodging the adversaries (of the gods) ; and, putting forth manifold (energy), he performed great (deeds).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is described that Indra begged his mother for अन्न (anna) (food), and saw that the milk in her breast was in the form of Soma.

ऐट्ट (aiṭṭa)—ईळिर्याच्चार्थः । (īḷiryāccārthaḥ |) ईळिरध्येषणाकर्मेति यास्कः । (īḷiradhyeṣaṇākarmeti yāskaḥ |) The meaning is: he desired, he begged.

गृत्सः (gṛtsaḥ)—For the word गृत्सः (gṛtsaḥ), formed from the root गृधु अभिकांक्षायां (gṛdhu abhikāṃkṣāyāṃ), the commentator gives the etymological sense: अभिकांक्ष्यते सर्वैर्देवैः शत्रुहननार्थमिति गृत्स इंद्रः । (abhikāṃkṣyate sarvairdevaiḥ śatruhananārthamiti gṛtsa iṃdraḥ |) That is, since all the deities desire Indra for the work of destroying enemies, Indra is called Gṛtsa.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

उ॒ग्रस्तु॑रा॒षाळ॒भिभू॑त्योजा यथाव॒शं त॒न्वं॑ चक्र ए॒षः ।
त्वष्टा॑र॒मिंद्रो॑ ज॒नुषा॑भि॒भूया॒मुष्या॒ सोम॑मसिबच्च॒मूषु॑ ॥ ४ ॥

ugrasturāṣāḷabhibhūtyojā yathāvaśaṃ tanvaṃ cakra eṣaḥ |
tvaṣṭāramiṃdro januṣābhibhūyāmuṣyā somamasibaccamūṣu ‖ 4 ‖

p. 110

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

उग्रः । तुराषाट् । अभिभूतिओजाः । यथावशं । तन्वं । चक्रे । विषः ।
त्वष्टारं । इंद्रः । जनुषा । अभिभूय । आमुष्य । सोमं । अपिबत् । चमूषु ॥

ugraḥ | turāṣāṭ | abhibhūtiojāḥ | yathāvaśaṃ | tanvaṃ | cakre | viṣaḥ |
tvaṣṭāraṃ | iṃdraḥ | januṣā | abhibhūya | āmuṣya | somaṃ | apibat | camūṣu ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

य एष इंद्र उग्रः शत्रोणां भयंकरस्तुराषाट् त्वरया शत्रोणामभिभविता अत एवाभिभूत्योजाः शत्रोणामभिभवनपराक्रमोपेतः सन् तन्वमात्मीयं शरीरं यथावशं यथाकामं नानाधिरूपोपेतं चक्रे । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । रूपंरूपं मघना बोभवीति । ऋग्वे. ३-५३-८ । इति स इंद्रो जनुषा जन्मना सामर्थ्येन त्वष्टारं त्वष्टृनामकमसुरमभिभूय चमूषु चमसेषु स्थितमामुष्य चोरयित्वा सोममपिबत् । त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रमित्यादि प्रासहा सोममपिबत्। तै. सं. २-४-१२। इति तैत्तिरीयकं॥ तुराषाट् । इत्वरा संभ्रमे । क्विप् । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना ऊट् । सहेश्छंदसि सह इति ण्णिः । कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलमिति समासः । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमिति तृतीयाया अलुक् । सहेः साडः स इति षत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । यथावशं । वशं काममनतिक्रम्येत्यव्ययीभावसमासः । समासस्वरः । आमुष्य । मुष स्तेये । ल्यप् । चमूषु । चमु अदने । कृषिचमितनिधनिसर्जिखर्जिभ्य ऊरित्यूप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this Indra is उग्रः (ugraḥ), terrible to enemies; तुराषाट् (turāṣāṭ), one who overcomes enemies with speed; hence अभिभूत्योजाः (abhibhūtyojāḥ), endowed with the might to overpower enemies. Being so, he made (चक्रे (cakre)) his own body यथावशं (yathāvaśaṃ), according to his wish, endowed with many kinds of forms. So too there is a mantra text: रूपंरूपं मघना बोभवीति (rūpaṃrūpaṃ maghanā bobhavīti) (Ṛgveda 3-53-8). That Indra, जनुषा (januṣā), by birth, that is, by his native power, overcame the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ, stole the Soma lying in the ladles (चमूषु (camūṣu), that is, in the cups), and drank it. The Taittirīya text says: त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रमित्यादि प्रासहा सोममपिबत्। (tvaṣṭā hataputro vīṃdramityādi prāsahā somamapibat|) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12). (The rest of the block is grammatical.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • एषः (eṣaḥ)—this Indra
  • उग्रः (ugraḥ)—being terrible
  • तुराषाट् (turāṣāṭ)—one who defeats enemies
  • अभिभूत्योजाः (abhibhūtyojāḥ)—possessing the brilliance that conquers enemies
  • तन्नं (tannaṃ)—his body
  • यथावशं (yathāvaśaṃ)—as he pleased
  • चक्रे (cakre)—he changed
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—that same Indra
  • जनुषा (januṣā)—by his natural power
  • त्वष्टारं (tvaṣṭāraṃ)—the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ
  • अभिभूय (abhibhūya)—having defeated
  • चमूषु (camūṣu)—that was in the ladle-vessel
  • सोमं (somaṃ)—the Soma
  • आमुष्य (āmuṣya)—having carried off
  • अपिबत् (apibat)—drank
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Indra, being terrible, a defeater of enemies, and possessed of the brilliance that conquers enemies, changed his body as he pleased. That same Indra, by his natural power, defeated the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ, carried off the Soma that was in the ladle-vessel, and drank it.

p. 111

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Fierce, rapid in assault, of overpowering strength, he made his form obedient to his will; having overcome Twashtri by his innate (vigour), and carried off the Soma juice, he drank it (deposited) in the ladles.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तुराषाट् (turāṣāṭ)—त्वरया शत्रूणामभिभवता । (tvarayā śatrūṇāmabhibhavatā |) Because he defeats enemies very quickly, Indra has the name तुराषाट् (turāṣāṭ).

अभिभूत्योजाः (abhibhūtyojāḥ)—शत्रुणामभिभवनपराक्रमोपेतः । (śatruṇāmabhibhavanaparākramopetaḥ |) The meaning is that Indra is endowed with the greatest prowess for defeating enemies. That is why the epithet उग्रः (ugraḥ), "terrible to enemies", is stated here.

यथावशं तन्नं चक्रे एषः (yathāvaśaṃ tannaṃ cakre eṣaḥ)—तन्नमात्मीयं शरीरं यथाकामं नानाविधरूपोपेतं चक्रे । (tannamātmīyaṃ śarīraṃ yathākāmaṃ nānāvidharūpopetaṃ cakre |) Since Indra is capable of taking on, in order to defeat enemies, the various forms that he likes, it is said here that at the time of destroying enemies he assumes whatever form (shape) he pleases. On this matter:

रूपंरूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं परि स्वां । (rūpaṃrūpaṃ maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānastanvaṃ pari svāṃ |) रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं प्रतिचक्षणाय । इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥ (rūpaṃrūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva tadasya rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya | iṃdro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18)

In Ṛks such as these it is said that, in order to conquer the Asuras who are masters of illusion, Indra assumes whatever forms he needs.

Regarding Indra overcoming Tvaṣṭṛ, carrying off the Soma in the ladles and drinking it: स इंद्रो जन्मना सामर्थ्येन त्वष्टनामकमसुरमभिभूय अस्य चमसपात्रेषु स्थितं सोमं चोरयित्वापिबत् । (sa iṃdro janmanā sāmarthyena tvaṣṭanāmakamasuramabhibhūya asya camasapātreṣu sthitaṃ somaṃ corayitvāpibat |) That Indra, by his own power, defeated the Asura named Tvaṣṭṛ, stole the Soma that Tvaṣṭṛ had placed in the ladle-vessels so that he might drink it, and drank it himself. Here Tvaṣṭṛ is described as an Asura. But this Tvaṣṭṛ is one of the Prajāpatis and the architect of the gods, and there are plenty of Ṛks in the Ṛgveda praising him. However, his son named Viśvarūpa, though priest to the gods, favoured the Asuras; therefore his father Tvaṣṭṛ too is called an Asura here. On this matter the commentator has given an itihāsa from the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as an example—

p. 112

त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रग्ं सोममाहरत्तस्मिन्निंद्र उपहवमैच्छत तन्नोपाह्वयत पुत्रं मेऽवधीरिति स यज्ञवेशसं तृत्वा प्रासहा सोममपिबत्तस्य यदत्यशिष्यत तत्त्वष्टाहवनीयमुप प्रावर्तयत्स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्वेति । (tvaṣṭā hataputro vīṃdragṃ somamāharattasminniṃdra upahavamaicchata tannopāhvayata putraṃ me 'vadhīriti sa yajñaveśasaṃ tṛtvā prāsahā somamapibattasya yadatyaśiṣyata tattvaṣṭāhavanīyamupa prāvartayatsvāheṃdraśatrurvardhasveti |) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12-1)

The Prajāpati Tvaṣṭṛ had a son named Viśvarūpa. Indra killed him for a certain reason. Enraged at this, Tvaṣṭṛ wished for a son who would kill Indra, and began to perform a sacrifice. But in that sacrifice, out of anger at Indra, that is, out of anger that he had killed his son, he did not invite Indra to the sacrifice and did not give him the Soma-drink. Indra, enraged at this, created an obstacle to his sacrifice and forcibly drank the Soma juice that was there. Unable to bear this, Tvaṣṭṛ poured the remainder of the Soma that Indra had left after drinking into the Āhavanīya fire and wished for a son who would kill Indra; and so on. The commentator has explained the meaning thus: what is stated here is the very matter of Indra's forcibly drinking the Soma.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

शु॒नं हु॑वेनु म॒घवा॑न॒मिंद्र॑म॒स्मिन्फरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सात् ।
शृ॒ण्वंत॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्तु॒ घ्नंतं॑ वृ॒त्राण॑ सं॒जितं॒ ॑ धनानां ॥ ५ ॥

śunaṃ huvenu maghavānamiṃdramasminphare nṛtamaṃ vājasāt |
śṛṇvaṃtamugramūtaye samattu ghnaṃtaṃ vṛtrāṇa saṃjitaṃ
dhanānāṃ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शुनं । हुवेम । मघवानं । इंद्रं । आस्मिन् । भरे । नृतमं । वाजसात् ।
शृण्वंतं । उग्रं । ऊतये । समत्सु । घ्नंतं । वृत्राणि । संजितं । धनानां ॥

śunaṃ | huvema | maghavānaṃ | iṃdraṃ | āsmin | bhare | nṛtamaṃ | vājasāt |
śṛṇvaṃtaṃ | ugraṃ | ūtaye | samatsu | ghnaṃtaṃ | vṛtrāṇi | saṃjitaṃ | dhanānāṃ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः। अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्धार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन् संग्रामे शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृद्धं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं शुघवानं धनवंतं अत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: "O Indra, वाजसात् (vājasāt): that in which there is साति (sāti), gain, of वाज (vāja), food, is वाजसाति (vājasāti). भरे (bhare): since warriors bear (बिभ्रति (bibhrati)) the fortune of victory by it, भर (bhara) is battle. In this battle we call you, शुनं (śunaṃ), swollen, grown strong through zeal. Or else शुनं (śunaṃ) is a name for happiness: one who gives happiness. You are मघवानं (maghavānaṃ), possessed of wealth, hence Indra, endowed with unsurpassed lordship, and नृतमं (nṛtamaṃ), in the highest degree the leader of the whole world. We, the Kuśikas, would call you for the sacrifice. Likewise, hearing the praise made by us…" (the sentence continues on the next page).

p. 113

क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संजितं सम्यग्वेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योरित्यस्य निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । ह्ययतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते शपो लुकि कृते च लिङ् रूपं । निघातः । भरे । भृञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । वाजसात् । षणु दाने । भावे क्तिन् । जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपवस्वरः । समत्तु । अद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति योद्धणामायूंषीति समदः संग्रामाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घ्नंतं । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेरिति घत्वं । संजितं । जि जये । क्विप् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(The sentence continues:) …"fierce, terrible to enemies; समत्तु (samattu), in battles, slaying (घ्नंतं (ghnaṃtaṃ)) all the demons that are marked by Vṛtra; and a thorough conqueror (संजितं (saṃjitaṃ)) of the wealth (धनानां (dhanānāṃ)) that belongs to enemies: we call you, for protection (ऊतये (ūtaye))." (The remainder of the block is grammatical. It also explains समत्सु (samatsu) as follows: they thoroughly devour the lives of warriors, therefore समदः (samadaḥ) are battles.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • वाजसात् (vājasāt)—which proceeds for the sake of food
  • भरे (bhare)—in battle
  • शुनं (śunaṃ)—one who increases through zeal, or one who produces happiness
  • मघवानं (maghavānaṃ)—wealthy
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—endowed with unsurpassed wealth
  • नृतमं (nṛtamaṃ)—the leader: you
  • हुवेम (huvema)—we call, praying
  • शृण्वंतं (śṛṇvaṃtaṃ)—one who listens to (our praises)
  • उग्रं (ugraṃ)—terrible to enemies
  • समत्तु (samattu)—in battles
  • वृत्राणि (vṛtrāṇi)—the Asuras beginning with Vṛtra
  • घ्नंतं (ghnaṃtaṃ)—one who strikes and destroys
  • धनानां (dhanānāṃ)—the wealth (of enemies)
  • संचितं (saṃcitaṃ)—you who gather it and give it (to us) NOTE
  • ऊतये (ūtaye)—for protection
  • (हुवेम (huvema)—we call, praying)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in the battle that proceeds for the sake of food, you who give happiness, are wealthy, endowed with unsurpassed wealth, are the leader, listen to our praises, are terrible to enemies, strike and destroy in battles the Asuras beginning with Vṛtra, and gather and give us the wealth of the enemies: we call you, praying, for protection.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The special topics of this Ṛk have already been explained earlier.

p. 114

Sūkta 49 (Maṇḍala 3)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

शंसा महामिति पंचर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । शंसा महामित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ समूळ्हे दशरात्रेष्टमेऽहनि मरुत्वतीयशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । शंसा महां महश्चित्त्वमिंद्र । आ. ८-७ । इति ॥ अनुवादवु—शंसा महां ऎंब ई सूक्तवु नाल्कनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि हन्नॊंदनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि ऐदु ऋक्कुगळिरुवुवु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ विश्वामित्रनु ऋषियु ; इंद्रनु देवतॆयु ; त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि शंसा महां ऎंदु मॊदलागि हेळिरुवुदु. समूळ दशरात्रवॆंब यागद ऎंटनॆय दिवस मरुत्वतीय शस्त्रमंत्रगळिगागि ई सूक्तद विनियोग विरुवुदॆंदु आश्वलायनशौतसूत्रद—शंसा महां महश्चित्त्वमिंद्र ऎंब सूत्रदिंद विवृत वागिरुवुदु (आ. ८-७). ॥ ओं ॥ सूक्त—४९ मंडल—३ ॥ अनुवाक—४ ॥ सूक्त—४९ ॥ अष्टक—३ ॥ अध्याय—३ ॥ वर्ग—१३ ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—५ ॥ । ऋषिः—विश्वामित्रः । । देवता—इंद्रः । । छंदः—त्रिष्टुप् ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the eleventh sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, of five ṛks. Its seer is Viśvāmitra, its deity Indra, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā marks it with the words शंसा महां (śaṃsā mahāṃ). It is used in the Marutvatīya śastra on the eighth day of the Samūḷha Daśarātra sacrifice, as the sūtra shows: शंसा महां महश्चित्त्वमिंद्र (śaṃsā mahāṃ mahaścittvamiṃdra) (Ā. Sū. 8-7). The block also gives the particulars: Maṇḍala 3, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 49, Aṣṭaka 3, Adhyāya 3, Varga 13, five ṛks.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

शंसा॑ म॒हामिंद्रं॒ यस्मि॒न्विश्वा॒ आ कृ॒स्टयः॑ सोम॒पाः ॒॑ काममव्यन् ।
यं सु॒क्रतुं॑ धि॒षणे॑ । विभ्वत॒ष्टं घ॒नं वृ॒त्राणां॑ ज॒नयं॑त ॒ देवाः ॥ १ ॥

śaṃsā mahāmiṃdraṃ yasminviśvā ā kṛsṭayaḥ somapāḥ
kāmamavyan |
yaṃ sukratuṃ dhiṣaṇe | vibhvataṣṭaṃ ghanaṃ vṛtrāṇāṃ janayaṃta
devāḥ ‖ 1 ‖

p. 115

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शंस महां । इंद्रं । यस्मिन् । विश्वाः । आ । कृष्टयः । सोमपाः । कामं ।
अव्वन् ।
यं । सुक्रतुं । धिषणे इति । विभ्वतष्टं । घनं । वृत्राणां । जनयंत । देवाः ॥

śaṃsa mahāṃ | iṃdraṃ | yasmin | viśvāḥ | ā | kṛṣṭayaḥ | somapāḥ | kāmaṃ |
avvan |
yaṃ | sukratuṃ | dhiṣaṇe iti | vibhvataṣṭaṃ | ghanaṃ | vṛtrāṇāṃ | janayaṃta | devāḥ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे होत महां महांतमिंड्रं शंस । शस्त्रैः स्तुहि । यस्मिन्निंद्रे रक्षितरि सति विश्वाः कृस्टयः सर्वे मनुष्याः सोमपा यज्ञमनुष्ठाय सोमपाः संतः कामं । काम्यत इति कामः स्वर्गादिः । तमाव्यन् सर्वतः प्राप्नुवंति । धिषणे देवमनुष्यादीनां धारयित्र्यौ । यद्वा । प्रगल्ले समर्थे स्वाश्रितान् रक्षितुमिति धिषणे द्यावापृथिव्यौ । देवाश्च सुक्रतुं । क्रतुः कर्म जगत्पालनादि । शोभनः क्रतुर्यस्यासौ सुक्रतुः । तादृशं विभृतष्टं विभुना ब्रह्मणा जगदाधिपत्ये स्थापितं महांतं वृत्राणां पापरूपाणां घनं हंतारं यमिंद्रं जनयंत । अजनयन् ॥ शंस । शन्नु स्तुतावित्यस्य लोटि रूपं । पादादित्वादनिघातः द्व्यचोऽतस्तिज इति संहितायां दीर्घः । अव्यन् । वी कांतिगत्यादिषु । लजि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । अट् स्वरः । सुक्रतुं । क्रत्वादयश्चेत्युत्तरसदाद्युदात्तः । धिषणे । इं धृषा प्रागल्ब इत्यस्माद्दषेर्धिष च संज्ञायामिति कु प्रत्ययः । धिष इत्यादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । घनं । हंतेः पुंसि संज्ञायामिति घः । हो हंतेरिति कुत्वं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । जनयंत । जनेर्न्यंतस्य लजि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Hotṛ, praise the great Indra with the śastras. Under the protection of this Indra, all men, having performed the sacrifice and become Soma-drinkers, obtain their desire." Kāma is what is desired, heaven and the like; Sāyaṇa glosses the verb as "they obtain it fully". The two धिषणे (dhiṣaṇe) are the two sustainers of gods, men and others. Or else they are bold and capable of protecting those who depend on them, that is, heaven and earth. The gods too (beget Indra). सुक्रतुं (sukratuṃ): kratu is work, such as the protection of the world; he whose work is excellent is sukratu. विभ्वतष्टं (vibhvataṣṭaṃ): established by Vibhu, that is Brahmā, in the sovereignty of the world. He is great, the घनं (ghanaṃ), the slayer of the Vṛtras, who are of the nature of sin. This Indra they begot.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यस्मिन् (yasmin)—in whose (Indra's) protection (O Hotṛ)
  • विश्वाः (viśvāḥ)—all
  • कृष्टयः (kṛṣṭayaḥ)—men
  • सोमपा (somapā)—having drunk Soma (at the close of the sacrifice)
  • कामं (kāmaṃ)—their desired object
  • अव्यन् (avyan)—obtain fully; (and)
  • धिषणे (dhiṣaṇe)—heaven and earth, which sustain all
  • देवाः (devāḥ)—all the gods as well
  • सुक्रतुं (sukratuṃ)—the excellent doer of deeds
  • विभ्वतष्टं (vibhvataṣṭaṃ)—one established by Vibhu for the sovereignty of the world
  • वृत्राणां (vṛtrāṇāṃ)—of Vṛtra and the other Asuras
  • घनं (ghanaṃ)—the destroyer
  • यं (yaṃ)—whom, that Indra
  • जनयंत (janayaṃta)—caused to be born, such a one
  • महां (mahāṃ)—of great nature
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—Indra
  • शंस (śaṃsa)—praise by reciting the śastras
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Hotṛ, praise with the recitation of the śastra-mantras that Indra of great nature, in whose protection all men, after performing the sacrifice and drinking Soma, obtain their desired object; whom heaven and earth, which sustain all, and all the gods also caused to be born: the excellent doer of deeds, established by Vibhu for the sovereignty of the world, the destroyer of Vṛtra and the other Asuras.

p. 116

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

I glorify the mighty Indra, in whom all men, drinking the Soma juice, obtain their wishes ; whom the powerful (heaven and earth) and the gods begot, the doer of great deeds, the slayer of the Vritras, who was fashioned by Vibhu (the creator)

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शंस महां इंद्रं (śaṃsa mahāṃ iṃdraṃ)—"O Hotṛ, praise in this sacrifice the greatly glorious Indra with śastra-mantras and the like": thus the sacrificer addresses the priest called Hotṛ. What the glory of Indra is, which is meant by the epithet महां (mahāṃ) ("greatly glorious"), the seer describes in the following sentences. यस्मिन् विश्वाः आ कृष्टयः सोमपाः कामं अव्यन् (yasmin viśvāḥ ā kṛṣṭayaḥ somapāḥ kāmaṃ avyan)—इंद्रे रक्षतरि सति सर्वे मनुष्याः यज्ञमनुष्ठाय सोमपाः संतः स्वर्गादिकामं सर्वतः प्राप्नुवंति (iṃdre rakṣatari sati sarve manuṣyāḥ yajñamanuṣṭhāya somapāḥ saṃtaḥ svargādikāmaṃ sarvataḥ prāpnuvaṃti). While the all-powerful Indra protects, all men perform sacrifices and other good rites, drink the Soma prescribed in those sacrifices, and as the fruit of it obtain the joys of heaven and the like. This is possible only through the glory of Indra. धीषणे देवाः सुक्रतुं विभ्वतष्टं वृत्राणां हंतारं यं जनयंत (dhīṣaṇe devāḥ sukratuṃ vibhvataṣṭaṃ vṛtrāṇāṃ haṃtāraṃ yaṃ janayaṃta)—Since the word धि (dhi) is read among the names of rites, the word धीषणे (dhīṣaṇe) may be explained as heaven and earth, which are capable in the rites that protect people, or all the creatures on the earth. It is said here that such heaven and earth, and the gods, produced Indra. That Indra, being capable of performing rites such as the protection of the world, is praised by the epithet सुक्रतुं (sukratuṃ); being established by Brahmā in the sovereignty of the world, by विभ्वतष्टं (vibhvataṣṭaṃ); and being the destroyer of sins, by घनं वृत्राणां (ghanaṃ vṛtrāṇāṃ). It is said here that heaven and earth and the gods produced such a greatly glorious Indra. The matter of heaven and earth producing Indra we have already mentioned earlier.

Ṛk 2

p. 117

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यं नु नकिः॒ पृत॑नासु स्व॒राजं॑ द्वि॒ता तर॑ति॒ नृत॑मं हरि॒ष्ठां ।
इ॒नत॑मः॒ सत्व॑भि॒र्यो ह॑ शू॒षैः पृ॑थु॒ज्रया॑ अमिना॒दायु॒र्दस्योः॑ ॥ २ ॥

yaṃ nu nakiḥ pṛtanāsu svarājaṃ dvitā tarati nṛtamaṃ hariṣṭhāṃ |
inatamaḥ satvabhiryo ha śūṣaiḥ pṛthujrayā aminādāyurdasyoḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

यं । नु । नकिः । पृतनासु । स्वराजं । द्विता । तरति । नृतमं । हरिस्थां ।
इनतमः । सत्वभिः । यः । ह । शूषैः । पृथुज्रयाः । अमिनात् । आयुः ।
दस्योः ॥ २ ॥

yaṃ | nu | nakiḥ | pṛtanāsu | svarājaṃ | dvitā | tarati | nṛtamaṃ | haristhāṃ |
inatamaḥ | satvabhiḥ | yaḥ | ha | śūṣaiḥ | pṛthujrayāḥ | amināt | āyuḥ |
dasyoḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पृतासु । व्याप्रियंतेऽत्र योद्धार इति पृतनाः संग्रामाः । तेषु स्वराजं हरिष्ठां हरिस्थां हरियुक्ते रथे वर्तमानं नृतमं बलस्य युद्धे नेतृतमं द्विता युद्ध मासाद्य सेनां द्विधा कृत्वा वर्तमानं यमिंद्रं नकिर्न कश्चिषपि तरति उत्तीर्य गच्छति । न कोऽप्यभ्यस्तीत्यर्थः । नु प्रसिद्धौ । स इंद्र इनतमोऽतिशयेन सेनास्वामी सत्वभिः परितः सीदद्विर्मरुद्भिः सह यो यान् गच्छन् शूष्यैः । शोषयंति परबलानीति शूषाणि बलानि । तैः पृथुज्रया युद्धं प्रति तीव्रवेगः सन् दस्यो शत्रोरायुरन्नं प्राणं वामिनात् । हिनस्ति । ह प्रसिद्धौ ॥ अत्र निरुक्तं । पृथुज्रयाः पृथुजवः । पृथुज्रया अमिनादायुर्दस्योः । प्रामापयुदायुर्दस्योः । ५-९ । इति ॥ तरति । त्य प्लवनतरणयोरित्यस्य लट रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । शपः पित्तादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । यः । या प्रापणी । औणादिकः कप्रत्ययः । आतो लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Pṛtanās are battles, where warriors engage. In them Indra is स्वराजं (svarājaṃ), self-ruling; हरिष्ठां (hariṣṭhāṃ) is हरिस्थां (haristhāṃ), standing in a chariot yoked with bay horses; नृतमं (nṛtamaṃ) is the best leader of strength in battle; द्विता (dvitā) means that, having come to battle, he proceeds dividing the enemy army in two. No one at all surpasses (तरति (tarati)) this Indra; the sense is that no one equals him. नु (nu) is a particle of well-known fact. That Indra, इनतमः (inatamaḥ), the greatest lord of the army, goes with the Maruts, the सत्वभिः (satvabhiḥ), who sit round about him. With his शूषैः (śūṣaiḥ), strengths that dry up (shoṣayanti) the forces of the foe, and being पृथुज्रयाः (pṛthujrayāḥ), of intense speed toward battle, he destroys the life, or the food, of the Dasyu, the enemy; ह (ha) is a particle of well-known fact. Sāyaṇa cites the Nirukta here, which explains पृथुज्रयाः (pṛthujrayāḥ) as पृथुजवः (pṛthujavaḥ) and then quotes the pāda of the ṛk, with a further word that is not clear (Ni. 5-9). NOTE

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • कृतनासु (kṛtanāsu)—in battles
  • स्वराजं (svarājaṃ)—shining by his own radiance
  • हरिष्ठां (hariṣṭhāṃ)—seated in a chariot yoked with horses
  • नृतमं (nṛtamaṃ)—the most excellent leader
  • द्विता (dvitā)—dividing the enemy army into two
  • यं (yaṃ)—that same Indra
  • नकिः (nakiḥ)—no one at all
  • तरति (tarati)—can surpass him
  • इनतमः (inatamaḥ)—as the most excellent commander
  • सत्वभिः (satvabhiḥ)—moving about with his companions the Maruts
  • यः (yaḥ)—which Indra
  • शूषैः (śūṣaiḥ)—with strength that dries up enemies
  • प्रथुज्रयाः (prathujrayāḥ)—running swiftly toward the battle
  • आयुः (āyuḥ)—the life of the enemy
  • अविनात् (avināt)—destroys
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same Indra, who shines in battles by his own radiance, is seated in a chariot yoked with horses, is the most excellent leader, and divides the enemy army in two, no one can surpass. As the most excellent commander, moving about with his companions the Maruts, running swiftly toward the battle with his enemy-withering strength, Indra destroys the lives of the enemies.

p. 118

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Whom, when borne by his steeds, foremost and eminent in battles, breaking in two the (hostile host), no one ever surpasses : supreme in sway, attended by his faithful Maruts, and hastening to combat, he has destroyed with foe-withering (energies) the existence of the Dasyu.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नकिः (nakiḥ)—Yāska says that the word नकिः (nakiḥ) is used in the sense of the nine "all-words" collection (sarvapada-samāmnāya), हिकं नुकं (hikaṃ nukaṃ) and the others (Ni. 3-13). In the present ṛk the meaning न कश्चिदसि (na kaścidasi), "no one is able", is stated for this word. NOTE नृतमं (nṛtamaṃ)—नेतृतमं (netṛtamaṃ): the best among leaders or chiefs. हरिष्ठां (hariṣṭhāṃ)—हरियुक्तेरथे वर्तमानं (hariyukterathe vartamānaṃ). The two horses of Indra are called Hari (Ni. 2-28). The sense is: Indra seated in a chariot to which such horses are yoked. इनतमः (inatamaḥ)—The word इन (ina) means lord. इनतमः (inatamaḥ) means one who is lord in an eminent or the highest degree. पृथुज्रयाः (pṛthujrayāḥ)—Yāska, taking this very ṛk as the example, gives the explanation पृथुज्रयाः पृथुजवः (pṛthujrayāḥ pṛthujavaḥ), "of extended speed", that is, one of great speed (Ni. 5-9). आयुः (āyuḥ)—Since the word आयुः (āyuḥ) means food (Ni. 3-9) and also life-breath or lifespan (Ni. 10-34), both meanings can be given here.
