rājā | vṛtraṃ | jaṃghanat | prāt | apāk | udak | atha | yajāte | vare | ā |
pṛthivyāḥ | 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे कुशिकाः कुशिकगोत्रोत्पन्ना हे पुत्रा उप प्रेत । अश्वस्य समीपे प्रकर्षण गच्छत । तत्र गत्वा चेतयध्वं । सावधाना भवत । यद्वा । आश्वरक्षिणः सावधानान् कुरुत । सुदासः पैजवनस्य राज्योऽश्वं राये तस्य दिग्विजयेन धनलाभाय प्र मुंचत । राजा देवानां स्वामींद्रो वृत्रं कर्मविघ्नकारिणमसुरं प्रागपागुदक् पूर्वपश्चिमोत्तरेषु देशेषु जंघनत् । भृशं हतवान् । तस्मादश्वं विमुंचतेति भावः । आधानंतरं पृथिव्या वर उत्तमे देवयजनदेशे यजाते । स राजा यजीत ॥ चेतयध्वं । चिती संज्ञान इत्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लोटि रूपं । आमंत्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्तेन तिजि उत्तरत्वान्न निघातः । जंघनत् । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य यज्लुकि नुगतोऽनुनासिकांतस्येत्यभ्यासस्य नुगागमः । तदंताल्लेट्यडागमः । प्राक् । अंचतेः क्विनि रूपं । अनिगंतोऽंचतावप्रत्यय इति गतेः स्वरः । यजाते । यजतेर्लॆट्प्याडागमः । निघातः । वरे । वृञ् वरण इत्यस्मात् ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्चेत्यप्पत्ययः । तस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Kuśikas, sons born in the Kuśika lineage, go forward to the horse", that is, approach the horse. Having gone there, "attend", that is, be watchful. Or else: make the horse-guards watchful. "Release the horse of Sudās Paijavana, the king, for wealth", that is, for gaining wealth by his conquest of the quarters. "The king", Indra, lord of the gods, has struck Vṛtra, the demon who obstructs rites, in the eastern, western and northern regions, that is, has smitten him heavily. Therefore release the horse: this is the sense. Afterwards "in the best of the earth", in the excellent place for the sacrifice to the gods, "he shall sacrifice": that king should sacrifice.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • कुशिकाः (kuśikāḥ)—O sages born in the Kuśika line
  • उप प्रेत (upa preta)—approach (the horse) and walk
  • चेतयध्वं (cetayadhvaṃ)—be watchful; or make the horse-guards watchful
  • राजा (rājā)—Indra, lord of all the gods
  • वृत्रं (vṛtraṃ)—the demon Vṛtra (who causes obstacles to the sacrificial rite)

p. 202

  • प्राक् (prāk)—in the east
  • अपाक् (apāk)—in the west
  • उदक् (udak)—in the north
  • जंघनत् (jaṃghanat)—has destroyed (therefore)
  • सुदासः (sudāsaḥ)—of the king named Sudās
  • अश्वं (aśvaṃ)—the horse
  • राये (rāye)—for the gaining of wealth
  • प्र मुंचत (pra muṃcata)—loosen and release
  • अथ (atha)—afterwards
  • पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ)—of the earth
  • वरे (vare)—in an excellent region
  • यजाते (yajāte)—perform the sacrifice (fearlessly)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sages of the Kuśika line, go to the horse and make the horse-guards watchful. Indra, lord of all the gods, has destroyed the demon Vṛtra, who obstructs the sacrificial rite, in all directions beginning with the east. Therefore, without the least fear, release the horse of King Sudās for the gaining of wealth. Afterwards perform the sacrifice fearlessly in an excellent region of the earth.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Approach, Kushikas, the steed of Sudas ; animate (him), and let him loose to (win) riches (for the raja); for the king (of the gods) has slain Vritra in the East, in the West, in the North, therefore let (Sudas) worship him in the best (regions) of the earth.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk describes how King Sudās performed the Aśvamedha sacrifice with the help of Viśvāmitra.

कुशिकाः उप प्र इत चेतयद्वं (kuśikāḥ upa pra ita cetayadvaṃ)—कुशिकगोत्रोत्पन्ना पुत्रा अश्वस्य समीपे गच्छत। गत्वा च सावधाना भवत। अश्वरक्षिणः सावधानान् कुरुतः (kuśikagotrotpannā putrā aśvasya samīpe gacchata| gatvā ca sāvadhānā bhavata| aśvarakṣiṇaḥ sāvadhānān kurutaḥ). The seer Viśvāmitra addresses his sons and kinsmen born in the Kuśika line, speaking thus: O sons and others of the Kuśika line, hear what I say. In this Aśvamedha sacrifice that King Sudās is performing, go near the sacrificial horse, remain there attentively, and help to guard it.

सुदासः अश्वं राये प्र मुंचत (sudāsaḥ aśvaṃ rāye pra muṃcata)—In the sacrifice (or the expedition of conquest) of Sudās, undertaken for the gain of wealth, release the sacrificial horse to wander. NOTE Here an explanation of "release the sacrificial horse to wander" is necessary. The sacrifice called Aśvamedha is one that only kings of the kṣatriya class perform. Much wealth is needed to perform this sacrifice. Therefore the king who sacrifices takes the initiation for the sacrifice, honours the sacrificial horse with the prescribed worship and the rest,

p. 203

and lets it wander freely for a period of one year. Following the horse, the king's men set out with an army, conquer the kings of whatever countries the horse goes to, collect tribute from them, and after one year return and join their own country. Until then the king keeps to observances such as brahmacarya, and after the horse has come back he performs the sacrifice: this is the custom. This very matter is indicated here by the sentence "release the horse for wealth", that is, release the horse for earning wealth. It is also a description of the conquest of the quarters undertaken for the gaining of wealth by the king named Sudās, son of Pijavana. NOTE The meaning of the latter half of this Ṛk is clear.

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

य इ॒मे रोद॑सी उ॒भे अ॒हमिंद्र॒मतु॑ष्टवं ।
वि॒श्वामि॑त्रस्य रक्षति॒ ब्रह्म॒दं भार॑तं॒ जनं॑ ॥ १२ ॥

ya ime rodasī ubhe ahamiṃdramatuṣṭavaṃ |
viśvāmitrasya rakṣati brahmadaṃ bhārataṃ janaṃ ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

यः । इमे इति । रोदसी इति । उभे इति । अहं । इंद्रं । अतुस्तवं ।
विश्वामित्रस्य । रक्षति । ब्रह्म । इदं । भारतं । जनं ॥ १२ ॥

yaḥ | ime iti | rodasī iti | ubhe iti | ahaṃ | iṃdraṃ | atustavaṃ |
viśvāmitrasya | rakṣati | brahma | idaṃ | bhārataṃ | janaṃ ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे कुशिकाः कुशिकपुत्रा योऽहं विश्वामित्र उभे इमे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्याविंद्रमतुष्टवं स्तावयामि । द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामिंद्रस्य स्तोत्रं मया कारितमित्यर्थः । यद्वा । उभयो रोदस्कोरंतरवस्थितमिंद्रं स्तौमि । स्तोत्रं कुर्वाणस्य विश्वामित्रस्य ममेदमिंद्रविषयं ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं भारतं भरतकुलं जनं रक्षति । पालयति ॥ अतुष्टवं । ष्टुञ् स्तुत् । ण्यंतस्य लुजं चजं रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । भारतं । भरतशब्द उत्सादिः । इांत्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Kuśikas, sons of Kuśika: I, Viśvāmitra, "have praised Indra" through "these two, heaven and earth", that is, I have caused praise: the praise of Indra has been made by me through heaven and earth. Or else: I praise Indra, who stands between the two worlds. This hymn of mine, of Viśvāmitra who is offering praise, concerning Indra, protects, guards, the people of the Bharata family.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः अहं (yaḥ ahaṃ)—I, who am renowned as Viśvāmitra
  • उभे इमे रोदसी (ubhe ime rodasī)—pervading between these two, heaven and earth
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—Indra
  • अतुष्टवं (atuṣṭavaṃ)—I praise
  • विश्वामित्रस्य (viśvāmitrasya)—of me, such a praiser
  • इदं ब्रह्म (idaṃ brahma)—this praise concerning Indra
  • भारतं जनं (bhārataṃ janaṃ)—all the people of the Bharata family
  • रक्षति (rakṣati)—protects

p. 204

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, who am renowned as Viśvāmitra, praise Indra, who pervades between these two, heaven and earth. This praise of Indra, by me who offer such praise, protects all the people of the Bharata family.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

I have made Indra glorified by these two, heaven and earth, and this prayer of Vishwamitra protects the race of Bharata.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

भारतं जनं (bhārataṃ janaṃ)—The people called Bharata were a very important people in the Ṛgveda period. From many Ṛks it is known that Viśvāmitra too was born in this people. In the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-11 and 12, when the seer Viśvāmitra praises the rivers Pipāṭ and Śutudrī, NOTE in the Ṛks यदंग त्वा भरताः संतरेयुर्गव्यन्ग्राम इषित इंद्रजूतः । (yadaṃga tvā bharatāḥ saṃtareyurgavyangrāma iṣita iṃdrajūtaḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3.33-1) NOTE अतारिषुर्भरता गव्यवः समभक्त विप्रः सुमतिं नदीनां । (atāriṣurbharatā gavyavaḥ samabhakta vipraḥ sumatiṃ nadīnāṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-12) he prays that the rivers should lessen their water so that his own people, the Bharata people, may be able to cross those rivers. Just as the seer Viśvāmitra is related to the Bharata people, the name of the seer Vasiṣṭha NOTE is also seen mentioned here and there along with theirs. The original ancestor of this Bharata people was Bharata himself. It is said in other Vedas too that he was a very renowned king: महते क्षत्राय महत अभसत्याय महते जानराज्यैषवो भरता राजा । (mahate kṣatrāya mahata abhasatyāya mahate jānarājyaiṣavo bharatā rājā |) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-10-2) as is said in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. This Bharata's name is also indicated in the Śunaḥśepa story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. The matter of this Bharata and the Bharata people will be explained in detail later.

p. 205

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

वि॒श्वामि॑त्राअरासत॒ ब्रह्मेंद्रा॑य व॒ज्रणे॑ ।
कर॒दिन्नः॑ सु॒राध॑सः ॥ १३ ॥

viśvāmitrāarāsata brahmeṃdrāya vajraṇe |
karadinnaḥ surādhasaḥ ‖ 13 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

विश्वामित्राः । अरासत । ब्रह्म । इंद्राय । वज्रिणे ।
करत् । इत् । नः । सुराधसः ॥ १३ ॥

viśvāmitrāḥ | arāsata | brahma | iṃdrāya | vajriṇe |
karat | it | naḥ | surādhasaḥ ‖ 13 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

विश्वामित्रा वज्रिणे वज्रहस्तायेंद्राय ब्रह्म स्तोत्रमरासत । अकुर्वन् । स्तुतः स इंद्रो नोऽस्मान् सुराधसः शोभनधनोपेतान् करदित् । करोत्वेव ॥ अरासत । रास्प शब्द इत्यस्य लजि बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् । निघातः । करत् । करोतेर्लुजि चेः कृमृद्यरुहिभ्यश्चंदसीत्यजादेशः । सुराधसः । आद्युदात्तं द्व्यंचदसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Viśvāmitras made a hymn (brahma, praise) for Indra, the vajra-holder, the one who has the thunderbolt in his hand. Being praised, may that Indra make us "possessed of fair wealth", that is, endowed with good riches: करदित् (karadit), let him indeed do it.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • विश्वामित्राः (viśvāmitrāḥ)—the kinsmen of Viśvāmitra
  • वज्रिणे (vajriṇe)—who holds the thunderbolt weapon
  • इंद्राय (iṃdrāya)—addressed to Indra
  • ब्रह्म (brahma)—the praise
  • अरासत (arāsata)—have composed (Indra, thus praised)
  • नः (naḥ)—us
  • सुराधसः (surādhasaḥ)—as possessors of excellent wealth
  • करदित् (karadit)—let him certainly make
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The kinsmen of Viśvāmitra have composed praise addressed to Indra, who holds the thunderbolt weapon. May Indra, thus praised, make us possessors of excellent wealth.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The Vishwamitras have addressd the prayer to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt ; may he therefore render us very opulent.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विश्वामित्राः (viśvāmitrāḥ)—Here the plural form Viśvāmitrāḥ is used to indicate Viśvāmitra and his sons, other relatives, those born in the Kuśika line, and others.

p. 206

अरासत (arāsata)—स्तोत्रमकुर्वन् (stotramakurvan). The word अरासत (arāsata) is formed from the root रासृ (rāsṛ) (रासृ शब्दे (rāsṛ śabde)), meaning "to make a sound". It means "they made a sound", that is, they recited praise.

Ṛk 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

किं ते॑ कृण्वंति॒ कीक॑टेषु॒ गावो॒ नाशिरं॑ दु॒ह्रे न त॑पंति ॒ घर्मं ।
आ नो॑ भर॒ प्रम॑गंदस्य॒ वेदो॑ नैचाशा॒खं म॑घवन्रंधया
नः ॥ १४ ॥

kiṃ te kṛṇvaṃti kīkaṭeṣu gāvo nāśiraṃ duhre na tapaṃti
gharmaṃ |
ā no bhara pramagaṃdasya vedo naicāśākhaṃ maghavanraṃdhayā
naḥ ‖ 14 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

कं । ते । कृण्वंति । कीकटेषु । गावः । न । आशिरम् । दुह्रे । न । तपंति । घर्म० ।
आ । नः । भर । प्रमगंदस्य । वेदः । नैचाशाखं । मघवन् । रंधये । नः ॥ १४ '

kaṃ | te | kṛṇvaṃti | kīkaṭeṣu | gāvaḥ | na | āśiram | duhre | na | tapaṃti | gharma0 |
ā | naḥ | bhara | pramagaṃdasya | vedaḥ | naicāśākhaṃ | maghavan | raṃdhaye | naḥ ‖ 14 '

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र कीकटॆः स्वनार्यनिवासेषु जनपदेषु । यद्वा । क्रियाभिर्यागदानहोमलक्षणाभिः किं फलिष्यतीत्यश्रद्धधानाः प्रत्युत पिबत खादतायमेव लोको न पर इति वदंतो नास्तिका कीयटाः । तेषु गावस्ते तव किं कृण्वंति । किं कुर्वंति । न क्वचित्तवोपयोगं कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः । अनुपयोगं दर्शयति आशिरं सोममिश्रणयोग्यं पयो न दुह्रे । न दुहंति । किंच घर्मं प्रवर्ग्याख्यकर्मोपयुक्तं महावीरपात्रं स्वपयःप्रदानद्वारेण न तपंति । न दीपयंति । एतेन णांनाय्याद्यर्थमपि नोपयुज्यंत इत्यपि सूचितं भवति । एवं क्वचिदसि नैरिके कर्मण्णनप युक्तास्ता गा नोऽस्मभ्यमा भर । अहर । न केवलं ता एव किं तर्हि प्रमगंदस । द्वैगुणादिलक्षणपरिमाणं गतोऽर्थो मामेव गमिष्यतीति बुद्ध्या परेषां ददातीति मगंदो वार्धुषिकः । तस्यापत्यं पुत्रादिः प्रमगंद प्रस्कण्वादिवदपत्यार्थ, प्रशब्देन द्योत्यते । तस्यात्यंतकुसीदिकुलस्य वेदो धनमाहर । किंच हे मघव न्नवन्निंद्र नैचाशाखं । नीचासु शूद्रयोनिषूत्पादिता शाखा पुत्रपौत्रादिपरंपरा येन स नीचाराखः । शूद्रापत्यैश्च केवलैः शूद्रवेदी पतत्त्वथ इति च पातकहेतुतेन स्मरणात् । पतितस्य संबंधि धनं नैचाशाख. । तद्वनु नोऽस्मभ्यं रुधय

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, what do the cattle do for you among the Kīkaṭas?" Kīkaṭas are the countries that are dwellings of non-Āryas; or else, the unbelieving nāstikas who, doubting what any rite of sacrifice, gift and oblation will yield, say "drink, eat, only this world exists, there is no other". What do the cattle among them do for you? They are of no use to you. He shows their uselessness: they do not milk the आशिरं (āśiraṃ), the milk fit for mixing with Soma. Further, the Mahāvīra vessel used in the rite called Pravargya, the घर्मं (gharmaṃ), they do not heat, they do not make it glow by giving it their milk. By this it is also suggested that they are not used even for the Sāṃnāyya and the like. Thus they are useless in any rite; "bring those cattle to us". Not only these: also the wealth of Pramagaṇḍa. A मगंद (magaṃda) is a usurer, who lends to others with the thought "the wealth, once it has grown to double and so on, will come back to me alone". His offspring, a son and the like, is Pramagaṇḍa; the sense of offspring is conveyed by the prefix प्र (pra), as in Praskaṇva and others. "Bring the wealth of that family of extreme usurers." Further, "O Maghavan, Indra, नैचाशाखं (naicāśākhaṃ)": he by whom a branch, a line of sons and grandsons, has been produced in low (women), in śūdra wombs, is नीचाशाख (nīcāśākha); for by the smṛti, one who marries a śūdra woman, and one who is a śūdra-husband with children only by śūdra women, falls, being a cause of sin. The wealth connected with such a fallen man is नैचाशाखं (naicāśākhaṃ); "accomplish that for us" (the text continues on the next page).

p. 207

साधय । एतेषां तद्धनं तव नोपयुज्यते अस्मदायत्तं तु तद्धनं यागादिद्वारा तवोऽपयुज्यते । तस्मात्तदस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छेति भावः ॥ एतमर्थं यास्कोऽपाह । किं ते कुर्वंति कीकटेषु गावः । कीकटो नाम देशोऽनार्यनिवासः । कीकटाः किंकृताः किं क्रियाभिरितिप्रेप्सा वा । नैव चाशिरं दुह्रे न तपंति घर्मं घरणं । आ हर नः प्रमगंदस्य धनानि । मगंदः कुसीदी मांगदो मामागमिष्यतीति च ददाति । तदसत्यं प्रमगंदोऽत्यंतकुसीदिकुलीनः । प्रमदको वा योऽयमेवास्ति लोको न पर इति प्रेप्पुः । पंडको वा पंडकः पंडगः प्रार्दको वा प्रार्दयत्यांडौ । आंडावाणी इव व्रीडयति । तत्स्थं नैचाशाखं। नीचाशाखो नीचैः शाखः । शाखाः शक्नोतेः । आणिररणात्। तन्नो मघवन्रंधयेति रध्यतिर्वशगमने । नि. ६-३२ । इति ॥ आशिरं । आज्‌पूर्वाच्चीणातेः क्विप्यपस्पृधेथामित्यादिना शिरित्यादेशः। दुह्रे। दुहेर्लिटीरयोर इति रेआदेशः । द्विर्वचनस्यविकल्पितत्वात् द्विर्वचनाभावः । चादिलोपे विभाषेति न निघातः । नैचाशाखं । तस्येदमित्यण् । प्रत्ययस्वरः। रंधय । रधेर्ण्यंतस्य रधिजभोरचीति नुमागमः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Accomplish it": their wealth is of no use to you, but our wealth, depending on us, is of use to you through sacrifices and the like; therefore give it to us, is the sense. Yāska says on this meaning: "What do the cattle do for you among the Kīkaṭas? Kīkaṭa is the name of a country, the dwelling of non-Āryas. Or the Kīkaṭas are किंकृताः (kiṃkṛtāḥ), those who ask 'what by rites?'. They do not milk the āśira, they do not heat the gharma. Bring us the wealth of Pramagaṇḍa. A मगंद (magaṃda) is a usurer: 'it will come to me', so he gives. That is untrue: Pramagaṇḍa is one born in an extremely usurious family; or प्रमदक (pramadaka), one who desires 'only this world exists, no other'; or पंडक (paṃḍaka), पंडग (paṃḍaga), or प्रार्दक (prārdaka), who ... ; नैचाशाखं (naicāśākhaṃ): नीचाशाख (nīcāśākha) is नीचैः शाखः (nīcaiḥ śākhaḥ) ... 'that, Maghavan, accomplish for us'; the root रध्यति (radhyati) is in the sense of coming into one's power" (Ni. 6-32). NOTE. The remainder of the block is grammar.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • कीकटेषु (kīkaṭeṣu)—among the community of unbelieving Kīkaṭas
  • गावः (gāvaḥ)—cattle
  • ते (te)—to you
  • किं कृण्वंति (kiṃ kṛṇvaṃti)—what use do they produce
  • आशिरं (āśiraṃ)—the milk fit for mixing with Soma
  • न दुह्रे (na duhre)—they do not yield
  • घर्मं (gharmaṃ)—the Mahāvīra vessel used in the Pravargya sacrifice
  • न तपंति (na tapaṃti)—they do not make it glow (therefore)
  • नः (naḥ)—to us who serve you in the sacrifice
  • आ भर (ā bhara)—bring (those cattle)
  • प्रमगंदस्य (pramagaṃdasya)—of the line of Pramagaṇḍa, of ill family
  • वेदः (vedaḥ)—the wealth (bring to us)
  • मघवन् (maghavan)—O wealthy Indra
  • नैचाशाखं (naicāśākhaṃ)—the wealth of those born in low lineage
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • रंधय (raṃdhaya)—accomplish
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, possessor of wealth, the cattle in the community of the unbelieving Kīkaṭas are not useful for your sacrifice; their milk is not used for mixing with Soma, and their milk does not make the Mahāvīra vessel of the Pravargya glow. Therefore bring those cattle to us, who serve you in sacrificing. Accomplish for us also the wealth of the line of the ill-born Pramagaṇḍa and of the other low branches.

p. 208

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

What do the cattle for you among the Kikasas ; they yield no milk to mix with the Soma, they need not the vessel (for the libation) : bring them to us : (bring also) the wealth of the son of the usurer, and give us, Maghavan, (the possessions) of the low branches (of the community).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कीकटेषु गावः ते किं कृण्वंति (kīkaṭeṣu gāvaḥ te kiṃ kṛṇvaṃti)—O Indra, the cattle among wicked people, non-Āryas and unbelievers, do no useful work for you; since wicked non-Āryas do not perform sacrifices and the like for Indra, the cattle among them and their milk are wasted, not used for sacrifices. So how could those cattle be of use to you, Indra? They are not, is the sense.

कीकटेषु (kīkaṭeṣu)—आनार्यनिवासेषु जनपदेषु । यद्वा । क्रियाभिर्यागदानहोमलक्षणाभिः किंफलिष्यतीत्यश्रद्दधानाः प्रत्युत पिबत खादतायमेव लोको न पर इति वदंतो नास्तिकाः कीकटाः तेषु। (ānāryanivāseṣu janapadeṣu | yadvā | kriyābhiryāgadānahomalakṣaṇābhiḥ kiṃphaliṣyatītyaśraddadhānāḥ pratyuta pibata khādatāyameva loko na para iti vadaṃto nāstikāḥ kīkaṭāḥ teṣu|) Kīkaṭas are the uncivilized earlier inhabitants of this country, not of the Ārya lineage, who do not perform sacrifices like Āryas, do not worship Indra and the other gods, and trouble the Āryas and their sacrifices. Or, though born in the Ārya line, they perform no good deeds such as sacrifice, gift and homa, and without faith in them say "what use are they? there is no world but this; no heaven, hell, sin or merit; all that is imagination; so eat and drink what you want to be happy": such wicked unbelievers. Thus the meaning has been explained.

आशिरं न दुह्रे न तपंति घर्मं (āśiraṃ na duhre na tapaṃti gharmaṃ)—सोममिश्रणयोग्यं पयः न दुहंति । किंच प्रवर्ग्यकर्मोपयुक्तं महावीरपात्रं स्वपयःप्रदानद्वारेण न दीपयंति । एतेन सांनाय्यार्थमपि नोपयुज्यंत इत्यपि सूचितं भवति । (somamiśraṇayogyaṃ payaḥ na duhaṃti | kiṃca pravargyakarmopayuktaṃ mahāvīrapātraṃ svapayaḥpradānadvāreṇa na dīpayaṃti | etena sāṃnāyyārthamapi nopayujyaṃta ityapi sūcitaṃ bhavati |) The milk that cattle among non-Āryas yield serves no good rite; they do not give milk for mixing with the Soma juice, that is, their milk is not useful for Soma mixed with the milk called gavāśira. Moreover, their milk cannot be used for the milk placed in the Mahāvīra vessel in the Pravargya sacrifice, nor for the Sāṃnāyya.

p. 209

नः आ भर (naḥ ā bhara)—Therefore Indra is prayed: bring to us the cattle that are among those wicked people.

प्रमगंदस्य वेदः (pramagaṃdasya vedaḥ)—द्वैगुण्यादिलक्षणपरिमाणं गतोऽर्थो मामेव गमिष्यतीति बुद्धा परेषां ददातीति मगंदो वार्धुषिकः। तस्यापत्यं पुत्रादिः प्रमगंदः । प्रस्कण्वादिवदपत्यार्थः प्रशब्देन द्योत्यते । तस्यात्यंतकुसीदकुलस्य वेदः धनमाहर । (dvaiguṇyādilakṣaṇaparimāṇaṃ gato 'rtho māmeva gamiṣyatīti buddhā pareṣāṃ dadātīti magaṃdo vārdhuṣikaḥ| tasyāpatyaṃ putrādiḥ pramagaṃdaḥ | praskaṇvādivadapatyārthaḥ praśabdena dyotyate | tasyātyaṃtakusīdakulasya vedaḥ dhanamāhara |) One who lends money to others with the evil thought that, lent to someone, it will come back with interest at double the sum, is called मगंद (magaṃda). His son is प्रमगंद (pramagaṃda). As the son of the sage Kaṇva is called Praskaṇva, the prefix प्र (pra) indicates the sense of son (apatya); so when the prefix प्र (pra) is joined to मगंद (magaṃda), Pramagaṇḍa means the son of Magaṇḍa. Indra is prayed to bring to us the unjustly acquired wealth of such a Pramagaṇḍa.

नैचाशाखं (naicāśākhaṃ)—नीचासु शूद्रयोनिषु उत्पादिता शाखा पुत्रपौत्रादिपरंपरा येन स नीचाशाखः । पतितस्य संबंधि धनं नैचशाखं । तद्धनं नः साधय । एतेषां तद्धनं तव नोपयुज्यते अस्मादायत्तं तु तद्धनं यागादिद्वारा तवोपयुज्यते । तस्मात्तदस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छेति भावः । (nīcāsu śūdrayoniṣu utpāditā śākhā putrapautrādiparaṃparā yena sa nīcāśākhaḥ | patitasya saṃbaṃdhi dhanaṃ naicaśākhaṃ | taddhanaṃ naḥ sādhaya | eteṣāṃ taddhanaṃ tava nopayujyate asmādāyattaṃ tu taddhanaṃ yāgādidvārā tavopayujyate | tasmāttadasmabhyaṃ prayaccheti bhāvaḥ |) The line of sons, grandsons and so on begotten by a Brāhmaṇa or others in low śūdra women is called "low branch". Since they are unfit for upanayana, Vedic study, sacrifice, gifts and other good rites and do not perform them, they are called fallen. Indra is prayed to bring to us also the wealth of such low-branch people, the fallen. For the non-Āryas, Pramagaṇḍas and fallen low-branch people mentioned before do not sacrifice or worship Indra and the other gods, so their cattle and wealth are not offered to Indra and are wasted; but if Indra brings that wealth to us, we shall use the milk of those cattle and their wealth for performing sacrifices and worshipping Indra, so the wealth will become as if useful to Indra. Hence the prayer "bring them to us" is uttered.

Yāska has given this explanation of the Mantra: किं ते कृण्वंति कीकटेषु गावो नाशिरं दुह्रे न तपंति घर्म० ॥ (kiṃ te kṛṇvaṃti kīkaṭeṣu gāvo nāśiraṃ duhre na tapaṃti gharma0 ‖) आ नो भर प्रमगंदस्य वेदो नैचाशाखं मघवन्बंधया नः ॥ (ā no bhara pramagaṃdasya vedo naicāśākhaṃ maghavanbaṃdhayā naḥ ‖)

p. 210

Its explanation is: किं ते कुर्वंति कीकटेषु गावः । कीकटा नाम देशोऽनार्यनिवासः । कीकटाः किंकृताः किं क्रियाभिरिति प्रेप्सा वा । नैव चाशिरं दुह्रे न तपंति घर्म० हर्म्यमा हर नः प्रमगंदस्य धनानि । मगंदः कुसीदी । मांगदो मामागमिष्यतीति च ददाति तदपत्यं प्रमगंदोऽत्यंतकुसीदिकुलीनः । प्रमदको वा योऽयमेवास्ति लोको न पर इति प्रेप्सुः । पंडको वा । पंडकः पंडगः प्रार्दको वा प्रार्दयत्यांडावांडावाणी इव व्रीडयति तस्तंभे । नैचाशाखं नीचाशाखो नीचैः शाखः । शाखाः शक्कोतेः । आणिररणात् । तन्नो मघवन्रंधयेति रध्यतिर्वशगमने ॥ (kiṃ te kurvaṃti kīkaṭeṣu gāvaḥ | kīkaṭā nāma deśo 'nāryanivāsaḥ | kīkaṭāḥ kiṃkṛtāḥ kiṃ kriyābhiriti prepsā vā | naiva cāśiraṃ duhre na tapaṃti gharma0 harmyamā hara naḥ pramagaṃdasya dhanāni | magaṃdaḥ kusīdī | māṃgado māmāgamiṣyatīti ca dadāti tadapatyaṃ pramagaṃdo 'tyaṃtakusīdikulīnaḥ | pramadako vā yo 'yamevāsti loko na para iti prepsuḥ | paṃḍako vā | paṃḍakaḥ paṃḍagaḥ prārdako vā prārdayatyāṃḍāvāṃḍāvāṇī iva vrīḍayati tastaṃbhe | naicāśākhaṃ nīcāśākho nīcaiḥ śākhaḥ | śākhāḥ śakkoteḥ | āṇiraraṇāt | tanno maghavanraṃdhayeti radhyatirvaśagamane ‖) (Ni. 6-32)

That is: the word Kīkaṭa is the name of the country where the non-Ārya earlier inhabitants of this land live. How did these non-Ārya dwellers get the name? "Or किं कृताः (kiṃ kṛtāḥ), किं क्रियाभिरिति प्रेप्सा वा (kiṃ kriyābhiriti prepsā vā)": unbelievers who, neglecting good rites, speak with contempt, "what use are sacrifices and rites?", got the name Kiṅkṛtāḥ, or Kīkaṭāḥ. The milk of cattle among them is not rightly used, because, since they do not sacrifice, their cattle's milk is not of use for sacrifices; it is of no use as the āśira substance to be added to Soma juice; nor are the products made by heating the milk, curd, ghee and the like, fit for sacrifice. Therefore bring to us the cattle among these uncivilized people. If we get those cattle, we shall sacrifice and offer their milk, curd, ghee and so on to Indra and the other gods. Therefore Indra is prayed to give us their cattle and wealth. Further, मगंदः (magaṃdaḥ) means कुसीदी (kusīdī), a merchant whose occupation is lending goods to others and after some time taking back the money with its interest. As the prefix प्र (pra) is joined to मगंद (magaṃda), प्रमगंद (pramagaṃda) means a Magaṇḍa or one of the usurer family; or the prefix प्र (pra) in the sense of excess means one born in an exceedingly bad family. Since he gains money unjustly by taking interest at one-for-two, bring us his wealth also. Or प्रमगंद (pramagaṃda) may mean प्रमदक (pramadaka): one who says, "there is only this visible world, no heaven or other worlds; so merit and sin mean nothing; to be happy now is all; why suffer? it is good to eat, drink and live at ease; hard sacrifices are of no use" (continuing).

p. 211

—such an unbeliever. Or प्रमगंद (pramagaṃda) may mean पंडकः (paṃḍakaḥ), पंडगः (paṃḍagaḥ) or प्रार्दक (prārdaka). पंडक (paṃḍaka) or पंडग (paṃḍaga) is a eunuch, one who is helpless like women. प्रार्दक (prārdaka) is one who behaves like women in dealings and the like, effeminate, shameless. Indra is prayed to bring the wealth of such persons also to us. And those born of upper-class parents among śūdra and other low castes are called low-branch people; since they are fallen and excluded from sacrifices and rites, their wealth is of no use for good rites. Therefore नैचाशाखं धनं (naicāśākhaṃ dhanaṃ): prayer is made that the wealth among such low-class people be brought to us. Here, since the root रध्यति (radhyati) has the sense "bring into one's power", the words मघवन् रंधय (maghavan raṃdhaya) in this Ṛk mean: O Indra, make (the wealth of the people mentioned above) come into our power.

Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒स॒र्प॒रीरम॑तिं॒ बाध॑माना बृ॒हन्मि॑माय ज॒मद॑ग्निदत्ता ।
आ सूर्य॑स्य दुहि॒ता त॑तान॒ श्रवो॑ दे॒वेष्व॒मृत॑मजु॒र्य० ॥

sasarparīramatiṃ bādhamānā bṛhanmimāya jamadagnidattā |
ā sūryasya duhitā tatāna śravo deveṣvamṛtamajurya0 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

ससर्परीः । अमतिं । बाधमाना । बृहत् । मिमाय । जमदग्निदत्ता ।
आ । सूर्यस्य । दुहिता । ततान । श्रवः । देवेषु । अमृतं । अजुर्यं ॥ १५ ॥

sasarparīḥ | amatiṃ | bādhamānā | bṛhat | mimāya | jamadagnidattā |
ā | sūryasya | duhitā | tatāna | śravaḥ | deveṣu | amṛtaṃ | ajuryaṃ ‖ 15 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

ससर्परीद्वृचे प्राहुरितिहासं पुराविदः । सौदासनृपयज्ञे वै वसिष्ठात्मजशक्तिना । विश्वामित्रस्याभिभूतं बलं वाक् च समंततः । वासिष्ठेनाभिभूतः स ह्यवासीदथ गाधिजः । तस्मै ब्राह्मीं तु सौरीं ना नाम्ना वाचं ससर्परीं । सूर्यवेश्मन आहृत्य ददुर्वै जमदग्नयः । कुशिकानां मतिः सा वागमतिं तामपानुदत् ॥ जमदग्निदत्ता जमदग्निभिः प्रज्वलिताग्निभिर्यषिभिरस्मभ्यं दत्तामतिमज्ञानं बाधमाना ससर्परीः सर्वत्र शब्दरूपतया सर्पणशीला वाक् बृहत्प्रभूतं यथा भवति तथा मिमाय । नभसि शब्दं करोति । सैषा सूर्यस्य दुहिता वाग्देवता देवेष्ट्विंद्रादिष्वजुर्यं क्षयरहितममृतममृतलक्षणं श्रवोऽन्नमा ततान । समंतात्स्वाहाकारवाचं तनोति ॥ जमदग्निदत्ता! दाण् दान इत्यस्यनिष्ठायां दो दद्वो-

Gist of the bhāṣya

Those versed in ancient lore tell the story relating to ससर्परी (sasarparī) in this Ṛk: at the sacrifice of King Sudāsa, Śakti, son of Vasiṣṭha, overcame the strength and speech of Viśvāmitra on every side; overcome by the Vāsiṣṭha, the son of Gādhi sank down. The Jamadagnis brought for him from the house of the Sun the Brahma-speech called Sasarpari, of solar nature, and gave it. That was the understanding of the Kuśikas, the speech, and it drove off their lack of understanding. जमदग्निदत्ता (jamadagnidattā): given to us by the Jamadagnis, the sages with blazing fires; अमतिं (amatiṃ) is ignorance; warding it off, ससर्परीः (sasarparīḥ), speech, whose nature is to move everywhere in the form of sound, मिमाय (mimāya) makes sound in the sky abundantly. This same daughter of the Sun, the goddess Speech, spreads among the gods, Indra and others, अजुर्यं (ajuryaṃ) imperishable, अमृतं (amṛtaṃ) of the nature of immortality, श्रवः (śravaḥ) food, in the form of the utterance of svāhā on all sides. The text continues with grammar on जमदग्निदत्ता (jamadagnidattā) (broken off at the end of the window).

p. 212

रिति ददादेशः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वसदप्रकृतिस्वरः । अजुर्युं । ज्ञ वयोहानौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । बहुलं छंदसीत्युत्वं । नञ्सुभ्यामित्यंतोदात्तत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This block holds only the grammatical tail of Sāyaṇa's comment on the preceding Ṛk (the forms जमदग्निदत्ता (jamadagnidattā) and अजुर्युं (ajuryuṃ): the substitution दद (dada) for the root, the accent of the compound, and the accent of अजुर्युं (ajuryuṃ)). It contains no statement of meaning; the Grammar remarks are left out of the Gist.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • जमदग्नि दत्ता (jamadagni dattā)—she who was given by the sages Jamadagni
  • अमतिं (amatiṃ)—ignorance
  • बाधमाना (bādhamānā)—she who destroys
  • ससर्परीः (sasarparīḥ)—she who pervades everywhere in the form of sound
  • बृहत् (bṛhat)—abundantly
  • मिमाय (mimāya)—she who makes sound (in the atmosphere)
  • सूरस्य दुहिता (sūrasya duhitā)—the daughter of Sūrya, the goddess of speech
  • देवेषु (deveṣu)—among the gods, Indra and the others
  • अजुर्यं (ajuryaṃ)—that which is without decay
  • अमृतं (amṛtaṃ)—that which is eternal
  • श्रवः (śravaḥ)—food
  • आ ततान (ā tatāna)—spread out widely
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The goddess of speech, who was given by the sage Jamadagni, who destroys ignorance, who pervades everywhere in the form of sound, who sounds abundantly in the atmosphere, and who is the daughter of Sūrya, has spread widely among the gods, Indra and the others, food that is without decay and eternal.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The daughter of Surya given by Jamadagni gliding everywhere and dissipating ignorance, has emitted a mighty (sound), and has diffused ambrosial imperishable food amongst the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Concerning this Ṛk and the next, ससर्परी (sasarparī), the ancients tell a story:

ससर्परीद्वचे प्राहुरितिहासं पुराविदः । सौदासनृपयज्ञे वै वसिष्ठात्मजशक्तिना ॥ विश्वामित्रस्याभिभूतं बलं वाक्च समंततः । वासिष्ठेनाभिभूतः स ह्यवासीदथ गाधिजः । तस्मै ब्राह्मीं तु सौरीं ना नाम्मा वाचं ससर्परीं । सूर्यवेश्मन आहृत्य ददुर्वै जमदग्नयः । कुशिकानां मतिः सा वागमतिं तामपानुदत् ॥ (sasarparīdvace prāhuritihāsaṃ purāvidaḥ | saudāsanṛpayajñe vai vasiṣṭhātmajaśaktinā ‖ viśvāmitrasyābhibhūtaṃ balaṃ vākca samaṃtataḥ | vāsiṣṭhenābhibhūtaḥ sa hyavāsīdatha gādhijaḥ | tasmai brāhmīṃ tu saurīṃ nā nāmmā vācaṃ sasarparīṃ | sūryaveśmana āhṛtya dadurvai jamadagnayaḥ | kuśikānāṃ matiḥ sā vāgamatiṃ tāmapānudat ‖)

The ancients tell a story concerning these Ṛks. In former times, when the sage Viśvāmitra was conducting the sacrifice of a king named Sudāsa, Śakti, a son of Vasiṣṭha,

p. 213

paralysed Viśvāmitra's strength and his power of speech. Because of this Viśvāmitra, the son of Gādhi, became devoid of strength and enveloped in ignorance, and had to remain silent, unable to utter mantras and the like. Then the aged sages called Jamadagnis brought from the abode of the Sun (from the orb of the Sun) the speech-power (vāk), endowed with the radiance of Brahman and known as the daughter of the Sun, and gave it to the sage Viśvāmitra. Through it Viśvāmitra and his kinsmen the Kuśikas were freed from the ignorance that had enveloped them and regained good understanding, knowledge, and the power of speech, or of reciting mantras. This is the matter described in this Ṛk and in the next.

जमदग्नि दत्ता (jamadagni dattā)—जमदग्निभिः प्रज्वलिताग्निभिर्यषिभिः (jamadagnibhiḥ prajvalitāgnibhiryaṣibhiḥ). The Bhāṣyakāra explains the word Jamadagni as sages who take care that the fire in the sacrifice does not go out but always burns well.

For the word Jamadagni, Yāska says जमदग्नयः प्रजमिताग्नयो वा प्रज्वलिताग्नयो वा तैरभिहुतो भवति (jamadagnayaḥ prajamitāgnayo vā prajvalitāgnayo vā tairabhihuto bhavati) (Ni. 7-24). That is, he gives the etymology that the word means those who have abundant fire, or those who kindle fires and make them burn well, or those who pray to Agni, "Blaze well in this sacrificial rite."

सूर्यस्य दुहिता (sūryasya duhitā)—वाग्देवता (vāgdevatā). The Bhāṣyakāra explains it as the goddess of speech, the daughter of Sūrya.

The chief sense of ससर्परीः अमतिं बाधमाना जमदग्नि दत्ता सूर्यस्य दुहिता बृहत् मिमाय देवेषु अजुर्यं अमृतं आ ततान (sasarparīḥ amatiṃ bādhamānā jamadagni dattā sūryasya duhitā bṛhat mimāya deveṣu ajuryaṃ amṛtaṃ ā tatāna) is this: the goddess of speech, the daughter of Sūrya, all-pervading, brought by the sage Jamadagnis, removed the ignorance of Viśvāmitra and the others and sounded in the atmosphere; that is, she uttered speech in the form of the svāhā-call, and she also brought and provided for Viśvāmitra and the others the undecaying, ambrosial food that was with Indra and the other gods.

Ṛk 16

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒स॒र्प॒रीर॑भर॒त्तूय॑मे॒भ्यो 5 धि॒ श्रवः॒ पांच॑जन्यासु कृ॒ष्टिषु॑।
सा प॒क्ष्या॒३॒॑ति नव्य॒मायु॒र्दधा॑ना॒ यां मे॑ पलस्ति जमद॒ग्नयो॑ ॒ ददुः ॥ १६ ॥

sasarparīrabharattūyamebhyo 5 dhi śravaḥ pāṃcajanyāsu kṛṣṭiṣu|
sā pakṣyāti navyamāyurdadhānā yāṃ me palasti jamadagnayo
daduḥ ‖ 16 ‖

p. 214

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

स सर्परीः । अभरत् । तूयं । विभ्यः । अधि । श्रवः । पांचजन्यासु । कृष्णिषु ।
सा । पक्ष्या । नव्यं । आयुः । दधाना । यां । मे! पलस्तिजमदग्नयः । ददुः ॥ १६ ॥

sa sarparīḥ | abharat | tūyaṃ | vibhyaḥ | adhi | śravaḥ | pāṃcajanyāsu | kṛṣṇiṣu |
sā | pakṣyā | navyaṃ | āyuḥ | dadhānā | yāṃ | me! palastijamadagnayaḥ | daduḥ ‖ 16 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

ससर्परीः सर्वत्र गद्यपद्यात्मकत्वेन सर्पणशीला वाग्गेवता पांचजन्यासु कृष्टषु। निषादपंचमाश्चत्वारो वर्णा: पंचजनाः। तत्संबंधिनीषु प्रजासु यच्छवोऽन्नं विद्यते तन्नोऽस्मभ्यमधि अधिकं यथा भवति तथा तूयं क्षिप्रमभरत्।भरतु। संपादयतु। पलस्तिजमदग्नयः पलस्तयः पलिता दीर्घायुषो जमदग्नयो मुनयो यां वाचं सूर्यादाहृत्य मे मह्यं ददुरदधुः पक्ष्या पक्षस्यपक्षादिनिर्वाहकस्य सूर्यस्य दुहिता सा वाक् नव्यं नवतरमायुरन्नं जीवनं वा दधाना मम कुर्वाणा भवतु ॥ पांचजन्यासु । बहिर्देवपंचजनेभ्यश्चति वक्तव्यमिति इाप्रत्ययः। इत्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पक्ष्या । पक्षे भवा । दिगादित्वाद्यत् । तित्स्वरितः । नव्यं । नवशब्दाद्वस्वादित्वात्स्वार्थिको यत् । पलस्तिजमदग्नयः पलस्तयो जमदग्नयः । कर्मधारय समासः । समासस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

ससर्परीः (sasarparīḥ) is the goddess of speech, who moves everywhere in the form of prose and verse. पांचजन्यासु कृष्टिषु (pāṃcajanyāsu kṛṣṭiṣu): the "five peoples" are the four classes (varṇas) with the Niṣāda as the fifth; among the subjects belonging to them, whatever food there is, let her quickly bring that to us, in greater measure (अधि (adhi)). पलस्तिजमदग्नयः (palastijamadagnayaḥ) are the grey-haired, long-lived sages Jamadagnis, who fetched the Speech from the Sun and gave her to me. पक्ष्या (pakṣyā) is the daughter of Sūrya, who manages the fortnight (pakṣa) and the like; may that Speech, bestowing on me newer life, or food, or livelihood (नव्यं आयुः (navyaṃ āyuḥ)), be mine.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • ससर्परीः (sasarparīḥ)—the goddess of speech, who spreads everywhere in forms of prose and verse
  • पांचजन्यासु (pāṃcajanyāsu)—fivefold
  • कृष्टिषु (kṛṣṭiṣu)—to the people
  • श्रवः (śravaḥ)—food
  • अधि (adhi)—abundantly
  • तूयं (tūyaṃ)—quickly
  • अभरत् (abharat)—may she procure and give
  • पलस्तिजमदग्नयः (palastijamadagnayaḥ)—the aged Jamadagnis
  • यां (yāṃ)—which goddess of speech
  • मे (me)—to me
  • ददुः (daduḥ)—offered
  • पक्ष्या सा (pakṣyā sā)—that goddess of speech, the daughter of the Sun
  • नव्यं (navyaṃ)—newer
  • आयुः (āyuḥ)—food, or life
  • दधाना (dadhānā)—may she go on giving
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the goddess of speech, who spreads everywhere in forms of prose and verse, procure food abundantly and quickly for the fivefold peoples. May that goddess of speech, the daughter of the Sun, whom the aged Jamadagnis offered to me, go on giving newer life.

p. 215

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May she, gilding everywhere, quickly bring us food (suited) to the five races of men: may she, the daughter of the sun whom the grey-haired Jamadagnis gave to me, (be) the bestower of new life. NOTE

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Viśvāmitra expresses his gratitude for the food and the rest which the goddess of speech had granted in the previous Ṛk, and prays to the goddess of speech.

पंचजन्यासु कृष्टिषु (paṃcajanyāsu kṛṣṭiṣu): The word कृष्टयः (kṛṣṭayaḥ) is read among the twenty-five words denoting men, such as मनुष्याः (manuṣyāḥ) and नराः (narāḥ) (Ni. 3-7). पंच कृष्टीनां (paṃca kṛṣṭīnāṃ) means पंच जनानां (paṃca janānāṃ). The Bhāṣyakāra explains this as निषादपंचमानां (niṣādapaṃcamānāṃ); Skandasvāmin as क्षितीनां मनुष्यजातीनां गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा इत्येतासां (kṣitīnāṃ manuṣyajātīnāṃ gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā ityetāsāṃ); and Veṅkaṭamādhava as मनुष्याणां पंचानां क्षितीनां निवसतां गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीति पंचत्वं (manuṣyāṇāṃ paṃcānāṃ kṣitīnāṃ nivasatāṃ gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsīti paṃcatvaṃ). According to Sāyaṇa's view, क्षितीनां (kṣitīnāṃ) means the people of five classes fit to dwell on the earth: Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, Śūdra and Niṣāda. Niṣādas are people who do not belong to the four classes beginning with the Brāhmaṇa and who live only by hunting animals. The Goṇḍas, Kolas, Bhillas and others, the earlier inhabitants of this country, belong to this class. They still live, in very small numbers, only in a few places such as the Central Provinces. The words पंच जनाः (paṃca janāḥ) and पंचकृष्टीः (paṃcakṛṣṭīḥ) occur in many places in the Ṛgveda— NOTE

That is, some say that the five peoples are five kinds of beings: Gandharvas, Pitṛs, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas. The opinion of Upamanyu and others is that the five are the four classes beginning with the Brāhmaṇa together with the hunter class called Niṣāda (Sāyaṇa has approved this). The Nairuktas say that Niṣādas are those who kill animals, or that they are so called because sin is full in them. Besides, there may have been five principal tribes at that time; the poet may have had this in mind and said पंच क्षितीनां (paṃca kṣitīnāṃ). In any case it is clear that even in the time of Yāska, the author of the Nirukta, there was a difference of opinion on this matter.

  1. [Yāska explains the five peoples:] देवा मनुष्याः पितरः पशवः पक्षिणश्चति पंच जनाः (devā manuṣyāḥ pitaraḥ paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaścati paṃca janāḥ): the five kinds are the gods, men, Pitṛs, animals and birds; and, secondly,

p. 216

  1. चत्वारो वर्णाः निषादपंचमाः पंच जना इत्यन्ये (catvāro varṇāḥ niṣādapaṃcamāḥ paṃca janā ityanye): the people of the four classes together with the Niṣādas, as another explanation. For both these meanings the authority of Vedic texts can be shown. One may first examine the etymology of the word क्षिति (kṣiti), and afterwards consider what meaning of पंचक्षिति (paṃcakṣiti) can be given in the present context.

क्षितीनां (kṣitīnāṃ): Sāyaṇa explains: क्षियंति निवसंति गच्छंति वा क्षितयो मनुष्याः (kṣiyaṃti nivasaṃti gacchaṃti vā kṣitayo manuṣyāḥ)—they dwell or they move about; therefore this epithet belongs to men. The author of the Nirukta has read the word क्षिति (kṣiti) among the twenty-five names of man beginning with नरः (naraḥ) (Ni. 3-7).

अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋतुवा । स वृत्रहा सनयो विश्ववेदाः पर्षद्विश्वाति दुरिता गृणंतं । (agnirnetā bhaga iva kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ deva ṛtupā ṛtuvā | sa vṛtrahā sanayo viśvavedāḥ parṣadviśvāti duritā gṛṇaṃtaṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-28-4). In such Ṛks, when the difference between men and the subjects belonging to the gods is shown, the word क्षिति (kṣiti) indicates men, the subjects of the earth. But in the present Ṛk it cannot be said precisely that earthly men alone are meant, because Indra's wealth pervades the whole of earth and atmosphere.

न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता आपश्चन शवसो अंशमापुः । स प्ररिक्वा त्वक्षसा क्ष्मो दिवश्च मरुत्वान्नो भवत्स्वंद्र ऊती । (na yasya devā devatā na martā āpaścana śavaso aṃśamāpuḥ | sa prarikvā tvakṣasā kṣmo divaśca marutvānno bhavatsvaṃdra ūtī |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-15). In such Ṛks it is described that the power of Indra, who is divine in nature and endowed with the quality of giving and the like, surpasses the power of all others in the world, that neither gods nor men could reach its end, and that Indra with his enemy-destroying and majestic power makes earth and heaven shine together. Since in the present Ṛk also Indra's wealth is described as all-pervading, it cannot be said that पंचजन्यासु (paṃcajanyāsu) means merely the group of four classes together with the Niṣāda as fifth. In this matter the author of the Nirukta does not state his own view but reports only the opinions of others.

पंचजना (paṃcajanā) “मम होत्रं जुषध्वं (mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ)” गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा आसुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः । (gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā āsurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ |) (Ni. 3-8). He has reported only the opinions of others: that some hold the five-fold groups to be Gandharvas, Pitṛs, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas, and that Upamanyu and others hold that the five peoples are the four classes beginning with the Brāhmaṇa together with the fifth group called Niṣādas.

p. 217

Formerly, when all the gods prayed to Agni to accept the oblation offered in the sacrifice for them and to distribute it to all, Agni agreed, saying:

तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुरा अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं । (tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4).

The author of the Bṛhaddevatā quotes this sentence, which gives the answer "Let the five peoples together enjoy this oblation," and shows and discusses the differences of opinion about the "five peoples."

प्रत्युवाचाथ तानग्निर्विश्वेदेवा यदूच मां । तत्करिष्ये जुषंतां तु होत्रं पंचजना मम ॥ (pratyuvācātha tānagnirviśvedevā yadūca māṃ | tatkariṣye juṣaṃtāṃ tu hotraṃ paṃcajanā mama ‖) (Bṛ. De. 7-66).

In this verse he states the answer Agni gave to the gods, and then explains the word पंचजन (paṃcajana).

शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः । उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते पंचजनाः स्मृताः ॥ (śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇaścāgnirete paṃcajanāḥ smṛtāḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 7-67).

That is, the fire at the entrance of the hall, the consecrated Āhavanīya fire, the Gārhapatya fire, which is the son of the sacrificer, and the southern and northern fires: these five kinds of fires are traditionally reckoned as the five classes. Besides this view,

मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ (manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 7-68).

According to the first opinion the serpents and Rākṣasas form one group; according to the second, the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas form one group.

यास्कौपमन्यवावेतानाहतुः पंच वै जनान् । निषादपंचमान्वर्णान् मन्यते शाकटायनः ॥ (yāskaupamanyavāvetānāhatuḥ paṃca vai janān | niṣādapaṃcamānvarṇān manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 7-69).

In this verse the author of the Bṛhaddevatā says that Yāska's view is the first. But in the Nirukta only the views of others are stated; Yāska has not given his own view precisely. Probably he may have accepted that one.

p. 218

(The Special Topics of the preceding Ṛk continue.)

ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते । (ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate |) (Bṛ. De. 7-20) It is the view of Śākapūṇi that the four priests beginning with the Hotṛ, together with the sacrificer, make up the group of five.

चक्षुःश्रोत्रं मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः । (cakṣuḥśrotraṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ |) गंधर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा ॥ (gaṃdharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā ‖) सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयंते हैतरेयके ॥ (sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyaṃte haitareyake ‖) (Bṛ. De. 7-21, 22) According to the spiritualists, the five peoples are the eye, the ear, the mind, speech and the breath. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa explains them as the Gandharvas and so on (Ai. Brā. 3-31-5). The Bṛhaddevatā, in explaining that Agni gave the gods the answer "let such five peoples also enjoy the oblation", likewise records these differences of opinion.

पक्ष्या (pakṣyā)—पक्षे भवा । (pakṣe bhavā |) Because he carries out the divisions of the year such as month and fortnight, the Sun is called "pakṣī". Here the instrumental case of पक्ष्या (pakṣyā) is said to have the sense of the genitive.

पलस्तिजमदग्नयः (palastijamadagnayaḥ)—पलस्तयः पलितदीर्घायुषो जमदग्नयो मुनयः । (palastayaḥ palitadīrghāyuṣo jamadagnayo munayaḥ |) The meaning is: the sages Jamadagni, long-lived, that is, aged men who have lived for a very long time. We explained the derivation of the word Jamadagni in the Special Topics of the previous Ṛk.

The sage Jamadagni is one of the seven sages. The hymns seen by Jamadagni in the Ṛgveda are Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-16 to 18 and 10-137-6, four Ṛks in all. The hymns seen by Jamadagni Bhārgava, that is, Jamadagni the son of Bhṛgu: Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-101 (16 Ṛks), 9-62 (30 Ṛks), 9-65 (30 Ṛks), 9-67 (3 Ṛks, verses 16–18); in all 79 Ṛks. Besides, a hymn seen by the two sages Jamadagni and Viśvāmitra together stands in the tenth Maṇḍala, Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-167 (4 Ṛks); in its last verse (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-167-4) the names of Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni are mentioned together. Further, Jamadagni's name is mentioned in Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-79-3; 9-97-51; Atharvaveda 2-32-3; 4-29-3; 5-28-7; 6-137-1; 18-3-15, 16; Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-12-4; 3-1-7-3; 3-52; 5-2-10-5; 4-11-3; Mai. Saṃ. 2-7-19; 4-2-9; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 16-19; 20-9; Vā. Saṃ. 3-62; 13-56; Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 9-4-14; 13-5-15; 21-10-5 to 7; 22-7-2; Ai. Brā. 7-16; Śa. Brā. 13-2-2-14; Tai. Ā. 1-9-7; Bṛ. U. 2-2-4;

p. 219

Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa 3-3-11; 4-3-1, and other places. In all these places Jamadagni is regarded as a friend of Viśvāmitra. Only in one place in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā is he indicated as an opponent of Vasiṣṭha.

The distinction of this Jamadagni is that he is famed as having played the part of chief priest in a special sacrifice called Caturātra, performed over four days. This is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā beginning पुष्टिकामश्च तूरात्रॆणायजत (puṣṭikāmaśca tūrātrèṇāyajata)NOTE and in the Pañcaviṃśa BrāhmaṇaNOTE (21-10-5 to 7). In the Atharvaveda (Atharvaveda 2-32-3; 6-137-1) Jamadagni is mentioned along with the sages Atri, Kaṇva, Asita and Vītahavya. As told in the story of Śunaśśepa in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 7-16), in Śunaśśepa's sacrifice Jamadagni played the part of the priest called Adhvaryu.

Ṛk 17

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स्थि॒रौ गावौ॑ भवतां वी॒ळुरक्षो॒ मेषा वि व॑र्हि॒ मा यु॒गं ॑ वि शारि ।
इंद्रः॑ पात॒ल्ये॑ ददतां॒ शरी॑तो॒ररि॑ष्टनेमे अ॒भि नः॑ सचस्व ॥१७॥

sthirau gāvau bhavatāṃ vīḷurakṣo meṣā vi varhi mā yugaṃ
vi śāri |
iṃdraḥ pātalye dadatāṃ śarītorariṣṭaneme abhi naḥ sacasva ‖17‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

स्थिरौ । गावौ । भवतां । वीळुः । अक्षः । मा । ईषा । वि । वर्हि । मा । युगं वि शारि ।
इंद्रः । पातल्येऽति । ददतां । शरीतोः । अरिष्टनेमे । अभि । नः । सचस्व ॥ १७ ॥

sthirau | gāvau | bhavatāṃ | vīḷuḥ | akṣaḥ | mā | īṣā | vi | varhi | mā | yugaṃ vi śāri |
iṃdraḥ | pātalye 'ti | dadatāṃ | śarītoḥ | ariṣṭaneme | abhi | naḥ | sacasva ‖ 17 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

राज्ञः सुदासो यज्ञेऽवभृथं कृत्वा यज्ञशालातो निर्गंतुमिच्छन् रथेऽश्वादिकं युंजानो विश्वामित्रो रथांगानि स्तौति । गावौ । गच्छत इति गावावश्च । स्थिरौ भवतां । अक्षश्च वीळुर्दृढो भवतु । ईषा दंडश्च मा वि वर्हि । वृद्यो मा भवतु । युगं च मा वि शारि । विशीर्णं मा भवतु । इंद्रः पातल्ये पतनशीले कीलके शरीतोर्विशरणात्पाक् ददतां । धारयतु । हे अरिष्टनेमे अहिंसितप्रधिविशिष्ट हे रथ नोऽस्मानभि अभिमुख्येन सचस्व । संगतो भव ॥ वि वर्हि । वृहि वृद्धौ । विपूर्वो वृहिर्विनाशे वर्तते । आस्मात्कर्मकर्तरि लुजि चिन् भावकर्म-

Gist of the bhāṣya

At King Sudās's sacrifice Viśvāmitra, having performed the concluding bath (avabhṛtha) and wishing to leave the sacrificial hall, yokes the horses and the rest to the chariot and praises the parts of the chariot. गावौ (gāvau) are the two that go (gacchataḥ); may the two be steady. May the axle be firm and strong. May the pole (īṣā) not be वृद्यो (vṛdyo) [sic as in the block]; may the yoke not split, not be shattered. May Indra hold the peg (pātalya), which is prone to fall, before it breaks. O chariot with unharmed felly (ariṣṭanemi), be joined with us, facing us. The rest of the block begins the derivation of वि वर्हि (vi varhi) from the root वृहि (vṛhi) (to grow), meaning destruction when preceded by वि (vi) (grammatical).

p. 220

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

षोरिति चिण् । चिणो लुगिति तप्रत्ययस्य लुक् । निघातः । युगं । युगशब्द उंभादिषु रथाद्युपकरणेऽर्थे घइंतत्वेन निपातनादगुणत्वं । तत्र पाठादंतोदात्तत्वं । शारि । शृ हिंसायामित्यस्य लुजि रूपं । अरिष्टनेमे । पादादित्वात् षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The block contains only grammatical notes (on वि वर्हि (vi varhi), युगं (yugaṃ), शारि (śāri), अरिष्टनेमे (ariṣṭaneme)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • गावः (gāvaḥ)—the horses
  • स्थिरौ (sthirau)—steady
  • भवतां (bhavatāṃ)—let them be
  • अक्षः (akṣaḥ)—the axle
  • वीळुः (vīḷuḥ)—let it be firm
  • ईषा (īṣā)—the pole in the middle of the chariot
  • मा वि वर्हि (mā vi varhi)—let it not be destroyed
  • युगं च (yugaṃ ca)—the yoke also
  • मा वि शारि (mā vi śāri)—let it not split
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • पातल्ये (pātalye)—the pegs of the chariot
  • शरीतोः (śarītoḥ)—before they split
  • ददतां (dadatāṃ)—let him hold
  • अरिष्टनेमे (ariṣṭaneme)—O chariot with unharmed felly
  • नः (naḥ)—us
  • अभि (abhi)—all around
  • सचस्व (sacasva)—keep joined
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the horses of our chariot be steady. Let its axle be firm. Let the pole in the middle of the chariot not be destroyed, and the yoke not split. Before the pegs of the chariot split, let Indra hold them. O chariot with unharmed felly, keep joined with us.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May the horses be steady, the axle be strong, the pole be not defective: the yoke not be rotten; may Indra preserve the two yoke-pins from decay .NOTE car with the uninjured fellies, be ready for us.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the close of King Sudās's sacrifice Viśvāmitra takes the avabhṛtha bath, prepares to leave the sacrificial hall, yokes horses to the chariot, and praises the chariot's parts, that is, wheel, felly, yoke and so on.

गावौ स्थिरौ भवतां (gāvau sthirau bhavatāṃ)—गवावश् (gavāvaś). Here the horses are addressed by the word "go" (cow). Hence गावौ (gāvau) means the two horses yoked to the chariot. The wish is expressed that they be steady, free from fear.

वीळु अक्ष (vīḷu akṣa)—the axle of the chariot, that is, the axle-beam between the two wheels. May it be firm, so that it does not break under the weight on a journey.

ईषा मा वि वर्हि (īṣā mā vi varhi)—दंडश्च व्यृद्वो मा भवतु । (daṃḍaśca vyṛdvo mā bhavatu |) The pole in the middle of the chariot, that is, the long beam fitted with its fastening, is not to be spoilt.

p. 221

मा युगं वि शारि (mā yugaṃ vi śāri)—विशीर्णं मा भवतु । (viśīrṇaṃ mā bhavatu |) Let the yoke not split apart.

इंद्रः पातल्ये शरीतो ददतां (iṃdraḥ pātalye śarīto dadatāṃ)—पतनशीले कीलके विशरणात् प्राक् इंद्रः धारयतु । (patanaśīle kīlake viśaraṇāt prāk iṃdraḥ dhārayatu |) If the pegs are likely to break and fall, may Indra, before they break and fall, hold them firmly so that they do not fall.

अरिष्टनेमे नः अभि सचस्व (ariṣṭaneme naḥ abhi sacasva)—अहिंसितप्रधिविशिष्ट हे रथ अस्मानाभिमुख्येन संगतो भव । (ahiṃsitapradhiviśiṣṭa he ratha asmānābhimukhyena saṃgato bhava |) O chariot with wheels that harm no one, make ready to depart and come and stand in front of us.

Ṛk 18

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

बलं॑ धेहि त॒नूषु॑ नो॒ बल॑मिंद्रान॒ळुत्सु॑ नः ।
बलं॑ तो॒काय॒ तन॑याय जी॒वसे॒ त्वं हि ब॑ल॒दा असि॑ ॥ १८ ॥

balaṃ dhehi tanūṣu no balamiṃdrānaḷutsu naḥ |
balaṃ tokāya tanayāya jīvase tvaṃ hi baladā asi ‖ 18 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

बलं । धेहि । तनूषु । नः । बलं । इंद्र । अनळुत्सु । नः ।
बलं । तोकाय । तनयाय । जीवसे । त्वं । हि । बलदाः । असि ॥ १८ ॥

balaṃ | dhehi | tanūṣu | naḥ | balaṃ | iṃdra | anaḷutsu | naḥ |
balaṃ | tokāya | tanayāya | jīvase | tvaṃ | hi | baladāḥ | asi ‖ 18 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र नोऽस्माकं तनूषु शरीरेषु बलं धेहि । नोऽस्मत्संबंधिरथवाहेष्टनळुत्सु बलं धेहि । तोकाय पुत्राय तनयाय पौत्राय च जीवसे चिरं जीवनाय बलमायुर्विधेहि । एतादृशं दातृत्वं कुत इत्यत आह। त्वं बलदाः। बलं ददातीति बलदाः । असि हि । सर्वेषु लोकेषु प्रसिद्धोऽसि खलु ॥ अनळुत्तु । वह प्रापणे । अनसि वहेः क्विबनसो दश्चेति क्विप् । अनसः सकारस्य दत्वं । वहेय्यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । वसुस्रंसुध्वंस्वनडुहां द इति हकारस्य दत्वं । कृदुत्तरस्वरः । असि । हियोगादनिघातः । सिपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, place strength in our bodies; place strength in the animals that draw our chariot (अनळुत्सु (anaḷutsu)); for our son and grandson, for long life, bestow strength and long life. Whence such giving? He says: you are बलदाः (baladāḥ), giver of strength; for you are renowned thus in all the worlds. The remainder explains अनळुत्सु (anaḷutsu) from the root वह (vaha) and the accents of असि (asi) (grammatical).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • नः (naḥ)—our
  • तनूषु (tanūṣu)—in the bodies
  • बलं (balaṃ)—strength
  • धेहि (dhehi)—give
  • नः (naḥ)—our
  • अनळुत्सु (anaḷutsu)—to the vehicles (the horses); बलं (balaṃ)—give strength

p. 222

  • तोकाय (tokāya)—to the son
  • तनयाय (tanayāya)—to the grandson
  • जीवसे (jīvase)—for a long life
  • बलं (balaṃ)—give strength
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • बलदाः असि हि (baladāḥ asi hi)—it is well known that you are the giver of strength
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, fill our bodies with strength. Give strength to our vehicles. Make strength for our sons and grandsons, that they may be long-lived. It is well known that you are the giver of strength to all.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Give strength, Indra, to our bodies; give strength to our vehicles; (give) strength to our sons and grandsons; that they may live (long); for you are the giver of strength,

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is prayed that Indra, being mighty, give strength on the journey to us, to the sons, grandsons and others who are with us, and to our vehicles, horses and the rest, and protect them from accidents and the like.

Ṛk 19

अ॒भि व्य॑यस्व खदि॒रस्य॒ सार॒मोजो॑ धेहि स्पंद॒ने शिं॒शपा॑यां।
अक्ष॑ वीळो पीळित वी॒ळय॑स्व॒ मा यामा॑द॒स्मादव॑ जीहिपो
नः ॥

naḥ ‖

अभि । व्ययस्व । खदिरस्य । सारं । ओजः । धेहि । स्पंदने । शिंशपायां ।
अक्ष । वीळो इति । वीळित । वीळयस्व । मा । यामात् । अस्मात् । अव । जीहिपः ।
नः ॥ १९ ॥

abhi | vyayasva | khadirasya | sāraṃ | ojaḥ | dhehi | spaṃdane | śiṃśapāyāṃ |
akṣa | vīḷo iti | vīḷita | vīḷayasva | mā | yāmāt | asmāt | ava | jīhipaḥ |
naḥ ‖ 19 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र खदिरस्य सारं । सारेण हि आणिः क्रियते । तं खदिरस्य सारभूतमाणिमभि व्ययस्व । अभितस्तत्तत्सा नेषु दार्ढार्थं निधेहि । स्पंदने रथस्य गमने सति शिंतपायां शिंशपाख्यदारुनिर्मिते रथस्य फलक ओजो धेहि । दार्ढ्यं कुरु । हे

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, खदिरस्य सारं (khadirasya sāraṃ): the linchpin (āṇi) is made of heartwood; fix that linchpin of khadira heartwood all about, in the several places, for firmness. When the chariot is in motion (spandana), give strength to the board (phalaka) of the chariot made of the wood called śiṃśapā; make it firm. O

p. 223

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

वीळो दृढ वीळितास्माभिर्दृढीकृत हे अक्ष वीळयस्व । त्वं दृढो भव । यद्वास्मान् दृढीकुरु । यामाद्धच्छतोस्माद्रथान्नोऽस्मान् माव जीहिपः । मा पीपतः ॥ खदिरस्य । अजिरशितिरेत्यादिना किरच् प्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातनादंतोदात्तः । वीळित । वीळयतेर्ण्यंतस्य निष्ठायामिडागमः । निष्ठायां सेटि! पा. ६-४-५२। इति णेर्लुक् । वीळियस्व । आमंत्रितस्याविद्यमानत्वेन पादादित्वादनिघातः । यामात् । या प्रापण इत्यस्मादर्तिस्तु सुहुसृ इत्यादिना मन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । जीहिपः । ओहाक् त्यागे । ण्यंतस्य लुजि चङि रूपं । अकारस्येकारश्चांदसः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) O firm axle, made firm by us, make yourself firm; or else make us firm. From this chariot as it goes, do not let us fall (मा पीपतः (mā pīpataḥ)). The rest is grammatical (खदिरस्य (khadirasya), वीळित (vīḷita), वीळियस्व (vīḷiyasva), यामात् (yāmāt), जीहिपः (jīhipaḥ)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • खदिरस्य (khadirasya)—of the khadira tree
  • सारं (sāraṃ)—the linchpin made of its heartwood
  • अभि व्ययस्य (abhi vyayasya)—fix so that it be firm
  • स्पंदने (spaṃdane)—while the chariot goes
  • शिंशपायां (śiṃśapāyāṃ)—to the boards made of śiṃśapā wood
  • ओजः (ojaḥ)—strength
  • धेहि (dhehi)—give
  • वीळः (vīḷaḥ)—firm
  • अक्ष (akṣa)—O axle
  • वीळितः (vīḷitaḥ)—since fixed firmly by us
  • वीळयस्प (vīḷayaspa)—be firm yourself
  • यामात् (yāmāt)—when we are going in the chariot
  • नः (naḥ)—us
  • मा अव जीहिपः (mā ava jīhipaḥ)—do not make us fall down
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, fix the linchpin, made of the heartwood of the khadira tree, so that it is firm. While the chariot is going, give strength to the boards made of śiṃśapā wood. O firm axle, since you have been fixed firmly by us, be firm yourself. When we are going in the chariot, do not make us fall down.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Fix firmly the substance of the Khayar (axle), give solidity to the shishu (floor) of the car : strong axle, strongly fixed by us, be strong ; cast us not from out of our conveyance.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

इंद्र खदिरस्य सारं अभि व्ययस्व (iṃdra khadirasya sāraṃ abhi vyayasva)—खदिरस्य सारभूतमाणिं अभितस्तत्तत्स्थानेषु दार्ढार्थ्यर्थं निधेहि । (khadirasya sārabhūtamāṇiṃ abhitastattatsthāneṣu dārḍhārthyarthaṃ nidhehi |) The ends of the axle fitted into the holes at the middle of the wheels are called linchpins (āṇi). If the wheel comes off from this linchpin, the chariot falls apart. Therefore the prayer is: with the ends of the axle-beam, made strong of khadira wood, make the chariot wheels stand firm so that they do not slip off.

स्पंदने शिंशपायां ओजः धेहि (spaṃdane śiṃśapāyāṃ ojaḥ dhehi)—रथस्य गमने सति शिंशपाख्यदारुनिर्मिते रथस्य फलक ओजो धेहि । (rathasya gamane sati śiṃśapākhyadārunirmite rathasya phalaka ojo dhehi |) दार्ढ्यं कुरु (dārḍhyaṃ kuru). Make the boards of śiṃśapā wood in the chariot stay firm, neither shaking nor breaking, while the chariot goes fast.

p. 224

In the same way, the prayer that the axle-tree too (akṣa) should be firm and not let us fall while the chariot is travelling has been explained.

Ṛk 20

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

आ॒युम॒स्मान्वन॒स्पति॒र्मा च॒ हा मा च॑ रीरिषत् ।
स्व॒स्त्या गृ॒हेभ्य॒ आव॒सा आ वि॒मोच॑नात् ॥ २० ॥

āyumasmānvanaspatirmā ca hā mā ca rīriṣat |
svastyā gṛhebhya āvasā ā vimocanāt ‖ 20 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अयं । अस्मान् । वनस्पतिः । मा । च । हाः । मा । च । रिरिषत् ।
स्वस्ति । आ । गृहेभ्यः । आ । अवस्यै । आ । विमोचनात् ॥ २० ॥

ayaṃ | asmān | vanaspatiḥ | mā | ca | hāḥ | mā | ca | ririṣat |
svasti | ā | gṛhebhyaḥ | ā | avasyai | ā | vimocanāt ‖ 20 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यजमान आत्मनः श्रेय आशास्ते । वनस्पतिर्वनस्पतिनिर्मितोऽयं रथो रथारूढानस्मान् मा च हाः । मा त्याक्षीत् । किंच मा रीरिषत् । आस्मान् मा विनाशयतु । किंचा गृहेभ्यः । यावद्गृहान् प्राप्नुयाम तावदस्मभ्यं स्वस्ति भवतु । तथावसै । पंचम्यर्थे चतुर्थि । यावद्रथवेगावसानं तावत् । आ विमोचनात् । यावद्रथयोजिताश्वविमोचनं तावत् स्वस्ति भवतु ॥ हाः । ओहाक् त्यागे ; लुजि मंत्रे घसेत्यादिना सिचो लुक् । पुरुषव्यत्ययः । चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निघातः । रीरिषत् । रिष हिंसायामित्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लुजि चजि रूपं । द्वितीयत्वान्निघातः । गृहेभ्यः । ग्रहेर्गेहे क इति कः । पंचम्यपाङ्परिभिरिति पंचमी । अवसै । षोऽंतकर्मणि । क्विप् । चतुर्थैकवचन आतो लोपाभावश्चांदसः । वृद्धिः । एकादेशस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer asks for his own welfare. The lord of the forest (वनस्पतिः (vanaspatiḥ)) is this chariot, made of wood: may it not abandon (हाः (hāḥ), from the root ओहाक् (ohāk), to leave) us who are mounted on it. May it not harm (रीरिषत् (rīriṣat)) us, that is, may it not destroy us. Further, until we reach our homes (गृहेभ्यः (gṛhebhyaḥ)) let there be well-being for us. Likewise अवसै (avasai): the dative stands in the sense of the ablative; "until the end of the chariot's speed". आ विमोचनात् (ā vimocanāt): until the unyoking of the horses harnessed to the chariot, let there be well-being.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • वनस्पतिः (vanaspatiḥ)—made of wood
  • अयं (ayaṃ)—this chariot
  • अस्मान् (asmān)—us
  • मा च हाः (mā ca hāḥ)—may it not abandon (not neglect)
  • मा च रीरिषत् (mā ca rīriṣat)—may it not harm
  • आ गृहेभ्यः (ā gṛhebhyaḥ)—until we reach home
  • स्वस्ति (svasti)—may it be well
  • आ अवस्यै (ā avasyai)—until the chariot's travelling ends, may it be well with us
  • आ विमोचनात् (ā vimocanāt)—until the horse is unyoked from the chariot, may it be well with us

p. 225

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this chariot, made of the lord of the forest, not abandon us. May it not harm us. Until we reach home, may it be well with us. Until the chariot's travelling ends, may it be well with us. Until the horse is unyoked from the chariot, may it be well with us.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May this lord of the forest never desert us nor do us harm : may we travel prosperously home until the stopping (of the car), until the unharness- ing (of the steeds).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here the chariot is called by the word vanaspati, because the chariot is made of wood (vanaspati = tree). The prayer is stated that such a chariot may bring us good fortune, so that no kind of trouble befalls us on our journey until we reach our home.

Ṛk 21

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इंद्रो॒तिभि॑र्बहु॒लाभि॑नोर् अ॒द्य या॑च्छे॒ष्ठाभि॑र्मघञ्छर
जिन्व ।
यो नो॒ द्वेष्ट्यध॑रः॒ सस्प॑दीष्ट॒ यमु॑ द्वि॒ष्मस्तमु॑ प्रा॒णो ॑ जहातु ॥ २१ ॥

iṃdrotibhirbahulābhinor adya yāccheṣṭhābhirmaghañchara
jinva |
yo no dveṣṭyadharaḥ saspadīṣṭa yamu dviṣmastamu prāṇo
jahātu ‖ 21 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

इंद्र । ऊतिभिः । बहुलाभिः । नः । अद्य । यार्श्रेष्ठाभिः । मघवन् । शूर ।
जिन्व ।
यः । नः । द्वेष्टि । अधरः । सः । पदीष्ट । यं । ऊं इति । द्विस्मः । तं । ऊं इति ।
प्राणः । जहातु ॥ २१ ॥

iṃdra | ūtibhiḥ | bahulābhiḥ | naḥ | adya | yārśreṣṭhābhiḥ | maghavan | śūra |
jinva |
yaḥ | naḥ | dveṣṭi | adharaḥ | saḥ | padīṣṭa | yaṃ | ūṃ iti | dvismaḥ | taṃ | ūṃ iti |
prāṇaḥ | jahātu ‖ 21 ‖

p. 226

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

इंद्रोतिभिरित्याद्याश्चतस्रो वसिष्ठद्वेषिण्यः । पुरा खलु विश्वामित्रशिष्यः सुदा नाम राजर्षिरासीत् । स च केनचित्कारणेन वसिष्ठद्वेष्योऽभूत् । विश्वामितस्तु शिष्यस्य रक्षार्थमाभिर्यग्निर्वसिष्ठमशपत् । इमा अभिशापरूपाः । ता ऋचो वसिष्ठा न शृण्वंति ॥ परस्य शापं करिष्यन् आदावात्मनो रक्षां कुरुते प्रथमेनार्धर्चेन । हे शूर शौर्यवन्नराभिभवशक्त हे मघवन्दनवन्निंद्र अद्यास्मिन्याले यात् । यातयतिर्वधकर्मा । यातयतीति यात् । सुपां सुलुगिति शपो लुक् । यातः शत्रून् हिंसतो नोऽस्थानूतिभिस्त्वदीयाभी रक्षाभिर्जिन्व । प्रीणय । कीदृशीभिः । बहुलाभिर्बह्वीभिः श्रेष्ठाभिः प्रशस्यतराभिः । अथ शपति । नोऽस्मान्यः शत्रुर्द्वैष्यो द्वैष्ट्यस्मद्विषयामप्रीतिं करोति सोऽधरो निकृष्टः सन् पदीष्ट । पततु । वयं च यमु द्विष्मस्तमु तं द्वेष्यं प्राणो देहमध्यॆ वर्तमानः पंचवृत्तिर्वायुर्जहातु । परित्यजतु । उशब्दौ पूरकौ ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse and the three following are directed against Vasiṣṭha. Formerly Sudās, a royal seer, was a disciple of Viśvāmitra; for some reason he became hated by Vasiṣṭha. To protect his disciple Viśvāmitra cursed Vasiṣṭha with these verses. These verses are of the nature of imprecations; the Vasiṣṭhas do not listen to these ṛcs. Intending to curse another, he first secures his own protection with the first half-verse. O hero, able to overcome enemies, O wealthy (मघवन् (maghavan)) Indra, today (यात् (yāt); the root यातयति (yātayati) has the sense of killing) protect and please us who are slaying enemies, with your many (बहुलाभिः (bahulābhiḥ)) and most excellent (श्रेष्ठाभिः (śreṣṭhābhiḥ)) protections. Then he curses: the enemy who hates us, making ill-will towards us, let him, being low (अधरः (adharaḥ)), fall (पदीष्ट (padīṣṭa)). And him whom we hate, let the breath (प्राणः (prāṇaḥ)), the five-fold wind abiding within the body, abandon. The two उ (u) are expletives.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • शूर (śūra)—O mighty one
  • मघवन् (maghavan)—O wealthy one
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • यात् (yāt)—us who are confronting enemies
  • बहुलाभिः (bahulābhiḥ)—of many kinds
  • श्रेष्ठाभिः (śreṣṭhābhiḥ)—excellent
  • ऊतिभिः (ūtibhiḥ)—with protections
  • जिन्व (jinva)—satisfy
  • नः (naḥ)—us
  • यः (yaḥ)—whichever enemy
  • द्वेष्टि (dveṣṭi)—hates
  • सः (saḥ)—he
  • अधरः (adharaḥ)—being low
  • पदीष्ट (padīṣṭa)—may he fall down
  • यमु (yamu)—whom
  • द्विष्मः (dviṣmaḥ)—we hate
  • तं (taṃ)—him
  • प्राणः (prāṇaḥ)—the breath
  • जहातु (jahātu)—may it abandon
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mighty and wealthy Indra, satisfy us, who confront enemies, with your many and excellent protections. May the enemy who hates us fall down, brought low. May he whom we hate die.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra, hero, possessor of wealth, protect us this day against our foes with many and excellent defences : may the vile wretch who hates us fall (before us) ; may the breath of life depart from him whom we hate.

p. 227

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This ṛc, beginning इंद्रोतिभिः (iṃdrotibhiḥ), and the three following express the hatred of the seer Viśvāmitra toward the seer Vasiṣṭha. Formerly there was a royal seer named Sudās, a disciple of Viśvāmitra. For another reason he earned Vasiṣṭha's hatred and became his enemy. To protect his disciple, Viśvāmitra cursed and reviled Vasiṣṭha with these four ṛcs. Therefore these ṛcs are of the nature of imprecation. The descendants of Vasiṣṭha do not listen to these ṛcs. Before cursing another, the seer desires his own protection; in the first half of this ṛc he asks for his own protection from Indra, and in the second half he asks for the subduing of the enemy. Since the meaning of this ṛc is clear, explanation is unnecessary. In the second half it is explained who our enemies are. Indra is prayed that evil may befall both kinds of enemy: those whom we hate and those who hate us. In the Yajurveda and other texts these two kinds of enemy are described, repeatedly, by the sentence योऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मः (yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ).

Ṛk 22

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

प॒र॒शुं चि॒द्वि त॑पति शिंब॒लं चि॒द्वि वृ॑श्चति ।
उ॒खा चि॑दिंद्र॒ येषं॑ती॒ प्रय॑स्ता॒ फेन॑मस्यति ॥ २२ ॥

paraśuṃ cidvi tapati śiṃbalaṃ cidvi vṛścati |
ukhā cidiṃdra yeṣaṃtī prayastā phenamasyati ‖ 22 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

परशुं । चित् । वि । तपति । शिंबलं । चित् । वि । वृश्चति ।
उखा । चित् । इंद्र । येषंती । प्रयस्ता । फेनं । अस्यति ॥ २२ ॥

paraśuṃ | cit | vi | tapati | śiṃbalaṃ | cit | vi | vṛścati |
ukhā | cit | iṃdra | yeṣaṃtī | prayastā | phenaṃ | asyati ‖ 22 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

परशुं चित् । चिच्छब्दः उपमार्थः । यथा परशुं कुठारं प्राप्य वृक्षो वि तपति विशिष्टतापयुक्तो भवति । एवं मदीयो द्वेष्टा वितसतु । शिंबलं चित् शल्मलीकुसुमं यथानायासेन वि वृश्चति विच्छिद्यते । एवं स द्वेष्टा विवृश्चति । विच्छिन्नावयवो भवतु । प्रयस्ता प्रहता येषंती स्रवंत्युखा चित् स्थालीव स द्वेष्टा मदीयमंत्रसामर्थ्येन प्रहतः सन् फेनमस्यति । फेनं मुखादुद्दिरतु ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

चित् (cit) has the sense of comparison. As a tree, on meeting the axe (परशुं (paraśuṃ)), is subjected to a special torment (वि तपति (vi tapati)), so may my enemy be tormented. As the Śālmalī flower (शिंबलं (śiṃbalaṃ)) is cut off without effort, so may that enemy be cut off, with his limbs severed. As a pot (उखा (ukhā)), struck and leaking, so may that enemy, struck by the power of my mantra, throw up foam (फेनं (phenaṃ)) from his mouth.

p. 228

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • परशुं चित् (paraśuṃ cit)—as a tree struck by an axe is wounded (so may our enemy too be wounded and tormented)
  • वितपति (vitapati)—is tormented
  • शिंबलं चित् (śiṃbalaṃ cit)—as the Śālmalī flower
  • वि वृश्चत् (vi vṛścat)—falls easily down from its branch (so may my enemy fall effortlessly to the ground)
  • प्रयस्ता (prayastā)—cracked
  • येषंती (yeṣaṃtī)—leaking
  • उखा चित् (ukhā cit)—as a pot lets water leak
  • फेनं अस्यति (phenaṃ asyati)—(so may my enemy too) pour foam from his mouth
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as a tree struck by an axe is wounded, so may our enemy too be wounded and tormented. As the Śālmalī flower falls easily from its stalk, so may my enemy fall effortlessly to the ground. As a cracked, leaking pot lets its water out, so may my enemy too pour foam from his mouth.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

As (the tree) suffers pain from the axe, as the Simal flower is (easily) cut off, as the injured cauldron leaking scatters foam, so may my enemy perish.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this ṛc it is explained through three illustrations how the enemy comes to ruin. परशुं चित् वि तपति (paraśuṃ cit vi tapati): as a tree, when cut with an axe, feels from the blows an unbearable torment (sorrow), so may one who is our enemy be tormented with sorrow. The word चित् (cit) in this ṛc is used in the sense of comparison, that is, "like". शिंबलं चित् वि वृश्चति (śiṃbalaṃ cit vi vṛścati): as the blossom of the Śālmalī tree drops off effortlessly at a mere breath of wind, so may the limbs of him who hates us, hands and the rest, be cut off and go to pieces. इंद्र प्रयस्ता येषंती उखा चित् फेनं अस्यति (iṃdra prayastā yeṣaṃtī ukhā cit phenaṃ asyati): O Indra, as a pot, when struck, breaks and the water in it leaks out, so may our enemy, struck down by the power of our mantra, pour foam from his mouth; that is, the meaning is, may he die.

p. 229

शिंबलं चित् वि वृश्चति (śiṃbalaṃ cit vi vṛścati): as the flower of the Śalmalī tree easily falls off, so may the enemy who hates us fall to the ground. May his limbs be cut off. इंद्र प्रयस्ता येषंती उखा चित् फेनं अस्यति (iṃdra prayastā yeṣaṃtī ukhā cit phenaṃ asyati): as a broken, cracked pot, struck, leaks, so may our enemy, struck down by the power of our mantra, pour foam from his mouth.

Ṛk 23

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

न साय॑कस्य चिकिते जनासो लो॒धं न॑यंति॒ पशु॒ मन्य॑मानाः ।
नावा॑जिनं वा॒जिना॑ हासयंति॒ न ग॑र्द॒भं पु॒रो अश्वा॑न्नयंति ॥ २३ ॥

na sāyakasya cikite janāso lodhaṃ nayaṃti paśu manyamānāḥ |
nāvājinaṃ vājinā hāsayaṃti na gardabhaṃ puro aśvānnayaṃti ‖ 23 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

न । सायकस्य । चिकिते । जनासः । लोधं । नयंति । पशु । मन्यमानाः ।
न । अवाजिनं । वाजिना । हासयंति । न । गर्दभं ' पुरः । अश्वात् । नयंति ॥ २३ ॥

na | sāyakasya | cikite | janāsaḥ | lodhaṃ | nayaṃti | paśu | manyamānāḥ |
na | avājinaṃ | vājinā | hāsayaṃti | na | gardabhaṃ ' puraḥ | aśvāt | nayaṃti ‖ 23 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पुरा खलु तपसः क्षयो मा प्रापदिति शापान्निवृत्तं मौनिनं विश्वामित्रं वसिष्ठपुरुषा बद्ध्वानीतवंतः । तान्प्रति विश्वामित्रो ब्रूते । हे जनासो जनाः सायकस्यावसानकारिणो विश्वामित्रस्य मंत्रगणसामर्थ्यं न चिकिते ' भविदिर्न ज्ञायते । अत एव लोधं लुब्धं तपसः क्षयो मा भूदिति लोभेन तूष्णीं स्थितमृषिं पशु मन्यमानाः । पशु इति निपातः पशुशब्दसमानार्थः । पशुवन्मन्यमाना एते नयंति । बद्ध्वा स्वकीयं देशं प्रापयंति । एवं स्वसामर्थ्यं प्रदर्श्य विसदृशो वसिष्टो मया सह स्पर्धितुं नार्हतीति धिक्करोति। नावाजिनमिति। अवाजिनं। वाचामिनो वाजिनः सर्वज्ञः । तद्विलक्षणं मूर्खजनं वाजिना वागीशा न हासयंति हास्यास्पदं न कुर्वंति । तेन सह न स्पर्धंत इत्यर्थः । तथा गर्दभं रासभमश्वात्पुरः पुरुस्तान्न नयंति । एवमेव विसदृशो वसिष्टो न मया स्पर्धितुमीष्ट इत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Formerly, when Viśvāmitra, silent and withdrawn from cursing lest his austerity be lost, was bound and brought by Vasiṣṭha's men, he addresses them. O people (जनासः (janāsaḥ)), the power of the group of mantras of Viśvāmitra, the "finisher" (सायकस्य (sāyakasya)), is not known (न चिकिते (na cikite)). Therefore they, regarding as a beast (पशु (paśu); पशु (paśu) is a particle equal in sense to the word पशु (paśu)) the greedy (लोधं (lodhaṃ)) seer who stayed silent from the greed that his austerity not be lost, lead (नयंति (nayaṃti)) him, that is, bind him and bring him to their own place. Thus, displaying his own power, he rebukes: Vasiṣṭha, unlike me, is not fit to compete with me. नावाजिनं (nāvājinaṃ): the अवाजिनं (avājinaṃ) is a foolish person, unlike the वाजिनः (vājinaḥ), the all-knowing master of speech; the masters of speech (वाजिना (vājinā)) do not make him a laughing-stock, that is, they do not compete with him. Likewise they do not lead (न नयंति (na nayaṃti)) an ass (गर्दभं (gardabhaṃ)) in front of a horse. Just so, the unlike Vasiṣṭha is not able to compete with me.

p. 230

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • जनासः (janāsaḥ)—O people
  • सायकस्य (sāyakasya)—of the destroying (Viśvāmitra's) power of mantra
  • न चिकिते (na cikite)—you are unable to know
  • लोधं (lodhaṃ)—the seer who has taken refuge in silence
  • पशु (paśu)—like an animal
  • मन्यमानाः (manyamānāḥ)—these men, having taken (him) to be
  • नयंति (nayaṃti)—are carrying (the seer) off to their own place
  • आवाजिनं (āvājinaṃ)—the unwise man
  • वाजिना (vājinā)—the learned
  • न हासयंति (na hāsayaṃti)—do not hold up to ridicule
  • गर्दभं (gardabhaṃ)—the ass
  • अश्वात् पुरः (aśvāt puraḥ)—in front of the excellent horse
  • न नयंति (na nayaṃti)—do not bring and set (it)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O people, you are unable to know the destroying power of Viśvāmitra's mantras. These men, having taken the seer, who had taken refuge in silence so that his austerity should not be wasted, to be like an animal, are carrying the seer off to their own place. The learned do not ridicule an unwise man. Nor do they put an ass in front of an excellent horse.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Men, (the might) of the destroyer is not known to you : regarding him as a mere animal, they lead him away desirous (silently to complete his devotions) : the wise condescend not to turn the foolish into ridicule, they do not lead the ass before the horse.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Viśvāmitra of old, lest the power of his austerity be wasted, observed a vow of silence and spoke to no one. For that very reason he kept quiet even towards his enemies, giving no curses and the like. Seeing this, the people on Vasiṣṭha's side took this Viśvāmitra to be like an animal that knows nothing, bound him tightly with ropes and went off carrying him. At that time Viśvāmitra speaks to those people in this manner— जनासः सायकस्य न चिकिते लोधं पशुं मन्यमानः नयंति (janāsaḥ sāyakasya na cikite lodhaṃ paśuṃ manyamānaḥ nayaṃti)—हे जनात अवसानकारिणो विश्वामित्रस्य मंत्रगणसामर्थ्यं भवद्भिर्न ज्ञायते । आत एव तपसु क्षयोमा भूदति तूष्णीं स्थितमृषिं पशुवत् मन्यमानः बध्वा स्वकीयं देशं प्रापयंति । (he janāta avasānakāriṇo viśvāmitrasya maṃtragaṇasāmarthyaṃ bhavadbhirna jñāyate | āta eva tapasu kṣayomā bhūdati tūṣṇīṃ sthitamṛṣiṃ paśuvat manyamānaḥ badhvā svakīyaṃ deśaṃ prāpayaṃti |). These people, knowing the power of the mantras of this seer Viśvāmitra, whom they intend to kill, and taking this seer—who for that very reason keeps silent and quiet, not speaking, out of fear that his austerity will be destroyed—to be an animal, bind him with a rope and are carrying him off to their own country.

p. 231

अवाजिनं—वाचां इनः स्वामी सर्वज्ञः । तद्विलक्षणं मूर्खजनं अवाजिनं (avājinaṃ—vācāṃ inaḥ svāmī sarvajñaḥ | tadvilakṣaṇaṃ mūrkhajanaṃ avājinaṃ). One who is lord of speech is called vājī; he is all-knowing. One who is the opposite of that is called avājī. Hence avājinam (accusative singular) means "a foolish man", such is the intention. अवाजिनं वाजिना न हासयंति । गर्दभं अश्वात्पुरतः न नयंति (avājinaṃ vājinā na hāsayaṃti | gardabhaṃ aśvātpurataḥ na nayaṃti)—Good men who have the power of speech, being all-knowing, do not laugh at and ridicule foolish people who know nothing. For does one bring an ass and make it stand before an excellent horse? No. That is: these Vasiṣṭhas and the rest are foolish people without power of speech and without power of mantra. Such people do not wish to compete with me, who am all-knowing through the power of mantra. That is why, with the intention of doing me harm by force, they have bound me with a rope and are carrying me off to their own country.

Ṛk 24

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इ॒म इं॑द्र भर॒तस्य॑ पु॒त्रा अ॑पपि॒त्वं चि॑कितु॒र्न प्र॑पि॒त्वं ।
हि॒न्वंत्यश्व॒मर॑णं॒ न नित्यं॒ ज्या॑वाजं॒ परि॑ णयंत्या॒जौ ॥ २४ ॥

ima iṃdra bharatasya putrā apapitvaṃ cikiturna prapitvaṃ |
hinvaṃtyaśvamaraṇaṃ na nityaṃ jyāvājaṃ pari ṇayaṃtyājau ‖ 24 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

इमे । इंद्र । भरतस्य । पुत्राः । अपपित्वं । चिकितुः । न । प्रपित्वं ।
हिन्वंत । अश्वं । अरणं । न । नित्यं । ज्यावाजं । परि । नयंति । आजौ ॥ २४ ॥

ime | iṃdra | bharatasya | putrāḥ | apapitvaṃ | cikituḥ | na | prapitvaṃ |
hinvaṃta | aśvaṃ | araṇaṃ | na | nityaṃ | jyāvājaṃ | pari | nayaṃti | ājau ‖ 24 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र भरतस्य पुत्रा भरतवंश्या इमे विश्वामित्रा अपपित्वमपगमनं वसिष्ठेभ्यश्चिकितुः । जानंति । प्रपित्वं प्रगमनं न जानंति । शिष्ठैः सह तेषां संगतिर्नास्ति । ब्राह्मणा एव त इत्यर्थः । अपि चाजौ संग्रामे नित्यं सहजमरणं नारिमिव वसिष्ठान्प्रत्यशं हिन्वंति । प्रेरयंति । ततश्च ज्यावाजं बलं धनुः परि णयंति । वसिष्ठान्हंतुं शरसंधानेन चरंति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, these sons of Bharata, the Viśvāmitras of Bharata's line, know अपपित्वं (apapitvaṃ), "going away" from the Vasiṣṭhas; they do not know प्रपित्वं (prapitvaṃ), "going towards". They have no association with the good (śiṣṭa); that is, those men are Brahmins indeed. Moreover, in battle they urge their horses against the Vasiṣṭhas as against an inborn, constant foe. Then they परि णयंति (pari ṇayaṃti) the bowstring-strong bow, going about fitting arrows in order to kill the Vasiṣṭhas.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • भरतस्य (bharatasya)—of the emperor Bharata
  • पुत्राः (putrāḥ)—born of his line
  • इमे (ime)—these Viśvāmitras and others
  • अपपित्वं (apapitvaṃ)—as being different from the offspring of Vasiṣṭha
  • चिकितुः (cikituḥ)—they know
  • प्रपित्वं (prapitvaṃ)—that the two are related
  • न (na)—they do not know
  • आजौ (ājau)—in battle

p. 232

  • नित्यं (nityaṃ)—inborn
  • अरणं न (araṇaṃ na)—like enemies
  • अश्वं (aśvaṃ)—horses
  • हिन्वंति (hinvaṃti)—drive forward against (the offspring of Vasiṣṭha) and confront (them)
  • ज्यावाजं (jyāvājaṃ)—their powerful bow
  • परिणयंति (pariṇayaṃti)—hold, fitting arrows
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, these Viśvāmitras, born of the line of the emperor Bharata, take themselves to be different from the offspring of Vasiṣṭha. They do not know that the two are related. Regarding them as their inborn enemies in battle, they drive their horses against them and confront them. They raise their powerful bows against them, fitting arrows.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

These sons of Bharata, Indra, understand severance (from the Vasisthas), not association (with them) ; they urge their steeds (agaist them) as against a constant foe ; they bear a stout bow (for their destruction) in battle.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The word prapitva (prapitve) has been read by Yāska among the "dviśa" names (Ni. 3-20)NOTE. And he gives the explanation: प्रपित्वेऽभीक इत्यासन्नस्य । प्रपित्वे प्राप्ते । अभीकेऽभक्ते । आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमागहि कण्वेषु सु सचा पिब (ऋ. सं. ८-४-३) इत्यपि निगम् भवतः ॥ (prapitve 'bhīka ityāsannasya | prapitve prāpte | abhīke 'bhakte | āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyamāgahi kaṇveṣu su sacā piba (ṛ. saṃ. 8-4-3) ityapi nigam bhavataḥ ‖). Saying that prapitva means being near, being in the vicinity, close relationship, he has recited as an example the Ṛk beginning आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमागहि कण्वेषु सु सचा पिब (āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyamāgahi kaṇveṣu su sacā piba) (Ṛ.
