Saṃ. 8-4-3). इंद्र भरतस्य इमे पुत्राः अपपित्वं चिकितुः न प्रपित्वं (iṃdra bharatasya ime putrāḥ apapitvaṃ cikituḥ na prapitvaṃ)—भरतवंश्या इमे विश्वामित्रादयः वसिष्ठेभ्यः अपगमनं जानंति प्रगमनं न जानंति । (bharatavaṃśyā ime viśvāmitrādayaḥ vasiṣṭhebhyaḥ apagamanaṃ jānaṃti pragamanaṃ na jānaṃti |). O Indra, the sons of Bharata, that is, Viśvāmitra and the others born of Bharata's line, regard these Vasiṣṭhas and the rest as born elsewhere, that is, as outsiders (or opponents, enemies). They regard it that there is no association with the Vasiṣṭhas, that is, no dealings and the like, and that there is no contact or friendship with the good men who are disciples of Vasiṣṭha and the rest. For there is mutual hostility between the descendants of Viśvāmitra and those of Vasiṣṭha. आजौ नित्यं अरणं न अश्वं हिन्वंति, ज्यावाजं परिनयंति (ājau nityaṃ araṇaṃ na aśvaṃ hinvaṃti, jyāvājaṃ parinayaṃti)—For that very reason, in battle the people of Bharata's line, that is, Viśvāmitra and the others, regarding the Vasiṣṭhas as their inborn enemies, charge their horses upon them in order to confront them. And in order to kill the descendants of Vasiṣṭha they string their bows, set arrows and take aim. Such is the main intention.

p. 233

This is the …-fourth sūkta.NOTE

Sūkta 54 (Maṇḍala 3)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पंचमेऽनुवाके नव सूक्तानि । तत्रेमं मह इति द्वाविंशत्यृचं प्रथमं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वदेवं विश्वामित्रपुत्रस्य वाक्पुत्रस्य वा प्रजापतेरार्षं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । इमं महे द्वधिकोक्तगोत्रः प्रजापतिर्हि वैश्वदेवं हेति । अस्मिन् सूक्त आद्याग्नेया ततः परं सप्तर्चो द्यावापृथिव्यास्ततः परा द्युदेवताका दशमी द्यावापृथिवैकादशी सावित्रि ततः परं सुकृदिति त्वाष्ट्रा र्भवी च विद्युद्रथेति मारुती सारस्वती च ततः परं तिस्रो विष्ट्हिंद्राग्नि देवताकाः स्वदस्वेत्याग्नीयाति। एवं वैश्वदेवं सूक्तं ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । अग्निप्रणयने राजन्यस्यॆमं मह इति प्रतिपत् । पंचम्यां पौर्णमास्यामित्यत्र सूत्रितं । इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषं । आ. २-१७ । इति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

In the fifth anuvāka there are nine sūktas. The first of them, इमं महे (imaṃ mahe), has twenty-two Ṛks; it is in Triṣṭubh, addressed to the Viśvedevas, and its seer is Prajāpati, son of Viśvāmitra or son of Vāc. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇikā: इमं महे द्वधिकोक्तगोत्रः प्रजापतिर्हि वैश्वदेवं हे (imaṃ mahe dvadhikoktagotraḥ prajāpatirhi vaiśvadevaṃ he). In this sūkta the first Ṛk is addressed to Agni; the seven after it to Heaven and Earth (Dyāvāpṛthivī); the next one to Dyu; the tenth to Heaven and Earth; the eleventh to Savitṛ; then the Ṛk सुकृत् (sukṛt) to Tvaṣṭṛ and the Ṛbhus; विद्युद्रथा (vidyudrathā) to the Maruts and Sarasvatī; the next three to Viṣṇu, Indra and AgniNOTE; and स्वदस्व (svadasva), the last, to Agni. Thus the sūkta is Vaiśvadeva. The use of the sūkta is by indication (laiṅgika): in the Agnipraṇayana, the Ṛk इमं महे (imaṃ mahe) is the opening verse (pratipad) for a Rājanya, as stated in the sūtra on the fifth-day full moon: इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषं (imaṃ mahe vidathyāya śūṣaṃ) (Ā. Sū. 2-17).

p. 234

॥ ओं ॥ सूक्त—५४ मंडल—३ ॥ अनुवाक—५ ॥ सूक्त—५४ ॥ अष्टक—३ ॥ अध्याय—३ ॥ वर्ग—२४, २५, २६, २७ ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—२२ ॥ ऋषिः—प्रजापतिर्वैश्वामित्रो वाच्यो वा ॥ देवता—विश्वेदेवाः ॥ छंदः—त्रिष्टुप् ॥

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इ॒मं म॒हे वि॑द॒थ्या॑य शू॒षं शश्व॒त्कृत्व॒ ईड्या॑य॒ प्र ज॑भ्रुः ।
शृ॒णोतु॑ नो॒ दम्ये॑भि॒रनी॑कैः शृ॒णोत्व॒ग्निर्दि॒वैरज॑स्रः ॥ १ ॥

imaṃ mahe vidathyāya śūṣaṃ śaśvatkṛtva īḍyāya pra jabhruḥ |
śṛṇotu no damyebhiranīkaiḥ śṛṇotvagnirdivairajasraḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

इमं । महे । विदथ्याय । शूषं । शश्वत् । कृत्वः । ईड्याय । प्र । जभ्रुः ।
शृणोतु । नः । दम्येभिः । अनीकैः । शृणोतु । अग्निः । दिव्यैः । अदस्रः ॥ १ ॥

imaṃ | mahe | vidathyāya | śūṣaṃ | śaśvat | kṛtvaḥ | īḍyāya | pra | jabhruḥ |
śṛṇotu | naḥ | damyebhiḥ | anīkaiḥ | śṛṇotu | agniḥ | divyaiḥ | adasraḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

महे महते विदथ्याय विदथे यज्ञे मंथनेन निष्पाद्यमानायेड्र्याय सर्वैः स्तुत्यायाग्नये शूषं सुखकरमिमं स्तोमं शश्वत्कृत्वो भूयो भूयः प्र जभ्रुः । प्रभरंति । प्रकर्षण धारयंति । उच्चारयंतीत्यर्थः । सोग्निर्दम्येभिः परेषां दमनकुशलैर्दमे गृहे विद्यमानैर्वानीकैस्तेजोभिर्युक्तः सन् नोस्मदीयमिमं स्तोमं शृणोतु। दिव्यैर्दिवि भव्यैस्तेजोभिरजस्रो निरंतरं युक्तोऽग्निरिमं स्तोमं शृणोतु। शश्वत्कृत्व ईड्याय प्र जभ्रुरिति स्वानामेवैनं तच्छृष्ट्यं गमयति । ऐ. ब्रा. १-२८ । इति ब्राह्मणानुसारेण महदादिगुणविशिष्टाय यजमानायेममग्निं प्रजभ्रुः प्रहरंत्यृत्विज इति वा व्याख्येयं। उत्तरार्धर्चः समान एव॥ विदथ्याय । तत्र भव इत्यर्थे भवे छंदसीति यत् । तित्स्वरितः । ईड्याय । ईडवंदॆ:-

Gist of the bhāṣya

To the great (महे (mahe)) विदथ्याय (vidathyāya)—vidatha being the sacrifice—that is, to Agni, who is produced in the sacrifice by churning and is ईड्याय (īḍyāya), to be praised by all, they bring forth (प्र जभ्रुः (pra jabhruḥ): they bear forward, hold up, utter) again and again (शश्वत्कृत्वः (śaśvatkṛtvaḥ)) this pleasing (शूषं (śūṣaṃ)) hymn. May that Agni, endowed with दम्येभिः (damyebhiḥ) radiances—skilled in subduing others, or present in the house (dama)—hear this hymn of ours. May Agni, constantly endowed with divine radiances, hear it. The second half of the verse is the same. Alternatively, following the Brāhmaṇa शश्वत्कृत्व ईड्याय प्र जभ्रुरिति स्वानामेवैनं तच्छृष्ट्यं गमयति । (śaśvatkṛtva īḍyāya pra jabhruriti svānāmevainaṃ tacchṛṣṭyaṃ gamayati |) (Ai. Brā. 1-28), it is to be explained that the officiants bring forth this Agni for the sacrificer, who is endowed with greatness and other qualities.

p. 235

त्यादिना उदात्तत्वं । दम्येभिः । तत्र साधुरिति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । दिव्यैः । दिवमर्हतीत्यर्थे छंदसि चेति यप्रत्ययः । अजस्रः । जसु मोक्षणे । नमिकंपीत्यादिना ताच्छिलिको रप्रत्ययः । नञ्जा समासे तस्य स्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The rest of the block gives the accent and derivation of the words दम्येभिः (damyebhiḥ), दिव्यैः (divyaiḥ) and अजस्रः (ajasraḥ) (with ईड्याय (īḍyāya) at its beginning): दम्येभिः (damyebhiḥ) in the sense "good in that", दिव्यैः (divyaiḥ) in the sense "worthy of heaven", अजस्रः (ajasraḥ) from the root जसु (jasu) in the sense of release, with the negative compound.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • महे (mahe)—who is of great nature
  • विदथ्याय (vidathyāya)—who is born for the sacrifice
  • ईड्याय (īḍyāya)—who is worthy of praise: addressing Agni
  • शूषं (śūṣaṃ)—pleasing
  • इमं (imaṃ)—this
  • स्तोमवन्नु (stomavannu)—hymn
  • शश्वत्कृत्वः (śaśvatkṛtvaḥ)—again and again
  • प्र जभ्रुः (pra jabhruḥ)—they offer
  • अग्निः (agniḥ)—Agni, the great one
  • दम्येभिः (damyebhiḥ)—that subdue enemies
  • अनीकैः (anīkaiḥ)—endowed with radiances
  • नः (naḥ)—this hymn of ours
  • शृणोतु (śṛṇotu)—may he hear
  • दिव्यैः (divyaiḥ)—endowed with divine radiances
  • अजस्रः (ajasraḥ)—always
  • शृणोतु (śṛṇotu)—may he hear
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To Agni, who is of great nature, who is born for the sacrifice, who is worthy of praise, they offer this hymn, which is praising and pleasing. May Agni, the great one, endowed with radiances that subdue enemies, hear this hymn of ours. May Agni, endowed with divine radiances, always hear.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

They recite repeatedly this gratifying praise to the great product of sacrifice (Agni) : may he who (is endowed) with domestic radiance hear us : may the imperishable Agni, (endowed) with divine radiance, hear us.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

महे विदथ्याय प्र जभ्रुः (mahe vidathyāya pra jabhruḥ)—Sāyaṇa has explained two kinds of meaning: महते यज्ञॆ मंथनेन निष्पाद्यमानाय सर्वैः स्तुत्याय अग्नये । (mahate yajñè maṃthanena niṣpādyamānāya sarvaiḥ stutyāya agnaye |); and महदादिगुणविशिष्टाय यजमानाय (mahadādiguṇaviśiṣṭāya yajamānāya). The first meaning indicates the greatness of Agni. The word vidatha is read by Yāska (Ni. 3-19) among the names of sacrifice. From this the meaning is explained thus: Agni, being produced in the sacrificial rite in his own abode by being churned from the araṇis, is praised by all, and for this Agni the officiants recite hymns many times. In the second meaning, in accordance with the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa “शश्वत्पृत्व ईड्याय प्रजभ्रुरिति स्थानामेवैनं तच्छैष्यं गमयति । (śaśvatpṛtva īḍyāya prajabhruriti sthānāmevainaṃ tacchaiṣyaṃ gamayati |)” (Ai. Brā. 1-28)NOTE, it is explained that the officiants have praised Agni many times for the sacrificer, who is endowed with qualities such as worthiness of honour. For a detailed explanation of this, see Ṛ. Saṃ. part 14, page 53

p. 236

The meaning of the word ईड्याय (īḍyāya) is explained in a way that relates it to both Agni and the sacrificer.

शूषं-सुखकरं । (śūṣaṃ-sukhakaraṃ |) The word शूष (śūṣa) is listed (Ni. 3-13) among the names of happiness. Here it is used in the sense "bringing happiness".

दम्येभिः—परेषां दमनकुशलैः । गृहे विद्यमानैर्वा । (damyebhiḥ—pareṣāṃ damanakuśalaiḥ | gṛhe vidyamānairvā |) The word दम (dama) is read (Ni. 4-4) among the names of the house. Here the word is used as an adjective of a word that denotes brilliance (tejas). Two meanings are therefore explained: the brilliances of Agni are capable of subduing enemies, or they shine on the altar of the sacrificial hall.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

महि महे दिवे अर्चा पृथिव्यै कामो म इच्छज्जरति
प्रजानन् ।
ययो॑र्ह॒ स्तोमे॑ वि॒दथे॑षु दे॒वाः स॑प॒र्यवो॑ मा॒दयं॑ते॒ सचा॒योः ॥ २ ॥

mahi mahe dive arcā pṛthivyai kāmo ma icchajjarati
prajānan |
yayorha stome vidatheṣu devāḥ saparyavo mādayaṃte sacāyoḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

महि । महे । दिवे । अर्च । पृथिव्यै । कामः । मे । इच्छन् । चरति । प्रजानन् ।
ययोः । ह । स्तोमे । विदथेषु । देवाः । सपर्यवः । मादयंते । सचा ।
आयोः ॥ २ ॥

mahi | mahe | dive | arca | pṛthivyai | kāmaḥ | me | icchan | carati | prajānan |
yayoḥ | ha | stome | vidatheṣu | devāḥ | saparyavaḥ | mādayaṃte | sacā |
āyoḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे स्तोतर्महे महत्यै दिने द्युलोकदेवताय्कॆ महत्यै पृथिव्यै च महि महत् त्वं प्रजानन् स्तोत्रमर्च । कुरु । मे मम कामो मनोरथः सर्वान् भोगानिच्छन् चरति । सर्वत्र वर्तते । आयोर्मनुष्यस्य विदथेषु यज्ञेषु ययोर्दानापृथिव्योः स्तोमे स्तोत्रे सपर्यवः पूजाकामा देवाः स्तोतारो वा सचा मादयंते ह सह माद्यंति खलु ॥ पृथिव्यै । उदात्तयण इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । सपर्यवः । सपर्यामिच्छतीत्यर्थे सुपः क्यच् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O worshipper, to the great (महे (mahe)) day, that is, to the deity of the heavenly world, and to the great earth, offer praise (अर्च (arca)), knowing (प्रजानन् (prajānan)) their greatness (महि (mahi))." My desire (कामः (kāmaḥ)), wishing for all enjoyments, ranges (चरति (carati)) everywhere. In the sacrifices (विदथेषु (vidatheṣu)) of the man (आयोः (āyoḥ)), in the praise (स्तोमे (stome)) of those two, heaven and earth, the gods (देवाः (devāḥ)), desirous of worship (सपर्यवः (saparyavaḥ)), or else the worshippers, rejoice (मादयंते (mādayaṃte)) together (सचा (sacā)); they do indeed rejoice together.

p. 237

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • महे (mahe)—(O worshipper,) to the one of great nature
  • दिवे (dive)—to the presiding deity of heaven
  • पृथिव्यै (pṛthivyai)—also to the presiding deity of the earth
  • महि (mahi)—(their) greatness
  • प्रजानन् (prajānan)—having known
  • अर्च (arca)—offer worship
  • मे (me)—my
  • कामः (kāmaḥ)—desire
  • इच्छन् (icchan)—wishing for all enjoyments
  • चरति (carati)—moves about everywhere
  • आयोः (āyoḥ)—of the man
  • विदथेषु (vidatheṣu)—in the sacrifices
  • ययोः (yayoḥ)—of which same heaven and earth
  • स्तोमे (stome)—at the time of praise
  • सपरवः (saparavaḥ)—desirous of worship
  • देवाः (devāḥ)—the worshippers (or the gods)
  • सचा (sacā)—gathering together
  • मादयंते (mādayaṃte)—rejoice
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshipper, knowing the greatness of the heavenly deity of great nature and of the earth deity, offer worship to them. At the time of praising these heaven and earth, the worshippers who desire to worship gather together and rejoice. My desire too moves everywhere, wishing for all enjoyments.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Knowing their greatness, offer worship to the vast heaven and to the earth : my desire, wishing (for felicity) proceeds (to them), in whose praise the gods, desirous of adoration, delight together with their worshippers at the sacrifice.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सपर्यवः देवाः सचा मादयंते— पूजाकामाः देवाः स्तोतारो वा सह माद्यंति खलु । (saparyavaḥ devāḥ sacā mādayaṃte— pūjākāmāḥ devāḥ stotāro vā saha mādyaṃti khalu |) In this Ṛk the greatness of heaven and earth is described. The word अयुः (ayuḥ) is listed (Ni. 3-8) among the names of man. For the word सपर्यवः (saparyavaḥ) Sāyaṇa gives two meanings: those who perform worship, and those who receive worship. The ṛtvijs of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice are glad to recite hymns for the sacrificer, who is eager to obtain his various wishes. The gods too are glad to hear these hymns. Therefore the seer's injunction is described here: let the ṛtvijs, who know well the greatness of heaven and earth, who are worthy of worship, praise them. By this it is also said that the greatness of heaven and earth, who fulfil the sacrificer's wish, is unsurpassed.

p. 238

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यु॒वोर्यु॒तं रो॑दसी स॒त्यम॑स्तु म॒हे षु णः॑ सुवि॒ताय॒ ॑ प्र भूतं ।
इ॒दं दि॒वे नमो॑ अग्ने पृथि॒व्यै स॑प॒र्यामि॒ प्रय॑सा॒ यामि॒ ॑ रत्नं ॥ ३ ॥

yuvoryutaṃ rodasī satyamastu mahe ṣu ṇaḥ suvitāya
pra bhūtaṃ |
idaṃ dive namo agne pṛthivyai saparyāmi prayasā yāmi
ratnaṃ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

युवोः । ऋतं । रोदसी इति । सत्यं । अस्तु । महे । सु । नः । सुविताय । प्र ।
भूतं ।
इदं । दिवे । नमः । आग्ने । पृथिव्यै । सपर्यामि । प्रयसा । यामि । रत्नं ॥ ३ ॥

yuvoḥ | ṛtaṃ | rodasī iti | satyaṃ | astu | mahe | su | naḥ | suvitāya | pra |
bhūtaṃ |
idaṃ | dive | namaḥ | āgne | pṛthivyai | saparyāmi | prayasā | yāmi | ratnaṃ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ युवोर्युवयोर्ऋतमानृशंस्यं सत्यं यथार्थमस्तु । युवां नोऽस्माकं महे महते सुवितायाभ्युदयायॆ यज्ञसमाप्त्यर्थं सु सुष्टु प्र भूतं । प्रभवतं । हे अग्ने दिने पृथिव्यै चेदं नमोऽस्तु । प्रयसा हनिर्लक्षणेनान्नेन सपर्यामि परिचरामि । रत्नमुत्तमं धनं यामि। याचे । यातिर्याञ्जा कर्मा ईमह इत्यादिषु पठितत्वात् ॥ षु । संहितायां सुइ इति षत्वं । णः । संहितायां नश्च धातुस्थोरुषभ्य इति णत्वं । सुविताय । इण् गत्। अधिकरणे क्तः। शोभनं गम्यतेऽस्मिन्निति सुवितं । उवजादेशश्छांदसः। भूतं । भवतेर्लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुकि रूपं । यद्वा । छांदसे लुजि सिचो गातिस्थेति लुक् । निघातः । दिवे पृथिव्यै । नमःस्वस्तीत्यादिना । पा। २-३-१६ । चतुर्थी । सपर्यामि कंड्वादिः परिचरणे वर्तते । प्रत्ययस्वरः । यामि । यातेर्लट रूपं । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O heaven and earth (रोदसी (rodasī)), let your ऋतं (ṛtaṃ), that is, freedom from cruelty (anṛśaṃsya), be true (सत्यं (satyaṃ)), that is, real. For our great (महे (mahe)) well-being (सुविताय (suvitāya)), that is, prosperity, and for the completion of the sacrifice, be fully (सु (su)) effective (प्र भूतं (pra bhūtaṃ)). O Agni, let this homage be to heaven and to earth. With oblation-food (प्रयसा (prayasā)) I serve them (सपर्यामि (saparyāmi), "I attend upon"). I ask (यामि (yāmi)) for excellent wealth (रत्नं (ratnaṃ)); the root या (yā) has the sense of asking, since it is read among īmahe and the like. He adds that the verb सपर्यामि (saparyāmi) has the sense of attending upon, and that because of the break between sentences यामि (yāmi) is not accentless. He also gives the dative of दिवे पृथिव्यै (dive pṛthivyai) by the rule नमःस्वस्तीत्यादिना (namaḥsvastītyādinā) (Pā. Sū. 2-3-16). The alternative on the aorist of भूतं (bhūtaṃ) belongs to the grammar.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • रोदसी (rodasī)—O heaven and earth
  • युवोः (yuvoḥ)—of you two
  • सत्यं (satyaṃ)—the nature that consists of truth
  • यतं (yataṃ)—as unobstructed
  • अस्तु (astu)—let it be eternal
  • नः (naḥ)—our
  • महे (mahe)—great
  • सुविताय (suvitāya)—for the completion of the sacrifice
  • सु प्रभूतं (su prabhūtaṃ)—be gracious
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni

p. 239

  • दिवे (dive)—to the deity of heaven
  • पृथिव्यै (pṛthivyai)—to the earth
  • इदं नमः (idaṃ namaḥ)—this homage is offered
  • प्रयसा (prayasā)—with food in the form of oblation
  • सपर्यामि (saparyāmi)—I worship
  • रत्नं (ratnaṃ)—excellent wealth
  • यामि (yāmi)—I ask for
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O heaven and earth, let the true nature of you two be unobstructed and eternal; be gracious to us for the completion of our great sacrifice. O Agni, this my homage is offered to the deity of heaven and to the earth. I worship them with food in the form of oblation and ask for excellent wealth.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Heaven and earth, may your truth be ever inviolable : be propitious to us for the due completion of the rite : this adoration (Agni) is offered to heaven and earth : I worship (them) with (sacrificial) food ; I solicit of them precious (wealth).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यवोः ऋतं रोदसी सत्यमस्तु—हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ युवयोः अनृशंस्यं यथार्थमस्तु । (yavoḥ ṛtaṃ rodasī satyamastu—he dyāvāpṛthivyau yuvayoḥ anṛśaṃsyaṃ yathārthamastu |) Yāska (Ni. 4-19) uses the word ऋत (ṛta) in the senses "truth" or "sacrifice" and in other senses as well. Here the commentator explains the word ऋत (ṛta) as "being of generous mind" and gives the sense of a prayer: let heaven and earth be generous-minded towards the sacrificer. The sacrificer's prayer is thus indicated: let the nature of heaven and earth, in regard to the sacrificer, be, in accordance with the sense, excellent and forbearing.

In the second sentence the word सुविताय (suvitāya) is used in the sense शोभनं गम्यते अस्मिन् इति सुवितं (śobhanaṃ gamyate asmin iti suvitaṃ), "that from which welfare comes". Therefore सुविताय अभ्युदयाय यज्ञसमाप्त्यर्थं (suvitāya abhyudayāya yajñasamāptyarthaṃ): for the completion of the sacrifice of the sacrificer who brings about welfare, may heaven and earth be purposeful; thus the sacrificer's wish is described. NOTE

The word प्रयस् (prayas) is listed (Ni. 3-9) among the names of food. The sacrificer's wish is stated: that he will satisfy heaven and earth with food in the form of oblation, and, bowing to Agni and worshipping heaven and earth, will pray in order to obtain excellent wealth.

p. 240

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

उ॒तो हि नां॑ पू॒र्व्या आ॑विवि॒द्र ऋता॑वरी रोदसी सत्य॒वाचः॑।
नर॑श्चिद्वां समि॒थे शूर॑सात् वनंदि॒रे पृ॑थिवि॒ वेवि॑दानाः ॥४॥

uto hi nāṃ pūrvyā āvividra ṛtāvarī rodasī satyavācaḥ|
naraścidvāṃ samithe śūrasāt vanaṃdire pṛthivi vevidānāḥ ‖4‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

उतो इति । हि । वां। पूर्व्याः । आविविद्रॆ । ऋतवरी इत्यृतवरी । रोदसी इति।
सत्यवाचः ।
नरः । चित् । वां । सम्‌इथे । शूरसातौ । ववंदिरे । प्रथिवि । वेविदानाः ॥ ४ ॥

uto iti | hi | vāṃ| pūrvyāḥ | āvividrè | ṛtavarī ityṛtavarī | rodasī iti|
satyavācaḥ |
naraḥ | cit | vāṃ | samithe | śūrasātau | vavaṃdire | prathivi | vevidānāḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

उतो अपि च हे ऋतावारी । ऋतं सत्यं । तद्वत्यौ हे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ पूर्वाः पूर्वे भवाः पुरातनाः सत्यवाचो महर्षयो नां युवाभ्यामाविविद्रॆ हि । तं तमपेक्षितमर्थं लेभिरे खलु । तथा हे पृथिवि शूरसात् शूराणां सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् तस्मिन्नमिथे संगमननिमित्ते यद्दे नरश्चिदद्यतना मनुष्याश्च वां युवयोर्माहात्म्यं वेविदाना जानंतोऽतो द्यावापृथिव्यौ ववंदिरे । स्तुवंति ॥ अविविद्रॆ । विद्ल लाभे इत्ययमुभयपदी । लिट इरयो र इति रेआदेशः । सह सुपेत्यत्र सहेति योगविभागादाजा सह समासः । समिथे । इण् गत् । समाण इति थक्प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

And further, O truthful (ऋतावरी (ṛtāvarī); ऋतं (ṛtaṃ) is truth, and the two possess it) heaven and earth, the ancient seers who speak truth (सत्यवाचः (satyavācaḥ)), born of old, obtained (आविविद्रॆ (āvividrè)) from you each desired object; they did indeed obtain it. So too, O earth, in the battle (समिथे (samithe)), the occasion of meeting, in which there is the winning (sāti) of heroes (शूरसातौ (śūrasātau)), men of the present day also, knowing (वेविदानाः (vevidānāḥ)) the greatness of you two, praise (ववंदिरे (vavaṃdire)) heaven and earth. The remainder of the block gives the grammar of अविविद्रॆ (avividrè) and समिथे (samithe).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • उतो (uto)—and
  • ऋतावरी (ṛtāvarī)—O truth-natured
  • रोदसी (rodasī)—heaven and earth
  • पूर्वाः (pūrvāḥ)—the ancient
  • सत्यवाचः (satyavācaḥ)—great seers who speak truth
  • वां (vāṃ)—by your grace
  • आ विविद्रॆ हि (ā vividrè hi)—obtained their desired objects
  • पृथिवि (pṛthivi)—O earth
  • शूरसात् (śūrasāt)—in which heroes fight
  • समिधे (samidhe)—in battle
  • नरश्चित् (naraścit)—all the men who fight
  • वां (vāṃ)—your
  • वेविदानाः (vevidānāḥ)—having known the greatness
  • ववंदिरे (vavaṃdire)—praise (you)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O heaven and earth, of truthful nature, did not the ancient great seers, who speak truth, obtain their desired objects by your grace? O earth, in the battle in which heroes fight, all the men who are warriors, knowing your greatness, praise you.

p. 241

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Heaven and earth, endowed with truth, they who are the ancient declarers of the truth, have obtained from you (what they desired) ; and so, earth, men cognizant (of the greatness of you both) have worshipped you for the sake of triumphing over (hostile) heroes in battle.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The unsurpassed and abundant greatness of heaven and earth is described: they bring grace to the ancient great seers who speak truth, and bring welfare to the heroes who fight in battles.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

को अ॒द्धा वे॑द॒ क इ॒ह प्र वो॑चद्दे॒वां अच्छा॑ प॒थ्या॒३॒॑३ का ॑ समेति ।
ददृ॑श्र एषामव॒मा सदां॑सि॒ परे॑षु॒ या गुह्ये॑षु व्र॒तेषु॑ ॥

ko addhā veda ka iha pra vocaddevāṃ acchā pathyā3 kā
sameti |
dadṛśra eṣāmavamā sadāṃsi pareṣu yā guhyeṣu vrateṣu ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

कः । अद्धा । वेद । कः । इह । प्र । वोचत् । देवान् । अच्छ । पथ्या । का । सम् ।
ऐति ।
ददृश्रे । एषां । अवमा । सदांसि । परेषु । या । गुह्येषु । व्रतेषु ॥ ५ ॥

kaḥ | addhā | veda | kaḥ | iha | pra | vocat | devān | accha | pathyā | kā | sam |
aiti |
dadṛśre | eṣāṃ | avamā | sadāṃsi | pareṣu | yā | guhyeṣu | vrateṣu ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

को वाद्दा सत्यभूतं तादृशमर्थं वेद । वेत्ति । को वेहास्मिन्प्रज्ञातमर्थं प्र वोचत् । प्र ब्रवीति । किं तत्तदुच्यते । देवानच्छाभिलक्ष्य का पथ्या पथि साधुः समीचीनः को वा मार्गः समेति । सम्यक् प्राप्नोतीति । इममर्थं न कश्चिज्ञानाति । न कोऽपि ब्रवीति । किं ते देवा विद्यंते । वाढमित्याह । एषां दिवि स्थितानां नक्षत्ररूपाणां देवानामवमाधोमुखानि सदांसि स्थानानि ददृश्रे । दृश्यंते । तथापि परेषूत्तमेषु गुह्येषु दुर्ज्ञानेषु व्रतेषु कर्मस्वनुष्ठतेषु या यानि

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Who (को (ko)) truly knows (अद्धा वेद (addhā veda)) such a true matter? Who here (इह (iha)) will declare (प्र वोचत् (pra vocat)) what is known about it? What is said? With reference to the gods (देवानच्छ (devānaccha)), what path (पथ्या (pathyā)), good and proper on the road, goes (समेति (sameti)) rightly, arrives properly? No one knows this matter; no one tells it." Do those gods then exist? He answers: certainly. The lower (अवमा (avamā)), downward-facing abodes (सदांसि (sadāṃsi)) of these gods, who stand in the sky in the form of stars, are seen (ददृश्रे (dadṛśre)). Yet in the highest (परेषु (pareṣu)), hidden (गुह्येषु (guhyeṣu)), hard-to-know rites (व्रतेषु (vrateṣu)) that are performed, which …

p. 242

दिवि देवस्थानानि लभ्यंते तत्रागंतुं को मार्ग इति वेदमंतरेण न कश्चिज्ञानातीत्यभिप्रायः ॥ अद्धा । स्वरादिसंतोदात्तत्वेन पठितश्वादंतोदात्तः । वोचत् । ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि लुजि ब्रुवो वचिरिति वच्यादेशः । अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्य इति चेरजादेशः । वच उमित्युमागमः । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa concludes his comment on the previous verse. The abodes of the gods are to be found in heaven, and no one but the Veda knows the road by which to reach them; this is the intended sense. The rest of the block is grammatical (the accent of अद्धा (addhā), the formation of वोचत् (vocat)) and is left to the grammar.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अद्धा (addhā)—the path that makes known the true meaning
  • कः वेद (kaḥ veda)—who indeed knows
  • इह (iha)—in this matter
  • कः (kaḥ)—who indeed
  • प्र वोचत् (pra vocat)—can declare the settled meaning
  • का पथ्या (kā pathyā)—what path
  • देवान् अच्छ (devān accha)—facing the gods
  • समेति (sameti)—takes one along (that too no one can know)
  • एषाः (eṣāḥ)—of these gods who are in the form of stars
  • अवमा (avamā)—downward-facing
  • सदांसि (sadāṃsi)—only the abodes
  • ददृश्रे (dadṛśre)—are seen
  • परेषु (pareṣu)—and the superior
  • गुह्येषु (guhyeṣu)—and the hidden
  • व्रतेषु (vrateṣu)—of the gods engaged in rites
  • या (yā)—whichever abodes there are (no one can know them)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Who indeed knows the path that makes known the true meaning? Who in this matter can declare the settled meaning? No one can know the path that leads one towards the gods. Only the downward-facing abodes of the gods who are in the form of stars are seen. No one can know the hidden abodes of the gods who are engaged in rites that are both superior and mysterious.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Who knows what is the truth, or who may here declare it? what is the proper path that leads to the gods? their inferior abiding places are beheld, as are those which (are situated) in superior mysterious rites.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

By the sentences को अद्धा वेद क इह प्रवोचत् का पथ्या अच्छा देवान् समिति (ko addhā veda ka iha pravocat kā pathyā acchā devān samiti) it is said that the nature of the gods, and the straight path by which to obtain their grace, can neither be known with certainty by anyone nor even be made known to others. It is also said that the greatness of Heaven and Earth, who contain such gods as if in subtle form, is beyond turning back. And it is said that this path, which is suited to reaching these gods seen in the form of stars, can be known through knowledge of the meaning of the Vedas and through performance of the rites the Vedas teach; thus the

p. 243

abundant greatness of the Vedas is declared. Sāyaṇa has expressed this idea in the sentence या परेषु गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ददृश्रे (yā pareṣu guhyeṣu vrateṣu dadṛśre) — उत्तमेषु दुर्ज्ञानेषु कर्मसु अनुष्ठितेषु यानि दिवि देवस्थानानि लभ्यंते तत्रा गंतुं को मार्ग इति वेदमंतरेण न कश्चित् जानाति (uttameṣu durjñāneṣu karmasu anuṣṭhiteṣu yāni divi devasthānāni labhyaṃte tatrā gaṃtuṃ ko mārga iti vedamaṃtareṇa na kaścit jānāti).

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

क॒विर्नृ॒चक्षा॑ अ॒भि षी॑मचष्ट ऋ॒तस्य॒ योना॒ विघृ॑ते॒ मदं॑ती।
नाना॑ चक्राते॒ सद॑नं॒ यथा॒ वेः स॑मा॒नेन॒ क्रतु॑ना संविदा॒ने॥

kavirnṛcakṣā abhi ṣīmacaṣṭa ṛtasya yonā vighṛte madaṃtī|
nānā cakrāte sadanaṃ yathā veḥ samānena kratunā saṃvidāne‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

कविः । नृचक्षाः । अभि । सीं । अचष्ट । ऋतस्य । योना । विघृते इति विघृते ।
मदंती इति ।
नाना । चक्राते इति । सदनं । यथा । वेः । समानेन । क्रतुना । संविदाने इति
संविदाने ॥ ६ ॥

kaviḥ | nṛcakṣāḥ | abhi | sīṃ | acaṣṭa | ṛtasya | yonā | vighṛte iti vighṛte |
madaṃtī iti |
nānā | cakrāte iti | sadanaṃ | yathā | veḥ | samānena | kratunā | saṃvidāne iti
saṃvidāne ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

कविः क्रांतदर्शि नृचक्षा नृणां द्रष्टा सूर्यः सीमेते द्यावापृथिव्यावभ्यचष्ट । सर्वतः पश्यति । ऋतस्य योना जलस्य स्थानेऽंतरिक्षे मदंती हृष्यंत्यौ विघृते । घृतमस्या ओषधयो जलममुष्या इति । एवंविधरसोपेते समानेन । समानमेतदुदकमुच्चैत्यव चाहभिः । भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नय इति परस्परप्रीणनाख्येनैकेन क्रतुना कर्मणा संविदाने परस्परमैकमत्यं प्राप्ते ते द्यावापृथिव्यौ नाना पृथग्भूतं सदनं स्थानं चक्राते । तथा च श्रुतिः । इमौ वै लोकौ सहास्तां तौ व्यैतामिति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । यथा वेः कुलायं नाना भवति तद्वत् ॥ अचष्ट । चक्षिज् व्यक्तायां वाचीत्यस्य लजः स्कोः संयोगाद्योरिति ककारलोपः । निघातः । संविदाने । विद ज्ञान इत्यस्य समो गमीत्यादिनात्मनेपदे शानच् । चित्तावंतोदात्तः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

कविः (kaviḥ) is the far-seeing one; नृचक्षाः (nṛcakṣāḥ) is the beholder of men, the Sun. He looks all round at these two, Heaven and Earth (सीं (sīṃ)). ऋतस्य योना (ṛtasya yonā): in the place of water, the atmosphere, the two are rejoicing. विघृते (vighṛte): of one of them the ghee is the herbs, of the other the water, as the text says, "ghee of this one is the herbs, water of that one"; so they are endowed with such juices. समानेन (samānena): "common is this water, rising and falling with the days; the clouds gladden the earth, the fires gladden the sky." Thus, by one rite, called the mutual gratifying, the two have attained mutual agreement (संविदाने (saṃvidāne)); yet Heaven and Earth have made (चक्राते (cakrāte)) separate abodes (नाना सदनं (nānā sadanaṃ)). The śruti says likewise: "These two worlds were together; they parted." The illustration: as the nest of a bird is separate, so are theirs.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • कविः (kaviḥ)—the far-seeing one
  • नृचक्षाः (nṛcakṣāḥ)—Āditya, who looks upon all creatures
  • सीं (sīṃ)—these Heaven and Earth
  • अभि अचष्ट (abhi acaṣṭa)—looks at all round
  • ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)—of water

p. 244

  • योना (yonā)—in the atmosphere, the place of origin
  • मदंती (madaṃtī)—rejoicing
  • विघृते (vighṛte)—Heaven and Earth, of diverse juices
  • वेः यथा (veḥ yathā)—as birds build separate nests
  • नाना (nānā)—different
  • सदनं (sadanaṃ)—dwelling-place
  • चक्राते (cakrāte)—though they have made
  • समानेन क्रतुना (samānena kratunā)—by rites that help one another
  • संविधाने (saṃvidhāne)—they have attained agreement
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Āditya, the far-seeing one, who looks upon all creatures, looks all round at these Heaven and Earth. Though Heaven and Earth, rejoicing in the atmosphere, the place where water originates, and of diverse juices, have made separate dwelling-places, as birds build separate nests, they have attained agreement through rites that help one another.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The far-seeing beholder of mankind (the sun), surveys this heaven and earth, rejoicing when deficient in moisture in the womb of the waters (the firmament), both concurrnig in community (of function), although they occupy various dwellings, like the diversified nests of a bird.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋतस्य योना मदंती विधृते समानेन क्रतुना संविदाने (ṛtasya yonā madaṃtī vidhṛte samānena kratunā saṃvidāne)—जलस्य स्थाने अंतरिक्षे हृष्यंत्यौ परस्परमैकमत्यं प्राप्ते ते द्यावापृथिव्यौ । (jalasya sthāne aṃtarikṣe hṛṣyaṃtyau parasparamaikamatyaṃ prāpte te dyāvāpṛthivyau |). The word ṛta is listed among the names of water (Ni. 3-24). Heaven and Earth dwell in joy in the atmosphere, where all the waters gather. They practise mutual helpfulness: the atmosphere supplies water to the earth, and the earth supplies the ghee fit for sacrifice. By this exchange of work the two bring about each other's growth. Sāyaṇa explains this idea with परस्परप्रीणनाख्यॆन कर्मणा परस्परमैकमत्यं प्राप्ते (parasparaprīṇanākhyèna karmaṇā parasparamaikamatyaṃ prāpte) and quotes the sentence समानमेतदुदकमुच्छैत्यवचाहभिः । भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नयः (samānametadudakamucchaityavacāhabhiḥ | bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvaṃti divaṃ jinvaṃtyagnayaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-51). From these activities of Heaven and Earth, नाना सदनं चक्राते (nānā sadanaṃ cakrāte)—पृथग्भूतं स्थानं चक्राते (pṛthagbhūtaṃ sthānaṃ cakrāte): they have made separate places. Having explained the meaning thus, Sāyaṇa cites on this point the sentence इमौ वै लोकौ सहा स्तां तौ वैतां (imau vai lokau sahā stāṃ tau vaitāṃ) (Ai. Brā. 4-27).

p. 245

यथा वेः—कुलायं नाना भवति तद्वत् (yathā veḥ—kulāyaṃ nānā bhavati tadvat): as a bird builds its nests in many ways to suit itself, so Heaven and Earth have made places of many kinds; this too is explained. Moreover, their living in agreement is for the benefit of the world. That the Āditya also helps in this matter is stated by the sentence नृचक्षाः सीं अभि अचष्ट (nṛcakṣāḥ sīṃ abhi acaṣṭa)—नृणां द्रष्टा सूर्यः एतौ द्यावापृथिवी सर्वतः पश्यति (nṛṇāṃ draṣṭā sūryaḥ etau dyāvāpṛthivī sarvataḥ paśyati).

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒मा॒न्या वियु॑ते दू॒रेअं॑ते ध्रु॒वे प॒दे त॑स्थतुर्जाग॒रूके॑।
उ॒त स्वसा॑रा युव॒ती भवं॑ती॒ आदु॑ ब्रुवाते मिथु॒नानि॒ नाम॑॥

samānyā viyute dūreaṃte dhruve pade tasthaturjāgarūke|
uta svasārā yuvatī bhavaṃtī ādu bruvāte mithunāni nāma‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

समान्या । वियुते इति वियुते । दूरेअंते इति दूरेअंते । ध्रुवे । पदे ।
तस्थतुः । जागरूके इति ।
उत । स्वसारा । युवती इति । भवंती इति । आत् । ऊं इति । ब्रुवाते इति । मिथुनानि । नाम ॥ ७ ॥

samānyā | viyute iti viyute | dūreaṃte iti dūreaṃte | dhruve | pade |
tasthatuḥ | jāgarūke iti |
uta | svasārā | yuvatī iti | bhavaṃtī iti | āt | ūṃ iti | bruvāte iti | mithunāni | nāma ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

समान्या समाने परस्परप्रीणनाख्येन कर्मणैकमत्यं गते वियुते वियुज्य वर्तमाने दूरेअंते । दूरेंतोऽवसानं ययोस्ते दूरेअंते । अविनाशिन्यौ ते द्यावापृथिव्यौ जागरूके जागरणशीले सत्यौ ध्रुवेऽविनाशिनि पदेऽंतरिक्षे तस्थतुः । तिष्ठतः । उतापि च युवती नित्यतरुणे स्वसारा भगिन्यावेकस्मादात्मनो जाते इति भवंती तस्थतुरित्यन्वयः । आदनंतरं मिथुनानि द्वंद्वानि नाम उर्वि पृथ्वी बहुले दूरेअंते रोदसी पुरोहिते इत्यादीनि नामानि ब्रुवाते । ते परस्परं ब्रूतः । उर्वादिभिर्द्वंद्वनामभिर्दावापृथिव्यावुच्येते इत्यर्थः ॥ समान्या । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्डादेशः । दूरेअंते । इण् गतौ । दुरीणो लोपश्च । उ. २-२० । इति रक्षृत्ययो धातोर्लोपश्च । रो रीति रेफलोपः । ढ्रलोप इति दीर्घः । अंतशब्दोऽमेरसिहसीत्यादिना तन्नत्ययांतः । सप्तम्युपमानेति बहुव्रीहिः । हलदंता-

Gist of the bhāṣya

समान्या (samānyā): the two being common, having reached agreement through the rite called the mutual gratifying; वियुते (viyute): remaining apart; दूरेअंते (dūreaṃte): those whose end is far away. These two, Heaven and Earth, being imperishable and जागरूके (jāgarūke), vigilant, stand in the firm, imperishable station, the atmosphere. Also, being युवती (yuvatī), ever young, and स्वसारा (svasārā), two sisters born of one self, they stand; this is the construction. After that, मिथुनानि (mithunāni), pairs, नाम (nāma), names such as उर्वि पृथ्वी बहुले दूरेअंते रोदसी पुरोहिते (urvi pṛthvī bahule dūreaṃte rodasī purohite) and others, ब्रुवाते (bruvāte), they say to each other; that is, Heaven and Earth are called by pair-names beginning with Urvī. The remainder of the block is grammatical derivation.

p. 246

दिति सप्तम्या अलुक् । पूर्वपदस्वरः । जागरूके । जागृ निद्राक्षय इत्यस्मात्ताच्छेल्यार्थे जागरूकः । पा. ३-२-१६५ । इत्येकप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । स्वसारा । न षट्स्वस्रादिभ्य इति जीपः प्रतिषेधः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This block contains only the remaining grammatical derivations (of जागरूके (jāgarūke) and स्वसारा (svasārā)), which are left to the grammar.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • समान्या (samānyā)—those who have attained agreement through mutually helpful acts
  • वियुते (viyute)—those who are separate
  • दूरेअंते (dūreaṃte)—those who are far away; Heaven and Earth
  • जागरूके (jāgarūke)—intent on their tasks
  • ध्रुवे (dhruve)—eternal
  • पदे (pade)—in the station of the atmosphere
  • तस्थतुः (tasthatuḥ)—have been established
  • उत (uta)—and
  • युवती (yuvatī)—ever young
  • स्वसारा (svasārā)—being sisters
  • भवंती (bhavaṃtī)—are
  • अदु (adu)—afterwards
  • मिथुनानि नाम (mithunāni nāma)—names in pairs
  • ब्रुवाते (bruvāte)—they designate and call
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and Earth, who have attained agreement through mutually helpful acts and are far away, intent on their tasks, have been established in the eternal station of the atmosphere; and, ever young and sisterly, they are designated and called by names in pairs.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Common (in function), disjoined, of distant termination, they remain vigilant in a permanent station : being, as it were, sisters, and ever young : they therefore address each other by twin appellations.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Because Heaven and Earth are mutually helpful (that is, for water to gather on the earth the atmosphere, and for water to gather in the atmosphere the earth, carry out their tasks in agreement), though separate in nature they live in agreement. It is described that, being ever young, abiding in an eternal place, being always devoted and intent on their respective tasks, and being born of the Self, they are designated and dealt with by pair-names only. आदु मिथुनानि नाम ब्रुवाते (ādu mithunāni nāma bruvāte)—आनंतरं उर्व्यादिभिः द्वंद्वनामभिर्द्यावापृथिव्यावुच्येते (ānaṃtaraṃ urvyādibhiḥ dvaṃdvanāmabhirdyāvāpṛthivyāvucyete). The Nirukta authors, when reciting the names of Heaven and Earth, have designated them in pair form only. It is explained that their origin, their activity and their state are the chief reason for reciting them thus.

p. 247

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

विश्वेदे॒ते जनि॑मा॒ सं वि॑विक्तो म॒हो दे॒वान्बिभ्र॑ती॒ न ॑ व्यथेते ।
एज॑द्दु॒नं प॑त्यते॒ विश्व॒मेकं॒ चर॑त्पत॒त्रि विषु॑णं॒ वि जा॒तं॥८॥

viśvedete janimā saṃ vivikto maho devānbibhratī na
vyathete |
ejaddunaṃ patyate viśvamekaṃ caratpatatri viṣuṇaṃ vi jātaṃ‖8‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

विश्वा । इत् । एते इति । जनिमा । सं । विविक्तः । महः । देवान् । बिभ्रती इति । न ।
व्यथेते इति ।
एजत् । ध्रुवं । पत्यते । विश्वं । एकं । चरत् । पतत्रि । विषुणं । वि । जातं ॥ ८ ॥

viśvā | it | ete iti | janimā | saṃ | viviktaḥ | mahaḥ | devān | bibhratī iti | na |
vyathete iti |
ejat | dhruvaṃ | patyate | viśvaṃ | ekaṃ | carat | patatri | viṣuṇaṃ | vi | jātaṃ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

एते द्यावापृथिव्यौ विश्वेज्जनिम सर्वाण्यपि भूतजातानि सं विविक्तः । अवकाशप्रदानेन संविभज्य कुरुतः । किंच महो महतो देवानिंद्रसूर्यादीन् सरित्समुद्रपर्वतादींश्च बिभ्रती बिभ्राणे आपि न व्यथेते । न खिद्येते । किंच विजज्जंगमात्मकं ध्रुवं स्थावरात्मकं च विश्वं जगदेकं स्थानं पृथिवीमेव सत्यते । अभिगच्छति । तथा चरच्चंचलं पशुजातं पतत्रि पक्षिजातं च विषुणं विश्वक् नानारूपमनयोर्मध्यॆ वितिष्ठते । योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥ विविक्तः । विचिर् पृथग्भावे । जुहोत्यादिः । निघातः । बिभ्रती । डुब्बञ् धारणपोषणयोरित्यस्य शतरि नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुरिति नुमभावः । अभ्यस्तस्वरः । विजत् । एजृ कंपने । शतरि रूपं । सत्यते । पद गतौ । दिवादिरात्मनेपदी । दकारस्य तकारो व्यत्ययेन । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

These two, Heaven and Earth, विश्वेज्जनिम (viśvejjanima), all beings, सं विविक्तः (saṃ viviktaḥ), separate and set apart by giving them room. Further, महः (mahaḥ), the great gods, Indra, Sūrya and others, and rivers, seas, mountains and the like, they bear, and yet न व्यथेते (na vyathete), they are not wearied. Further, the moving एजत् (ejat) and the standing ध्रुवं (dhruvaṃ) world, the whole विश्वं (viśvaṃ), goes to one place, the earth alone. So too the moving herds of animals चरत् (carat) and the flocks of birds पतत्रि (patatri), of manifold forms, stand between these two; a suitable verb is to be supplied. The rest of the block is grammatical derivation.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • एते (ete)—these Heaven and Earth
  • विश्वेत् (viśvet)—all
  • जनिम (janima)—beings
  • सं विविक्तः (saṃ viviktaḥ)—have separated and placed in their places
  • महः (mahaḥ)—of great nature
  • देवान् (devān)—the gods, Indra and others
  • बिभ्रती (bibhratī)—though bearing
  • न व्यथेते (na vyathete)—they do not suffer weariness
  • विजत् (vijat)—what is moving
  • ध्रुवं (dhruvaṃ)—and what is standing
  • विश्वं (viśvaṃ)—the whole world too
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—one place (in the form of the earth)
  • पत्यते (patyate)—resorts to
  • चरत् (carat)—animals and others that move about
  • पतत्रि (patatri)—birds
  • विषुणं (viṣuṇaṃ)—being of manifold forms
  • वि (vi)—are placed (between Heaven and Earth)

p. 248

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and earth have separated all the beings that have come into being and placed them in their own places. Though they bear the gods, Indra and the others, who are of great nature, they suffer no distress. The whole world, moving and stationary alike, rests on one single place, which is of the form of the earth. The animals and others that move about, and the birds, being of many forms, are established between heaven and earth and move about.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

These two keep all born things discrete, and, although comprehending the great divinities, are not distressed : all moving and stationary beings rest upon one (basis), whether animals, or birds, or creatures of various kinds.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

By the sentences एते विश्वेत् संविविक्तः महः देर्वा बिभ्रती न व्यथेते (ete viśvet saṃviviktaḥ mahaḥ dervā bibhratī na vyathete) it is made clear that heaven and earth provide room for all living beings to exist separately; and that, although they bear gods such as Indra, who are of abundant power, and also rivers, oceans and mountains, no distress arises in them from this. The greatness of heaven and earth is described both because the earth bears the beings that exist in stationary and moving forms, and because the atmosphere provides room for the birds, which are of the nature of moving creatures.

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

सना॑ पुरा॒णमध्ये॑म्या॒रान्म॒हः पि॒तुर्ज॑नि॒तुर्जा॒मि तन्नः॑ ।
दे॒वासो॒ यत्र॑ पनि॒तार॒ एवै॑रु॒रौ प॒थि व्यु॑ते त॒स्थुरं॒तः ॥ ९ ॥

sanā purāṇamadhyemyārānmahaḥ piturjaniturjāmi tannaḥ |
devāso yatra panitāra evairurau pathi vyute tasthuraṃtaḥ ‖ 9 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सना । पुराणं । अधि । एमि । आरात् । महः । पितुः । जनितुः । जामि । तत् । नः ।
देवासः । यत्र । पनितारः । एवैः । उरौ । पथि । विउते ! तस्थुः । अंतरिति ॥ ९ ॥

sanā | purāṇaṃ | adhi | emi | ārāt | mahaḥ | pituḥ | janituḥ | jāmi | tat | naḥ |
devāsaḥ | yatra | panitāraḥ | evaiḥ | urau | pathi | viute ! tasthuḥ | aṃtariti ‖ 9 ‖

p. 249

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे द्यौर्महो महत्याः पितुः सर्वस्य पालयित्रा जनितुर्जनयित्रास्तव पना सनातनं पुराणं पूर्वक्रमागतं नोऽस्माकं तज्ञामि जामित्वं । सर्वमेकस्माज्ञातमिति द्यौर्भगिनी भवति । तादृशं भगिनीत्वं तदारादधुनाध्येमि । स्मरामि । दिवः पितृत्वे जनयित्तृत्वे च मंत्रवर्णः । द्यौर्मे पिता जनिता नाभिरत्र! ऋग्वे १-१६४-३३। इति । यत्र यस्यां दिव्यंतर्मध्य उरौ विस्तीर्णे व्युते विविक्ते पथि नभसि पनितारस्त्वां स्तुवंते देवासो देवा एवैर्गमनसाधनैः स्वैः स्वैर्वाहनैः सहिता: संतस्तस्थुः । तत्र स्थिता देवा मदीयं स्तोत्रं शृण्वंतिति भावः ॥ पुराणं । पुराशब्दात् शैषिकार्थे सायंचिरमिति ट्युप्रत्ययः । पुराणप्रोक्तेषु ब्राह्मणकल्पेष्टिति निपातनात्तुडभावः । निपातनादेवांतोदात्तत्वं । एमि । इक् स्मरणे । अदादिः । लटि रूपं । निघातः । व्युते । वेञ् त्यतुसंताने । कर्मणि क्तः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः । तस्तुः । तिष्ठतेर्लिट रूपं । यत्रयोगादनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Heaven (Dyaus), you are great, the protectress of all and the begetter. That ancient kinship with us, descended in due order from earlier times, is the relation of a sister: it is said that "Dyaus is a sister", since everything is born from one. I now call to mind that sisterhood. For Heaven's being father and begetter there is a mantra text: द्यौर्मे पिता जनिता नाभिरत्र (dyaurme pitā janitā nābhiratra) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-33). In the middle of heaven, in the wide, separated path, the gods, your praisers, stand together with their own vehicles, the means of travel; the meaning is that the gods standing there hear my praise.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • महः (mahaḥ)—she who is of great nature
  • पितुः (pituḥ)—the protectress
  • जनितुः (janituḥ)—the cause of origin, the deity presiding over the heaven-world
  • सना (sanā)—eternal
  • पुराणं (purāṇaṃ)—come down continuously from of old
  • नः (naḥ)—that is with us
  • तत् जामि (tat jāmi)—that kinship
  • आरात् (ārāt)—now
  • अध्येमि (adhyemi)—I call to mind
  • अस्य (asya)—of this same heaven
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—in the middle
  • उता (utā)—that is wide
  • व्युते (vyute)—that is separate
  • पथि (pathi)—on the path
  • पनितारः (panitāraḥ)—those who praise you
  • देवासः (devāsaḥ)—Indra and others, of divine nature
  • ऎवैः (èvaiḥ)—with their own horses
  • तस्थुः (tasthuḥ)—are stationed
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The deity of the heaven-world, who is of great nature, protectress and cause of origin, I now call to mind that eternal kinship with us, come down continuously from of old. In the middle of this same heaven, on the wide and separate path, Indra and the other gods, who praise you and are of divine nature, are stationed with their own horses.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

I consider at present the eternal and ancient sisterhood to us of you, our great protectress and progenitrix, within whose vast and separated path your eulogists, the gods, travel in their chariots.

p. 250

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is described that the deity Heaven is a kinsman to all who have been born, because she is the cause of their origin and their protectress, and that this kinship has existed from very ancient times. In this matter the mantra दौर्मे पिता जनिता नाभिरत्र (daurme pitā janitā nābhiratra) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-174-33) is cited. NOTE It is described that in the heaven-world made by this deity for the gods' travelling, the gods, moving about with their own vehicles, praise this deity Heaven in the separate and wide atmosphere; and that these gods may hear the hymns recited by the Ṛtvijs in the sacrifices performed by the sacrificer.

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इ॒मं सोमं॑ रोदसी॒ प्र ब्र॑वीम्यदू॒दराः॑ शृणवन्नग्निजि॒ह्वाः ।
मि॒त्रः स॒म्राजो॒ वरु॑णो॒ युवा॑न आदि॒त्यासः॑ क॒वय॑ पप्रथा॒नाः ॥ ८० ॥

imaṃ somaṃ rodasī pra bravīmyadūdarāḥ śṛṇavannagnijihvāḥ |
mitraḥ samrājo varuṇo yuvāna ādityāsaḥ kavaya paprathānāḥ ‖ 80 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

इमं। स्तोमं । रोदसी इति । प्र । ब्रवीमि । यदूदराः। शृणवन् । अग्निजिह्वाः ।
मित्रः । सम्रराजः । वरुणः । युवानः । आदित्यासः । कवयः । पप्रथानाः ॥ १० ॥

imaṃ| stomaṃ | rodasī iti | pra | bravīmi | yadūdarāḥ| śṛṇavan | agnijihvāḥ |
mitraḥ | samrarājaḥ | varuṇaḥ | yuvānaḥ | ādityāsaḥ | kavayaḥ | paprathānāḥ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्याविमं युष्मदीयं स्तोमं प्र ब्रवीमि । प्रकर्षण वदामि । ऋदूदराः । ऋदु मृदु उदरं येषां ते ऋदूदराः । यद्वा । मृदुरुदरे सोमो-येषां ते ऋदूदराः । अग्निजिह्वाः । अग्निर्जिह्वास्थानीयो येषां ते तथोक्ताः । सम्राजः सम्यग्दीप्यमाना युवानो नित्यतरुणाः । यद्वा । यजमानानभिमतफलैर्मिश्रीकुर्वंतः । कवयः क्रांतदर्शिनः पप्रथानाः स्वानि स्वानि कर्माणः प्रथयंतो मित्रादयो देवाः शृणवन् । तदिदं स्तोत्रं शृण्वंतु ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Heaven and Earth, I recite this your praise forcefully. ऋदूदराः (ṛdūdarāḥ): those whose belly is soft; or else, those in whose belly the Soma is soft. अग्निजिह्वाः (agnijihvāḥ): those whose tongue-substitute is Agni. सम्राजः (samrājaḥ): shining well; युवानः (yuvānaḥ): ever young; or else, those who mingle the sacrificers with the fruits they desire. कवयः (kavayaḥ): far-seeing; पप्रथानाः (paprathānāḥ): spreading abroad their own acts. May the gods, Mitra and the rest, hear; let them hear this praise.

p. 251

शृणवन् । श्रु श्रवण इत्यस्य लेट्यडागमः । अग्निजिह्वाः । त्रिचक्रादित्वादंतोदात्तत्वं। पप्रथानाः । प्रथ प्रख्यान इत्यस्य कानचि रूपं । चित्तादंतोदात्तः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Only grammar is given in this block.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • रोदसी (rodasī)—O heaven and earth
  • इमं (imaṃ)—this, addressed to you
  • स्तोमं (stomaṃ)—the praise
  • प्र ब्रवीमि (pra bravīmi)—I recite
  • युदूदराः (yudūdarāḥ)—those of soft belly
  • अग्निजिह्वाः (agnijihvāḥ)—those who have Agni itself as tongue
  • सम्राजः (samrājaḥ)—the shining ones
  • युवानः (yuvānaḥ)—the ever young
  • कवयः (kavayaḥ)—the far-seeing
  • पप्रधानाः (papradhānāḥ)—those who carry out their own duties
  • मित्रः (mitraḥ)—Mitra
  • वरुणः (varuṇaḥ)—Varuṇa
  • आदित्यासः (ādityāsaḥ)—the Ādityas also
  • शृणवन् (śṛṇavan)—may they listen and hear
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O heaven and earth, I recite this praise addressed to you. May Mitra, Varuṇa and the Ādityas, who have soft bellies, have Agni as their tongue, are shining, ever young, far-seeing, and fulfil their own duties, listen and hear it.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

I repeat this hymn, heaven and earth, to you ; and may the soft-bellied, fire-tongued Mitra, royal Varuna, the youtful Adityas, all cognizant of the past, and proclaiming (their own acts), hear it.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ऋदूदरः- ऋदु मृदु उदरं येषां ते । यद्वा मृदुरुदरे सोमो येषां ते (ṛdūdaraḥ- ṛdu mṛdu udaraṃ yeṣāṃ te | yadvā mṛdurudare somo yeṣāṃ te). The word ऋदूदर (ṛdūdara) is explained by Yāska (Ni. 6-4) as ऋदूदरसोमो मृदुरुदुरेष्टिति वा (ṛdūdarasomo mṛdurudureṣṭiti vā). The nature of the gods is described: their belly is soft, or they bear soft Soma in the belly. युवानः—नित्यतरुणाः । यद्वा यजमानान् अभिमतफलैः मिश्रीकुर्वंतः (yuvānaḥ—nityataruṇāḥ | yadvā yajamānān abhimataphalaiḥ miśrīkurvaṃtaḥ). The nature of the gods is explained: they are always in youth; or they favour the sacrificers who satisfy them with offerings of oblations, so that their wishes are fulfilled. It is explained that the gods, having such greatness, spreading abroad their duties, receiving oblations only through Agni, and ever shining, may hear the praises of heaven and earth recited by us the sacrificers.

p. 252

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

हिर॑ण्यपाणिः सवि॒ता सु॑जि॒ह्वस्त्रिरा दि॒वो वि॒दथे॒ पत्य॑मानः ।
दे॒वेषु॑ च सवितः॒ श्लोक॒मश्रे॒राद॒स्मभ्य॒मा सु॑व स॒र्वता॑तिं ॥

hiraṇyapāṇiḥ savitā sujihvastrirā divo vidathe patyamānaḥ |
deveṣu ca savitaḥ ślokamaśrerādasmabhyamā suva sarvatātiṃ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

हिरण्यपाणिः । सविता । सुजिह्वः । त्रिः । आ । दिवः । विदथे । पत्यमानः ।
देवेषु । च । सवितरिति । श्लोकं । अश्रेः । आत् । अस्मभ्यं । आ । सुव । सर्वतातिं ॥११॥

hiraṇyapāṇiḥ | savitā | sujihvaḥ | triḥ | ā | divaḥ | vidathe | patyamānaḥ |
deveṣu | ca | savitariti | ślokaṃ | aśreḥ | āt | asmabhyaṃ | ā | suva | sarvatātiṃ ‖11‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हिरण्यपाणिः । दानार्थं हिरण्यं पाणौ हस्ते यस्य स तथोक्तः । यद्वा । देवकर्तृकयागे सवितुर्ऋत्विग्भूतस्य हस्ते प्राशित्रं भक्षणार्थमद्वर्यवो ददुः । तत्पाशित्रं तस्य हस्तौ चिच्छेद । ततोऽध्वयवो हिरण्ययौ हस्तौ कृत्वा संदधुः । ततोऽयं हिरण्यपाणिः । तथा च कौषीतकं । सवित्रॆ प्राशित्रं प्रतिजह्रुस्तत्तस्य पाणी प्रचिच्छेद तस्मै हिरण्ययौ प्रतिदधुस्तस्माद्धिरण्यपाणिरिति । सुजिह्वः । शोभनवाक् सविता विदथे यज्ञे त्रिस्तिषु सवनेषु दिवो नभसः सकाशादा पत्यमान आगच्छन् भवतीति शेषः । परोऽर्धर्चः प्रत्यक्षः । हे सवितस्त्वं देवेषु स्तोतृषु विद्यमानं च श्लोकं । श्लोक्यतेऽनेनेति श्लोकः स्तोत्रं । तदश्रेः । प्राप्पुहि च । आदनंतरं सर्वतातिं सर्वमपेक्षितं फलमस्मभ्यमा सुव । प्रेरय ॥ हिरण्यपाणिः । हिरण्यशब्दं यास्को बहुधा निर्वक्ति । हिरण्यं कस्माद्ध्रियत आयम्यमानमिति वा ह्रियते जनाज्जनमित्यादिना । नि. २-१० । पाणिशब्दं च निर्विवेच । पाणिः पणायतेः पूजाकर्मणः । नि. २-२६ । इति ॥ हर्य कांतिगत्योः । हर्यतेः कन्यन् हिर चेति कन्यन् हिर इत्ययमादेशो धातोः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । पत्यमानः। पद गत्। दिवादिरात्मनेपदी । दकारस्य तकारश्चांदसः । अश्रेः। श्रिञ् सेवायामित्यस्य लजि बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् । चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निघातः . सुव । षू प्रेरणे । तुदादिः । सर्वतातिं । सर्वदेवात्तातिल् स्वार्थिकः । लित्सर्वः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

हिरण्यपाणिः (hiraṇyapāṇiḥ): he in whose hand there is gold for giving. Or else: at a sacrifice performed by the gods, the Adhvaryus gave the Prāśitra to Savitṛ, who was an Ṛtvij, for eating; it cut off his hands, and the Adhvaryus made golden hands and attached them; hence he is golden-handed. So says the Kauṣītaka: सवित्रॆ प्राशित्रं प्रतिजह्रुस्तत्तस्य पाणी प्रचिच्छेद तस्मै हिरण्ययौ प्रतिदधुस्तस्माद्धिरण्यपाणिरिति (savitrè prāśitraṃ pratijahrustattasya pāṇī praciccheda tasmai hiraṇyayau pratidadhustasmāddhiraṇyapāṇiriti). सुजिह्वः (sujihvaḥ): of good speech. Savitṛ, at the sacrifice, at the three pressings, comes down from the sky. The second half-verse is direct address: O Savitṛ, accept the praise, श्लोक (śloka) (that by which one is praised, a hymn), existing among the gods, the praisers; and then grant us सर्वतातिं (sarvatātiṃ), every desired fruit. Yāska explains हिरण्य (hiraṇya) in many ways, beginning हिरण्यं कस्माद्ध्रियत (hiraṇyaṃ kasmāddhriyata) (Ni. 2-10), and पाणि (pāṇi): पाणिः पणायतेः पूजाकर्मणः (pāṇiḥ paṇāyateḥ pūjākarmaṇaḥ) (Ni. 2-26).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • हिरण्यपाणिः (hiraṇyapāṇiḥ)—he who has a hand of gold
  • सुजिह्वः (sujihvaḥ)—he who has excellent speech
  • सविता (savitā)—Savitṛ
  • विदथे (vidathe)—at the sacrifice
  • त्रिः (triḥ)—at the three pressing times
  • दिवः (divaḥ)—from the atmosphere

p. 253

  • आ पत्यमानः (ā patyamānaḥ)—comes down
  • सवितः (savitaḥ)—O Savitṛ
  • देवेषु (deveṣu)—made for the gods
  • श्लोकं (ślokaṃ)—the praise
  • अश्रेः (aśreḥ)—accept
  • आत् (āt)—thereafter
  • सर्वतातिं (sarvatātiṃ)—the fruit desired by all
  • अस्मभ्यं (asmabhyaṃ)—to us
  • आ सुव (ā suva)—provide
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Savitṛ, who has a hand of gold and excellent speech, comes down to the sacrifice at the three pressing times. O Savitṛ, accept the praise made for the gods. Thereafter provide us with the fruit desired by all.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The golden-handed, soft-tongued Savitri is descending from heaven (to be present) thrice (daily) at the sacrifice : accept, Savitri, the praise (recited by) the worshippers, and thereupon grant to us all our desires.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हिरण्यपाणिः सविता— दानार्थं हिरण्यं पाणौ यस्य (hiraṇyapāṇiḥ savitā— dānārthaṃ hiraṇyaṃ pāṇau yasya). Sāyaṇa explains the meaning as: the god Savitṛ holds gold in his hand for giving; and he gives another meaning for this phrase: यद्वा देवकर्तृकयागे सवितुः ऋत्विगूतस्य हस्ते प्राशित्रं भक्षणार्थमध्वर्यवो ददुः । तत्पाशित्रं तस्य हस्तौ चिच्छेद । ततो अध्वर्यवो हिरण्ययौ हस्तौ कृत्वा संदधुः । ततोऽयं हिरण्यपाणिः (yadvā devakartṛkayāge savituḥ ṛtvigūtasya haste prāśitraṃ bhakṣaṇārthamadhvaryavo daduḥ | tatpāśitraṃ tasya hastau ciccheda | tato adhvaryavo hiraṇyayau hastau kṛtvā saṃdadhuḥ | tato 'yaṃ hiraṇyapāṇiḥ). And so the Kauṣītaka: “सवित्रे प्राशित्रं प्रतिजह्रुः तत्तस्य पाणी प्रचिच्छेद तस्मै हिरण्ययौ प्रतिदधुः तस्मात् हिरण्यपाणिः (savitre prāśitraṃ pratijahruḥ tattasya pāṇī praciccheda tasmai hiraṇyayau pratidadhuḥ tasmāt hiraṇyapāṇiḥ)”. When the gods performed a sacrifice, they offered the oblation into the hand of the god Savitṛ. It cut off his hand. Then the Adhvaryus made a hand of gold and joined it; from this the name Hiraṇyapāṇi became famous: thus the second meaning is explained. It is expressed as a wish that this god come to the sacrificial hall of the sacrificer performing the sacrifice. Yāska has explained the meaning of the word हिरण्य (hiraṇya) and of the word पाणि (pāṇi): हिरण्यं कस्मात् ध्रियत आयम्यमानमिति ना क्रियते जनाज्जनं (hiraṇyaṃ kasmāt dhriyata āyamyamānamiti nā kriyate janājjanaṃ) (Ni. 2-10). पाणिः पणायतेः पूजाकर्मणः (pāṇiḥ paṇāyateḥ pūjākarmaṇaḥ) (Ni. 2-26). NOTE श्लोकं आश्रेः— श्लोक्यते अनेनेति श्लोकः स्तोत्रं (ślokaṃ āśreḥ— ślokyate aneneti ślokaḥ stotraṃ). It is described that the god Savitṛ, having come to the sacrificial hall, may hear the praise recited by the Ṛtvijs.

p. 254

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

सु॒कृत्सु॑पा॒णिः स्ववां॑ ऋ॒तावा॑ दे॒वस्त्वष्टाव॑से॒ तानि॑ नो धात्।
पू॒ष॒ण्वंत॑ ऋभवो मादयध्वमू॒र्ध्वग्रा॑णोणो अध्व॒रम॑तष्ट ॥ १२ ॥

sukṛtsupāṇiḥ svavāṃ ṛtāvā devastvaṣṭāvase tāni no dhāt|
pūṣaṇvaṃta ṛbhavo mādayadhvamūrdhvagrāṇoṇo adhvaramataṣṭa ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सुकृत् । सुपाणिः । स्ववान् । ऋतवा । देवः । त्वष्टा । अवसे । तानि । नः । धात् ।
पूषण्वंतः । ऋभवः । मादयध्वं । ऊर्ध्वग्रावानः । अध्वरं । अतष्ट ॥ १२ ॥

sukṛt | supāṇiḥ | svavān | ṛtavā | devaḥ | tvaṣṭā | avase | tāni | naḥ | dhāt |
pūṣaṇvaṃtaḥ | ṛbhavaḥ | mādayadhvaṃ | ūrdhvagrāvānaḥ | adhvaraṃ | ataṣṭa ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सुकृत्सुष्टु जगतः कर्ता सुपाणिः कल्याणपाणिः स्ववान् धनवानृतावा सत्यसंकल्पस्वष्टा देवस्तानि यान्यस्माकमपेक्षितान्यवसे रक्षणाय नोऽस्मभ्यं धात् । ददातु । ऋभवः । उरु भांतीत्यृभवः । हे ऋभवः पूषण्वंतः पूष्णा सहिता यूयं मादयध्वं । अस्मान् धनप्रदानेन हृष्टान् कुरुत । ऊर्ध्वग्रावाणः सोमाभिषवार्थमुद्यतग्रावाणः संत ऋत्विज इममस्मदीयमध्वरमतष्ट।अकुर्वन्॥ अतष्ट । तक्ष त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । ऊदित्वादत्रेडभावः । झलो झलीति सिलोपः । स्कोः संयोगाद्योरिति ककारलोपः । बहुवचनस्यैकवचनं छांदसं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

सुकृत् (sukṛt) is the good maker of the world; सुपाणिः (supāṇiḥ) is the one with auspicious hands; स्ववान् (svavān) is the wealthy one; ऋतावा (ṛtāvā) is the one whose resolve is true. May the god Tvaṣṭṛ, such as this, grant us for our protection those things we desire. ऋभवः (ṛbhavaḥ): those who shine widely (uru bhāntī) are the Ṛbhus. O Ṛbhus, you who are accompanied by Pūṣan, gladden us, make us glad by giving wealth. ऊर्ध्वग्रावाणः (ūrdhvagrāvāṇaḥ): the priests, holding the pressing stones raised for pressing the Soma, have performed this sacrifice of ours. अतष्ट (ataṣṭa) means "they performed".

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • सुकृत् (sukṛt)—the excellent performer of rites
  • सुपाणिः (supāṇiḥ)—one with excellent hands
  • स्ववान् (svavān)—the wealthy one
  • ऋतावा (ṛtāvā)—one of true resolve
  • त्वष्टा देवः (tvaṣṭā devaḥ)—Tvaṣṭṛ, who is divine in nature
  • तानि (tāni)—those things that are desired by us
  • अवसे (avase)—for our protection
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • धात् (dhāt)—may he give
  • ऋभवः (ṛbhavaḥ)—O Ṛbhus
  • पूषण्वंतः (pūṣaṇvaṃtaḥ)—you who are united with the god Pūṣan
  • मादयध्वं (mādayadhvaṃ)—gladden us
  • ऊर्ध्वग्रावाणः (ūrdhvagrāvāṇaḥ)—priests who hold up the stones (to press the Soma juice)
  • अध्वरं (adhvaraṃ)—(our) sacrifice
  • अतष्ट (ataṣṭa)—have accomplished
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Tvaṣṭṛ, the excellent performer of rites, the one with excellent hands, the wealthy one, the one of true resolve, divine in nature, give us for our protection the things we desire. O ### Printed p. 255 Ṛbhus, you who are united with the god Pūṣan, gladden us. The priests, holding up the stones to crush and press out the Soma juices, have accomplished our sacrifice.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May the divine Twashtri, the able artificer, the dextrous-handed, the possessor of wealth, the observer of truth, bestow upon us those things (which are necessary) for our preservation : Ribhus, associated with Pushan, make us joyful, as they (the priests), with uplifted stones, prepare the sacred libation.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

त्वष्टा देवः (tvaṣṭā devaḥ)—The god called Tvaṣṭṛ is the one who has fashioned the world beautifully and is skilled with his hands. Since this god is of true resolve and is wealthy, the yajamāna's wish is set forth openly: may he fulfil our desires for the protection of us, the yajamānas. ऊर्ध्वग्रावाणः (ūrdhvagrāvāṇaḥ)—सोमाभिषवार्थमुद्यतग्रावाणः (somābhiṣavārthamudyatagrāvāṇaḥ). The priests hold stones raised in their hands in order to press the Soma juice. The prayer is described thus: the sacrifices having been completed, may the god called Pūṣan come with the Ṛbhus to the sacrificial hall, be satisfied by the offering of the oblations, and bestow wealth on the yajamānas. #### Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

वि॒द्युद्र॑था म॒रुत॑ ऋष्टि॒मंतो॑ दि॒वो मर्या॑ ऋ॒तजा॑ता ॒॑ अयासः ।
सर॑स्वती शृणवन्य॒ज्ञॆया॑सो॒ धाता॑ र॒यिं स॒हवी॑रं तुरासः ॥

vidyudrathā maruta ṛṣṭimaṃto divo maryā ṛtajātā
ayāsaḥ |
sarasvatī śṛṇavanyajñèyāso dhātā rayiṃ sahavīraṃ turāsaḥ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

विद्युत्ठरथाः । मरुतः । ऋष्टिमंतः । दिवः । मर्याः । ऋतजाताः । अयासः ।
सरस्वती । शृणवन् । यज्ञियासः । धात । रयिं । सहवीरं । तुरासः ॥ १३ ॥

vidyutṭharathāḥ | marutaḥ | ṛṣṭimaṃtaḥ | divaḥ | maryāḥ | ṛtajātāḥ | ayāsaḥ |
sarasvatī | śṛṇavan | yajñiyāsaḥ | dhāta | rayiṃ | sahavīraṃ | turāsaḥ ‖ 13 ‖

p. 256

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

विद्युद्रथा विद्योतमानरथोपेता ऋष्टिमंतो दीप्तिमंतः। ऋष्टिरायुधविशेषः । तद्वंतो वा दिवो द्योतमाना मर्याः शत्रूणां मारयितार ऋतजाता उदकाद्यज्ञाद्वा प्रादुर्भूताः । यद्वा । ऋतमुदकं जातं येभ्यस्ते ऋतजाताः। अयासः सततगमनशीला यज्जियासो यज्ञार्हा मरुतः सरस्वती । गद्यपद्यरूपेण प्रसरणमस्या अस्तीति सरस्वती । वाग्देवता च । एते सर्वॆ देवा मदीयमिमं स्तोमं शृणवन् । शृण्वंतु । तुरासोऽस्माकं फलप्रदाने त्वरणयुक्ता हे मरुतः सहवीरं पुत्रसहितं रयिं धनंधात। अस्मभ्यं धत्त ॥ धात । दधातेर्लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति शवोलुक् । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तबादेशः पादादित्पादनिघातः । तपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । तुरासः । तुर त्वरणे । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । आमंत्रितत्वान्निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

विद्युद्रथा (vidyudrathā): the Maruts are furnished with shining chariots. ऋष्टिमंतः (ṛṣṭimaṃtaḥ): radiant; or ऋष्टि (ṛṣṭi) is a particular weapon and they possess it. दिवः (divaḥ): shining. मर्याः (maryāḥ): those who cause enemies to die. ऋतजाता (ṛtajātā): born from water or from sacrifice; or else, those from whom water (ṛtam) was born are ऋतजाताः (ṛtajātāḥ). अयासः (ayāsaḥ): those whose nature is constant movement. Yajjiyāsaḥ: the Maruts, worthy of sacrifice. सरस्वती (sarasvatī): she who has a flowing forth (prasaraṇa) in the forms of prose and verse; she is also the deity of speech. May all these gods hear this my praise (शृणवन् (śṛṇavan) = शृण्वंतु (śṛṇvaṃtu)). तुरासः (turāsaḥ): O Maruts, eager to grant us the fruit, give us wealth together with sons (सहवीरं (sahavīraṃ)); धात (dhāta) means "bestow on us".

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • विद्युद्रथाः (vidyudrathāḥ)—those whose chariot is lightning (or those whose chariot shines like lightning)
  • ऋष्टिमंतः (ṛṣṭimaṃtaḥ)—those who have brilliant weapons
  • दिवः (divaḥ)—the resplendent ones
  • मर्याः (maryāḥ)—destroyers of enemies
  • ऋतजाताः (ṛtajātāḥ)—those born from water
  • आयासः (āyāsaḥ)—those of constant motion
  • यज्ञियासः (yajñiyāsaḥ)—those worthy of sacrifice
  • मरुतः (marutaḥ)—the Marut deities
  • सरस्वती (sarasvatī)—(and) the goddess of speech as well
  • शृणवन् (śṛṇavan)—let (them) hear (our praises)
  • तुरासः (turāsaḥ)—O Maruts, eager (to give us the fruit)
  • सहवीरं (sahavīraṃ)—together with heroic sons
  • रयिं (rayiṃ)—wealth
  • धातं (dhātaṃ)—give us
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Marut deities, whose chariots shine like lightning, who have brilliant weapons, who are resplendent, destroyers of enemies, born from water, of constant motion, worthy of sacrifice, and the goddess of speech as well, hear our praises. O Marut deities, eager to give us the fruit, give us wealth together with heroic sons.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May the Maruts, whose cars are the lightning, who are armed with spears, resplendent, destroyers of foes, from whom the waters proceed, (who are) unresting and adorable, and may Saraswati hear (my prayer); and may you (Maruts), speedy in your liberality, bestow (upon us) riches and good offspring. ### Printed p. 257

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मरुतः (marutaḥ)—The Marut deities travel in a shining chariot. ऋष्टिमंतः (ṛṣṭimaṃtaḥ): they shine with radiance, or they hold the weapon called ऋष्टि (ṛṣṭi). ऋतजाताः (ṛtajātāḥ): born from water, or born from sacrifice, or the causes of the production of water. अयासः (ayāsaḥ): these Maruts are of a nature always to move about. The yajamānas' desired prayer is set forth: may they, together with the goddess of speech, who exists as the spreading forth of speech in prose and verse, hear the praises recited by the priests at our sacrifices; and since these Maruts are quick in granting the yajamānas' wishes, may they bestow sons and wealth on the yajamāna. #### Ṛk 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

विष्णुं॒ स्तोमा॑सः पुरुद॒स्मम॒र्का भग॑स्येव का॒रिणो॒ याम॑नि
ग्मन् ।
उ॒रु॒क्र॒मः क॑कु॒हो यस्य॑ पू॒र्विर्न म॑र्धंति युव॒तयो॒ ॑ जनित्रीः ॥ १४ ॥

viṣṇuṃ stomāsaḥ purudasmamarkā bhagasyeva kāriṇo yāmani
gman |
urukramaḥ kakuho yasya pūrvirna mardhaṃti yuvatayo
janitrīḥ ‖ 14 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

विष्णुं । स्तोमासः । पुरुदस्मं । अर्काः । भगस्य इव ! कारिणः । यामनि । ग्मन् ।
उरुक्रमः । ककुहः । यस्य । पूर्वी न मर्धंति । युवतयः । जनित्री ॥ १४ ॥

viṣṇuṃ | stomāsaḥ | purudasmaṃ | arkāḥ | bhagasya iva ! kāriṇaḥ | yāmani | gman |
urukramaḥ | kakuhaḥ | yasya | pūrvī na mardhaṃti | yuvatayaḥ | janitrī ‖ 14 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

स्तोमासः । स्तूयंत विभिरिति स्तोमाः स्तोत्राणि । आर्का अर्चनीयानि शस्त्राणि च भगस्येव धनस्य कारणः कर्तृणीव स्थितानि तानि यामनि संततं प्रतायमानेऽस्मिन्यज्ञॆ पुरुदस्मं बहुकर्माणं । यद्वा । बहून् दस्यत्युपक्षपयतीति पुरुदस्मः । तं विष्णुं देवं ग्मन् । गच्छंतु । पूर्विर्बहो जनित्रीः सर्वस्य जनयित्र्यो युवतयः परस्परमसंकीर्णाः ककुहः । कं स्कुभंति विस्तारयंतीति ककुभो दिशः । यद्वा । ककुबुच्छयार्थः उच्छ्रता इव हि दिशो वृक्षाग्रेषूपलभ्यमानास्तिष्ठंति । एता दिशो विष्णोराज्ञां न मर्धंति । न हिंसंति । स विष्णु- Vol. 17

Gist of the bhāṣya

स्तोमासः (stomāsaḥ): that by which one is praised are stomas, hymns of praise. आर्का (ārkā): adorable praises and śastras. Standing as if they were makers (कारिणः (kāriṇaḥ)) of भग (bhaga), wealth, let them go (ग्मन् (gman) = गच्छंतु (gacchaṃtu)) to the god Viṣṇu, पुरुदस्मं (purudasmaṃ) "of many works", in this sacrifice that is continuously extended (यामनि (yāmani)). Or else, he destroys (दस्यति (dasyati)) many, hence पुरुदस्मः (purudasmaḥ). पूर्वीः (pūrvīḥ): many; जनित्रीः (janitrīḥ): the producers of all; युवतयः (yuvatayaḥ): mutually unmixed; ककुहः (kakuhaḥ): the directions, for they spread out the sky. Or else kakubh has the sense of height: the directions stand as if raised up, seen at the tops of trees. These directions do not violate (न मर्धंति (na mardhaṃti) = न हिंसंति (na hiṃsaṃti)) the command of Viṣṇu. That Viṣṇu is ### Printed p. 258 उरुक्रमः (urukramaḥ): उरु (uru) is great, क्रम (krama) the stride of his feet, he whose stride is great. In the Trivikrama incarnation he stood having pervaded the entire world with one single foot.

रुरुक्रमः । उरुर्महान् क्रमः पादविक्षेपो यस्य सः । त्रिविक्रमावतार एकेनैव पादेन सर्वं जगदाक्रम्यातिष्ठत ॥ ग्मन् । गमेर्लुजि मंत्रे घसेत्यादिना चेर्लुक् ककुभः । पृषोदरादित्वाद्रूपस्वरसिद्धिः ॥

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • स्तोमासः (stomāsaḥ)—our hymns of praise
  • आर्काः (ārkāḥ)—the śastra-mantras worthy of worship
  • भगस्येव कारिणिः (bhagasyeva kāriṇiḥ)—being the causes of our prosperity
  • यामनि (yāmani)—in our sacrifice
  • पुरुदंसं (purudaṃsaṃ)—the doer of many works
  • विष्णुं (viṣṇuṃ)—Viṣṇu
  • ग्मन् (gman)—let them reach
  • पूर्वीः (pūrvīḥ)—the many
  • जनित्रीः (janitrīḥ)—the cause of the world's origin
  • युवतयः (yuvatayaḥ)—those that are separate
  • ककुहः (kakuhaḥ)—the directions
  • यस्य (yasya)—of which Viṣṇu (the command)
  • न मर्धंति (na mardhaṃti)—they do not transgress (that Viṣṇu)
  • उरुक्रमः (urukramaḥ)—has a wide stride
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May our hymns of praise and the śastra-mantras worthy of worship, being the causes of our prosperity, reach in our sacrifice Viṣṇu, the doer of many works. That Viṣṇu, whose command the directions, many in number, the cause of the world's origin, each separate, do not transgress, has a wide stride.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May (our) praises and prayers, the causes of good fortune, attain at this sacrifice Vishnu, the object of many rites : he, the wide-stepping ; whose commands the many-blending regions of space, the generators (of all beings), do not disobey.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अर्काः (arkāḥ)—अर्चनीयानि शस्त्राणि च (arcanīyāni śastrāṇi ca). The Nirukta-author has stated the meaning of the word अर्क (arka) in four ways: mantra, deity, tree, food (Ni. 5-4). Here Sāyaṇa has said that the word is used in the sense of a mantra that praises the greatness of a deity. पुरुदस्मं (purudasmaṃ)—बहुकर्माणं (bahukarmāṇaṃ); यद्वा बहून् दस्यति उपक्षपयति (yadvā bahūn dasyati upakṣapayati). For this word two meanings are explained: one who does many works, or one who destroys many enemies. स्तोमासः अर्काः पुरुदस्मं ग्मन् (stomāsaḥ arkāḥ purudasmaṃ gman)—स्तोत्राणि शस्त्राणि च बहुकर्माणं तं देवं विष्णुं गच्छंतु (stotrāṇi śastrāṇi ca bahukarmāṇaṃ taṃ devaṃ viṣṇuṃ gacchaṃtu). It is explained that the hymns recited by the priests, which are the means of obtaining wealth, and the śastra-mantras, are also for winning the favour of Viṣṇu, who performs many works and ### Printed p. 259 destroys many wicked ones. ककुहः (kakuhaḥ)—"They expand the sky", that is, the directions make manifest the extent of the sky. Also: यद्वा ककुबुच्छयार्थः (yadvā kakubucchayārthaḥ), उच्च्रिता इव दिशः वृक्षाग्रेषूपलभ्यमानाः तिष्ठंति (uccritā iva diśaḥ vṛkṣāgreṣūpalabhyamānāḥ tiṣṭhaṃti): since the directions are lofty, as if connected with the tops of trees, the directions are high regions. Thus the meaning of the word kakup is set out. पूर्वीः जनित्रीः ककुहः युवतयः विष्णोराज्ञां न मर्धंति (pūrvīḥ janitrīḥ kakuhaḥ yuvatayaḥ viṣṇorājñāṃ na mardhaṃti)—It is described that even these directions, many in number, producing everything, each separate, do not transgress the command of Viṣṇu, who is full of greatness. This Viṣṇu is उरुक्रमः (urukramaḥ)—उरुः महान् पादविक्षेपः यस्य सः (uruḥ mahān pādavikṣepaḥ yasya saḥ): one with a great placing of the feet. It is described that by a single placing of his foot he has pervaded the whole earth, and so the greatness of Viṣṇu is described as unsurpassed. #### Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इंद्रो॒ विश्वै॑र्वी॒र्य्यै॒३॒ः॑ पत्य॑मान उ॒भे आ प॑प्रौ॒ रोद॑सी ॒ महित्वा ।
पु॒रं॒द॒रो वृ॑त्र॒हा धृ॒ष्णुषे॑णः सं॒गृभ्या॑ न॒ आ भ॑रा॒ भूरि॑ प॒श्वः॥

iṃdro viśvairvīryyaiḥ patyamāna ubhe ā paprau rodasī
mahitvā |
puraṃdaro vṛtrahā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇaḥ saṃgṛbhyā na ā bharā bhūri paśvaḥ‖

महित्वा ।

mahitvā |
puramdaraḥ | vṛtrahā | dhṛṣṇusenaḥ | samagṛbhya | naḥ | ā | bhara | bhūri | paśvaḥ ‖15‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

विश्वैः सर्वीर्वैः सामर्थ्यैः पत्यमानः प्राप्यमाणः स इंद्र उभे रोदसी द्यावाप्पथिव्यौ महित्वा स्वकीयेन महिम्ना पप्रौ । पूरयामास । शेषः प्रत्यक्षकृतः ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra, who is attained (पत्यमानः (patyamānaḥ) = प्राप्यमाणः (prāpyamāṇaḥ)) by all powers (विश्वैः वीर्यैः (viśvaiḥ vīryaiḥ)), filled (पप्रौ (paprau) = पूरयामास (pūrayāmāsa)) both रोदसी (rodasī), heaven and earth, with his own greatness (महित्वा (mahitvā)). The rest is in the second person, as if before the eyes. ### Printed p. 260

पुरंदरः शत्रुपुरां दारयिता वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य हंता धृष्णुषेणः पराभिभवनशीलसेनोपेतः स त्वं पश्वः पशून् संगृभ्य संगृह्य नोऽस्मभ्यं भूरि प्रभूतं यथा भवति तथा भर । देहि । यद्वा । पश्वः पशोर्भूरि बहुत्वं बहून् पशूंश्च यच्छेति ॥ पुरंदरः । दृ विदारण इत्यस्य पुरशब्द उपपदे पूःसर्वयोर्दारिसहोरिति खच्प्रत्ययः । वाचंयमपुरंदरौ चेति निपातनात्पूर्वपदस्यामागमः । चित्तादंतोदात्तः। धृष्णुषेणः । पूर्वपदादिति संहितायां षत्वं । यदा षत्वं तदा रषाभ्यामिति णत्वं । संगृभ्य । ग्रहेल्यपि स्थानिवद्भावात्संप्रसारणं । हृग्रहोर्भश्चंदसीति भत्वं । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । पश्वः । पशुशब्दात् शसः जसादिषु छंदसि वावचनमिति सवर्णदीर्घाभावः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

पुरंदरः (puraṃdaraḥ): the breaker of enemy cities; वृत्रहा (vṛtrahā): the slayer of Vṛtra; धृष्णुषेणः (dhṛṣṇuṣeṇaḥ): possessed of an army whose nature is to overpower others. You, such as this, having gathered (संगृभ्य (saṃgṛbhya) = संगृह्य (saṃgṛhya)) the cattle (पश्वः (paśvaḥ) = पशून् (paśūn)), bring (भर (bhara) = देहि (dehi)) them to us abundantly (भूरि (bhūri) = प्रभूतं (prabhūtaṃ)). Or else, भूरि (bhūri) means plurality: give many cattle.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • विश्वैः (viśvaiḥ)—all
  • वीर्यैः (vīryaiḥ)—by powers
  • पत्यमानः (patyamānaḥ)—united
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • उभे रोदसी (ubhe rodasī)—both heaven and earth
  • महित्वा (mahitvā)—by his greatness
  • आ पप्रौ (ā paprau)—has filled (O Indra)
  • पुरंदरः (puraṃdaraḥ)—the destroyer of enemy cities
  • वृत्रहा (vṛtrahā)—the slayer of Vṛtra
  • धृष्णुषेणः (dhṛṣṇuṣeṇaḥ)—you who have an army that destroys enemies
  • पश्वः (paśvaḥ)—cattle
  • संगृह्य (saṃgṛhya)—having gathered
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • भूरि (bhūri)—so as to be abundant
  • आ भर (ā bhara)—provide
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, united with all powers, has filled both heaven and earth with his greatness. O Indra, you, the destroyer of enemy cities, the slayer of Vṛtra, who have an army that destroys enemies, gather cattle in abundance and give them to us.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra, invested with all energies, has filled both heaven and earth with his greatness : you are the destroyer of cities, the slayer of Vritra, the leader of a conquering host, collect cattle and bestow them abundantly upon us.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

इंद्रः विश्वैः वीर्यैः पत्यमानः (iṃdraḥ viśvaiḥ vīryaiḥ patyamānaḥ)—सर्वैः सामर्थ्य्यैः प्राप्यमाणः इंद्रः (sarvaiḥ sāmarthyyaiḥ prāpyamāṇaḥ iṃdraḥ). The meaning of the word इंद्र (iṃdra) is explained in various ways by Yāska (Ni. 10-8). It is described that Indra, being full of manifold and complete power, has filled heaven and earth with his greatness.

p. 261

Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, endowed with an army bent on overcoming foes, is prayed to bring plenty of cattle to us, the sacrificers. The Sanskrit of this prayer is वृत्रहा धृष्णुसेनः नः पश्वः भूरि आ भर (vṛtrahā dhṛṣṇusenaḥ naḥ paśvaḥ bhūri ā bhara)—पराभिभवनशीलसेनोपेतः वृत्रस्य हंता अस्मभ्यं पशून् भूरि यथा भवति तथा आभर । (parābhibhavanaśīlasenopetaḥ vṛtrasya haṃtā asmabhyaṃ paśūn bhūri yathā bhavati tathā ābhara |), and alternatively यद्वा पशोः भूरि बर्हू पशूंश्च यच्छ (yadvā paśoḥ bhūri barhū paśūṃśca yaccha). In Kannada: may Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, accompanied by armies able to defeat enemies, graciously grant us, the sacrificers, many animals such as cows, so that they gather to us in plenty; or may he grant plentiful animals alone. Such is the prayer expressed.

Ṛk 16

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

नास॑त्या मे पि॒तरा॑ बंधु॒पृच्छा॑ सजा॒त्य॑म॒श्विनो॒श्चारु॒ नाम॑ ।
यु॒वं हि स्तो र॑यि॒दौ नो॑ रयी॒णां दा॒त्रं र॑क्षेथे॒ अक॑वै॒रद॑ब्धा ॥ १६ ॥

nāsatyā me pitarā baṃdhupṛcchā sajātyamaśvinoścāru nāma |
yuvaṃ hi sto rayidau no rayīṇāṃ dātraṃ rakṣethe akavairadabdhā ‖ 16 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

नासत्या । मे । पितरा । बंधुपृच्छा । सजात्यं । अश्विनोः । चारु । नाम ।
युवं । हि । स्थः । रयिद्दौ । नः । रयीणां । दात्रं । रक्षेथे इति । अकवैः । अदद्दा ॥

nāsatyā | me | pitarā | baṃdhupṛcchā | sajātyaṃ | aśvinoḥ | cāru | nāma |
yuvaṃ | hi | sthaḥ | rayiddau | naḥ | rayīṇāṃ | dātraṃ | rakṣethe iti | akavaiḥ | adaddā ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे नासत्यावश्विन् बंधुपृच्छा । हविष्पदातृत्वेन बंधूनस्मानपेक्षितमर्थं पृच्छत इति बंधूनां प्रष्टारौ । युवां मे पितरौ पालयितारौ भवतं । युवयोरश्विनोः सजात्यं सजाते भवं संगतं चारु नाम कमनीयं खलु । हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां नोऽस्मभ्यं रयीणां धनानां मध्यॆ रयिदावुत्तमस्य धनस्य दातारौ स्थो हि । भवथः खलु। किंच आदब्बा केनाप्यतिरस्कृतौ युवां दात्रं हविषां दातारं मामकवैरकुत्सितैः शोभनैः कर्मभी रक्षेथे । पालयतं ॥ नासत्या । नभ्राण्नपादित्यादिना निपातनान्नञ्ञः प्रकृतिभावः । बंधुपृच्छा । पृच्छेः क्विप् । सुपां सुलुगिति सुपो डादेशः । सजात्यं । सजाते भवं । भवे छंदसीति यत् । तित्स्वरितः । स्थः । अस्तेर्लट रूपं । हियोगादनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, bandhupṛcchā": since by giving oblations we are their kinsmen, they ask us the object we desire, and so are "questioners of kinsmen". "You two are my parents", my protectors. This "common-birth" (सजात्यं (sajātyaṃ), what exists in the same birth, conjoined) of you two Aśvins is a lovely name. "O Aśvins, you are the givers to us of the best wealth among riches (रयिदौ (rayidau))". Further, unbaffled by anyone, you two protect me, the giver of the oblations, with good deeds that are blameless (अकवैः (akavaiḥ) = अकुत्सितैः (akutsitaiḥ), the unblameable). Protect me.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • नासत्या (nāsatyā)—O Aśvin gods
  • बंधुपृच्छा (baṃdhupṛcchā)—you who, being kinsmen to us, ask and learn our desired objects
  • मे (me)—to me
  • पितरा (pitarā)—be protectors

p. 262

  • अश्विनोः (aśvinoḥ)—of you two
  • सजात्यं (sajātyaṃ)—being one together
  • चारु नाम (cāru nāma)—is attractive
  • युवं (yuvaṃ)—you two
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • रयीणां (rayīṇāṃ)—among the whole group of riches
  • रयिदौ (rayidau)—as givers of the best wealth
  • स्थः हि (sthaḥ hi)—are you not
  • अदब्धा (adabdhā)—you who are not harmed by others
  • दात्रं (dātraṃ)—me, who offer the oblation
  • अकवैः (akavaiḥ)—with good deeds
  • रक्षेथे (rakṣethe)—protect
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, you who, being kinsmen to us, ask and learn our desired objects, be protectors to me. Your being joined together is attractive to the sight. You are the givers to us of the best wealth among all wealth. You, who are not harmed by others, protect me, the offerer of the oblation, with good deeds.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Nasatyas, my protectors, inquirers (after the wishes) of your kinsman, beautiful is your cognate appellation of Ashwins ; be to us the liberal donors of riches : you, are irresistible, protect the offer (of the oblation) with unblameable (defences).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नासत्या बंधुपृच्छा मे पितरौ (nāsatyā baṃdhupṛcchā me pitarau)—अश्विनौ हविस्पदातृत्वेन बंधूनस्मान् अपे क्षितमर्थं पृच्छतः युवां पालयितारौ भवतं । (aśvinau havispadātṛtvena baṃdhūnasmān ape kṣitamarthaṃ pṛcchataḥ yuvāṃ pālayitārau bhavataṃ |). The word Nāsatyau is explained by Yāska (Ni. 6-13) in two or three ways. The Aśvin gods, as kinsmen would inquire, inquire into and learn the wishes of the sacrificers who please them with offerings of oblations, and fulfil them; therefore the prayer is explained as asking that they be protectors of the sacrificers. रयिदौ नो रयीणां (rayidau no rayīṇāṃ)—धनानां मध्ये उत्तमस्य धनस्य दातारौ (dhanānāṃ madhye uttamasya dhanasya dātārau): the meaning is described that among the various kinds of wealth the Aśvin gods grant the sacrificer the best wealth. अदब्धा (adabdhā)—केनाप्यहिंसितौ (kenāpyahiṃsitau): it is declared that the Aśvin gods are those who are harmed by no one; and अकवैः रक्षेथे (akavaiḥ rakṣethe)—अकुत्सितैः शोभनकर्मभिः पालयितं (akutsitaiḥ śobhanakarmabhiḥ pālayitaṃ): that they should protect the sacrificers so that good rites, not open to blame, are performed continually.
