‖ 17 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे कवयो मेधाविनो हे देवा वो युष्माकं तत्तादृशं महत्पभूतं नाम कर्म नमनं वा चारु मनोहरं खलु । यद्येन कर्मणा विश्वे सर्वॆ यूयमिंद्र इंद्रोपलक्षिते लोके देवा भवथ ह देवत्वं प्राप्नुथ खलु । हे पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूत हे इंद्र त्वं प्रियेभिः प्रियतमैर्यभुभिः । ऋतेन भवंत्यृतेन भांतीति वा । ऋभभिर्देवैः सखासि । इंद्रसहिता ऋभवो यूयमिमामस्यदीयां धियं स्तुतिं नोऽस्माकं सातये धनादिलाभार्थं तक्षत । स्वीकुरुत ॥ यत् । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना सुपो लुक् । भवथ ॥ भवतेर्लटि रूपं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । सख ऋभुभिरित्यस्य संहितायामृत्यक इति प्रकृतिभावो ह्रस्वत्वं च ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O wise ones (कवयः (kavayaḥ)), O gods, that great, abundant नाम (nāma)—either 'action' or 'bowing'—of yours is surely charming; by which action all of you attain godhood in the world marked by Indra." "O Indra, invoked by many, you are a friend with the Ribhus, your dearest." The Ribhus are explained as those who come into being by ṛta (truth, order), or who shine by ṛta. "You Ribhus, together with Indra, accept (तक्षत (takṣata), 'receive') this praise of his for our gain of wealth and the like."

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • कवयः (kavayaḥ)—O wise gods
  • वः (vaḥ)—to you
  • तत् (tat)—that well-known
  • महत् (mahat)—and abundant
  • नाम (nāma)—action
  • चारु (cāru)—is dear
  • यत् (yat)—by which very action
  • विश्वे (viśve)—all of you together
  • इंद्रे (iṃdre)—in Indra's world
  • देवाः भवथ ह (devāḥ bhavatha ha)—have you not attained godhood
  • पुरुहूत (puruhūta)—O Indra, invoked by many
  • प्रियेभिः (priyebhiḥ)—who are dearest to you
  • ऋभुभिः (ṛbhubhiḥ)—with the Ribhus
  • सखा (sakhā)—you are a friend
  • इमां (imāṃ)—offered by us
  • धियं (dhiyaṃ)—the praise
  • नः (naḥ)—for us
  • सातॆये (sātèye)—for the gain of wealth
  • तक्षत (takṣata)—accept

p. 264

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise gods, the well-known and abundant action is dear to you. By that very action have you all not attained godhood in Indra's world? O Indra, invoked by many, you are a friend with the Ribhus, who are dearest to you. Accept the praise offered by us for the gain of wealth for us.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Sages acquainted with the past, excellent is that beautiful appellation under which you have both become gods in (the sphere of) Indra : Indra, the invoked of many, a friend, (associated) with the beloved Ribhus, shape this prayer for our benefit.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कवयः (kavayaḥ)—मेधा विनः (medhā vinaḥ). The word kavi is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). By this word the gods are addressed as being wise. Of these gods महत् नमनं चारु (mahat namanaṃ cāru)—प्रभूतं नमनं मनोहरं (prabhūtaṃ namanaṃ manoharaṃ): it is described that their excessive performance of deeds is beneficial to the world and attractive to the minds of all. And यत् विश्वे इंद्रे देवाः भवथ (yat viśve iṃdre devāḥ bhavatha)—येन कर्मणा सर्वॆ यूयं इंद्रो सलक्षिते लोके देवत्वं प्राप्नुथ । (yena karmaṇā sarvè yūyaṃ iṃdro salakṣite loke devatvaṃ prāpnutha |). Their excellent performance of rites is praised thus: by the rites these gods perform, they obtain a shining godhood and dwell in the world where Indra dwells. Although Indra is addressed by the word purūhūta, it is declared that this Indra is a friend of the gods called Ribhus, and that the Ribhus, coming with Indra to the sacrificial hall and hearing the sacrificer's praises, should grant wealth and the like to the sacrificer.

Ṛk 18

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒र्य॒मा नो॒ अदि॑तिर्य॒ज्ञया॒सोऽद॑ब्धानि॒ वरु॑णस्य व्र॒तानि॑।
यु॒योत॑ नो अनप॒त्यानि॒ गंतोः॑ प्र॒जावा॑न्नः पशु॒मां ॑ ॒ अस्तु गातुः ॥ १८ ॥

aryamā no aditiryajñayāso 'dabdhāni varuṇasya vratāni|
yuyota no anapatyāni gaṃtoḥ prajāvānnaḥ paśumāṃ
astu gātuḥ ‖ 18 ‖

p. 265

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

आर्यमा । नः । अदितिः । यज्ञियासः । आदब्बानि । वरुणस्य । व्रतानि ।
युयोत । नः । अनपत्यानि । गंतोः । प्रजावान् । नः । पशुमान् । अस्तु । गातुः॥

āryamā | naḥ | aditiḥ | yajñiyāsaḥ | ādabbāni | varuṇasya | vratāni |
yuyota | naḥ | anapatyāni | gaṃtoḥ | prajāvān | naḥ | paśumān | astu | gātuḥ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अर्यमा । ऋच्छति सर्वदा गच्छतीत्यर्यमा सूर्यः । आदितिर्देवमाता यज्जियासो यज्ञार्हा देवा यस्य वरुणस्य व्रतानि कर्माण्यदब्बान्यहिंसितानि भवंति स वरुणस्ते चार्यमादयो देवा नोऽस्मानक्षंत्विति शेषः । ते यूयं नोऽस्माकमनपत्यान्यपत्यानां पुत्राणामहितानि कर्माणि । यद्वा । पतनकारणं न भवतीत्यपत्यं । तदन्यान्यनपत्यानि पतनकारणानि कर्माणि गंतोः सन्मार्गाद्युयोत। पृथक्कुरुत । यथा तान्यहितानि कर्माणि न स्पृशंति तथा कुरुतेत्यर्थः । अथ गातुः । गायंति स्तुवंतींद्रादीनत्रेति गातुर्गृहं । नोऽस्मदीयं गृहं पशुमान्पश्वादियुक्तं प्रजावानपत्योपेशमस्तु ॥ आर्यमा । ऋ गत् । श्वन्नु क्षन्निहन्नेदन्नित्यादिना निपातनाद्रूपसिद्धिः । अदितिः । दीज् क्षय इत्यस्य कर्तरि क्तिच् । नञा समासः । अदितिरदीनेति यास्कः । छांदसं ह्रस्वत्वं । नञा: स्वरः । युयोत । यौतेरमिश्रीभावकर्मणो लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति शप श्लुः । तप्तनबिति तप्रत्ययस्य तबादेशः । गंतोः । गम्ल गत् । सितनिगमिमसिसच्यविधाण्‌क्रुशिभ्य इति तुन्प्रत्ययः । नित्तादाम्युदात्तः । गातुः । गापाहिभ्यश्चेति तुप्रत्ययः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Aryaman: "he goes (ऋच्छति (ṛcchati)) always", hence Aryaman, the Sun. Aditi is the mother of the gods. यज्जियासो (yajjiyāso) are the gods worthy of sacrifice. Varuṇa's व्रतानि (vratāni), his works, are unharmed (adabbāni = ahiṃsitāni). That Varuṇa and those gods, Aryaman and the rest, "may protect us" (the verb to be supplied). You, as to us: अनपत्यानि (anapatyāni) are deeds that are not beneficial to अपत्यानां (apatyānāṃ), sons. Or else: what is not a cause of falling is apatya; the others, अनपत्यानि (anapatyāni), are deeds that are causes of falling. Separate us (युयोत (yuyota)) from these, from the right path (गंतोः (gaṃtoḥ)): act so that those harmful deeds do not touch us. Then गातुः (gātuḥ): people sing, praise Indra and the others here, hence गातुः (gātuḥ) is the house. May our house be पशुमान् (paśumān), furnished with cattle and the like, and प्रजावान् (prajāvān), possessed of offspring.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अरमा (aramā)—Aryaman, the god NOTE
  • अदितिः (aditiḥ)—Aditi, mother of the gods
  • यज्ञियासः (yajñiyāsaḥ)—the gods worthy of sacrifice
  • वरुणस्य (varuṇasya)—of Varuṇa
  • व्रतानि (vratāni)—the works
  • आदब्बानि (ādabbāni)—being unharmed
  • नः (naḥ)—may they protect us
  • अनपत्यानि (anapatyāni)—deeds opposed to offspring
  • गंतोः (gaṃtoḥ)—than the right path NOTE
  • युयोत (yuyota)—let them separate (let them make us not enter the wrong path)
  • नः (naḥ)—our house
  • पशुमान् (paśumān)—furnished with cattle and the like
  • प्रजावान् (prajāvān)—possessed of progeny
  • अस्तु (astu)—let it be
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Aryaman, Aditi the mother of the gods, the gods worthy of sacrifice, and the works of Varuṇa too, being unharmed, protect us. Destroying the deeds opposed to our offspring, let them keep us always on the right path. May our house be furnished with cattle and the like, and possessed of progeny.

p. 266

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May Aryaman, Aditi the adorable (gods), and the unimpeded functions of Varuna (protect) us : keep us from (following) the course unpro- pitious to offspring, and may our dwelling be abundant in progeny and cattle.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

आर्यमा (āryamā)—ऋच्छति सर्वदा गच्छतीत्यर्यमा सूर्यः (ṛcchati sarvadā gacchatītyaryamā sūryaḥ). Sāyaṇa explains that the Sun is designated by the word Aryaman because he is always in motion. The explanation of Durgācārya is अरीणां तमसां नियंता (arīṇāṃ tamasāṃ niyaṃtā) (Ni. 11-24). Various meanings of the word Aditi are explained by Yāska. Here the word is used in the sense "mother of the gods". Because the works of the goddess Aditi, mother of the gods, of the Sun, of Varuṇa and of the gods worthy of sacrifice cause harm to no one, the prayer is made that these gods protect us, the sacrificers. For the word अनपत्यानि (anapatyāni): अपत्यानां पुत्राणामहितानि कर्माणि (apatyānāṃ putrāṇāmahitāni karmāṇi)—deeds not beneficial to sons; and else, पतनकारणं न भवतीतपत्यं तदन्यान्यनपत्यानि पतन कारणानि कर्माणि (patanakāraṇaṃ na bhavatītapatyaṃ tadanyānyanapatyāni patana kāraṇāni karmāṇi)—or else, deeds that are not a cause of falling are अपत्य (apatya); deeds other than these are अनपत्य (anapatya) and are therefore known as causes of falling. नः गंतोः युयोत (naḥ gaṃtoḥ yuyota): it is wished that these gods grant that deeds not beneficial to the sacrificers' sons do not occur, or that they keep away from the proper path the deeds that cause the sacrificers' fall. गातुः (gātuḥ)—गायंत्यत्रेंद्रादीनिति गातुर्गृहं (gāyaṃtyatreṃdrādīniti gāturgṛhaṃ). The sacrificial hall, where Indra and the others are praised, is designated by the word गातुः (gātuḥ). The favour of these gods is wished for, that the sacrificer's house be filled with cattle and offspring.

Ṛk 19

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

दे॒वानां॑ दू॒तः पु॑रु॒ध प्रसू॒तोऽना॑गान्नो वोचतु स॒र्वता॑ता ।

devānāṃ dūtaḥ purudha prasūto 'nāgānno vocatu sarvatātā |

p. 267

शृणोतु नः पृथिवी द्यौरुतापः सूर्यो नक्षत्रैरुर्वंगतरिक्षं ॥ १९ ॥

śṛṇotu naḥ pṛthivī dyaurutāpaḥ sūryo nakṣatrairurvaṃgatarikṣaṃ ‖ 19 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

देवानां । दूतः । पुरुध । प्रसूतः । अनागान् । नः । वोचतु । सर्वताता ।
शृणोतु । नः । पृथिवी । द्यौः । उत । अपः । सूर्यैः । नक्षत्रैः । उरु । अंतरिक्षं ॥

devānāṃ | dūtaḥ | purudha | prasūtaḥ | anāgān | naḥ | vocatu | sarvatātā |
śṛṇotu | naḥ | pṛthivī | dyauḥ | uta | apaḥ | sūryaiḥ | nakṣatraiḥ | uru | aṃtarikṣaṃ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पुरुध पुरुषु बहुषु देशेषु प्रसूतोऽग्निहोत्रार्थं विहितः । यद्वा । पुरुभिर्यजमानैः प्रसूतो यष्टव्यदेवाह्वानार्थं प्रेरितो देवानां दूतः । तथा च तैत्तिरीयकं । अग्निर्दॆवानां दूत आसीदिति । तादृशोऽग्निः कर्मकर्तृसाधनवैगुण्येन सापराधानप्यस्माननागाननागसः । सर्वताता सर्वत्र वोचतु । ब्रवीतु । किंच पृथिवी द्यौश्च उतापि चापः सूर्यश्च नक्षत्रैरुरु विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षं च । एते सर्वे देवा नोऽस्मदीयां स्तुतिं शृणोतु । शृण्वंतु । प्रत्येकविवक्षयैकवचनं ॥ प्रसूतः । षू प्रेरणे । कर्मणि क्तः । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः । अनागान् । शसि सकारलोपश्कांदसः । सवर्णदीर्घे कृते तस्माच्छसो न इति नत्वं । वोचतु । वच परिभाषणे । व्यत्ययो बहुलमिति शपोऽजादेशः । वच उम् । गुणः । निघातः । नक्षत्रैः । नक्ष गत् । अमिनक्षियजिबंधिपतिभ्योऽत्रन्नित्यत्रन्प्रत्ययः । नित्वादाद्युदात्तः । यद्वा । न क्षरति न क्षेयत इति वा नक्षत्रं । नभ्राण्णपादिति नञः प्रकृतिभावः । नञः स्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

पुरुध (purudha): प्रसूतः (prasūtaḥ) in many places (पुरुषु बहुषु देशेषु (puruṣu bahuṣu deśeṣu)), that is, appointed for the Agnihotra. Or else, impelled by many sacrificers to invite the gods to be sacrificed to, he is the messenger of the gods. So the Taittirīya text says अग्निर्दॆवानां दूत आसीदिति (agnirdèvānāṃ dūta āsīditi). May such an Agni, even though we are at fault through defects in the rite, the performer and the means, declare us everywhere (सर्वताता (sarvatātā)) to be अनागान् (anāgān), sinless; वोचतु (vocatu) means "let him say". Further: Earth and Heaven, and the Waters, the Sun, and the wide atmosphere with its stars—may all these gods hear our praise. The singular verb is used because each is intended separately.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • पुरुध (purudha)—in many regions
  • प्रसूतः (prasūtaḥ)—produced (for the sacrifice)
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—to the gods
  • दूतः (dūtaḥ)—the messenger; Agni
  • नः (naḥ)—us
  • अनागान् (anāgān)—as sinless
  • सर्वताता (sarvatātā)—in all places
  • वोचतु (vocatu)—let him proclaim
  • पृथिवी (pṛthivī)—Earth
  • द्यौः (dyauḥ)—the world of heaven
  • उत (uta)—and
  • आपः (āpaḥ)—the deity of the waters
  • सूर्यः (sūryaḥ)—the Sun NOTE
  • नक्षत्रैः (nakṣatraiḥ)—existing together with the stars
  • उरु (uru)—extensive
  • अंतरिक्षं (aṃtarikṣaṃ)—the atmosphere
  • नः (naḥ)—our praise
  • शृणोतु (śṛṇotu)—let it hear
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni, who is produced for the sacrifice in many regions and is the messenger of the gods, proclaim us everywhere as sinless. May the earth, the world of heaven, and the water-dei

p. 268

Ṛk 19 (continued)

Bhāvārtha (continued) …and the vast firmament together with the stars, the sun and the deity of the waters, shall also hear our praise.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May the messenger of the gods, engendered in many places, everywhere proclaim us void of offence : may earth and heaven, the waters, the sun, and the vast firmament, with the constellations, here us.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुरुध प्रसूतः (purudha prasūtaḥ)—पुरुषु बहुषु देशेषु अग्निहोत्रार्थं विहितः (puruṣu bahuṣu deśeṣu agnihotrārthaṃ vihitaḥ) । Or else: पुरुभिर्यजमानैः प्रसूतः यष्टव्यदेवाह्वानार्थं प्रेरितः । (purubhiryajamānaiḥ prasūtaḥ yaṣṭavyadevāhvānārthaṃ preritaḥ |) । Agni is praised as one who is placed by the sacrificers in many places for the performance of the Agnihotra; or as one who is sent forth by many sacrificers in the sacrifices in order to bring the gods. And in accordance with the statement of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā अग्निर्देवानां दूत आसीत् (agnirdevānāṃ dūta āsīt) (Tai. Saṃ.) he is also spoken of as देवानां दूतः (devānāṃ dūtaḥ), the messenger who brings the gods.

नः अनगान् सर्वताता वोचतु (naḥ anagān sarvatātā vocatu)—कर्मकर्तृसाधनवैगुण्येन सापराधानस्मान् अनागसः सर्वत्र ब्रवीतु । (karmakartṛsādhanavaiguṇyena sāparādhānasmān anāgasaḥ sarvatra bravītu |) । When we, the sacrificers, perform the sacrifices, we become guilty of offence through deficiency in the rite, in the doers and in the materials needed for the work; Agni is therefore prayed to release us from our deficiency.

पृथिवी, दौः, आपः, सूर्यः, अंतरिक्षं च नः शृणोतु (pṛthivī, dauḥ, āpaḥ, sūryaḥ, aṃtarikṣaṃ ca naḥ śṛṇotu)—The earth, the heaven, the deity of the waters, the sun and the firmament filled with stars: may these also hear the praises recited by the sacrificers. Thus the wish is expressed.

Ṛk 20

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

शृ॒ण्वंतु॑ नो॒ वृष॑णः॒ पर्व॑तासो ध्रु॒वक्षे॑मास॒ इळ॑या॒ ॑ मदंतः ।
आ॒दि॒त्यैनो॒ आदि॑तिः शृणोतु॒ यच्छं॑तु नो म॒रुतः॒ शर्म॑ ॒ भद्रं ॥ २० ॥

śṛṇvaṃtu no vṛṣaṇaḥ parvatāso dhruvakṣemāsa iḷayā
madaṃtaḥ |
ādityaino āditiḥ śṛṇotu yacchaṃtu no marutaḥ śarma
bhadraṃ ‖ 20 ‖

p. 269

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शृण्वंतु । नः । वृषणः । पर्वतासः । ध्रुवक्षेमासः । इळॆया । मदंतः ।
आदित्यैः । नः । अदितिः । शृणोतु । यच्छंतु । नः । मरुतः । शर्म । भद्रं ॥ २० ॥

śṛṇvaṃtu | naḥ | vṛṣaṇaḥ | parvatāsaḥ | dhruvakṣemāsaḥ | iḷèyā | madaṃtaḥ |
ādityaiḥ | naḥ | aditiḥ | śṛṇotu | yacchaṃtu | naḥ | marutaḥ | śarma | bhadraṃ ‖ 20 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

वृषणोऽभिमतफलसेचका मरुतः पर्वतासः । पृणंति पूरयंत्यर्थिनां कामानिति पर्वता गाव्राभिमानिनो देवाः ध्रुवक्षेमासो निश्चलस्थाना इळया हविर्लक्षणेनान्नेन मदंतो माद्यंतः संतो नोऽस्मदीयां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतु । किंच आदित्यैरपत्यभूतैरादित्यैरुपेतादितिर्नोऽस्मदीयां स्तुतिं शृणोतु । मरुतश्च नोऽस्मभ्यं भद्रं कल्याणकरं शर्म सुखं यच्छंतु । ददतु ॥ आदित्यैः । अदितेरपत्यानीत्यर्थे दित्यदितीति ण्यः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तः । सुपा सहैकादेशे कृत एकादेश उदात्तः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts are the "showerers", who sprinkle the fruit that is desired; they are the पर्वतासः (parvatāsaḥ): "they fill (पृणंति (pṛṇaṃti)) the wishes of those who seek", hence पर्वताः (parvatāḥ), the deities presiding over the pressing-stones. ध्रुवक्षेमासः (dhruvakṣemāsaḥ) means those whose abode is unmoving. Gladdened by the food (इळया (iḷayā)) in the form of the oblation, may they hear our praise. Further, may Aditi, accompanied by the Ādityas who are her offspring, hear our praise; and may the Maruts grant us auspicious, beneficent comfort (शर्म (śarma)), that is, happiness. यच्छंतु (yacchaṃtu) means "let them give".

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • वृषणः (vṛṣaṇaḥ)—the Maruts, bestowers of what is desired
  • पर्वतासः (parvatāsaḥ)—the deities presiding over the mountains, too
  • ध्रुवक्षेमासः (dhruvakṣemāsaḥ)—having an unmoving abode
  • इळया (iḷayā)—with the food in the form of the oblation
  • मदंत (madaṃta)—rejoicing
  • नः (naḥ)—our praise
  • शृण्वंतु (śṛṇvaṃtu)—let them hear
  • आदित्यैः (ādityaiḥ)—together with the Ādityas, her sons
  • अदितिः (aditiḥ)—Aditi
  • नः (naḥ)—our praise
  • शृणोतु (śṛṇotu)—let her hear
  • मरुतः (marutaḥ)—the Maruts
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • भद्रं (bhadraṃ)—auspicious
  • शर्म (śarma)—happiness
  • यच्चंतु (yaccaṃtu)—let them give
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Maruts, bestowers of what is desired, and the deities presiding over the mountains also, having an unmoving abode and rejoicing in the food that takes the form of the oblation, hear our praise. May Aditi, together with the Ādityas who are her sons, hear our praise. May the Maruts give us auspicious happiness.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May the (divine) showerers (of benefits), the deities of the mountains, and those abiding in flxed habitations, propitiated by the sacrificial food, hear us : may Aditi, with the Adityas, hear us : may the Maruts grant us auspicious felicity.

p. 270

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पर्वतासः (parvatāsaḥ)—पृणंति पूरयति अर्थिनां कार्मा इति पर्वताः ग्रावाभिमानिनो देवाः । (pṛṇaṃti pūrayati arthināṃ kārmā iti parvatāḥ grāvābhimānino devāḥ |) । Because they fulfil the wishes of those who take refuge in them, the deities presiding over the stones are designated by the word पर्वत (parvata). The prayer is described thus: these deities, the Marut deities who grant the sacrificers' desires, and the goddess Aditi together with her sons the Ādityas, satisfied by the offering of the sacrificers' oblations, shall hear the praises recited by the sacrificers.

Ṛk 21

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

सदा॑ सु॒गः पि॑तु॒मां अ॑स्तु॒ पंथा॒ मध्वा॑ देवा॒ ओष॑धीः॒ सं ॑ पिपृक्त ।
भगो॑ मे अग्ने स॒ख्ये न मृ॑ध्या॒ उद्रा॒यो अ॑श्यां॒ सद॑नं ॒ पुरुक्षोः ॥ २१ ॥

sadā sugaḥ pitumāṃ astu paṃthā madhvā devā oṣadhīḥ saṃ
pipṛkta |
bhago me agne sakhye na mṛdhyā udrāyo aśyāṃ sadanaṃ
purukṣoḥ ‖ 21 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सदा । सुगः । पित्रुमान् । अस्तु । पंथाः । मध्वा । देवाः । ओषधीः । सं । पिपृक्त
भगः । मे । अग्ने । सख्ये । न । मृध्याः । उत् । रायः । अश्यां । सदनं । पुरुषोः॥

sadā | sugaḥ | pitrumān | astu | paṃthāḥ | madhvā | devāḥ | oṣadhīḥ | saṃ | pipṛkta
bhagaḥ | me | agne | sakhye | na | mṛdhyāḥ | ut | rāyaḥ | aśyāṃ | sadanaṃ | puruṣoḥ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

प्रवत्स्यन्यजमानः सदा सुग इत्यृचं जपन् गच्छेत् । सूत्रितं च । सदा सुगः पितुमा अस्तु पंथा इति पंथानमवरुह्य । आ. २-५ । इति ॥ हे अग्ने अस्माकं पंथा मार्गः सदा सर्वदा सुगः सुखेन गंतुं शक्यः पितुमानन्नवांश्चास्तु । हे देवा मध्वा माधुर्येर्पेतेनोंदकेनौषधीः सं पिपृक्त । संपर्चयत । सेचयतेत्सर्थः । हे अग्ने त्वया सख्यॆ संजाते सति मे मम भगो धनं न मृध्याः । न विनश्यतु । किंच रायो धनस्य पुरुक्षोर्बह्वन्नस्य च सदनं स्थानमुदश्यां । प्राप्नुयां ॥ सदा । स्वरादिष्वाद्युदात्तत्वेन पाठादाद्युदात्तः । पिपृक्त । पृची संपर्के । लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति शपः श्लुः । बहुलं छंदसीत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । मृध्याः । मृधिर्हिंसार्थः । लिजि तिजां तिजो भवंतीति तिपः सिप् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

A sacrificer about to set out should go reciting the ṛc सदा सुगः (sadā sugaḥ). It is also given in the sūtra: सदा सुगः पितुमा अस्तु पंथा इति पंथानमवरुह्य (sadā sugaḥ pitumā astu paṃthā iti paṃthānamavaruhya) (Ā. Sū. 2-5). "O Agni, may our path be always easy to travel and rich in food. O gods, with water endowed with sweetness, saturate (सं पिपृक्त (saṃ pipṛkta), "bring together", that is, "make them wet") the plants. O Agni, now that friendship with you has arisen, may my fortune (भगः (bhagaḥ), wealth) not be destroyed. And may I attain (Sanskrit udaśyām) the abode of wealth (रायः (rāyaḥ)) and of much food (पुरुक्षोः (purukṣoḥ))."

p. 271

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • (O Agni) पंथाः (paṃthāḥ)—our path
  • सदा (sadā)—always
  • सुगः (sugaḥ)—fit to be travelled with ease
  • पितुमान् (pitumān)—furnished with food
  • अस्तु (astu)—let it be
  • देवाः (devāḥ)—O gods
  • मध्वा (madhvā)—with water endowed with sweetness
  • ओषधीः (oṣadhīḥ)—the plants
  • सं पिपृक्त (saṃ pipṛkta)—serve (make the plants thrive with the sweet juice) NOTE
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • सख्यॆ (sakhyè)—when your friendship exists
  • मे (me)—my
  • भगः (bhagaḥ)—wealth
  • न मृध्याः (na mṛdhyāḥ)—let it not be destroyed
  • रायः (rāyaḥ)—of wealth (and)
  • पुरुक्षोः (purukṣoḥ)—of abundant food
  • सदनं (sadanaṃ)—the abode
  • उत् आश्ल्यां (ut āślyāṃ)—may I obtain NOTE
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, may our path always be fit to be travelled with ease and furnished with food. O gods, fill the plants with sweet juice. O Agni, while your friendship is with me, may my wealth not be destroyed; and may the abode of abundant wealth and food be obtained by me.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May our path ever be easy of going, and provided with food : sprinkle, gods, the plants with sweet water : (safe) in your friendship, Agni, may my fortune never be impaired, but may I occupy a dwelling (abounding) with riches and ample food.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That the sacrificer who performs a sacrifice should go reciting this ṛc सदा सुगः (sadā sugaḥ) when he travels, is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra सदा सुगः पितुमा अस्तु पंथा इति पंथानमवरुह्य (sadā sugaḥ pitumā astu paṃthā iti paṃthānamavaruhya) (Ā. 2-5).

पितुर्मा (piturmā)—अन्नर्मा (annarmā) NOTE. The word पितु (pitu) is stated among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). The sacrificers pray to Agni that their path be pleasant and provided with food. The wish of the sacrificers is described thus: may the gods make the herbs grow with sweet waters, and may Agni bring about for the sacrificers increase, so that there is no deficiency of wealth and of abundant food.

p. 272

Ṛk 22

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स्वद॑स्व ह॒व्या समिषो॑ दिदीह्यस्म॒द्र्य१॒॑ग्सं मि॑मीहि॒ श्रवां॑सि ।
विश्वां॑ अग्ने पृ॒त्सु ताञ्जे॑षि॒ शत्रू॒नहा॒ विश्वा॑ सु॒मना॑ दीदिही
नः ॥ २२ ॥

svadasva havyā samiṣo didīhyasmadryagsaṃ mimīhi śravāṃsi |
viśvāṃ agne pṛtsu tāñjeṣi śatrūnahā viśvā sumanā dīdihī
naḥ ‖ 22 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

स्वदस्व । हव्या । सं । इषः । दिदीहि । अस्मद्र्यक् । सं। मिमीहि । श्रवांसि ।
विश्वान् । अग्ने । पृत्सु । तान् । जेषि । शत्रून् । अहा । विश्वा । सुमनाः । दीदिहि।
नः ॥ २२ ॥

svadasva | havyā | saṃ | iṣaḥ | didīhi | asmadryak | saṃ| mimīhi | śravāṃsi |
viśvān | agne | pṛtsu | tān | jeṣi | śatrūn | ahā | viśvā | sumanāḥ | dīdihi|
naḥ ‖ 22 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पशौ पुरोडाशस्विस्थकृतः स्वदस्व हव्येति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । स्वदस्व हव्या समिषो दिदीहीति पुरोडाशस्विस्थकृतः । आ. ३-५ । इति ॥ हे अग्ने हव्या हवनयोग्यानि हवींषि स्वदस्व । स्वादय । अस्माकमिषोऽन्नानि सं दिदीहि । सम्यक् प्रकाशय । दीपितानि तानि श्रवांस्यन्नान्यस्मद्रगस्मदभिमुखानि सं मिमीहि ' समानय । कुर्वित्यर्थः । ततः पृत्सु संग्रामेषु तान्बाधकान्विश्वान्य शत्रून् जेषि । जय । अथ सुमनाः शोभनमनस्कः सन् नोऽस्माकं विश्वाहा सर्वा ण्यहानि दीदिहि । अग्निहोत्रादिकर्मयोग्यानि प्रकाशय ॥ स्वदस्व । स्वद आस्वादने । लोटि रूपं । थासो लसार्वधातुकस्वरे धातुस्वरः । दिदीहि । दिवु क्रीडादावित्यस्य लोटि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः । परत्वात् हलि चेति दीर्घत्वे कृते पश्चाद्वलि लोपः । निघातः । अस्मद्रक् । अस्मानंचतीत्यंचतेः क्विप् । विश्वद्गेवयोश्च टेरिति यणः स्वरितत्वं । मिमीहि । माज् माने शब्दे च। जुहोत्यादिः । तस्य लोटि व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । निघातः । सुमनाः ! सोर्मनसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । दीदिहि । दिवेर्यज्‌लुकि लोटि तुजादित्पादभ्यासस्य दीर्घः । वलि लोपः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal sacrifice, for the puroḍāśa-sviṣṭakṛt, स्वदस्व हव्या (svadasva havyā) is the yājyā. It is also given in the sūtra: स्वदस्व हव्या समिषो दिदीहीति पुरोडाशस्विस्थकृतः (svadasva havyā samiṣo didīhīti puroḍāśasvisthakṛtaḥ) (Ā. 3-5). "O Agni, make the oblations fit for offering pleasing to the taste (स्वदस्व (svadasva), "make them taste sweet"). Cause our foods (इषः (iṣaḥ)) to shine forth well. When they have been made to shine, bring those foods (श्रवांसि (śravāṃsi)) together, facing us; make them so. Then conquer in the battles all those hostile enemies. And, being well-disposed, make shine for us all days, that is, make them fit for rites such as the Agnihotra."

p. 273

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • हव्या (havyā)—the oblations fit for the sacrifice
  • खादस्व (khādasva)—eat NOTE
  • इषः (iṣaḥ)—food
  • सं दिदीहि (saṃ didīhi)—furnish (to us) completely
  • श्रवांसि (śravāṃsi)—foods
  • अस्मद्रक् (asmadrak)—so as to face us
  • सं मिमीहि (saṃ mimīhi)—bring and set down
  • पृत्सु (pṛtsu)—in battles
  • विश्वान् (viśvān)—all
  • शत्रुन् (śatrun)—enemies (those)
  • जेषि (jeṣi)—conquer
  • सुमनाः (sumanāḥ)—having a favourable mind
  • नः (naḥ)—for us
  • विश्वा अहा (viśvā ahā)—all days
  • दीदिहि (dīdihi)—make shine so as to be fit for the Agnihotra
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, eat the oblations fit for the sacrifice. Furnish us complete food. Bring and set the foods facing us. In battles conquer all the enemies. With a favourable mind, make all days shine for us so as to be fit for the Agnihotra.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Taste (Agni) the oblations; make manifest (for us) abundant food : measure out the viands before us : you overcome all those (who are) our enemies in conflict : favorably inclined towards us lighten up all our (cere- monies) day by day.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That in the animal sacrifice, when the puroḍāśa-sviṣṭakṛt offering is made, this ṛc सदस्य हव्या (sadasya havyā) NOTE is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra सदस्व हव्या समिषो दिदीहीति पुरोडाशस्विस्थकृतः (sadasva havyā samiṣo didīhīti puroḍāśasvisthakṛtaḥ) (Ā. 3-5). The wishes prayed for are these: may Agni taste the oblations offered by the sacrificers; grant food to the sacrificers; provide bright foods easily; conquer the sacrificers' enemies; be gracious towards the sacrificers; and grant that rites such as the Agnihotra be accomplished without obstacle.

Sūkta 55 (Maṇḍala 3)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

उषसः पूर्वा इति द्वाविंशत्यृचं द्वितीयं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । उषस इत्यनुक्रमणिका । प्रजापतेरार्षं वैश्वदेवं प्रजापतिर्हि वैश्वदेवं हेति पूर्वसूक्ते हशब्दप्रयोगात् । सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । अत्राद्योषस्या ततः परं नवर्चोS-

Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning उषसः पूर्वा (uṣasaḥ pūrvā), of twenty-two ṛcs, is the second sūkta (of this group), in the Triṣṭubh metre. Its deity is Uṣas, according to the Anukramaṇikā. Its seer is Prajāpati, and it is addressed to the Viśvedevas, since the word ह (ha) is used in the preceding sūkta (प्रजापतिर्हि वैश्वदेवं हेति (prajāpatirhi vaiśvadevaṃ heti)). The sūkta's ritual use is indicated by the text itself (लैंगिकः (laiṃgikaḥ)). Here the first … NOTE

p. 274

ग्न्यादिदेवतास्ततः पराहोरात्रदेवताका ततश्चतस्रो रोदस्योः पंचदशी द्युनिशोर्वा षोडशी दिद्देवताका ततः षडृचो वर्षत इंद्रस्य केचिदग्नेष्टुश्चेति मन्यंते ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(This block continues Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta.) After the verses to Agni and the other deities comes a verse addressed to Day-and-Night (ahorātra-devatākā). Then four verses are to Rodasī, and the fifteenth is to Rodasī or to Dyunīśa (the heaven and the night). The sixteenth has the quarters (dik) as its deity. Then six verses are addressed to the rain-giving Indra; some hold that they belong to Agni and Tvaṣṭṛ. NOTE

Anuvāda: This sūkta, Uṣasaḥ pūrvāḥ, is the second sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has twenty-two Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is introduced with the word उषसः (uṣasaḥ).

For this sūkta, as stated for the preceding sūkta, Prajāpati is the deity, and the Viśvedevas are the deity. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The use of the sūkta in ritual is by indication (laiṅgika). In this sūkta the first Ṛk has Uṣas as its deity; the nine Ṛks after it (Ṛks 2–10) are to Agni and the others; the next Ṛk (Ṛk 11) is to Day-and-Night; the next three Ṛks (12–14) are to Rodasī; the fifteenth Ṛk is to Rodasī or to Dyunīśau; the sixteenth Ṛk is to the quarters; the six Ṛks after that are said to be to Indra, Parjanyātmā, Tvaṣṭṛ or Agni.

Sūkta 55. Maṇḍala 3; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 55. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 3; Vargas 28, 29, 30, 31. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 22. Ṛṣi: Prajāpati Vaiśvāmitra, or Vāc. Deity: the Viśvedevas. 1. Uṣas. 2–10. Agni. 11. Day-and-Night. 12–14. Rodasī. 15. Rodasī or Dyunīśau. 16. The quarters. 17–22. Indra, Parjanyātmā, Tvaṣṭṛ and Agni. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

उ॒षसः॒ पूर्वा॒ अध॒ यद्व्यू॒षुर्म॒हद्धि ज॑ज्ञॆ अ॒क्षरं॑ प॒दे
गोः ।
व्र॒ता दे॒वाना॒मुप॒ सु प्र॒भूष॑न्म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑॥

uṣasaḥ pūrvā adha yadvyūṣurmahaddhi jajñè akṣaraṃ pade
goḥ |
vratā devānāmupa su prabhūṣanmahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ‖

p. 275

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

उषसः । पूर्वाः । अध । यत् । विऊषुः । महत् । वि । जज्ञे । अक्षरं । पदे ।
गोः ।
व्रता । देवानां । उप । नु । प्रभूषन् । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥

uṣasaḥ | pūrvāḥ | adha | yat | viūṣuḥ | mahat | vi | jajñe | akṣaraṃ | pade |
goḥ |
vratā | devānāṃ | upa | nu | prabhūṣan | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पूर्वा उदयकालात्पाचीना उषसो यद्यदा व्यूषुर्व्यच्छंति अध तदानीमक्षरं । न क्षरतीत्यक्षरं । अविनाश्यादित्याख्यं महत्प्रभूतं ज्योतिर्गॊरुदकस्य पदे स्थाने समुद्रे नभसि वा वि जज्ञे । उत्पद्यते । अथोदिते सूर्ये प्रभूषन्नग्निहोत्रादिकर्मसु प्रभवितुमिच्छन्यजमानो व्रता कर्माणि देवानां नु क्षिप्रमुप समीपं तिष्ठति । योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । तदिदं देवानामेकं मुख्यमसुरत्वं । आस्यति क्षिपति सर्वानित्यसुरः प्रबलः । तस्य भावोऽसुरत्वं प्राबल्यं । महदैश्वर्यं ॥ व्यूषुः । उष प्लुष दाह इत्यस्य विपूर्वस्य लिट्युसि रूपं । सहेति योगविभागात्समासः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः। प्रभूषन्। भवतेः सनि द्विर्वचनस्य छंदसि विकल्पितत्पादत्र द्विर्वचनाभावः । तदंताच्चतरि रूपं । प्रादिसमासः । शतुर्लसार्वधातुकस्वरे धातुस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Pūrvāḥ" means the dawns that come before the time of sunrise. When they shine forth, then the imperishable (that which does not decay) great, abundant light called Āditya (the sun) is born in the "pada" of "go", that is, in the place of water: in the sea or in the sky. Then, once the sun has risen, the sacrificer who wishes to prosper in rites such as the Agnihotra offers the rites (व्रता (vratā) = rites) to the gods quickly; "upa" (near) is to be completed with a suitable verb, "stands near". This is the one chief "asuratva" of the gods. One who throws down (आस्यति (āsyati)) all is Asura, the mighty; his state is asuratva, might; "mahat" is lordship.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • पूर्वा (pūrvā)—preceding, earlier than the time of sunrise
  • उपसः (upasaḥ)—the dawns
  • यत् (yat)—when
  • व्यूषुः (vyūṣuḥ)—they shine forth
  • अध (adha)—immediately thereafter
  • अक्षरं (akṣaraṃ)—the imperishable
  • महत् (mahat)—and abundant light
  • गोः (goḥ)—of water
  • पदे (pade)—in the sky, the place of water
  • वि जज्ञॆ (vi jajñè)—becomes visible
  • प्रभूषन् (prabhūṣan)—(after sunrise) the sacrificer desiring to perform the sacrifice
  • व्रता (vratā)—his own sacrificial and other rites
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—to the gods
  • नु (nu)—quickly
  • उप (upa)—offers
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the dawns, which come before the time of sunrise, shine forth, immediately the imperishable great light becomes visible in the sky, the place of water. After sunrise the sacrificer who desires to perform the sacrifice offers his sacrificial and other rites to the gods. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

p. 276

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

When the preceding dawns appear, the great imperishable (light) is engendered in the (firmament, the) sphere of the waters, and then the worshipper is alert to perform the rites (due to) the gods, for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अक्षरं (akṣaraṃ)—न क्षरतीत्यक्षरं । (na kṣaratītyakṣaraṃ |) अविनाश्यादित्याख्यं । (avināśyādityākhyaṃ |) महत् प्रभूतं ज्योतिः । (mahat prabhūtaṃ jyotiḥ |) The word akṣara is said among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23) and among the names of water (Ni. 2-24). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning of this word as the radiance that never meets destruction, famed by the name Āditya, and shining abundantly.

गोः पदे विजज्ञे (goḥ pade vijajñe)—उदकस्य स्थाने समुद्रे नभसि वा उत्पद्यते । (udakasya sthāne samudre nabhasi vā utpadyate |) The Nirukta-writers have explained the meaning of the word go in various ways. Sāyaṇa describes that after the time of dawn passes, the sun rises in the sea, where waters are abundant, or in the sky, and that the word go is used in the sense of sea or sky.

व्रता (vratā)—कर्माणि । (karmāṇi |) The word vrata is explained by Yāska (Ni. 2-13): वृणोतीति व्रतं (vṛṇotīti vrataṃ), वारयतीति व्रतं (vārayatīti vrataṃ), अवृणोतीति शरीरं इति व्रतं । (avṛṇotīti śarīraṃ iti vrataṃ |) First: शुभमशुभं वा कृतं सदा वृणोति कर्तारं (śubhamaśubhaṃ vā kṛtaṃ sadā vṛṇoti kartāraṃ)—the fruit, good or bad, follows the one who did the work. Therefore the word vrata means action. Second: because it keeps those who practise rites such as the Agnihotra from enjoying objects of enjoyment, the meaning vrata is described. Third: because it is transformed into the seven bodily constituents, food too is called by the word vrata.

प्रभूषन् व्रता देवानां उपः नु नेष्यति (prabhūṣan vratā devānāṃ upaḥ nu neṣyati)—अग्निहोत्रादि कर्मसु प्रभवितुमिच्छ यजमानः कर्माणि देवानां उप समीपं नेष्यति— (agnihotrādi karmasu prabhavitumiccha yajamānaḥ karmāṇi devānāṃ upa samīpaṃ neṣyati—) it is explained that after the sun has half risen, the sacrificer who wishes to prosper offers the rites he performs, to win the satisfaction of the gods.

देवानां असुरत्वं एकं महत् (devānāṃ asuratvaṃ ekaṃ mahat)—in this sentence Sāyaṇa explains the word asura thus: अस्यति क्षिपति सर्वानित्यसुरः प्रबलः (asyati kṣipati sarvānityasuraḥ prabalaḥ), तस्य भावः असुरत्वं प्राबल्यं । (tasya bhāvaḥ asuratvaṃ prābalyaṃ |) He who has abundant power to subdue all is Asura, and the power of one so endowed is asuratva. It is described that, in accord with the performance of sacrifices and so on, with the manifestation of the sun's rising, and because of the course of the dawn-times, the lordship of the gods is complete, in its abundant greatness, and chiefly praiseworthy.

p. 277

The word asura is said among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-22). And: असुराः असुरताः स्थानेष्टस्ताः स्थानेभ्य इति वा अपि ना असुरिति प्राणनाम अस्तः शरीरे भवति तेन तद्वंतः (asurāḥ asuratāḥ sthāneṣṭastāḥ sthānebhya iti vā api nā asuriti prāṇanāma astaḥ śarīre bhavati tena tadvaṃtaḥ) (Ni. 3-8): that is, those who are settled in a region or place, or those who have fallen from their places, or those who have restless breath; thus Yāska has explained the meaning of asura. And Yāska cites the Brāhmaṇa passage सोर्दॆवानसृजत तत् सुराणां सुरत्वं असोरसुरानसृजत तदसुराणामसुरत्वमिति विज्ञायते (sordèvānasṛjata tat surāṇāṃ suratvaṃ asorasurānasṛjata tadasurāṇāmasuratvamiti vijñāyate): Brahmā created the gods from a praiseworthy region of the Supreme Self, and created the asuras from an unpraiseworthy region.

For the word asura here the commentator gives the meaning निरसितारं देवं (nirasitāraṃ devaṃ): the god who overcomes (enemies). Although the sense "demons" is current for asura, in many places the word has a meaning favourable to the gods. In this Aṣṭaka the word asura occurs in about ten Ṛks, and everywhere it has the sense of the gods.

In the Ṛk दिवो अस्तोष्यसुरस्य वीरैरिषुध्येव मरुतो रोदस्कोः । (divo astoṣyasurasya vīrairiṣudhyeva maruto rodaskoḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-1): असुरस्य निरसितव्यानामसुराणां निरसितुः । (asurasya nirasitavyānāmasurāṇāṃ nirasituḥ |) कर्मणि षष्ठी । (karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī |) निरसितारं तमेव देवं (nirasitāraṃ tameva devaṃ) (Rudra): the meaning is Rudra, who overcomes the asuras.

शतं राज्यो नाधमानस्य निष्काञ्चितमश्वान्प्रयतान्त्सद्य आदं । शतं कक्षीवा असुरस्य गोनां दिवि श्रवोजरमा ततान ॥ (śataṃ rājyo nādhamānasya niṣkāñcitamaśvānprayatāntsadya ādaṃ | śataṃ kakṣīvā asurasya gonāṃ divi śravojaramā tatāna ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-2). Here: असुरस्य धनानां निरसितुर्दानशीलस्य राज्ञः स्वनयस्य । (asurasya dhanānāṃ nirasiturdānaśīlasya rājñaḥ svanayasya |) That is, "of the king Svanaya, who gives wealth and the like"; thus the word asura refers to King Svanaya.

इंद्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेंद्राय मही पृथिवी वरीमभिर्दुम्मसाता वरीमभिः ॥ (iṃdrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnateṃdrāya mahī pṛthivī varīmabhirdummasātā varīmabhiḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-1). Here the word asura is explained असुरः निरसनशीलः शत्रूणां पुण्यकृतामेव तन्निवासात् (asuraḥ nirasanaśīlaḥ śatrūṇāṃ puṇyakṛtāmeva tannivāsāt) (दौः द्युलोकः (dauḥ dyulokaḥ)): it is an epithet of the word दौः (dauḥ), the heavenly world, which is a dwelling for the meritorious who perform sacrifices and so on and gives no room to their enemies.

प्र सा क्षितिरसुर या महि प्रिय ऋतावानावृतमा घोषतो बृहत् । (pra sā kṣitirasura yā mahi priya ṛtāvānāvṛtamā ghoṣato bṛhat |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-4). In this Ṛk the word asura is explained हे असुरा असुर् बलवंतौ मित्रावरुणौ । (he asurā asur balavaṃtau mitrāvaruṇau |) As an epithet of Mitra and Varuṇa it states their strength and power.

p. 278

त्वं राजेंद्र ये च देवा रक्षा नृन्पाह्यसुर त्वमस्मान् । (tvaṃ rājeṃdra ye ca devā rakṣā nṛnpāhyasura tvamasmān |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-174-1). In this Ṛk: असुर शत्रूणां निरसितः हे इंद्र । (asura śatrūṇāṃ nirasitaḥ he iṃdra |) "O Indra, who overcomes enemies"; the word asura is used of Indra.

त्वमग्ने रुद्रो असुरो महो दिवस्त्वं शर्धो मारुतं पृक्ष ईशिषे । (tvamagne rudro asuro maho divastvaṃ śardho mārutaṃ pṛkṣa īśiṣe |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-6). In this Ṛk the word asura gives the sense: असुरः शत्रूणां निरसिता रुद्रोऽसि । (asuraḥ śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā rudro 'si |) "You are Rudra, who conquers the enemy."

त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः । (tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-10). Here the word asura means हे असुर शत्रूणां क्षेपक वरुण । (he asura śatrūṇāṃ kṣepaka varuṇa |) "O Varuṇa, who overthrows enemies"; the word asura refers to Varuṇa.

मा नो वधैर्वरुण ये त इष्टावेनः कृण्वंतमसुर भ्रीणंति । (mā no vadhairvaruṇa ye ta iṣṭāvenaḥ kṛṇvaṃtamasura bhrīṇaṃti |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-7). In this Ṛk too: हे असुर पापकृतां निरसितः वरुण । (he asura pāpakṛtāṃ nirasitaḥ varuṇa |) "Varuṇa, who restrains those who do wrong"; it refers to Varuṇa.

बृहस्पते तपुषाश्नेव विध्य वृक्कद्वरसो असुरस्य वीरान् । (bṛhaspate tapuṣāśneva vidhya vṛkkadvaraso asurasya vīrān |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-30-4). In this Ṛk the word असुरस्य (asurasya) is an epithet of the word वृकद्वरसः (vṛkadvarasaḥ): संवृतद्वारस्य असुरस्य (saṃvṛtadvārasya asurasya)—of the asura who has shut and barred the door; thus the ordinary meaning of asura is explained.

पिता यज्ञा नामसुरो विपश्चितां विमानमग्निर्वयुनं च वाघतां । (pitā yajñā nāmasuro vipaścitāṃ vimānamagnirvayunaṃ ca vāghatāṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-4). In this Ṛk: असुरो बलप्रदः (asuro balapradaḥ)—the word asura is used of Agni.

Here the word एक (eka) is used in the sense "chief", not as a numeral. And the word महत् (mahat), Sāyaṇa's explanation says, means lordship, that is, having everything under one's control. By this it is suggested that the might of the gods is unequalled, or that the gods have the power, unattainable by any others, of keeping everything under their control. And this being so, the

p. 279

might of this lordship is also chief; thus a threefold meaning is also suggested through the relation of subject and predicate in the words एकं असुरत्वं महत् (ekaṃ asuratvaṃ mahat).

In this Ṛk, which describes the power of the deity Uṣas, it is described that since the performance of sacrifices and other rites by sacrificers, the sunrise and other activities come about through the unsurpassed lordship of the deity Uṣas, the greatness of the deity is chief.

In every Ṛk of this sūkta the fourth pāda of this Ṛk, महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं (mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ), is recited again and again like a refrain.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

मोषूणो॒ आत्र॑ जुहुरंत दे॒वा मा पूर्वे॑ अग्ने पि॒तरः॑ ॒ पदज्ञाः ।
पु॒रा॒ण्योः सद्म॑नोः के॒तुरं॒तर्म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑॥

moṣūṇo ātra juhuraṃta devā mā pūrve agne pitaraḥ
padajñāḥ |
purāṇyoḥ sadmanoḥ keturaṃtarmahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

मो इति । सु । नः । अत्र । जुहुरंत । देवाः । मा । पूर्वे । अग्ने । पितरः ।
पदज्ञाः ।
पुराण्योः । सद्मनोः । केतुः । अंतः । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ २ ॥

mo iti | su | naḥ | atra | juhuraṃta | devāḥ | mā | pūrve | agne | pitaraḥ |
padajñāḥ |
purāṇyoḥ | sadmanoḥ | ketuḥ | aṃtaḥ | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे अग्ने आत्रास्मिन्काले देवा नोऽस्मान् सु सुष्टु मो जुहुरंत । मा हिंस्युः । तथा पदज्ञाः कर्माण्यनुष्ठाय देवपदमनुभवंतः पूर्व पुरातनाः पितरो मा हिंसिपुः । यस्मात्केतुर्यज्ञानां प्रज्ञापकः । सूर्यः पुराणोः पुरातनयोः सद्मनोः । सीदंत्यनयोर्देवमनुष्या इति सद्मनी रोदसी । तयोरंतॆर्मध्य उदेति । तस्मादत्र मा हिंसंतित्यर्थः । महद्देवानामित्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥ जुहुरंत । हृ प्रसह्यकरणे । लुजि जुहोत्यादित्वात् श्लुः । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । बहुलं छंदसीत्युत्वं । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वाददादादेशाभावे०ंतादेशः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, at this time (अत्र (atra)) may the gods not harm us (नः (naḥ)); सु (su) (well), मो जुहुरंत (mo juhuraṃta): let them not harm." Likewise the ancient fathers (पितरः (pitaraḥ)), who know the step (पदज्ञाः (padajñāḥ)), having performed rites and attained the divine station, must not harm us. For the sun, the signal (केतुः (ketuḥ)) who makes the sacrifices known, rises between the two ancient dwellings (सद्मनोः (sadmanoḥ)): they are called sadmanī, heaven and earth, because gods and men dwell (sīdanti) in them. Therefore here (at that time) they do not harm; this is the meaning. महद्देवानामित्यादि (mahaddevānāmityādi) is as before.

p. 280

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • अत्र (atra)—at this time of the sacrifice
  • देवा: (devā:)—the gods
  • नः (naḥ)—us
  • सु मो जुहुरंतॆ (su mo juhuraṃtè)—let them not harm in the least
  • पदज्ञा: (padajñā:)—those who have attained godhood
  • पूर्वे (pūrve)—and ancient
  • पितरः (pitaraḥ)—our fathers also
  • मा (mā)—let them not harm us
  • केतुः (ketuḥ)—the sun, who makes the sacrificial work known
  • पुराण्योः (purāṇyoḥ)—of the ancient
  • सद्मनोः (sadmanoḥ)—heaven and earth
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—shining in the middle (let him not harm us)
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, at this time of the sacrifice let the gods not harm us in the least; let our ancient fathers too, who have attained godhood, not harm us. Let the sun, who makes the sacrificial work known, shining in the middle of ancient heaven and earth, not harm us. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Let not the gods, Agni, now do us harm, nor the ancient progenitors, who have come to know the degree (of divinity) ; nor the manifester of light between the two ancient dwellings (earth and heaven, the sun) ; for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

केतुः पुराण्योः सद्मनोः अंतः (ketuḥ purāṇyoḥ sadmanoḥ aṃtaḥ)—यज्ञानां प्रज्ञापकः सूर्यः पुरातनयोः (yajñānāṃ prajñāpakaḥ sūryaḥ purātanayoḥ) सीदंत्यनयोः देवमनुष्या इति सद्मनी (sīdaṃtyanayoḥ devamanuṣyā iti sadmanī) तयोः मध्यॆ उदेति । (tayoḥ madhyè udeti |) Having explained the meaning of the word ketu as the sun, who marks the required time of duty, the performance of sacrifice, the commentary says that this sun rises in the middle of heaven and earth, which have existed from ancient times and have granted gods and men the opportunity to live in comfort. At this time of rising, Agni is prayed to: देवाः पितरः नः मा जुहुरंत (devāḥ pitaraḥ naḥ mā juhuraṃta) अर्स्मा मा हिंस्युः (arsmā mā hiṃsyuḥ)—let the gods, and also the fathers who have attained the state of gods through the performance of sacrifices and other rites, not harm us, the sacrificers. The word sadmanī is said among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22).

पितरः (pitaraḥ)—Among the dead, the meritorious dwell in the third heaven; they are called fathers. They are the original progenitors, who followed the ancient paths (10-15-8, 10): the dead follow the very path laid out by these ṛṣis and go to their vicinity.

p. 281

(10-14-2, 7, 15). He is connected with the third step of Viṣṇu (10-15-3; compare 1-154-5). Two sūktas have the Pitṛs as deity (10-15; 10-54).

Among the Pitṛs there are the groups of the Navagvas, Virūpas, Aṅgirases, Atharvans, Bhṛgus and Vasiṣṭhas (10-14-4 to 6; 10-15-8). The last four of these are names. They are also the names of the seers of the Atharvaveda and of the second and seventh maṇḍalas of the Ṛgveda. Among them the Aṅgirases have a special relation to Yama (10-14-3, 5). The Pitṛs are also divided into avarāḥ (lower rank), parāḥ (higher rank) and madhyamāḥ (middle rank). Although they are not all known to their descendants, Agni knows all of them (10-15-1, 2, 13). The favour of the Pitṛs is prayed for together with the Dawns, rivers, mountains, heaven and earth, Pūṣan and the Ṛbhus (6-52-4; 6-75-10; 7-35-12; 1-06-3). There is a prayer that they grant wealth, offspring and long life to their descendants who seek their gracious glance (10-14-6) (10-15-7, 11; A. Ve. 18-3-14; 18-4-62) NOTE. The Vasiṣṭhas are prayed to help their descendants (7-33-1; compare 10-15-8); Turuṣva, Yadu and Ugradeva are also praised individually (1-36.18).

The Pitṛs are immortal (A. Ve. 6-41-3); they are also called gods (10-56-4). In the Aṅgirases and some groups, priesthood is joined to divinity. Some acts of creation are also ascribed to certain Pitṛs: it was they who made the sky adorned with stars; light by day and darkness by night came from them (18-68-11); they found the hidden light and brought about the dawn (7-26-4; compare 10-107-1); and together with Soma they spread out heaven and earth (8.48-13). Just as there is a difference between the Agni that carries the oblation to the gods (havyavāha) and the Agni that burns the corpse (kravyād) (10-16-9), so there is a difference between the path of the gods and the path of the ancestors (10-2-7; compare 10-18-1; 10-88-15). In the same way a distinction between the world of heaven and the world of the Pitṛs is stated; the door of the world of the gods is said to lie in the north-east (Śa. Brā. 6-6-2-9) and the door of the world of the Pitṛs in the south-east (Śa. Brā. 13-8-1-5). The Pitṛs and men are different classes, and their creation is also separate (Tai. Brā. 2-3-8-2). The Pitṛs dwell on earth, in the atmosphere and in heaven (A. Ve. 18-2-49; compare Ṛ. Ve. 10-15-2).

The ancient Pitṛs once offered a Soma oblation (10-15-8). They pass their time happily with Yama (10-14-1; compare 10-135-1 and A. Ve. 18-4-10) and feast with the gods (7-76-4). Living like the gods, they sometimes receive the worship proper to the gods, and Indra and

p. 282

the worship proper to the gods. They come in the chariot of Indra and the gods (10-15-10). They too have a longing for the Soma juice (10-15-5, 6); seated facing south on the darbha seat, they drink the pressed drink (10-15-5, 6). They are eager to drink the Soma juice prepared for them; they are invited to come with Yama, his father Vivasvat and Agni, and with them to accept what has been offered (10-15-8 to 11; 10-14-4, 5). They come in thousands and sit down in order on the darbha seat (10-15-10, 11). When the Pitṛs come to the sacrificial hall, certain piśācas also mingle with them in the guise of their friends (Ā. Ve. 18-2-28) NOTE.

When food is offered to the gods one says "svāhā", and when it is given to the Pitṛs one says "svadhā" (10-14-3); in all rites this distinction between the share of the gods and that of the Pitṛs must be kept (Śa. Brā. 4-4-2-2). They too receive worship; the prayers are that they listen to the entreaty of their followers, take their side, and forgive the lapses that naturally occur, and so on (10-15-2, 6; compare 3-55-2).

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

वि मे॑ पुरु॒त्रा प॑तयंति॒ कामाः॒ शम्यच्छा॑दीद्ये पू॒र्व्याणि॑ ।
समि॑द्दे अ॒ग्नावृ॒तमिद्व॑देम म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥३॥

vi me purutrā patayaṃti kāmāḥ śamyacchādīdye pūrvyāṇi |
samidde agnāvṛtamidvadema mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖3‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

वि । मे । पुरुत्रा । पतयंति । कामाः । शमि । अच्छ । दीद्ये । पूर्व्याणि ।
सम्इद्दे । अग्नौ । ऋतं । इत् । वदेम । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥

vi | me | purutrā | patayaṃti | kāmāḥ | śami | accha | dīdye | pūrvyāṇi |
samidde | agnau | ṛtaṃ | it | vadema | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे अग्ने मे मम पुरुत्रा बहवः कामा अभिलाषा वि पतयंति । विविधं गच्छंति । शम्यग्निष्टोमादिलक्षणं कर्माच्चाभिलक्ष्याहं पूर्वाणि पुरातनानि स्तोत्राणि तदर्थं दीद्ये । दीपयामि । पश्चाद्यज्ञार्थमग्नौ समिद्धे दीप्यमाने सत्यृतमित् सत्यमेव वदेम । अनृतवचने हि यज्ञे वैगुण्यं स्यादिति ॥ पुरुत्रा । देवमनुष्यपुरुषेत्यादिना त्राप्रत्ययः । पतयंति । पत्लृ गत् । स्वार्थिको ण्च् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, my many desires (कामाः (kāmāḥ), longings) go off in various directions (वि पतयंति (vi patayaṃti)). Aiming at a rite such as the Agniṣṭoma (शमि (śami) is the rite), I kindle (दीद्ये (dīdye): I light up) ancient hymns for its sake. Afterwards, when the fire is kindled for the sacrifice, we shall speak only the truth, for if untruth is spoken there would be a defect in the sacrifice.

p. 283

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मे (me)—my
  • पुरुत्रा (purutrā)—of many kinds
  • कामाः (kāmāḥ)—desires
  • वि पतयंति (vi patayaṃti)—spread out in various ways
  • शमि (śami)—the rite of the form of Agniṣṭoma and the like
  • अच्छ (accha)—aiming at
  • पूर्वाणि (pūrvāṇi)—ancient hymns
  • दीद्ये (dīdye)—I recite, making them shine
  • अग्नौ (agnau)—when Agni
  • समिद्धे (samiddhe)—is kindled (for the sacrifice)
  • ऋतमित् (ṛtamit)—only true speech
  • वदेम (vadema)—we utter
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, my desires, of many kinds, spread out in various ways. For the sake of the rite of the form of Agniṣṭoma and the like, I recite ancient hymns, making them shine. When Agni is kindled for the sacrifice, we utter only true speech. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Variously do my manifold desires alight : present at the solemnity, I recite ancient (hymns) : when the fire is kindled we speak indeed the truth, for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शमि अच्छ पूर्वाणि दीद्ये (śami accha pūrvāṇi dīdye)—अग्निष्टोमादिलक्षणं कर्म अभिलक्ष्य अहं पुरातनानि स्तोत्राणि तदर्थं दीपयामि । (agniṣṭomādilakṣaṇaṃ karma abhilakṣya ahaṃ purātanāni stotrāṇi tadarthaṃ dīpayāmi |). The word शमि (śami) is listed among the names of rites (Ni. 3-2). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as sacrificial rites such as the Agniṣṭoma. The sacrificer, addressing Agni, recites praises so that his many desires may be fulfilled; and, as for अनृतवचने हि यज्ञॆ वैगुण्यं स्यादिति ऋतमित् सत्यवेव वदेम (anṛtavacane hi yajñè vaiguṇyaṃ syāditi ṛtamit satyaveva vadema), he explains that if falsehood is spoken while the sacrifice is going on, the sacrifice would not yield its full fruit or would be afflicted with deficiency, and therefore he speaks true words. It is described that Agni, having heard the sacrificer's praises, fulfils all his wishes, and that he possesses a chief and unequalled greatness.

p. 284

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒मा॒नो राजा॒ विभृ॑तः पुरु॒त्रा शये॑ श॒यासु॒ प्रयु॑तो॒ ॑ वनानु ।
अ॒न्या व॒त्सं भर॑ति॒ क्षेति॑ मा॒ता म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑॥४॥

samāno rājā vibhṛtaḥ purutrā śaye śayāsu prayuto
vanānu |
anyā vatsaṃ bharati kṣeti mātā mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ‖4‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

समानः । राजा । विभृतः । पुरुत्रा । शये । शयासु । प्रयुतः । वना । अनु ।
अन्या । वत्सं । भरति । क्षेति । माता । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ ४ ॥

samānaḥ | rājā | vibhṛtaḥ | purutrā | śaye | śayāsu | prayutaḥ | vanā | anu |
anyā | vatsaṃ | bharati | kṣeti | mātā | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

समानः साधारणः सर्वेषां । यद्वा । एक एव राजा दीप्यमानोऽग्निः पुरुत्रा बहुषु देशेषु विभृतोऽग्नि होत्रार्थं विहृतो भवति । यद्वा । राजाभिषुतः सोमः सर्वेषु देशेषु यज्ञार्थं विहृतो भवति । स चाग्निः सोमो वा शयासु शेरते हविरादयः पदार्था अत्रेति शया वेद्यः । तासु शये । शेते । निवसति । वनानु अनुवनं वनेष्वरणिरूपेषु काष्ठेषु प्रयुतो विभक्तोऽग्निर्वर्तते । सोमश्चेद्वनेषु चमसेषु विभक्तो वर्तते । तस्य द्वे मातरौ द्यावापृथिव्यौ । तयोरन्या द्यौरस्या भूमेर्जायमानतया वत्सं वत्सभूतमग्निं सोमं वा भरति । वृष्टा दिरूपेण भरति । पोषयति । माता वसुधा क्षेति । केवलं निवासयति ॥ विभृतः । हृञ् हरणे । कर्मणि क्तः । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । पुरुत्रा । अधिकरणे त्राप्रत्ययः । शये । शीज् स्वप्ने । लोपस्त इति तकारलोपः । शीजः सार्वधातुके गुणः । शयासु । शीञ् स्वप्ने । एरजित्यधिकरणेऽच् । भरति । भृञ् भरणे । भूवादिः । एकान्याभ्यां समर्थाभ्यामिति पूर्वस्य न निघातः । क्षेति । क्षि निवासगत्योरित्यस्य लटि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

समानः (samānaḥ) means common to all. Or else: the one shining king, Agni, is carried about (विभृतः (vibhṛtaḥ)) in many places for the Agnihotra. Or else: the king is the pressed Soma, who is carried about in all places for the sacrifice. That Agni or Soma lies (शये (śaye): rests, dwells) in the शयासु (śayāsu), that is, the altars, where the oblations and other things lie. In the वनानु (vanānu), that is, in the logs of wood in the form of the araṇi, Agni exists, distributed; if it is Soma, he exists distributed in the वनेषु (vaneṣu), the cups (चमसेषु (camaseṣu)). He has two mothers, heaven and earth. Of these, the one, heaven, bears (भरति (bharati)) the child (वत्सं (vatsaṃ))—Agni or Soma, who is born of the other, the earth—by rain and the like; she nourishes him. The mother, earth, क्षेति (kṣeti): merely gives a dwelling.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • समानः (samānaḥ)—he who is common to the whole world (the one sole lord)
  • राजा (rājā)—Agni, the shining one
  • पुरुत्रा (purutrā)—in many regions
  • विभृतः (vibhṛtaḥ)—is carried (for the sacrifice)
  • शयासु (śayāsu)—in the sacrificial altars
  • शये (śaye)—is established
  • वनानु (vanānu)—in the logs of the form of araṇi
  • प्रयुतः (prayutaḥ)—is distributed
  • अन्या (anyā)—one (of heaven and earth), the heavenly world
  • वत्सं (vatsaṃ)—Agni, who is like a son
  • भरति (bharati)—nourishes
  • माता (mātā)—the earth, who is of the form of a mother

p. 285

  • क्षेति (kṣeti)—gives room to dwell
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the one sole lord of the whole world, the shining one, is carried to many regions for the sacrifice and is established in the sacrificial altars. He lies hidden, distributed, in the logs of the form of araṇi. Of heaven and earth, the heavenly world nourishes Agni, who is like a son; the earth, who is of the form of a mother, gives room to dwell. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The universal sovereign is conveyed to many directions : he sleeps in the places of repose : he is connected with the forests : one mother (heaven) nourishes the child ; the other (earth) gives him a dwelling : great and unqualled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

समानः राजा पुरुत्रा विभृतः (samānaḥ rājā purutrā vibhṛtaḥ)—सर्वेषां साधारणः दीप्यमानो अग्निः बहुषु देशेषु अग्निहोत्रार्थं विहृतो भवति । (sarveṣāṃ sādhāraṇaḥ dīpyamāno agniḥ bahuṣu deśeṣu agnihotrārthaṃ vihṛto bhavati |). One kind of meaning is stated: Agni, who is regarded by all without any distinction of less or more, and who shines with abundant radiance, moves about in many regions so that the Agnihotra and other rites performed by sacrificers may be accomplished.

In the second meaning the word राजा (rājā) is used in the sense of Soma. Soma (and likewise Agni), though one, is pressed at one time in the many different sacrifices and is thus common to all the priests. It is therefore explained that he is useful for the sacrifice in all regions.

शयासु (śayāsu)—शेरते हविरादयः पदार्थाः अत्र (śerate havirādayaḥ padārthāḥ atra): it is described as the sacrificial altars on which things in the form of oblations and other things are placed. Both Agni and this Soma are established on the altars by the priests and others.

Agni is वनानु प्रयुतः (vanānu prayutaḥ)—he is separate in the piece of wood that is in the form of the araṇi. In the same way Soma too वनेषु चमसेषु विभक्तः वर्तते (vaneṣu camaseṣu vibhaktaḥ vartate)—he is placed so as to be separate in the vessel called camasa which is used in the sacrifice.

p. 286

By these two statements, समानः राजा पुरुत्रा विधृतः शयासु शेरते (samānaḥ rājā purutrā vidhṛtaḥ śayāsu śerate), a common property of Agni and Soma is stated, so that their similarity is understood. Yāska has read the word वन (vana) among the names of rays (Ni. 2-15). Sāyaṇa has explained the meanings araṇi and camasa. Heaven and earth perform the function of a mother for Agni and for Soma.

अन्या वत्सं भरति (anyā vatsaṃ bharati)—द्यौः अन्याः भूमेः जायमानतया वत्सभूतमग्निं सोमं वा पोषयति । (dyauḥ anyāḥ bhūmeḥ jāyamānatayā vatsabhūtamagniṃ somaṃ vā poṣayati |). The heavenly world nourishes Soma, who is produced on the earth, and Agni, who is produced from the araṇis, by supplying waters in the form of rain, as one nourishes a child.

माता क्षेति (mātā kṣeti)—वसुधा निवासयति (vasudhā nivāsayati). The earth provides a dwelling-place so that the two may live happily. Producing and providing a dwelling-place are both the function of a mother. Since this function is the same for both Agni and Soma, the earth is the mother of both. The heavenly world, too, is a mother because it nourishes and makes them grow; and thus the unequalled might of the gods is described.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

आ॒क्षित्पूर्वा॒ स्वप॑रा अनू॒रुत्स॒द्यो जा॒तासु॒ तरु॑णीष्ट्॒वंतः ।
अं॒तर्व॑तीः सवते॒ अप्र॑वीता म॒हद्दे॒वेना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥

ākṣitpūrvā svaparā anūrutsadyo jātāsu taruṇīṣṭvaṃtaḥ |
aṃtarvatīḥ savate apravītā mahaddevenāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

आक्षितित् । पूर्वासु । अपराः । अनूरुत् । सद्यः । जातासु । तरुणीषु । अंतरिति ।
अंतःसवतीः । सुवते । अप्रवीताः । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ ५ ॥

ākṣitit | pūrvāsu | aparāḥ | anūrut | sadyaḥ | jātāsu | taruṇīṣu | aṃtariti |
aṃtaḥsavatīḥ | suvate | apravītāḥ | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पूर्वासु जीर्णास्वोषधीष्वाक्षिदावर्तमानस्तथापरा नव्या ओषधीरनूरुदनुरुंधन् उत्पत्त्यानुगुण्येनानुतिष्ठन्नग्निः सूर्यो वा सद्यो जातासु तदानीमुत्पन्नासु तरुणेषु पल्लवितास्वोषधीष्वंतर्वर्तते । ता ओषधयोऽप्रवीताः

Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, or Sūrya, abiding (आक्षित् (ākṣit)) in the old, decayed herbs, and likewise following (अनूरुत् (anūrut)) the new herbs, acting in accord with their origin, is within the herbs that have just been born (सद्यो जातासु (sadyo jātāsu)), that is, newly arisen, young and sprouted. Those herbs are अप्रवीताः (apravītāḥ) … (the text of the block breaks off here; the next window continues).

p. 287

Ṛk 5 (continued)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

केनापि पुरुषेणानिषिक्तरेतस्का अनभ्यक्ता वा अंतवर्ततीरग्निना गर्भवत्यो भूत्वा सुवते । फलं पुष्पं चोत्पादयंति । तदिदं देवानामैश्वर्यं ॥ आक्षित् । क्षि निवासगत्योः । क्विप् । अनूरुत् । अनौ रुध कामे । अस्मात् क्विप् । अन्वेषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः । कृत्स्वरः । तरुणीषु । नञ्

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the verse's explanation. Those plants, without having been impregnated by any male, or unanointed, are filled within by Agni and become pregnant. They bear fruit and produce flowers. This is the lordship of the gods.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • पूर्वासु (pūrvāsu)—in the ancient plants
  • आक्षित् (ākṣit)—Agni, who had pervaded
  • अपराः (aparāḥ)—in the new plants
  • अनूरुत् (anūrut)—enters (afterwards)
  • सद्यो जातासु (sadyo jātāsu)—in those just produced
  • तरुणीषु (taruṇīṣu)—in the plants in the form of shoots
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—enters within
  • अप्रवीताः (apravītāḥ)—even though there is no contact with a male
  • अंतर्वतीः (aṃtarvatīḥ)—those plants that bear a womb (embryo)
  • सुवते (suvate)—bear flowers and the like
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who had pervaded the ancient plants, comes to be within the new plants. Those plants, becoming pregnant even without contact with a male, bear flowers and fruits. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Existing in ancient plants, abiding afterwards in new, he enters into the young (herbs) as soon as they are produced : unimpregnated they become pregnant and bear fruit : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the feminine words पूर्वासु (pūrvāsu) अपराः (aparāḥ), जातासु (jātāsu), तरुणेषु (taruṇeṣu), अंतर्वतीः (aṃtarvatīḥ) are used, and also the verbal forms अक्षित् (akṣit) and अनूरुत् (anūrut). In describing the greatness of Agni or Sūrya, who performs actions so that the growth of the world may be continuous, the juxtaposition of the words used here describes, by transfer and in the manner of poetry, the story of a householder, or of a lover, who carries on the life of the world. As a lustful man abandons an aged woman, Agni abandons पूर्वासु आक्षित् जीर्णासु ओषधीषु आवर्तमानः (pūrvāsu ākṣit jīrṇāsu oṣadhīṣu āvartamānaḥ), the plants that are very old and withering;

p. 288

and अपराः अनुरुत्—नव्याः ओषदीः उत्पत्यानुगुण्येन अनु तिष्ठन् (aparāḥ anurut—navyāḥ oṣadīḥ utpatyānuguṇyena anu tiṣṭhan): he follows the tender herbs that are newly growing and radiant, in keeping with their growth. By this too the conduct of a lover is understood. जातासु तरुणीषु अंतः—तदानीं उत्कन्नासु पल्लवितासु ओषधीषु अंतः वर्तते (jātāsu taruṇīṣu aṃtaḥ—tadānīṃ utkannāsu pallavitāsu oṣadhīṣu aṃtaḥ vartate): he abides within the herbs that have just then been born and are furnished with new sprouts, remaining inside them so that they may grow, and nourishing them. Thus the greatness of Agni is stated: he is the cause of the origin, continuance and dissolution of plants. But the herbs, like women in the world, obtain flowers, fruits and the like even without connection with a male; since such a making is the work of the gods, the might of the gods is described as extraordinary.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

श॒युः प॒रस्ता॒दध॒ नु द्वि॑मा॒ताबं॑ध॒नश्च॑रति व॒त्स एकः॑ ।
मि॒त्रस्य॒ ता वरु॑णस्य व्र॒तानि॑ म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥ ६ ॥

śayuḥ parastādadha nu dvimātābaṃdhanaścarati vatsa ekaḥ |
mitrasya tā varuṇasya vratāni mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शयुः । परस्तात् । अध । नु । द्विमाता । अबंधनः । चरति । वत्सः । एकः ।
मित्रस्य । ता । वरुणस्य । व्रतानि । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ ६ ॥

śayuḥ | parastāt | adha | nu | dvimātā | abaṃdhanaḥ | carati | vatsaḥ | ekaḥ |
mitrasya | tā | varuṇasya | vratāni | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

द्विमाता । हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ मातरौ यस्य स द्विमाता । यद्वा । ध्वयोर्लोकयोर्निमार्ता सूर्यः परस्तात्पश्चिमायां दिश्यस्तवेलायां।शयुः शयानोऽव्याप्रियमाणो भवति । अध नु अथोदयवेलायामेको द्यावापृथिव्यो 8 साधारणस्तयो रसादानाद्वत्सः पुत्रोऽबंधनोऽप्रतिबद्धगतिरनालंबन एकः सन् चरति । नभसि गच्छति । ता तानीमानि मित्रस्य वरुणस्य मित्रावरुणयोर्व्रतानि कर्माणि। शयुः । शीज् स्वप्ने । भृमृशीत्य चरीत्यादिना उप्रत्ययः । द्विमाता । नद्यृतश्चेति प्राप्तस्य कप ऋतश्चंदसीति प्रतिषेधः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

द्विमाता (dvimātā): he whose two mothers are heaven and earth. Or else, he who is the maker of the two worlds: Sūrya. परस्तात् (parastāt): in the western quarter, at the time of setting, he is शयुः (śayuḥ), lying down, not active. अध नु (adha nu): then, at the time of rising, the one calf, common to heaven and earth, their son because he draws their sap, अबंधनः (abaṃdhanaḥ), with unobstructed course and without support, being alone, चरति (carati), moves in the sky. ता (tā): these are the व्रतानि (vratāni), the works, of Mitra and Varuṇa, of Mitra-and-Varuṇa.

p. 289

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • द्विमाता (dvimātā)—Āditya, who has both heaven and earth as mother
  • परस्तात् (parastāt)—in the western quarter
  • शयुः (śayuḥ)—is laid to rest
  • अध नु (adha nu)—afterwards (at the time of rising)
  • एकः (ekaḥ)—the one common (to both heaven and earth)
  • वत्सः (vatsaḥ)—son (Āditya)
  • अबंधनः (abaṃdhanaḥ)—having an unhindered course
  • चरति (carati)—moves in the sky
  • ता (tā)—all these goings and comings (of Āditya)
  • मित्रस्य (mitrasya)—of Mitra (and)
  • वरुणस्य (varuṇasya)—of Varuṇa
  • व्रतानि (vratāni)—are the works
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Āditya, who has both heaven and earth as mother, is laid to rest in the western quarter. Afterwards, at the time of rising, the son (Āditya), common to both heaven and earth, moves in the sky with unhindered course. All these goings and comings of Āditya are the works of Mitra and Varuṇa. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The child of two mothers sleeps in the west, but (in the morning) the single infant proceeds unobstructed (through the sky) : these are the functions of Mitra and Varuna : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

द्विमाता परस्तात् शयुः (dvimātā parastāt śayuḥ)—द्वे द्यावापृथिव्यौ मातरौ यस्य सः (dve dyāvāpṛthivyau mātarau yasya saḥ). यदा द्वयोर्लोकयोः निर्माता (yadā dvayorlokayoḥ nirmātā). Sūrya has both heaven and earth as mother. Since heaven and earth have granted room to the whole world, they are said to be mothers of Sūrya also. Or else, since Sūrya is the protector of the two worlds, earth and the middle region, he is the maker of the two worlds; thus a second meaning is described. That at the time of setting this Sūrya is without the spreading of his rays is the meaning stated by the words शयुः शयानः (śayuḥ śayānaḥ). एकः अबंधनः वत्सः चरति (ekaḥ abaṃdhanaḥ vatsaḥ carati)—Sāyaṇa has explained this sentence in two ways. First: द्यावापृथिव्योः साधारणः तयोः रसादानात् पुत्रः अप्रतिबद्धगतिः नभसि चरति (dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ sādhāraṇaḥ tayoḥ rasādānāt putraḥ apratibaddhagatiḥ nabhasi carati). Since Sūrya draws up the waters in earth and the middle region, he stands in an equal relation to both of them, heaven and earth, and this Sūrya moves in the middle region without any obstruction; thus the meaning is explained. In the second meaning, this Sūrya is अनालंबनः (anālaṃbanaḥ), without any support, and moves alone in the middle region (so that he does not fall down); thus it is described.

p. 290

That heaven and earth are described as the mother-hood of Sūrya; that at setting Sūrya becomes lustreless, without the spreading of his rays; that, drawing the sap of heaven and earth (as if drinking milk), he has the state of a son; and that he moves in the middle region as if unobstructed and without any support: all these acts are the acts of Mitra and Varuṇa, and the might of these gods is described as full of greatness and pre-eminent.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

द्वि॒मा॒ता होता॑ वि॒दथे॑षु स॒म्राळन्वग्रं॒ चर॑ति॒ क्षेति॑ बु॒ध्नः ।
प्र रण्या॑नि रण्य॒वाचो॑ भरंते म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥

dvimātā hotā vidatheṣu samrāḷanvagraṃ carati kṣeti budhnaḥ |
pra raṇyāni raṇyavāco bharaṃte mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

द्विमाता । होता । विदथेषु । सम्‌राट् । अनु । अग्रं । चरति । क्षेति । बुध्नः ।
प्र । रण्यानि । रण्यवाचः । भरंते । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ ७ ॥

dvimātā | hotā | vidatheṣu | samrāṭ | anu | agraṃ | carati | kṣeti | budhnaḥ |
pra | raṇyāni | raṇyavācaḥ | bharaṃte | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

द्विमाता द्वयोर्लोकयोर्निर्माता विदथेषु यज्ञेषु होता देवानामाह्वाता सम्राट् यज्ञेषु सम्यग्राजमानोऽग्निरन्नग्रमग्रे दिवि चरति । सूर्यभूतस्तत्र वर्तते । बुध्नः सर्वस्य कर्मणो मूलभूततः सन् क्षेति । भूम् वसति । यद्वा । अग्रं मुख्यं भागं चरति । भक्षयति । क्षेति । यज्वनां गृहेषु निवसति । यद्वा । बुद्धः प्रतिष्ठांतेभागी स्विष्टकृद्रूपेण । प्रतिष्ठा वै स्विष्टकृदिति श्रुतेः । किंच रण्यवाचो रमणीयवाचः स्तोतारो रण्यानि रमणीयानि स्तोत्राणि प्र भरंते । प्रणयंति । कुर्वंति । तदिदं देवानामैश्वर्यं । चरति । चादिलोप इति न निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

द्विमाता (dvimātā): the maker of the two worlds. विदथेषु (vidatheṣu): in sacrifices होता (hotā), the caller of the gods; सम्राट् (samrāṭ): Agni, shining well in the sacrifices, अन्वग्रं चरति (anvagraṃ carati), moves first in the sky; being Sūrya, he abides there. बुध्नः (budhnaḥ): being the root of all action, क्षेति (kṣeti): he dwells on earth. Or else: अग्रं (agraṃ) means the principal portion, and चरति (carati) means he eats it; क्षेति (kṣeti): he dwells in the houses of sacrificers. Or else: बुद्धः (buddhaḥ) (read thus) is प्रतिष्ठा (pratiṣṭhā), the sharer at the end in the form of Sviṣṭakṛt, from the Śruti प्रतिष्ठा वै स्विष्टकृदिति श्रुतेः (pratiṣṭhā vai sviṣṭakṛditi śruteḥ). Moreover, the रण्यवाचः (raṇyavācaḥ), reciters of pleasing speech, प्र भरंते (pra bharaṃte), compose and offer रण्यानि (raṇyāni), pleasing praises. This is the lordship of the gods.

p. 291

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • द्विमाता (dvimātā)—he who has both heaven and earth as mother
  • विदधेषु (vidadheṣu)—in sacrifices
  • होता (hotā)—the caller of the gods
  • सम्राट् (samrāṭ)—and the shining one, Agni
  • अन्वग्रं (anvagraṃ)—at the forepart of the middle region
  • चरति (carati)—moves (in the form of Sūrya)
  • बुद्धः (buddhaḥ)—being the root of all actions
  • क्षेति (kṣeti)—dwells on the earth
  • रण्यवाचः (raṇyavācaḥ)—reciters with pleasing speech
  • रण्यानि (raṇyāni)—pleasing praises
  • प्र भरंतॆ (pra bharaṃtè)—make in abundance
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who has both heaven and earth as mother, who calls the gods at sacrifices, and who is shining, moves at the forepart of the middle region in the form of Sūrya. Being the root of all actions, he dwells on the earth. Reciters with pleasing speech make pleasing praises. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The child of two mothers, thc invoker of the gods at sacrifices, the universal sovereign, proceeds thenceforward (in the sky) : the root (of all), he abides (in the houses of the pious) : the reciters of pleasant (words) offer him agreeable (praises) : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Agni is द्वयोर्लोकयो निर्माता (dvayorlokayo nirmātā), the maker of the two worlds, earth and the middle region; therefore he is designated by the word द्विमाता (dvimātā). Since he brings the gods to accept the oblation, he is the Hotṛ. Since he shines greatly with radiance in the sacrifices, he is the sovereign. And since he is the root cause of all actions, he is described in this Ṛk as बुद्धः (buddhaḥ). अन्वग्रं चरति—अग्रे दिवि सूर्यभूतस्तत्र वर्तते (anvagraṃ carati—agre divi sūryabhūtastatra vartate): Agni shines in the middle region as Sūrya. Having thus described the identity of Agni with Sūrya, Sāyaṇa describes a second meaning: अग्रं मुख्यं भागं चरति भक्षयति (agraṃ mukhyaṃ bhāgaṃ carati bhakṣayati), Agni, the chief cause of all actions, eats the principal portions of the oblation in the sacrifices. बुद्धः क्षेति—सर्वस्य कर्मणो मूलभूतस्सन् भूमौ वसति यद्वा यज्वनां गृहेषु निवसति (buddhaḥ kṣeti—sarvasya karmaṇo mūlabhūtassan bhūmau vasati yadvā yajvanāṃ gṛheṣu nivasati): Agni, being the root cause of all actions, dwells on the earth

p. 292

or else dwells in the houses of those devoted to sacrifice; thus two meanings are explained. And बुद्धः प्रतिष्ठा अंते भागी स्विष्टकृद्रूपेण (buddhaḥ pratiṣṭhā aṃte bhāgī sviṣṭakṛdrūpeṇa): by the homa called Sviṣṭakṛt, performed in sacrifices, he receives the oblation offered at the end. Therefore Agni is described as the one who establishes stability. For the meaning प्रतिष्ठौ (pratiṣṭhau) of the word बुद्ध (buddha), the Śruti sentence “प्रतिष्ठौ वै स्विष्टकृत् (pratiṣṭhau vai sviṣṭakṛt)” is cited. रण्यवाचः रण्यानि प्रभरंते—रमणीयवाचः स्तोत्रारः रमणीयानि स्तोत्राणि प्रकर्षेण कुर्वंति (raṇyavācaḥ raṇyāni prabharaṃte—ramaṇīyavācaḥ stotrāraḥ ramaṇīyāni stotrāṇi prakarṣeṇa kurvaṃti). रणौ रमणीयौ सांग्राम्यावा (raṇau ramaṇīyau sāṃgrāmyāvā) (Ni. 6-24): the word रण (raṇa) has been explained by Yāska, meaning that they recite pleasing praises. That Agni exists in identity with Sūrya and is the root cause of all actions, and other such things, are the principal glories of the gods and remain in might; thus it is described.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

शूर॑स्येव॒ युध्य॑तो अंत॒मस्य॑ प्रती॒चीनं॑ ददृशे॒ विश्व॑मा॒यत् ।
अं॒तर्म॒तिश्व॑रति नि॒ष्पिधं॒ गोर्म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥

śūrasyeva yudhyato aṃtamasya pratīcīnaṃ dadṛśe viśvamāyat |
aṃtarmatiśvarati niṣpidhaṃ gormahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖

शूरस्य इव । युध्यतः । अंतमस्य । प्रतीचीनं । ददृशे । विश्वं । आयत् ।
अंतः । मतिः । चरति । निःसिधं । गोः । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ ८ ॥

śūrasya iva | yudhyataḥ | aṃtamasya | pratīcīnaṃ | dadṛśe | viśvaṃ | āyat |
aṃtaḥ | matiḥ | carati | niḥsidhaṃ | goḥ | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अंतमस्य समीपे वर्तमानस्य दावाग्नेरायदभिमुखमागच्छद्विश्वं भूतजातं प्रतिचीनं पराङ्मुखं ददृशे । दृश्यते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । शूरस्येव । यथा युध्यतो युद्धं कुर्वाणस्य शूरस्य समर्थस्य राज्णोऽभिमुखमागच्छत्परबलं पराङ्मुखं दृश्यते तद्वत् । मतिः सर्वैर्ज्ञायमानः सोऽग्निर्गोरुदकस्य निष्पिधं हिंसिकां दीप्तिमंतश्च रति । अंतर्धारयति ॥ युध्यतः । युध संप्रहारे । दिवादिः ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

अंतमस्य (aṃtamasya): of the forest fire that stands near; the whole creation coming towards it (आयत् (āyat), advancing to meet it) is seen प्रतिचीनं (praticīnaṃ), turned away, ददृशे (dadṛśe), is seen. The illustration is शूरस्येव (śūrasyeva): as the hostile army coming to meet a brave, capable king who is fighting a battle is seen turned away, so here. मतिः (matiḥ): that Agni, known by all, holds within himself (Sāyaṇa: अंतर्धारयति (aṃtardhārayati)) गोः (goḥ), of the cow (that is, of water), the destructive निष्पिधं (niṣpidhaṃ) radiance. This is the lordship of the gods (as in the refrain).

p. 293

Ṛk 8 (continued)

तस्य शतरि रूपं । अंतमस्य । अंतशब्दादत इनिठनाविति ठन् । अतिशयेनांतिक इत्यर्थे तमस् । तमॆः तादेश्येति तादिलोपः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । प्रतीचीनं । प्रतिपूर्वस्यांचतेः क्विन् । तस्माद्विभाषांचेरदिक्स्त्रियामिति खः । ईनादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । आयत् । या प्रापण इत्यस्याज् पूर्वस्य शतरि रूपं आज्‌पूर्वस्य अय पय गतावित्यस्य शतरि रूपं वेति व्युत्पत्त्यनवधारणादनवग्रहः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This block gives only the grammatical derivations of the words of the preceding bhāṣya; the Grammar section carries them. It ends by saying that, because the derivation is not settled, no definite choice (anavagraha) is made for आयत् (āyat): it may be the present participle of या प्रापण (yā prāpaṇa) with आज् (āj) before it, or of the root अय पय (aya paya) (to go) with आज् (āj) before it.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

  • आयत् (āyat)—going towards
  • विश्वं (viśvaṃ)—all beings too
  • युध्यतः (yudhyataḥ)—of the one who fights
  • शूरस्येव (śūrasyeva)—as enemy armies turn their backs and run on seeing a hero
  • प्रतीचीनं (pratīcīnaṃ)—turned away
  • ददृशे (dadṛśe)—appear
  • मतिः (matiḥ)—Agni, who is known by all
  • गोः (goḥ)—of the water
  • निष्पिधं (niṣpidhaṃ)—radiant
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—in the interior
  • चरति (carati)—moves
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods

  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and ordinary NOTE
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All beings approaching the nearby forest fire appear turned away, just as enemy armies turn their backs and flee on seeing a fighting hero. Agni, known to all, moves in the radiant interior of the water. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

All (creatures) approaching too near his confines are beheld with their faces turned away as (an enemy) flies from a combatant : obvious (to all), he penetrates the water for its destruction : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अंतमस्य—समीपे वर्तमानस्य (aṃtamasya—samīpe vartamānasya). This word is used as an adjective. Following the meaning of the comparison sentence, Sāyaṇa explains the noun qualified as the forest fire. शूरस्य युद्धतः आयत् विश्वं प्रतीचीनं ददृशे (śūrasya yuddhataḥ āyat viśvaṃ pratīcīnaṃ dadṛśe)—यथा युद्धं कुर्वाणस्य शूरस्य समर्थस्य राज्ञः अभिमुखमागच्छत् भूतजातं परबलं पराङ्मुखं दृश्यते (yathā yuddhaṃ kurvāṇasya śūrasya samarthasya rājñaḥ abhimukhamāgacchat bhūtajātaṃ parabalaṃ parāṅmukhaṃ dṛśyate)—as an enemy army that has come to face a king engaged in battle turns back through the king's power, so, with समीपे वर्तमानस्य दावाग्नेः विश्वं प्रतीचीनं ददृशे (samīpe vartamānasya dāvāgneḥ viśvaṃ pratīcīnaṃ dadṛśe)—all who come to confront the fiercely blazing forest fire, unable to extinguish it, turn back; thus the incomparable greatness of the forest fire is described. ### Printed p. 294 The word मतिः (matiḥ) is explained as सर्वैः ज्ञायमानः (sarvaiḥ jñāyamānaḥ): Agni is known to all by his own natural quality. This Agni गोः निष्पिधं अंतश्चरति (goḥ niṣpidhaṃ aṃtaścarati)—उदकस्य हिंसिकां दीप्तिं अंतर्धारयति (udakasya hiṃsikāṃ dīptiṃ aṃtardhārayati)—he bears even in the midst of the waters the abundant radiance (power) that drinks up the waters; thus the Aurvāgni (the fire in the earth) is described briefly. So in this Ṛk both the forest fire and the Aurvāgni are described briefly. The abundant might of the gods, being such, is described as unequalled.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पलितः पालयिता पूर्णो वा देवानां दूतोऽग्निरास्वोषधीषु नि वेवेति । नितरां वाप्य वर्तते । महान् सोऽग्नी रोचनेन सूर्येण सहांता रोदस्योर्मद्यॆ चरति । वपूंषि नानाविधानि रूपाणि बिभ्रत् सोऽग्निर्नोऽस्मान् यष्ट्वानभि वि चष्टे । विशेषेणानुग्रहदृष्ट्या पश्यति ॥ वेवेति । वी गत्यादिषु । यज्जलुकि ईडभावे रूपं । रोचनेन ! सहार्थे तृतीया । भिभ्रत् । डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोरित्यस्य शतरि रूपं । अभ्यस्तस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

पलितः (palitaḥ) means protector, or full. Agni, the messenger of the gods, नि वेवेति (ni veveti) constantly abides in these plants. Being great, he moves with रोचनेन (rocanena), the sun, between heaven and earth. Bearing manifold forms (वपूंषि (vapūṃṣi)), he looks upon us, the sacrificers, वि चष्टे (vi caṣṭe), with a particularly favouring eye. (Remaining text: grammar of वेवेति (veveti), रोचनेन (rocanena) (third case in the sense of "together with") and भिभ्रत् (bhibhrat).)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, full-natured and messenger of the gods, has pervaded these plants. The great Agni, as the shining sun, moves between heaven and earth. Bearing manifold forms, he looks upon us, the sacrificers, with a favouring eye. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

In those (plants) the aged messenger (of the gods) constantly abides : mighty, he passes with the radiant (sun) thorough the regions of space ; assuming various forms, he looks (complacently) upon us : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पलितः— पालयिता पूर्णो वा (palitaḥ— pālayitā pūrṇo vā). Agni is explained as the protector of all, or as full with complete greatness. He is also described as देवानां दूतः (devānāṃ dūtaḥ), messenger of the gods, because he calls the gods to the sacrificial hall to receive the oblation and carries each god's oblation to him. By the sentence मर्हा रोचनेन अंतः चरति (marhā rocanena aṃtaḥ carati) Agni, full of greatness, is described as moving with the sun between heaven and earth. But in Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-75-7) the identity with the sun and a separate movement are described. This Agni, वपूंषि बिभ्रत् नः अभि वि चष्टे (vapūṃṣi bibhrat naḥ abhi vi caṣṭe), bearing various forms, looks upon us the sacrificers greatly favouringly. ### Printed p. 296 #### Ṛk 10
