agniḥ | tā | viśvā | bhuvanāni | veda | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

विष्णुर्वाप्नो गोपाः सर्वस्य गोपायिता प्रिया प्रियतमान्यमृता क्षयरहितानि धामानि तेजांसि दधानः सोऽग्निः परमं पाथः स्थानं पाति । रक्षति । यद्वा । धामानि लोकधारकाण्यमृतोदकानि दधानः सन् परमं पाथ उदकस्य स्थानमंतरिक्षं पाति । सोऽग्निस्ता तानि विश्वा सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातानि वेद । जानाति ॥ गोपाः । गोपायतेः क्विप्यतोलोपयलोपौ । अग्निष्टेत्यत्र संहितायां युष्मत्तत्तत्कुः स्वंतः पादमिति षत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ) is the pervader and गोपाः (gopāḥ) the protector of all. Bearing most dear (प्रिया (priyā)) and imperishable (अमृता (amṛtā)) splendours (धामानि (dhāmāni)), that Agni guards the highest place (परमं पाथः (paramaṃ pāthaḥ)). Or else: bearing the world-sustaining immortal waters, he guards the supreme place of water, the atmosphere. That Agni knows all those beings (भुवनानि (bhuvanāni)). (Remaining text: grammar of गोपाः (gopāḥ) and the change to ṣ in अग्निष्टा (agniṣṭā).)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ)—the all-pervading
  • गोपाः (gopāḥ)—the protector of all
  • प्रिया (priyā)—most dear
  • अमृता (amṛtā)—imperishable
  • धामानि (dhāmāni)—splendours
  • दधानः (dadhānaḥ)—possessing; Agni
  • परमं पाथः (paramaṃ pāthaḥ)—the highest path
  • पाति (pāti)—protects
  • अग्निः (agniḥ)—that same Agni
  • ता विश्वा भुवनानि (tā viśvā bhuvanāni)—all those well-known worlds
  • वेद (veda)—knows
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is all-pervading, protector of all, and possessor of most dear and imperishable splendours, protects the highest path. He knows all the worlds. The might of the gods is great and unequalled. ### Printed p. 297

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Pervading and protecting (all), possesing grateful and immortal radiance, he preserves the supreme path (of the rains), for Agni knows all these worlds : great and unqueualled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विष्णुः गोपाः अमृता धामानि दधानः—व्याप्तः सर्वस्य गोपायिता क्षयरहितानि तेजांसि दधानः (viṣṇuḥ gopāḥ amṛtā dhāmāni dadhānaḥ—vyāptaḥ sarvasya gopāyitā kṣayarahitāni tejāṃsi dadhānaḥ): Agni pervades everything, protects all, and bears splendours that are ever without decline—this is one kind of meaning; in it धामानि (dhāmāni) is explained as splendours. In the second meaning धामानि (dhāmāni) is said to be लोकधारकाणि (lokadhārakāṇi) and अमृता (amṛtā) waters. Hence लोकधारकाणि उदकानि दधानः अग्निः उदकस्य स्थानमंतरिक्षं पाति (lokadhārakāṇi udakāni dadhānaḥ agniḥ udakasya sthānamaṃtarikṣaṃ pāti)—Agni, bearing the world-sustaining waters, protects the atmosphere, the place of the waters. The word अमृत (amṛta) is stated by Yāska among the names of water (Ni. 2-24). सः अग्निः विश्वा भुवनानि वेद—सर्वाणि भूतजातानि जानाति (saḥ agniḥ viśvā bhuvanāni veda—sarvāṇi bhūtajātāni jānāti). The word भुवन (bhuvana) is given the meaning "living beings"; because Agni knows all the manifold beings, he is described as omniscient. Thus Jātavedas Agni is described in another manner. So in the preceding Ṛks Agni's manifold existence—as lightning-fire, Vaiśvānara fire, forest fire, Aurva fire—has been described briefly.

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

नाना॑ चक्राते य॒म्या॒३॒॑श्वपूं॑षि॒ तयो॑र॒न्यद्रोच॑ते कृ॒ष्णम॒न्यत् ।
श्यावी॑ च॒ यदरु॑षी च॒ स्वसा॑रौ म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥

nānā cakrāte yamyāśvapūṃṣi tayoranyadrocate kṛṣṇamanyat |

नाना । चक्राते इति । यम्या । वपूंषि । तयोः । अन्यत् । रोचते । कृष्णं । अन्यत् ।
श्यावी । च । यत् । अरुषी । च । स्वसारौ । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥

nānā | cakrāte iti | yamyā | vapūṃṣi | tayoḥ | anyat | rocate | kṛṣṇaṃ | anyat |
śyāvī | ca | yat | aruṣī | ca | svasārau | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖

p. 298

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यम्या यमरूपे मिथुनभूते अहश्च रात्रिश्चेत्येते नाना नानाविधानि वपूंषि शुक्लकृष्णादीनि रूपाणि चक्राते । कुरुतः । श्यावी कृष्णवर्णारुषी शुक्लतयारोचमाना यत् ये परस्परं स्वसारौ भवतस्तयोर्मध्येऽन्यदर्जुनमहो रोचते । किरणसंबंधाद्वीप्यते । अन्यद्रात्रिलक्षणं कृष्णं तमस्संबंधात् कृष्णवर्णमाभाति ॥ यम्या । सुपो डादेशः । रोचते । एकान्याभ्यां समर्थाभ्यामिति न निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

यम्या (yamyā), the twin pair, day and night, चक्राते (cakrāte) make manifold (नाना (nānā)) forms (वपूंषि (vapūṃṣi)), white, black and so on. श्यावी (śyāvī) is the black-coloured one and अरुषी (aruṣī) the one shining through whiteness; as the two are sisters (स्वसारौ (svasārau)) of each other, of them one, the bright day, रोचते (rocate) shines through its connection with the rays; the other, characterised as night, appears black through its connection with darkness. (Remaining text: grammar of यम्या (yamyā) (ḍā substitution) and रोचते (rocate) (no nighāta).)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यम्या (yamyā)—day and night as a pair
  • नाना (nānā)—manifold (white and black)
  • वपूंषि (vapūṃṣi)—forms
  • चक्राते (cakrāte)—have assumed
  • श्यावी (śyāvī)—the black-coloured night
  • अरुषी (aruṣī)—the day full of light
  • यत् स्वसारौ (yat svasārau)—they are sisters of each other
  • तयोः (tayoḥ)—of them
  • अन्यत् (anyat)—the day
  • रोचते (rocate)—shines with light
  • अन्यत् (anyat)—the night
  • कृष्णं (kṛṣṇaṃ)—has assumed a black colour
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Day and night, in the form of a pair, have assumed manifold forms, white and black. The night and the day full of light are sisters of each other. Of them the day shines with light and the night wears a black colour. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The twin pair (day and night) adopt various forms : one of them shines brightly, the other is black : twin sisters are they, one black and the other white : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यम्या—मिथुनभूते (yamyā—mithunabhūte). This word is stated among the names of night (Ni. 2-18). श्यावी—कृष्णवर्णा (śyāvī—kṛṣṇavarṇā). This word too is read among the names of night (Ni. 2-18). In this Ṛk day and night are described. Of these, the day, through the spread of the sun's rays, is अरुषी—शुक्लवर्णा (aruṣī—śuklavarṇā), bright; the night, through its connection with darkness, is कृष्णं (kṛṣṇaṃ), black. Day and night परस्परं स्वसारौ भवतः (parasparaṃ svasārau bhavataḥ): because each follows the other, they are described as sisters. Yāska also—

p. 299

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

(Yāska also, in the passage) अहश्च कृष्ण महरर्जुनं च विवर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः । (ahaśca kṛṣṇa mahararjunaṃ ca vivartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1), explains: अहश्च कृष्णं रात्रि: शुक्लं चाहरर्जुनं च विवर्तेते रजसी वेदितव्याभिः प्रवृत्तिभिः । (ahaśca kṛṣṇaṃ rātri: śuklaṃ cāhararjunaṃ ca vivartete rajasī veditavyābhiḥ pravṛttibhiḥ |) Day and night, these two, shine with the forms of white and black colour. Of these, the one that is white through its connection with the rays and bestows light on living beings is day. Night is black in colour and brings living beings rest from their activity. By their regular goings and comings (night passes, day comes; day passes, night comes), or by their effect, they are described as benefactors of living beings. The overwhelming might of the deities of day and night, who bear the forms of white and black as day and night and exist in manifold forms through their turnings, is beyond description.

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

मा॒ता च॒ यत्र॑ दुहि॒ता च॑ धे॒नू स॑ब॒र्दुघे॑ धा॒पये॑ते ॒ समीची ।
ऋ॒तस्य॒ ते सद॑सीळे अं॒तर्म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥ १२ ॥

mātā ca yatra duhitā ca dhenū sabardughe dhāpayete
samīcī |
ṛtasya te sadasīḷe aṃtarmahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖ 12 ‖

माता । च । यत्र । दुहिता । च । धेनू इति । सबर्दुघे इति सबःदुघे । धापयेते
इति । समीची इति सम्ईची ।
ऋतस्य । ते इति । सदसि । ईळे । अंतः । महत् । देवानां । आसुरत्वं । एकं ॥ १२ ॥

mātā | ca | yatra | duhitā | ca | dhenū iti | sabardughe iti sabaḥdughe | dhāpayete
iti | samīcī iti samīcī |
ṛtasya | te iti | sadasi | īḷe | aṃtaḥ | mahat | devānāṃ | āsuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

माता सर्वेषां निर्मातृत्वान्माता पृथिवी च दुहिता दूरे निहिता द्यौश्च । दुहिता दुर्हिता दूरे हिता दोग्देवेति यास्कः । एते सबर्दुघ्ने सबरः स्वीयस्य क्षीररूपस्य रसस्य दॊग्धौ आत एव धेनू जगतः प्रीणयित्र्यौ द्यावापृथिव्यौ यत्रांतरिक्षे समीची परस्परं संगते सत्यौ धापयेते स्वकीयं रसमन्योन्यं पाययेते ऋतस्योदकस्य सदसि स्थानभूते तस्मिन्नंतरिक्षेंतः स्थिते द्यावापृथिव्या-

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Mother": because she is the maker of all, the earth is the mother; "daughter" (duhitā) is Heaven, placed far away. Yāska: दुहिता दुर्हिता दूरे हिता दोग्देवेति (duhitā durhitā dūre hitā dogdeveti). These two are "sabardughe": sabar is their own sap in the form of milk, and they are the milkers of it; hence they are "dhenū", the two nourishers of the world, Heaven and Earth. In the firmament, where, meeting each other, they make each other drink their own sap, in the seat of ṛta, that is, of water — that firmament — I praise Heaven and Earth standing within it. (The block continues on the next page.)

p. 300

वीळे । अहं सौमि । यद्वा । वृष्टिलक्षणं रसं द्यौः पृथिवीं धापयत आहुतिलक्षणं रसं द्यां पृथिवीत्येवमन्योन्यं माता च दुहिता च भवतः । ऋतस्य सदसि स्थाने यज्ञसदने स्थितोऽहं ते उभे सौमि ॥ सबर्दुघे । सबःशब्दः क्षीरवाचीति संप्रदायविद आहुः । तस्मिन्नुपपदे दुह प्रपूरण इत्यस्माद्दातोर्दुहः । कब्बश्चेति कप्पत्ययो घश्चांतादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । धापयेते । धेट् पान इत्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लटि निगरणचलनार्थेभ्यश्चेति परस्पैपदे प्राप्ते पादिसु धेट् उपसंख्यानमित्यात्मनेपदं । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing) "I praise." Or else: Heaven makes the earth drink the sap in the form of rain, and the earth makes Heaven drink the sap in the form of the oblation; so each is mother and daughter to the other. Standing at the seat of ṛta, the place of sacrifice, I praise both. "Sabardughe": those versed in tradition say that the word sabar denotes milk; the second member is formed from the root duh, "to fill".

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • माता (mātā)—the earth, in the form of the mother
  • दुहिता च (duhitā ca)—and also the firmament, placed far away NOTE
  • सबर्दुघे (sabardughe)—milking together their sap in the form of milk
  • धेनू (dhenū)—like milch cows that bring satisfaction to the world
  • यत्र (yatra)—in which firmament
  • समीची (samīcī)—meeting together
  • धापयेते (dhāpayete)—exchanging their respective saps, they make each other drink
  • ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)—of water
  • सदसि (sadasi)—in the firmament, which is its seat
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—Heaven and Earth, standing within
  • ईळे (īḷe)—I praise
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The earth, in the form of the mother, and the far-placed firmament, milking together their sap in the form of milk, like milch cows that satisfy the world, meet together in the firmament and, exchanging their respective saps, make each other drink. In the firmament, the seat of water, I praise Heaven and Earth standing within it. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Where the mother and the daughter, two productive milch cows, unite, they nourish each other : I worship them both in (the firmament), the dwel- ling of the waters : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

माता—सर्वेषां निर्मातृत्वात् माता पृथिवी। (mātā—sarveṣāṃ nirmātṛtvāt mātā pṛthivī|) Because she brings forth everything, moving and unmoving, the earth is called the mother. दुहिता-दूरे नीता द्यौः च । (duhitā-dūre nītā dyauḥ ca |) Because the firmament is very far from the earth, it is designated duhitṛ (daughter).

p. 301

Yāska has explained the meaning of the word duhitā as दुहिता, दूरेहिता, दोग्दीर्वा (duhitā, dūrehitā, dogdīrvā) (Ni. 3-4). Because, though far away and given to another in the proper manner, she wishes the welfare of her own people, the duhitā (daughter) is described as beneficial even though she may cause sorrow; and he explains that the word is derived from the root duh in the sense "to fill", that is, "to milk".

These Heaven and Earth: ऋतस्य सदसि समीची धापयेते—उदकस्य स्थानभूते तस्मिन् अंतरिक्षे परस्परं संगते सत्यौ स्वकीयां रसं अन्नोन्यं पाययेते । (ṛtasya sadasi samīcī dhāpayete—udakasya sthānabhūte tasmin aṃtarikṣe parasparaṃ saṃgate satyau svakīyāṃ rasaṃ annonyaṃ pāyayete |) In the firmament, where the waters gather, staying inseparable from one another, offering their respective saps to each other in exchange, they go on satisfying the worlds like cows that yield milk. One kind of meaning has been described thus.

यद्वा वृष्टिलक्षणं रसं दौः पृथिवीं धापयते । आहुतिलक्षणं रसं द्यां पृथिवीति एवं माता दुहिता च भवतः । (yadvā vṛṣṭilakṣaṇaṃ rasaṃ dauḥ pṛthivīṃ dhāpayate | āhutilakṣaṇaṃ rasaṃ dyāṃ pṛthivīti evaṃ mātā duhitā ca bhavataḥ |) In the first meaning, motherhood of Heaven and Earth is established with regard to the world through their doing good to it, and daughterhood through their satisfying the world with their saps. In the second meaning, since the earth makes Heaven drink the sap in the form of the oblation and Heaven makes the earth drink the sap in the form of rain, there arises between the two a motherhood in the sense of mutual nourishing, and a daughterhood through the milking of the sap; this is what is described as the second meaning.

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒न्यस्या॑ व॒त्सं रि॑ह॒ती मि॑माय॒ कया॑ भु॒वा नि द॑धे धे॒नुरूधः॑।
ऋ॒तस्य॒ सा पय॑सापिन्व॒तेळा॑ म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥

anyasyā vatsaṃ rihatī mimāya kayā bhuvā ni dadhe dhenurūdhaḥ|
ṛtasya sā payasāpinvateḷā mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अन्यस्याः । वत्सं । रिहती । मिमाय । कया । भुवा । नि । दधे । धेनुः । ऊधः ।
ऋतस्य । सा । पयसा । अपिन्वत । इळा । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥१३॥

anyasyāḥ | vatsaṃ | rihatī | mimāya | kayā | bhuvā | ni | dadhe | dhenuḥ | ūdhaḥ |
ṛtasya | sā | payasā | apinvata | iḷā | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖13‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अन्यस्याः पृथिव्या वत्समग्निं रिहत्युदकधारारूपया जिह्वया लिहती द्यौर्मिमाय । मेघद्वारा ध्वनिं करोति । धेनुः प्रीणयित्री सा द्यौः कया जलवर्जितया

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Of the other", that is, of the earth, Heaven licks the calf, Agni, with a tongue in the form of streams of water, and lows: through the cloud she makes a sound. "Dhenu" is the nourishing Heaven; "kayā": with the waterless (earth)…

p. 302

भुवा तत्रत्यं जलमादाय स्वकीयमूधो मेघरूपं नि दधे । उदकेन निहितमकरोत् । सा जलवर्जितेळा पृथिव्यृतस्य सत्यभूतस्यादित्यस्य पयसोदकेनापिन्वत । वर्षकाले सिक्ता भवति । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिः । मनु. ३-७६ । इति स्मृतेः ॥ रिहती । लिह आस्वादन इत्यस्य शतरि रूपं । शतुरनुम इति जीप उदात्तत्वं । अपिन्वत । पिवि सेचने । मुचादिरात्मनेपदी । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing) …taking the water from there, she places her own udder, in the form of cloud; she makes it stored with water. That waterless Iḷā, the earth, is swelled by the water of Āditya, who is the truth (ṛta); she is sprinkled in the rainy season. For the smṛti says आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिः (ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭiḥ) (Manu. 3-76). NOTE

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अन्यस्या: (anyasyā:)—of the earth, one of the two worlds
  • वत्सं (vatsaṃ)—the calf-like Agni
  • रिहती (rihatī)—licking with a tongue in the form of streams
  • मिमाय (mimāya)—(through the cloud) the presiding deity of the world of heaven makes a sound
  • धेनुः (dhenuḥ)—Heaven, the bringer of pleasure
  • कया (kayā)—waterless
  • भुवा (bhuvā)—from the earth (drawing the water)
  • ऊधः (ūdhaḥ)—her udder in the form of cloud
  • नि दधे (ni dadhe)—she places
  • सा (sā)—that
  • इळा (iḷā)—the earth, being waterless
  • ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)—of Āditya, who is of the nature of truth
  • पयसा (payasā)—with the water
  • अपिन्वत (apinvata)—is drenched
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Licking, with a tongue in the form of streams, Agni, the calf-like son of the earth, one of the two worlds, the presiding deity of the world of heaven makes a sound through the cloud. The nourishing world of heaven, drawing water from the waterless earth, gives her udder, in the form of cloud, to the earth. That waterless earth is drenched by the water of Āditya, who is of the nature of truth. The might of the gods is great and unequalled. NOTE

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Licking the calf of the other, one of them lows aloud : the milch cow offers her udder for the one that is without moisture (the earth), and she (the earth) is refreshed by the milk of the rain : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धेनुः—प्रीणयित्री सा द्यौः । (dhenuḥ—prīṇayitrī sā dyauḥ |) The word dhenu is stated among the words for speech (Ni. 2-23). The meaning is explained thus: the world of heaven is the dhenu (cow), and it satisfies. In this Ṛk, in a poetic style, the world of heaven is called a cow, and the nature of a cow toward her calf is described. Moreover, it is not natural for one cow to nourish the calf of another.

p. 303

Here: पृथिव्याः वत्समग्निं उदकधारारूपया जिह्वया लिहती द्यौ: मेघद्वारा ध्वनिं करोति । (pṛthivyāḥ vatsamagniṃ udakadhārārūpayā jihvayā lihatī dyau: meghadvārā dhvaniṃ karoti |) The world of heaven satisfies with streams of water Agni, who is like the son of the earth or is her son (as a cow licks her calf with love), and, as a cow makes the sound that calls her calf near, makes the sound of the clouds. By this the thunder of the clouds is presented as the calf-calling sound of the cow.

Of the world of heaven, भुवा ऊधः निदधे—तत्रत्यं जलवादाय स्वकीयं मेघरूपं ऊधः उदकेन निहितमकरोत् । (bhuvā ūdhaḥ nidadhe—tatratyaṃ jalavādāya svakīyaṃ megharūpaṃ ūdhaḥ udakena nihitamakarot |) Gathering the waters that are on the earth, she makes her udder, which is in the form of cloud, full of sap. Afterwards, when the rainy season arrives, इळा ऋतस्य पयसा अपिन्वत (iḷā ṛtasya payasā apinvata): the earth is drenched with waters from the side of Āditya, who is of the nature of truth. Having explained the meaning thus, he cites the Manu-smṛti text आदित्याज्ञायते वृष्टिः वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः (ādityājñāyate vṛṣṭiḥ vṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ) (Manu. 3-17): from Āditya comes rain, from rain food, and from food the creatures. NOTE Thus, because Heaven and Earth are engaged in the origin and so on of the worlds, the might of the gods is explained as unequalled.

Ṛk 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

पद्या॑ वस्ते पुरु॒रूपा॒ वपूं॑ष्युद्॒र्वा त॑स्थौ॒ त्र्यविं॒ रेरि॑हाणा।
ऋ॒तस्य॒ सद्म॒ वि च॑रामि वि॒द्वान्म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥१४॥

padyā vaste pururūpā vapūṃṣyudrvā tasthau tryaviṃ rerihāṇā|
ṛtasya sadma vi carāmi vidvānmahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖14‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

पद्या । वस्ते । पुरुरूपा । वपूंषि । ऊर्ध्वा । तस्थौ । त्रिअपिं । रेरिहाणा ।
यतस्य । सद्म । वि । चरामि । विद्वान् । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ १४ ॥

padyā | vaste | pururūpā | vapūṃṣi | ūrdhvā | tasthau | triapiṃ | rerihāṇā |
yatasya | sadma | vi | carāmi | vidvān | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 14 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पद्या । जगत्प्रष्टुः परमेश्वरस्य पद्भां जातत्वात्पद्या भूमिः । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । पद्भां भूमिः । ऋग्वे. १०-९० १४ । इति । यद्वा । पादसंचारे साधुः पद्या भूमिः पुरुरूपा नानाविधस्वरूपाणि वपूंषि स्थावरजंगमात्मकानि रूपाणि वस्ते । आच्छादयति । सैषा भूमिरूर्ध्वोत्तरवेद्यात्मनोन्नता सती स्वसारभूतेन हविषा त्रैविं । सार्धसंवत्सरवयस्को वत्सस्त्रविरित्युच्यते । तत्प्रमाणमादित्यं ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Padyā": the earth is padyā because she was born from the feet (pad) of the Lord, the creator of the world. So the mantra says पद्भां भूमिः (padbhāṃ bhūmiḥ) (Ṛg. 10-90-14). Or else: the earth is padyā as being good for movement on foot. Padyā, the earth, wears (vaste) manifold bodies, forms of the nature of the unmoving and the moving; that is, she covers them. This earth, standing high as the northern altar, with the oblation that is her own essence NOTE, (licks) the "trayavi": a calf of one and a half years is called travi; Āditya is of that measure.

p. 304

श्रीन् लोकानवति स्वतेजसा व्याप्पोतीति त्र्यविरिति वा । रेरिहाणा लिहती तस्थौ । ऋतस्य सत्यभूतस्यादित्यस्य सद्म स्थानं विद्वान् जानानोऽहं वि चरामि । हविर्भिस्तमादित्यं परिचरामि ॥ पद्या । पादशब्दाव्यवे छंदसीति यत् । पद्यत्यतदर्थे । पा- ६-३-५३ । इति पादस्य पद्भावः । यद्वा । तत्र साधुरिति यत् । यतोऽनाथ इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । त्र्यविं । अव रक्षणादिसु । इन्नितीन्प्रत्ययः । कृत्सरः । रेरिहाणा । लिह आस्वादन इत्यस्य यज्‌लुकि शानचि रूपं । अभ्यस्तस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing) Or "trayavi" because he protects the three worlds, pervading them with his own splendour. Licking (rerihāṇā), she stands. Knowing the seat, the abode, of ṛta, that is, of Āditya who is truth, I move about: I serve that Āditya with oblations.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • पद्मा (padmā)—the earth NOTE
  • पुरुरूपा (pururūpā)—of manifold forms
  • वपूंषि (vapūṃṣi)—forms of the nature of the unmoving and the moving
  • वस्ते (vaste)—she wears
  • ऊर्ध्वा (ūrdhvā)—from a high place in the form of the northern altar
  • त्रैविं (traiviṃ)—Āditya, who is like a son of one and a half years NOTE
  • रेरिहाणा (rerihāṇā)—licking by means of the oblation
  • तस्थौ (tasthau)—she stands
  • यतस्य (yatasya)—of Āditya, who is of the nature of truth NOTE
  • सद्म (sadma)—the abode
  • विद्वान् (vidvān)—I who know
  • वि चरामि (vi carāmi)—I worship him
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and without a second
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The earth wears forms of many kinds, of the nature of the unmoving and the moving. From a high place in the form of the northern altar she stands licking, by means of the oblation, Āditya, who is like a son of one and a half years. I, who know the abode of Āditya, who is of the nature of truth, worship him with oblations. The might of the gods is great and without a second.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The earth wears bodies of many forms : she abides on high cherishing her year and a half old (calf) : knowing the abode of the truth (the sun), I offer worship : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the earth, जगत्प्रष्टुः परमेश्वरस्य पद्भ्यां जातत्वात् (jagatpraṣṭuḥ parameśvarasya padbhyāṃ jātatvāt), since she was born from the feet of the Supreme Lord who made the whole universe, is designated by the word padyā. On this point the mantra is also cited: पद्भ्यां भूमि (padbhyāṃ bhūmi) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-14). Or else, पादसंचारे साधुः (pādasaṃcāre sādhuḥ): because she has made for all living beings a way fit for moving about on their own feet, the word padyā is used in the sense of the earth.

p. 305

For the things born of her, this earth, पुरुरूपा वपूंषि वस्ते (pururūpā vapūṃṣi vaste), makes bodies furnished with manifold forms, fixed or moving, and covers their true nature.

त्रैविं—सार्थसंवत्सरवयस्कः वत्सः (traiviṃ—sārthasaṃvatsaravayaskaḥ vatsaḥ): the meaning is given as a calf one and a half years old. Or त्री लोकान् अवति स्वतेजसा व्याप्न्नोति (trī lokān avati svatejasā vyāpnnoti): he is explained as the one who pervades and protects the three worlds with his splendour.

ऊर्ध्वा—उत्तरवेदात्मना उन्नता । (ūrdhvā—uttaravedātmanā unnatā |) This earth is described as standing high in the sacrificial hall in the form of the northern altar, and as satisfying, with the oblations (by the offering of the oblation), Āditya, denoted by the word travi, who is of the measure of a calf of one and a half years.

The sacrificer, who knows the true nature of this Āditya and the dwelling-place where he abides, offers oblations to Āditya; and the might of the gods is described as unequalled and full of greatness.

Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

प॒दे इ॑व॒ निहि॑ते द॒स्मे ं॒तस्तयो॑र॒न्यद्गुह्य॑मा॒विर॒न्यत् ।
स॒ध्री॒ची॒ना प॒थ्या॒३॒॑सा विषू॑ची म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥

pade iva nihite dasme ṃtastayoranyadguhyamāviranyat |
sadhrīcīnā pathyāsā viṣūcī mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

पदे इवेति पदेऽइव । निहिते इति निहिते । दस्मे । अंतरिति । तयोः। अन्यत् । गुह्यं।
आविः । अन्यत् ।
सध्रीचीना। पथ्या । सा । विषूची । महत् । देवनां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ ८५ ॥

pade iveti pade 'iva | nihite iti nihite | dasme | aṃtariti | tayoḥ| anyat | guhyaṃ|
āviḥ | anyat |
sadhrīcīnā| pathyā | sā | viṣūcī | mahat | devanāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 85 ‖

NOTE

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पदे इव । पद्येते ज्ञायेते तत्तदसाधारणलिंगेनेति पदे । अहश्च रात्रिश्चेत्येते दस्मे सर्वैर्दर्शनीये ते उभे अंतर्नभसि मध्ये निहिते स्थापिते इव वर्तेते । तयोरहोरात्रयोरन्यद्रात्रिलक्षणं गुह्यमप्रकाशमानतॆया गूढमि-

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Padye iva": the two are known (padyete) by their respective distinctive marks, hence "pade". Day and night, these two, "dasme", visible to all, stand, as it were, placed (nihite) within the sky, in the middle. Of the two, day and night, the other, that of the nature of night, is "guhya": hidden, because it does not shine… (the block breaks off here).

p. 306

वास्ते । अन्यदहराविः सूर्यप्रकाशेन प्रकटं भवति । सध्रीचीनाहोरात्रयोः परस्परमेलनरूपा पथ्या मार्गः । काल इत्यर्थः । सा विषूची । पुण्यकृतोऽपुण्यकृतश्च प्राप्नोतीति विषूची भवति । सर्वे जना अहोरात्रयोर्वर्तंते । यद्वा । पदे इव देवमनुष्यादीनां स्थानभूते द्यावापृथिव्यावंतरंतरिक्षे निहिते वर्तेते । तयोरन्यद्दौर्गुह्यमस्माभिरदृश्यमानतया गूढं वर्तते । अन्यत्पृथिव्याविः सर्वैर्दृश्यमानत्वेन प्रकटा भवति । सध्रीचीनेति पूर्ववत् ॥ सध्रीचीना । सहपूर्वादंचतेः क्विन् । सहस्य सध्रिरिति सध्र्या देशः । विभाषांचेरदिक्स्त्रियामिति खः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his explanation of the preceding verse. The other of the two, the day, becomes manifest through the light of the sun. सध्रीचीना (sadhrīcīnā) is the path (पथ्या (pathyā)) formed by the day and night meeting each other, that is, time. That path is विषूची (viṣūcī): it reaches the doers of merit and the doers of demerit alike. All people live within day and night.

Alternatively, the two पदे इव (pade iva) are heaven and earth, the abodes of gods, men and others, which lie placed within the atmosphere. Of these two, one is hidden because we cannot see it; the other, the earth, is manifest because it is seen by all. सध्रीचीना (sadhrīcīnā) and the rest are as before.

(The rest of the block is grammar.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • दस्मे (dasme)—visible to all
  • पदे इव (pade iva)—the day and the night, both
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—in the midst of the atmosphere
  • निहिते (nihite)—are placed
  • तयोः (tayoḥ)—of those two
  • अन्यत् (anyat)—the night
  • गुह्यं (guhyaṃ)—is hidden
  • अन्यत् (anyat)—the other one, the day
  • आविः (āviḥ)—is manifest
  • सध्रीचीना (sadhrīcīnā)—joined together with both of these
  • सा पथ्या (sā pathyā)—the path in the form of time
  • विसूची (visūcī)—is common to the whole universe
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Day and night, both visible to all, are placed in the middle region of the atmosphere. Of the two, the night is hidden and the day is manifest. The path in the form of time, which is joined to both of them together, is common to the whole universe. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Like two (distinguishing) impressions, they (day and night) are placed visible in the midst (between heaven and earth), one hidden, one manifest : the path (of both) is common, and that is universal (for good and evil): great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अहश्च रात्रिश्चेत्येते सर्वैः दर्शनीये तत्तदसाधारणलिंगेन ज्ञायमाने नभसि मध्यॆ स्थापिते इव वर्तेते । (ahaśca rātriścetyete sarvaiḥ darśanīye tattadasādhāraṇaliṃgena jñāyamāne nabhasi madhyè sthāpite iva vartete |). The qualities that belong to day and to night, and their respective marks, are known by everyone as distinguishing them from each other. Since these day-and-nights are endowed with a charming form, they appear as if placed within the atmosphere. They are described as follows: the path that is favourable to both is time; this time is विषूची (viṣūcī), that is, पुण्यकृतो अपुण्यकृतश्च प्राप्नोति (puṇyakṛto apuṇyakṛtaśca prāpnoti), it pervades all, the virtuous and the sinful alike; and सर्वे जना अहोरात्रयोर्वर्तंते (sarve janā ahorātrayorvartaṃte), it provides all living beings with room to live.

p. 307

The second meaning concerns heaven and earth. यद्वा पदे इव देवमनुष्यादीनां स्थानभूते द्यावापृथिव्य अंतरंतरिक्षे निहिते वर्तते । तयोरन्यत् अन्या द्यौः गुह्यमस्माभिः अदृश्यमानतॆया गूढा वर्तते । अन्या पृथिवी आविः सर्वैः दृश्यमानतेन प्रकटा भवति । (yadvā pade iva devamanuṣyādīnāṃ sthānabhūte dyāvāpṛthivya aṃtaraṃtarikṣe nihite vartate | tayoranyat anyā dyauḥ guhyamasmābhiḥ adṛśyamānatèyā gūḍhā vartate | anyā pṛthivī āviḥ sarvaiḥ dṛśyamānatena prakaṭā bhavati |). सध्रीचीनेत्यादि पूर्ववत् (sadhrīcīnetyādi pūrvavat). Heaven and earth, which are like dwelling places of gods and men, lie in the atmosphere. Of these, the world of heaven is hidden in a way unknown to us, so that it cannot be seen by us, just as the night is hidden among day and night. The earth is manifest in a form that is known to all, as the day is bright with the light of the sun. Since the time that corresponds to the mutual adherence of these two is the same for the virtuous and the sinful, it is uneven. Because heaven and earth give room to all beings to live, they are benefactors of all; and the might of the gods is described as extraordinary and pre-eminent.

Ṛk 16

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

आ धे॒नवो॑ धुनयंता॒मशि॑श्वीः सब॒र्दुघाः॑ शश॒या अप्र॑दुग्धाः
नव्या॑नव्या युव॒तयो॒ भवं॑तीर्म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑॥

ā dhenavo dhunayaṃtāmaśiśvīḥ sabardughāḥ śaśayā apradugdhāḥ
navyānavyā yuvatayo bhavaṃtīrmahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ‖

आ । धेनवः । धुनयंतां । अशिश्वीः । सबर्दुघाः । शशयाः । अप्रदुग्धाः ।
नव्याःनव्याः । युवतयः । भवंतीः । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं ॥ १६ ॥

ā | dhenavaḥ | dhunayaṃtāṃ | aśiśvīḥ | sabardughāḥ | śaśayāḥ | apradugdhāḥ |
navyāḥnavyāḥ | yuvatayaḥ | bhavaṃtīḥ | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ ‖ 16 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

धेनवो वृष्टिद्वारा सर्वस्य जगतः प्रीणयित्र्योऽशिश्वीः शिशुरहिताः । यद्वा । शिकवो न भवंतीत्यशिश्वीः । शशया नभसि शयाना वर्तमानाः केनाप्यप्रमग्ता अक्षीण-

Gist of the bhāṣya

The धेनवः (dhenavaḥ) are the cows that gratify the whole world by means of rain. अशिश्वीः (aśiśvīḥ) means "without young"; or else, शिकवो न भवंतीत्यशिश्वीः (śikavo na bhavaṃtītyaśiśvīḥ), "they are not infants". शशयाः (śaśayāḥ) are those lying in the sky, unharmed by anyone and undiminished in sap (the sentence continues on the next page).

p. 308

रसाः सबर्दुघा उदकलक्षणस्य क्षीरस्य दोग्धो युवतयः परस्परमिश्रणोपेता नव्या नव्या अतिशयेन नूतना भवंतीर्दिशो मेघा ना आ धुनयंतां । आदुहंतु । मेघपक्षेशिश्वीर्भवंतीत्यत्र लिंगव्यत्ययः ॥ धुनयंतां । धूञ् कंपने । णिचि धूञ् प्रीणोर्नुग्वक्तव्यः । पा- ७-३-३७-१ । इति नुक् । ह्रस्वश्चांदसः । अशिश्वीं । सख्यशिश्वीति भाषायामिति व्यत्ययेन छंदसि भवति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

सबर्दुघाः (sabardughāḥ) are those that yield the milk that has the form of water. युवतयः (yuvatayaḥ) are those endowed with mutual mixing. The quarters, or the clouds, becoming exceedingly new, नव्या नव्या (navyā navyā), are to be shaken, आ धुनयंतां (ā dhunayaṃtāṃ), that is, आदुहंतु (āduhaṃtu), "let them milk out". In the case of the clouds, in "aśiśvīr bhavanti" there is an exchange of gender. (The rest of the block is grammar.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • धेनवः (dhenavaḥ)—the cows that gratify the world
  • अशिश्वीः (aśiśvīḥ)—those without young
  • शशयाः (śaśayāḥ)—those that remain fixed in the atmosphere
  • अप्रदुग्धाः (apradugdhāḥ)—those full of sap
  • सबर्दुघाः (sabardughāḥ)—those that pour out the milk that has the form of water
  • युवतयः (yuvatayaḥ)—those that are mutually joined
  • नव्यानव्याः (navyānavyāḥ)—those that always attain newness
  • भवंतीः (bhavaṃtīḥ)—being so, the clouds (or the quarters)
  • आ धुनयंतां (ā dhunayaṃtāṃ)—let them be shaken (for the sake of each one)
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the clouds, which gratify the world, are without young, abide fixed in the atmosphere, are full of sap, pour out the milk that has the form of water, are mutually joined and always attain newness, be shaken, each for its own purpose. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May the milch cows without their young, abiding (in the heaven), and though unmilked, yet yielding milk, and ever fresh and youthful, be shaken (so as to perform their functions) : great and unequalled is the might of the gods.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Anukramaṇikā says that this sixteenth mantra of the sūkta has the quarters (दिग्वचनतॆ (digvacanatè)) as its deity. In the bhāṣya Sāyaṇa explains the meaning thus: दिशः मेघा वा आ धुनयंतां आ दुहंतु (diśaḥ meghā vā ā dhunayaṃtāṃ ā duhaṃtu), "let the quarters or the clouds keep us in joy". Neither a word for the quarters nor a word for the clouds is used here separately; only the epithets are common to both kinds of meaning, clouds or quarters. The clouds gratify the world by pouring rain. "Aśiśvī" means being without sons, or not having children; शशयाः (śaśayāḥ) means remaining in the atmosphere itself;

p. 309

अप्रदुग्दाः (apradugdāḥ) means being filled with water; सबर्दुघाः (sabardughāḥ) means milking the milk that has the form of water; युवतयः (yuvatayaḥ) means being joined together mutually; नव्यानव्याः (navyānavyāḥ) means being in an ever-new manner. Since all these qualities belong to the quarters as well, the prayer of the sacrificer is stated: let these clouds, or these quarters, keep us, the sacrificers, in joy.

Ṛk 17

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यद॒न्यासु॑ वृष॒भो रोर॑वीति॒ सो अ॒न्यस्मि॑न्यू॒थे नि द॑धाति॒ रेतः॑ ।
स हि क्षपा॑वा॒न्त्स भगः॒ स राजा॑ म॒हद्दे॒वाना॑मसुर॒त्वमेकं॑ ॥

yadanyāsu vṛṣabho roravīti so anyasminyūthe ni dadhāti retaḥ |
sa hi kṣapāvāntsa bhagaḥ sa rājā mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖

यत् । अन्यासु । वृषभः । रोरवीति । सः । अन्यस्मिन् । यूथे । नि । दधाति । रेतः ।
सः । हि । क्षपावान् । सः । भगः । सः । राजा । महत् । देवानां । असुरत्वं । एकं॥
॥ १७ ॥

yat | anyāsu | vṛṣabhaḥ | roravīti | saḥ | anyasmin | yūthe | ni | dadhāti | retaḥ |
saḥ | hi | kṣapāvān | saḥ | bhagaḥ | saḥ | rājā | mahat | devānāṃ | asuratvaṃ | ekaṃ‖
‖ 17 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

वृषभोऽपां वर्षको यद्यः पर्जन्यात्मेंद्रोऽन्यासु दिक्षु रोरवीति मेघद्वारा भृशं शब्दं करोति स पर्जन्य इंद्रोऽन्यस्मिन्यूथे दिशां वृंदे रेत उदकं नि दधाति । तत्र वर्षति । लोके हि वृषभः कासुचिद्दोषु रेतःसेकार्थं रवं करोत्यन्यस्मिन् गोयूथे रेतः सिंचति । तद्वत् । स इंद्रः क्षपावान् । क्षिपति शत्रूनुदकं वेति क्षेपणवान् । यद्वा । क्षपा रात्रिः । तथा रात्रि पर्याययागानां स्तोत्राणां भागभूता या रात्रिः सोच्यते । तद्वान् । स भगः । सर्वैर्भजनीयः । स राजा हि । तत्तत्कर्मानुरूपफलप्रदानेन सर्वेषां राजा खलु ॥ रोरवीति । रु शब्द इत्यस्य यज् लुगंतस्य लटि रूपं । एकान्याभ्यां समर्थाभ्यामिति प्रथमस्य न निघातः। यूथे । यु मिश्रणे । तिथपृष्ट गूथयूथप्रोथा इति थक्प्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातनाद्दीर्घः । रेतः । रीज् क्षरण इत्यस्मात् सुरीभ्यां तुट् चेत्यसुन्नत्ययस्तुडागमश्च । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The bull, the rainer of waters, is Indra in the form of Parjanya. When he roars loudly among the other quarters by means of the clouds, that same Parjanya-Indra deposits रेतः (retaḥ), water, in another herd, the multitude of the quarters; there it rains. In the world a bull makes a roar over certain cows in order to shed seed, and sheds seed in another herd of cows; it is like that. That Indra is क्षपावान् (kṣapāvān): क्षिपति शत्रूनुदकं वेति (kṣipati śatrūnudakaṃ veti), he throws enemies or water, so he is possessed of throwing. Or else क्षपा (kṣapā) is night: the night that forms a part of the hymns of the rātri-paryāya sacrifices is called so, and he possesses it. He is भगः (bhagaḥ), to be worshipped by all. He is the king, for by granting fruit in accordance with each deed he is king of all. (The rest of the block is grammar.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ)—the water-pourer
  • यत् (yat)—the Indra, of the nature of Parjanya, who
  • अन्यासु (anyāsu)—in the other quarters
  • गोरवीति (goravīti)—makes a sound by means of the cloud NOTE
  • सः (saḥ)—that same Indra of the nature of Parjanya

p. 310

  • अन्यस्मिन् यूथे (anyasmin yūthe)—in another quarter
  • रेतः (retaḥ)—the water in the form of rain
  • नि दधाति (ni dadhāti)—pours down
  • सः (saḥ)—that same Indra
  • क्षपावान् (kṣapāvān)—possessed of night
  • सः (saḥ)—he
  • भगः (bhagaḥ)—venerable
  • सः (saḥ)—he
  • राजा हि (rājā hi)—is also the lord
  • देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods
  • असुरत्वं (asuratvaṃ)—the might
  • महत् (mahat)—is great
  • एकं (ekaṃ)—and unequalled
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the maker of rain and of the nature of Parjanya, makes the sound of thunder in one quarter by means of the cloud and pours down rain in another quarter. Indra is possessed of night, venerable and the lord. The might of the gods is great and unequalled.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

When the showerer roars in other (regions) he sends down the rain upon a different herd, for he is the victor, the asuspicious, the sovereign : great and unequalled is the might of the gods,

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The word रेतः (retaḥ) is listed among the names of water (Ni. 2-24). Indra, who is in the form of Parjanya, is described as being in the form of a bull. वृषभः अपां वर्षकं अन्यासु दिक्षु मेघद्वारा भृशं शब्दं करोति अन्यस्मि यूथे दितां वृंदे उदकं वर्षति । लोके हि वृषभः कासुचित् गोषु रेतस्सेकार्थं रवं करोति अन्यस्मिन् गोयूथे रेतस्सिंचति तद्वत् । (vṛṣabhaḥ apāṃ varṣakaṃ anyāsu dikṣu meghadvārā bhṛśaṃ śabdaṃ karoti anyasmi yūthe ditāṃ vṛṃde udakaṃ varṣati | loke hi vṛṣabhaḥ kāsucit goṣu retassekārthaṃ ravaṃ karoti anyasmin goyūthe retassiṃcati tadvat |) NOTE. In the world a bull, while bellowing in a herd of cows, unites with a cow in another herd. In the same way Indra, making a sound through the clouds in order to pour rain in one quarter, pours water in the form of rain in another quarter; thus the likeness to a bull is established for Indra.

Two kinds of meaning are set out for the word क्षपावान् (kṣapāvān) NOTE. For the word क्षपा (kṣapā) the meaning "throwing, hurling" (क्षेपण (kṣepaṇa)) is given. From this it is explained that Indra is one who drives away enemies, or one who pours waters down for the worlds.

The word क्षपा (kṣapā) is listed among the names of night (Ni. 2-18). Sāyaṇa says क्षपा रात्रिः । रात्रि पर्याययागानां स्तोत्राणां भागभूता या रात्रिः सोच्यते । तद्वान् । (kṣapā rātriḥ | rātri paryāyayāgānāṃ stotrāṇāṃ bhāgabhūtā yā rātriḥ socyate | tadvān |). By the word क्षपा (kṣapā) night is meant. In the sacrifices performed at night, the nights suitable for reciting hymns contain hymns of Indra; therefore Indra is possessed of क्षपा (kṣapā). Thus the second meaning is explained.

p. 311

सः भगः राजा हि—सर्वैः भजनीयः । तत्तत्कर्मानुपफलप्रदनेन सर्वेषां राजा। (saḥ bhagaḥ rājā hi—sarvaiḥ bhajanīyaḥ | tattatkarmānupaphalapradanena sarveṣāṃ rājā|). Indra is one worthy of being served by all, and gives to each the fruit corresponding to his respective deeds; therefore he is the lord. And the might of the gods is described as extraordinary and pre-eminent.
