But it must be examined whether the division of the seasons in the Ṛksaṃhitā is as it is now in use, or whether the divisions there differ from the present reckoning.

For the epithet त्रिपाजस्यः (tripājasyaḥ) Sāyaṇa has explained that the divisions named Grīṣma, Varṣā and Hemanta are the chest region of the year. If the doubt arises whether the meaning "chest" or the meaning "strength" is right for the word pājasya, he has also stated that there is no impropriety in giving this meaning, since the chest is the strongest of all the limbs. And for the word त्र्युधा (tryudhā) he has explained that the three divisions Vasanta, Śarad and Hemanta are like the udder region of the year. In the present context one must see whether these divisions of the year are stated in the same way everywhere, or whether the number of the seasons differs from one place to another.

Grīṣma, Varṣā, Hemanta is one division; Vasanta, Śarad, Hemanta is another division.

Here Hemanta is common to both. There is no separate division called the Śiśira season; it should be understood as included in Hemanta. Therefore, whether the number of seasons is five or six cannot be stated as "this and thus". There are many differences in this division. The number of the seasons is stated as three in some places, as five in others, as six in some passages and as seven in one or two contexts. But these reckonings cannot be said to contradict one another. In places such as यजाता यतुभिध्र्रुवेभिः (yajātā yatubhidhrruvebhiḥ) (1-84-18) NOTE there is no reckoning of number but merely a mention of the seasons, yet the epithet dhruvebhiḥ tells us the nature of the season. But in some other places there is no distinction by names of the seasons; the number of the seasons must be known from the number alone. For example:

त्रिनाभि चक्रमजरमनर्वं यत्रेमा विश्वा भुवनाधि तस्थुः । (trinābhi cakramajaramanarvaṃ yatremā viśvā bhuvanādhi tasthuḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-2)

p. 343

In the phrase त्रिनाभि चक्रं (trinābhi cakraṃ) the word trinābhi ("three-naved") points to the parts of the year. Explaining this passage, the Nirukta-writers say:

संवत्सरप्रधान उत्तरोर्धर्चस्त्रिनाभिचक्रं त्रैशितुः संवत्सरो ग्रीष्मो वर्षा हेमंत इति ॥ (saṃvatsarapradhāna uttarordharcastrinābhicakraṃ traiśituḥ saṃvatsaro grīṣmo varṣā hemaṃta iti ‖) (Ni. 4-26).

This year consists of three naves. The naves are the Grīṣma (summer) season, the Varṣā (rainy) season and the Hemanta (winter) season. This year, made of three seasons, is described as त्रिनाभिचक्रं (trinābhicakraṃ). The meaning is that Āditya (the sun) turns by repetition the wheel of the year, which has these parts, which like a wheel goes round again and again, and which is ageless and without a rival (anarva). Supporting this very meaning, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says:

तिस्रो रात्रिर्व्रतं चरति (tisro rātrirvrataṃ carati) त्रयो वा ऋतवः संवत्सरस्य .... .... (trayo vā ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsarasya .... ....) (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-28).

This rule is that there are to be three nights. Since the year has three seasons, the rule must follow this number. This year is Āditya. In such places only the number three is stated, yet in the Ṛksaṃhitā the names themselves are expressly stated:

यत्पुरुषेण हविषा देवा यज्ञमतन्वत । वसंतो अस्यासीदाज्यं ग्रीष्म इध्मश्वरद्भविः ॥ (yatpuruṣeṇa haviṣā devā yajñamatanvata | vasaṃto asyāsīdājyaṃ grīṣma idhmaśvaradbhaviḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-6).

This sacrifice, which has the form of the Puruṣa, reflects the principle of the year. For it, spring is the ghee, summer the fuel, and autumn the oblation: thus the names of three seasons are given. But in the sentence पंचपादं पितरं द्वादशाकृतिं (paṃcapādaṃ pitaraṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ) (1-164-12), "five-footed" means five seasons. एतत् हेमंतशिशिरयोः एकत्राभिप्रायं (etat hemaṃtaśiśirayoḥ ekatrābhiprāyaṃ) NOTE. There is no separate Śiśira; Hemanta and Śiśira together make one. Hence the number five is in order. In contrast, in sentences such as साकंजानां सप्तथमाहुरेकजं (sākaṃjānāṃ saptathamāhurekajaṃ) (1-164-15) seven seasons are indicated; here the Śiśira season has a place of its own. Moreover: चैत्रादीनां द्वादशानां मासानां द्वयमेलनेन वसंताद्याः षडृतवो भवंति । अधिकमासेन एकः उत्पद्यते सप्तमर्तुः । (caitrādīnāṃ dvādaśānāṃ māsānāṃ dvayamelanena vasaṃtādyāḥ ṣaḍṛtavo bhavaṃti | adhikamāsena ekaḥ utpadyate saptamartuḥ |). Caitra and Vaiśākha together make one season; thus one season for each pair of months, and another season for the intercalary month. So there are six for twelve months, and a seventh season for the thirteenth month; this too is so. To call Hemanta and Śiśira together by the single name Hemanta-Śiśira is customary in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā and similar works.

p. 344

वसंतमृतूनां प्रीणामि स मा प्रीतः प्रीणातु ग्रीष्ममृतूनां प्रीणामि स मा प्रीतः प्रीणातु । वर्षाऋतूनां प्रीणामि ता मा प्रीताः प्रीणंतु । शरदमृतूनां प्रीणामि सा मा प्रीता प्रिणातु । हेमंतशिशिरावृतूनां प्रीणामि तौ मा प्रित्वा प्रीणीतां ॥ (vasaṃtamṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmi sa mā prītaḥ prīṇātu grīṣmamṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmi sa mā prītaḥ prīṇātu | varṣāṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmi tā mā prītāḥ prīṇaṃtu | śaradamṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmi sā mā prītā priṇātu | hemaṃtaśiśirāvṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmi tau mā pritvā prīṇītāṃ ‖) (Śai. Saṃ. 1-6-2). NOTE

I satisfy the spring season; may it, satisfied, gladden me. I satisfy the summer season; may it, satisfied, satisfy me. I nourish the rainy season; may it, nourished, gladden me. I satisfy the autumn season; may it, satisfied, satisfy me. I satisfy the Hemanta-Śiśira seasons; may they, satisfied, satisfy me. Thus the number of the seasons is stated, and it is expressly given as five. Supporting this, पंचोपदधाति । पंच वा ऋतवः (paṃcopadadhāti | paṃca vā ṛtavaḥ): here a definite count of five is made. Likewise, in sentences such as ग्रीष्मो हेमंत उत नो वसंतश्वरद्वर्षास्सुवितं नो अस्तु (grīṣmo hemaṃta uta no vasaṃtaśvaradvarṣāssuvitaṃ no astu), five seasons without Śiśira are stated in many places. This number agrees with the number in the Ṛksaṃhitā sentence पंचारे चक्रे (paṃcāre cakre).

In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, when the nature of Āditya is described, the seasons are given as his limbs in this way:

संवत्थरोऽसि परिवत्थरोऽसि । इदावत्सरोऽसि दुवत्सरोऽसि । इद्वत्सरोऽसि वत्सरोऽसि तस्य ते वसंतश्शिरः । ग्रीष्मो दक्षिणः पक्षः । वर्षाः पुच्छं । शरदुत्तरः पक्षः । हेमंतो मध्यं । (saṃvattharo 'si parivattharo 'si | idāvatsaro 'si duvatsaro 'si | idvatsaro 'si vatsaro 'si tasya te vasaṃtaśśiraḥ | grīṣmo dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | varṣāḥ pucchaṃ | śaraduttaraḥ pakṣaḥ | hemaṃto madhyaṃ |) (Tai. Brā. 3-10-4-1).

For this Āditya the Grīṣma season is the right wing, the rainy season the tail, the autumn season the left wing, Hemanta the middle, and spring, the foremost of all, the head: so the description is both material and spiritual. Here too Śiśira is included within Hemanta.

But in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa there is a difference of another kind. Here the description of the form of the sacrificial Self is made up of limbs that are seasons. Instead of joining the Hemanta and Śiśira seasons as elsewhere, it joins the rainy season and autumn together as वर्षाशरदावृतू (varṣāśaradāvṛtū). There are also places where Hemanta and Śiśira are divided and the names of six seasons are stated together: षड्भिः पचति । षड्वा ऋतवः । ऋतुभिरेवैनां पचति (ṣaḍbhiḥ pacati | ṣaḍvā ṛtavaḥ | ṛtubhirevaināṃ pacati) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-1-7-2) and similar passages state "six" plainly.

p. 346

When the division is made into six in this way, the description of the present Ṛk is that the first three seasons show one power of the year and the other three another power. Among them, Grīṣma, Varṣā and Hemanta are described as tripājasya, and Vasanta, Śarad and Hemanta as tryudhā. It was thus said that in these seasons brightness and strength, these two qualities, belong first to the group of three, while the bestowing of wealth and wholesome things belongs to the second group of three. But the power of the seasons is reckoned in one way in one place and in another way elsewhere. For example, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says that the Prayāja sacrifice, the root of all victory, is the essence of the principle of the seasons. In the Prayāja sacrifice the five, Samidh, Tanūnapāt, Iḍa, Barhi and Svāhā, are the chief principles. These five exert their influence on the five seasons in order, and in accordance with that influence the five seasons become fruitful to the sacrificer. This is described in the present Ṛk by retodhāḥ.

ऋतवो ह वै प्रयाजाः । तस्मात्पंच भवंति पंच हृतवः । देवाश्च वा असुराश्च । उभये प्राजापत्याः पस्प धिर एतस्मिन् यज्ञे प्रजापत् पितरि संवत्सरेऽस्माकमयं भविष्यत्यस्माकमयं भविष्यतीति । (ṛtavo ha vai prayājāḥ | tasmātpaṃca bhavaṃti paṃca hṛtavaḥ | devāśca vā asurāśca | ubhaye prājāpatyāḥ paspa dhira etasmin yajñe prajāpat pitari saṃvatsare 'smākamayaṃ bhaviṣyatyasmākamayaṃ bhaviṣyatīti |) (Śa. Brā. 1-5-3-1, 2).

The year is the principle of Prajāpati. The gods and the asuras, both born of Prajāpati, fell into doubt about their father Prajāpati, who is the year, and quarrelled. The gods insisted that it belonged to them, the asuras that it belonged to them.

ततो देवाः । अर्चंतः श्राम्यंतश्चेरुस्त एतान् प्रयाजान् ददृशुस्त्यैरयजंत तैर्यतून् संवत्सरं प्राजयन्नृतुभ्यः संवत्सरात्सपत्नान् .... .... .... तस्मात्संवत्सरात्सपत्नानंतरेति ॥ (tato devāḥ | arcaṃtaḥ śrāmyaṃtaścerusta etān prayājān dadṛśustyairayajaṃta tairyatūn saṃvatsaraṃ prājayannṛtubhyaḥ saṃvatsarātsapatnān .... .... .... tasmātsaṃvatsarātsapatnānaṃtareti ‖) (Śa. Brā. 1-5-3-3).

Then the gods, worshipping and practising austerity, propitiated the deity presiding over the year. They saw the Prayāja and with its help made their worship. Then they won over the seasons and the year.

स आश्राव्याह । समिधो यजेति तद्वसंतग्ं समिंधे । स वसंतः समिद्धोऽन्यानृतून् समिंध ऋतवः समिद्धाः प्रजाश्च प्रजनयंत्योषधीश्च पचंति । (sa āśrāvyāha | samidho yajeti tadvasaṃtagṃ samiṃdhe | sa vasaṃtaḥ samiddho 'nyānṛtūn samiṃdha ṛtavaḥ samiddhāḥ prajāśca prajanayaṃtyoṣadhīśca pacaṃti |) (Śa. Brā. 1-5-3-8).

Then the Adhvaryu says to the Hotṛ, "Recite the yājyā mantra to the fuel-sticks." Then spring is kindled. The kindled spring brings forth the other seasons too. All the other seasons, kindled, cause the birth of creatures and make the plants bear fruit.

स वै समिधो यजति । वसंतो वै समिद्वसंतमेव तद्देवा अवृंजत वसंतात्सपत्नानंतरायन् .... .... .... वसंतात्सपत्नानंतरेति । (sa vai samidho yajati | vasaṃto vai samidvasaṃtameva taddevā avṛṃjata vasaṃtātsapatnānaṃtarāyan .... .... .... vasaṃtātsapatnānaṃtareti |) (Śa. Brā. 1-5-3-9). NOTE

Then he recites the yājyā mantra to the fuel-sticks. The presiding deity of this fuel is spring itself. On this occasion the gods won over spring and destroyed the enemies of spring. Therefore spring is a bringer of victory.

अथ तनूनपातं यजति । ग्रीष्मो वै तनूनपात् ग्रीष्मो ह्यासां प्रजानां तनूस्तपति ग्रीष्ठमेव तद्देवा अवृंजत ग्रीष्मात्सपत्नानंतरायन् ॥ (atha tanūnapātaṃ yajati | grīṣmo vai tanūnapāt grīṣmo hyāsāṃ prajānāṃ tanūstapati grīṣṭhameva taddevā avṛṃjata grīṣmātsapatnānaṃtarāyan ‖) (Śa. Brā. 1-5-3-10).

Then he recites the yājyā to the deity Tanūnapāt. The gods won over Grīṣma, which burns enemies, by this mantra and by worship, and made it so that the fruit of Grīṣma did not reach their enemies.

अथेडो यजति । वर्षा वा इड इति हि वर्षा इडो यदिदं क्षुद्रग्ंसरीसृपं ग्रीष्महेमंताभ्यां नित्यक्तं भवति तद्वर्षा ईडितमिवान्नमिच्छमानं चरति....॥ (atheḍo yajati | varṣā vā iḍa iti hi varṣā iḍo yadidaṃ kṣudragṃsarīsṛpaṃ grīṣmahemaṃtābhyāṃ nityaktaṃ bhavati tadvarṣā īḍitamivānnamicchamānaṃ carati....‖) (Śa. Brā. 1-5-3-11).

Then, at the time of reciting the yājyā to Iḍa, the gods won over the rainy season. Creatures troubled in the summer and in the Hemanta season regain vitality again in this season, and they announce rain.

In the same way, when the mantra is recited to Barhi, they won over the deity presiding over autumn. All the plants that were struck down in Grīṣma and Hemanta regain vitality in this season. When the recitation is made to the deity Svāhā, they made present to themselves Hemanta, the end of the year. They made it so that the final benefit of the year did not fall to the asuras. These seasons, which accomplished the desired aims of the gods, grant desired aims to man also. This very point is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in sentences such as "he recites to the fuel-sticks; he wins spring among the seasons":

समिधो यजति वसंतमेवर्तूनामवरुंधे तनूनपातं यजति ग्रीष्ममेवावरुंध इडो यजति वर्षा एवावरुंधे बर्हिर्यजति शरदमेवावरुंधे (samidho yajati vasaṃtamevartūnāmavaruṃdhe tanūnapātaṃ yajati grīṣmamevāvaruṃdha iḍo yajati varṣā evāvaruṃdhe barhiryajati śaradamevāvaruṃdhe)

p. 347

स्वाहाकारं यजति हेमंतमेवावरुंधे तस्मात्साहाकृता हेमन् पशवोऽव सीदंति समिधो यजत्युषस एव देवतानामवरुंधे तनूनपातं यजति यज्ञमेवावरुंधे इडो यजति पशूनेवावरुंधे बर्हिर्यजति प्रजामेवावरुंध समानयत उपभृतस्तेजो वा आज्यं प्रजा बर्हिः प्रजास्वेव तेजो दधाति स्वाहाकारं यजति वाचमेवावरुंदे ॥ (svāhākāraṃ yajati hemaṃtamevāvaruṃdhe tasmātsāhākṛtā heman paśavo 'va sīdaṃti samidho yajatyuṣasa eva devatānāmavaruṃdhe tanūnapātaṃ yajati yajñamevāvaruṃdhe iḍo yajati paśūnevāvaruṃdhe barhiryajati prajāmevāvaruṃdha samānayata upabhṛtastejo vā ājyaṃ prajā barhiḥ prajāsveva tejo dadhāti svāhākāraṃ yajati vācamevāvaruṃde ‖) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-1-1, 2). NOTE

Besides this, the seasons have natural powers that also indicate the duties of the castes and stages of life.

ब्रह्मैव वसंतः । क्षत्रं ग्रीष्मो विडेव वर्षास्तस्माद्ब्राह्मणो वसंत आदधीत ब्रह्म हि वसंतस्तस्मात् क्षत्रियो ग्रीष्म आदधीत क्षत्रग्ं हि ग्रीष्मस्त स्माद्वैश्यो वर्षास्वादधीत विड्डि वर्षाः (brahmaiva vasaṃtaḥ | kṣatraṃ grīṣmo viḍeva varṣāstasmādbrāhmaṇo vasaṃta ādadhīta brahma hi vasaṃtastasmāt kṣatriyo grīṣma ādadhīta kṣatragṃ hi grīṣmasta smādvaiśyo varṣāsvādadhīta viḍḍi varṣāḥ) (Śa. Brā. 2-1-3-5).

Spring is of the nature of Brahman. Therefore a Brāhmaṇa should establish the fire in spring. Grīṣma is of the nature of the Kṣatra; therefore a Kṣatriya should do so in the Grīṣma season; and since the rainy season is of the nature of the Vaiśya, a Vaiśya should perform it in the rainy season.

वसंता ब्राह्मणोऽग्निमादधीत । वसंतो वैब्राह्मणस्यर्तुः । स्व एवैनमृतावाधाय । ब्रह्मवर्चसी भवति । मुखं ना एतदृतूनां । यद्वसंतः । यो वसंताग्निमाधत्ते । मुख्य एव भवति । ग्रीष्मो वै राजन्यस्यर्तुः । स्व एवैनमृतावाधाय । इंद्रियावी भवति । शरदि वैश्य आदधीत । शरद्वै वैश्यस्यर्तुः । स्व एवैनमृतावाधाय । पशुमान् भवति । (vasaṃtā brāhmaṇo 'gnimādadhīta | vasaṃto vaibrāhmaṇasyartuḥ | sva evainamṛtāvādhāya | brahmavarcasī bhavati | mukhaṃ nā etadṛtūnāṃ | yadvasaṃtaḥ | yo vasaṃtāgnimādhatte | mukhya eva bhavati | grīṣmo vai rājanyasyartuḥ | sva evainamṛtāvādhāya | iṃdriyāvī bhavati | śaradi vaiśya ādadhīta | śaradvai vaiśyasyartuḥ | sva evainamṛtāvādhāya | paśumān bhavati |) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-2-6, 7).

A Brāhmaṇa should perform the sacrifice in the spring season. For spring is the Brāhmaṇa's own season. If he sacrifices in his own season, he becomes endowed with Brahmanical splendour. This spring season is the first (or the chief) of all the seasons; therefore one who sacrifices in the chief season of all becomes esteemed and honoured among men. A Kṣatriya should sacrifice in the Grīṣma season, for Grīṣma is the Kṣatriya's own season. A Kṣatriya who sacrifices in his own season becomes mighty. A Vaiśya should sacrifice in the autumn season, for autumn is the Vaiśya's own season. A Vaiśya who sacrifices in his own season becomes possessed of wealth such as cattle. Thus the rule of seasons laid down for Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas is stated here. This description of nature accords with the description in the present Ṛk, traināka, "having three qualities".

p. 348

Moreover, the description of threefold natures by epithets such as tryudhā, tripājasyaḥ and tryanīkaḥ may be said to show that the seasons, the limbs of the year, represent the three worlds.

संवत्सर एषोऽग्निरिम उ लोकाः संवत्सरः तस्य यदूर्ध्वं पृथिव्या अर्वाचीनमंतरिक्षात्तदस्यैषा द्वितीया चितिस्तद्वस्य ग्रीष्म ऋतुः ॥ (saṃvatsara eṣo 'gnirima u lokāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ tasya yadūrdhvaṃ pṛthivyā arvācīnamaṃtarikṣāttadasyaiṣā dvitīyā citistadvasya grīṣma ṛtuḥ ‖) (Śa. Brā. 8-2-1-7).

This year reflects the three worlds as well. Its limbs, the seasons, are the representatives of the respective worlds. The world that is above the earth and below the atmosphere has the form of the Grīṣma season. (Spring is included in it; the sense is that the first pair of seasons reflects the first world.)

संवत्सर एषोग्निरिम उ लोकाः संवत्सरस्तस्यांतरिक्षमेव मध्यमा चितिरंतरिक्षमस्य वर्षा शरदावृतू तद्यदेता अत्रोपदधाति । (saṃvatsara eṣognirima u lokāḥ saṃvatsarastasyāṃtarikṣameva madhyamā citiraṃtarikṣamasya varṣā śaradāvṛtū tadyadetā atropadadhāti |) (Śa. Brā. 8-3-2-7).

The principle of these three worlds is contained in the year itself. The second fire-layer reflects the atmosphere, the middle of these worlds. The rainy season and autumn, the middle limbs of the year, are both representatives of this atmosphere; that is, they have that nature.

यदूर्ध्वमंतरिक्षात् अर्वाचीनं दिवः तदस्यैषा चतुर्थी चितिस्तद्वस्य हेमंत ऋतुः ॥ (yadūrdhvamaṃtarikṣāt arvācīnaṃ divaḥ tadasyaiṣā caturthī citistadvasya hemaṃta ṛtuḥ ‖) (Śa. Brā. 8-4-2-15).

The representative of the world that lies above the atmosphere and at the side of the heavenly world is the Hemanta season. In this way the limbs of the year reflect the limbs of the three worlds. Since the one principle of Agni pervades the three worlds also in the forms of Vāyu and Āditya, this Agni is the all-pervading Lord.

प्रजापतिरेषोग्निः संवत्सर उ प्रजापतिस्तस्य यदूर्ध्वं .... .... (prajāpatireṣogniḥ saṃvatsara u prajāpatistasya yadūrdhvaṃ .... ....) (Śa. Brā. 8-4-2-16).

This Agni is Prajāpati, the all-pervading one, the cause of the creation of the universe. This Prajāpati is the three worlds. These worlds are the all-pervading year. The seasons, the limbs of this year, reflect also the limbs of Prajāpati. Thus they declare the greatness of the principle of the year, which has three qualities (traināka).

p. 349

ऋषभो वा एष ऋतूनां यत्संवत्सरः ... .... ऋषभ एष यज्ञानां । (ṛṣabho vā eṣa ṛtūnāṃ yatsaṃvatsaraḥ ... .... ṛṣabha eṣa yajñānāṃ |) (Śa. Brā. 13-1-2-2).

As the Aśvamedha, which gives the most excellent fruit, is the best of all sacrifices, so the year is the bull among the seasons. This description shows the purport of the epithet vṛṣabhaḥ in the present Ṛk.

Retodhāḥ: this epithet may refer to Āditya or to the year. It was stated earlier that the rays of Āditya are described by the word retas. Retas means either the seed that produces the world, or the water that is the cause of the origin and protection of beings. And when explaining the sentence आपो वै सर्वॆ देवा सर्वाणि भूतानि (āpo vai sarvè devā sarvāṇi bhūtāni) (Śa. Brā. 10-5-4-14), Sāyaṇa said: अर्चिषो ह्यापसूरकिरणानामेव वृष्टिकर्तकृत्वात् कार‍्यकारणयोरभेदेन अर्चिवा आप इत्युक्तं । (arciṣo hyāpasūrakiraṇānāmeva vṛṣṭikartakṛtvāt kāryakāraṇayorabhedena arcivā āpa ityuktaṃ |). Since he says that, because the sun's rays are the cause of the streams of water, the rays are described figuratively as streams, the word retas here too can be given that meaning. Moreover, when explaining the sentence षळिद्यमा ऋषयो देवजा इति (ṣaḷidyamā ṛṣayo devajā iti) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-15), he said षड्रश्मयः षण्णां ऋतूनां प्रवर्तकाः (ṣaḍraśmayaḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ ṛtūnāṃ pravartakāḥ): the six rays of Āditya are the causes of the six seasons. Just as the rays of Āditya are described as retodhāḥ, in the same way in the present Ṛk the limbs of the year are described as retodhāḥ.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒भीक॑ आसां पद॒वीर॑बोध्यादि॒त्याना॑मह्वे॒ चारु॒ नाम॑ ।
आप॑श्चिदस्मा अरमंत दे॒वीः पृथ॒ग्वजं॑तीः॒ परि॑ षीमवृंजन् ॥ ४ ॥

abhīka āsāṃ padavīrabodhyādityānāmahve cāru nāma |
āpaścidasmā aramaṃta devīḥ pṛthagvajaṃtīḥ pari ṣīmavṛṃjan ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अभीके । आसां । पदवीः । अबोधि । आदित्यानां । अह्वे । चारु । नाम ।
आपः । चित् । अस्मै । अरमंत । देवीः । पृथक् । व्रजंतीः । परि । सीं । अव्वंजन् ॥

abhīke | āsāṃ | padavīḥ | abodhi | ādityānāṃ | ahve | cāru | nāma |
āpaḥ | cit | asmai | aramaṃta | devīḥ | pṛthak | vrajaṃtīḥ | pari | sīṃ | avvaṃjan ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

संवत्सर आसामोषधीनामभीके समीपे पदवीः । पदानि तत्तद्वनविशिष्टपुष्पफलादीनि वेति प्रजनयतीति पदवीः सन् अबोधि । बुध्यते । सावधानो वर्तते ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

The year (संवत्सर (saṃvatsara)) is "awake" (अबोधि (abodhi)), that is, it is attentive, near these plants (āsāmoṣadhīnāṃ), as पदवीः (padavīḥ). He explains पदानि (padāni) as the flowers, fruits and the like special to this or that forest, and the year produces them. NOTE

p. 350

तथादित्यानां । आदित्या मासाः संख्यासाम्यात् । यद्वा । आदित्यसंक्रमणनिमित्तत्वादादित्या मासाः । मेषादिस्थे सवितरि यो यो मासः प्रपूर्यते चांद्रश्चैत्राद्यः स ज्ञेय इति स्मृतेः । तेषां चैत्रादीनां मासानां चारु नाम मधुश्च माधवश्चेत्यादि नामधेयमहे । आह्वयामि । उच्चारयामीत्यर्थः । किंच देवीर्द्योतनशीलाः पृथगितस्ततो व्रजंतीर्गच्छंत्य अपश्चित् आपोऽप्यस्मै संवत्सरायारमंत । संवत्सरसंबंधिमासचतुष्टये वृष्टिद्वारा रमंते । ता आपः सीमेनं संवत्सरं पर्यवृंजन् । अष्टसु मासेषु परिवर्जयंति ॥ पदवीः । वी गत्यादिषु । क्विप् । अबोधि । बुध अवगमन इत्यस्य लुजि दीपजनबुधपूरितायिप्यायिभ्योऽन्यतरस्यामिति कर्तरि चिणो लुक् । निघातः । आदित्यानां । आदित्यसंबंधिन इत्यर्थे दित्यदित्यादित्यपत्युत्तरपदाण्ण्य इति ण्यः । अतोलोपयलोपौ । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अह्वे । ह्वयतेर्लुजि सिच आत्मनेपदेष्टन्यतरस्यामित्यजादेशः । गुणः । निघातः । अवृंजन् । वृजी वर्जन इत स्य लजः श्वमि रूपं । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Likewise आदित्यानां (ādityānāṃ): the Ādityas are the months, from the equality of number (twelve). Or else: the months are Ādityas because they are caused by the sun's passage (from sign to sign). He cites the smṛti: when the sun stands in Meṣa and the other signs, the lunar month beginning with Caitra that is then filled out is to be known by that sign. Of those months, Caitra and the others, "I call" (अह्वे (ahve)), that is, I utter, the beautiful names, Madhu, Mādhava and so on. Further, the shining (देवीः (devīḥ)) waters (अपश्चित् (apaścit) = āpo 'pi), going hither and thither, delight (अरमंत (aramaṃta)) in this year: in the four months belonging to the year they take delight through rain. Those waters avoid (पर्यवृंजन् (paryavṛṃjan)) this year (सीं (sīṃ) = enaṃ) in eight months. The rest of the block gives grammar, which is left out here.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • संवत्सरः (saṃvatsaraḥ)—the year
  • आसां (āsāṃ)—of these plants
  • अभीके (abhīke)—which are near
  • पदवीः (padavīḥ)—the paths (the fruits, flowers and so on of the respective plants)
  • अबोधि (abodhi)—knows
  • आदित्यानां (ādityānāṃ)—of the twelve months beginning with Caitra
  • चारु (cāru)—beautiful
  • नाम (nāma)—names
  • अह्वे (ahve)—I utter and recite
  • देवीः (devīḥ)—shining
  • पृथक् (pṛthak)—in separate forms
  • व्रजंतीः (vrajaṃtīḥ)—flowing
  • अपश्चित् (apaścit)—waters
  • अस्मै (asmai)—in the rain-time of this year
  • अरमंत (aramaṃta)—rest
  • सीं (sīṃ)—this same year
  • परि अवृंजन् (pari avṛṃjan)—(in the remaining seasons) abandon
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The year knows the nature of the flowers, fruits and the like that belong to each plant according to the season. I utter and recite the beautiful names of the twelve months beginning with Caitra. The shining waters, flowing in separate forms, rest in the rain-time of this year; they abandon this same year in the remaining seasons.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

(The year) is awake, the path in the vicinity of those (plants) : I call upon the beautiful name of the Adityas; the divine waters wandering severally (now) give it delight, and (now) depart from it.

p. 351

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The nature of the year, the seat of prosperity, is described in this Ṛk also. The members of the year, the causes of abundance of food, and its divisions beginning with the seasons, are praised.

Abhīke—The word अभीक (abhīka) is read among the names of battle and also among the names of "near" (Ni. 2-17; 3-29). प्रसित्त्ये (prasittye) and अभीके (abhīke) are two synonymous words. The word अभीक (abhīka) is formed from the root अंच (aṃca), meaning "to go", joined with the prefix अभि (abhi). The use of this word in the Ṛk

ज्योतिरद्यदन्ने अकृणोदु लोकं प्रावन्मनुं दस्यवे करभीकं । (jyotiradyadanne akṛṇodu lokaṃ prāvanmanuṃ dasyave karabhīkaṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-92-5)

makes the situation clear. The radiance of King Soma is described here. This radiance protects the good and punishes the wicked. The text says that it protected Manu and confronted the Dasyu. To say "confronted", it says that अभीकं (abhīkaṃ) became inclined to go towards the enemy; that is, it tried to confront and punish the enemy. Likewise in

यो दभ्रेभिर्हव्यो यश्च भूरिभिर्यो अभिके वरिवोविन्नृषाह्ये । (yo dabhrebhirhavyo yaśca bhūribhiryo abhike varivovinnṛṣāhye |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-38-4)

and similar places the meaning is likewise "battle". The sense is that Indra is invoked at times of battle just as at times of sacrifice. In some places the word also means a secluded place. For example, in

ज्योतिर्वृणीत तमसो विजानन्नारे स्याम दुरितादभीके । (jyotirvṛṇīta tamaso vijānannāre syāma duritādabhīke |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-7)

दुरितादभीके (duritādabhīke) means "in a secluded region free of sin". In the present Ṛk, अभीके पदवीः (abhīke padavīḥ) means an object that surrounds and is near.

The bhāṣya states that the word अदित्यानां (adityānāṃ) is a synonym for the members of the year. Sāyaṇa explains as follows how the word Āditya is used for a month. First, संख्या साम्यात् आदित्याः मासाः । (saṃkhyā sāmyāt ādityāḥ māsāḥ |) The number of months is twelve and the number of Ādityas is twelve; therefore the word Āditya is meant to denote the twelve months. Or, secondly, because of the connection with the sun's transit, each month is called by the usage "Āditya". Such transits, beginning with Meṣa, are twelve. Therefore the meaning here is that Āditya is the month.

p. 352

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Cāru nāma—Because the number of the months follows the number of the Ādityas, the word आदित्यानां (ādityānāṃ), which expresses identity, is used. To show that the names of these months are very attractive and satisfying, they are described as चारु नाम (cāru nāma). Madhu, Mādhava, Śukra, Śuci, Nabha, Nabhasya, Iṣa, Ūrja, Saha, Sahasya, Tapa and Tapasya are the names of the twelve months. These are called the twelve months beginning with Caitra. To understand how the epithet चारु नाम (cāru nāma) fits these names, one must know the description of their nature.

उपयाम गृहीतोऽसि मधवे त्वेत्येवाध्वर्युर्गृह्णात्युपयामगृहीतोऽसि माधवाय त्वेति प्रतिप्रस्थातैतावेव वासंतिकौ स यद्वसंत ओषधयो जायंते वनस्पतयः पच्यंते तेनो हैतौ मधुश्च माधवश्च । (upayāma gṛhīto 'si madhave tvetyevādhvaryurgṛhṇātyupayāmagṛhīto 'si mādhavāya tveti pratiprasthātaitāveva vāsaṃtikau sa yadvasaṃta oṣadhayo jāyaṃte vanaspatayaḥ pacyaṃte teno haitau madhuśca mādhavaśca |) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-1-14)

Of the seasonal cups, the Adhvaryu takes one and the Pratiprasthātṛ the other. The Adhvaryu recites "I offer this to Madhu", and the Pratiprasthātṛ "I offer this to Mādhava" (Vā. Saṃ. 7-30). Madhu and Mādhava are both months of the spring season. In this season the plants and the rest become laden with fruit and flowers, and the trees bear ripe fruit. Because trees and the rest thus have sweetness, the two names Madhu and Mādhava are well known for the two months that are members of this season.

उपयाम गृहीतोऽसि । शुक्राय तैत्येवाध्वर्युर्गृह्णात्युपयामगृहीतोऽसि शुचये त्वेति प्रतिप्रस्थातैतानेव गैष्मौ स यदेतयोर्बलिष्ठं तपति तेनो हैत् शुक्रश्च शुचिश्च ॥ (upayāma gṛhīto 'si | śukrāya taityevādhvaryurgṛhṇātyupayāmagṛhīto 'si śucaye tveti pratiprasthātaitāneva gaiṣmau sa yadetayorbaliṣṭhaṃ tapati teno hait śukraśca śuciśca ‖) (Ka Brā. 4-3-1-15)NOTE

The Adhvaryu takes the third cup and the Pratiprasthātṛ the fourth. The Adhvaryu recites "I offer this to Śukra", and the Pratiprasthātṛ "I offer this to Śuci". Śukra and Śuci are both members of the summer season. Because there is intense heat at that time, they have these names. Śukra means bright, and Śuci means radiant.

उपयामगृहीतोऽसि नभसे तैत्येवाध्वर्युर्गृह्ण्यात्युपयामगृहीतोऽसि नभस्याय तैति प्रतिप्रस्थातैतावेव वार्षिकावमुतो वै दिवो वर्षति तेनो हैत् नभश्च नभस्यश्च ॥ (upayāmagṛhīto 'si nabhase taityevādhvaryurgṛhṇyātyupayāmagṛhīto 'si nabhasyāya taiti pratiprasthātaitāveva vārṣikāvamuto vai divo varṣati teno hait nabhaśca nabhasyaśca ‖) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-196)NOTE

p. 353

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Then the offering is made to Nabha and Nabhasya. Both are months connected with the rainy season. Because rain falls from the sky, the names Nabha and Nabhasya are well known for these two.

इषे त्वेत्येवाध्वर्युर्गह्नाति .... .... ऊर्जेत्वेति प्रतिप्रस्थातैतावेव शरदौ स यच्छरद्यूर्ग्रस ओषधयः पच्यंते तेनो हैतानिषश्चोर्जश्च ॥ (iṣe tvetyevādhvaryurgahnāti .... .... ūrjetveti pratiprasthātaitāveva śaradau sa yaccharadyūrgrasa oṣadhayaḥ pacyaṃte teno haitāniṣaścorjaśca ‖) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-1-17)

Again the offering is made to Iṣa and Ūrja. Iṣa means sap, and Ūrja means food. Both are members of the autumn season. In this autumn the plants and the rest become full of sap and there is abundance of food, so the names Iṣa and Ūrja are well known.

उपयामगृहीतोऽसि सहसे तैत्येवाध्वर्युर्गृष्णाति उपयामगृहीतोऽसि सहस्याय त्वेति प्रतिप्रस्थातैतावेव हैमंतिकौ स यद्धेमंत इमाः प्रजाः सहसेव स्वं वशमुपनयते तेनो हैतौ सहश्च सहस्यश्च ॥ (upayāmagṛhīto 'si sahase taityevādhvaryurgṛṣṇāti upayāmagṛhīto 'si sahasyāya tveti pratiprasthātaitāveva haimaṃtikau sa yaddhemaṃta imāḥ prajāḥ sahaseva svaṃ vaśamupanayate teno haitau sahaśca sahasyaśca ‖) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-1-18)

The offering is made to Sahas and Sahasya. Both are members of the winter (Hemanta) season. Hemanta draws all beings under its control by force. Sahas means strength or radiance. Therefore its members are named Saha and Sahasya.

तपसे त्वेत्येवाध्वर्युर्गृष्णाति उपयाम गृहीतोऽसि तपस्याय त्वेति प्रतिप्रस्थातैतावेव शैशिरा स यदेतयोर्बलिष्ठं श्यायति तेनो हैत् तपश्च तपस्यश्च ॥ (tapase tvetyevādhvaryurgṛṣṇāti upayāma gṛhīto 'si tapasyāya tveti pratiprasthātaitāveva śaiśirā sa yadetayorbaliṣṭhaṃ śyāyati teno hait tapaśca tapasyaśca ‖) (Śa. Brā. 4-3-1-19)

The two months Tapa and Tapasya are likewise members of the cool season (Śiśira). At this time the body shrinks with cold and wastes away, so these names are well known for the months of this season. In this way the nature of the twelve months has been described. In the same manner it is explained in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā also, beginning "मधुश्च माधवश्च (madhuśca mādhavaśca)" (Tai. Saṃ. 4-4-1-1).

The year, which thus contains five seasons and twelve months, is described as "पंच पादं पितरं द्वादशाकृतिं (paṃca pādaṃ pitaraṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-12). Describing the same point, the Śatapatha says:

तस्य सप्तदश सामिधेन्यः । सप्तदशो वै संवत्सरो द्वादशमासाः पंचर्तवः संवत्सरः प्रजापतिः ॥ (tasya saptadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ | saptadaśo vai saṃvatsaro dvādaśamāsāḥ paṃcartavaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ ‖) (Śa. Brā. 6-2-2-8)

p. 354

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Prajāpati, consisting of twelve months and five seasons, is the year-self with seventeen members. Thus the text shows the relation between Prajāpati and the seventeen sāmidhenī mantras, which are a part of the sacrifice.

आसां आदित्यानां पदवीः अबोधि (āsāṃ ādityānāṃ padavīḥ abodhi)—Since it is said that the year, which has these twelve months and consists of the seasons, has known the nature and power of the several months, one must ask what the "path" of the several months is, and what their natures are. When the names of the months, Madhu, Mādhava, Śukra, Śuci and the rest, were given, their nature was described along with them, as stated above. The paths of the months must now be examined.

द्वादशारं नहि तज्जराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य । आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः ॥ (dvādaśāraṃ nahi tajjarāya varvarti cakraṃ pari dyāmṛtasya | ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiśca tasthuḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-11)

द्वादश प्रधयश्चक्रमेकं त्रीणि नभ्यानि क उ तच्चिकेत । तस्मिन्त्साकं त्रिशता न शंकवोऽर्पिताः षष्टिर्न चलाचलासः । (dvādaśa pradhayaścakramekaṃ trīṇi nabhyāni ka u tacciketa | tasmintsākaṃ triśatā na śaṃkavo 'rpitāḥ ṣaṣṭirna calācalāsaḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-48)

In these Ṛks, in the present sūkta, and in the two mantras above, the description is clear. The members belong to the Āditya, or to the year which has the form of Āditya. The wheel which is the year has twelve felloes and three hubs. According to one reckoning, three hundred and sixty members that revolve on this wheel are fixed together like pegs. Here the three hundred and sixty members indicate the number of days. According to another reckoning the number is seven hundred and twenty; these indicate day and night both. All these are the sons of the Āditya, or of the year that has the form of Āditya. The same reckoning is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa also, in the description of the Caturviṃśa stoma. Only in the Śrautasūtra belonging to the Sāma branch are some differing reckonings found:

  1. 324 days to the year: 12 months of 27 days.
  2. 351 days: 12 months of 27 days and again 27 days.
  3. 354 days: 6 months of 30 days and 6 months of 29 days.

The reason for the differences in reckoning, the difference between the solar and the lunar measure, and the matter of the solstices will be explained in detail later when occasion arises.

The sense is that, having such members, the year knows the path of nature, with its fruits, flowers and the like, clearly nourished according to each season.

p. 355

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

श्री ष॒दस्था॑ सिंधव॒स्त्रिः क॑वी॒नामु॒त त्रि॑मा॒ता वि॒दथे॑षु ॒ सम्राट् ।
ऋ॒ताव॑री॒र्योष॑णास्ति॒स्रो अप्या॒स्तिरा दि॒वो वि॒दथे॒ पत्य॑मानाः ॥ ५ ॥

śrī ṣadasthā siṃdhavastriḥ kavīnāmuta trimātā vidatheṣu
samrāṭ |
ṛtāvarīryoṣaṇāstisro apyāstirā divo vidathe patyamānāḥ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

त्रि । सधस्था । सिंधवः । त्रिः । कवीनां । उत । त्रिमाता । विदथेषु । सम्‌राट् ।
ऋत्यवरीः । योषणाः । तिस्रः । अप्याः । त्रिः । अ । दिवः । विदथे । पत्यमानाः ॥ ५ ॥

tri | sadhasthā | siṃdhavaḥ | triḥ | kavīnāṃ | uta | trimātā | vidatheṣu | samrāṭ |
ṛtyavarīḥ | yoṣaṇāḥ | tisraḥ | apyāḥ | triḥ | a | divaḥ | vidathe | patyamānāḥ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

प्रजापतिः स्वविज्ञानं सिंधूनां निवेदयति । हे सिंधव आपः सर्वसाक्षिण्यो यूयं । त्री षधस्था त्रयो लोकाः । ते च प्रत्येकं त्रिर्भवंति ! तथा त्रयो वा इमे त्रिवृतो लोका इति श्रुतिः । न द्याव इंद्रमोजसा नांतरिक्षाणि वज्रीणं न विव्यचंत भूमयः । ऋग्वे. ८-६-१५ । इति प्रत्येकं बहुवचनश्रवणात् । बहुवचनं च कपिंजलन्यायेन त्रित्वे पर्यवसितं । ते च लोकाः कवीनां देवानां निवासस्थानानि भवंति । उतापि च त्रिमाता त्रयाणाममीषां लोकानां निर्माता संवत्सरः सूर्यो वा विदथेषु यज्ञेषु सम्राट् यजनीयतया सम्यग्दीप्यमानो वर्तते। तथा ऋतावरीरुदकवत्योऽप्या नभस्या आप्तव्या ना तिस्रो योषणास्त्रि संख्याका इलासरस्वतीभारतीत्येवंरूपाः परस्परमिश्रणोपेता देवता विदथे यज्ञॆ दिवो दिवसस्य तिस्त्रिषु सवनेष्वा पत्यमाना आगच्छंत्यो भवंति ॥ सधस्था । पूर्वपदादिति संहितायां षत्वं । योषणाः । युष इति सौत्रो धातुः । ल्युटि रूपं । लित्स्वरः । तिस्रः । तिसृभ्यो जस इत्याद्यु दात्तत्वं । अप्याः । अप् इत्यंतरिक्षनाम । तत्र भवाः । भवे छंदसीति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्यु दात्तत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Prajāpati declares his own knowledge to the rivers. "O rivers, waters, witnesses of all, you are त्री षधस्था (trī ṣadhasthā), the three worlds; and each of them is threefold." The Śruti says, "These three worlds are threefold." This is because the plural is heard for each of them, as in "न द्याव इंद्रमोजसा नांतरिक्षाणि वज्रीणं न विव्यचंत भूमयः (na dyāva iṃdramojasā nāṃtarikṣāṇi vajrīṇaṃ na vivyacaṃta bhūmayaḥ)" (Ṛg. 8-6-15); and the plural, by the kapiñjala rule, ends in the number three. Those worlds are the dwelling-places of the कवीनां (kavīnāṃ), the gods. Further, त्रिमाता (trimātā), the maker of these three worlds, the year or the sun, shines forth at the sacrifices (विदथेषु (vidatheṣu)) as सम्राट् (samrāṭ), fully resplendent as the one to be worshipped. Likewise the ऋतावरीः (ṛtāvarīḥ), those possessing water, the अप्याः (apyāḥ) ... नभस्या आप्तव्या ना (nabhasyā āptavyā nā)NOTE, the three women, three in number, of the forms Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, deities endowed with mutual mixing, come at the sacrifice during the three pressings of the day (दिवो दिवसस्य तिस्त्रिषु सवनेष्वा (divo divasasya tistriṣu savaneṣvā)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • सिंधवः (siṃdhavaḥ)—O waters in the form of streams
  • कवीनां (kavīnāṃ)—for the gods
  • त्रि षधस्था (tri ṣadhasthā)—the three worlds, which are dwelling-places
  • त्रिः (triḥ)—are also of three forms
  • उत (uta)—and
  • त्रिमाता (trimātā)—the year (or the sun), who knows the measure of these three worldsNOTE
  • विदथेषु (vidatheṣu)—at the sacrifices
  • सम्राट् (samrāṭ)—has adorned the position of sovereign
  • ऋतावरीः (ṛtāvarīḥ)—those filled with water

p. 356

  • अप्याः (apyāḥ)—having the form of rain
  • तिस्रः योषणाः (tisraḥ yoṣaṇāḥ)—the three women also
  • विदथे (vidathe)—at the sacrifice
  • दिवः त्रिः (divaḥ triḥ)—at the three pressing-times of the day
  • आ पत्यमानाः (ā patyamānāḥ)—come down
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O waters in the form of streams, the three worlds, the dwelling-places of the gods, are also of three forms. And the year, or the sun, who knows the measure of these three worlds, has adorned the position of sovereign at the sacrifices. The three women, filled with water and having the form of rain, also come down every day at the three pressing-times of the sacrifice.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Rivers, the dwelling-places of the intelligent gods are thrice three; the measurer of the three (worlds) is the sovereign at sacrifices : three female (divinities) of the waters charged with the rains descend from heaven at the thrice (repeated) solemnity.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

A very profound meaning lies in this mantra. Seen superficially, three different ideas seem to illumine three separate points: first, the all-pervading lordship of the gods; second, the greatness of the year; third, the coming of the women at the three pressing-times. But on closer view these ideas are connected with one another and finally end in the exposition of a single principle.

Before understanding what it means that the three worlds are dwelling-places for the gods and that these three worlds are threefold (trivṛt), that is, have three forms, one must note what is distinctive in the use of the word कवि (kavi) as a synonym for the word देव (deva).

कवीनां (kavīnāṃ)—If कवीनां (kavīnāṃ) is taken to mean देवानां (devānāṃ), one and the same entity must be indicated by both words. The context must be one in which both words denote the same form and nature. One must therefore examine what the word देवानां (devānāṃ) indicates. When the etymologies of the names of gods such as Indra and Agni are given, the nature of the gods is also stated.

स योऽयं मध्ये प्राणः । एष एवेंद्रस्तानेष प्राणान्मध्यत इंद्रियेणैंद यदैन्थ तस्मादिंद इंधो ह वै तमिंद्र इत्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवास्त्रइद्धाः सत्त नाना पुरुषानसृजंत । (sa yo 'yaṃ madhye prāṇaḥ | eṣa eveṃdrastāneṣa prāṇānmadhyata iṃdriyeṇaiṃda yadaintha tasmādiṃda iṃdho ha vai tamiṃdra ityācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devāstraiddhāḥ satta nānā puruṣānasṛjaṃta |) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-1-2)

p. 357

Among the vital airs within the body, the chief breath is well known as Indra. This chief breath kindles the other vital airs by its own power. Because it makes them blaze in this way, the name Indra became famous from this very quality of kindling (इंधानः (iṃdhānaḥ)). But one could simply call it इंधानः (iṃdhānaḥ); why then was it called Indra? Because the gods are always fond of what lies beyond the world. इंधानः (iṃdhānaḥ) would be a description in the manner of worldly poetry. To go beyond such worldly description and cross into the realm of the hidden is the mark of the gods. Hence the gods became famous as "lovers of the hidden".

अथ यो गर्भोऽंतरासीत् । सोऽग्रिरसृज्यत स यदस्य सर्वस्याग्रमसृज्यत तस्मादग्रिरग्रिर्ह वै तमग्निरित्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवाः । (atha yo garbho 'ṃtarāsīt | so 'grirasṛjyata sa yadasya sarvasyāgramasṛjyata tasmādagriragrirha vai tamagnirityācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devāḥ |) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-1-11)

The supreme principle that arose from the embryo within Brahman became famous as Agri. Because it was produced first of all beings in the universe, it was called Agri. The gods, who delight in the hidden sense, called this very one Agni. By these explanations the nature of the gods is described: it is the gods' character to convey, or reveal, or deepen the hidden meaning. This quality is common to gods and poets. A hidden meaning that lies beyond the ordinary human view is possible only for the gods. If that godhood is present in a man, he is called a poet (kavi). He has a vision better and more divine than that of an ordinary man. Though he has obtained human birth, he is reckoned a god.

विज्ञानमात्मानंदात्मनो हैव सर्वे देवाः सा हैषैव देवानामद्धाविद्या स ह स न मनुष्यो य एवंविद्देवानाग्ं हैव स एकः ॥ (vijñānamātmānaṃdātmano haiva sarve devāḥ sā haiṣaiva devānāmaddhāvidyā sa ha sa na manuṣyo ya evaṃviddevānāgṃ haiva sa ekaḥ ‖) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-5-13)

Vijñāna means special knowledge. It is full of bliss; true knowledge is the cause of this bliss. Such true knowledge is possible for the gods, not for man. If anyone among men is able to obtain this knowledge, he too is reckoned a god; thus the nature of godhood is shown. For this very reason they have explained the word kavi as "one who sees beyond" (krāntadarśin). The Nirukta authors have read this word among the names of the intelligent, कविः (kaviḥ), मनीषी (manīṣī) and so on (Ni. 3-15).

मेधावी कविः क्रांतदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्वा (medhāvī kaviḥ krāṃtadarśano bhavati kavatervā) (Ni. 12-13)

p. 358

The Nirukta authors' derivation is that this word, formed from the root क्रम् (kram), means one whose vision goes beyond, or, formed from the root कम् (kam), means a worshipper who praises. Both derivations show an intellect and a disposition that grasp the true meaning. Just as the example above explains that the gods have the power to obtain knowledge of the highest truth, so the poet too has an unworldly and extraordinary power of knowing all affairs of past, present and future. On many occasions Sāyaṇa has said that देव (deva) is a synonym of the word kavi. Although he is a man, the poet has godhood in him because he has divine sight; and the sense is that he has a power beyond the human. Though physically he has two eyes, his inner eye equals a thousand eyes.

सहस्रणीथाः कवयो ये गोपायंति सूर्यं । यमहीन् तपस्वतो यम शपोजा अपि गच्छतात् ॥ (sahasraṇīthāḥ kavayo ye gopāyaṃti sūryaṃ | yamahīn tapasvato yama śapojā api gacchatāt ‖) (Ma. Saṃ. 0-154-5) NOTE

The poets have a thousand eyes and see beyond; they have the power to protect even the Āditya. [A thousand-eyed one may mean one with a thousand eyes, or a guide to thousands of followers. If "guide" is meant, it means one who knows the meaning of the principle and has the power to teach others.] Because they have such power,

समुद्रे अंतः कवयो वि चक्षते मरीचीनां पदमिच्छंति वेधसः (samudre aṃtaḥ kavayo vi cakṣate marīcīnāṃ padamicchaṃti vedhasaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-177-1)

these poets who see beyond know the supreme principle that dwells within the orb of the Āditya, and they also desire to attain identity with it. Moreover,

तां द्योतमानां स्वर्यं मनीषामृतस्य पदे कवयो नि पांति (tāṃ dyotamānāṃ svaryaṃ manīṣāmṛtasya pade kavayo ni pāṃti) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-173-2)

ऋतस्य पदं कवयो नि पांति गुहा नामानि दधिरे पराणि (ṛtasya padaṃ kavayo ni pāṃti guhā nāmāni dadhire parāṇi) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-5-2)

Thus the power of the poets is described: the poets, who see beyond and possess godhood, enter the path of Ṛta and know the most hidden and most exalted secret. (This same matter is explained in detail in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 13, pp. 377-379.) Because this extraordinary power is also revealed in the present mantra, the synonym कवीनां (kavīnāṃ) is used to designate the gods. Such gods pervade the universe; therefore they are त्रिषधस्थ (triṣadhastha).

p. 359

त्रिषधस्था—त्रयो लोकाः देवानां निवासस्थानानि भवंति । (triṣadhasthā—trayo lokāḥ devānāṃ nivāsasthānāni bhavaṃti |) The three worlds are the dwelling places of the gods. Each of these is again of three kinds.

तिस्र एव देवता इति नैरुक्ताः । अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानः । वायुर्वा इंद्रो वा अंतरिक्षस्थानः । सूर्यो द्युस्थानः ॥ तासां महाभाग्यात् एकैकस्या अपि बहूनि नामधेयानि भवंति ॥ (tisra eva devatā iti nairuktāḥ | agniḥ pṛthivīsthānaḥ | vāyurvā iṃdro vā aṃtarikṣasthānaḥ | sūryo dyusthānaḥ ‖ tāsāṃ mahābhāgyāt ekaikasyā api bahūni nāmadheyāni bhavaṃti ‖) (Ni. 7-5)

For the three deities Agni, Vāyu or Indra, and Āditya, the three worlds are the abode: the earth for Agni, the atmosphere for Vāyu or Indra, the heaven-world for Āditya. The Nirukta authors say that because of their greatness they have endless other names too, and thus describe the nature of the gods who occupy these three worlds. The Ṛk Saṃhitā likewise states that the three worlds are the abode of these three deities, who have endless varieties:

सूरो नो दिवस्सातु वातो अंतरिक्षात् । अग्निर्नः पार्थिवेभ्यः (sūro no divassātu vāto aṃtarikṣāt | agnirnaḥ pārthivebhyaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-158-1)

When it is prayed that Sūra of the heaven-world, Vāyu of the atmosphere and Agni of the earth protect us, the three worlds indicated by त्रिषधस्था (triṣadhasthā) are described.

The word सधस्थ (sadhastha) means a common place. In some places this word is also a synonym for the atmosphere. It is also customary to call the altar-place where all the priests sit together and perform the sacrifice सधस्थ (sadhastha). Moreover, as has been said earlier, Sāyaṇa in his commentary on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-1 explains it as सधस्थं सह स्थानं पुण्यकृतां सहनिवासयोग्यं भूरादिलोकसप्तकं । (sadhasthaṃ saha sthānaṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ sahanivāsayogyaṃ bhūrādilokasaptakaṃ |), the seven worlds where the virtuous may dwell, or सहस्थानं सत्यलोकं (sahasthānaṃ satyalokaṃ), the Satya world, which is above all worlds and is the highest of all. Looking at त्रिषधस्था (triṣadhasthā) in the present passage, it is not easy to state the precise meaning. The order earth, atmosphere, heaven-world for the three deities Agni, Vāyu and Sūra is probably stated in many places. But in the Śatapatha and other texts a special feature is shown in this context:

ब्रह्म वा इदमग्र आसीत् । तद्देवानसृजत । तद्देवान्त्सृष्टैषु लोकेषु व्यारोहयदस्मिन्नेव लोकेऽग्निं वायुमंतरिक्षे दिव्येव सूर्यं । अथ येऽत ऊर्ध्वा लोकाः । तद्या आत ऊर्ध्वा देवतास्तेषु ता देवता व्यारोहयत् (brahma vā idamagra āsīt | taddevānasṛjata | taddevāntsṛṣṭaiṣu lokeṣu vyārohayadasminneva loke 'gniṃ vāyumaṃtarikṣe divyeva sūryaṃ | atha ye 'ta ūrdhvā lokāḥ | tadyā āta ūrdhvā devatāsteṣu tā devatā vyārohayat) (Śa. Brā. 11-2-3-1)

p. 360

Brahman, who existed before the creation of the universe, created the three deities beginning with Agni and established them in the three worlds beginning with the earth. But the deities more exalted than these he established in three worlds more exalted than the earth and the rest. This is what is said. Continuing the same matter, there is an explanation that shows the unity of all the worlds. Explaining what is meant by the three worlds being threefold (trivṛt), and what the purport is, Sāyaṇa says that in the Ṛk

न द्याव इंद्रमोजसा नांतरिक्षाणि वज्रिणं । न विव्यचंत भूमयः (na dyāva iṃdramojasā nāṃtarikṣāṇi vajriṇaṃ | na vivyacaṃta bhūmayaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-15)

the plurals "heavens", "atmospheres", "earths" occur, and that it should be understood here in the same way. But how the threefold division is, he has not said. Later, in the commentary on the same Ṛk 8-6-15, he relies on the Āraṇyaka sentence cited, saying that they are threefold as stated in the sentence त्रयो वा इमे त्रिवृतो लोकाः (trayo vā ime trivṛto lokāḥ) (I. Ā. 1-1-2) NOTE. Here too the nature of the three divisions is not stated. Moreover, he says that it should be understood here as in the mantra

तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन् त्रीग्ंरुत द्यून् त्रीणि व्रता विदथे अंतरेषां (tisro bhūmīrdhārayan trīgṃruta dyūn trīṇi vratā vidathe aṃtareṣāṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-8)

But in the cited 2-27-8 it does not mean that the earth itself is threefold. In this very Ṛk Sāyaṇa says आत्र भूमिशब्दः लोकत्रये वर्तते (ātra bhūmiśabdaḥ lokatraye vartate): here the word bhūmi means the three worlds. Hence it is understood that it does not mean the earth is of three kinds. He says it should be understood here as in the sentence "यो द्वितीयस्यां तृतीयस्यां पृथिव्यां (yo dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ)". Whether, therefore, the earth and the rest are each individually of three kinds, or whether naming one is as if naming the other three as well, will be examined later.

त्रिमाता—त्रयाणां अमीषां लोकानां निर्माता संवत्सरः सूरोऽन्या । (trimātā—trayāṇāṃ amīṣāṃ lokānāṃ nirmātā saṃvatsaraḥ sūro 'nyā |) The year, or Sūrya, the maker of these three worlds beginning with the earth. Since the description विदधेषु सम्राट् (vidadheṣu samrāṭ) is present, one must examine whether त्रिमाता (trimātā) means the year alone, or Sūrya alone, or whether being sovereign in the sacrifice (vidatha) is natural to both the year and Sūrya. How

p. 361

Sūrya can be the triple maker and sovereign in the sacrifice, so, only if the year also has both functions, is त्रिमाता (trimātā) here one of the two; that is the purport.

The year too has obtained the quality of triple maker only through Āditya. The relation of Āditya and the year is itself the root of the origin of all gods, men and the rest in the three worlds. Agni, Āditya and the year, these three principles are the lords of the sacrifice. From the union of these three the sacrifice arises; the sacrifice is the root of creation, and the sacrifice is the root of this union. Thus the identity of cause and effect also explains the beginninglessness of creation and the relation of sacrifice to creation.

अप्पु हिमे लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिता आदित्य आसज्जनमादित्ये हीमे लोका दिग्भिरासक्ताः....संवत्सर एषोऽग्निर्यतवः शिक्क्यमृतुभिर्हि संवत्सरः शक्नोति.... (appu hime lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitā āditya āsajjanamāditye hīme lokā digbhirāsaktāḥ....saṃvatsara eṣo 'gniryatavaḥ śikkyamṛtubhirhi saṃvatsaraḥ śaknoti....) (Śa. Brā. 6-7-1-17, 18)

The principle of creation set out in such sentences, and its relation to the principle of sacrifice, will also be explained later in the commentary on the Puruṣa Sūkta.

विधथेषु (vidhatheṣu)—The use of the word vidatha in the senses of knowledge, sacrifice, sacrificial assembly, observance of rule, and the sacrificial power indicated thereby, has been explained earlier.

तिस्रः योषणाः आ पत्यमानाः (tisraḥ yoṣaṇāḥ ā patyamānāḥ) At the time of sacrifice three women descend. The commentator says they are Iḷā, Bhāratī and Sarasvatī. The nature of these three deities has been told earlier, when the Āprī Sūktas were explained (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part 11, pp. 263-266). Even so, in the present passage, where the description is headed by Āditya, one must examine what relation these three deities, who have a sacrificial connection, have with Āditya.

देव्यस्ति स्रः श्रिताश्चैनं त्वष्टा चैवैतदाश्रयः (devyasti sraḥ śritāścainaṃ tvaṣṭā caivaitadāśrayaḥ) (Bṛ. De. 1-108)

A sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā says that the three goddesses have resorted to this Agni and are contained within Agni; and in the sentences that follow it is stated still more clearly:

तिप्रस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्तास्तिस्थानैवेह सा तु वाक् । त्रिविधेनोच्यते नाम्ना ज्योतिषु त्रिषु वर्तिनी ॥ अग्निमेवानुगेळा तु मध्यं प्राप्ता सरस्वती । अमू स्थिताधिलोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ ॥ सैषा तु त्रिविधा वाग्वै दिवि च व्योम्नि चेह च । व्यस्ता चैव समस्ता च भजत्यग्नीनिमानपि ॥ (tiprastu devyo yāḥ proktāstisthānaiveha sā tu vāk | trividhenocyate nāmnā jyotiṣu triṣu vartinī ‖ agnimevānugeḷā tu madhyaṃ prāptā sarasvatī | amū sthitādhilokaṃ tu bhāratī bhavati hyasau ‖ saiṣā tu trividhā vāgvai divi ca vyomni ceha ca | vyastā caiva samastā ca bhajatyagnīnimānapi ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-12 to 14)

p. 362

अयं प्रयोगस्त्वेतेषां ज्योतिषां त्रिषु वर्ततां । (ayaṃ prayogastveteṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ triṣu vartatāṃ |) (Bṛ. De. 1.90)

त्रिसो देव्यति (triso devyati) means the presiding goddesses of speech, who are in the three worlds. Of them Iḷā followed the earthly Agni; Sarasvatī occupied the middle world; Bhāratī became resident in the heaven-world. Yet all three goddesses serve the earthly Agni. In some places the word इळा (iḷā) is explained as food in the form of the oblation. In इळायास्पुत्रो वयुनेऽजनिष्ट (iḷāyāsputro vayune 'janiṣṭa) the relation of Iḷā to Agni is shown. Epithets such as धृतपदी धृतहस्ता (dhṛtapadī dhṛtahastā) are likewise words indicating a connection with Agni.

आ नो यज्ञं भारती ताम्रमेवा मनुष्पदिह चेतॆयंती । तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदंतु ॥ (ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tāmramevā manuṣpadiha cetèyaṃtī | tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadaṃtu ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-8)

Citing this Ṛk, the Nirukta authors have explained the above purport clearly. भरतः आदित्यः तस्य भाः भारती (bharataḥ ādityaḥ tasya bhāḥ bhāratī) (Ni. 8-13): Bharata is Sūrya; his radiance is named Bhāratī. सर इत्युदकनाम । तद्वती स्तनितादिरूपा माध्यमिका च वाक् । (sara ityudakanāma | tadvatī stanitādirūpā mādhyamikā ca vāk |): Sarasvatī is a transformed form of the atmospheric goddess of speech, who has water and the sound of thunder and the like. Thus Bhāratī is the radiance of Āditya of the heaven-world; Sarasvatī is the manifestation of Vāyu of the atmosphere; Iḷā is the radiance of the earthly Agni. In this way these three deities, as representatives of the three worlds, give primacy to the sacrifice and take part in it. Moreover,

तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्योक्षश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरंतं ॥ (tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajyokṣaśyātsūryamuccaraṃtaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-25-4)

Since in this Ṛk the word भारतः (bhārataḥ) is an epithet of Agni, some hold that the radiance connected with him may be named Bhāratī.

होतायक्षत्तिस्रो देवीरपसामपस्तमा अच्छिद्रमद्येदमपस्तन्वतां । देवेभ्यो देवीर्देवमपो वियंत्वाज्यस्य होतरज ॥ (hotāyakṣattisro devīrapasāmapastamā acchidramadyedamapastanvatāṃ | devebhyo devīrdevamapo viyaṃtvājyasya hotaraja ‖) (Śai. Brā. 3-6-2-2) NOTE

In explaining this sentence of the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa it is said: इडा,सरस्वती, भारतीत्येवंरूपास्तिस्रोऽष्टमप्रयाजदेव्यस्तद्रूपमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु । (iḍā,sarasvatī, bhāratītyevaṃrūpāstisro 'ṣṭamaprayājadevyastadrūpamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu |). Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, these three are the deities of the eighth prayāja mantra, goddesses that reflect Agni.

p. 363

This Agni, the lord of the whole sacrifice, who has all three of these forms, is the Āditya described in the present Ṛk.

एतद्भूतेषु लोकेषु अग्निभूतं स्थितं त्रिधा । ऋषयो गीर्भिरर्चंति व्यंजितं नामभिस्त्रिभिः ॥ (etadbhūteṣu lokeṣu agnibhūtaṃ sthitaṃ tridhā | ṛṣayo gīrbhirarcaṃti vyaṃjitaṃ nāmabhistribhiḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 1-64)

This Agni is present in all beings and in all worlds, and he abides in the form of fire. He became manifest in a different form in each of the three worlds, and he is praised under the names Agni, Vāyu and Āditya. The three powers who are special manifestations of such an Agni (Iḍā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī) are asked to come at the three times of pressing (savana) and see that the sacrifice is completed in all its parts.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

त्रिरा दि॒वः स॑वित॒र्वार्या॑णि दि॒वेदि॑व॒ आ सु॑व॒ त्रिर्नो॒ अह्नः॑ ।
त्रि॒धातु॑ रा॒य आ सु॑वा॒ वसू॑नि॒ भग॑ त्रातर्थिषणे सा॒तये॑
धाः ॥ ६ ॥

trirā divaḥ savitarvāryāṇi divediva ā suva trirno ahnaḥ |
tridhātu rāya ā suvā vasūni bhaga trātarthiṣaṇe sātaye
dhāḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

त्रिः । आ । दिवः । सवितः । वार्याणि । दिवेऽदिवे । आ । सुव । त्रिः । नः । अह्नः ।
त्रिधातु । रायः । आ । सुव । वसूनि । भग । त्रातः । धिषणे । सातये । धाः ॥ ६ ॥

triḥ | ā | divaḥ | savitaḥ | vāryāṇi | dive 'dive | ā | suva | triḥ | naḥ | ahnaḥ |
tridhātu | rāyaḥ | ā | suva | vasūni | bhaga | trātaḥ | dhiṣaṇe | sātaye | dhāḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सवितः सर्वस्य प्रेरक हे आदित्य दिवो द्युलोकादागत्य त्वं वार्याणि सर्वैः संभजनीयानि धनानि दिने दिने प्रतिदिनं त्रिरा सुव । त्रिवारमस्मभ्यं प्रेरय । प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः । तदेवोच्यते । भग सर्वैर्भजनीय त्रातरस्माकं रक्षक हे आदित्य त्रिधातु त्रिधातूनि पशुकनकरत्नभेदेन त्रिप्रकाराणि वसूनि धनानि रायः । रांति क्षीरादीनीति रायो गोधनानि । तानि च नोऽस्मभ्यमह्नः संबंधिषु त्रिस्त्रिषु सवनेष्वा सुव । प्रयच्छ । धिषणे माध्यमिके हे वाक् सातये धनलाभाय धाः । आस्मान् कुरु ॥ त्रिः । द्वित्रिचतुर्भ्यः सुच् । पा ५-४-१८ । इति सुच् । चित्स्वरः । सुव । शू प्रेरणे । तुदादिः । लोटि रूपं । त्रिधातु । डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोरित्यस्मात्सितनिगमिमसीत्यादिना तुन्प्रत्ययः । धिषणे । आमंत्रितत्वान्निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Savitṛ" is the impeller of all. Sāyaṇa addresses him as Āditya: "O Āditya, coming from the heavenly world, bestow on us every day, three times, the desirable (vāryāṇi) riches that all may enjoy." Ā suva means "impel, give." He then says what is asked. "Bhaga" is the one whom all revere, and "trātṛ" is our protector, so both address Āditya. "Tridhātu" means riches (vasūni) of three kinds: cattle, gold and jewels. "Rāyaḥ" means cattle-wealth, so called because it gives (rānti) milk and so on. These riches are to be given to us at each of the three pressings belonging to the day. "Dhiṣaṇe" is the middle (mādhyamikā) Vāk; "sātaye" means for the gain of wealth, and "dhāḥ" means "make us (so)."

p. 364

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • सवितः (savitaḥ)—O Āditya, impeller of the world
  • दिवः (divaḥ)—coming from the heavenly world
  • वार्याणि (vāryāṇi)—riches desired by all
  • दिवेदिवे (divedive)—every day
  • त्रिः (triḥ)—at the three times
  • आ सुव (ā suva)—supply
  • भग (bhaga)—O Āditya, in the form of Bhaga, revered by all
  • त्रातः (trātaḥ)—protector
  • त्रिधातु (tridhātu)—in the forms of cattle, gold and jewels
  • वसूनि (vasūni)—riches
  • रायः (rāyaḥ)—wealth in the form of cattle
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • अह्नः (ahnaḥ)—of each day
  • त्रिः (triḥ)—at the time of the three pressings
  • आ सुव (ā suva)—supply
  • धिषणे (dhiṣaṇe)—O middle Vāk
  • सातये (sātaye)—for the gain of our wealth
  • धाः (dhāḥ)—show favour
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Āditya, impeller of the world, come from the heavenly world and supply, every day at the three times, the riches that all desire. O Āditya, in the form of Bhaga, revered and protector of all, supply to us at the three pressings of each day riches in the form of cattle, gold and jewels, and wealth in the form of cattle. O goddess Vāk of the middle region, show favour so that we may gain wealth.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Savitri, desended fron heaven, bestow upon us blessings thrice every day: Bhaga, saviour, grant us thrice a day riches of three elements: Dhishana enable us to acquire (wealth).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this mantra a prayer for the wealth desired is addressed to three deities: Savitṛ, Bhaga and Dhiṣaṇā. The sense is that these three preside over the three kinds of wealth and bestow it. From Āditya the "tridhātu" is asked for.

The word "tridhātu" has been explained as wealth in the form of cattle, gold and jewels. The word is used in many places with different meanings. Where it is used for the principles (tattva) in the form of earth, water and fire, or for the qualities (guṇa) in the form of sattva, rajas and tamas, this has been explained in detail in Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part 11, pp. 583-586.

"Dhiṣaṇe": this word is read among the names of heaven and earth, along with "svadhe" and "purandhī" (Ni. 3-21). धिषणा वाक् धिषेर्दधात्यर्थे धीसादिनीति वा (dhiṣaṇā vāk dhiṣerdadhātyarthe dhīsādinīti vā) (Ni. 8-3). It is said that the word may be derived from the root धिष् (dhiṣ), which gives the sense "holds." Or, "dhīsādinī iti vā": it extends the intellect, that is, it makes the meaning clear. This is

p. 365

the view of the Nirukta authors. In some places Sāyaṇa has explained it as Vāk in the form of mantra, and in others as the middle Vāk. In some places, such as मा च्येद्म रश्मी .... .... धिषणाया उपस्थे (mā cyedma raśmī .... .... dhiṣaṇāyā upasthe) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-109-3), it means the bag that holds the Soma juice, as was explained earlier.

The word is used in all three numbers, and in some contexts its meaning has to be decided from the number and from the context.

When it is in the singular, it means Vāk, praise in the form of speech, or the bag that holds Soma juice. In places such as वैश्वानराय धिषणां (vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇāṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-1) it can easily be said to mean praise.

When the dual "dhiṣaṇe" is used, it generally means heaven and earth. It is formed from the root धिष् (dhiṣ), meaning "hold firmly," and it is a synonym for heaven and earth, which hold all the worlds. प्रजापतिर्वै प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा ता द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां पर्यागृह्णात् (prajāpatirvai prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā tā dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ paryāgṛhṇāt) (Śa. Brā. 3-8-4-17). It may be said that heaven and earth keep under their control and bear all the worlds created by Prajāpati, and are therefore known as "dhiṣaṇe."

But where the plural is used in some places, it is not easy to state the meaning of the word.

इरावतीर्वरुण धेनवो वां मधुमद्वां सिंधवो मित्र दुह्रे । त्रयस्तस्फुर्वृषभासस्ति सृणाः धिषणानां रेतोधा वि द्युमंतः ॥ (irāvatīrvaruṇa dhenavo vāṃ madhumadvāṃ siṃdhavo mitra duhre | trayastasphurvṛṣabhāsasti sṛṇāḥ dhiṣaṇānāṃ retodhā vi dyumaṃtaḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-2)

Here heaven and earth, together with the atmosphere within them, are included, so Sāyaṇa has explained "dhiṣaṇānām" as "of earth, atmosphere and heaven." But in this place that meaning is not directly indicated by the word. He first explains "dhiṣaṇānām" as "sthānānām" (of the places), and then, asked what the places are, explains them as the three worlds. This meaning was given earlier in the explanation of the word "dhiṣṇya." Besides this, in some other places where the plural is used, even Sāyaṇa shows a little difficulty. For example:

The passage beginning धिषणास्ता देवीः (dhiṣaṇāstā devīḥ) (Śa. Brā. 6-5-4-5) NOTE

p. 366

These Dhiṣaṇās are dear to all the gods. They are made to blaze at the seat (sadhastha) of the earth. These Dhiṣaṇās, ancient, of divine form and dear to all the gods, are manifestations of the goddess Vāk. It is with the help of speech that everything is kindled and illumined. Where such a description is given, a hidden, essential meaning is present.

The word "dhiṣaṇe" is in the dual, and it can also be a vocative. In the present mantra, "he mādhyamike vāk" (O middle Vāk) addresses the goddess Vāk.

"Sātaye": it is formed from the root सन् (san), which gives the sense "obtain." Words such as वाजसातिः (vājasātiḥ) and वाजसातये (vājasātaye) are well known. Here the prayer is to show favour so that wealth may be obtained.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

त्रिरा दि॒वः स॑वि॒ता सो॑षवीति॒ राजा॑ना मि॒त्रावरु॑णा सुपा॒णी ।
आप॑श्चि दस्य॒ रोद॑सी चिदु॒र्वी रत्नं॑ भिक्षंत सवि॒तुः स॒वाय॑॥ ७ ॥

trirā divaḥ savitā soṣavīti rājānā mitrāvaruṇā supāṇī |
āpaści dasya rodasī cidurvī ratnaṃ bhikṣaṃta savituḥ savāya‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

त्रिः। आ। दिवः । सविता । सोषवीति । राजाना । मित्रावरुणा । सुपाणी इति सुपाणी ।
आपः । चित् । अस्य । रोदसी इति । चित् । उर्वी इति । रत्नं । भिक्षंत । सवितुः। सवाय॥

triḥ| ā| divaḥ | savitā | soṣavīti | rājānā | mitrāvaruṇā | supāṇī iti supāṇī |
āpaḥ | cit | asya | rodasī iti | cit | urvī iti | ratnaṃ | bhikṣaṃta | savituḥ| savāya‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सविता देवो दिवो दिवसस्य त्रिस्त्रिषु कालेष्टा सोषवीति । अस्मभ्यं धनान्यासुवतु । प्रेरयतु । किंच राजाना राजानौ सुपाणी कल्याणपाणी मित्रावरुणावापः। आप्पोति सर्वं जगदित्याप अंतरिक्षं । नित्यबहुवचनांतत्वादृहुवचनं । चिदपि च उर्वि विस्तीर्णे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावेता देवताः सवितुः प्रेरकस्यास्य देवस्य सवाय सवेन प्रेरणेन रत्नमपेक्षितमर्थं भिक्षंत । याचंते ॥ सोसवीति । पू प्रेरण इत्यस्य यज्लुकि लटि रूपं । मित्रावरुणा । देवताद्वंद्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । भिक्षंत । भिक्ष याज्ञायामित्यस्य लजि रूपं । सवाय । जवसव् च । पा. ३-३-५६-४ । इत्यजंतत्वेन निपातनादंतोदात्तत्वं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The god Savitṛ, three times (triḥ) each day (divaḥ), "soṣavīti": let him impel wealth to us. Further, the two kings, Mitra and Varuṇa, with fair hands (सुपाणी (supāṇī), "of auspicious hands"), the "āpaḥ," and the two broad ones, heaven and earth (रोदसी (rodasī)), these deities ask for what they want, "ratna," through the impelling (सवाय (savāya)) of this impelling god Savitṛ. "Āpaḥ" is the atmosphere, because it pervades (āpnoti) the whole world. It is a word that is always plural, hence the plural. "Cit" means "also." "Bhikṣanta" means "they ask."

p. 367

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • सविता (savitā)—the god Savitṛ
  • दिवः (divaḥ)—of the day
  • त्रिः (triḥ)—at the three times
  • आ सोषवीति (ā soṣavīti)—may he supply wealth to us
  • राजाना (rājānā)—the two lords of the world
  • सुपाणी (supāṇī)—possessing excellent hands
  • मित्रावरुणा (mitrāvaruṇā)—Mitra and Varuṇa
  • आपः चित् (āpaḥ cit)—the atmosphere too
  • उर्वि (urvi)—broad
  • रोदसी (rodasī)—heaven and earth
  • सवितुः (savituḥ)—of the impeller
  • अस्य (asya)—of this god
  • सवाय (savāya)—by the impelling
  • रत्नं (ratnaṃ)—wealth
  • भिक्षंत (bhikṣaṃta)—they ask
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Savitṛ supply us with wealth at the three times of the day. Mitra and Varuṇa, lords of the world and possessing excellent hands, the atmosphere, and the broad heaven and earth also ask for the wealth they desire from this impeller, Āditya.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May Savitri bestow upon us wealth at the (three periods) of the day, for the well-handed Mitra and Varuna, the waters, the vast heaven and earth, solicit precious things from the liberality of Savitri.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The present mantra praises Savitṛ: heaven and earth, Mitra and Varuṇa, and the other deities, known by epithets such as ऋतवाना (ṛtavānā), ऋतावृधः (ṛtāvṛdhaḥ) and राजाना (rājānā), look for Savitṛ's favour and perform their duties only by his impulsion. "उतेशिषे प्रसवस्य त्वमेक इत् (uteśiṣe prasavasya tvameka it)": you alone are the source and lord of the whole universe. Describing his position in this way, the mantra shows Savitṛ's greatness. What Savitṛ's place is in the sovereignty of the gods will be explained in the introduction to Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 3-62.

Mitra and Varuṇa have two epithets, राजाना (rājānā) and सुपाणी (supāṇī). These epithets show the nature of Mitra and Varuṇa. The nature of Mitra and Varuṇa is described in mantras such as ययोर्धाम धर्मणा रोचते बृहद्ययो रुभे रोदसी नाधसी वृत् (yayordhāma dharmaṇā rocate bṛhadyayo rubhe rodasī nādhasī vṛt) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-5). They pervade the universe and shine of themselves, and they make the whole universe shine by their own light.

आपः (āpaḥ): आप्रोति सर्वं जगत् इत्यापः अंतरिक्षं (āproti sarvaṃ jagat ityāpaḥ aṃtarikṣaṃ). Because it pervades the whole world, the atmosphere has the name "āpaḥ." The Nirukta authors also include this word among the names of the atmosphere.

p. 368

In some places "āpaḥ" means the water in the atmosphere, but the intended sense is understood to be the atmosphere that is its support. In some places the question "what is āpaḥ?" appears in the Śruti text itself.

प्रजां धर्मेण दाधारैवमेते मनः पितरं परिचरंत्यापश्च वरुणश्च ० यावदन्वापो यावदनु वरुणस्तावानस्यलोको भवति नास्य तावल्लोको जीर्यते यावदेतेषां न जीर्यतेऽपां च वरुणस्य च य एवमेताः मनसो विभूतिं वेद । (prajāṃ dharmeṇa dādhāraivamete manaḥ pitaraṃ paricaraṃtyāpaśca varuṇaśca 0 yāvadanvāpo yāvadanu varuṇastāvānasyaloko bhavati nāsya tāvalloko jīryate yāvadeteṣāṃ na jīryate 'pāṃ ca varuṇasya ca ya evametāḥ manaso vibhūtiṃ veda |) (I. Ā. 2-1-7) NOTE

Prajāpati, described as the Supreme Person, created Varuṇa and Apaḥ (water) by his mental resolve alone. Water serves as a help to good works, Varuṇa watches over the order of creatures, and Prajāpati makes this resolve fruitful; so they attend on him. Since this is the description, there is room for the doubt as to what the principle "āpaḥ" is. Therefore:

आसा ३ इत्याप इति तदिदमाप एवेदं वै मूलमदस्तूलमयं पितैते पुत्रा यत्र ह क्व च पुत्रस्य तत्पितुः । (āsā 3 ityāpa iti tadidamāpa evedaṃ vai mūlamadastūlamayaṃ pitaite putrā yatra ha kva ca putrasya tatpituḥ |) (I. Ā. 2-1-8) NOTE

What is āpaḥ? What, in truth, is the nature of this principle? Its greatness is as follows: everything in the universe is pervaded by this water; it is the root cause of the creation of the universe, and the rest is its effect. The Person who is the support of this water-principle is the father. Since this is the description, it is understood that "āpaḥ" is not merely the atmosphere, but has a wider extent than the atmosphere. The etymology given in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also supports this view.

सेदग्ं सर्वमाप्नोत्यदिदं किं च यदाप्नोत्तस्मादापः ॥ (sedagṃ sarvamāpnotyadidaṃ kiṃ ca yadāpnottasmādāpaḥ ‖) (Śa. Patra 6-1-19) NOTE

The etymology is that what has the power to pervade everything is known by the name "āpaḥ." But what does it pervade? In some places it is said to pervade the whole universe, moving and unmoving, and not merely one fixed world such as the atmosphere. It is also taught that it is the Supreme Brahman principle.

स योऽपो ब्रह्मेत्युपास्त आप्नोति सर्वान्यामान् ॥ (sa yo 'po brahmetyupāsta āpnoti sarvānyāmān ‖) (Chā. U. 7-10-2)

It says that one who worships water as Brahman obtains all the aims of human life. But here it does not mean water as the complete Brahman. Water and fire are all parts of Brahman. Even so,

p. 369

Identity is stated; and it is also made known that the world of waters is a created world and not something existing before the creation of the universe:

आत्मा वा इदमेक एवाग्र आसीन्नान्यत्किंचन मिषत् । स ई क्षत । लोकान्नु सृजा इति । इमांल्लोकानसृजत । अंभोमरीचीर्मरमापः । (ātmā vā idameka evāgra āsīnnānyatkiṃcana miṣat | sa ī kṣata | lokānnu sṛjā iti | imāṃllokānasṛjata | aṃbhomarīcīrmaramāpaḥ |) (Ai. Ā. 9-4-1) NOTE

It says: before the creation of the universe only this principle of the Self existed; nothing else existed. Then, desiring the work of creation, it created these four worlds: Ambhaḥ, Marīci, Mara and Āpaḥ. Of these, Ambhaḥ is the heavenly world. [Ambhaḥ commonly means water, but in this quoted sentence it means the heavenly world, which lies above the atmosphere.] Marīci is the atmosphere pervaded by radiance. Mara, subject to death, is this earth. What lies below this is the world of waters (Āpaḥ). Ordinarily only the three divisions heaven, earth and atmosphere are well known, but here a fourth is added.

If such contexts are examined, a difference appears between the atmosphere as explained in the bhāṣya on the present Ṛk and the world called Āpaḥ explained in the quoted sentence. Even so, because of its pervasiveness the derivation of the word Āpaḥ fits both places. Whether it be the atmosphere or the world below the earth, the purport is that everything is nourished by the grace of Savitṛ.

उर्वी रोदसी (urvī rodasī)—the very extensive heaven and earth. From a gross point of view the epithet उर्वी (urvī) for the word रोदसी (rodasī) seems slightly unsuitable. The word उर्वी (urvī) means "very extended". रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य विरोधनात् (rodasī dyāvāpṛthivya virodhanāt): because heaven and earth are bound and limited by a bounded limit (sīmā), they have the synonym रोदसी (rodasī). So the doubt arises naturally that the epithet उर्वी (urvī), which shows wide extent, cannot suit a world that is limited and bound. The Nirukta-author has read the word उर्वी (urvī) among the names of the earth and again among the names of "heaven and earth" (Ni. 1-1; 1-30). So it cannot be said that there is any incongruity here. Since the word रोदसी (rodasī) is here a synonym of heaven and earth, उर्वी (urvī) must be taken to mean "extended". It is a very meaningful word for indicating greatness and extent.

अयं मे पीत उदियर्ति वाचमयं मनीषामुशतीमजीगः । अयं षळुर्वीरमिमीत धीरो न याभ्यो भुवनं कच्चनारे ॥ (ayaṃ me pīta udiyarti vācamayaṃ manīṣāmuśatīmajīgaḥ | ayaṃ ṣaḷurvīramimīta dhīro na yābhyo bhuvanaṃ kaccanāre ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-3)

p. 370

This King Soma has created the six Urvīs; no region in the world lies beyond these Urvīs. These six are all-pervading. When this is said, which are these six Urvīs? They are the earth, the heavenly world, day, night, the waters and the plants. How? In the Śatapatha mantra

षण्मोर्वीर्गंहसस्पांत्वग्निश्च पृथिवी चापश्च वाजश्च रात्रिश्चेता मा देवताः (ṣaṇmorvīrgaṃhasaspāṃtvagniśca pṛthivī cāpaśca vājaśca rātriścetā mā devatāḥ) (Śa. Brā. 1-5-1-22)

there is an enumeration of which these Urvīs are. On this basis Sāyaṇa quoted this Brāhmaṇa sentence and explained as stated above. The same is continued and explained in the Ṛk-saṃhitā too; each Urvī is described with an epithet.

अयं स यो वरिमाणं पृथिव्या वर्षाणं दिवो अकृणोदयं सः । अयं पीयूषं त्रिसृषु प्रवत्सु सोमो दाधारोर्वं १ तरिक्षं ॥ अयं विदच्चित्रदृशीकमर्णः शुक्रसद्मनामुषसामनीके । अयं महान्महता स्यंभनेनोद्द्यामस्तभ्नाद्वषभो मरुत्वान् ॥ (ayaṃ sa yo varimāṇaṃ pṛthivyā varṣāṇaṃ divo akṛṇodayaṃ saḥ | ayaṃ pīyūṣaṃ trisṛṣu pravatsu somo dādhārorvaṃ 1 tarikṣaṃ ‖ ayaṃ vidaccitradṛśīkamarṇaḥ śukrasadmanāmuṣasāmanīke | ayaṃ mahānmahatā syaṃbhanenoddyāmastabhnādvaṣabho marutvān ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-4, 5)

This Soma made the extent of the earth still greater; he increased the height of the heavenly world; he caused the three kinds of plants to spread throughout the universe; he increased the very extended atmosphere; he lit the world-attracting light of the sun endlessly; likewise he caused the middle world to become extended; and so on: the extension of all the worlds indicated by the word उर्वी (urvī) is described. Besides:

आ यः पप्र जायमान उर्वी दूरेदृशा भासा कृष्णाध्वा । (ā yaḥ papra jāyamāna urvī dūredṛśā bhāsā kṛṣṇādhvā |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-10-4)

Agni, whose path is black, as soon as he was born pervaded the very extended Urvīs, that is, all of heaven and earth. Here the word Urvī is a synonym for heaven and earth only; or it may be a synonym for the earth alone. For example:

उर्वाः पदो नि दधाति सानौ रिंहत्योधो अरुषासो अस्य ॥ (urvāḥ pado ni dadhāti sānau riṃhatyodho aruṣāso asya ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-146-2)

Agni sets his foot on the altar of the earth, very extended and high like a peak; so here the word Urvī indicates the earth alone.

Thus, when the word Urvī indicates endless extension, is this epithet fitting for Rodasī, which has a fixed limit? Here it may be said that the epithet is entirely proper.

p. 371

How? The etymology विरोधनाद्रोदसी (virodhanādrodasī) can be given only in one context; the pervasiveness to be indicated by the word रोदसी (rodasī) is itself well known. With this purport, when describing the nature of the Aśvin deities too (?), because this pervasiveness exists, identity of the Aśvin deities with heaven and earth is stated. NOTE

अथ यदश्विनावितीमे ह वै द्यावापृथिवी प्रत्यक्षमश्विनाविमे हीदग्ंसर्वमाश्नुनातां पुष्करस्रजावित्यग्निरेवास्यै पुष्करमादित्योऽमुष्यै (atha yadaśvināvitīme ha vai dyāvāpṛthivī pratyakṣamaśvināvime hīdagṃsarvamāśnunātāṃ puṣkarasrajāvityagnirevāsyai puṣkaramādityo 'muṣyai) (Śa. Brā. 4-1-5-16)

The Aśvin deities are directly manifest in this very form of heaven and earth. Because they have a nature that pervades every region, they have this name. They are called Puṣkara-srajas. Agni and Āditya are these Puṣkaras: Agni is the lotus (puṣkara) of the earth, Āditya that of the heavenly world.

शौर्णवाभोः दृच्छेत्वस्मिन् अश्विनौ मन्यते स्तुता । अहोरात्रौ च तावेव स्यातां तावेन रोदसी ॥ (śaurṇavābhoḥ dṛcchetvasmin aśvinau manyate stutā | ahorātrau ca tāveva syātāṃ tāvena rodasī ‖) (Bṛ. De. 7-126)

An opinion that this very heaven and earth, well known as Rodasī, are also well known as the Aśvin deities has been cited in the Bṛhaddevatā and other works. It is because of this attribute of pervasiveness that the name arises; therefore the epithet उर्वी (urvī) is proper.

The word रोदसी (rodasī) is used in the dual, but in some places it is also used in the singular. In those contexts it is not easy to say definitely what it means. In some cases the word occurs in one and the same mantra in both the first half and the second half; then a different meaning has to be given for each occurrence. For example:

इदुग्राः शवसा धृष्णुषेणा उभे युजंत रोदसी सुमेके ! अध स्मैषु रोदसी स्वशोचिरामवत्सु तस्थौ न रोकः ॥ (idugrāḥ śavasā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇā ubhe yujaṃta rodasī sumeke ! adha smaiṣu rodasī svaśocirāmavatsu tasthau na rokaḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-66-6)

This mantra praises the Maruts. The meaning of the first sentence is that these Maruts yoke both heaven and earth; and the meaning of the second sentence is that Rodasī unites her radiance in these Maruts. But who is this Rodasī? Sāyaṇa has explained it as the middle speech (mādhyamikā vāk). One view is that this Rodasī is the wife of Rudra.

p. 372

Another view is that she is the wife of the Maruts. "Wife of Rudra" means the mother of the Maruts. Rudra is Vāyu. This wife of Vāyu is the middle speech. The radiance in the form of lightning in that speech, joined with thunder, is called Rodasī. Supporting this very view:

रोदसी देवपत्नीनां अथर्वांगिरसे यथा (rodasī devapatnīnāṃ atharvāṃgirase yathā) (Bṛ. De. 2-143)

According to the Atharvāṅgirasa view, Rodasī is one of the wives of the gods: here is an example with the singular used. Even in such places, since the attribute of pervasiveness is present, the epithet उर्वी (urvī) is natural. In the present mantra the meaning is: heaven and earth, very extended and all-pervading.

सवितुः (savituḥ)—सवाय (savāya)—these two words also describe the nature of Savitṛ. Because he is the impeller of the world, the impelling function of the deity known by the word Savitṛ is described by these words. This attribute of Savitṛ will be explained further on. Mitra and Varuṇa, and heaven and earth, though they are purifiers of the world, maintainers of the world's order, givers of wealth and possessed of the highest greatness, all have their activity accomplished only by the impulsion of this Savitṛ: this is the purport of the description.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

त्रिरु॑त्त॒मा दू॒णशा॑ रोच॒नानि॒ त्रयो॑ राजं॒त्यसु॑रस्य वी॒राः ।
ऋ॒तवा॑न इषि॒रा दू॒ळभा॑स॒स्त्रिरा दि॒वो वि॒दथे॑ संतु दे॒वाः ॥८॥

triruttamā dūṇaśā rocanāni trayo rājaṃtyasurasya vīrāḥ |
ṛtavāna iṣirā dūḷabhāsastrirā divo vidathe saṃtu devāḥ ‖8‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

त्रिः । उत्तमा । दुःनशा । रोचनानि । त्रयः । राजंति । असुरस्य । वीराः ।
ऋतवानः । इषिराः । दुःदभासः । त्रिः । आ । दिवः । विदथे । संतु । देवाः ॥ ८ ॥

triḥ | uttamā | duḥnaśā | rocanāni | trayaḥ | rājaṃti | asurasya | vīrāḥ |
ṛtavānaḥ | iṣirāḥ | duḥdabhāsaḥ | triḥ | ā | divaḥ | vidathe | saṃtu | devāḥ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

दूणशा दुर्नशा केनापि विनाशयितुमशक्यानि रोचनानि दीप्यमानानि त्रिस्त्रिण्यंतमानि स्थानानि संति । एतेषु त्रिषु स्थानेष्टसुरस्य । अस्यति क्षिपति सर्वमित्यसुरः कालात्मा संवत्सरः । तस्य वीराः पुत्रास्त्रयोऽग्नि वायुसूर्यरूपा राजंति शोभंते । तानेव विशिनष्टि । ऋतावानः । ऋतं सत्यभूतमग्निहोत्रादिकं कर्म

Gist of the bhāṣya

दूणशा (dūṇaśā) is दुर्नशा (durnaśā): the bright (रोचनानि (rocanāni), shining) places, that cannot be destroyed by anyone, are three in number, the highest. In these three places there are the sons (वीराः (vīrāḥ)) of the Asura. Asura is he who throws out (अस्यति (asyati)) everything: the year, whose nature is Time. His three sons, in the forms of Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, shine. He now qualifies them: ऋतावानः (ṛtāvānaḥ); ऋतं (ṛtaṃ) is the rite such as the Agnihotra, which is true (the text breaks off here and continues on the next page).

p. 373

तद्वंतः । इषिरा यज्ञार्थं शीघ्रगतिमंतो दूळभासो दुर्दभासः केनापि स्वतेजसा तिरस्कर्तुमशक्या एते सर्वे देवा विदथेऽस्मदीये यज्ञे दिवोऽह्नः संबंधिषु त्रिस्त्रिषु सवनेष्वा संतु । समंताद्यजनीयतया भवंतु ॥ उत्तमा । उत्तमशश्वत्तमौ सर्वत्रेत्युंभादिषु पाठादंतोदात्तत्वं । दूणशा । नशेः कृच्छार्थे खल् । दुरो दाशनाशदभेषूत्वं वक्तव्यमिति रेफस्योत्वं । उत्तरपदादेः ष्टुत्वं । लित्स्वरः । दूळभासः । पूर्ववदुत्वष्टुत्वे ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya
