॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्रावरुणावस्मे आस्मासु तदभिलषितं तादृशं वसु धनं स्यात् । भवतु । हे मरुतः सर्ववीरः सर्वॆषु कर्मसु वीरः समर्थो रयिः पुत्रपौत्रयुक्तः पशुसंघः । पशवो वै रयिरिति तैत्तिरीयकं । सोऽस्मे अस्माकं भवतु । वरूत्रिः सर्वैः संभजनीया देवपल्यः शरणैः । शृणंति शीतादिक्षेशमिति शरणानि गृहाः । तैरस्मानवंतु । होत्रा । हूयंतेऽस्यां हवींशीति । यद्वा । हूयते तत्र प्राण इति होत्रा वाक् । तथा च श्रुतिः । वाचि हि प्राणं जुहुमः प्राणे वा वाचं । कौ. उ. २-५ । इति । यद्वा । होत्रेति यज्ञनाम । हूयते तत्र हविरिति । यज्ञश्च वागुच्यते। वाचं यच्छंति वाग्वै यज्ञः । ऐ- ब्रा. ५-२४ । इति ब्राह्मणं । तादृशी भारती सरस्वती दक्षिणाभिगॊरूपाभिर्दक्षिणाभिः । यद्वा । उदाराभिर्वाग्निरस्मान् पालयतु ॥ वसु ष्यादित्यत्र संहितायां पूर्वपदादिति षत्वं । वरूत्रिः । ग्रसितस्कभितेत्यादिना जीबंतत्वेन निपातनादिष्टसिद्धिः । होत्रा । हु दानादनयोः । हुयामाश्रुभसिभ्यस्त्रन्नित्यधिकरणे त्रन्प्रत्ययः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, let that desired wealth be ours. O Maruts, let the wealth called सर्ववीरः (sarvavīraḥ) be ours: सर्ववीरः (sarvavīraḥ) means capable (वीरः (vīraḥ)) in all rites. This रयिः (rayiḥ) is a herd of cattle together with sons and grandsons; "cattle indeed are wealth" says the Taittirīya text. Let the वरूत्रीः (varūtrīḥ), the wives of the gods who are to be resorted to by all, protect us with शरणैः (śaraṇaiḥ), that is, with houses; houses are शरणानि (śaraṇāni) because they break (शृणंति (śṛṇaṃti)) cold and similar afflictions. As to होत्रा (hotrā): it is that in which oblations are offered; or else speech is होत्रा (hotrā) because the vital breath (प्राण (prāṇa)) is offered in it. Accordingly the śruti: वाचि हि प्राणं जुहुमः प्राणे वा वाचं (vāci hi prāṇaṃ juhumaḥ prāṇe vā vācaṃ) (Kau. U. 2-5NOTE). Or else होत्रा (hotrā) is a name of the sacrifice, because the oblation is offered in it; and the sacrifice is also called speech, as the Brāhmaṇa says: वाचं यच्छंति वाग्वै यज्ञः (vācaṃ yacchaṃti vāgvai yajñaḥ) (Ai. Brā. 5-24). Such a Bhāratī, Sarasvatī, is to protect us with दक्षिणाभिः (dakṣiṇābhiḥ), that is, with gifts in the form of cows; or else, with generous speeches.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्रावरुणा (iṃdrāvaruṇā)—O Indra and Varuṇa
  • अस्मे (asme)—to us
  • तत् (tat)—that which we desired
  • वसु (vasu)—wealth
  • स्यात् (syāt)—may it come
  • मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts
  • सर्ववीरः (sarvavīraḥ)—all-capable
  • रयिः (rayiḥ)—wealth accompanied by sons and grandsons
  • अस्मे (asme)—may it come to us
  • वरूत्रिः (varūtriḥ)—the venerable wives of the gods
  • शरणैः (śaraṇaiḥ)—with houses fit for dwelling
  • अस्मान् (asmān)—us
  • अवंतु (avaṃtu)—let them protect
  • होत्रा (hotrā)—the goddess of speech
  • भारती (bhāratī)—Sarasvatī (or Sarasvatī in the form of speech)
  • दक्षिणाभिः (dakṣiṇābhiḥ)—with wealth of cattle or wealth of speech
  • अस्मान् (asmān)—us (let them protect)

p. 532

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, may the wealth we desired come to us. O Maruts, may all-capable wealth, accompanied by sons and grandsons, come to us. May the venerable wives of the gods protect us with houses fit for dwelling; may the goddess of speech and Sarasvatī protect us with wealth of cattle or wealth of speech.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May there be to us, Indra and Varuna, such wealth (as we covet): may there be, Maruts, to us wealth (of cattle) and numerous descendants: may the delightful (wives of the gods) shelter us with dwellings : may Hotra, and Bharati (enrich) us with gifts.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वरूत्रीः (varūtrīḥ)—सर्वैः संभजनीया देवपत्न्यः (sarvaiḥ saṃbhajanīyā devapatnyaḥ): the wives of the gods, such as Bhāratī, venerable to all; thus their venerability is also stated. The word is used more often simply in the sense "protectors". In places such as वरूत्रीभिः सुशरणो नो अस्तु त्वष्टा सुदत्रो वि दधातु रायः (varūtrībhiḥ suśaraṇo no astu tvaṣṭā sudatro vi dadhātu rāyaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-22), वरूत्रीभिः (varūtrībhiḥ) is explained as उपद्रवाणां वारयित्रीभिः देवपत्नीभिः (upadravāṇāṃ vārayitrībhiḥ devapatnībhiḥ), that is, by the wives of the gods who ward off troubles. But in अहिर्बुध्न्य उत नः शृणोतु वरूत्र्येकधेनुभिर्नि पातु (ahirbudhnya uta naḥ śṛṇotu varūtryekadhenubhirni pātu) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6 38-5) it is stated that the word वरुत्री (varutrī) is a synonym of the goddess of speech; one may also say "the protecting goddess of speech". In the present verse the plural वरूत्रीः (varūtrīḥ) is used, so one may say in general "the wives of the gods".

Whether these words होत्रा भारती (hotrā bhāratī) denote separate special deities, or whether they should be understood as "Bhāratī, qualified by the epithet Hotrā", is itself doubtful to the commentator.

होत्रा (hotrā)—Three kinds of meaning can be given to this word. First, हूयंते अस्यां हवींषि इति (hūyaṃte asyāṃ havīṃṣi iti): because oblations are offered in her, she may be a special deity called Hotrā

p. 533

(or a Bhāratī of such a nature). In places such as होत्राः संयाजयंति (hotrāḥ saṃyājayaṃti) (Śa. Brā. 4-2-1-32) the word होत्राः (hotrāḥ) is explained as "wives of the gods"; and in contexts such as दिशः सप्त होत्राः (diśaḥ sapta hotrāḥ) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1 20) it is stated to mean the deities of the directions. This will be explained further on. In the present verse the meaning as a deity is given first, and then, secondly, हूयते तत्र प्राण इति होत्रा वाक् (hūyate tatra prāṇa iti hotrā vāk): because the oblation is offered in speech, speech itself is what the word होत्रा (hotrā) denotes. He says that this meaning is stated on the authority of the śruti sentence वाचि हि प्राणं जुहुमः प्राणे वा वाचं (vāci hi prāṇaṃ juhumaḥ prāṇe vā vācaṃ); but he does not say which source this is. Thirdly, होत्रॆति यज्ञनाम हूयते अत्र हविरिति (hotrèti yajñanāma hūyate atra haviriti): because the oblation is offered in the sacrifice, the sacrifice too is denoted by the word होत्रा (hotrā). Or else the sacrifice is itself well known as speech. Thus: वाचं यच्छंति । वाग्वै यज्ञः । (vācaṃ yacchaṃti | vāgvai yajñaḥ |) (I. Ā. 5-24NOTE). To restrain speech is to restrain the sacrifice itself; for speech and sacrifice are identical, both are of undivided nature: thus the non-difference of speech and sacrifice is stated. Besides this, in several other places a conjugal relation between speech and sacrifice is shown, and the unity of the two is indicated. The relation that exists between mind and speech exists also between sacrifice and speech. Indicating this same relation, how होत्रा (hotrā) in the present verse may be explained as the sacrifice whose nature is speech: first one must know how this unity came about. This relation is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. The story tells first of the difference between sacrifice and speech and afterwards of the unity of the two, in this way.

ते देवा यज्ञमब्रुवन् । योषा ना इयं वागुपमंत्रयस्व ह्वयिष्यते वै त्वेति स्वयं ना हैवैक्षत योषा ना इयं वागुपमंत्रय्यै ह्वयिष्यते वै मेति तामुपामंत्रयत .... .... ॥ (te devā yajñamabruvan | yoṣā nā iyaṃ vāgupamaṃtrayasva hvayiṣyate vai tveti svayaṃ nā haivaikṣata yoṣā nā iyaṃ vāgupamaṃtrayyai hvayiṣyate vai meti tāmupāmaṃtrayata .... .... ‖) (Tai. Brā. 3-2-1-9NOTE). The gods said to the sacrifice: "Speech is a woman; make a sign to her to come near you." Or else the sacrifice thought in its own mind: "Speech is a woman. If I make a sign to that speech to come near me, then that woman too will make the same sign to me." But at the very first, speech refused the sacrifice's sign. That is characteristic of a woman.

p. 534

ते होचुः । उपैव भगवो मंत्रयस्व ह्वयिष्यते वै त्वेति तामुपामंत्रयत सा हैनं जुहुवे तस्मादु स्त्री पुमांसग् ह्वयत एवोत्तमग्ं स होवाचाह्वत नै मेति ॥ (te hocuḥ | upaiva bhagavo maṃtrayasva hvayiṣyate vai tveti tāmupāmaṃtrayata sā hainaṃ juhuve tasmādu strī pumāṃsag hvayata evottamagṃ sa hovācāhvata nai meti ‖) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-1-21). Then the gods said: "Make a sign to her again in the form of an invitation. She will certainly not reject it but will give a reply." Then in the same way the sacrifice-person made a sign in the form of an invitation. She too made the same sign and called him. Then he thought: "She too has called me."

ते देवा ईक्षांचक्रिरे । योषा ना इयं वाग्यदेनं न युवितेहैव मा तिष्ठंतमभ्येहीति ब्रूहि तां तु न आगतां प्रतिप्रब्रूतादिति सा हैनं तदेव तिष्ठंतमभ्येयाय तस्मादु स्त्री पुमांसग्ं संस्कृते तिष्ठंतमभ्यैति ताग्ंहैभ्य आगतां प्रतिप्रोवाचेयं वागादिति ॥ (te devā īkṣāṃcakrire | yoṣā nā iyaṃ vāgyadenaṃ na yuvitehaiva mā tiṣṭhaṃtamabhyehīti brūhi tāṃ tu na āgatāṃ pratiprabrūtāditi sā hainaṃ tadeva tiṣṭhaṃtamabhyeyāya tasmādu strī pumāṃsagṃ saṃskṛte tiṣṭhaṃtamabhyaiti tāgṃhaibhya āgatāṃ pratiprovāceyaṃ vāgāditi ‖) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-1-22). "This speech is a woman. This woman, belonging to the company of the Asuras, might draw the sacrifice-person to herself and win him over; then the sacrifice-person might join the Asuras." So thinking, they said to the sacrifice-person: "Do not go to her; make her come to you." In that way he made her come, and afterwards told the gods of her arrival.

तान् देवाः । असुरेभ्योंतरायंस्ताग् स्वीकृत्याग्नावेव परिगृह्य सर्वहुतमजुहवुराहुतिर्हि देवानाग्ं स यामेवामूमनुष्टुभाजुहवुस्तदेवैनां तद्देवाः स्वकुर्वत तेऽसुरा आत्तवचसो हेलवो हेलव इति वदंतः पराबभूवुः ॥ (tān devāḥ | asurebhyoṃtarāyaṃstāg svīkṛtyāgnāveva parigṛhya sarvahutamajuhavurāhutirhi devānāgṃ sa yāmevāmūmanuṣṭubhājuhavustadevaināṃ taddevāḥ svakurvata te 'surā āttavacaso helavo helava iti vadaṃtaḥ parābabhūvuḥ ‖) (Tā. Prā. 3-2-1-23NOTE). As soon as the woman in the form of speech, having left the Asuras, approached the sacrifice-person, the gods separated her completely from them and cut the relation she had with them. They made her wholly enveloped by fire and offered her to the gods as a full oblation. And because she was offered preceded by the anuṣṭubh metre, speech too, having become of the nature of the sacrifice, joined their side. The Asuras fled crying out.

सोऽयं यज्ञो वाचमभिदधौ । मिथुन्येनया स्यामिति ताग्ं संबभूव । (so 'yaṃ yajño vācamabhidadhau | mithunyenayā syāmiti tāgṃ saṃbabhūva |) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-1-25)

p. 535

In this way the sacrifice-person, enamoured of the woman in the form of speech and wishing to be united with her, took her wholly into himself.

इंद्रो ह वा ईक्षांचक्रे । महद्वा इतोऽभ्वं जनिष्यते यज्ञस्य च मिथुनाद्वाचश्च यन्मा तन्नाभिभवेदिति स इंद्र एव गर्भो भूत्वैतन्निथुनं प्रविवेश ॥ (iṃdro ha vā īkṣāṃcakre | mahadvā ito 'bhvaṃ janiṣyate yajñasya ca mithunādvācaśca yanmā tannābhibhavediti sa iṃdra eva garbho bhūtvaitannithunaṃ praviveśa ‖) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-1-26). After that union Indra thought: "If this conjugal relation of sacrifice and speech is left as it is, a great demonic form may arise from this pair. Without giving it room, I myself must enter into their womb." So he himself entered as the embryo of the pair.

Thus, because speech was offered in the sacrifice in the form of a full oblation, and because complete unity resulted from this offering, Sāyaṇa holds that in the present verse the name होत्रा (hotrā) is applied to speech in the form of the sacrifice. He has shown the sentence quoted above from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as the basis. And saying "such a Bhāratī, of the form of speech", he has also stated that the word होत्रा (hotrā) is an epithet of Bhāratī.

भरतः आदित्यः तस्य।भाः (bharataḥ ādityaḥ tasya|bhāḥ) (Ni. 8-13): the Āditya has the synonym Bharata, and the author of the Nirukta gives the explanation that his light is well known by the name Bhāratī.

अमू स्थिताधिलोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ । सैषा तु त्रिविधा वाग्वै दिवि च व्योम्मि चेह च ॥ (amū sthitādhilokaṃ tu bhāratī bhavati hyasau | saiṣā tu trividhā vāgvai divi ca vyommi ceha ca ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-13). Among the deities in the form of speech who stand in the three worlds, the deity on the earth is called Bhāratī. Bhāratī, standing in the heavenly world, took refuge in the Āditya; that is what the author of the Nirukta calls आदित्यस्य भाः (ādityasya bhāḥ). But in देव्यस्ति स्रः श्रिताश्चैनं त्वष्टा चैवैतदाश्रयः । (devyasti sraḥ śritāścainaṃ tvaṣṭā caivaitadāśrayaḥ |) (Bṛ. De. 1-108) it is stated that these three deities, shining as radiance in the three worlds, all serve the terrestrial fire, so that everything is finally declared to be connected with Agni. In saying so, support can be shown also in the Ṛk Saṃhitā: तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्योक्षश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरंतं । य इंद्राय सुनवामेत्याह नरे नर्याय नृतमाय नृणां ॥ (tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajyokṣaśyātsūryamuccaraṃtaṃ | ya iṃdrāya sunavāmetyāha nare naryāya nṛtamāya nṛṇāṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-25-4)

p. 536

Agni, the lord of oblations, is Bhārata: Agni himself is called by the word Bhārata. Because she served such an Agni, that deity is called Bhāratī. But what is the nature of this deity? As Sāyaṇa has stated in his commentary on the present verse (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-3), it is explained precisely that for Hotrā, prāṇa, speech and sacrifice alike a meaning referring to Bhāratī can be given on the basis of Saṃhitā and Brāhmaṇa passages. प्राणो भूत्वा प्रजा धारयन् भारतः (prāṇo bhūtvā prajā dhārayan bhārataḥ): Agni, having become prāṇa and sustaining creatures, was called Bhārata; Sāyaṇa cites this sentence of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Ṛ. Saṃ. Bhā. 4-25-4).

शरणैः (śaraṇaiḥ)—शृणंति शीतादिक्लेशमिति शरणानि गृहाः (śṛṇaṃti śītādikleśamiti śaraṇāni gṛhāḥ): houses are called शरण (śaraṇa) because they ward off cold and similar afflictions and are protective. Durgācārya, following the view of the author of the Nirukta, explained this word as "strength". Since there is a place that is spacious for dwelling and gives shelter, the meaning "strength" or "house" may be given according to context. In उदुष्य शरणे दिवो ज्योतिरयंस्त सूर्यः । अग्निर्न शुक्रः समिधान आहुतः ॥ (uduṣya śaraṇe divo jyotirayaṃsta sūryaḥ | agnirna śukraḥ samidhāna āhutaḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-25-19) the word शरणे (śaraṇe) is explained as आदित्यस्य स्थाने नभसि (ādityasya sthāne nabhasi): since the sky is the spacious dwelling-place of the Āditya, the word शरण (śaraṇa) is explained as the sky. In many contexts such as मदेम शरणे सखायः (madema śaraṇe sakhāyaḥ) (7-19-8) the meaning "dwelling-house" is the established one.

दक्षिणाभिः (dakṣiṇābhiḥ)—सत्वान् दक्षयतीत्यनेन इति दक्षिणा (satvān dakṣayatītyanena iti dakṣiṇā): because it is the means of increasing the power of sacrifices and similar rites, it is called दक्षिणा (dakṣiṇā); the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa gives this explanation of the word (Kau. Brā. 15-1NOTE). The relation between sacrifice and dakṣiṇā is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā thus: यज्ञो दक्षिणा मभ्यध्यायत्ताग्ं समभवत् । (yajño dakṣiṇā mabhyadhyāyattāgṃ samabhavat |) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-3-6). Just as above it was said how Indra entered the womb of the pair when the sacrifice-person, desiring relation with speech, entered conjugal relation with her, so here too the relation between sacrifice and dakṣiṇā is stated in the same way.

p. 537

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

बृह॑स्पते जु॒षस्व॑ नो ह॒व्यानि॑ विश्वदेव्य ।
रास्व॒ रत्ना॑नि दा॒शुषे॑ ॥ ४ ॥

bṛhaspate juṣasva no havyāni viśvadevya |
rāsva ratnāni dāśuṣe ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

बृहस्पते । जुषस्व । नः । हव्यानि । विश्वदेव्य ।
रास्व । रत्नानि । दाशुषे ॥ ४ ॥

bṛhaspate | juṣasva | naḥ | havyāni | viśvadevya |
rāsva | ratnāni | dāśuṣe ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

विश्वदेव्य सर्वदेवहित हे बृहस्पते नोऽस्मत्संबंधीनि हव्यानि हवनयोग्यानि पुरोडाशादीनि हवींषि जुषस्व । सेवस्व । ततस्त्वं दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय मह्यं रत्नान्युत्तमानि धनानि रास्व। देहि ॥ रास्व। रा दाने। व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Bṛhaspati, benevolent to all the gods, accept our oblations, that is, the offerings fit for the fire, such as the puroḍāśa cake and the other havis. Having accepted them, give precious, excellent riches to me, the sacrificer who has given the oblation. The root रा (rā) means "to give", and the ātmanepada form रास्व (rāsva) is explained as a vyatyaya (an irregular exchange of voice).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • विश्वदेव्य (viśvadevya)—one who brings welfare to all
  • बृहस्पते (bṛhaspate)—O Bṛhaspati
  • नः (naḥ)—given by us
  • हव्यानि (havyāni)—the oblations
  • जुषस्व (juṣasva)—partake of
  • दाशुषे (dāśuṣe)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
  • रत्नानि (ratnāni)—riches in the form of jewels
  • रास्व (rāsva)—give
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, who brings welfare to all gods and men, partake of the oblations given by us. Provide wealth to the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Brihaspati, friend of all the gods, accept our oblations: grant precious treasures to the offerer.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Bṛhaspati, qualified by the epithet विश्वदेव्य बृहस्पते (viśvadevya bṛhaspate), is praised and prayed to for his favour. विश्वदेव्य (viśvadevya) can mean either "one connected with the Viśvedevas" or "one beneficial to all the gods". Being beneficial to all is the very nature of Bṛhaspati; the nirvacana (etymological explanation) of this word shows it.

p. 538

बृहस्पतिः बृहतः पाता ना पालयिता ना । (bṛhaspatiḥ bṛhataḥ pātā nā pālayitā nā |) (Ni. 10-11) बृहंतौ पाति यल्लोकौ एष द्वौ मध्यमोत्तमौ । बृहता कर्मणा तेन बृहस्पतिरितीळितः ॥ (bṛhaṃtau pāti yallokau eṣa dvau madhyamottamau | bṛhatā karmaṇā tena bṛhaspatiritīḷitaḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 2-39) The name Bṛhaspati arises either because he fully protects the great middle and highest worlds, or because he is the performer of a great rite. बृहत् इति महतो नामदेयं (bṛhat iti mahato nāmadeyaṃ) (Ni. 17): "bṛhat" is the name of what is great. The meaning is that he protects all the worlds, which are of great nature. The Nirukta authors have described Bṛhaspati as a deity belonging to the world of Indra (the middle world). इंद्राश्रयस्तु पर्जन्यो रुद्रो वायुर्बृहस्पतिः । वरुणः कश्च मृत्युश्च देवश्च ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥ (iṃdrāśrayastu parjanyo rudro vāyurbṛhaspatiḥ | varuṇaḥ kaśca mṛtyuśca devaśca brahmaṇaspatiḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 1-122) Parjanya, Rudra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa, Ka, Mṛtyu and the god Brahmaṇaspati: all of these are deities in the world of Indra, included within Indra and of Indra's nature. The Bṛhaddevatā also states this, following the divisions of the Nirukta authors (Ni. 5-4,5). But by this division Bṛhaspati's nature does not become restricted to a region. From the very fact that he protects all the worlds of great nature, Bṛhaspati's great nature is also understood. एकविग्ंशतिं वशा अनूबंध्या आलभते मैत्रावरुणीर्वैश्वदेवीर्बार्हस्पत्या एतासां देवतानामाप्त्यै तद्यद्बार्हस्पत्यान्ता भवंति ब्रह्म वै बृहस्पतिस्तदु ब्रह्मण्येवांततः प्रतितिष्ठति ॥ (ekavigṃśatiṃ vaśā anūbaṃdhyā ālabhate maitrāvaruṇīrvaiśvadevīrbārhaspatyā etāsāṃ devatānāmāptyai tadyadbārhaspatyāntā bhavaṃti brahma vai bṛhaspatistadu brahmaṇyevāṃtataḥ pratitiṣṭhati ‖) (Śa. Brā. 13 5-4-25) After the oblation called udayanīya, if one performs the rite called paśubandha, which is helpful to Mitrāvaruṇa, the Viśvedevas and Bṛhaspati, in order to obtain the favour of these deities, they are satisfied. That Bṛhaspati's name is placed at the end here shows that Bṛhaspati is the deity worthy of the homage of all. This Bṛhaspati is the Supreme Brahman; Bṛhaspati reflects the Brahman principle that pervades the world. In this way Bṛhaspati's greatness is shown. The relation between Bṛhaspati and the Viśvedevas is also close. The epithet विश्वदेव्य (viśvadevya) too indicates it. Other śrutis also say the same. For example,

p. 539

ते देवा अबिभयुरस्माकं विप्रेमाणमन्विदमसुरा अभविष्यंतीति ते प्युत्क्रम्यामंत्रयंताग्निर्वसुभिरुदक्रामदिंद्रो रुद्रैर्वरुण आदित्यैर्बृहस्पतिर्विश्वैर्देवैः ॥ (te devā abibhayurasmākaṃ vipremāṇamanvidamasurā abhaviṣyaṃtīti te pyutkramyāmaṃtrayaṃtāgnirvasubhirudakrāmadiṃdro rudrairvaruṇa ādityairbṛhaspatirviśvairdevaiḥ ‖) (Ai. Brā. 4-24) Seeing the might of the Asuras, all the gods were afraid. Seeking a remedy, they all came out, thinking of the next step. Then Agni came out thinking together with the Vasus, Indra with the Rudras, Varuṇa with the Ādityas, and Bṛhaspati with the Viśvedevas. Thus the relation between Bṛhaspati and the Viśvedevas is shown. बृहस्पतये तप्त विश्वदेव्यावते स्वाहेति । आयं वै बृहस्पतियोऽयं पवते तस्मा एवैनं जुहोति तस्मादाह बृहस्पतयेत्तेति विश्वदेव्यावत इति तदस्मिन् विश्वान्स्वर्वान् देवानन्नाभजति । (bṛhaspataye tapta viśvadevyāvate svāheti | āyaṃ vai bṛhaspatiyo 'yaṃ pavate tasmā evainaṃ juhoti tasmādāha bṛhaspatayetteti viśvadevyāvata iti tadasmin viśvānsvarvān devānannābhajati |) (Śa. Brā. 14-2-20) Bṛhaspati is the form of the wind, all-pervading and spread through every region. The offering is to be made addressed to this Bṛhaspati, together with the Viśvedevas. For that very reason the offering must be made reciting the mantra beginning बृहस्पतिये त्वा (bṛhaspatiye tvā); then it is as though offered to Bṛhaspati together with the Viśvedevas. Thus their relation is shown. The all-pervading wind, and the principle of sound (śabda) that reflects the wind-principle, are both marked by the name Bṛhaspati. एष उ एव बृहस्पतिः । वाग्वै बृहती, तस्या एष पतिः । तस्मादु बृहस्पतिः । (eṣa u eva bṛhaspatiḥ | vāgvai bṛhatī, tasyā eṣa patiḥ | tasmādu bṛhaspatiḥ |) (Bṛ. U. 1-3-20) Bṛhaspati is the Word-Brahman. How? Speech is Bṛhatī, and this deity is the lord of speech; therefore he is renowned as Bṛhaspati. In this manner Bṛhaspati is described.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

शुचि॑म॒र्कैर्बृह॒स्पति॑मध्व॒रेषु॑ नमस्यत ।
अना॒म्योज॒ आ च॑के ॥ ५ ॥

śucimarkairbṛhaspatimadhvareṣu namasyata |
anāmyoja ā cake ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शुचिं । अर्कैः । बृहस्पतिं । अध्वरेषु । नमस्यत ।
अनामि । ओजः । आ । चके ॥ ५ ॥

śuciṃ | arkaiḥ | bṛhaspatiṃ | adhvareṣu | namasyata |
anāmi | ojaḥ | ā | cake ‖ 5 ‖

p. 540

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे ऋत्विजो यूयमध्वरेषु शुचिं शुद्धं बृहस्पतिमर्क्करर्चनीयैः स्तोत्रैर्नमस्यत । परिचरत । अनाम्यनमनशीलं परैरनभिभवनीयमोजस्तस्य बलमा चके । सर्वतो याचे ॥ बृहस्पतिं । वनस्पत्यादित्वादुभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । चके । कर्मेर्लिट्युत्तमे मकारलोपश्रांदसः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests, in the sacrifices worship the pure Bṛhaspati with praise-hymns fit to be chanted (arka); serve him. अनामि (anāmi) means unbending, that which others cannot overpower; his ओजः (ojaḥ) is his strength. आ चके (ā cake) means "I ask for it on every side". The word Bṛhaspati has the accent of both members of the compound, because it belongs to the vanaspati-type compounds. चके (cake) is the perfect of the root kṛ in the first person, with the loss of the letter m, which is Vedic.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अध्वरेषु (adhvareṣu)—in the sacrifices
  • शुचिं (śuciṃ)—the pure
  • बृहस्पतिं (bṛhaspatiṃ)—Bṛhaspati
  • अर्कैः (arkaiḥ)—with venerable praises
  • नमस्यत (namasyata)—worship
  • अनामि (anāmi)—that which enemies cannot diminish
  • ओजः (ojaḥ)—strength
  • आ चके (ā cake)—I ask (from him)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, in the sacrifices worship the pure Bṛhaspati with venerable praises. I ask from him strength that enemies cannot diminish.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Adore the pure Brihaspati at sacrifices with hymns : I solicit of him unsurpassable strength.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अध्वरेषु शुचिं (adhvareṣu śuciṃ)—"pure in the sacrifices": this describes the nature of Bṛhaspati. When the epithet "pure" (śuci) is applied to the sacrificial fire there is a special meaning, and it indicates a special quality of Agni. For example, अग्निशुचिर्व्रततमशुचिर्विप्रः शुचिः कविः । शुची रोचत आहुतः । उदग्ने शुचयस्तव शुक्रा भ्राजंत ईरते । तव ज्योतीगंष्यर्चयः ॥ (agniśucirvratatamaśucirvipraḥ śuciḥ kaviḥ | śucī rocata āhutaḥ | udagne śucayastava śukrā bhrājaṃta īrate | tava jyotīgaṃṣyarcayaḥ ‖) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-14-8) All the observances of Agni are pure. He is a pure sage (vipra), a pure poet (kavi). When the oblation is offered he shines by this very purity. O Agni, your flames, pure and bright, shine and rise with radiance. In this way the distinction of Agni, who is of the nature of radiance, with a body of flame kindled by ghee, stainless and shining, is praised. To show that the same radiance is in Bṛhaspati, the epithet "pure" is used here. Or else, since Bṛhaspati is a portion of Agni, this epithet is quite proper. In the Ṛk-saṃhitā itself there are many statements showing the identity of Agni and Bṛhaspati. For example,

p. 541

अच्छा वदा तना गिरा जराय्कॆ ब्रह्मणस्पतिं । अग्निं मित्रं न दर्शतं ॥ (acchā vadā tanā girā jarāykè brahmaṇaspatiṃ | agniṃ mitraṃ na darśataṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-38-13) The scholar Max Müller has translated this Ṛk thus: "Speak out for ever, with thy voice to praise the lord of prayer, Agni, who is like a friend, the bright one." The meaning given is: recite the praise of Agni, the lord of hymns, who is like a friend. That is, it shows that the word Bṛhaspati is an epithet of Agni; the meaning is that Agni is Bṛhaspati. [Sāyaṇa has explained Bṛhaspati as Maruddaṇa. That is one view. But to say that it is an epithet of Agni is the proper one here.] तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानमुक्थ्यं । बृहस्पतिं मनुषो देवतातये विप्रं श्रोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदं ॥ (taṃ śubhramagnimavase havāmahe vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvānamukthyaṃ | bṛhaspatiṃ manuṣo devatātaye vipraṃ śrotāramatithiṃ raghuṣyadaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-26-2) In this mantra, which says "we call, for our protection, Agni, friend of men, worthy of praise, Mātariśvan, Bṛhaspati", Sāyaṇa too explains बृहस्पतिं (bṛhaspatiṃ) precisely in the sense of Agni: बृहतः यज्ञस्य पालयितारं (bṛhataḥ yajñasya pālayitāraṃ), "Agni, protector of the great sacrifice". आ वेधसं नीलपृष्ठं बृहंतं बृहस्पतिं सदने साधयध्वं । सादद्योनिं दम आ दीदिवांसं हिरण्यवर्णमरुषं सपेम ॥ ( (ā vedhasaṃ nīlapṛṣṭhaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ sadane sādhayadhvaṃ | sādadyoniṃ dama ā dīdivāṃsaṃ hiraṇyavarṇamaruṣaṃ sapema ‖ () (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-43-12) Here Sāyaṇa, explaining this mantra as referring to Agni, says: बृहतः परिवृढस्य कर्मणः स्वामीति बृहस्पतिरग्नि रुच्यते। तथा नीलवर्णधूमपृष्ठत्वसदनसादनहिरण्यवर्णत्वादिलिंगैरप्यग्निरेव बृहस्पतिः । (bṛhataḥ parivṛḍhasya karmaṇaḥ svāmīti bṛhaspatiragni rucyate| tathā nīlavarṇadhūmapṛṣṭhatvasadanasādanahiraṇyavarṇatvādiliṃgairapyagnireva bṛhaspatiḥ |) Because he is the lord of very great rites, Agni is denoted by the word Bṛhaspati. The epithets "blue-backed", "golden-coloured" and the like also describe the qualities of Agni in the form of Bṛhaspati; this he has stated exactly. The phrase अर्कैः नमस्यत (arkaiḥ namasyata) also supports the above meaning. The Aitareya-Āraṇyaka mantra अग्निर्वा अर्कः (agnirvā arkaḥ) (Ai. Ā. 1-4-1) and एषोऽग्निरर्को यत्पुरुषः स यो हैतमेवमग्निमर्कं पुरुषमुपास्तेय महमग्निरर्कोऽस्मीति विद्यया हैवास्यैष आत्मन्नग्निरर्कश्चितो धवति ॥ (eṣo 'gnirarko yatpuruṣaḥ sa yo haitamevamagnimarkaṃ puruṣamupāsteya mahamagnirarko 'smīti vidyayā haivāsyaiṣa ātmannagnirarkaścito dhavati ‖) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-4-5) state the identity: Agni in the form of the Puruṣa is Arka; Agni in the form of the fire-altar (citi) is also Arka. [The special meanings of arka have been explained in detail in Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 12, p. 445.]

p. 542

Here only the relation between Agni, in the form of Bṛhaspati, and Arka is indicated, showing the propriety of the use of the words "pure" (śuci) and "arka" in the present Ṛk. Just as the word śuci shows Bṛhaspati's sacrificial nature, the synonym śukra shows his spiritual nature. बृहस्पतिर्वै शुक्रो भूत्वेदस्याभयायासुरेभ्यः क्षयायेमामविद्यामसृजत् (bṛhaspatirvai śukro bhūtvedasyābhayāyāsurebhyaḥ kṣayāyemāmavidyāmasṛjat) (Maitrya. Panisat. 7-9) NOTE Bṛhaspati, becoming Śukra, created for the gods the light of knowledge and for the Asuras the darkness of ignorance. Just as the word śuci shows a special quality of Agni, so the word śukra too shows a special quality of Agni. This quality of Śukra became famous in the Purāṇas and elsewhere as Śukrācārya. This name shows spiritual truth rather than historical fact.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

वृ॒ष॒भं च॑र्षणी॒नां वि॒श्वरू॑प॒मदा॑भ्यं ।
बृह॒स्पतिं॒ । वरे॑ण्यं ॥ ६ ॥

vṛṣabhaṃ carṣaṇīnāṃ viśvarūpamadābhyaṃ |
bṛhaspatiṃ | vareṇyaṃ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

वृषभं । चर्षणीनां । विश्वरूपं । अदाभ्यं ।
बृहस्पतिं । वरेण्यं ॥ ६ ॥

vṛṣabhaṃ | carṣaṇīnāṃ | viśvarūpaṃ | adābhyaṃ |
bṛhaspatiṃ | vareṇyaṃ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणां वृषभमभिमतफलवर्षकं विश्वरूपं व्याप्तरूपं । यद्वा । विश्वरूपानामकगोवाहनोपेतं । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । बृहस्पतिर्विश्वरूपामुपाजत । ऋग्वे. १-१६१-६ । इति । अदाभ्यं केनाप्यतिरस्करणीयं वरेण्यं सर्वैर्भजनीयं बृहस्पतिं । अभिमतफलं याच इति पूर्वणान्वयः ॥ विश्वरूपं । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं । यद्वा । विश्वरूपास्य सतीति अर्शआदिश्वादच् प्रत्ययः । मरुद्वृधादित्वात्पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं । अदाभ्यं । दभेश्चेति वक्तव्यमिति ण्यत्पत्ययः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Bṛhaspati is the bull (the showerer of desired fruits) of the चर्षणीनां (carṣaṇīnāṃ), the men; विश्वरूपं (viśvarūpaṃ) means "of all-pervading form". Or else, he is "accompanied by a cow-vehicle named Viśvarūpā". The mantra text says so: बृहस्पतिर्विश्वरूपामुपाजत (bṛhaspatirviśvarūpāmupājata) (Ṛg. 1-161-6). अदाभ्यं (adābhyaṃ) means "not to be slighted by anyone"; वरेण्यं (vareṇyaṃ) means "to be served by all". "I ask Bṛhaspati for the desired fruit": the construction links with the earlier verse. The remaining discussion concerns the accent of विश्वरूपं (viśvarūpaṃ) (in a bahuvrīhi, initial-member final-udātta; or, in the alternative, with the affix ac after the arśa-ādi group) and the formation of अदाभ्यं (adābhyaṃ) with the affix ṇyat.

p. 543

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • चर्षणीनां (carṣaṇīnāṃ)—to men
  • वृषभं (vṛṣabhaṃ)—the giver of desired things
  • विश्वरूपं (viśvarūpaṃ)—the one of many forms
  • अदाभ्यं (adābhyaṃ)—the one who is rejected by no one
  • वरेण्यं (vareṇyaṃ)—the one worthy of the worship of all
  • बृहस्पतिं (bṛhaspatiṃ)—Bṛhaspati (I beseech)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I beseech Bṛhaspati, who gives desired things to men, who has many forms, who is rejected by no one, and who is worthy of the worship of all.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The showerer (of benefits) on men, the omniform, the irreproachable, the excellent Brihaspati.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning for the epithet विश्वरूपं (viśvarūpaṃ). First, व्याप्तरूपं (vyāptarūpaṃ): one whose form pervades all regions. Second, यद्वा निश्वरूपानाम गोवाहनोपेतं (yadvā niśvarūpānāma govāhanopetaṃ): one who has as his vehicle the cow named Viśvarūpa. Both kinds of explanation describe the nature of Bṛhaspati.

Earlier it was explained, in एष उ एव बृहस्पतिः (eṣa u eva bṛhaspatiḥ) and वाग्वै बृहस्पतिः (vāgvai bṛhaspatiḥ), that Speech, which is all-pervading, is Bṛhaspati; that the Udgītha, which has many forms such as Aṅgirasa and Ayāsya and is all-pervading, is Bṛhaspati; and that Agni, who pervades the universe through names and forms such as Vaiśvānara, is Bṛhaspati. That showed Bṛhaspati's all-pervasiveness. Here the propriety of this epithet must be examined through the explanation विश्वरूपानामगोवाहनोपेतं (viśvarūpānāmagovāhanopetaṃ).

अरुण्यो गाव उषसां । श्यावा सवितुः । विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः ॥ (aruṇyo gāva uṣasāṃ | śyāvā savituḥ | viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ ‖) (Ni. 2-28). Just as the horses called Harī are well known for Indra, the ruddy cows for Uṣas, the goats for Pūṣan, and likewise vehicles suited to the other deities, so for Bṛhaspati the cow called Viśvarūpā is well known as the vehicle. Sāyaṇa too cites the passage बृहस्पतेर्विश्वरूपामुपाजत (bṛhaspaterviśvarūpāmupājata) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-161-6) and says that, as Viśvarūpā there means the cow of that name, so here too the sense is "one who has the cow named Viśvarūpa". However, while explaining Ṛk 1-161-6 he also raises the doubt why the word विश्वरूपां (viśvarūpāṃ) should be taken as meaning a cow, and gives the answer.

p. 544

धेनुं सबर्दुघां चक्रुरमृतं सबरुच्यते । बृहस्पतेरथाश्विभ्यां रथं दिव्यं त्रिवंधुरं ॥ (dhenuṃ sabardughāṃ cakruramṛtaṃ sabarucyate | bṛhaspaterathāśvibhyāṃ rathaṃ divyaṃ trivaṃdhuraṃ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-85, 86). This says that the Ṛbhus made for Bṛhaspati a cow that yields nectar. The name Viśvarūpā is not mentioned. Some hold that this cow is the goddess of Speech, that the varieties of Speech, which has many natures, are what has all forms, and that Speech, which has the nature of the supreme Brahman, is the nectar. Scriptural statements can be shown in support of this purport as well.

. यद्यप्यत्र गौरिति विशेषो न श्रुतः तथापि पूर्वं धेनुं कर्त्वा इत्युत्तत्वात् परस्ताच्च ये धेनुं विश्वजुवं विश्वरूपां इति वक्ष्यमाणत्वाच्च विश्वरूपा गौः इत्येवाध्यवसीयते ॥ (. yadyapyatra gauriti viśeṣo na śrutaḥ tathāpi pūrvaṃ dhenuṃ kartvā ityuttatvāt parastācca ye dhenuṃ viśvajuvaṃ viśvarūpāṃ iti vakṣyamāṇatvācca viśvarūpā gauḥ ityevādhyavasīyate ‖). In the present verse there is no qualified noun "cow". Still, because the making of a cow was mentioned before (1-161-3), and because later too the creation of a cow is stated with विश्वरूपां (viśvarūpāṃ), the sense here too must be "cow". So Sāyaṇa explains Ṛk 1-161-6.

Moreover: रथं ये चक्रुः सुवृतं नरेष्ठां ये धेनुं विश्वजुवं विश्वरूपां । त आ तक्षन्त्वृभवो रयिं नः स्ववसः स्वपसः सुहस्ताः ॥ (rathaṃ ye cakruḥ suvṛtaṃ nareṣṭhāṃ ye dhenuṃ viśvajuvaṃ viśvarūpāṃ | ta ā takṣantvṛbhavo rayiṃ naḥ svavasaḥ svapasaḥ suhastāḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-33-8). Here it is clear that the Ṛbhus created for Bṛhaspati the cow called Viśvarūpā. The same point is made in the present verse, and Bṛhaspati's nature is described by the epithet विश्वरूपं (viśvarūpaṃ).

वरेण्यं (vareṇyaṃ)—संभजनीयं (saṃbhajanīyaṃ): Bṛhaspati, who is worthy of worship; Bṛhaspati is worthy of worship for all the gods and for men. ब्रह्म हि बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्म हि ब्राह्मणाः (brahma hi bṛhaspatirbrahma hi brāhmaṇāḥ) (Śa. Brā. 5-1-5-6). ब्रह्म वै बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणैवैनं तद्भिषज्यति (brahma vai bṛhaspatirbrahmaṇaivainaṃ tadbhiṣajyati) (Ai. Brā. 4-19). In such passages Bṛhaspati's worthiness of worship is praised. Here the favour of Bṛhaspati, who has such greatness, is prayed for.

p. 545

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

इ॒यं ते॑ पूषन्नाघृणे सुष्टु॒तिर्दे॑व॒ नव्य॑सी ।
अ॒स्माभि॒स्तुभ्यं॑ शस्यते ॥ ७ ॥

iyaṃ te pūṣannāghṛṇe suṣṭutirdeva navyasī |
asmābhistubhyaṃ śasyate ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

इयं । ते । पूषन् । आफृणे । सुस्तुतिः । देव । नव्यसी ।
अस्माभिः । तुभ्यं । शस्यते ॥ ७ ॥

iyaṃ | te | pūṣan | āphṛṇe | sustutiḥ | deva | navyasī |
asmābhiḥ | tubhyaṃ | śasyate ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

आघ्रणे आगतदीप्तिमन् हे पूषन् देव नव्यसी नवतरेयं सुष्टुतिः शोभ नस्तुतिरूपा वाक् ते त्वत्संबंधिनी भवति । सैषा स्तुतिरस्माभिः स्तोतृभिस्तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं शस्यते । तां जुषस्वेत्युत्तरेणान्वयः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Āghṛṇi (one whose radiance has arrived), O Pūṣan, O god: this newer, fresh laudation, a speech of praise that is beautiful, is yours, related to you. This praise is uttered by us, the praisers, for you, for your sake. The construction is with the following verse: "Enjoy it."

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • आघृणे (āghṛṇe)—O shining one
  • पूषन् देव (pūṣan deva)—O god Pūṣan
  • नव्यसी (navyasī)—new
  • इयं सुष्टुतिः (iyaṃ suṣṭutiḥ)—and excellent, this praise
  • ते (te)—to be offered to you
  • अस्माभिः (asmābhiḥ)—by us, the praisers
  • तुभ्यं (tubhyaṃ)—addressed to you
  • शस्यते (śasyate)—is praised
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining god Pūṣan, this praise, new and excellent, is to be offered to you. It has been composed by us, the praisers, in your honour.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Divine, resplendent, Pushan, this, your most recent laudation, is uttered by us to you.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पूषन् (pūṣan)—पूषा यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत् पूषा भवति (pūṣā yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tat pūṣā bhavati) (Ni. 12-16). The author of the Nirukta has shown this derivation of the word: since he nourishes the world, attaining an abundance of rays, he is named Pūṣā. To show that this definition is fitting, the Nirukta-writer has cited as authority a passage of the Ṛk Saṃhitā.

p. 546

शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि । विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥ (śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadviṣurūpe ahanī dyaurivāsi | viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣanniha rātirastu ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1). O Pūṣan, you possess a variety of radiance. Day and night are all the effect of your radiance. All your actions filled with wisdom also point to the power of the Sun. You are one who possesses exceedingly great radiance. Thus a Ṛk describing Pūṣan's quality is cited, showing that radiance is his special quality.

पुष्यन् क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः । तेनैनमस्तौत्पोषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पंचभिः ॥ (puṣyan kṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ | tenainamastautpoṣeti bharadvājastu paṃcabhiḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 2-63). He is called Pūṣā because, destroying darkness with his mass of radiance, he nourishes the earth so that it attains fullness. The seer Bharadvāja praised Pūṣan with hymns addressed to this god, in five sūktas. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā state that in that context all of Pūṣan's good qualities are described.

इयं वै पूषा पूषेयं हीवं सर्वं पुष्यति यदिदं किंच । (iyaṃ vai pūṣā pūṣeyaṃ hīvaṃ sarvaṃ puṣyati yadidaṃ kiṃca |) (Śa. Brā. 14-4-2-25). In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa his nature is described thus: he is called Pūṣan because he nourishes all things. There is room for discussion on whether Pūṣan is only one of the twelve Ādityas or an independent deity distinct from them.

यास्ते पूषन्नावो अंतः समुद्रे हिरण्ययिरंतरिक्षे चरंति । ताभिर्यासि दूत्यां सूर्यस्य कामेन कृत श्रव इच्छमानः ॥ (yāste pūṣannāvo aṃtaḥ samudre hiraṇyayiraṃtarikṣe caraṃti | tābhiryāsi dūtyāṃ sūryasya kāmena kṛta śrava icchamānaḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-3). O Pūṣan, the beneficial, ray-formed boat of yours that sails in the ocean of the atmosphere: together with that ray-formed boat you act as the Sun's messenger. From such passages it is shown that points of difference between the Sun and Pūṣan appear. In Sūkta 8-29 of the Ṛ. Saṃ., where the nature of the Viśvedevas is described, no solar quality is specified in the description of Pūṣan. So it is argued that, contrary to the traditional view, Pūṣan is not an Āditya deity; he is a deity of "herdsman" nature who has obtained a distinct character of his own.

p. 547

The main part of the hymns to the deity Pūṣan is in the sixth Maṇḍala of the Ṛk Saṃhitā. As stated in the Bṛhaddevatā, it appears that the seers of the Bhāradvāja line took Pūṣan as their chief deity. Some call this portion the Pūṣa-saṃhitā. Besides, in other parts of the Saṃhitā too Pūṣan is praised, together with other deities such as Indra and Soma. Descriptions such as Kaparda, Paśusādhanī, Aṣṭrā, Karambhād and Ajāśva give a definite picture of Pūṣan. Along with the ordinary qualities that other deities also have, a special aspect of Pūṣan seems to be prominent in the sixth Maṇḍala. It is stated plainly that he is the deity who protects herds, that by the grace of this deity the cattle-wealth of worshippers should increase, and that he is the protector of cattle that have lost their way.

पूषा गा अन्वेतु नः पूषा रक्षत्वर्वतः । पूषा वाजं सनोतु नः ॥ (pūṣā gā anvetu naḥ pūṣā rakṣatvarvataḥ | pūṣā vājaṃ sanotu naḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-54-5). मार्किर्नेशन्माकीं रिषन्माकीं सं शारि केवटे । अथारिष्टाभिरा गहि । (mārkirneśanmākīṃ riṣanmākīṃ saṃ śāri kevaṭe | athāriṣṭābhirā gahi |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-54-7). Thus, praying in many ways, they pray that their cattle-wealth be increased.

From the above examples, though Pūṣan may be called an independent deity, it is not possible to say that he is distinct from the twelve Ādityas; and to say so would be wrong. For, although epithets such as protector of cattle show Pūṣan's distinctness, he is described as a deity who is a mass of radiance, just as the deities Sūrya, Aryaman, Bhaga and others are described. Yāska counts Pūṣan as one of the twelve Ādityas. The scholar Bloomfield too, following Yāska's view, maintains, on the basis of the epithet आफृणि (āphṛṇi) in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48.16; 6-53-6; 6-55-1, that Pūṣan is an Āditya deity who makes light shine.NOTE Some oppose this view. They argue that the word आफृणि (āphṛṇi), used also in the present Ṛk, can describe the quality of any radiant deity; that this epithet may be used of any deity full of radiance; that there is no rule that it must be an Āditya; that, for example (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-60-20), in some places the epithet applies to Agni; and that by this one epithet alone Pūṣan cannot be determined to be an Āditya deity. Yāska, the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā and others of the Vedic tradition maintain that आफृणि (āphṛṇi) is a special quality showing Pūṣan's distinctness alone. When Yāska gives the definition of this word in the Nirukta, he explains it as आफृणिराहृतहृणिः (āphṛṇirāhṛtahṛṇiḥ),

p. 548

and indicating the word in the Ṛk एहि वां विमुचो नपादाघृणे सं सचावहै । रथीर्यतस्य नो भव । (ehi vāṃ vimuco napādāghṛṇe saṃ sacāvahai | rathīryatasya no bhava |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-55-1), he states his view. But in आगतहृणिः (āgatahṛṇiḥ) he has not given a precise meaning for the word हृणि (hṛṇi). The word हृणि (hṛṇi) is read among the words for brightness (Ni. 2-28) and also among the names of anger (Ni. 4-9). Therefore Durgācārya, commenting on this word, says: अफृणिशब्दो दीप्तिवाचकः । दीप्तिकर्मसु च पठित एवायं हृणिः इति (aphṛṇiśabdo dīptivācakaḥ | dīptikarmasu ca paṭhita evāyaṃ hṛṇiḥ iti). Since the word हृणि (hṛṇi) is read among words denoting brightness, one meaning is "shining"; and क्रोधोऽपि हृणिरुच्यते (krodho 'pi hṛṇirucyate): since the word हृणि (hṛṇi) also means anger, another is "let us serve that Pūṣan whose anger may be directed upon us". Thus he shows that two kinds of explanation are possible. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā explain this epithet in yet another way.

तृचो विश्वेषां देवानां पूष्ण आघृणये तृचः । आसक्तो हि घृणिस्तस्य दध्नः पूर्णो दृती रथे ॥ आघृणिस्तत्सुतः पूषा कीरिभी रिभ्यते ततः ॥ (tṛco viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ pūṣṇa āghṛṇaye tṛcaḥ | āsakto hi ghṛṇistasya dadhnaḥ pūrṇo dṛtī rathe ‖ āghṛṇistatsutaḥ pūṣā kīribhī ribhyate tataḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-95, 96). Since a leather bag filled with curds (an intoxicating liquid) is tied to his chariot, he has the name आफृणि (āphṛṇi); and for that very reason the poets who praise him praise Pūṣan as आफृणि (āphṛṇi). Generally Sāyaṇa, in all places where this word occurs, explains it as आगतदीप्ते पूषन् (āgatadīpte pūṣan). This word (आफृणि (āphṛṇi)) is an epithet of Agni only at 8-60-20. In all other places it is an epithet of Pūṣan and states his distinctness.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

तां जु॑षस्व॒ गिरं॒ मम॑ वाज॒यंती॑मवा॒ धियं॑ ।
व॒धू॒युरि॑व॒ योष॑णां ॥ ८ ॥

tāṃ juṣasva giraṃ mama vājayaṃtīmavā dhiyaṃ |
vadhūyuriva yoṣaṇāṃ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शां । जुषस्व । गिरं । मम । वाजयंतीं । अव । धियं ।
वधूयुःइव । योषणां ॥ ८ ॥

śāṃ | juṣasva | giraṃ | mama | vājayaṃtīṃ | ava | dhiyaṃ |
vadhūyuḥiva | yoṣaṇāṃ ‖ 8 ‖

p. 549

हे पूषन् स्तोत्रं कुर्वाणस्य मम तां तादृशीं गिरं स्तुतिलक्षणां वाचं जुषस्व । सेवस्व । स्तुत्या प्रीतस्त्वं वाजयंतीं वाजमन्नमिच्छंतीं हर्षकारिणीं धियमिमां स्तुतिं प्रत्यव । अभिगच्छ । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वधूयुरिव । यथा वधूयुः स्त्रीकामो योषणां स्त्रीयं प्रत्यागच्छति तद्वत् ॥ वाजयंतीं । वाजशब्दादिच्छतीत्यर्थे क्यच् । तदंताच्छतरि जीपि रूपं । जीपोऽनुदात्तत्वे प्रत्ययस्वरः । अव । अव रक्षणादिश्वित्यस्य लोटि रूपं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Pūṣan, accept (जुषस्व (juṣasva), "serve") that speech of mine, of me who am praising, a speech whose nature is praise. Pleased by the praise, come towards this hymn (धियं (dhiyaṃ)), which seeks food (वाज (vāja), "food") and gives delight." The illustration is वधूयुरिव (vadhūyuriva): as a वधूयुः (vadhūyuḥ), one desirous of a woman, goes towards a woman (योषणां (yoṣaṇāṃ)), so Pūṣan is to come towards the praise. वाजयंतीं (vājayaṃtīṃ) is formed from the word वाज (vāja) in the sense "desires", and अव (ava) is the imperative of the root अव (ava) meaning "protect" and so on.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • Hey (Pūṣa-deva)
  • मम (mama)—of me, who am the praiser
  • अव (ava) is given last; see below
  • तां गिरं (tāṃ giraṃ)—this speech, which has the form of praise
  • जुषस्व (juṣasva)—accept
  • वाजयंतीं (vājayaṃtīṃ)—that which procures food
  • धियं (dhiyaṃ)—this praise
  • योषणां (yoṣaṇāṃ)—towards a woman
  • वधूयुरिव (vadhūyuriva)—as one desirous of a woman comes
  • अव (ava)—come to meet
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, accept this speech of mine, the praiser, which has the form of praise. As a man desirous of a woman comes towards a woman, so come towards this delight-giving praise, which procures food.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Be pleased by this my praise, and incline to this food-supplicating laudation as an uxorious (husband) to his wife.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The two words गिरं (giraṃ) and धियं (dhiyaṃ) are synonyms for "praise" here. स्तुतयो गिरः गृणातेः (stutayo giraḥ gṛṇāteḥ) (Ni. 1-11): the Nirukta-writers have shown the etymology that the word गिर् (gir) is derived from the root गृ (gṛ), which means "to make a sound". To support this, they explain it by showing the example of the word गिरः (giraḥ), in the sense of praise, in the Ṛk तमिद्वर्थंतु नो गिरः सदावृधं (tamidvarthaṃtu no giraḥ sadāvṛdhaṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-13-18). NOTE

धियं (dhiyaṃ)—this word is read among the names of works (karma). NOTE Indeed, quoting the Ṛk महो अर्णः सरस्वती प्रचेतयति केतुना । धियो विश्वा विराजति ॥ (maho arṇaḥ sarasvatī pracetayati ketunā | dhiyo viśvā virājati ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-12), the Nirukta-writers explain सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानानि (sarvāṇi prajñānāni), that is, "all our meditations (dhyāna), full of understanding"; and since praise too is meditative and rich in understanding,

p. 550

it too is denoted by the word धी (dhī). In some contexts the praisers, who are devoted to meditation, are also denoted by the word धी (dhī). In the present place धियं (dhiyaṃ) means "praise".

The relation between Pūṣan and the praise that has the form of धी (dhī) is compared with the relation between a young woman and a young man. As a well-adorned, refined and beautiful woman attracts an excellent man, so a refined praise attracts Pūṣan; this simile-description is poetic. It is not rare in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā that the love between Agni and the other gods and the oblation, between the praises and the gods, and between Indra and Soma, is likened to the bond of love between newly youthful lovers.

शये वव्रिश्चरति जिह्वयादन्रेरिह्यते युवतिं विश्वतिः सन् । (śaye vavriścarati jihvayādanrerihyate yuvatiṃ viśvatiḥ san |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-4-4): Agni, the lord of the house and its people, embraces with his mouth of flame the young woman in the form of the oblation; or else he embraces the young woman in the form of the earth.

अयं योनिश्च कृमा यं वयं ते जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासाः । (ayaṃ yoniśca kṛmā yaṃ vayaṃ te jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsāḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-3-2): O Agni, as a wife is adorned with excellent garments and ornaments and is thereby satisfied, for her husband's pleasure, so for your coming we prepare this place of sacrifice, the northern altar, well refined and make it attractive to you. In the same way the attractive relation between praise and the deity is described here as well. In places such as उक्ते वायुस्य रण्यसि (ukte vāyusya raṇyasi) (8-12-18) and यस्मिन्नु कानि रण्यंति विश्वानि च श्रवस्या (yasminnu kāni raṇyaṃti viśvāni ca śravasyā) (8-16-2), Indra and the others taking delight joined with the praises, and the praises taking delight joined with Indra and the other gods, are described in an attractive manner. Situations in which this delight and satisfaction are likened to the joy and satisfaction arising from the attractive union of newly youthful lovers are very plentiful, as in those cited above. In the present Ṛk too, explaining the same point, the praise is likened to a beautiful woman and Pūṣan to a young man so desirous of a woman. That is, the purport is that the praiser's praise is adorned and refined in such a way as to attract Pūṣan.

p. 551

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यो विश्वा॒भि वि॒पश्य॑ति॒ भुव॑ना॒ संच॒ पश्य॑ति ।
स नः प्रूषाविता भुवत् ॥ ९ ॥

yo viśvābhi vipaśyati bhuvanā saṃca paśyati |
sa naḥ prūṣāvitā bhuvat ‖ 9 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

यः । विश्वा । अभि । विपश्यति । भुवना । सं । च । पश्यति ।
सः । नः । पूषा । अविता । भुवत् ॥ ९ ॥

yaḥ | viśvā | abhi | vipaśyati | bhuvanā | saṃ | ca | paśyati |
saḥ | naḥ | pūṣā | avitā | bhuvat ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यः पूषा विश्वा भुवना सर्वाल्लोकानभि अभिमुख्येन विपश्यति विशेषेण पश्यति । किंच तानि सं पश्यति तत्तद्वस्तुयाथात्म्यं सम्यक् जानाति । स तादृशः पूषा देवो नोऽस्माकमविता रक्षको भुवत् । भवतु ॥ विपश्यति । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । तिजि चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः । पश्यति । अत्र सकर्मकत्वात्परस्मैपदं । पूर्ववदनिघातः । भवत् । भवतेर्लॆट्ट्यडागमः । भूसुवोस्तिजीति गुणप्रतिषेध उवजादेशः । निघातः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Pūṣan who looks upon (अभि विपश्यति (abhi vipaśyati)) all the worlds, all the regions, directly and in particular; and moreover (सं पश्यति (saṃ paśyati)) sees them thoroughly, that is, knows rightly the true nature of each thing: may that Pūṣan, the god, be our protector (अविता (avitā), "guardian"); भुवत् (bhuvat) means "may he be".

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः (yaḥ)—which Pūṣa-deva
  • विश्वा (viśvā)—all
  • भुवना (bhuvanā)—worlds
  • अभि विपश्यति (abhi vipaśyati)—looks upon and sees (and)
  • सं पश्यति (saṃ paśyati)—is able to know subtly the true nature of every thing
  • सः (saḥ)—such
  • पूषा (pūṣā)—Pūṣa-deva
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • अविता (avitā)—as protector
  • भुवत् (bhuvat)—may he be
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Pūṣa-deva, who looks upon and sees all the worlds and who knows subtly the real nature of every thing, be our protector.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May that Pushan, who looks upon all the worlds, who thoroughly contemplates them, be our protector.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The very quality of seeing the whole universe, which is described as the intrinsic quality of Savitṛ and of Āditya, is described in the present Ṛk too. By the sentence विश्वा भुवना अभि विपत्यति (viśvā bhuvanā abhi vipatyati) NOTE the quality of Āditya, the eye of the world, is in effect stated; that is, it was said earlier that the epithet आफृणिः (āphṛṇiḥ) specifically shows the Āditya-nature in Pūṣan. By this very radiance Pūṣan has the power of looking at the whole universe.

p. 552

प्रपथे पथामजनिष्ट पूषा प्रपथे दिवः प्रपथे पृथिव्याः । उभे अभि प्रियतमे सदस्ये आ च परा च चरति प्रजानन् ॥ (prapathe pathāmajaniṣṭa pūṣā prapathe divaḥ prapathe pṛthivyāḥ | ubhe abhi priyatame sadasye ā ca parā ca carati prajānan ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-6). The description that Pūṣan moves everywhere, watching over and protecting the paths of all the worlds, namely the path that goes to the atmosphere, the excellent path that leads to the world of heaven, and the excellent path of the earth, is itself the path of Āditya's travel through the universe. When it is said that he looks upon all such worlds, there is a repetition: अभि विपश्यति (abhi vipaśyati); संपश्यति (saṃpaśyati). For सं पश्यति (saṃ paśyati), तत्तद्वस्तुयाथात्मं सम्यग् जानाति (tattadvastuyāthātmaṃ samyag jānāti) means: he knows fully the subtle nature of those several things. Such power of right seeing is not possible for anyone but the Self of the universe; it is not to be perceived by ordinary sight. Even a knower of the truth who wishes for that power of right seeing asks only for Pūṣan's grace. Thus:

हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण सत्यस्यापिहितं मुखं । तत्त्वं पूषन्नपावृणु सत्यधर्माय दृष्टये । पूषन्नेकर्षे यम सूर्य प्राजापत्य व्यूह रश्मीन् । समूह तेजो यत्ते रूपं कल्याणतमं तत्ते पश्यामि ॥ (hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukhaṃ | tattvaṃ pūṣannapāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye | pūṣannekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn | samūha tejo yatte rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamaṃ tatte paśyāmi ‖) (Bṛ. U. 5-15-1,2). Brahman, whose nature is truth, is covered by the disc whose form is light. O Pūṣan, I too, who am devoted to the truth (satya-dharma), ask you to remove this covering so that I may see it. O Pūṣan, you alone are the sage of the nature of truth! The Āditya, the eye of the world, is Prājāpatya. With the help of all your radiance, gather together all the truths. Grant the power to know all the truths. In this way Pūṣan, who is thus prayed to, is indeed the deity who sets forth the Āditya-principle. The seeing power of Savitṛ of such Āditya-form is shown by the sentences अभि विपश्यति (abhi vipaśyati), संपश्यति (saṃpaśyati). The prayer of the next mantra is to obtain the power of knowing the divine form of this greatly eminent Savitṛ.

p. 553

Introduction to the Gāyatrī great mantra

The name Gāyatrī is well known for the tenth Ṛk of this sūkta, तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं (tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ). This Ṛk is read in all three Vedas: in the Ṛgveda at 3-62-10; in the Sāmaveda at 1462; in the Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) at 3-35; 22-9; 30-2; 36-3; in the Taittirīya-Saṃhitā (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) at 1-5-6-4; 4-1-11-1; and in the Taittirīya-Āraṇyaka at 1-11-2. In these places this Gāyatrī mantra is read. Further, except for the Yajurveda, which is largely prose, the other three Vedas, the Ṛgveda, Sāmaveda and Atharvaṇa, all begin with Ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre. NOTE

Although in general this is the name of a metre with three pādas of eight syllables each, it has become customary to call this very Ṛk "the Gāyatrī" among all the mantras of this metre. Since the word गायत्रि (gāyatri) is derived from the root गै (gai) (to sing), the word means a Ṛk suited for singing. Therefore the greater part of the Sāmaveda, which is recited in the form of song, consists of Ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre taken from the Ṛgveda. As said in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-1, the sentence गायंति त्वा गायत्रिणः (gāyaṃti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ) means: O Indra, the officiating priests, such as the Udgātṛ, who sing with mantras of the Gāyatrī metre, praise you with Sāma mantras and sing.

As the Ṛgveda has the first (chief) place among the Vedas, the Gāyatrī metre has the first place among the metres. And as the Brāhmaṇa has the foremost place among the three classes, Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya and Vaiśya, so the Gāyatrī has the foremost place among the metres. Therefore in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa of the Yajurveda:

गायत्रीभिर्ब्राह्मणस्यादध्यात् । गायत्रछंदा वै ब्राह्मणः । स्वस्य छंदसः प्रत्ययनस्त्वाय । (gāyatrībhirbrāhmaṇasyādadhyāt | gāyatrachaṃdā vai brāhmaṇaḥ | svasya chaṃdasaḥ pratyayanastvāya |) त्रिष्टुग्भी राजन्यस्य । त्रिष्टुप्छंदा वै राजन्यः । स्वस्य छंदसः प्रत्ययनस्त्वाय । (triṣṭugbhī rājanyasya | triṣṭupchaṃdā vai rājanyaḥ | svasya chaṃdasaḥ pratyayanastvāya |) जगतीभिर्वैश्यस्य । जगतीछंदा वै वैश्यः । स्वस्य छंदसः प्रत्ययनस्त्वाय । (jagatībhirvaiśyasya | jagatīchaṃdā vai vaiśyaḥ | svasya chaṃdasaḥ pratyayanastvāya |) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-6, 7)

So it is said. That is, in the ādhāna rite (ādhāna means newly establishing the sacrificial fire) and in the other sacrificial rites the Brāhmaṇa should perform the proceedings with mantras of the Gāyatrī metre alone. For it is said that the Gāyatrī metre is the Brāhmaṇa's own metre; and

p. 554

likewise the Kṣatriya (the king) should perform the proceedings at sacrifices and the like with mantras of his own metre, the Triṣṭubh, and the Vaiśya with mantras of his own metre, the Jagatī. Not only this, but in the chief acts performed in sacrifices the rite is to be performed first with mantras of the Gāyatrī metre. Thus:

गायत्रीरन्वाह गायत्रं वै प्रातस्सवनं (gāyatrīranvāha gāyatraṃ vai prātassavanaṃ) (Ai. Brā. 28-9) त्रैष्टुभं वै माध्यंदिनं सवनं (traiṣṭubhaṃ vai mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ) (Ai. Brā. 28-10) जागतं वै तृतीयसवनं (jāgataṃ vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ) (Ai. Brā. 28-15)

So it is said in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. That is, the chief ritual parts of the sacrifice are the three savanas: the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing. Savana is the particular rite of crushing the soma plants with stones and squeezing out the juice. It must be done with mantras and as prescribed. Therefore in the morning-pressing rite performed in the morning, the act called abhiṣavaṇa, squeezing out this soma juice, is performed with mantras of the Gāyatrī metre; in the midday pressing with mantras of the Triṣṭubh metre, and in the third pressing with mantras of the Jagatī metre. Therefore, among the chief acts to be performed in a sacrifice, the mantras of the Gāyatrī metre have the pre-eminence. And if we examine the relation between deities and metres, it is said that the Gāyatrī metre is dear to Agni, the Triṣṭubh to Indra, and the Jagatī to the Viśve-devāḥ.

Since it is said अष्टाक्षरा गायत्री । गायत्री ब्रह्मवर्चसं (aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī | gāyatrī brahmavarcasaṃ) (Śai. Brā. 2-3-3-9) NOTE and so on, if the Brāhmaṇa performs rites with mantras of the Gāyatrī metre he becomes endowed with Brahmanical lustre. If the king (Kṣatriya) does so with mantras of the Triṣṭubh metre, he obtains vigour, strength and fame. If the Vaiśya does so with mantras of the Jagatī metre, he obtains wealth of cattle, riches, prosperity and the like. This is said in many places in the Yajurveda.

Further, for all the 114 sūktas in the ninth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda, Soma, called Pavamāna Soma, is the deity. But the first 67 sūktas of this maṇḍala are in the Gāyatrī metre. All these were seen by various seers. Known as the Pavamāna sūktas, they have received great pre-eminence from the time of the Vedas. Their importance and glory are described there itself:

यः पावमानीरध्येति .... .... .... सर्वं स पूतमश्नाति । (yaḥ pāvamānīradhyeti .... .... .... sarvaṃ sa pūtamaśnāti |) पावमानीयो अध्येति .... .... .... । (pāvamānīyo adhyeti .... .... .... |) तस्मै सरस्वती दुहे क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकं । (tasmai sarasvatī duhe kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakaṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-67-31, 32)

p. 555

That is, whatever man studies (recites) these Pāvamānī sūktas, composed of ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre, obtains all his desired objects and prospers. The goddess Sarasvatī fulfils all his desires and also pours out milk, ghee, honey, water and every kind of abundance for him. All this is the greatness of the Gāyatrī mantra as stated in the Vedas. The precedence it has in the matter of the meaning of the Gāyatrī mantra now under discussion, and similar matters, are explained in the Special Topics of this ṛk.

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

तत्स॑वि॒तुर्वरे॑ण्यं॒ भर्गॊ॑ दे॒वस्य॑ धीमहि ।
धियो॒ यो नः॑ प्रचो॒दया॑त् ॥ १० ॥

tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargò devasya dhīmahi |
dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

तत् । सवितुः । वरेण्यं । भर्गः । देवस्य । धीमहि ।
धियः । यः । नः । प्रचोदयात् ॥ १० ॥

tat | savituḥ | vareṇyaṃ | bhargaḥ | devasya | dhīmahi |
dhiyaḥ | yaḥ | naḥ | pracodayāt ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

दशरात्रस्य षष्ठेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे तत्सवितुरिति द्वे ऋचौ प्रतिपत्तृचस्य द्वितीयातृतीये । सूत्रितं च । तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे दोषो आगात् । आ. ८-१ । इति ॥ अभिप्लवपृष्ठ्यषडहयोर्द्वितीयेऽहनि वैस्वदेवशस्त्रे प्रतिपत्तृचस्यैते एव प्रथमाद्वितीये । सूत्रितं च । तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे आविश्वदेवं । आ. ७-६ । इति ॥ यः सविता देवो नोऽस्माकं धियः कर्माणि धर्मादिविषया वा बुद्दीः प्रचोदयात् प्रेरयेत् तत्तस्य देवस्य सवितुः सर्वांतर्यामितया प्रेरकस्य जगत्सष्टुः परमेश्वरस्य वरेण्यं सर्वैरुपास्यतया ज्ञेयतया च संभजनीयं भर्गोऽविद्यातत्कार्ययोर्भजनाद्भर्गः स्वयंज्योतिः परब्रह्मात्मकं तेजो धीमहि । वयं ध्यायामः । यद्वा । तदिति भर्गोविशेषणं । सवितुर्देवस्य तत्तादृशं भर्गो धीमहि । किं तदित्यपेक्षायामाह । य इति लिंगव्यत्ययः । यद्भर्गो धियः प्रचोदयात् । तद्धायेमेति समन्वयः । यद्वा । यः सविता सूरो धियः कर्माणि प्रचोदयात् प्रेरयति तस्य सवितुः सर्वस्य प्रसवितुर्देवस्य द्योत-

Gist of the bhāṣya

Use: on the sixth day of the Daśarātra, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, the two ṛks beginning तत्सवितुः (tatsavituḥ) are the second and third ṛks of the Pratipat tṛca. It is laid down in the sūtra तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे दोषो आगात् (tatsaviturvareṇyamiti dve doṣo āgāt) (Ā. Sū. 8-1). On the second day of the Abhiplava and Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍahas, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, these same two are the first and second ṛks of the Pratipat tṛca. It is laid down: तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे आविश्वदेवं (tatsaviturvareṇyamiti dve āviśvadevaṃ) (Ā. Sū. 7-6).

Meaning: the god Savitṛ who may impel (प्रचोदयात् (pracodayāt)) our धियः (dhiyaḥ), our rites, or our thoughts concerned with dharma and the like: of that god Savitṛ, the impeller as inner controller of all, the creator of the world, Parameśvara, we meditate on the वरेण्यं (vareṇyaṃ), which is to be resorted to by all as the object of worship and of knowledge, the भर्गः (bhargaḥ). It is called bhargas because it consumes (bhajana) ignorance and its effects; it is self-luminous light, of the nature of the Supreme Brahman. धीमहि (dhīmahi) means "we meditate".

Or else: तत् (tat) is an adjective of भर्गः (bhargaḥ): of the god Savitṛ we meditate on that bhargas of such a kind. If it is asked "what is that?", he answers: यः (yaḥ) here is a change of gender; the bhargas which may impel our thoughts; the construction is "may we meditate on that". Or else: the Savitṛ who is the sun impels धियः (dhiyaḥ), rites; of that Savitṛ, the god who gives birth to all, the shining sun (the sentence continues on the next page) ### Printed p. 556

मानस्य सूरस्य तत्सर्वद्र्दृश्यमानतॆया प्रसिद्धं वरेण्यं सर्वैः संभजनीयं भर्गः पापानां तापकं तेजोमंडलं धीमहि । धैयतया मनसा धारयेम । यद्वा । भर्गःशब्देनान्नमभिधीयते । यः सविता देवो धियः प्रचोदयति तस्य प्रसादाद्भर्गोऽन्नादिलक्षणं फलं धीमहि । धारयामः । तस्याधारभूता भवेमेत्यर्थः । भर्गःशब्द स्यान्नपरत्वे धीशब्दस्य कर्मपरत्वे चाथर्वणं । वेदांश्चंदांसि सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गॊ देवस्य कवयोऽन्नमाहुः कर्माणि धियस्तदु ते प्रब्रवीमि प्रचोदयंत्सविता याभिरेतीति । गो. ब्रा. १-३२ ॥ भर्गः । भ्रष्ट पाके । असुन् । भ्रस्टो रोपधयो रमन्यतरस्यां । पा. ६-४-४७ । इति रोपधयोर्लोपो रमागमः । न्यंक्वादिपाठात् कुत्वं । धीमहि । ध्यायतेर्लिजि बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणं । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । यद्वा । धीज् आधारे । लिजि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । प्रचोदयात् । चोदयतेर्लेट्याडागमः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । आगमस्यानुदात्तत्वे णिचः स्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) … of that sun, the visible, universally known, desirable bhargas, the orb of light that burns up sins, we hold in the mind as the object of meditation.

Or else: the word भर्गः (bhargaḥ) denotes food. Through the grace of the god Savitṛ who impels thoughts, we take up (धीमहि (dhīmahi), we hold) the fruit characterised by food and the like; that is, may we become its support. For भर्गः (bhargaḥ) in the sense of food and धी (dhī) in the sense of rites, the Atharvaṇa text is cited: वेदांश्चंदांसि सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गॊ देवस्य कवयोऽन्नमाहुः कर्माणि धियस्तदु ते प्रब्रवीमि प्रचोदयंत्सविता याभिरेतीति । (vedāṃścaṃdāṃsi saviturvareṇyaṃ bhargò devasya kavayo 'nnamāhuḥ karmāṇi dhiyastadu te prabravīmi pracodayaṃtsavitā yābhiretīti |) (Go. Brā. 1-32)NOTE.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः (yaḥ)—who
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • धियः (dhiyaḥ)—the intelligence concerned with rites
  • प्रचोदयात् (pracodayāt)—impels
  • तत् (tat)—such
  • देवस्य (devasya)—of the god, of divine nature
  • सवितुः (savituḥ)—of Savitṛ
  • वरेण्यं (vareṇyaṃ)—to be worshipped by all
  • भर्गः (bhargaḥ)—the light
  • धीमहि (dhīmahi)—we meditate on
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We meditate on the light, worshipped by the whole world, of such a Savitṛ, the god of divine nature, who impels in us the intelligence concerned with rites.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

We meditate on that desirable light of the divine Savitri, who influences our pious rites.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the sixth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, while the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, this ṛk तत्सवितुः (tatsavituḥ) and the next ṛk देवस्य सवितुः (devasya savituḥ) are to be recited as the second and third ṛks of the Pratipat tṛca (a tṛca is a group of three ṛks). This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे दोषो आगात् (tatsaviturvareṇyamiti dve doṣo āgāt) (Ā. 8-1).

And on the second day of the sacrifices called Abhiplava, Pṛṣṭhya and Ṣaḍaha, while the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, these two ṛks are to be recited as the first and second ṛks of the Pratipat tṛca. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे आ विश्वदेवं (tatsaviturvareṇyamiti dve ā viśvadevaṃ) (Ā. 7-6). ### Printed p. 557 1) Sāyaṇa's explanation of the purport of the mantra तत्सवितुः (tatsavituḥ).

Sāyaṇa has shown that two kinds of meaning are possible for the word सवितृ (savitṛ) in this ṛk, and in accordance with it he has also explained the word भर्ग (bharga).

First, सवितृ (savitṛ) means Parameśvara, the inner controller of all, the impeller of the world, the creator of the world. The meaning of the word भर्ग (bharga) is the radiance that is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman. Because it destroys ignorance and the evil deeds that result from it, this radiance is well known by the apt name भर्ग (bharga). Because it is to be worshipped and revered by all, it has the adjective वरेण्यं (vareṇyaṃ). The word धी (dhī) means intellect. The purport is: let us meditate on this radiance, of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, which destroys ignorance, and may Savitṛ impel us to meditate in that way.

Second, सवितृ (savitṛ) means the sun, famous in the world. The word धी (dhī) means rites in worship of the sun. भर्ग (bharga) means the orb of light of Āditya, which destroys sin. The prayer is: may Savitṛ, the sun, impel us, who meditate on such an orb of light, to be devoted to rites.

Further, if on the authority of the Brāhmaṇa sentence वेदाश्चंदांसि तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गॊ देवस्य कवयोऽन्नमाहुः (vedāścaṃdāṃsi tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargò devasya kavayo 'nnamāhuḥ) (Go. Brā. 1-3-2)NOTE the word भर्ग (bharga) is taken to mean food, the purport becomes: by the grace of that Savitṛ who impels our intellect to be devoted to good rites, let us obtain fruit in the form of food and the like. If the meaning of the word sava�tṛ is shown to differ in this way, does the doctrine (tattva) then differ? Is a difference in the nature of the deity worshipped being stated? Do the words सवितृ (savitṛ), सूर (sūra), आदित्य (āditya), परब्रह्म (parabrahma) show different forms of one and the same principle, or do they show differences of principle as well? Such an inquiry is quite necessary in the present context.

  1. Since the deity Savitṛ conveys the principle, the Gāyatrī is what the word सावित्रि (sāvitri) denotes.

तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं (tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ) is the great Gāyatrī mantra, famous in the world. It has Savitṛ as its deity; for that very reason it is also well known by the name सावित्रि (sāvitri). The Upaniṣad mantra गायत्रि मेव सावित्रीमनुब्रूयात् (gāyatri meva sāvitrīmanubrūyāt) teaches this identity (Bṛ. U. 5-14-5). The word सवितृ (savitṛ) means the Supreme Brahman; that the Supreme Brahman is the deity worshipped in this mantra is the (sentence continues on the next page) ### Printed p. 558 purport of the Upaniṣads. But since there is also room for objections, such as the pūrvapakṣa छंदोऽभिधानान्न (chaṃdo 'bhidhānānna) (Bra. Sū. 1-1-25), which state a meaning contrary to this purport and deny that the Supreme Brahman is the deity worshipped in this mantra, the meaning of this mantra must be examined thoroughly and its profound purport found out. This determination of the purport rests on the meaning of the word सवितृ (savitṛ).

  1. The nature of Savitṛ as expressing the one principle.

It is the view of some among modern scholars that words such as सूर (sūra), सवितृ (savitṛ), आदित्य (āditya) show, in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, the diversity and the distinct kinds of deities.

"Savitri is comparatively a younger member of the Vedic Pantheon; this fact is simply corroborated by the very name of that God. The genesis of सवितृ (savitṛ) indicates cleanly a very last phase in the evolution of Vedic religious thought. The earlier and more important Gods of the Rig-Veda like वरुण (varuṇa), मित्र (mitra) and इंद्र (iṃdra) are mainly the personification of natural phenomena."

In this and similar ways Western scholars such as Oldenberg have expressed their opinion. The meaning is that deities such as Varuṇa, Indra and Mitra are ancient and Savitṛ is a more recent deity. That is, the conception of Savitṛ as a deity came to the ṛṣis who composed the Ṛk-saṃhitā only after a long time; the conception of this deity did not exist at first. The purport is that, having grasped the profundity of the variety of creation, they afterwards developed the conception of a special deity named Savitṛ in order to reflect that principle. Their view is that in this way a difference of name indicates a difference of deity. But careful examination shows that this is not quite the right opinion.

एक एनाग्निर्बहुधा समिद्ध एकः सूरो विश्वमनु प्रभूतः । एकैवोषाः सर्वमिदं वि भात्येकं वा इदं वि बभूव सर्वं ॥ (eka enāgnirbahudhā samiddha ekaḥ sūro viśvamanu prabhūtaḥ | ekaivoṣāḥ sarvamidaṃ vi bhātyekaṃ vā idaṃ vi babhūva sarvaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-58-2).

As this mantra states clearly, the idea that one principle, which impels and nourishes all the affairs of the universe, pervades the universe is indicated, clearly and subtly, in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā.

यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोऽंशसंभवं ॥ (yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā | tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejo 'ṃśasaṃbhavaṃ ‖) (Bha. Gī. 10-41)NOTE ### Printed p. 559 Just as is said in this sentence of the Gītā, the Nirukta authors too have thus stated the nature of the groups of deities described in Vedic literature, and the highest principle that is the source of all deities:

महाभाग्याद्देवताया एक आत्मा बहुधा स्तूयते । .... .... एकस्य आत्मनः अन्ये देवाः प्रत्यंगानि भवंति ॥ (mahābhāgyāddevatāyā eka ātmā bahudhā stūyate | .... .... ekasya ātmanaḥ anye devāḥ pratyaṃgāni bhavaṃti ‖) (Ni. 7-4).

The principle that is the source of all deities is one only. But the infinite qualities of that principle are manifested in infinite forms, and all the diversities are only distinctions of the manifold glory of this principle. The Vedic sentence एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदंति (ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadaṃti) (1-164-46) also conveys this same point. तत्तत् स्थानविभागेन तत्र तत्रेह दृश्यते (tattat sthānavibhāgena tatra tatreha dṛśyate) (Bṛ. De. 1-70): the place and the nature of the action of each indicate the quality of that deity, but the original principle is one.

यो नः पिता जनिता यो विधाता धामानि वेद भुवनानि विश्वा । यो देवानां नामधा एक एव तं संप्रश्नं भुवना यंत्यन्या ॥ (yo naḥ pitā janitā yo vidhātā dhāmāni veda bhuvanāni viśvā | yo devānāṃ nāmadhā eka eva taṃ saṃpraśnaṃ bhuvanā yaṃtyanyā ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-82-3).

Viśvakarman alone, the producer of the whole world, created the many kinds of deities such as Indra and pervaded the whole universe. Because he is the producer of everything, he has also obtained the name Savitṛ. And Prajāpati, the creator, is described as Savitṛ and as Tvaṣṭṛ:

देवस्त्वष्टा सविता विश्वरूपः पुपोष प्रजाः पुरुधा जजान । इमा च विश्वा भुवनान्यस्य महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥ (devastvaṣṭā savitā viśvarūpaḥ pupoṣa prajāḥ purudhā jajāna | imā ca viśvā bhuvanānyasya mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖) (Mu. Saṃ. 3-55 - C.F)NOTE

गर्भे नु नौ जनिता दंपती कर्देवस्त्वष्टा सविता विश्वरूपः । नकिरस्य प्र मिनंति व्रतानि वेद नावस्य पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ (garbhe nu nau janitā daṃpatī kardevastvaṣṭā savitā viśvarūpaḥ | nakirasya pra minaṃti vratāni veda nāvasya pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-10-5).

In all such places Prajāpati, the creator and impeller of the world, is described as showing variety through difference of name and difference of action, while being originally the one principle of all. Therefore the opinion that a separate deity named Savitṛ, of a form different from deities such as Sūra, Āditya, Agni and Indra, exists and is described in embodied form is mistaken. Creation of the world, impelling the world's affairs, regulating those affairs, and all such activities are related to Savitṛ. To establish that this Savitṛ is Āditya, the Supreme Person within Āditya, the Vedic sentences that are the basis of this conclusion have to be examined carefully. ### Printed p. 560 सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता (savitā sarvasya prasavitā) (Ni. 10-31): because he is the producer of everything, the name is Savitṛ. Having shown this etymology of the word, the Nirukta authors cite

सविता यंत्रृः पृथिवीमरम्णादस्कंभने सविता द्यामद्यंहत् । अश्वमिनाधुक्षद्दुनिमंतरिक्षमतूर्ते बद्धं सविता समुद्रं ॥ (savitā yaṃtrṛḥ pṛthivīmaramṇādaskaṃbhane savitā dyāmadyaṃhat | aśvaminādhukṣaddunimaṃtarikṣamatūrte baddhaṃ savitā samudraṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-149-1).

Savitṛ has made the earth supported; he has made the unsupported atmosphere stand firm; and he has made the cloud that spreads over the sky pour rain. Having thus described Savitṛ's greatness, they ask कं अन्यं मध्यमात् एवं अवक्षत् (kaṃ anyaṃ madhyamāt evaṃ avakṣat): leaving aside the deity of the atmosphere, what other deity would the ṛṣi praise in this way? In answer, they state that आदित्योऽपि सवितोच्यते (ādityo 'pi savitocyate), that Savitṛ is also a synonymous name of Āditya. They cite the ṛk

हिरण्यस्तूपः सवितर्यथा त्वांगिरसो जुह्वे वाजे अस्मिन् । एवा त्वार्चन्नवसे वंदमानः सोमस्येवांशुं प्रति जागराहं ॥ (hiraṇyastūpaḥ savitaryathā tvāṃgiraso juhve vāje asmin | evā tvārcannavase vaṃdamānaḥ somasyevāṃśuṃ prati jāgarāhaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-19-5),

show that Āditya has the epithet Savitṛ, and indicate that the words आदित्य (āditya) and सवितृ (savitṛ) are synonymous names.

  1. Description of the divine nature of Savitṛ, the controller of the universe, with the etymology of the word सवितृ (savitṛ).

The root सू (sū), from which the word सवितृ (savitṛ) comes, has different senses: 1) ṣū in the sense of impelling; 2) ṣūṅ in the sense of release of the young from the womb. Words formed from this root are used in the senses of "create", "impel" and "pour out" (oblations and the like). Sāyaṇa has explained the word सवितृ (savitṛ) in all these senses as suits each context. By explaining these meanings he has shown that Savitṛ alone is the controller of the whole world. That Savitṛ is the lord of creation, maintenance and the regulations is evident from the Ṛk-saṃhitā's own descriptions.

तत्सविता वोऽमृतत्वमासुवदगोह्यं यच्छ्रवयंत ऐतन । त्यं चिच्चमसमसुरस्य भक्षणमेकं संतमकृणुता चतुर्वयं ॥ (tatsavitā vo 'mṛtatvamāsuvadagohyaṃ yacchravayaṃta aitana | tyaṃ ciccamasamasurasya bhakṣaṇamekaṃ saṃtamakṛṇutā caturvayaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-110-3).

p. 561

In the Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-110-3) quoted above, the deed of the Ṛbhus, who by Savitṛ's favour made the single cup (camasa) into four, must be taken as relating to the first creation of the world. Turning a state that is immortal and endless into a mortal form, and so making it finite, is the work of creation. This work of making things limited (bounded) belongs to the deity Savitṛ (or Sūra), the controller of the order of the seasons.

In all the passages यः पार्थिवानि विममे स एतशो रजांसि देवः सविता महित्वना । (yaḥ pārthivāni vimame sa etaśo rajāṃsi devaḥ savitā mahitvanā |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-3) and मानेनेव तस्थिना अंतरिक्षे वि यो ममे पृथिवीं सूरेयण । (māneneva tasthinā aṃtarikṣe vi yo mame pṛthivīṃ sūreyaṇa |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-5), the use of the root मा (mā) with the prefix वि (vi) indicates the controlling work of Savitṛ who is of the form of the sun, and of the sun who is of the form of Savitṛ. It was Savitṛ's work to bring the three worlds, which were formless, into a formed shape. As in the Ṛk 1-110-3 quoted above, so in the Atharva-saṃhitā too there is the description चमस यस्मिन् यशो निहितं विश्वरूपं (camasa yasmin yaśo nihitaṃ viśvarūpaṃ) (A. Ve. 10-8-9)NOTE. This description is the very one stated in the Īśāvāsyopaniṣad: हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण सत्यस्यापिहितं मुखं (hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukhaṃ) (Īśa. 15)NOTE. The word पूष (pūṣa) addressed in this mantra of the Īśāvāsya means Sūra (the sun). The prayer here is: "Be the one who opens the face of the true Brahman of the solar orb, hidden by the golden vessel." The Ṛk-saṃhitā describes that the Ṛbhus made the truth, which was covered, imperceptible and beyond the senses, and which in its oneness was formless, into a formed thing, and produced variety so that it might become perceptible to the world. [That in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-161-11 the word ऋभु (ṛbhu) was explained as the sun's rays and the word अगोह्य (agohya) as the sun has been stated earlier, in the special topics of that Ṛk.] The Ṛbhus too, the pupils of Savitṛ who is of the form of the sun (Ai. Brā. 3-30), are the sun's rays. But then everything would be included in the sun alone.

This is like Savitṛ's lordship described in sentences such as वनानि विभ्यो नकिरस्य तानि व्रता देवस्य सवितुर्मिनंति। (vanāni vibhyo nakirasya tāni vratā devasya saviturminaṃti|) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-7) and यस्येंद्रो वरुणो (yasyeṃdro varuṇo) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-9). The lordship of Indra and others is also described by sentences such as एको विश्वस्यभुवनस्य राजा (eko viśvasyabhuvanasya rājā) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-2). Since such descriptions occur for every deity,

p. 562

another question arises: what then is Savitṛ's distinction? In answer, some have expressed the opinion that such a description is only figurative and holds no distinction; Savitṛ, like the other deities, is one of the lesser particular deities. To know Savitṛ's distinction, the nivid mantra relating to Savitṛ must be recited. For example:

न प्रमिये सवितुर्दैव्यस्य तद्यथा विश्वं भुवनं धारयिष्यति । यत्पृथिव्या वरिमन्ना स्वंगुरिर्वर्षन्दिवः सुवति सत्यमस्य तत् ॥ (na pramiye saviturdaivyasya tadyathā viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ dhārayiṣyati | yatpṛthivyā varimannā svaṃgurirvarṣandivaḥ suvati satyamasya tat ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-55-4)

In mantras of this kind Savitṛ's chief quality is described. Here activities such as the regulation of the universe and the protection of truth are indicated. In the same way,

  1. Varuṇa too, the overseer of Ṛta, is nothing but a particular manifestation of Savitṛ's glory.

In passages such as त्रिपंचाशः क्रीळति व्रात एषां देव इव सविता सत्यधर्मा (tripaṃcāśaḥ krīḷati vrāta eṣāṃ deva iva savitā satyadharmā) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-34-8), the protection of truth is shown to be Savitṛ's special quality. जगतः स्थातुरुभयस्य यो वशी (jagataḥ sthāturubhayasya yo vaśī) (4-53-6): Savitṛ is the master of the whole world, moving and unmoving. विश्वस्य हि श्रुष्टये .... .... .... रमते परिज्मन् (viśvasya hi śruṣṭaye .... .... .... ramate parijman) (2-38-2): whether subtle or gross, a thing moves only by his regulation. The Atharvaṇa describes the same in sentences such as देवस्य सवितुः सर्वे कर्म कृण्वंतु मानवाः । (devasya savituḥ sarve karma kṛṇvaṃtu mānavāḥ |) (A. Ve. 6-23-3). All this is like the description of the god Varuṇa, overseer of Ṛta. Therefore it must also be examined whether there is a difference between Savitṛ and Varuṇa; whether they are different deities, or two forms of one principle, or one thing described by different qualities.

If certain Saṃhitā sentences are examined, they appear to state the identity of Varuṇa and Savitṛ. For example, प्र त्वा मुंचामि वरुणस्य पाशाद्येन त्वाबध्नात् सविता सुशेवः । (pra tvā muṃcāmi varuṇasya pāśādyena tvābadhnāt savitā suśevaḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-24): here Varuṇa's noose and Savitṛ's noose are alike. In the commentary Sāyaṇa says that Varuṇa, impelled by Savitṛ, binds the born creatures with his noose. But releasing the person so bound is also Savitṛ's work, or must come about through his grace. That the protection of right conduct, the protection of truth and the regulation of the universe are a common property of Savitṛ and Varuṇa

p. 563

is clear in the passages 2-38-2; 3-33-6; 4-53-4; 10-34-8; 10-139-3 and others where Savitṛ is described, and in the Ṛks 6-70-1; 7-86-1; 8-41-10; 8-42-1 and others where Varuṇa is described. Because he upholds the order of the universe, Savitṛ is also addressed as Mitra: उत रात्रिमुभयतः परीयस उत मित्रो भवसि देव धर्मभिः (uta rātrimubhayataḥ parīyasa uta mitro bhavasi deva dharmabhiḥ) (5-81-4). The purport is that, being lord of the work of sustaining the world, Savitṛ is also famed by the name Mitra. As सर्वस्य प्रसविता (sarvasya prasavitā) (the impeller of all), the act of generation is not Savitṛ's work alone; he is also the cause of the world's continuance. बृहत्सुम्मः प्रसवीता निवेशनो जगतः (bṛhatsummaḥ prasavītā niveśano jagataḥ) and so on (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-53-6): thus Savitṛ's greatness is described.
