rarakṣa | tān | sukṛtaḥ | viśvavedāḥ | dipsaṃtaḥ | it | ripavaḥ | na | aha | debhuḥ‖13‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अत्रेयमैतिहासिकी कथा । उचथ्यस्य गर्भिणीं ममतानामधेयां भार्यां तदनुजो बृहस्पतिरचकमत । तस्यां रेत अधित्सुं तु बृहस्पतिं गर्भस्थं रेतोऽब्रवीत् । रेतोऽत्र मा सैक्षीरहमत्र वसामिति। एवमुक्तो बृहस्पतिर्निरुद्धरेतस्कः सन् रेतोरूपं गर्भं शशाप । जात्यंधत्वरूपं दीर्घं तमः प्राप्नुहीति । ततस्तस्यां दीर्घतमा अजनिष्ठ । स चांध्यपरिहारायाग्निं स्तुत्वा चक्षुरलभतेति। तदिदानीमाह । हे अग्ने पायवो रक्षकाः पश्यंतोऽंधोऽयमिति कृषादृष्टा पश्यंतस्ते तव ये रश्मयो मामतेयं ममतायाः पुत्रमंधं चक्षुर्हिनं दीर्घतमसं दुरितादांध्यलक्षणाच्छापादरक्षणन् चक्षुष्पदानेनापालयन् । विश्वदेवा विश्वप्रज्ञो भवान् सुकृतः शोभनं चक्षुष्पदानादिकर्म कृतवतस्तान्रस्मिन्नरक्ष । आदरेण परिगृह्य पालयति । तेषां परिग्रहसिद्धिरभिधीयते । दिप्पंत इत् दंभितुं परिभवितुमिच्छंत एव रिपवः शत्रव एनं दीर्घतमसं नाह देभुः । नैव परिभवंति खलु ॥ मामतेयं । ममताया अपत्यमित्यर्थॆ स्त्रीभ्यो ढक् । दिप्पंतः । दन्नु दंभे । सनीवंतर्धेत्यादिना इडभावः । दंभ इच्चीतीकारः । देभुः । श्रंथिग्रंथिदंभिष्टंजीनामपसंख्यानमिति लिटः कित्वादुपधालोपः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa first gives the traditional story. Bṛhaspati, the younger brother of Ucathya, desired Ucathya's pregnant wife, named Mamatā. When he wished to deposit his seed in her, the child in the womb told him: "Do not pour seed here; I dwell here." Thus addressed, Bṛhaspati, his seed obstructed, cursed the embryo: "Obtain long darkness in the form of congenital blindness." Then Dīrghatamas was born of her, and to remove his blindness he praised Agni and obtained sight. This is what the verse now says. O Agni, those protectors, your rays, looking on him with the thought "this one is blind," protected Māmateya, the son of Mamatā, blind, that is, Dīrghatamas, from misfortune, that is, from the curse of blindness, by giving him eyes. You, all-knowing, protected those rays that had done good deeds such as the giving of sight, taking them to yourself with regard. The accomplishment of their being so taken is now stated: the enemies, even while wishing to injure and overcome this Dīrghatamas, did not overcome him.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • पायवः (pāyavaḥ)—protecting
  • पश्यंतः (paśyaṃtaḥ)—looking with a gracious eye
  • ते (te)—your
  • ये (ye)—those very rays which
  • मामतेयु (māmateyu)—the son of Mamatā

p. 782

  • अंधं (aṃdhaṃ)—blind Dīrghatamas
  • दुरितात् (duritāt)—from the sin in the form of a curse
  • अरक्षन् (arakṣan)—protected
  • विश्ववेदाः (viśvavedāḥ)—you who are all-knowing
  • सुकृतः (sukṛtaḥ)—having excellent works
  • तान् (tān)—those rays
  • ररक्ष (rarakṣa)—protect
  • दिप्संत इत् (dipsaṃta it)—even though their purpose was destruction
  • रिपवः (ripavaḥ)—enemies
  • नाह देभुः (nāha debhuḥ)—could not harm
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, those rays of yours, protecting and looking with a gracious eye, protected Dīrghatamas, the son of Mamatā and blind, from the sin in the form of a curse. You, the all-knowing, protect those rays that have excellent works. Even though their purpose was destruction, the enemies could not harm him.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Those your protecting ( rays ), Agni, which, beholding (what had chanced), preserved the blind son of Mamata from misfortune : he, knowing all things, cherished those benevolent ( rays ), and his enemies, intending to destroy him, wrought him no harm.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मामतेयं (māmateyaṃ)—Regarding the protection of the son of the woman named Mamatā, the commentator has told a historical story. Mamatā, the wife of the sage named Ucathya, was pregnant. Then Bṛhaspati, the younger brother of Ucathya, saw that woman, was infatuated, became attached to her and had intercourse with her. At the time of the emission of seed, the child who was in the womb said to Bṛhaspati: "O Bṛhaspati, I am now in the womb; therefore do not discharge your seed into this woman's womb." Hearing this, Bṛhaspati became angry with that child in the womb, who had obstructed him at the time of releasing the seed, and pronounced a curse that the child in the womb should be born blind. Therefore the child born of that woman was born blind and became a sage famed by the name Dīrghatamāḥ (since he could not see, it always appeared to him as if it were long darkness, dīrgham tamaḥ). There is the narrative that this sage Dīrghatamāḥ praised Agni and obtained his eyes (sight). That very matter is explained here by the sentence मामतेयं दुरितात् अरक्षन् (māmateyaṃ duritāt arakṣan).

ubhā | śaṃsā | sūdaya | satyatāte | anuṣṭuyā | kṛṇuhi | āhrayāṇa ‖ 14 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अप्रयाण अलज्जितगमन । अप्रयाणोऽह्रीतयान इति यास्कः । तादृश हे अग्ने वयं स्तोतारस्त्वया सधन्यस्वप्रसादात्समानधनास्तोतास्त्वया रक्षिता वयं तव प्रणीती प्रणीत्या तव प्रेरणेनानुज्ञया वाजानन्नान्यश्याम । प्राप्नुयाम । हे सत्यताते । सत्यं तनोतीति ना सत्यं तायते यस्मिन्निति ना सत्यतातिः । हे सत्यताते शंसा पापानां शंसितारावुभावासन्नविप्रकृष्टौ शत्रू सूदय । जहि । अनुष्टुयानुक्रमेण कृणुहि । अस्मिन्सूक्ते प्रतिपादितमर्थं कुरु ॥ सधन्यः । धनमेषामस्तीति छंदसीवनपावितीप्रत्ययः । एरनेकाच इति यण् । उदात्तस्वरितयोरिति स्वरितत्वं । अनुष्टुया । अपदुःसुषु । स्थ इति विधीयमानः कुप्रत्ययो बहुलवचनादनुपूर्वस्यापि भवति । सुपांसुलुगिति तृतीयाया याजादेशः। अह्रयाण । ह्री लच्चायां । बहुलं छंदसीति शपः श्लुभावाभावः । अनित्यमागमशासनमिति मुगभावः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"Apraṇa" (ahrayāṇa) means of unashamed going; "अप्रयाणोऽह्रीतयान इति यास्कः (aprayāṇo 'hrītayāna iti yāskaḥ)" (so Yāska). O such Agni, we, the praisers, being "sadhanya," that is, possessed of equal wealth through your favour, protected by you, may through your guidance (प्रणीती (praṇītī)), your impulse and leave, attain वाजान् (vājān), foods. O सत्यताते (satyatāte): one who extends truth, or one in whom truth is extended. O Satyatāti, destroy the two enemies, near and far, who are the utterers (calumniators) of evils. अनुष्टुया (anuṣṭuyā): in due order, do कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi), that is, accomplish what has been set forth in this hymn.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अह्रयाण (ahrayāṇa)—O Agni, of unhesitating going
  • वयं (vayaṃ)—we, the praisers
  • त्वया (tvayā)—by your favour
  • सधन्यः (sadhanyaḥ)—possessed of excellent wealth
  • त्वोताः (tvotāḥ)—protected by you
  • तव (tava)—your
  • प्रणीती (praṇītī)—by favour
  • वाजान् (vājān)—horsesNOTE
  • आश्याम (āśyāma)—we obtain
  • सत्यताते (satyatāte)—O Agni, who increase truth
  • शंसा (śaṃsā)—desiring sin
  • उभा (ubhā)—both kinds of enemies, the distant and the near
  • सूदय (sūdaya)—destroy
  • अनुष्टुया (anuṣṭuyā)—in order
  • तृणुहि (tṛṇuhi)—fulfil the purpose of our prayer

p. 784

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of unhesitating going, we the praisers, possessed through your favour of excellent wealth and protected by you, obtain horses through your favour. O Agni, who increase truth, whether the enemies who wish us treachery are far away or nearby, destroy them; and fulfil the purpose of our prayer.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Agni, you are freed from shame, by you we are made opulent ; by you we are protected ; may we, through your guidance, attain abundant food: cherisher of truth, destroy both ( sorts of calumniators ), those who are nigh, those who are far off, and in due course fulfil (our desires). #### Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अया ते अग्ने समिधा विधेम प्रति स्तोमं शस्यमानं
गृभाय ।
दहाशसो रक्षसः पाह्यगस्मान्‌द्रुहो निदो मित्रमहो
अवद्यात् ॥ १५ ॥

ayā te agne samidhā vidhema prati stomaṃ śasyamānaṃ
gṛbhāya |
dahāśaso rakṣasaḥ pāhyagasmāndruho nido mitramaho
avadyāt ‖ 15 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अया । ते । अग्ने । संइधा । विधेम । प्रति । स्तोमं । शस्यमानं । गृभाय ।
दह । अशसः । रक्षसः । पाहि । अस्मान् । द्रुहः । निदः । मित्रमहः । अवद्यात् ॥१५॥

ayā | te | agne | saṃidhā | vidhema | prati | stomaṃ | śasyamānaṃ | gṛbhāya |
daha | aśasaḥ | rakṣasaḥ | pāhi | asmān | druhaḥ | nidaḥ | mitramahaḥ | avadyāt ‖15‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे अग्ने अयानया समिधा दीप्या स्तुत्या ते त्वां विधेम । परिचरेम । अस्माभिः शस्यमानमिमं स्तोमं स्तोत्रं प्रति गृभाय । प्रतिगृहाण । अशसः । शंसंति स्तुवंतीति शसः स्तोतारः । ते न भवंतीत्यशसो नृशंसाः । तान्रक्षसो दह ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, with this समिधा (samidhā), this shining praise, we serve you. Accept (गृभाय (gṛbhāya), take) this hymn of praise recited by us. अशसः (aśasaḥ): those who praise are "śasaḥ," praisers; those who are not such are "aśasaḥ," ill-speakers. Burn those rākṣasas.

p. 785

भस्मसात्कुरु । हे मित्रमहो मित्रैः पूजनीय हे अग्ने द्रुहो द्रोग्धुर्निदो निंदकादवद्यात्परिवावाच्चास्मान् पाहि । रक्ष ॥ गृभायॆ । ग्रहेर्लोटि छंदसि शायजपीति श्नः शायच् । हृग्रहोर्भः । पाहि । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः । निदः । णिदि कुत्सायां । क्विप् । आगमशासनस्यानित्यत्वान्नुमभावः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । अवद्यात् । अवद्यपण्येति यत् । ययतोश्चातदर्थे । पा, ६-२-१५६ । इत्यंतोदात्तत्वं । मित्रमहो अवद्यादित्यत्र संहितायामव्यादवद्यादित्येजः प्रकृतिभावः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Reduce them to ashes. O मित्रमहो (mitramaho), worthy of worship by friends, O Agni, protect us from the oppressor (द्रुहः (druhaḥ)), from the reviler (निदः (nidaḥ)), from blame (अवद्यात् (avadyāt)), that is, from reproach.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • अया समिधा (ayā samidhā)—by this shining praise
  • ते (te)—you
  • विधेम (vidhema)—we serve
  • शस्यमानं (śasyamānaṃ)—recited by us
  • इमं स्तोमं (imaṃ stomaṃ)—this hymn of praise
  • प्रति गृभाय (prati gṛbhāya)—accept
  • अशसः (aśasaḥ)—who do not praise you
  • रक्षसः (rakṣasaḥ)—the rākṣasas
  • दह (daha)—burn
  • मित्रमहः (mitramahaḥ)—O Agni, worthy of worship by friends
  • द्रुहः (druhaḥ)—of the treacherous one
  • निदः (nidaḥ)—reviling
  • अवद्यात् (avadyāt)—from reproach
  • अस्मान् (asmān)—us
  • पाहि (pāhi)—protect
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, we serve you with this shining praise. Accept this hymn of praise recited by us. Burn the rākṣasas who do not praise you. O Agni, worthy of worship by friends, protect us from the reviling reproach of the treacherous one.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May we propitiate you, Agni, by this fuel : accept the praise that is recited by us : consume the unadoring Rakshasas ; you who are to be honoured by (your) friends, preserve us from the reproach of the oppressor and the reviler.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अया (ayā)—अनया (anayā). For the convenience of the metre, the middle letter, the na, of the word अनया (anayā) has been dropped, giving अया (ayā). Or else it appears that in that period both the word अनया (anayā) and the word अया (ayā) were current. For the use of the word अया (ayā) in place of अनया (anayā) is frequent in the Ṛgveda. For example: चोदः कुवित्तु तुज्यात्सातये धियः शुचिप्रतीकं तमया धिया गृणे ॥ (codaḥ kuvittu tujyātsātaye dhiyaḥ śucipratīkaṃ tamayā dhiyā gṛṇe ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-143-6)

p. 786

… the Ṛg-Veda also appears to have both forms current. For the use of the word आया (āyā) in place of अया (ayā) is frequent in the Ṛg-Veda. For example:

अया धिया मनवे श्रुष्टिमाव्या साकं नरो दंसनैरा चिकित्सॆरे । (ayā dhiyā manave śruṣṭimāvyā sākaṃ naro daṃsanairā cikitsère |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-166-13)

अयो ते अग्ने विधेमोर्जो नपादश्वमिष्टे । एना सूक्तेन सुजात ॥ (ayo te agne vidhemorjo napādaśvamiṣṭe | enā sūktena sujāta ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-6-2)

In the word आया (āyā) in these Ṛks the letter n has been elided. In the same way, dropping the letter आ (ā) of the word आत्मना (ātmanā) and using it as त्मना (tmanā) is also current in the Ṛg-Veda.

समिधा (samidhā)—The word समित् (samit) ordinarily means something that blazes well, that is burning. In this same sense the word is also used for the dried sticks of certain trees employed for the oblation. But here the Bhāṣyakāra has given the meaning "by a praise that makes the qualities of Agni manifest". In this Ṛk there is room for both meanings, fuel-stick and praise.

अशसः (aśasaḥ)—शंसंति स्तुवंतीति शसः स्तोतारः । ते न भवंतीत्यशसो नृशंसाः । (śaṃsaṃti stuvaṃtīti śasaḥ stotāraḥ | te na bhavaṃtītyaśaso nṛśaṃsāḥ |). The Bhāṣyakāra's explanation is that people who praise the gods are called शसः (śasaḥ), and wicked people who do not praise are called अशसः (aśasaḥ).

The concluding verses of the Bhāṣya and the colophon (Sanskrit, not translated in the Kannada): वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖) इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण, सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये तृतीयाष्टके चतुर्थोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa, sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye tṛtīyāṣṭake caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖) ओं तत्सत् (oṃ tatsat)

Here the fourth adhyāya in the third Aṣṭaka of the Ṛg-Veda Saṃhitā, with the Śrī Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and the Kannada translation, is concluded.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖) शुभं शुभयात् (śubhaṃ śubhayāt) मगळं (magaḷaṃ)

ओं (oṃ) श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः (śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ)

वागीशाद्या सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (vāgīśādyā sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖) यस्य निश्यसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (yasya niśyasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyokhilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖) तृतीयाष्टकमध्यस्थ चतुर्थोऽध्याय आदरात् । व्याख्यातः सायणार्ये ण पंचमो व्याकरिष्यते ॥ (tṛtīyāṣṭakamadhyastha caturtho 'dhyāya ādarāt | vyākhyātaḥ sāyaṇārye ṇa paṃcamo vyākariṣyate ‖) वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖)

Ṛg-Veda Saṃhitā with the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya. The fifth adhyāya in the third Aṣṭaka.

Sūkta 5 (Maṇḍala 4)

Hymns of the Fourth Maṇḍala, 5–18. The fifth hymn.

In this hymn Vaiśvānara Agni is praised. Although we have earlier given extensive explanations about Vaiśvānara Agni many times, here we explain, as Yāska has stated them, the matters Yāska has set out at length in the Nirukta, and the differing opinions of other sages.

p. 788

वैश्वानरः। इति त्रीणि पदानि । वैश्वानरः कस्माद्विश्वान्नरान्नयति । विश्व एनं नरा नयंतीति वा । अपि ना विश्वानर एव स्यात् प्रत्यृतः सर्वाणि भूतानि तस्य वैश्वानरः ॥ (vaiśvānaraḥ| iti trīṇi padāni | vaiśvānaraḥ kasmādviśvānnarānnayati | viśva enaṃ narā nayaṃtīti vā | api nā viśvānara eva syāt pratyṛtaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tasya vaiśvānaraḥ ‖) (Ni. 7-21).

Now we shall explain the word वैश्वानर (vaiśvānara). This word वैश्वानर (vaiśvānara) denotes a deity possessing the meaning of the three words विश्वान् नरान् नयति (viśvān narān nayati). Why did Vaiśvānara get this name? This god विश्वान् नरान् नयति (viśvān narān nayati)—leads all people along the good path; that is, he is the one who sets all people on the good path; therefore this god is named Vaiśvānara.

Or: विश्व एनं नरा नयंतीति (viśva enaṃ narā nayaṃtīti)—all people carry this god in the sacrifices they perform to the northern altar. That is, when performing the rite called Agni-praṇayana in sacrifices, they take Agni, churned and produced at the place of its origin, according to rule to the northern altar and establish it there. Or, all people take Agni to their own houses and establish it in places such as the great kitchen for the work of cooking; therefore this Agni is called Vaiśvānara. Or Viśvānara himself is Vaiśvānara. This Viśvānara pervades the bodies of all creatures, dwells there in the form of the digestive fire and digests the food and the like that creatures eat. Therefore the Viśvānara in the bodies of all creatures is Vaiśvānara Agni. NOTE

वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम राजा हिकं भुवनानामभि श्रीः । इतो जातो विश्वमिदं विचष्टे वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण ॥ (vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma rājā hikaṃ bhuvanānāmabhi śrīḥ | ito jāto viśvamidaṃ vicaṣṭe vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-98-1).

This Ṛk praises Vaiśvānara Agni: may we become worthy of the favourable mind of Vaiśvānara Agni. For this Vaiśvānara Agni is a king, and a king is the support of all worlds. Born in this world, he looks upon the whole universe; together with the sun he pervades everything. This is the main purport of the Ṛk.

Who is Vaiśvānara Agni? Is he a deity of the middle region?

इतो जातः सर्वमिदनुभिविपश्यति वैश्वानरः संयतते सूर्येण राजा यः सर्वेषां भूतानामभिश्रयणीयस्तस्य वयं वैश्वानरस्य कल्याण्यां मत् स्यामेति । तत्को वैश्वानरः । मध्यम इत्याचार्याः ॥ (ito jātaḥ sarvamidanubhivipaśyati vaiśvānaraḥ saṃyatate sūryeṇa rājā yaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmabhiśrayaṇīyastasya vayaṃ vaiśvānarasya kalyāṇyāṃ mat syāmeti | tatko vaiśvānaraḥ | madhyama ityācāryāḥ ‖) (Ni. 7-22).

This is the explanation of the Ṛk. This Vaiśvānara Agni, born in this very world, is able to see the whole universe; together with the sun he pervades the whole universe. May we become worthy of the best mind, that is, the favour, of such a Vaiśvānara Agni. He is the king and the support of all created beings.

p. 789

But who is this Vaiśvānara? What is his nature? Some teachers say that Vaiśvānara is a deity dwelling in the middle region (the atmosphere), because their view is that this Vaiśvānara is the cause of rain. Therefore a Ṛk describing the part this Vaiśvānara plays in the rain-rite is cited here:

प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचंते । वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वा अधूनोत्कृष्टा अन शंबरं भेत् ॥ (pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacaṃte | vaiśvānaro dasyumagnirjaghanvā adhūnotkṛṣṭā ana śaṃbaraṃ bhet ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6).

I shall describe in particular the greatness of this Vaiśvānara Agni, the giver of what is desired. Many people serve with devotion this Vaiśvānara Agni, the slayer of Vṛtra. This Vaiśvānara Agni destroyed Vṛtra the Dasyu. He split (killed) Śambara (the cloud) and made the waters stored in the clouds fall on the earth as rain. This is the main purport of the Ṛk.

This is Yāska's explanation NOTE:

प्रब्रवीमि तन्महित्वं माहाभाग्यं वृषभस्य वर्षितुरपां यं पूरवः पूरयि तव्या मनुष्या वृत्रहणं मेघहनं सचंते सेवंते वर्षकामाः । दस्युर्दस्यतेः क्षयार्थादुपदस्यंत्यस्मिन्न्रसा उपदासयति कर्माणि तमग्निर्वैश्वा नरो घ्नन्नवादूनोदपः काष्ठा अभिनच्छंबरं मेघं ॥ (prabravīmi tanmahitvaṃ māhābhāgyaṃ vṛṣabhasya varṣiturapāṃ yaṃ pūravaḥ pūrayi tavyā manuṣyā vṛtrahaṇaṃ meghahanaṃ sacaṃte sevaṃte varṣakāmāḥ | dasyurdasyateḥ kṣayārthādupadasyaṃtyasminnrasā upadāsayati karmāṇi tamagnirvaiśvā naro ghnannavādūnodapaḥ kāṣṭhā abhinacchaṃbaraṃ meghaṃ ‖) (Ni. 7-23).

So it stands. I shall describe in a special manner the great majesty (the surpassing power) of this Vaiśvānara Agni who pours down rain-water. People who desire what they wish for and who long for rain serve with reverence, with praises and the like, this Vaiśvānara Agni who destroys Vṛtra (the cloud). The word दस्यु (dasyu), formed from the root दस् (das) "to destroy", denotes a wicked one who prevents the water from falling on the earth and ruins it. Vaiśvānara Agni struck such a Dasyu, Śambara (the cloud; the word शंबर (śaṃbara) is read among the names of the cloud), scattered the waters collected in the cloud and made them fall on the earth as rain. This is the main purport.

The view of the earlier Yājñikas that Vaiśvānara is Āditya (objections and answers on this point)

अथासावादित्य इति पूर्वे याज्ञिकाः । एषां लोकानां रोहेण सवनानां रोह आम्मातो रोहात् प्रत्यवरोहश्चिकीर्षितस्तामनुकृतिं होताग्नि- मारुते शस्त्रे वैश्वानरीयेण सूक्तेन प्रतिपद्यते सोऽपि न स्तोत्रियमाद्रियेताग्नेयो हि भवति । तत आगच्छति मध्यस्थाना देवता रुद्रं च मरुतश्च ततोऽग्निमिहस्थानमत्रवै स्तोत्रियं शंसति. (athāsāvāditya iti pūrve yājñikāḥ | eṣāṃ lokānāṃ roheṇa savanānāṃ roha āmmāto rohāt pratyavarohaścikīrṣitastāmanukṛtiṃ hotāgni- mārute śastre vaiśvānarīyeṇa sūktena pratipadyate so 'pi na stotriyamādriyetāgneyo hi bhavati | tata āgacchati madhyasthānā devatā rudraṃ ca marutaśca tato 'gnimihasthānamatravai stotriyaṃ śaṃsati.) (Ni. 7-23).

p. 790

Certain earlier teachers, skilled in the performance of sacrifices, say that this Āditya visible to our eyes is Vaiśvānara. They give the reason thus. In sacrificial rites such as the morning pressing there is an order of rohā and avaroha, that is, ascent and descent. In the worlds also it is so: the earth (the lower region), the atmosphere (the middle region), heaven (the celestial region). Likewise in the pressings there are three: the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing. In sacrifices the Hotṛ at the morning pressing invokes and praises the deities of the earth region, at the midday pressing the deities of the middle region, and at the third pressing the deities of the celestial region (heaven). This is the order of ascent. After the ascent comes the order of descent: first the deities of the celestial region, then those of the middle region, then those of the earth region are praised in order. This is the order of descent. In the order of descent they praise first Vaiśvānara Agni with the hymn वैश्वानराय पृथुपाजसे (vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-1), then the middle-region deities Rudra and the Maruts with the hymn आते पितर्मरुतां (āte pitarmarutāṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23-1), then Agni, the deity of the earth region, with the hymn यज्ञायज्ञा वो अग्नये (yajñāyajñā vo agnaye) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-1). Since in the order of descent the praise of Vaiśvānara Agni comes first, and since Āditya is a deity of the celestial region, this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya. This is their line of argument.

अथापि वैश्वानरीयो द्वादशकपालो भवत्येतस्य हि द्वादशविधं कर्म । (athāpi vaiśvānarīyo dvādaśakapālo bhavatyetasya hi dvādaśavidhaṃ karma |).

Moreover, to Vaiśvānara Agni an oblation of twelve potsherds is always offered; and for Āditya also, आदित्यं द्वादशकपालं (ādityaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ), the offering of twelve potsherds is prescribed. Just as for Āditya an offering in twelve parts, indicating the twelve months, is prescribed, so it is for Vaiśvānara Agni; therefore this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya.

अथापि ब्राह्मणं भवत्यसौ ना आदित्योऽग्निर्वैश्वानरः ॥ (athāpi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavatyasau nā ādityo 'gnirvaiśvānaraḥ ‖).

Moreover, there is also a Brāhmaṇa statement that this Āditya is Vaiśvānara Agni.

अथापि निवित् सौर्यवैश्वानरी भवत्या यो द्यां भात्या पृथिवीमित्येष हि द्यानापृथिव्यानाभासयति । (athāpi nivit sauryavaiśvānarī bhavatyā yo dyāṃ bhātyā pṛthivīmityeṣa hi dyānāpṛthivyānābhāsayati |)

p. 791

A nivid mantra is a particular mantra that praises one deity, praising that deity's distinction in the midst of the śastra mantras; it is a separate mantra inserted and recited among the śastra mantras. Here, when the nivid mantras addressed to Āditya are recited, the Saurya-Vaiśvānarī mantra is recited; that is, that nivid mantra praises both the sun and Vaiśvānara Agni (sings the qualities of those deities). That mantra begins आ यो द्यां भात्या प्रथिवीं (ā yo dyāṃ bhātyā prathivīṃ) and means "who lights heaven and earth with his own light". The one who lights heaven and earth with his own light is Āditya; therefore Vaiśvānara Agni, as taught in this mantra, is Āditya too.

अथापि छांदोमिकं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवति दिवि पृष्ठो अरोचत इत्येष हि दिवि पृष्ठो अरोचतेति । (athāpi chāṃdomikaṃ sūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavati divi pṛṣṭho arocata ityeṣa hi divi pṛṣṭho arocateti |).

And the Chāndomika hymn दिवि पृष्ठो अरोचत (divi pṛṣṭho arocata) (Vā. Saṃ. 33-92) has the sun-and-Vaiśvānara as its deity. In it it is said that he shines on the back (the lower part) of heaven. One who shines in heaven is Āditya. Since Vaiśvānara is praised in this very hymn, this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya.

अथापि हविष्वांतीयं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवति (athāpi haviṣvāṃtīyaṃ sūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavati).

And the hymn हविष्वांतमजरं (haviṣvāṃtamajaraṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-1), called Haviṣvantīya (the hymn recited at the time of drinking the oblation), has the sun and Vaiśvānara Agni as its deities; that is, this hymn is addressed to Saurya-Vaiśvānara Agni. In the Ṛk of this hymn

विश्वस्था अग्निं भुवनाय देवा वैश्वानरं केतुमह्नामकृण्वन् । (viśvasthā agniṃ bhuvanāya devā vaiśvānaraṃ ketumahnāmakṛṇvan |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-2)

it is said that the gods appointed this Vaiśvānara Agni to produce the ahas (days, daytimes), in order to give light to the whole world. Since it is the sun who produces the days, and since this Vaiśvānara Agni too has the power to produce days, Vaiśvānara Agni and Āditya are one person; that is, this Vaiśvānara Agni is Āditya. All this is the view of the earlier teachers, the Yājñikas.

The view of Śākapūṇi that Vaiśvānara is the earthly Agni (not Āditya) (objections and answers on this point)

अयमेवाग्निर्वैश्वानर इति शाकपूणिः । विश्वानरावेते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी वैश्वानरोऽयं यत्ताभ्यां जायते । कथं नृयमेताभ्यां जायत इति यत्र वैद्युतः शरणमभिहंति यावदनुपात्तो भवति मध्यमधर्मैव तावद्भवत्युदकेंधनः शरीरोपशमन उपादीयमान एवायं संपद्यत उदकोपशमनः शरीरदीप्तिः ॥ (ayamevāgnirvaiśvānara iti śākapūṇiḥ | viśvānarāvete uttare jyotiṣī vaiśvānaro 'yaṃ yattābhyāṃ jāyate | kathaṃ nṛyametābhyāṃ jāyata iti yatra vaidyutaḥ śaraṇamabhihaṃti yāvadanupātto bhavati madhyamadharmaiva tāvadbhavatyudakeṃdhanaḥ śarīropaśamana upādīyamāna evāyaṃ saṃpadyata udakopaśamanaḥ śarīradīptiḥ ‖)

p. 792

The view of the teacher called Śākapūṇi is that this earthly Agni is Vaiśvānara Agni. For the earthly Agni arises from two lights (viśvānara fires): the light of Āditya in the celestial region and the lightning light in the middle region. Therefore the fire born of the viśvānara fires is called Vaiśvānara Agni; that is, the earthly Agni is Vaiśvānara Agni. How the earthly Agni arises from the two lights, the light of Āditya and the light of lightning, they now explain. The light of Āditya, which undergoes no change in place or nature, is called the first quality. That is, this light of Āditya, staying where it is, draws up by its rays the waters of oceans and other reservoirs and turns those waters into clouds. This is the work of the first light. Next the lightning fire is called the second. The nature of this lightning fire is the "middle quality", that is, different. This lightning fire has the nature of moving in the midst of the waters (the clouds) and of striking and destroying trees, houses and the like on which people depend; that is, because this lightning fire is able to move in water, it cannot be quenched by water (as ordinary fire is quenched). And ordinary fire, kindled by trees, wood and the like, begins to blaze; but when the lightning fire touches trees and the like, it is quenched there itself, that is, its force ends right there; it does not grow from trees and the like. And this lightning fire cannot be held with the hands and the like. This is the nature of the lightning fire. But the nature of the earthly (ordinary) fire is quite the opposite: the earthly fire can be increased by wood and the like, quenched by water, and held with the hands. These are the natural qualities of the earthly fire.

An explanation is necessary on how the earthly Agni arises from the two lights, that of the celestial region and that of the middle region. Āditya, the light of the celestial region, attracts by his rays the waters of oceans and other reservoirs and turns them into clouds; when the lightning fire that appears in those clouds touches trees and the like, the earthly fire arises and burns. This is well known in the world. Therefore it is explained here that the earthly Agni arises from both lights, that of the celestial region and that of the middle region. Hence the earthly Agni, born of the two lights that are viśvānara fires, is called Vaiśvānara Agni.

अथादित्यादुदीचीप्रथमसमावृत्त आदित्ये कंसं वा मणिं वा परिमृज्य प्रतिस्वरे यत्र शुष्कगोमयमसंस्पर्शयन् धारयति यत् प्रदीप्यते सोऽयमेव संपद्यते । (athādityādudīcīprathamasamāvṛtta āditye kaṃsaṃ vā maṇiṃ vā parimṛjya pratisvare yatra śuṣkagomayamasaṃsparśayan dhārayati yat pradīpyate so 'yameva saṃpadyate |)

p. 793

They give another example of the earthly fire arising from Āditya. When the sun has come in the atmosphere facing the northern direction, that is, at midday, when he is very hot, if one holds a well-shining copper plate or a mirror facing the sun and makes its rays converge (gather together) and fall on a powder of dry cow-dung placed on the ground, fire at once catches. This too is an example showing that the earthly fire arises from Āditya.

अथाप्याह—वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण—न च पुनरात्मनात्मा संयततेऽन्येन्नैवान्यः संयतत इति इममादधात्यमुतोऽमुष्य रश्मयः प्रादुर्भवंतीतोऽस्यार्चिषस्तयोर्भासोः संसंगं दृष्ट्वावमवक्ष्यत् । (athāpyāha—vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa—na ca punarātmanātmā saṃyatate 'nyennaivānyaḥ saṃyatata iti imamādadhātyamuto 'muṣya raśmayaḥ prādurbhavaṃtīto 'syārciṣastayorbhāsoḥ saṃsaṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvāvamavakṣyat |)

In the example given before, in the sentence वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण (vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa), the seer, the beholder of the mantra, has said that Vaiśvānara Agni, joined with the sun, spreads, that is, pervades everything. Since the sun's position does not change, it is impossible that the sun goes forward from his place with Vaiśvānara Agni and pervades. A thing can be in one place at one time, but it cannot be there and also go forward. Only if another thing joins it can it pervade another place. Therefore here the sun is one and Vaiśvānara Agni another; the two together are able to pervade everything. Here the earthly fire is kindled right here (on the earth). The light of Āditya, setting out from the celestial world by way of the rays, meets the earthly fire on the earth. That is, the light of the sun and the light of Agni join as one and that light spreads everywhere by the rays; it is with this thought in mind that the seer, the beholder of the mantra, spoke the sentence वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण (vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa).

अथ यान्येतान्यौत्तमिकानि सूक्तानि भागानि ना सावित्राणि ना सौर्याणि वा पौष्णानि वा वैष्णवानि वा वैश्वदेन्यानि वा तेषु वैश्वानरीयाः प्रवादा अभविष्यन्नादित्यकर्मणा जैनमस्तोष्यन्नित्युदेषीत्यस्तमेषीति विपर्येषीति ॥ आ (atha yānyetānyauttamikāni sūktāni bhāgāni nā sāvitrāṇi nā sauryāṇi vā pauṣṇāni vā vaiṣṇavāni vā vaiśvadenyāni vā teṣu vaiśvānarīyāḥ pravādā abhaviṣyannādityakarmaṇā jainamastoṣyannityudeṣītyastameṣīti viparyeṣīti ‖ ā) आग्नेयेष्टेव हि सूक्तेषु वैश्वानरीयाः प्रवादा भवंति । अग्निकर्माणा चैनं स्तौतीति वहसीति पचसीति दहसीति ॥ (āgneyeṣṭeva hi sūkteṣu vaiśvānarīyāḥ pravādā bhavaṃti | agnikarmāṇā cainaṃ stautīti vahasīti pacasīti dahasīti ‖)

If Vaiselvānara were Āditya, then in the hymns or Ṛks relating to Āditya or Savitṛ, or in the hymns in which Sūrya, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu or the Viśve-devas are the subjects, the qualities and distinctions pertaining to Āditya would be attributed to Vaiśvānara Agni, that is (as is said of the sun) "you rise, you set, you travel in the atmosphere", and so on in the sense …

p. 794

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

…they ought to have been praised by signifying sentences and the like. But it is not so. Only in the hymns that concern Agni are the sentences describing Agni's qualities and functions, such as carrying the oblation, cooking and burning, said in a way that applies also to Vaiśvānara-Agni. That is, Agni's own qualities are applied to Vaiśvānara-Agni and described. Therefore Vaiśvānara-Agni is the terrestrial fire and not Āditya.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यथो एतद्वर्षकर्मणा ह्येनं स्तोतीत्यस्मिन्नप्येतदुपपद्यते । समानमेतदुदकमुच्चैत्यव चाहभिः । भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नयः ॥

yatho etadvarṣakarmaṇā hyenaṃ stotītyasminnapyetadupapadyate | samānametadudakamuccaityava cāhabhiḥ | bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvaṃti divaṃ jinvaṃtyagnayaḥ ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Yāska says that this, too, holds in the case of the one who is praised through the rain-action (the rain-work). The water is common to both: it goes up and, by the days, comes down again (े । समानमेतदुदकमुच्चैत्यव चाहभिः । भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नयः ॥ (e | samānametadudakamuccaityava cāhabhiḥ | bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvaṃti divaṃ jinvaṃtyagnayaḥ ‖)). He then cites the Ṛk: the Parjanyas quicken the earth, the fires quicken heaven. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-51)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

इति सा निगदव्याख्याता ॥

iti sā nigadavyākhyātā ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Yāska says that this Ṛk is "nigada-explained" NOTE. (Ni. 7-23)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

There are mantras that praise this Vaiśvānara-Agni as the one who impels the rain-action. Since Āditya is the impeller of the rain-action, Vaiśvānara-Agni would also possess Āditya's qualities; so can one not say that Vaiśvānara-Agni is Āditya himself? No, it is not so. As the days come again and again after the night has passed, so the waters come again and again from the earth up to the atmosphere and from the atmosphere to the earth. So the waters and the days have a common property. Therefore the deity Parjanya satisfies the earth with rain-water, and the fires satisfy heaven. How Agni satisfies heaven: the oblations and the like that the sacrificers offer into Agni in the sacrifice take, in subtle form, that is in the form of smoke, a shape fit for the gods, and bring satisfaction to the gods; the gods, being pleased, bring satisfaction to the dwellers of the earth through rain. Moreover, according to the sentence अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते (agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate), the oblation offered into Agni gladdens Āditya who is in heaven; so Agni satisfies heaven or Āditya. Rain became the means of mutual help from the earth to heaven and from heaven to the earth. For these reasons Agni, or Vaiśvānara-Agni, is praised as the cause of the rain-action; it does not follow clearly from this that Vaiśvānara is Āditya himself. Since the meaning of this Ṛk is clear, no further explanation is needed.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

कृष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत्पतंति । त आववृत्रन्तदनादृतस्यादिद्भृतेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते ॥

kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divamutpataṃti | ta āvavṛtrantadanādṛtasyādidbhṛtena pṛthivī vyudyate ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa cites the Ṛk without a gloss of his own. It says: the bay, fair-winged ones, clothing themselves in the waters, fly up to heaven towards the dark course; they turned back from the seat of ṛta, and then the earth is wetted with ghṛta (water). (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-47)

p. 795

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

कृष्णं निरयणं रात्रिरादित्यस्य हरयः सुपर्णा हरणा आदित्यरश्मयस्ते यदामुतोऽर्वांचः पर्यावर्तंते सहस्थानादुदकस्यादित्यादथ धृतेनोदकेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते धृतमित्युदकनाम जिघर्तॆः सिंचतिकर्मणः ॥

kṛṣṇaṃ nirayaṇaṃ rātrirādityasya harayaḥ suparṇā haraṇā ādityaraśmayaste yadāmuto 'rvāṃcaḥ paryāvartaṃte sahasthānādudakasyādityādatha dhṛtenodakena pṛthivī vyudyate dhṛtamityudakanāma jighartèḥ siṃcatikarmaṇaḥ ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Yāska explains the verse. The dark course (niyāna, niraya) is the night of Āditya. The bay, fair-winged ones (hari, suparṇa) are the bearers, the rays of Āditya. When they turn back from there, from the common seat of the water, Āditya, then the earth is wetted with ghṛta, i.e. water. dhṛtam is a name of water, from the root जिघर्ति (jigharti), which has the sense of sprinkling. (Ni. 7-24)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The rays, which carry water and have an excellent motion, cover with water the dark cloud (or the night) of fixed course; that is, joined with water they spread upward towards heaven. Again they return from Āditya, the seat of the water. At once the earth is wetted (soaked) with water. Here niraya·ṇa may be said to mean a course of movement; the ordinary meaning of this word is a path of exit. Āditya has two courses of movement, one dark in colour and one bright. The dark course may be understood as the night or as the southern course (dakṣiṇāyana); or the movement of the southern course may itself be called Āditya's night-movement. Durgācārya wrote the following explanation of the above Nirukta sentence—

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

नियानं निरयणं निर्गतिः (निर्याति) निर्गच्छंत्येतदिति नियानं वर्त्म पंथाः। तच्च पुनरेतत् । रात्रि आदित्यस्य । द्वे ह्यस्यायने शुक्लं चोत्तरं कृष्णं च दक्षिणं । सा हि दैवीरात्रिरभिप्रेता । ततो ब्रवीति रात्रिरादित्यस्य ज्योतिषः । स एष भगवानादित्यो यदा जगदनुग्रहाय गर्भमुदकमात्मन्याधित्सुरुत्त रायणं प्रतिपद्यते तदैते हरयः रसहरणाः सुपर्णास्तस्य रश्मयः सर्वस्मादस्माल्लोकादपोवसानाः आत्मन्याच्छादयंतः आददानाः दिवं द्योतनवंतमेतमादित्यं प्रत्युत्पतंति ।

niyānaṃ nirayaṇaṃ nirgatiḥ (niryāti) nirgacchaṃtyetaditi niyānaṃ vartma paṃthāḥ| tacca punaretat | rātri ādityasya | dve hyasyāyane śuklaṃ cottaraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca dakṣiṇaṃ | sā hi daivīrātrirabhipretā | tato bravīti rātrirādityasya jyotiṣaḥ | sa eṣa bhagavānādityo yadā jagadanugrahāya garbhamudakamātmanyādhitsurutta rāyaṇaṃ pratipadyate tadaite harayaḥ rasaharaṇāḥ suparṇāstasya raśmayaḥ sarvasmādasmāllokādapovasānāḥ ātmanyācchādayaṃtaḥ ādadānāḥ divaṃ dyotanavaṃtametamādityaṃ pratyutpataṃti |

Gist of the bhāṣya

Durga says: niyāna is going out; it is the way, the path. That is the night of Āditya. For he has two courses, the bright northern and the dark southern; the southern is the intended divine night; therefore the text says "the night of Āditya's light". When the venerable Āditya, wishing for the good of the world to place the embryo, water, in himself, enters the northern course, then these bay ones, the carriers of sap, the fair-winged, his rays, covering themselves with the waters from this whole world, taking them, fly up towards the shining Āditya. (Nirukta-vyākhyā 7-24)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Āditya's course is of two kinds: one belongs to the northern course and the other to the southern. One is called bright and the other dark. Here "night" is a synonym for the dark course. कृष्णं नियानं नियमनं रात्रिः । देवानां हि रात्रिर्दक्षिणायनं । (kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ niyamanaṃ rātriḥ | devānāṃ hi rātrirdakṣiṇāyanaṃ |) "In that" means in that rainy season. The night-time of the gods is called the southern course. When Āditya follows the course of the northern course, all his rays spread through the world, gather water from every region, and join Āditya again at the right time of this night. This is the rainy season; in this season the rain pours down in plenty. धृत (dhṛta) is a name for water; the word ghṛta is formed from the root जिघर्ति (jigharti), "to sprinkle".

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अथापि ब्राह्मणं भवत्यग्निर्वा इतो वृष्टिं समीरयति धामच्छदिति खलु भूत्वा वर्षति मरुतः सृष्टां वृष्टिं नयंति । यदा खलु वासानादित्योग्निं रश्मिभिः पर्यावर्ततेऽथ वर्षतीति ।

athāpi brāhmaṇaṃ bhavatyagnirvā ito vṛṣṭiṃ samīrayati dhāmacchaditi khalu bhūtvā varṣati marutaḥ sṛṣṭāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ nayaṃti | yadā khalu vāsānādityogniṃ raśmibhiḥ paryāvartate 'tha varṣatīti |

Gist of the bhāṣya

There is also a Brāhmaṇa: Agni sends the rain from here; having become "dhāmacchad" he rains; the Maruts lead the released rain. When Āditya, clothing himself, turns Agni about with his rays, then it rains. NOTE

p. 796

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यथो एतद्रोहात् प्रत्यवरोहश्तिकीर्षित इत्याम्नायवचनादेतद्भवति । यथो एतद्वैश्वानरीयो द्वादशकपालो भवतीत्यनिर्वचनं कपालानि भवंत्यस्ति हि सौर्य एककपालः पंचकपालश्च । यथो एतद्ब्राह्मणं भवतीति-बहुभक्तिवादीनि हि ब्राह्मणानि भवंति-पृथिवी वैश्वानरः संवत्सरो वैश्वानरो ब्राह्मणो वैश्वानर इति ॥

yatho etadrohāt pratyavarohaśtikīrṣita ityāmnāyavacanādetadbhavati | yatho etadvaiśvānarīyo dvādaśakapālo bhavatītyanirvacanaṃ kapālāni bhavaṃtyasti hi saurya ekakapālaḥ paṃcakapālaśca | yatho etadbrāhmaṇaṃ bhavatīti-bahubhaktivādīni hi brāhmaṇāni bhavaṃti-pṛthivī vaiśvānaraḥ saṃvatsaro vaiśvānaro brāhmaṇo vaiśvānara iti ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa (Yāska) adds that this also follows from the Āmnāya statement about ascent and descent NOTE. The statement that the Vaiśvānarīya has twelve potsherds is no explanation; potsherds belong to the offering, and there is also a Saurya offering with one potsherd and one with five. And as to the Brāhmaṇa statement: Brāhmaṇas speak with many figurative ascriptions; "the earth is Vaiśvānara, the year is Vaiśvānara, the Brāhmaṇa is Vaiśvānara". (Ni. 7-24)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Besides this, many Brāhmaṇa sentences also support this meaning. For example, there is the Brāhmaṇa sentence "Agni sends the rain from this world": अग्नेवै धूमो जायते, धूमादभ्रं, अभ्रात् वृष्टिरिति ह विज्ञायते (agnevai dhūmo jāyate, dhūmādabhraṃ, abhrāt vṛṣṭiriti ha vijñāyate)—smoke arises from Agni; from the smoke the cloud and from the cloud the rain; so it is to be understood. Or, when this Āditya makes Agni turn back with his rays, rain comes. Or, by the order of ascent and descent, that is, the oblation offered into Agni reaches, as subtle smoke, the gods in heaven, they are satisfied, and from that the rain-action comes about: for saying this there is no other support than the Brāhmaṇa sentence. The statement that the offering for Vaiśvānara-Agni is of twelve potsherds and that for Sūrya of one potsherd or five is not connected with this matter; it belongs only to the acts that are parts of the sacrifice. In some other Brāhmaṇa sentences, पृथिवी वैश्वानरः (pṛthivī vaiśvānaraḥ) and so on, it is said that the earth is Vaiśvānara, the year is Vaiśvānara, the Brāhmaṇa is Vaiśvānara; that is right. But in this context it does not mean that the deities such as the earth are Vaiśvānara-Agni; these are praising sentences, spoken to describe Vaiśvānara's qualities, saying that Vaiśvānara has the qualities of deities such as the earth.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यथो एतन्निवित्सौर्यवैश्वानरी भवतीत्यस्यैव सा भवति—यो विड्भो मानुषीभ्यो दीदेत्-इत्येष हि विड्भो मानुषीभ्यो दीप्यते । यथो एतच्छांदोमिकं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवतीत्यस्यैवैतद्भवति जमदग्निभिराहुत इति। जमदग्नयः प्रजमिताग्नयो वा प्रज्वलिताग्नयो ना तैरभिहुतो भवति ॥

yatho etannivitsauryavaiśvānarī bhavatītyasyaiva sā bhavati—yo viḍbho mānuṣībhyo dīdet-ityeṣa hi viḍbho mānuṣībhyo dīpyate | yatho etacchāṃdomikaṃ sūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavatītyasyaivaitadbhavati jamadagnibhirāhuta iti| jamadagnayaḥ prajamitāgnayo vā prajvalitāgnayo nā tairabhihuto bhavati ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Saurya-Vaiśvānarī nivid belongs to him (Agni): "he who shines for the human clans"; for he shines for the human clans. And the Chandomika hymn that is Saurya-Vaiśvānara, "invoked by the Jamadagnis", also belongs to him. The Jamadagnis are kindled fires, or blazing fires; by them he is invoked NOTE. (Ni. 7-24)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

There is a nivid-hymn that praises Sūrya and Vaiśvānara. This hymn is recited in the Āgnimāruta-śastra.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अग्निर्वैश्वानरः सोमस्य मत्सत् । विश्वेषां देवानां समित् । अजस्रं दैवं ज्योतिः । यो विड्भ्यो मानुषीभ्यो दीदेत् । द्युषु पूर्वासु दिद्युतानः । अजर उषसामनीके । आ यो द्यां भात्या पृथिवीं । और्वमुत-

agnirvaiśvānaraḥ somasya matsat | viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ samit | ajasraṃ daivaṃ jyotiḥ | yo viḍbhyo mānuṣībhyo dīdet | dyuṣu pūrvāsu didyutānaḥ | ajara uṣasāmanīke | ā yo dyāṃ bhātyā pṛthivīṃ | aurvamuta-

Gist of the bhāṣya

The text of the hymn begins: Agni Vaiśvānara, may he rejoice in the Soma; the sāmidhenī of all the gods; unceasing divine light; he who shines for the human clans; shining in the former days; ageless at the front of the dawns; who shines upon heaven and earth… (continued on the next page).

p. 797

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

रिक्षं । ज्योतिषा यज्ञाय शर्म संयत् । अग्निर्वैश्वानर इह श्रवदिह सोमस्य मत्सत् । प्रेमां देवो देवहूतिमवतु देव्या धिया । प्रेदं ब्रह्म प्रेदं क्षत्रं । प्रेमं सुन्वंतं यजमानमवतु । चित्रश्चित्ताभिरूतिभिः। श्रवद्ब्रह्मण्यवसागमत् ॥

rikṣaṃ | jyotiṣā yajñāya śarma saṃyat | agnirvaiśvānara iha śravadiha somasya matsat | premāṃ devo devahūtimavatu devyā dhiyā | predaṃ brahma predaṃ kṣatraṃ | premaṃ sunvaṃtaṃ yajamānamavatu | citraścittābhirūtibhiḥ| śravadbrahmaṇyavasāgamat ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn continues: the wide atmosphere; with his light he gives shelter to the sacrifice; may Agni Vaiśvānara hear here and rejoice in the Soma; may the god favour this invocation of the gods with his divine thought; this prayer, this lordly power; may he favour the sacrificer who presses the Soma; wondrous with wondrous helps, may he come hearing the prayer with his aid.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This hymn is recited in the Āgnimāruta-śastra addressed to Vaiśvānara-Agni. In the middle of this mantra there is the sentence यो विड्भो मानुषीभ्यो दीदेत् (yo viḍbho mānuṣībhyo dīdet). Some may say: the one who shines for the benefit of human subjects is Sūrya, so here Sūrya himself is addressed by the word Vaiśvānara, and there is no difference between Sūrya and Vaiśvānara-Agni. Not so. This mantra is recited addressed to Agni. The meaning that the terrestrial fire on the sacrificial altar shines for the benefit of the sacrificers and other people also fits this mantra. Therefore it should be said that Vaiśvānara-Agni is not Sūrya but the terrestrial fire. Besides, in the Chandomika sacrifice called Daśarātra the Saurya-Vaiśvānara hymn जमदग्निभिराहुतः (jamadagnibhirāhutaḥ) is recited. This hymn also does not belong to Sūrya; it applies to Agni. For the word jamadagni means a fire well kindled and blazing. In sacrifices and the like, when offering into Agni, it is the custom to make Agni blaze with fuel, ghee and other substances and to make the offerings into that well-burning Agni itself. So the meaning is that this points to the terrestrial fire and not to Āditya (or Sūrya).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यथो एतद्धविष्वांतीयं सूक्तं सौर्यवैश्वानरं भवतीत्यस्यैव तद्भवति । हविष्वांतमजरं स्वर्विदि दिविस्सृश्याहुतं जुष्टमग्नौ । तस्य भर्मणे भुवनाय देवा धर्मणे कं स्वधया पप्रथंत ॥

yatho etaddhaviṣvāṃtīyaṃ sūktaṃ sauryavaiśvānaraṃ bhavatītyasyaiva tadbhavati | haviṣvāṃtamajaraṃ svarvidi divissṛśyāhutaṃ juṣṭamagnau | tasya bharmaṇe bhuvanāya devā dharmaṇe kaṃ svadhayā paprathaṃta ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning हविष्वांतमजरं (haviṣvāṃtamajaraṃ) (Haviṣvāntīya), the Saurya-Vaiśvānara hymn, also belongs to him (Agni). The verse says: the oblation, ageless, knowing heaven (svarvid), touching heaven, offered, welcome in Agni; for the bearing, becoming and holding of the world the gods, with svadhā, spread it out. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-1)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हविर्यत्सानीयमजरं सूर्यविदि दिविस्पृश्यभिहुतं जुष्टमग्नौ तस्य भरणाय च भावनाय च धारणाय च चैतेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः कर्मभ इममग्निमन्नेनापप्रथंतेति.

haviryatsānīyamajaraṃ sūryavidi divispṛśyabhihutaṃ juṣṭamagnau tasya bharaṇāya ca bhāvanāya ca dhāraṇāya ca caitebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ karmabha imamagnimannenāpaprathaṃteti.

Gist of the bhāṣya

Yāska explains: the oblation that is ageless, सूर्यविदि (sūryavidi), touching heaven, offered into Agni and welcomed; for the bearing, becoming and holding, for all these acts, the gods increase this Agni with food. (Ni. 7-25)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Moreover, the hymn हविष्वांतमजरं (haviṣvāṃtamajaraṃ) has the Saurya-Vaiśvānara-Agni as deity. If it is said that the Vaiśvānara praised in this hymn is Āditya, that is not right. The Vaiśvānara-Agni spoken of there is the terrestrial fire. This becomes clear if the meaning is examined: this oblation, ageless, that is imperishable, and pleasing, is offered, before it is drunk, into this Agni who touches heaven with his light and knows the sun well.

p. 798

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, for the bearing, holding, becoming and other acts of that oblation, join food with it and make it grow; this is the main sense of the Ṛk. Before drinking the oblation spoken of in this hymn or Ṛk, they offer it into Agni. This oblation is imperishable and pleasant to the mind (for drinking). They offer it into the sacrificial fire that touches the sky (heaven) with its flames, that is, that is well kindled and is aware of the sun. In order that this oblation may have the powers of holding, nourishing, bearing, becoming and so on, the gods add food to it and make it increase. Since the offering of the oblation is spoken of here, the offering belongs to Agni, that is to the terrestrial fire, not to Sūrya. They offer into Agni and not into Sūrya. Therefore the deity Vaiśvānara set forth in this hymn is not Āditya or Sūrya; it must be said that it is the terrestrial fire.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अथाप्याह— अपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्यत विशो राजानमुप तस्थु र्ऋग्मीयं । आ दूतो अग्निरभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥

athāpyāha— apāmupasthe mahiṣā agṛbhyata viśo rājānamupa tasthu rṛgmīyaṃ | ā dūto agnirabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

He says further: in the lap of the waters the great ones were seized; the clans waited upon the king, the worthy of praise; the messenger Agni brought Vaiśvānara from afar, from Vivasvat; Mātariśvan. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अपामुपस्थ उपस्थाने महत्यंतरिक्षलोक आसीना महांत इति वागृह्णत माध्यमिका देवगणा विश इव राजानमुपतस्थु र्यग्नियमृग्यंतमिति वार्चनीयमिति ना पूजनीयमिति वाहरद्यं दूतो देवानां विवस्वत आदित्याद्वि वस्वाद्विवासनवान् प्रेरितवतः परागताद्वापि वास्याग्नेर्वैश्वानरस्य मातरिश्वानमाहर्तारमाड ॥ मातरिश्वा वायुर्मा तर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति मातर्याश्वनितीति वा ॥

apāmupastha upasthāne mahatyaṃtarikṣaloka āsīnā mahāṃta iti vāgṛhṇata mādhyamikā devagaṇā viśa iva rājānamupatasthu ryagniyamṛgyaṃtamiti vārcanīyamiti nā pūjanīyamiti vāharadyaṃ dūto devānāṃ vivasvata ādityādvi vasvādvivāsanavān preritavataḥ parāgatādvāpi vāsyāgnervaiśvānarasya mātariśvānamāhartāramāḍa ‖ mātariśvā vāyurmā taryaṃtarikṣe śvasiti mātaryāśvanitīti vā ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Yāska explains: "in the lap of the waters", in the great atmosphere world, seated, the great ones (mahānta), the divine hosts of the middle region, waited upon him as clans upon a king, upon the praiseworthy or the worshipful; the messenger of the gods, from Vivasvat, i.e. Āditya, the radiant, or from one sent, or from afar; Mātariśvan brought Vaiśvānara Agni NOTE. Mātariśvan is the wind: he breathes in the mātar (the atmosphere), or मातर्याश्वनितीति वा (mātaryāśvanitīti vā). (Ni. 7-26)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

And on this point another Ṛk is cited as an example. Near the lap of the waters, that is in the wide atmosphere world, the greatly glorious Mādhyamika (atmosphere-dwelling) gods welcomed this Agni. As subjects receive their king with great honour, so the gods welcomed and honoured this Agni, who is to be set forth by mantras, worshipful and venerable. Mātariśvan (the wind), who lives in the atmosphere, first impelled by the gods, brought Vaiśvānara-Agni from Āditya, who is in a very distant region. Vaiśvānara-Agni first became visible in the atmosphere to Mātariśvan himself. That Mātariśvan brought Vaiśvānara-Agni from near Āditya who was in the very distant region.

p. 799

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mātariśvan means the wind. The wind gets the name Mātariśvan either because it lives in the atmosphere or because it moves swiftly in the atmosphere. What is to be noted here is that it is said that the gods of the atmosphere brought Agni from the region where Sūrya is. No one can bring Sūrya from one region to another; only Agni can be brought. So it must be understood that here Vaiśvānara means the terrestrial fire. Besides, in many mantras the qualities of Sūrya (Āditya) are said of Vaiśvānara-Agni: in the twelfth Ṛk of the Haviṣkānta hymn, in the mantra विश्वस्मा अग्निं भुवनाय देवा वैश्वानरं केतुमह्नामकृण्वन् (viśvasmā agniṃ bhuvanāya devā vaiśvānaraṃ ketumahnāmakṛṇvan), it is said that the gods made Vaiśvānara-Agni the maker of the days (ahas). Although the quality of being the maker of the days belongs properly to Sūrya, here this quality is said of Vaiśvānara-Agni. For this Agni is said to be of the nature of all the deities in mantras such as अग्निः सर्वादेवताः (agniḥ sarvādevatāḥ) (Ai. Brā. 2-1-2) and इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुः (iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuḥ) (1-164-46); so it is common to ascribe to Agni the qualities of Sūrya and other deities. Therefore Vaiśvānara-Agni is the terrestrial fire, not Āditya.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अथैनमेताभ्यां सर्वाणि स्थानान्यभ्यापादं स्तौति । मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् । मायामू तु यज्जियानामेतामपो यत्तूर्णिश्चरति प्रजानन् ॥

athainametābhyāṃ sarvāṇi sthānānyabhyāpādaṃ stauti | mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūryo jāyate prātarudyan | māyāmū tu yajjiyānāmetāmapo yattūrṇiścarati prajānan ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Then with these two verses he praises him in all places from the foot. The verse says: the head of the world he becomes; at night he is Agni, then Sūrya is born rising at dawn; … (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6) NOTE

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

मूर्धा मूर्तमस्मिन्दीयते मूर्धायः सर्वेषां भूतानां भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् स एव प्रज्ञां त्वेतां मन्यंते यज्ञियानां देवानां यज्ञसंपादिनामपो यत्कर्म चरति प्रजानन् सर्वाणि स्थानान्यनु संचरते त्वरमाणः ॥

mūrdhā mūrtamasmindīyate mūrdhāyaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūryo jāyate prātarudyan sa eva prajñāṃ tvetāṃ manyaṃte yajñiyānāṃ devānāṃ yajñasaṃpādināmapo yatkarma carati prajānan sarvāṇi sthānānyanu saṃcarate tvaramāṇaḥ ‖

Gist of the bhāṣya

Yāska explains: mūrdhā, that on which the head is placed; he becomes the head of all beings; at night Agni, then Sūrya is born rising at dawn; he himself … of the sacrificial gods who accomplish the sacrifice, the work he moves about knowing; hastening he moves through all places. (Ni. 7-27) NOTE

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The terrestrial fire is praised in many contexts as containing the distinguishing qualities of other special deities such as Sūrya. In this matter the author of the Nirukta has given two Ṛks as examples: for all living creatures Agni is absolutely necessary for life. Without Agni (the heat in the body, which is called Vaiśvānara-Agni) it is impossible to live. Such an Agni (the Agni in the form of Sūrya) shines at night as lord of the world that contains all creatures. In the morning the same Agni rises in the form of Sūrya. The gods can know the unique power and capacity of such an Agni, that is, how, being Sūrya by day and Agni by night, he carries out his duty.

p. 800

Here Agni is said to be the lord of the night. To convey the meaning "lord", the word मूर्धा (mūrdhā) is used in this ṛk. This word comes to mean "lord" in the following way: among the various limbs of the body the head (mūrdhā, śiras) is the chief, as the saying सर्वस्य गात्रस्य शिरः प्रधानं (sarvasya gātrasya śiraḥ pradhānaṃ) shows. Therefore the use of the word mūrdhā here conveys the meaning "lord". The meaning is that Agni is the lord of all beings during the night. In the night, when there is no heat of the sun, Agni himself provides the beings with heat and light and discharges the sun's function. In the morning this same Agni rises as the sun and protects beings. The sages and others who perform sacrifice are able to know this power and capacity of the deities. The intention is that Agni has the power to move swiftly in all regions in order to do this work. That this ṛk says that Agni performs the sun's function is praise of Agni's uncommon quality; it does not mean that Agni is the Āditya. Or else it should be understood that this ṛk indicates that Agni possesses the powers and capacities of the other deities.

The following ṛk is for a fuller explanation of it.

स्तोमेन हि दिवि देवासो अग्निमजीजनञ्क्तिभी रोदसिप्रां । तनू अकृण्वन्त्रेधा भुवे कं स ओषधीः पचति विश्वरूपाः ॥ (stomena hi divi devāso agnimajījanañktibhī rodasiprāṃ | tanū akṛṇvantredhā bhuve kaṃ sa oṣadhīḥ pacati viśvarūpāḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-10)

स्तोमेन हि यं दिवि देवा अग्निमजनयञ्क्तिभिः कर्मभिद्यावापृथिव्योः पूरणं तमकुर्वंस्त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः यदस्य दिवि तृतीयं तदसावादित्य इति हि ब्राह्मणं तदंगीकृत्य स्तौति. (stomena hi yaṃ divi devā agnimajanayañktibhiḥ karmabhidyāvāpṛthivyoḥ pūraṇaṃ tamakurvaṃstredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmaṃtarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ yadasya divi tṛtīyaṃ tadasāvāditya iti hi brāhmaṇaṃ tadaṃgīkṛtya stauti.) (Ni. 7-28).

The gods, by praise, brought Agni into being in heaven. That Agni, by his powers and capacities, filled and illumined heaven and earth. Again, those gods made that Agni three-formed. That Agni ripens all the plants (the herbs), that is, makes them grow and prosper.

The Agni whom the gods brought into being and established in heaven by the stoma (praise) pervaded heaven and earth by his powers and capacities. That is, the teacher Śākapūṇi says that the gods produced Agni in order that he might dwell in the three places: earth, atmosphere and heaven. In this matter there is also a Brāhmaṇa sentence यदस्य दिवि तृतीयं (yadasya divi tṛtīyaṃ) …

p. 801

… तदसावादित्यः (tadasāvādityaḥ): the third form of Agni which shines in heaven is that very Āditya who is visible to our eyes. Accepting this view, the seer praises Agni in the next ṛk.

अथैनमेतयादित्यीकृत्य स्तौति (athainametayādityīkṛtya stauti). यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्जियासो दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयं । यदा चरिष्णू मिथुनावभूतामादित प्रापश्यन् भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ (yadedenamadadhuryajjiyāso divi devāḥ sūryamāditeyaṃ | yadā cariṣṇū mithunāvabhūtāmādita prāpaśyan bhuvanāni viśvā ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-11).

यदैनमदधुर्यज्जियाः सर्वे दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयमदितेः पुत्रं यदा चरिष्णू मिथुनौ प्रादुरभूतां सर्वदा सहचारिणावुषाश्चादित्यश्च । म (yadainamadadhuryajjiyāḥ sarve divi devāḥ sūryamāditeyamaditeḥ putraṃ yadā cariṣṇū mithunau prādurabhūtāṃ sarvadā sahacāriṇāvuṣāścādityaśca | ma). मिथुनौ कस्मान्मिनोतिः श्रयतिकर्मा, थु इति नामकरणस्थकारो वा नयतिः परो, वनिर्वा, समाश्रितावन्योन्यं नयतो, वनुतो वा, मनुष्यमिथुनावप्यैतस्मादेव, मेधंतावन्योन्यं वनुत इति वा. (mithunau kasmānminotiḥ śrayatikarmā, thu iti nāmakaraṇasthakāro vā nayatiḥ paro, vanirvā, samāśritāvanyonyaṃ nayato, vanuto vā, manuṣyamithunāvapyaitasmādeva, medhaṃtāvanyonyaṃ vanuta iti vā.). (2. 72-9) NOTE

Accepting the view that this Agni is the Āditya, the seer praises with this ṛk. When the gods, worthy of sacrifice, established in heaven the sun, the son of Aditi, and when this pair of deities (Uṣas and Āditya) were created and began to move together, then they saw all the beings of the world.

When the gods, worthy of sacrifice, that is, praised in sacrifices and the like, established the Āditya (the sun), the son of Aditi, in heaven, and when the two who are mithunabhūta, that is, always together (the two, Uṣas and Āditya) came into being, from then on these two deities, Uṣas and Āditya, move always together and became able to see all the beings in the world.

Here the derivation of the word mithuna is given. The word mithuna is formed from the root minoti, which has the sense of "resorting to". That is: the root mi in the word mithuna has the meaning "resort to"; thu, or the letter tha, is the affix; the last letter na is from the root nayati (नयतिः परः (nayatiḥ paraḥ)), and indicates the meaning "leads" or "carries" another. So the word mithuna means two that resort to each other mutually and remain together. समाश्रित् अन्योन्यं प्रति आत्मानं नयतः कालं वा समाश्रितौ भवतः परस्परं संभक्तौ (samāśrit anyonyaṃ prati ātmānaṃ nayataḥ kālaṃ vā samāśritau bhavataḥ parasparaṃ saṃbhaktau) NOTE. That is, the word mithunau means two who resort to each other mutually, or, in respect of time, that after one time another comes

p. 802

(night, day and so on) is the meaning it conveys. In the case of human beings too, the word mithuna means two persons who resort to each other, or who pass their time together in mutual affection.

अथैनमेतयाग्नीकृत्य स्तौति (athainametayāgnīkṛtya stauti). यत्रा वदेते अवरः परश्च यज्ञन्योः कतरो नौ वि वेद । अ शेकुरित्सधमादं सखायो नक्षंत यज्ञं क इदं वि वोचत् ॥ (yatrā vadete avaraḥ paraśca yajñanyoḥ kataro nau vi veda | a śekuritsadhamādaṃ sakhāyo nakṣaṃta yajñaṃ ka idaṃ vi vocat ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-17).

यत्र विवदेते दौन्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः कतरो नौ यज्ञे भूयो वेदेत्याशक्नुवंति सत्सहमदनं समानख्याना ऋत्विजस्तेषां यज्ञं समश्नुवानानां को न इदं विपक्ष्यतीति ॥ (yatra vivadete daunyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ kataro nau yajñe bhūyo vedetyāśaknuvaṃti satsahamadanaṃ samānakhyānā ṛtvijasteṣāṃ yajñaṃ samaśnuvānānāṃ ko na idaṃ vipakṣyatīti ‖) (Ni. 7-30).

Taking this Vaiśvānara Agni to be the earthly Agni, the seer praises with this ṛk. Of the lower and the upper Agnis who know the matter of sacrifice, which knows more? Who is able to decide this question? The ṛtvijs and others who take equal shares in the sacrifice are able to decide it.

दैन्य होतारौ (dainya hotārau) means the hotṛs of divine nature: the Agni named Hotṛ who invites the gods to the sacrifice. Since the word hotārau is in the dual, the two deities are the earthly (the sacrificial Agni) established on earth, and the Vāyu or lightning-Agni in the middle region. Since both are only other forms of Agni, they are addressed with the dual word hotārau. अवरः परश्च (avaraḥ paraśca) means "the lower and the upper". "Lower" is to be understood as the earthly Agni in the place of earth, and परः (paraḥ) as the Agni (lightning) in the middle region. Which of these two has the greater knowledge? Among the ṛtvijs who, taking equal shares, that is, the chief roles, in sacrificial rites, know the matter of sacrifice well, which ṛtvij is able to decide this question?

The following ṛk is for a fuller explanation of it.

यावन्मात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं सुपर्णो,३वसते मातरिश्वः । तावद्धधात्युप यज्ञमायान्ब्राह्मणो होतुरवरो निषीदन् ॥ (yāvanmātramuṣaso na pratīkaṃ suparṇo,3vasate mātariśvaḥ | tāvaddhadhātyupa yajñamāyānbrāhmaṇo hoturavaro niṣīdan ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88)

यावन्मात्रमुषसः प्रत्यक्तं भवति प्रतिदर्शनमिति वास्तुपमानस्य संप्रत्यर्थे प्रयोग इहेव निधेहीति यथा सुपर्ण्यः सुपतना एता रात्रयो (yāvanmātramuṣasaḥ pratyaktaṃ bhavati pratidarśanamiti vāstupamānasya saṃpratyarthe prayoga iheva nidhehīti yathā suparṇyaḥ supatanā etā rātrayo)

p. 803

वसते मातरिश्वन् ज्योतिर्वर्णस्य तावदुपदधाति यज्ञमागच्छन् ब्राह्मणो होतास्याग्नेर्होतुरवरो निषीदन् ॥ (vasate mātariśvan jyotirvarṇasya tāvadupadadhāti yajñamāgacchan brāhmaṇo hotāsyāgnerhoturavaro niṣīdan ‖) (Ni. 7-31)

Another ṛk is given as an example in this matter. In the previous ṛk Agni and Vāyu are praised; in this ṛk Agni alone is praised. Mātariśvan (Vāyu) asked a man: can the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ taking part in the sacrifice, hold, that is, know, the knowledge of Agni, the hotṛ of the gods (the understanding in the performance of sacrifice)? The man replied to this as follows. O Mātariśvan, for as long as (for how long) the birds of fine wings hold the dawn, for so long the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated on the sacrificial altar near the sacrificial fire, in a place lower than Agni, holds it (that is, by Agni's grace knows it to a small extent).

The word न (na) in this ṛk does not have the sense of comparison; it has the sense of "now" (samprati). Just as the word iha means "here", yet the sentence इहैव निधेहि (ihaiva nidhehi) means "put it now", so it should be understood. Therefore the phrase यावनात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं (yāvanātramuṣaso na pratīkaṃ) NOTE means: for as long as, that is, for how long (only a short time) the dawn-time at the end of the night spreads, for just so long. The sentence सुपर्ण्यः सुपतना एता रात्रयो वसते मातरिश्वन (suparṇyaḥ supatanā etā rātrayo vasate mātariśvana) means: O Mātariśvan, the birds of fine wings, flying, hold the dawn-time. That is, "birds" here means the nights. The word suparṇyaḥ which indicates this, meaning "of various wings", conveys the sense of the various (fine) colours of the dawn-time. Therefore suparṇyaḥ means that when Uṣas rises at the end of the night, that Uṣas has various or beautiful colours. The extent of this dawn-time is very small. Since sunrise follows very quickly after the dawn-time, the dawn-time is very small in extent: the intention is, only for a very short time. The human hotṛ is inferior to Agni, the divine hotṛ; therefore the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated in a place lower than Agni installed on the sacrificial altar, performs the hotṛ's work only for a very short time, by the grace of Agni, who is of special wisdom: this is the main intention. By this the smallness of man and the greatness of Agni become evident. Since this ṛk says that the brāhmaṇa, the human hotṛ, seated on the sacrificial altar, performs the hotṛ's work praising Agni, the divine hotṛ, it is clearly evident that here Vaiśvānara Agni means the earthly Agni who is praised, and not the Āditya.

p. 804

होतृजपस्त्वनग्निर्वैश्वानरीयो भवति देव सवितरेतु त्वा वृणतेऽग्निं होत्राय सह पित्रा वैश्वानरेणेतीममेवाग्निं सवितारमाह सर्वस्य प्रसवितारं मध्यमं वोत्तमं वा पितरं । यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरुप्यतेयमेव सॊग्निर्वैश्वानरः । निसातमेवैते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी एतेन नामधेयेन भजेते भजेते ॥ (hotṛjapastvanagnirvaiśvānarīyo bhavati deva savitaretu tvā vṛṇate 'gniṃ hotrāya saha pitrā vaiśvānareṇetīmamevāgniṃ savitāramāha sarvasya prasavitāraṃ madhyamaṃ vottamaṃ vā pitaraṃ | yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirupyateyameva sògnirvaiśvānaraḥ | nisātamevaite uttare jyotiṣī etena nāmadheyena bhajete bhajete ‖) (Ni. 7-31).

The japa-mantras and the like recited by the hotṛ in the sacrifice praise Vaiśvānara by addressing him. The mantra-japa (is that of) Agni: देवसवितरेतं त्वा वृणतेऽग्निं होत्राय सह पित्रा वैश्वानरेण (devasavitaretaṃ tvā vṛṇate 'gniṃ hotrāya saha pitrā vaiśvānareṇa) NOTE. An explanation of the sentence "O shining god Savitṛ, the hotṛ has chosen you, that is, Agni, along with your father Vaiśvānara, for the praise" is necessary. Here the seer calls Agni himself Savitṛ. Here Savitṛ (the word savitṛ) means the producer of all things (or beings); the word is used here in this sense. He addresses as father either Vāyu, who belongs to the middle region, or the Āditya, who belongs to the highest (heavenly) place.

The god who is praised in the sūkta, and the god for whom (with whom in view) the oblation is offered, that Vaiśvānara is this earthly Agni.

As stated in sentences such as सूर्यो वैश्वानरः । अग्निर्वैश्वानरः । (sūryo vaiśvānaraḥ | agnirvaiśvānaraḥ |), the light of lightning-form in the middle region and the light of Āditya-form in heaven, both these lights, are spoken of by the one name Vaiśvānara. That is, the earthly Agni, spoken of by the word Vaiśvānara, shines in three forms: in heaven as Āditya, in the atmosphere as lightning, on earth as the earthly Agni: this is the main intention.

This is the … sūkta. NOTE

चतुर्थे मंडले प्रथमेऽनुवाके दश सूक्तानि । वैश्वानरायेति पंचदशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं नामदेवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वानराग्नि देवताकं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । वैश्वानराय वैश्वानरीयमिति ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

In the fourth Maṇḍala, in the first anuvāka, there are ten sūktas. The fifth, beginning वैश्वानराय (vaiśvānarāya), has fifteen ṛks; its seer is नामदेवस्य (nāmadevasya) NOTE; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Vaiśvānara Agni. The Anukramaṇikā says वैश्वानराय वैश्वानरीयमिति (vaiśvānarāya vaiśvānarīyamiti). The use in ritual (viniyoga) is laiṅgika, that is, by the indication of the text itself.

p. 805

Anuvāda

In the first anuvāka of the fourth maṇḍala there are ten sūktas. Of them this sūkta beginning "Vaiśvānarāya" is the fifth. It has fifteen ṛks. Vāmadeva is the seer of this sūkta; Vaiśvānara Agni is the deity; Triṣṭubh is the metre. The Anukramaṇikā says: "vaiśvānarāya vaiśvānarāyam" NOTE. The use in ritual is laiṅgika.

Sūkta 5

Maṇḍala 4. Anuvāka 1. Sūkta 5. Aṣṭaka 3. Adhyāya 5. Vargas 1, 2, 3. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Vāmadeva. Deity: Vaiśvānara. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

वै॒श्वा॒न॒राय॑ मी॒ळ्हुषे॑ स॒जोषाः॑ क॒था दा॑शेमा॒ग्नये॑ ॒ बृ॒हद्भाः ।
अनू॑नेन बृह॒ता व॒क्षथे॒नोप॑ स्तभायदुप॒मिन्न रोधः॑ ॥१॥

vaiśvānarāya mīḷhuṣe sajoṣāḥ kathā dāśemāgnaye
bṛhadbhāḥ |
anūnena bṛhatā vakṣathenopa stabhāyadupaminna rodhaḥ ‖1‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

वैश्वानराय । मीळ्हुषे । सजोषाः । कथा । दाशेम । अग्नये । बृहत् । भाः ।
अनूनेन । बृहता । वक्षथेन । उप । स्तभायत् । उपमित् । न । रोधः ॥ १ ॥

vaiśvānarāya | mīḷhuṣe | sajoṣāḥ | kathā | dāśema | agnaye | bṛhat | bhāḥ |
anūnena | bṛhatā | vakṣathena | upa | stabhāyat | upamit | na | rodhaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सजोषाः सजोषसः समानप्रीतियुक्ता वयमृत्विग्यजमाना वैश्वानराय विश्वानरसंबंधिन एतन्नामकाय विळ्हुषेभिमतवृष्टादिसेक्रे बृहद्बृहते महते भा भासमानायाग्नये देवाय कथा कथं केन प्रकारेण दाशेम दद्याम। साम-

Gist of the bhāṣya

सजोषाः (sajoṣāḥ): we, ṛtvijs and sacrificers, united in equal affection. वैश्वानराय (vaiśvānarāya): for the god of this name, who belongs to all men. मीळ्हुषे (mīḷhuṣe): to the sprinkler of desired things such as rain. बृहत् (bṛhat): great; भाः (bhāḥ): shining; to the god Agni, who is great and shining. कथा (kathā): how, in what manner, shall we give (दाशेम (dāśema))? By implication it is understood that the thing given is an oblation.

p. 806

र्थाद्धविरिति गम्यते । अथवा बृहद्भा इत्युत्तरत्र योज्यं । कथा दाशेमेत्युक्तं । किं तत्राधिक्यमिति तदुच्यते । योग्निर्बृहन्महान्भा भासमानश्च सन् अनूनेनाविकलेन संपूर्णेन अत एव बृहता प्रभूतेन वक्षथेन वोढव्येन स्वशरीरेणोप स्तभायत् । उपस्तभ्याति । सामर्थ्याद्दामिति शेषः । द्युलोकं प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । उपमिन्न रोधः । उप समीपे मीयते क्षिप्यत इत्युपमित् स्थूणा। सा यथा तृणाच्छादनादिनिरोधकं वंशादिकमुपस्तभ्याति तद्वत् । यद्वा । वक्षथेनोक्तलक्षणेन फलादिवाहकेन स्तोत्रेण सह द्युलोकमुपस्तभायत् । स्तभायत्। स्तन्भुः सौत्रो धातुः । लजु छंदसि शायजपीति व्यत्ययेनाहावपि शायजादेशः । बहुलं छंदसीत्यडागमाभावः । किमिव । उपमिन्न रोधः । उप समीपे मीयत इत्युपमिदुदकं । कूलमिव ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Or else बृहद्भाः (bṛhadbhāḥ) is to be joined with what follows. "How shall we give" has been said; what is the excellence in it? That is stated. The Agni who, being great and shining, with an unimpaired, complete, therefore abundant, "to-be-carried" (वक्षथेन (vakṣathena)) body of his own, props up (उपस्तभायत् (upastabhāyat); he props up) the heaven, "the heaven" being supplied from the sense; that is, he reaches the heavenly world. An illustration: उपमिन्न रोधः (upaminna rodhaḥ). उपमित् (upamit) is a post, which is placed (मीयते (mīyate)) near (उप (upa)); as it supports the bamboo or the like that holds the thatch, so he. Or else: with the praise, of the nature stated, that carries the fruits and so on (वक्षथेन (vakṣathena)), he props up the heaven. स्तभायत् (stabhāyat): the root stambh is a sautra root. Another alternative: उपमिन्न रोधः (upaminna rodhaḥ): उपमित् (upamit), "that which is measured near", is water; he is like a bank (कूलमिव (kūlamiva)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • वैश्वानराय (vaiśvānarāya)—to him who is famed by the name Vaiśvānara
  • मीळ्हुषे (mīḷhuṣe)—who bestows desired things
  • बृहत् (bṛhat)—of vast form
  • भाः (bhāḥ)—shining
  • अग्नये (agnaye)—to Agni
  • सजोषाः (sajoṣāḥ)—we, ṛtvijs and others
  • कथा (kathā)—in what manner indeed
  • दाशेम (dāśema)—shall we offer the oblation
  • अनूनेन (anūnena)—complete, without deficiency
  • बृहता (bṛhatā)—of vast form
  • वक्षथेन (vakṣathena)—with his body
  • रोधः (rodhaḥ)—the atmosphere
  • उपमिन्न (upaminna)—as a pillar holds up a beam and keeps it standing
  • उपस्तभायत् (upastabhāyat)—he has lifted and holds up
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In what manner shall we, ṛtvijs and sacrificers, gathered together, offer the oblation to Agni, who is famed by the name Vaiśvānara, bestower of desired things, of vast form and shining? That same Vaiśvānara Agni, with his complete, vast body, has lifted and holds up the atmosphere, as a pillar holds up a beam.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

How may we present rejoicing ( fit offerings ) to Agni, the showerer (of benefits) ; to Vaishwanara, he, who, bright with great lustre, sustains the heaven, with his entire vast and insupportable ( bulk ), as a pillar (sustains a roof).

p. 807

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

मा निं॑दत॒ य इ॒मां मह्यं॑ रा॒तिं दे॒वो द॒दौ मर्त्या॑य ॒॑ स्व॒धावा॑न् ।
पाका॑य॒ गृत्सो॑ अ॒मृतो॒ विचे॑ता वैश्वान॒रो नृत॑मो ॒ ॒ यह्वो अग्निः ॥ २ ॥

mā niṃdata ya imāṃ mahyaṃ rātiṃ devo dadau martyāya
svadhāvān |
pākāya gṛtso amṛto vicetā vaiśvānaro nṛtamo
yahvo agniḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

मा । निंदत । यः । इमां । मह्यं । रातिं । देवः । ददौ । मर्त्याय । स्वधावान् ।
पाकाय । गृत्सः । अमृतः । विचेताः । वैश्वानरः । नृतमः । यह्वः । अग्निः ॥ २ ॥

mā | niṃdata | yaḥ | imāṃ | mahyaṃ | rātiṃ | devaḥ | dadau | martyāya | svadhāvān |
pākāya | gṛtsaḥ | amṛtaḥ | vicetāḥ | vaiśvānaraḥ | nṛtamaḥ | yahvaḥ | agniḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे होत्रादयोऽमुं वैश्वानरमग्निं मा निंदत । निंदां मा कुरुत । स्तुतेत्यर्थः । यो देवो दीप्यमानोऽग्निः स्वधावानस्मृद्दत्तेन हविर्लक्षणेनान्नेन तद्वान् सन् मर्त्याय मरणधर्माय पाकाय परिपक्वप्रज्ञाय मह्यं यजमानायेमामिदानीं दीयमानप्रकारां रातिं धनं ददौ । दत्तवान् । स विशेष्यते। गृतो मेधावी । मेधाविनामैतत् । अमृतोऽमरणस्वभावो विचेता विशिष्टप्रज्ञो वैश्वानरो विश्वैर्नरैराहवनीयादिरूपेण नीयमानो नृतमो नेतृतमः फलादीनां यहो महान् । महन्नामैतत् । अग्निरंगनादिगुणविशिष्टः । तादृशमग्निं स्तुतेति भावः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the priests, the hotṛs and others: do not revile this Vaiśvānara Agni; praise him. The shining Agni, who is svadhāvān, possessed of the food in the form of the oblation given by us, has given this wealth, of the kind now being given, to me, the sacrificer, who am mortal and of ripened wisdom. He is further described: gṛtsa is "wise" (a name for the wise); he is immortal by nature, of distinguished understanding; Vaiśvānara, because he is led by all men in the forms of the Āhavanīya and the rest; nṛtama, the best leader, mighty (yahva is a name for "great") in fruits and the like; and Agni, endowed with the qualities of going and so on. The sense is: praise such an Agni.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः (yaḥ)—who
  • देवः (devaḥ)—being resplendent
  • स्वधावान् (svadhāvān)—and possessing food in the form of oblation
  • मर्त्याय (martyāya)—to the mortal
  • पाकाय (pākāya)—to one of ripened knowledge
  • मह्यं (mahyaṃ)—to me
  • इमां रातिं (imāṃ rātiṃ)—this wealth
  • ददौ (dadau)—gave (such an Agni)
  • मा निंदत (mā niṃdata)—do not revile (that Agni)
  • गृत्सः (gṛtsaḥ)—wise
  • अमृतः (amṛtaḥ)—free from mortality
  • विचेताः (vicetāḥ)—of distinguished understanding
  • वैश्वानरः (vaiśvānaraḥ)—carried by all
  • नृतमः (nṛtamaḥ)—the best among leaders
  • यह्वः (yahvaḥ)—great-souled
  • अग्निः (agniḥ)—worthy of worship (he is)

p. 808

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Do not revile that Agni who, being resplendent and possessed of food in the form of oblation, has given this wealth to me, a mortal of ripened knowledge. That same Agni is wise, free from mortality, of distinguished understanding, carried by all, the best among leaders, great-souled and worthy of worship.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Reproach not the divine (Agni), who, accepting the oblation, has given the wealth to me, his mortal (worshipper) of mature (intellect); Agni, who is wise, immortal, discriminating, (who is) Vaishwanara, chief conductor (of rites), the mighty.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

साम॑ द्वि॒बर्हा॒ महि॑ ति॒ग्मभृ॑ष्टिः स॒हस्र॑रेता वृष॒भस्तुवि॑ष्मान् ।
प॒दं न गोरप॑गूळ्तं विवि॒द्वान्॒ग्निर्मह्यं॒ प्रेदु॑ वोचन्मनी॒षां ॥ ३ ॥

sāma dvibarhā mahi tigmabhṛṣṭiḥ sahasraretā vṛṣabhastuviṣmān |
padaṃ na gorapagūḷtaṃ vividvāngnirmahyaṃ predu vocanmanīṣāṃ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

साम । द्विबर्हाः । महि । तिग्मभृष्टिः । सहस्ररेताः । वृषभः । तुविष्मान् ।
पदं । न । गोः । अपगूळ्तं । विविद्वान् । अग्निः । मह्यं । प्र । इत् । ऊं इति ।
वोचत् । मनीषां ॥ ३ ॥

sāma | dvibarhāḥ | mahi | tigmabhṛṣṭiḥ | sahasraretāḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | tuviṣmān |
padaṃ | na | goḥ | apagūḷtaṃ | vividvān | agniḥ | mahyaṃ | pra | it | ūṃ iti |
vocat | manīṣāṃ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

द्विबर्हा द्वयोर्मध्यमोत्तमयोः स्थानयोः परिवृढस्तिग्मभृष्टिस्तीक्ष्णतेजाः सहस्ररेता बहुविधहिरण्यरेतस्कः रेतःशब्दः सारवाची । प्रभूतसारो ना । वृषभो वर्षिता कामानां तुविष्टान्बहुधन ईदृशोऽयमग्निरत्यंतगोपितं गोः पदं न नष्टाया गोः पदमिवापगूळ्हमत्यंतरहस्यं । मनीषाशब्दो ज्ञानवाची सन्नत्र ज्ञातव्ये वर्तते । मनीषां ज्ञातव्यं महि महत्पूज्यं सामास्मदभिमतं स्तोत्रं विविद्वान् विशेषेण जानन् प्रेदु वोचत् । प्रैव ब्रवीतु ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Dvibarhāḥ: encompassing the two places, the middle and the highest. Tigmabhṛṣṭi: of sharp splendour. Sahasrareta: possessing manifold golden seed (the word reta denotes essence; compare "of abundant essence"). Vṛṣabha: the showerer of desires. Tuviṣmān: rich in wealth. Such is this Agni. Like the footprint of a lost cow, which is hidden, the thing is utterly secret. The word manīṣā, denoting knowledge, here stands for what is to be known. May Agni, who knows especially the great, venerable sāman, the praise-song we desire, declare it forth to me.

p. 809

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • द्विबर्हाः (dvibarhāḥ)—he who occupies both the middle and the highest places
  • तिग्मभृष्टिः (tigmabhṛṣṭiḥ)—of sharp splendour
  • सहस्ररेताः (sahasraretāḥ)—of abundant essence
  • वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ)—showerer of desires
  • तुविष्टान् (tuviṣṭān)—possessing abundant wealth
  • अग्निः (agniḥ)—Agni
  • गो पदं न (go padaṃ na)—like the footprint of cows that have been led away secretly
  • अपगूह्नं (apagūhnaṃ)—utterly secret
  • मनीषां (manīṣāṃ)—to be known
  • महि (mahi)—venerable
  • साम (sāma)—the sāman, of the nature of praise
  • विविद्वान् (vividvān)—knowing especially well
  • मह्यं (mahyaṃ)—to me
  • प्रेदु वोचत् (predu vocat)—may he teach so that I understand
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni, who occupies both the middle and the highest places, of sharp splendour, of abundant essence, showerer of desires, possessing abundant wealth, knowing especially well the sāman—utterly secret like the footprint of hidden cows, to be known necessarily by men, venerable and of the nature of praise—teach it to me so that I understand.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May Agni, filling both (the middling and most excellent condition), bright shining, of manifold vigour, the showerer of (benefits) the possessor of affluence, (who comprehends) by (his) wisdom the mysterious sacred hymn, as (they track) the footsteps of a (missing) cow, reveal (the sense) to me.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

प्र ता अ॒ग्निर्ब॑भसत्ति॒ग्मजं॑भ॒स्तपि॑ष्ठेन शो॒चिषा॒ यः सु॒राधाः॑ ।
प्र ये मि॒नंति॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ धाम॑ प्रि॒या मि॒त्रस्य॒ चेत॑तो ॒॑ ध्रुवाणि ॥ ४ ॥

pra tā agnirbabhasattigmajaṃbhastapiṣṭhena śociṣā yaḥ surādhāḥ |
pra ye minaṃti varuṇasya dhāma priyā mitrasya cetato
dhruvāṇi ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

प्र । तान् । अग्निः । बभसत् । तिग्मृजंभः । तपिष्ठेन । शोचिषा । यः । सुराधाः ।

pra | tān | agniḥ | babhasat | tigmṛjaṃbhaḥ | tapiṣṭhena | śociṣā | yaḥ | surādhāḥ |

p. 810

प्र । ये । मिनंति । वरुणस्य । धाम । प्रिया । मित्रस्य । चेततः । ध्रुवाणि ॥ ४ ॥

pra | ye | minaṃti | varuṇasya | dhāma | priyā | mitrasya | cetataḥ | dhruvāṇi ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

योऽग्निः सुराधाः शोभनधनः स तिग्मजंभस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः सन् तपिष्ठेन शोचिषातिशयेन शत्रूणां तापकेन तेजसा तान्वक्ष्यमाणान् द्वेष्टान्बभसत् । प्रकर्षेण भर्त्सयतु । दहत्वित्यर्थः ॥ भस भर्त्सनदीप्योः । लेटीतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः ॥ तानित्युक्तं कानित्याह । ये द्वेषारश्चेततो जानतः । एतदुभयविशेषणं । मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च प्रिया प्रियाणि ध्रुवाणि स्थिराणि धाम धामानि तेजःस्थानानि कर्माणि ना प्र मिनंति । प्रकर्षेण हिंसंति । मीञ् हिंसायां । मीनातेर्निगम इति ह्रस्वत्वं । विकरणस्वरः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, who is surādhāḥ, of excellent wealth, being sharp-toothed (tigmajambha), may with his most scorching radiance, which burns enemies, drive off and consume those haters to be named, "them". Who are they? Those enemies who, knowing (cetataḥ—this qualifies both Mitra and Varuṇa), do not diminish but violently injure the dear and firm abodes of splendour, that is, the rites, of Mitra and Varuṇa.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • ये (ye)—which enemies
  • चेततः (cetataḥ)—the wise
  • मित्रस्य वरुणस्य (mitrasya varuṇasya)—of Mitra and Varuṇa
  • प्रिया (priyā)—dear
  • ध्रुवाणि (dhruvāṇi)—firm
  • धाम (dhāma)—abodes of splendour
  • प्र मिनंति (pra minaṃti)—injure; those
  • तान् (tān)—those enemies
  • सुराधाः (surādhāḥ)—possessing excellent wealth
  • तिग्मजंभः (tigmajaṃbhaḥ)—possessing a sharp weapon
  • अग्निः (agniḥ)—Agni
