॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

तव । त्विषः । जनिमन् । रेजत । द्याः । रेजत् । भूमिः । भियसा । स्वस्य । मन्योः ।
ऋघायंत । सुभ्वः । पर्वतासः । आर्दन् । धन्वानि । सरयंते । आपः ॥ २ ॥

tava | tviṣaḥ | janiman | rejata | dyāḥ | rejat | bhūmiḥ | bhiyasā | svasya | manyoḥ |
ṛghāyaṃta | subhvaḥ | parvatāsaḥ | ārdan | dhanvāni | sarayaṃte | āpaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र त्विषो दीप्यमानस्य तव त्वदीये जनिमन् जन्मनि सति द्यौरंतरिक्षं स्वस्य त्वदीयान्मन्योः कोपात् । पंचम्यर्थे षष्ठी । भियसा जातभयेन रेजत । अरेजत् । अकंपत । भूमिश्च रेजत् । कंपमाना बभूव । सुभ्वो महांतः

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when you, the shining one (त्विषः (tviṣaḥ)), were born (जनिमन् (janiman)), heaven, that is the atmosphere, trembled (रेजत (rejata)) through fear arisen from your own anger (मन्योः (manyoḥ)); the genitive stands in the sense of the ablative. The earth also trembled. The सुभ्वः (subhvaḥ), the great ones… (the block breaks off here; the next window continues).

p. 960

पर्वतासः। पर्वता मेघाः। ऋघायंत। सस्यादीनां वृष्टिप्रदानार्थं नियामकेन त्वयाबाध्यंत । तथा मेघा आर्दन् । प्राणिनां पिपासारूपां पीडामुहिंसन् । तथा मेघा धन्वान्युदकरहितान्वेशानापोऽपः सरयंते । गमयंति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The "mountains" (parvatas) are clouds. They were constrained (ṛghāyanta) by you, the controller, so that they might give rain to crops and the like. The clouds also "afflicted" (ārdan): they destroyed the pain of thirst in living beings. And the clouds make the waters flow (sarayante, cause to go) over the arid, waterless regions (dhanvāni).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • (Hail Indra)
  • त्विषः (tviṣaḥ)—radiant one
  • तव (tava)—your
  • जनिमन् (janiman)—at the time of birth
  • द्यौः (dyauḥ)—the atmosphere
  • स्वस्य (svasya)—your
  • मन्योः (manyoḥ)—(born) of wrath
  • भियसा (bhiyasā)—through fear
  • रेजत (rejata)—trembled
  • भूमिः (bhūmiḥ)—the earth also
  • रेजत् (rejat)—trembled
  • सुभ्वः (subhvaḥ)—of mighty form
  • पर्वतासः (parvatāsaḥ)—the clouds
  • ऋघायंत (ṛghāyaṃta)—became subject to your control (therefore)
  • आर्दन् (ārdan)—cooling (the scorched regions)
  • धन्वानि (dhanvāni)—even in the waterless barren land
  • आपः (āpaḥ)—the waters in the form of rain
  • सरयंते (sarayaṃte)—they pour down
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, at the birth of you, the radiant one, the atmosphere trembled with the fear born of your wrath. The earth too shook. The mighty clouds, brought under your control, quench the thirst of living beings and cool the scorched regions, and pour waters in the form of rain even on the waterless barren land.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

At the birth of you who are resplendent, trembled heaven ( and ) trembled the earth through fear of your wrath; the mighty clouds were confined ; they destroyed (the distress of drought), spreading the waters over the dry places.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

भि॒नद्दि॒रिं शव॑सा॒ वज्र॑मि॒ष्णन्ना॑विष्कृण्णा॒न् स॑हसा॒न ओजः॑ ।
वधी॑द्वृ॒त्रं वज्रे॑ण मंदसा॒नः सर॒न्नापो॒ जव॑सा ह॒तवृ॑ष्ठीः ॥

bhinaddiriṃ śavasā vajramiṣṇannāviṣkṛṇṇān sahasāna ojaḥ |
vadhīdvṛtraṃ vajreṇa maṃdasānaḥ sarannāpo javasā hatavṛṣṭhīḥ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

भिनत् । गिरिं । शवसा । वज्रं । इष्णन् । आविःकृण्वानः । सहसाना । ओजः ।
वधीत् । वृत्रं । वज्रेण । मंदसानः । सरन् । आपः । जवसा । हतवृष्टिः ॥ ३ ॥

bhinat | giriṃ | śavasā | vajraṃ | iṣṇan | āviḥkṛṇvānaḥ | sahasānā | ojaḥ |
vadhīt | vṛtraṃ | vajreṇa | maṃdasānaḥ | saran | āpaḥ | javasā | hatavṛṣṭiḥ ‖ 3 ‖

p. 961

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सहसानः शत्रूणामभिभवन्नोजस्तेज आविष्कृण्वान आविष्कुर्वन्निंद्रो वज्रमिष्ठिन् वज्रं प्रेरयन् शवसा बलेन गिरिं पर्वतजातं भिनत् । अभिनत् । बिभेद । किंच मंदसानः सोमेन मोदमान इंद्रो वज्रेण वृत्रं वृत्रनामानमसुरं वधीत् । अवधीत् । जघान । तत आपो वृत्रेणावृतान्युदकानि हतवृष्टीः । हतो वृषा वृत्रो यासां ता हतवृष्ट्यः । ता वृत्रवधानंतरं निवारणरहिताः सत्यो जवसा वेगेन सरन् । असरन् । अगच्छन् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, overpowering (sahasānaḥ) his enemies and manifesting his might (ojaḥ), hurling his thunderbolt, split by his strength the mountain (giri) born of the cloud (parvata). Further, Indra, exhilarated by Soma, slew with the thunderbolt the asura named Vṛtra. Then the waters, which had been enclosed by Vṛtra, are hatavṛṣṭīḥ: those whose bull (vṛṣā) Vṛtra was slain. After the killing of Vṛtra they were free of obstruction and flowed (saran) swiftly.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • सहसानः (sahasānaḥ)—Indra, the subduer of enemies
  • ओजः (ojaḥ)—his own splendour
  • आविष्कृण्वानः (āviṣkṛṇvānaḥ)—manifesting
  • वज्रं (vajraṃ)—the thunderbolt
  • इष्टन् (iṣṭan)—hurling
  • शवसा (śavasā)—by his strength
  • गिरिं (giriṃ)—the mountain
  • भिनत् (bhinat)—he split
  • मंदसानः (maṃdasānaḥ)—Indra, satisfied by drinking Soma
  • वज्रेण (vajreṇa)—with the thunderbolt
  • वृत्रं (vṛtraṃ)—the asura called Vṛtra
  • वधीत् (vadhīt)—he killed (afterwards)
  • आपः (āpaḥ)—the waters
  • हतवृष्टिः (hatavṛṣṭiḥ)—free of obstruction
  • जवसा (javasā)—with speed
  • सरन् (saran)—flowed
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the subduer of enemies, manifesting his splendour and hurling the thunderbolt, split the mountain by his strength. Indra, satisfied by drinking Soma, slew Vṛtra with the thunderbolt. Then the waters flowed swiftly, free of obstruction.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The subduer of foes, manifesting his energy and hurling his thunderbolt, shattered the mountain by his strength: he slew Vritra with the thunderbolt, exulting, and the waters whose obstructor was destroyed rushed forth with rapidity.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

सु॒वीर॑स्ते जनि॒ता म॑न्यत॒ द्यौरिंद्र॑स्य क॒र्ता स्वप॑स्तमो भूत् ।
य ईं॑ ज॒जान॑ स्व॒र्यं॑ सु॒वज्र॒मन॑पच्युतं॒ सद॑सो॒ न भूम॑॥

suvīraste janitā manyata dyauriṃdrasya kartā svapastamo bhūt |
ya īṃ jajāna svaryaṃ suvajramanapacyutaṃ sadaso na bhūma‖

p. 962

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सुवीरः । ते । जनिता । मन्यत । द्यौः । इंद्रस्य । कर्ता । स्वपःतमः । भूत् ।
यः । ईं । जजान 'स्वर्यं । सुवज्रं । अनपच्युतं । सदसः । न । भूम ॥ ४ ॥

suvīraḥ | te | janitā | manyata | dyauḥ | iṃdrasya | kartā | svapaḥtamaḥ | bhūt |
yaḥ | īṃ | jajāna 'svaryaṃ | suvajraṃ | anapacyutaṃ | sadasaḥ | na | bhūma ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र यः प्रजापतिः स्वर्यमृत्विगादिभिः स्तुत्यं सुवज्रं शोभनवज्रोपेतं सदसः स्वकीयात्स्वर्गाख्यात्स्थानादनपच्युतं विनाशरहितं च । नेति समुच्चयार्थे । भूम भूम्ना महत्वेन युक्तमीमेनं त्वां जजान । अजीजनत् ॥ जन जनन इति धातुः ॥ द्यौद्योतमानस्ते तव जनिता जनयिता स प्रजापतिः सुवीरः शोभनपुत्रवानहमस्मिति मन्यत । अमन्यत । किंच इंद्रस्य कर्तृंद्रस्य जनयिता प्रजापतिः स्वपस्तमोऽत्यंतं शोभनकर्माभूत् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the Prajāpati who begot you (jajāna, "caused to be born"; the root is jana, "to be born/beget") is praised (svarya) by the priests and the like; he is possessed of a fine thunderbolt (suvajra), unfallen (anapacyuta) from his own seat called heaven, and indestructible. The word na is in the sense of "and" (conjunction). You, Indra, are endowed with greatness (bhūma). The shining one (dyau), your begetter (janitā), that Prajāpati, thought (manyata): "I have a fine son (suvīra)." Further, the maker (kartā) of Indra, the Prajāpati who begot Indra, became (abhūt) exceedingly skilled in good works (svapastama).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • (O Indra) यः (yaḥ)—which Prajāpati
  • स्वर्यं (svaryaṃ)—one praised by the priests
  • सुवज्रं (suvajraṃ)—one endowed with an excellent thunderbolt
  • सदसः (sadasaḥ)—from his own place, heaven
  • अनपच्युतं (anapacyutaṃ)—one who suffers no fall
  • भूम (bhūma)—endowed with greatness
  • ईं (īṃ)—you, who are Indra
  • जजान (jajāna)—created; such a one
  • द्यौः (dyauḥ)—the shining one
  • ते जनिता (te janitā)—your begetter, Prajāpati
  • सुवीरः (suvīraḥ)—that he had obtained an excellent son
  • मन्यत (manyata)—understood
  • इंद्रस्य (iṃdrasya)—of Indra
  • कर्ता (kartā)—the begetter, Prajāpati
  • स्वपस्तमः (svapastamaḥ)—as the doer of an excellent work
  • भूत् (bhūt)—he became
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Prajāpati who created you, Indra, who are praised by the priests, endowed with an excellent thunderbolt, without fall from your own place, heaven, and endowed with greatness—that shining Prajāpati, your begetter, understood that he had obtained an excellent son. Prajāpati, the begetter of Indra, became the doer of an excellent work.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Heaven, your progenitor, conceived (I have obtained) a worthy son; the maker of Indra was the accomplisher of a most excellent work; he who begot the adorable (Indra), armed with the thunderbolt, irremovable from his station, and endowed with greatness.

p. 963

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

य एक॑ इच्छा॒वय॑ति॒ प्र भूमा॒ राजा॑ कृष्णी॒नां पु॑रुहू॒त ॑ इंद्रः ।
स॒त्यमे॑न॒मनु॒ विश्वे॑ मदंति रा॒तिं दे॒वस्य॑ गृण॒तो म॒घोनः॑॥

ya eka icchāvayati pra bhūmā rājā kṛṣṇīnāṃ puruhūta
iṃdraḥ |
satyamenamanu viśve madaṃti rātiṃ devasya gṛṇato maghonaḥ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

यः । एकः । इत् । च्यवयति । प्र । भूम । राजा । कृष्टीनां । पुरुहूतः । इंद्रः ।
सत्यं । एनं । अनु । विश्वे । मदंति । रातिं । देवस्य । गृणतः । मघोनः ॥ ५ ॥

yaḥ | ekaḥ | it | cyavayati | pra | bhūma | rājā | kṛṣṭīnāṃ | puruhūtaḥ | iṃdraḥ |
satyaṃ | enaṃ | anu | viśve | madaṃti | rātiṃ | devasya | gṛṇataḥ | maghonaḥ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

कृष्णीनां सर्वासां प्रजानां राजा प्रभुः पुरुहूतो बहुभिराहूत एक इद्देवानां मध्यॆ मुख्य एव य इंद्रो भूम भूतं निष्पन्नं शत्रुभ्यो भयं प्र च्यावयति । प्रकर्षेण नाशयति । विश्वे सर्वॆ यजमाना मघोनो मघवतः । हनिर्लक्षणधनवत इत्यर्थः । देवस्येंद्रसमाश्रयात् द्योतमानस्य गृणतः स्तुवतो रातिं बंधुमेनमिंद्रमनु लक्ष्मीकृत्य सत्यमेव नदंति । स्तुवंति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is the king, the lord of all subjects (kṛṣṭi), invoked by many (puruhūta), alone (eka it) the chief among the gods. He utterly destroys (pra cyāvayati) the bhūma, the fear that has arisen from enemies. All sacrificers, maghonaḥ, that is, wealthy, possessed of wealth characterised by oblation, aiming at (anu) this Indra, who is the friend (rāti, "bandhu") of the shining (devasya, through resorting to Indra) praiser (gṛṇataḥ), verily praise him (he reads nadanti, "they praise").NOTE

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • कृष्णीनां (kṛṣṇīnāṃ)—of all subjects
  • राजा (rājā)—the lord
  • पुरुहूतः (puruhūtaḥ)—one invoked by many
  • एक इत् (eka it)—chief of all gods, men and the rest
  • यः इंद्रः (yaḥ iṃdraḥ)—which Indra
  • भूम (bhūma)—the fear arising from enemies
  • प्र च्यावयति (pra cyāvayati)—destroys; such a one
  • मघोनः (maghonaḥ)—possessing wealth in the form of oblations
  • देवस्य (devasya)—shining
  • गृणतः (gṛṇataḥ)—to the praiser
  • रातिं (rātiṃ)—a friend
  • एनं अनु (enaṃ anu)—aiming at this Indra
  • सत्यं (satyaṃ)—in truth
  • विश्वे (viśve)—all sacrificers too
  • मदंति (madaṃti)—praise
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All sacrificers praise in truth this Indra, who is lord of all subjects, invoked by many, chief of all gods, men and the rest, who destroys the fear arisen from enemies, and who is a friend to the praiser, who is shining and possesses wealth in the form of oblations.

p. 964

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

All men, praising the munificence of the divine Maghavan, verily glorify him who alone casts down many, Indra, the king of men, the adored of many.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒त्रा सोमा॑ अभवन्नस्य॒ विश्वे॑ स॒त्रा मदा॑सो बृह॒तो ॑ मदिस्थाः ।
स॒त्राभ॑वो॒ वसु॑पति॒र्वसू॑नां॒ दत्ते॒ विश्वा॑ अधिथा इंद्र कृ॒ष्टीः॥

satrā somā abhavannasya viśve satrā madāso bṛhato
madisthāḥ |
satrābhavo vasupatirvasūnāṃ datte viśvā adhithā iṃdra kṛṣṭīḥ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सत्रा । सोमाः । अभवन् । अस्य । विश्वे । सत्रा । मदासः । बृहतः । मदिष्टाः ।
सत्रा । अभवः । वसुपतिः । वसूनां । दत्ते । विश्वाः । अधिथाः । इंद्र । कृष्टीः ॥ ६ ॥

satrā | somāḥ | abhavan | asya | viśve | satrā | madāsaḥ | bṛhataḥ | madiṣṭāḥ |
satrā | abhavaḥ | vasupatiḥ | vasūnāṃ | datte | viśvāḥ | adhithāḥ | iṃdra | kṛṣṭīḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

विश्वे सर्वॆ सोमा अस्येंद्रस्य सत्रा । सत्रेति सत्यनामैतत् । सत्यमेव प्रभूता अभवन् । किंच मदासो मदा मदकराः सोमा बृहतो महतोऽस्येंद्रस्य मदिष्टा मादयितृतमाः सत्रा सत्यमेवाभवन् । हे इंद्र त्वं वसुपतिर्धनपतिः । न केवलं धनपतिः किंतु वसूनां सर्वेषां पश्वादीनां धनानां पतिः सत्रा सत्यमेवाभवः । भवसि । हे इंद्र त्वं दत्ते धने निमित्तभूते सति विश्वाः सर्वाः कृष्टीः स्तोत्रिः प्रजा अधिथाः । धारयसि ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

All the Soma-offerings of this Indra were truly (satrā; he says "satrā" is a name for truth) abundant. Further, the intoxicating (madāsaḥ) Soma-offerings were truly the most exhilarating (madiṣṭhāḥ) to the great Indra. O Indra, you are lord of wealth (vasupati); not only lord of wealth, but truly lord of all vasu, all riches such as cattle. O Indra, when wealth is given as the cause, you uphold (adhithāḥ, "you support") all the subjects (kṛṣṭi), the praising people.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • विश्वे (viśve)—all
  • सोमाः (somāḥ)—the Soma-offerings
  • सत्रा (satrā)—truly
  • अस्य (asya)—belonging to Indra alone
  • अभवन् (abhavan)—became
  • मदासः (madāsaḥ)—the intoxicating Soma-offerings
  • बृहतः (bṛhataḥ)—to Indra, of mighty form
  • मदिष्टाः (madiṣṭāḥ)—as satisfying
  • सत्रा (satrā)—truly they became
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • (त्वं (tvaṃ)—you)
  • वसुपतिः (vasupatiḥ)—as lord of wealth
  • वसूनां (vasūnāṃ)—as lord also of all riches in the form of cattle and the like
  • सत्रा (satrā)—truly
  • अभवः (abhavaḥ)—you are
  • दत्ते (datte)—by reason of wealth (by giving)
  • विश्वाः कृष्टीः (viśvāḥ kṛṣṭīḥ)—all the subjects
  • अधिथाः (adhithāḥ)—you have upheld
  • अध (adha)—and
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • जायमानः (jāyamānaḥ)—having been born
  • प्रथमं (prathamaṃ)—at the very beginning
  • अमे (ame)—when the fear caused by Vṛtra arose
  • विश्वाः (viśvāḥ)—all

p. 965

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All the Soma-offerings truly became Indra's own. The intoxicating Soma-offerings truly became satisfying to the mighty Indra. O Indra, you are lord of wealth and lord of all wealth in the form of cattle and the like. By the giving of wealth you uphold all subjects (you nourish them).

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Truly are all libations his; the inebriating draughts are truly most exhilarating to the mighty Indra : truly are you the lord of wealth, of (all sorts of) treasures : you, Indra, support all people by the gift (of riches).

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

त्वमध॑ प्रथ॒मं जाय॑मा॒नोऽमे॒ विश्वा॑ अधिथा इंद्र कृ॒ष्टीः।
त्वं प्रति॑ प्र॒वत॑ आ॒शया॑न॒महिं॒ वज्रे॑ण मघव॒न्वि वृ॑श्चः ॥ ७ ॥

tvamadha prathamaṃ jāyamāno 'me viśvā adhithā iṃdra kṛṣṭīḥ|
tvaṃ prati pravata āśayānamahiṃ vajreṇa maghavanvi vṛścaḥ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

त्वं । अध । प्रथमं । जायमानः । अमे । विश्वाः । अधिथाः । इंद्र । कृष्टीः ।
त्वं । प्रति । प्रवतः । आशयानं । अहिं । वज्रेण । मघुवन् । वि । वृश्चः ॥ ७ ॥

tvaṃ | adha | prathamaṃ | jāyamānaḥ | ame | viśvāḥ | adhithāḥ | iṃdra | kṛṣṭīḥ |
tvaṃ | prati | pravataḥ | āśayānaṃ | ahiṃ | vajreṇa | maghuvan | vi | vṛścaḥ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अध अपि च प्रथममेव जायमानस्त्वममे वृत्रनिमित्ते भये सति विश्वाः सर्वाः कृष्टीः प्रजा अधिथाः । रक्षकत्वेन धारयसि । हे मघवन्थनवन्निंद्र त्वं प्रति प्रवतः प्रति प्रवणानुदकवतो देशान् लक्ष्मीकृत्याशयानमपां निरोधकमहिं वृत्रनामानमसुरं वज्रेण वि वृश्चः । व्यवृश्च ॥ छिन्नवानसि ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Adha means "and also". As soon as you were born, when there was fear because of Vṛtra (ame), you upheld (adhithāḥ) all the subjects (kṛṣṭi) as their protector. O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, you, aiming at the regions where the water runs downward (pratipravataḥ), cut with the thunderbolt Ahi, the asura named Vṛtra, who lay (āśayānam) blocking the waters.

p. 966

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as soon as you were born, you took under your protection all the subjects who were distressed by fear caused by Vṛtra. O wealthy Indra, you cut with the thunderbolt Vṛtra who lay blocking the flowing waterways.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra, as soon as you were born, you took the progeny who were afraid of Vritra under your protection. O Maghavan, you smote with your thunderbolt, Ahi, who was obstructing the flow of waters.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स॒त्रा॒हणं॒ दाधृ॑षिं॒ तुम्र॒मिंद्रं॑ म॒हाम॑पा॒रं वृ॑ष॒भं ॒॑ सुवज्रं ।
हंता॒ यो वृ॒त्रं सनि॑तो॒त वाजं॒ दाता॑ म॒घानि॑ म॒घवा॑ ॒॑ सुराधाः ॥ ८ ॥

satrāhaṇaṃ dādhṛṣiṃ tumramiṃdraṃ mahāmapāraṃ vṛṣabhaṃ
suvajraṃ |
haṃtā yo vṛtraṃ sanitota vājaṃ dātā maghāni maghavā
surādhāḥ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सत्राहनं । दधृषिं । तुम्रं । इंद्रं । महां । अपारं । वृषभं । सुवज्रं ।
हंता । यः । वृत्रं । सनिता । उत । वाजं । दाता । मघानि । मघवा । सुराधाः॥

satrāhanaṃ | dadhṛṣiṃ | tumraṃ | iṃdraṃ | mahāṃ | apāraṃ | vṛṣabhaṃ | suvajraṃ |
haṃtā | yaḥ | vṛtraṃ | sanitā | uta | vājaṃ | dātā | maghāni | maghavā | surādhāḥ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

इंद्रस्य वृत्रघ्नः पशौ सत्राहणमिति हविषोऽनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । सत्राहणं दादृषिं तुम्रमिंद्रं सहदानुं पुरुहूत क्षियंतं । आ. ३.८ । इति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal sacrifice to Indra as Vṛtra-slayer, "सत्राहणं (satrāhaṇaṃ)" is the anuvākyā of the oblation. It is also stated in the sūtra: सत्राहणं दादृषिं तुम्रमिंद्रं सहदानुं पुरुहूत क्षियंतं । आ. ३.८ । इति ॥ (satrāhaṇaṃ dādṛṣiṃ tumramiṃdraṃ sahadānuṃ puruhūta kṣiyaṃtaṃ | ā. 3.8 | iti ‖) (Ā. 3.8).

p. 967

Ṛk 8 (continued)

सत्राहणं बहूनां शत्रूणां हंतारं दाधृषिमत्यंतं धर्षकं तुम्रं । तुमिः प्रेरणकर्मा । शत्रूणां प्रेरकं महां महांतमपारमपरिमाणं । विनाशरहितमित्यर्थः । वृषभं कामानां वर्षितारं सुवज्रं शोभनेन वज्रेणोपेतमिंद्रं । वयं स्तोतारः स्तुमेति शेषः । य इंद्रो वृत्रं वृत्रनामानमसुरं हंता हिंसिता भवति । उतापि च य इंद्रो वाजमन्नं सनिता दाता भवति । सुराधाः शोभनधनयुक्तो यो मघवेंद्रो मघानि धनानि दाता भवति । तमिंद्रं स्तुमेति पूर्णेन्वयः ॥ अत्र सर्वत्र तृनंतत्वान्न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठीप्रतिषेधे सति द्वितीयैव भवति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses सत्राहणं (satrāhaṇaṃ) as the slayer of many enemies; दाधृषिं (dādhṛṣiṃ) as the extremely bold one, the assailant; तुम्रं (tumraṃ) as the impeller of enemies, since the root तुमिः (tumiḥ) has the sense of impelling. महां (mahāṃ) means great, and अपारं (apāraṃ) unmeasured, that is, free from destruction. kṛṣabhaṃ is not in the text; वृषभं (vṛṣabhaṃ) means the showerer of desires, and सुवज्रं (suvajraṃ) Indra endowed with a fine thunderbolt. "We, the praisers, praise" is the word to be supplied. He who is the slayer of Vṛtra, the asura of that name, and he who is the giver of वाजं (vājaṃ), food; सुराधाः (surādhāḥ) means endowed with fine wealth; and Maghavan Indra is the giver of riches. "We praise that Indra" completes the construction. Throughout, because the words end in the affix tṛn, the genitive is barred and only the accusative occurs.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • सत्राहणं (satrāhaṇaṃ)—the destroyer of many enemies
  • दाधृषिं (dādhṛṣiṃ)—the subduer of enemies
  • तुम्रं (tumraṃ)—the harmer of enemies
  • महां (mahāṃ)—the great one
  • अपारं (apāraṃ)—the one without limit
  • वृषभं (vṛṣabhaṃ)—the showerer of desires
  • सुवज्रं (suvajraṃ)—the one endowed with the excellent thunderbolt (and)
  • यं (yaṃ)—who
  • वृत्रं (vṛtraṃ)—Vṛtra
  • हंता (haṃtā)—has destroyed
  • उत (uta)—and
  • (यः (yaḥ)—who)
  • वाजं (vājaṃ)—to food
  • सनिता (sanitā)—is the giver; such a one
  • सुराधाः (surādhāḥ)—endowed with excellent wealth
  • (यः (yaḥ)) मघवा (maghavā)—(which) Indra
  • मघानि (maghāni)—riches
  • दाता (dātā)—gives; such a one
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—Indra (we shall praise)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We shall praise Indra, who has destroyed many enemies, subdues enemies, harms enemies, is without limit, showers desires, is endowed with the excellent thunderbolt, destroys Vṛtra, gives food, and, being endowed with excellent wealth, gives riches.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

(We praise) the slayer of many foes, the courageous, the discomfiter (of enemies), the great, the unbounded, the showerer (of benefits), the wielder of the bright thunderbolt, him who is the destroyer of Vritra, the bestower of food, the giver of wealth, Maghavan the possessor of riches .

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice offered to Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, when the oblation is offered, this Ṛk beginning सत्राहणं (satrāhaṇaṃ) is to be used as the Anuvākyā mantra. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra सत्राहणं दाधृषिं तुम्रमिंद्रं सहदानुं पुरुहूत क्षियंतं (satrāhaṇaṃ dādhṛṣiṃ tumramiṃdraṃ sahadānuṃ puruhūta kṣiyaṃtaṃ) (Ā. 3-8).

p. 968

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒यं वृत॑श्चातयते समी॒चीर्य आ॒जिषु॑ म॒घवा॑ शृ॒ण्व एकः॑।
अ॒यं वाजं॑ भरति॒ यं स॒नोत्य॒स्य प्रि॒यासः॑ स॒ख्ये स्या॑म ॥९॥

ayaṃ vṛtaścātayate samīcīrya ājiṣu maghavā śṛṇva ekaḥ|
ayaṃ vājaṃ bharati yaṃ sanotyasya priyāsaḥ sakhye syāma ‖9‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अयं । वृतः । चातयते । संईचीः। यः । आजिषु । मघना । शृण्वे । एकः ।
अयं । वाजं । भरति । यं । सनोति । अस्य । प्रियासः । सख्ये । स्याम ॥ ९ ॥

ayaṃ | vṛtaḥ | cātayate | saṃīcīḥ| yaḥ | ājiṣu | maghanā | śṛṇve | ekaḥ |
ayaṃ | vājaṃ | bharati | yaṃ | sanoti | asya | priyāsaḥ | sakhye | syāma ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

मघवा धनवान्य इंद्रआजिषु संग्रामेष्वेको मुख्य एव शृण्वे । श्रूयते। अयमिंद्रः सविाचीः संगता वृतः । वृण्वंत्याच्छादयंति लोकानिति वृतः शत्रुसेनाः । ताश्चातयते । नाशयति । अयमिंद्रो यं वाजं यदन्नं सनोति । यजमानाय ददाति । तं वाजं भरति । यजमानस्य तवन्नं दातुं बिभर्ति । स्तोतारो वयमस्यॆवंभूतस्येंद्रस्य सख्ये सखत्वे प्रियासः प्रियाः स्याम । भवेनु ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Maghavan, the wealthy Indra, is heard of as the one chief in battles. This Indra destroys the assembled वृतः (vṛtaḥ); वृतः (vṛtaḥ) are the enemy armies, because they cover (vṛṇvaṃti) the worlds. He destroys them. The food that this Indra bestows on the sacrificer, that food he bears, that is, he carries it to give it to the sacrificer. We, the praisers, may we be dear in the friendship of this Indra, such as he is. "May we be" is the sense.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मघवा (maghavā)—the wealthy
  • यः (yaḥ)—which Indra
  • आजिषु (ājiṣu)—in battles
  • एकः (ekaḥ)—as the one chief leader
  • शृण्वे (śṛṇve)—is renowned
  • अयं (ayaṃ)—that same Indra
  • समीचीः (samīcīḥ)—that are gathered together
  • वृतः (vṛtaḥ)—the enemy armies
  • चातयते (cātayate)—destroys
  • अयं (ayaṃ)—this same Indra
  • यं वाजं (yaṃ vājaṃ)—what food
  • सनोति (sanoti)—he gives to the sacrificer
  • भरति (bharati)—(that) he holds ready to bestow
  • अस्य (asya)—of this Indra
  • सख्ये (sakhye)—by reason of friendship
  • प्रियासः (priyāsaḥ)—dear to him
  • स्याम (syāma)—may we be
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Indra, the wealthy, who is renowned in battles as the one chief leader, destroys the enemy armies that are gathered together. The very food that this Indra gives to the sacrificer, that he holds ready to bestow on him. By reason of the friendship of this Indra, may we be dear to him.

p. 969

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

This Maghavan, who destroys assembled hosts, is he who is renowned as chief in battles : he brings the food which he bestows (upon the worship- per) : may we be held dear in his friendship.

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒यं शृ॑ण्वे॒ अध॒ जय॑न्नु॒त घ्नन्व॒यमु॒त प्र कृ॑णुते ॒ यु॒धा गाः ।
य॒दा स॒त्यं कृ॑णु॒ते म॒न्युमिंद्रो॒ विश्वं॑ दृ॒ळं भ॑यत॒ ॑ एजदस्मात्॥ १० ॥

ayaṃ śṛṇve adha jayannuta ghnanvayamuta pra kṛṇute
yudhā gāḥ |
yadā satyaṃ kṛṇute manyumiṃdro viśvaṃ dṛḷaṃ bhayata
ejadasmāt‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अयं । शृण्वे । अध । जयन् । उत । घ्नन् । अयं । उत । प्र । कृणुते । युधा।
गाः ।
यदा । सत्यं । कृणुते । मन्युं । इंद्रः । विश्वं । दृळं । भयते । एजत् । अस्मात्॥

ayaṃ | śṛṇve | adha | jayan | uta | ghnan | ayaṃ | uta | pra | kṛṇute | yudhā|
gāḥ |
yadā | satyaṃ | kṛṇute | manyuṃ | iṃdraḥ | viśvaṃ | dṛḷaṃ | bhayate | ejat | asmāt‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अधापि च अयमिंद्रो जयन् शत्रुन्विजयन् शृण्वे । श्रूयते । सर्वत्र प्रख्यातो भवति । उतापि च घ्नन् शत्रुन्हिंसन् सर्वत्र श्रूयते । उतापि चायमिंद्रो युधा यद्धेन गाः पशून्पृ कृणुते । शत्रुसकाशादाहरति । किंच इंद्रो यदा मन्युं कोपं सत्यमेव कृणुते । द्विषदर्थं करोति । तदानीं दृढं स्थिरं स्थावररूपमेजत्कंपमानं जंगमरूपं च विश्वं समस्तं जगदस्मादिंद्राध्वयते । बिभेति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Moreover this Indra, conquering enemies, is heard of, that is, is famed everywhere; and slaying enemies he is heard of everywhere. This Indra also by battle (युधा (yudhā)) takes गाः (gāḥ), cattle: he carries them off from the enemy's possession. Further, when Indra makes his anger (मन्युं (manyuṃ)) true, that is, acts for the sake of the foe, then the whole world, firm, that is, of stationary form, and एजत् (ejat), trembling, that is, of moving form, fears this Indra.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अध (adha)—and
  • अयं (ayaṃ)—this Indra
  • जयन् (jayan)—in conquering the enemy (as victorious)
  • शृण्वे (śṛṇve)—is renowned
  • उत (uta)—and
  • घ्नन् (ghnan)—he is renowned also as the destroyer of enemies
  • उत (uta)—and
  • अयं (ayaṃ)—this Indra
  • युधा (yudhā)—by battle
  • गाः (gāḥ)—cows

p. 970

  • प्र कृणुते (pra kṛṇute)—carries them off from the enemies
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • यदा (yadā)—when
  • मन्युं (manyuṃ)—anger
  • सत्यं कृणुते (satyaṃ kṛṇute)—he makes manifest in truth (then)
  • दृळं (dṛḷaṃ)—that which is immovably firm
  • एजत् (ejat)—and that which is of moving nature
  • विश्वं (viśvaṃ)—the whole world, consisting of the stationary and the moving
  • अस्मात् (asmāt)—from this Indra
  • भयते (bhayate)—is seized with fear
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Indra is renowned at the time of battle as the conqueror of the enemy and the destroyer of enemies. And Indra fights and carries off cattle from the enemies. When this Indra manifests his anger in truth, then the whole world, both what is immovably firm and what is of moving nature, is seized with fear of this Indra.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

This (Indra), is renowned, whether conquering or slaying (his foes), or whether in conflict he recovers the cattle : when Indra truly entertains anger, all that is stationary or moveable is in fear of him.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

समिंद्रो॒ गा अ॑जय॒त्सं हिर॑ण्या॒ सम॑श्वि॒या म॒घवा॒ यो ह॑ ॒ पूर्वीः ।
ए॒भिर्नृभि॒र्नृत॑मो अस्य शा॒कै रा॒यो वि॑भ॒क्ता सं॑भ॒रश्च॒ वस्वः॑ ॥

samiṃdro gā ajayatsaṃ hiraṇyā samaśviyā maghavā yo ha
pūrvīḥ |
ebhirnṛbhirnṛtamo asya śākai rāyo vibhaktā saṃbharaśca vasvaḥ ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सं । इंद्रः । गाः । अजयत् । सं । हिरण्या । सं । अश्विया । मघवा । यः । ह ।
पूर्वीः ।
एभिः । नृभिः । नृतमः । अस्य । शाकैः । रायः । विभक्ता । संभरः । च । वस्वः ॥११॥

saṃ | iṃdraḥ | gāḥ | ajayat | saṃ | hiraṇyā | saṃ | aśviyā | maghavā | yaḥ | ha |
pūrvīḥ |
ebhiḥ | nṛbhiḥ | nṛtamaḥ | asya | śākaiḥ | rāyaḥ | vibhaktā | saṃbharaḥ | ca | vasvaḥ ‖11‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यो ह यः खलु मघवा धनवानिंद्रोगा असुराणां समजयत् । सम्मक् जितवान् भवति । किंच हिरण्या हिरण्यानि हितरमणीयानि शत्रुसंबंधीनि धनानि समअ. ३. ५. व. २३ ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 97i यत् । तथा अश्वियाश्वियानि शत्रुसंबंधिनोऽश्वसमूहान् सम्यक् जयति स्म । तथा पूर्विर्बह्वीः शत्रुसेनाः समजयत् । इंद्रः सर्वान् शत्रून् जित्वा सकलमपि पश्वादिधनमपहृतवानित्यर्थः । शाकैः सामर्थ्य्यन्रृतमो नेतृतमः पश्वादीनामतिशयेन निर्वाहकः स इंद्र एभिन्नृभिर्नेतृभिः स्तोतृभिः स्तुतः सन् अस्य रायः पश्वादिरूपस्य धनस्य विभक्ता स्तोतृभ्यो विभागस्य कर्ता । दाता भवतीत्यर्थः । किंच वस्वो वसुनो धनस्य संभरश्च संभर्ता धारकश्च भवति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Maghavan, the wealthy Indra, who has fully conquered the गाः (gāḥ), the cattle of the asuras. हिरण्या (hiraṇyā) are हिरण्यानि (hiraṇyāni), wealth that is beneficial and delightful, belonging to the enemy; these he conquered completely. Likewise अश्विया (aśviyā) are अश्विया (aśviyā), the enemy's herds of horses; he conquered them completely. Likewise he conquered पूर्वीः (pūrvīḥ), the many enemy armies. The sense is that Indra, having conquered all enemies, carried off all their wealth in cattle and the rest. शाकैः (śākaiḥ) means by his powers; नृतमः (nṛtamaḥ) is the foremost leader, the one who in the highest degree brings about cattle and the rest. That Indra, praised by these leaders, the praisers, is विभक्ता (vibhaktā) of this रायः (rāyaḥ), the wealth in the form of cattle and the rest, that is, the maker of its division among the praisers: he is the giver. And further he is संभरः (saṃbharaḥ) of वस्वः (vasvaḥ), the wealth: its bearer and holder.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः (yaḥ)—which
  • मघवा (maghavā)—wealthy
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • गाः (gāḥ)—the cows of the asuras
  • सं अजयत् (saṃ ajayat)—conquered completely
  • हिरण्या (hiraṇyā)—their wealth
  • सं (saṃ) (अजयत् (ajayat))—seized completely
  • अश्विया (aśviyā)—took all their horses completely (and)
  • पूर्विः (pūrviḥ)—conquered their boundless armies; that Indra
  • शाकैः (śākaiḥ)—endowed with powers
  • नृतमः (nṛtamaḥ)—and being the leader
  • एभिः नृभिः (ebhiḥ nṛbhiḥ)—(praised) by these human praisers
  • अस्य रायः (asya rāyaḥ)—of this wealth
  • विभक्ता (vibhaktā)—becomes the divider
  • वस्वः (vasvaḥ)—of this same wealth
  • संभरश्च (saṃbharaśca)—he becomes also the holder
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wealthy Indra who has completely conquered all the boundless enemy armies, carried off the cows and horses of the asuras, and completely seized all their wealth, that same Indra, endowed with powers and being the leader, praised by these human praisers, becomes the giver of that wealth to the sacrificers. And he becomes also the holder of the wealth.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra, the lord of opulence, who has overcome many (enemies) has completely won (their) cattle, (their) gold, (their) horses : chief leader by his energies, praised by these his worshippers, he is the distributor of riches, the bestower of wealth.

kiyatsvi diṃdro adhyeti mātuḥ kiyatpiturjanituryo

yaḥ | asya | śuṣmaṃ | muhukaiḥ | iyarti | vātaḥ | na | jūtaḥ | stanayatbhiḥ |
abhraiḥ ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

य इंद्रो मातुर्जनन्याः सकाशात्कियत्स्विद्यावद्बलमध्येति । अधिगच्छति । पितुः सकाशात्कियद्यावद्बलमधिगच्छति । य इंद्रो जनितुर्जयितुर्यस्मात्पजापतेः सकाशादिदं दृश्यमानं जगज्जजान ! अजनयत् । य इंद्रस्तस्मात्पजापतेः सकाशादस्य जगतः शुष्मं यावद्बलं मुहुकैर्मुहुर्मुहुरियर्ति । प्रेरयति । स्तनयद्धिर्गर्जद्दिरभ्रैर्मेघैर्जूतः प्रेरितो वातो न वायुरिव तथा स इंद्रः स्तोतृभिर्जूतः प्रेरितो हविष्पदानार्थमाहूतो भवति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who derives from his mother, the one who bore him, कियत्स्वित् (kiyatsvit), as much strength as there is; and from his father he obtains as much strength as there is. The Indra from whom, as जनितुः (janituḥ), the begetter, namely Prajāpati, this visible world was born, that is, was produced: that Indra, from that Prajāpati, sets in motion again and again (मुहुकैः (muhukaiḥ)) शुष्मं (śuṣmaṃ), the strength, of this world. As the wind (वातो न (vāto na)) is driven by thundering (स्तनयद्भिः (stanayadbhiḥ)) clouds, so that Indra is impelled by the praisers and, being invoked, comes to bestow the oblation.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः (yaḥ)—which Indra
  • जनितुः (janituḥ)—with the help of Prajāpati, the begetter of the world
  • जजान (jajāna)—created this world
  • यः (yaḥ)—which Indra
  • स्तनयद्भिः (stanayadbhiḥ)—by thundering
  • अभ्रैः (abhraiḥ)—clouds
  • जूतः (jūtaḥ)—impelled
  • वातो न (vāto na)—like the wind
  • अस्य (asya)—of this world
  • शुष्मं (śuṣmaṃ)—the strength
  • मुहुकैः (muhukaiḥ)—again and again
  • इयर्ति (iyarti)—sets in motion; (that) इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—that same Indra
  • मातुः (mātuḥ)—from his mother
  • कियत् स्वित् (kiyat svit)—some strength
  • अध्येति (adhyeti)—obtains
  • कियत् (kiyat)—some strength
  • पितुः (pituḥ)—obtains from his father
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who created this world with the help of Prajāpati, the begetter of the world, and who, like the wind driven by thundering clouds, sets in motion the strength of this world again and again, that same Indra obtains some strength from his mother. And he obtains some strength from his father also.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Some portion (of his strength) Indra derives from his mother, some- portion from his father : he who, through his progenitor, has begotten (the

p. 973

world), and animates its vigour repeatedly, as the wind is driven by thundering clouds.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

क्षि॒यंतं॑ त्व॒मक्षि॑यंतं कृणो॒तीय॑र्ति रे॒णुं म॒घवा॑ ॒॑ समोहं ।
वि॒भं॒ज॒नुर॒शनि॑माइव॒ द्यौरु॒त स्तो॒तारं॑ म॒घवा॒ वसौ॑ धात्॥

kṣiyaṃtaṃ tvamakṣiyaṃtaṃ kṛṇotīyarti reṇuṃ maghavā

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

क्षियंतं । त्वं । अक्षियंतं । कृणोति । इयर्ति । रेणुं । मघवा । संओहं ।
विभंजनुः । अशनिमान्इव । द्यौः । उत । स्तोतारं । मघवा । वसौ । धात् ॥

kṣiyaṃtaṃ | tvaṃ | akṣiyaṃtaṃ | kṛṇoti | iyarti | reṇuṃ | maghavā | saṃohaṃ |
vibhaṃjanuḥ | aśanimāniva | dyauḥ | uta | stotāraṃ | maghavā | vasau | dhāt ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

मघवा धनवानिंद्रः क्षियंतं धनराहित्येन क्षीयमाणं त्वमेकं जनमक्षियंतं धनेनाक्षीयमाणं कृणोति । करोति । अकिंचनः कश्चित्पुरुष इंद्रं स्तुत्वा धनसमृद्धोऽभवदित्यर्थः । अशनिमानशनिना युक्तो द्यौरिवांतरिक्षमिन विभंजनुः शत्रूणां विशेषेण भंजको मघवेंद्रः समोहं समूढं रेणुं पापमियर्ति ! स्तोतुः सकाशात्पेरयति । उतापि च मघवा धनवानिंद्रः स्तोतारं वसौ धने धात् । अधात् । निदधाति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Maghavan, the wealthy Indra, makes क्षियंतं (kṣiyaṃtaṃ), one who is declining through want of wealth, त्वं (tvaṃ), a single man, अक्षियंतं (akṣiyaṃtaṃ), one not declining but possessed of wealth. The sense is that some penniless man, having praised Indra, became rich in wealth. Like द्यौः (dyauḥ), the sky, furnished with the thunderbolt (अशनिमान् (aśanimān)), Indra Maghavan, विभंजनुः (vibhaṃjanuḥ), the special breaker of enemies, drives away रेणुं (reṇuṃ), the dust, that is, sin, समोहं (samohaṃ), that has been piled together: he sets it in motion away from the praiser. And further Maghavan, the wealthy Indra, places the praiser in वसौ (vasau), wealth: धात् (dhāt) is "has placed", he establishes. NOTE

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मघवा (maghavā)—(O Indra) you who are wealthy
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • क्षियंतं (kṣiyaṃtaṃ)—the man who is perishing through want of wealth
  • अक्षियंतं (akṣiyaṃtaṃ)—so that, not perishing, he becomes prosperous
  • कृणोति (kṛṇoti)—you make
  • अशनिमान् (aśanimān)—furnished with lightning
  • द्यौः (dyauḥ) (इव (iva))—like the sky
  • विभंजनुः (vibhaṃjanuḥ)—the destroyer of enemies
  • मघवा (maghavā)—Indra
  • समोहं (samohaṃ)—that has been gathered together
  • रेणुं (reṇuṃ)—sin
  • इयर्ति (iyarti)—drives away
  • उत (uta)—and
  • मघवा (maghavā)—the wealthy Indra
  • स्तोतारं (stotāraṃ)—the praiser
  • वसौ (vasau)—in the midst of wealth
  • धात् (dhāt)—places

p. 974

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are wealthy make a man who is perishing for lack of wealth not perish but become well nourished. Indra, the destroyer of enemies, like the sky with its thunderbolt, drives away the sin that has been heaped up together; and Indra the wealthy sets the worshipper amid riches.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

You are the Maghavan who makes one man destitute, another prosperous, who (scatters from his worshipper) the accumulated dust (of sin,) the destroyer ( of foes ), like the heaven with the thunderbolt, Maghavan conducts his worshipper to wealth

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

ayaṃ cakramiṣaṇatsūryasya naitaśaṃ rīramatsṛmāṇaṃ |

आ । कृष्णः । ईं । जुहुराणः । जिघर्ति । त्वचः । बुद्धे । रजसः । अस्य । योनौ ॥ १४ ॥

ayaṃ | cakraṃ | iṣaṇat | sūryasya | ni | etaśaṃ | rīramat | sasyamāṇaṃ |
ā | kṛṣṇaḥ | īṃ | juhurāṇaḥ | jigharti | tvacaḥ | buddhe | rajasaḥ | asya | yonau ‖ 14 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानमित्यर्धर्चॆ । ऋग्वे. १-६१-१५ । पूर्वं काचिदाख्यायिका सूचिता । अत्राप्ययं चक्रमिति पूर्वार्धे सा सूच्यते । स्वश्वनामा कश्चिद्राजा । स च पुत्रार्थं सूर्यमुपास्ते । स च सूर्यः पुत्ररूपेण स्वयमेव तत्रोत्पन्नः सन् एतशाख्येन महर्षिणा सार्धं युद्धं चकार । तदानीं स यषिर्युद्दे जयार्थमिंद्रं तुष्टाव । स इंद्रस्तेन स्तूयमानः सन् स्वश्वपुत्रस ूर्यस्य संबंधिनः संग्रामादेनमपालयदिति । अयमिंद्रः सूर्यस्य चित्रमायुधमिषणत् । प्रैरयत् । ससृमाणु युद्धार्थं सरंतं गच्छंतमेतरना-

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that in the half-verse प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं (praitaśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ) (Ṛg. 1-61-15) a certain story was already hinted at, and that it is hinted at here too in the first half of the verse beginning अयं चक्रं (ayaṃ cakraṃ). A king named Svaśva worshipped Sūrya for the sake of a son. Sūrya himself was born there in the form of a son and fought a battle with the great sage named Etaśa. Then that sage praised Indra for victory in the battle. Indra, being praised by him, protected him from the battle with Sūrya, who was the son of Svaśva. Then the verse: this Indra hurled the wondrous weapon of Sūrya; he restrained the sage called Etaśa, who was going forth to the fight (the text continues on the next page).

p. 975

मानमृषिं नि रीरमत् । न्यरीरमत् । निवारितवान् । जुहुराणः कुटिलं यथा भवति तथा संचरन् कृष्णः कृष्णवर्णो मेघस्त्वचस्तेजसो बुद्धे मूलभूते रजसोऽस्योदकस्य योन्सौ स्थानेंतरिक्षे स्थितमीमेनमिंद्रमा जिघर्ति। आसिंचति । शत्रूणां प्रेरिताच्चक्रादेस्रस्तं ररक्षेत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Etaśa was held back, restrained. Moving in a crooked course, the dark-coloured cloud, standing in the sky, which is the root of radiance and the birthplace of this water, sprinkles Indra. The meaning is: he protected him from the discus and other weapons hurled by the enemies.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अयं (ayaṃ)—this Indra
  • सूर्यस्य (sūryasya)—of Sūrya
  • चक्रं (cakraṃ)—the weapon called the discus
  • इषणत् (iṣaṇat)—hurled
  • सस्यमाणं (sasyamāṇaṃ)—who had set out for battle
  • एतशं (etaśaṃ)—the sage named Etaśa
  • नि रीरमत् (ni rīramat)—restrained
  • जुहुराणः (juhurāṇaḥ)—moving crookedly
  • कृष्णः (kṛṣṇaḥ)—the dark-coloured cloud
  • त्वचः (tvacaḥ)—of radiance
  • बुध्ने (budhne)—which is the root
  • अस्य रजसः (asya rajasaḥ)—of this water
  • योन्सौ (yonsau)—being in the sky, which is the place of origin
  • ईं (īṃ)—upon Indra
  • आ जिघर्ति (ā jigharti)—pours down rain and cools
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra hurled the weapon of Sūrya called the discus, and restrained the sage Etaśa who had set out for battle. The dark, crookedly moving cloud, being in the sky, which is the root of radiance and the birthplace of water, pours rain upon Indra and cools him.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

He has hurled the wheel ( of the chariot ) of the sun, and has stopped Etasa going forth to (battle): the dark undulating cloud bedews him, (staying) at the root of radiance in the regions of its waters ;

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The commentator indicates that there is an ancient story in the commentary on the Ṛk प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं (praitaśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-15) and explains it again here: स्वश्वनामा कश्चिद्राजा । स च पुत्रार्थं सूर्यमुपास्ते । स च सूर्यः पुत्ररूपेण स्वयमेव तत्रोत्पन्नः सन् एतशाख्येन महर्षिणा सार्धं युद्धं चकार । तदानीं स यषिर्युद्दे जयार्थमिंद्रं तुष्टाव । स इंद्रस्तेन स्तूयमानः सन् स्वश्वपुत्रस ूर्यस्य संबंधिनः संग्रामादेनमपालयदिति । (svaśvanāmā kaścidrājā | sa ca putrārthaṃ sūryamupāste | sa ca sūryaḥ putrarūpeṇa svayameva tatrotpannaḥ san etaśākhyena maharṣiṇā sārdhaṃ yuddhaṃ cakāra | tadānīṃ sa yaṣiryudde jayārthamiṃdraṃ tuṣṭāva | sa iṃdrastena stūyamānaḥ san svaśvaputrasa ūryasya saṃbaṃdhinaḥ saṃgrāmādenamapālayaditi |) (Sā. Bhā.). In ancient times there was a king named Svaśva. He worshipped Sūrya so that he might have a son. Then Sūrya himself was born to him as a son. While this son was fighting with a sage named Etaśa,

p. 976

that sage Etaśa praised Indra so that he might win the battle. Then Indra, pleased with his praise, protected the sage Etaśa in the battle connected with Svaśva's son. This matter is indicated in this Ṛk.

Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

असि॑क्न्यां॒ यज॑मानो॒ न होता॑ ॥ १५ ॥

asiknyāṃ yajamāno na hotā ‖ 15 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

असिक्नां । यजमानः । न । होता ॥ १५ ॥

asiknāṃ | yajamānaḥ | na | hotā ‖ 15 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

एकपदेयमृक् पूर्वर्चा सह दृष्टांतत्वेन संबद्यते । असिक्न्यां रात्रौ यजमानो न यजमान इव होता होतारमाह्वातारमुग्निं । द्वितीयार्थे प्रथमा । सोमेनासिंचति तद्वन्मेघ इंद्रमासिंचतीत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This one-word Ṛk is connected with the preceding verse as an illustration. असिक्न्यां (asiknyāṃ) means at night; यजमानो न (yajamāno na) means like a sacrificer; होता (hotā) is the Hotṛ, the caller, namely Agni; the nominative stands for the accusative. As the sacrificer sprinkles him with soma, so the cloud sprinkles Indra.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • असिक्नां (asiknāṃ)—at night
  • यजमानो होता न (yajamāno hotā na)—as the sacrificer pours ghee and the like on the Hotṛ, Agni
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the sacrificer at night-times pours ghee and the like on the Hotṛ, Agni, and becomes the cause of Agni's satisfaction, so the cloud poured rain and became the cause of Indra's satisfaction.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

As the sacrificer (pours the oblation) at night upon the fire.

Ṛk 16

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

ग॒व्यंत॒ इंद्रं॑ स॒ख्याय॒ विप्रा॑ अश्वा॒यंतो॒ वृष॑णं वा॒ज. ॑ यंतः ।

gavyaṃta iṃdraṃ sakhyāya viprā aśvāyaṃto vṛṣaṇaṃ vāja.
yaṃtaḥ |

p. 977

जनीयंतो जनिदामक्षितोतिमा च्यावयामोऽवते न
कोशं ॥ १६ ॥

janīyaṃto janidāmakṣitotimā cyāvayāmo 'vate na
kośaṃ ‖ 16 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

गव्यंतः । इंद्रं । सख्याय । विप्राः । अश्वयंतः । वृषणं । वाजयंतः ।
जन्सियंतः । जन्सिदां । अक्षितऊतिं । आ । च्यवयामः। अवते । न । कोशं ॥ १६ ॥

gavyaṃtaḥ | iṃdraṃ | sakhyāya | viprāḥ | aśvayaṃtaḥ | vṛṣaṇaṃ | vājayaṃtaḥ |
jansiyaṃtaḥ | jansidāṃ | akṣitaūtiṃ | ā | cyavayāmaḥ| avate | na | kośaṃ ‖ 16 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

गव्यंतो गा इच्छंतोऽश्वायंतोऽश्वानिच्छंतो वाजयंतो वाजमन्नमिच्छंतो जनीयंतो जायाश्चेच्छंतो विप्रा मेधाविनः स्तोतारो वयं सख्यायेंद्रसंबंधिने सखित्वाय वृषणं कामानां वर्षितारं जनिदां जाया. प्रदमक्षितोतिमक्षिणरक्षं । सर्वदा रक्षाकरमित्यर्थः । एवंभूतमिंद्रमा च्यावयामः । आगमयामः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अवते कूपे । अवत इति कूपनाम अवतोऽवटः क्रिविरिति कूपनामसु पाठात् । कोशं न जलोद्धरणपात्रमिव । पुरुषा जलोद्धरणपात्रं जलेन पूरयितुं कूपे यथाच्यावयंति तथा वयमाच्यावयाम इत्यर्थः 8

Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the wise praisers, desiring cattle, horses, food and wives, for friendship with Indra, bring to us Indra, the showerer of desires, the giver of wives, whose protection is unfailing, that is, always protecting. The illustration: as into a well, like a vessel for drawing water. As men lower a water-drawing vessel into a well to fill it with water, so we bring him. He cites the Nighaṇṭu reading of avato avaṭaḥ kriviḥ among the names of a well, to show that अवत (avata) is a name for a well.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • गव्यंतः (gavyaṃtaḥ)—those who wish for cows
  • अश्वायंतः (aśvāyaṃtaḥ)—those who wish for horses
  • वाजयंतः (vājayaṃtaḥ)—those who need food
  • जनीयंतः (janīyaṃtaḥ)—those eager to obtain wives
  • विप्राः (viprāḥ)—we, the wise (praisers)
  • सख्याय (sakhyāya)—to win friendship
  • वृषणं (vṛṣaṇaṃ)—showerer of desires
  • जनिदां (janidāṃ)—giver of wives
  • अक्षितोतिं (akṣitotiṃ)—giver of everlasting protection
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—Indra
  • अवते (avate)—into a well
  • कोशं न (kośaṃ na)—as one lowers a water vessel
  • आ च्यावयामः (ā cyāvayāmaḥ)—we urge him to come down to us
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We (the praisers), wise, wishing for cattle, horses, food and wives, to win friendship with Indra, urge Indra, the showerer of desires, the giver of wives, the giver of everlasting protection, to come down to us, as a water vessel is lowered into a well.

p. 978

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

May we (who are) wishing for cattle, for horses, for food, for wives, through his friendship induce Indra, the showerer ( of benefits ) the giver of wives, the unwearied granter (of protection) to come down, as a bucket (is lowered) into a well.

Ṛk 17

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

त्रा॒ता नो॑ बोधि॒ ददृ॑शान आ॒सिर॑भिख्या॒ता म॑र्डि॒ता सो॒म्यानां॑ ।
सखा॑ पि॒ता पि॒तृत॑मः पित्थ॒णां कर्ते॑मु लो॒कमु॑श॒ते व॑यो॒धाः॥ १७ ॥

trātā no bodhi dadṛśāna āsirabhikhyātā marḍitā somyānāṃ |
sakhā pitā pitṛtamaḥ pitthaṇāṃ kartemu lokamuśate vayodhāḥ‖ 17 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

त्राता । नः । बोधि । ददृशानः । आपिः । अभिख्याता । मर्डिता । सोम्यानां ।
सखा । पिता । पितृतमः । पित्थणां । कर्ता । ईं । ऊं इति । लोकं । उशते ।
वयोऽधाः ॥ १७ ॥

trātā | naḥ | bodhi | dadṛśānaḥ | āpiḥ | abhikhyātā | marḍitā | somyānāṃ |
sakhā | pitā | pitṛtamaḥ | pitthaṇāṃ | kartā | īṃ | ūṃ iti | lokaṃ | uśate |
vayo 'dhāḥ ‖ 17 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र आपिराप्तो ददृशानः सर्वं पालकत्वेन पश्यंत्वं नोऽस्माकं त्राता रक्षको बोधि । भव । किंच । अभिख्याताभिद्रष्टा मर्डिता सुखयिता सोम्यानां सोमार्हाणां यजमानादीनां सखा प्रजापतिना समानख्यातिः पिता पालकः । केवलं पालको न किंतु पित्यणां पालकानां मध्यॆ पितृतमोऽतिशयेन पालकः कर्तेमु पित्यणां स्रष्टा च त्वं लोकं स्वर्गादिलोकमुशते कामयमानाय स्तोत्रे वयोधाः । वय इत्यन्ननामैतत् । अन्नप्रदो भव ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are a kinsman and see all as protector, be our saviour. Further: be the overseer and giver of happiness to those fit for soma, the sacrificers and others; a friend, of fame equal to Prajāpati; a protector. Not merely a protector: among protectors the supreme protector, and the maker of the protectors; to the praiser desiring the world, heaven and the rest, be the वयोधाः (vayodhāḥ). वयः (vayaḥ) is a name for food; be the giver of food.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • (O Indra) आपिः (āpiḥ)—kinsman to us
  • ददृशानः (dadṛśānaḥ)—you who look kindly upon all
  • नः (naḥ)—to us
  • तात्रा (tātrā)—that you should be the protector
  • भोधि (bhodhi)—know (be the protector)

p. 979

  • अभिख्याता (abhikhyātā)—one who looks after all of us like a supervisor
  • मर्डिता (marḍitā)—giver of happiness
  • सोम्यानां (somyānāṃ)—to the sacrificers worthy to offer soma
  • सखा (sakhā)—friend
  • पिता (pitā)—protector
  • पित्थणां (pitthaṇāṃ)—among protectors
  • पितृतमः (pitṛtamaḥ)—the best protector
  • कर्ता ईं उ (kartā īṃ u)—you, the creator of all
  • लोकं (lokaṃ)—the world, heaven and the rest
  • उशते (uśate)—to the praiser who desires
  • वयोधाः (vayodhāḥ)—be the giver of food
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are our kinsman and look kindly on all, be our protector. You who look after all of us like a supervisor, give happiness, are a friend to the sacrificers worthy of offering soma, a protector, the best protector among all protectors, and the creator of all, be the giver of food to the praiser who desires heaven and the other worlds.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Be our preserver, you who are looking (benevolently upon) all ; a kinsman (to us); a supervisor (of all things), a bestower of felicity on those who are worthy (to offer) libations ; a friend, a protector, a defender in the highest degree among defenders, a creater : (be you, who bestow) the world of heaven upon him who desires it, the giver to us of food.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र त्वं सखीयतां सखित्वमिच्छतामस्माकमविता रक्षिता बोधि। भव। तथा गृणानः 8 स्तूयमानस्त्वं सखा भव । हे इंद्र स्तुवते स्तुतिं कुर्वते मह्यं वयोऽन्नं धाः । अधाः । धेहि । हे इंद्र सबाधो बाधासहिता वयं हि वयं

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, be the protector of us who desire friendship. Being praised, be our friend. O Indra, to me who praise you, give food. O Indra, we, together with our troubles, … (the block breaks off here in this window).

p. 980

खलु ते त्वामा चक्रम । आह्वयामः । किं कुर्वंतः । अभिः प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानैः शमीभिः स्तुतिरूपैः कर्मभिर्महयंतस्त्वां पूजयंतः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The sentence continues from the previous page. "We (खलु (khalu)) call you (आ चक्रम (ā cakrama), "we invoke"), worshipping you with these visibly present holy rites (शमीभिः (śamībhiḥ)) that take the form of praise."

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • सखीयतां (sakhīyatāṃ)—to us who desire your friendship
  • अविता (avitā)—as a protector
  • बोधि (bodhi)—know (regard yourself)
  • गृणानः (gṛṇānaḥ)—you who are praised
  • सखा (sakhā)—become our friend
  • स्तुवते (stuvate)—to me who praise you
  • वयः (vayaḥ)—food
  • धाः (dhāḥ)—give
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • सबाधः (sabādhaḥ)—as those who suffer affliction
  • वयं (vayaṃ)—we
  • आभिः शमीभिः (ābhiḥ śamībhiḥ)—with these rites in the form of praise
  • महयंतः (mahayaṃtaḥ)—worshipping you
  • ते (te)—you
  • आ चक्रम (ā cakrama)—we pray and call
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, know that you must be the protector of us who desire your friendship. You, who deserve to be praised, be our friend. Give food to me who praise you. O Indra, we, enduring the affliction of austerity, worship you with these rites in the form of praise, and we pray to you and call you.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Regard yourself as a protector of those who desire your friendship ; be a friend deserving of commendation : grant, Indra, food to him who praises (you) : suffering difficulties, we make our supplications to you, worshipping you with these holy rites.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 3-8) explains that in the sacrifice addressed to Indra Vṛtrahan, when the oblation of the puroḍāśa is made, this Ṛk beginning स्तुत इंद्रः (stuta iṃdraḥ) is to be used as the yājyā mantra, by the sūtra सुत इंद्रो मघवा यद्ध वृत्रैवा वस्व इंद्रः सत्यः सम्राट् (suta iṃdro maghavā yaddha vṛtraivā vasva iṃdraḥ satyaḥ samrāṭ).

Ṛk 19

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स्तु॒त इंद्रो॑ म॒घवा॒ यद्ध॑ वृ॒त्रा भूरी॒ण्येको॑ अप्र॒तीनि॑
हंति ।

stuta iṃdro maghavā yaddha vṛtrā bhūrīṇyeko apratīni
haṃti |
