मर्ताः ॥१९ ॥

asya priyo jaritā yasya śarmannakirdevā vārayaṃte na
martāḥ ‖19 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

स्तुतः । इंद्रः । मघवा । यत् । ह । वृत्रा । भूरीणि । एकः । अप्रतीनि । हंति ।
अस्य । प्रियः । जरिता । यस्य । शर्मन् । नकिः । देवाः । वारयंते । न । मर्ताः ॥

stutaḥ | iṃdraḥ | maghavā | yat | ha | vṛtrā | bhūrīṇi | ekaḥ | apratīni | haṃti |
asya | priyaḥ | jaritā | yasya | śarman | nakiḥ | devāḥ | vārayaṃte | na | martāḥ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

इंद्रस्य वृत्रघ्नः पुरोडाशस्य स्तुत इंद्र इति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । स्तुत इंद्रो मघवा यद्ध वृत्रैना वस्व इंद्रः सत्यः सम्राट् । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥ यद्ध यदा खलु मघवा धनवानिंद्रः स्तुतोऽस्माभिः स्तुतो भवति तदेंद्र एकोऽसहाय एव भूरीणि बहून्यप्रतीन्यप्रतिगमनानि । अभिगमनयुक्तानीत्यर्थः । वृत्रा वृत्राणि शत्रुन्हंति । हिनस्ति । यस्येंद्रस्य शर्मन् शर्मण्याश्रये वर्तमानं स्तोतारं देवा नकिर्वारयंते । निवारणं न कुर्वंति । मर्ताश्च न निवारयंते अस्येंद्रस्य जरिता स्तोता प्रियो भवति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

स्तुत इंद्रः (stuta iṃdraḥ) is the yājyā for the puroḍāśa of Indra Vṛtrahan, and it is prescribed in the sūtra (Ā. 3-8). When Indra, the possessor of wealth (मघवा (maghavā)), is praised by us, then he alone, without helper, slays many (भूरीणि (bhūrīṇi)) foes (वृत्रा (vṛtrā)) who are अप्रतीनि (apratīni), that is, "not to be approached" or "not yielding". The worshipper who dwells in the shelter (शर्मन् (śarman)) of this Indra is not obstructed by gods or by mortals. The praiser of this Indra is dear to him.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • युद्ध (yuddha)—when
  • मघवा (maghavā)—the wealthy
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • स्तुतः (stutaḥ)—is praised (then)
  • एकः (ekaḥ)—he alone
  • भूरीणि (bhūrīṇi)—numerous
  • अप्रतीनि (apratīni)—and not yielding to others
  • वृत्रा (vṛtrā)—all enemies
  • हंति (haṃti)—destroys
  • यस्य (yasya)—of that Indra
  • शर्मन् (śarman)—the praiser who is in his protection
  • देवाः (devāḥ)—the gods
  • नकिः वारयंते (nakiḥ vārayaṃte)—cannot oppose
  • मर्ताः (martāḥ)—mortals also
  • न (वारयंते) (na (vārayaṃte))—cannot oppose
  • अस्य (asya)—to this Indra
  • जरिता (jaritā)—the praiser
  • प्रियः (priyaḥ)—becomes dear
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as Indra, the possessor of wealth, is praised, he, without the help of others, alone destroys all the numerous enemies who yield to none. Neither gods nor humans can oppose the praiser who is under Indra's protection. The praiser becomes dear to this Indra.

p. 982

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

When Indra, the posssessor of opulence, is glorified, he singly destroys many unyielding foes: the worshipper is dear to him (who relies) on his protection, and neither gods nor men molest him

Ṛk 20

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

ए॒वा न॒ इंद्रो॑ म॒घवा॑ विर॒ष्यी कर॑त्स॒त्या च॑र्षणी॒धृद॑न॒र्वा।
त्वं राजा॑ ज॒नुषां॑ धेह्य॒स्मे अधि॒ श्रवो॒ माहि॑नं॒ यज्ज॑रि॒त्रॆ॥

evā na iṃdro maghavā viraṣyī karatsatyā carṣaṇīdhṛdanarvā|
tvaṃ rājā januṣāṃ dhehyasme adhi śravo māhinaṃ yajjaritrè‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

एव । नः । इंद्रः । मघवा । विरप्सी । करत् । सत्या । चर्षणीधृत् । अनर्वा ।
त्वं । राजा । जनुषां । धेहि । अस्मे इति । अधि । श्रवः । माहिनं । यत् । जरित्रे ॥२०॥

eva | naḥ | iṃdraḥ | maghavā | virapsī | karat | satyā | carṣaṇīdhṛt | anarvā |
tvaṃ | rājā | januṣāṃ | dhehi | asme iti | adhi | śravaḥ | māhinaṃ | yat | jaritre ‖20‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अग्निमारुतशस्त्र एवा न इंद्र इति परिधानीया । सूत्रितं च । एवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरप्यीति परिदध्यात् । आ. ५-२० । इति ॥ विरष्यी बहुविधशब्दवान् चर्षणीधृत् सर्वासां प्रजानां धारयितानर्वाप्रत्यृतः । केनापि प्रतिकूलेन न प्राप्त इत्यर्थः । मघवा धनवानिंद्र एवैवमस्माभिः स्तुतः सन् नोऽस्माकं सत्या सत्यरूपाण्यभिमतानि फलानि करत् । करोतु । हे इंद्र जनुषां जन्मवतां सर्वॆषां राजा प्रभुत्वं माहिनं महिन्नोपेतं यच्छ्रवो यद्यशो जरित्रे स्तोत्रे देयं तद्यशोऽस्मे अस्मास्वधि अधिकत्वेन धेहि ॥ एवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरष्यीत्युत्तमया परिदधातीयं वा इंद्रो मघवा विरष्यीत्यादि ब्राह्मणं । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३८ ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Agnimāruta-śastra, एवा न इंद्रः (evā na iṃdraḥ) is the concluding verse (paridhānīyā). It is prescribed: एवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरप्यीति परिदध्यात् (evā na iṃdro maghavā virapyīti paridadhyāt) (Ā. 5-20). Indra is विरष्यी (viraṣyī), "of many kinds of sound"; चर्षणीधृत् (carṣaṇīdhṛt), the upholder of all peoples; अनर्वा (anarvā), "not met" by any hostile force. Thus praised by us, may Indra, the wealthy, bring about for us true (सत्या (satyā)), real desired fruits. O Indra, lord of all born beings, place upon us in abundance the great glory which is to be given to the praiser. The Brāhmaṇa says: एवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरष्यीत्युत्तमया परिदधातीयं वा इंद्रो मघवा विरष्यीत्यादि ब्राह्मणं (evā na iṃdro maghavā viraṣyītyuttamayā paridadhātīyaṃ vā iṃdro maghavā viraṣyītyādi brāhmaṇaṃ) (Ai. Brā. 3-38).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • विरष्यी (viraṣyī)—of many kinds of sound
  • चर्षणीधृत् (carṣaṇīdhṛt)—who upholds all peoples
  • अनर्वा (anarvā)—unobstructed
  • मघवा (maghavā)—wealthy
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • एना (enā)—thus praised by us
  • नः (naḥ)—for us

p. 983

  • सत्या (satyā)—true fruits
  • करत् (karat)—may he bring about
  • जनुषां (januṣāṃ)—of all beings that are born
  • राजा (rājā)—the lord
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • माहिनं (māhinaṃ)—endowed with greatness
  • यत् श्रवः (yat śravaḥ)—the fame that is
  • जरित्रॆ (jaritrè)—to us who are praisers
  • अस्मे (asme)—in us
  • अधि धेहि (adhi dhehi)—cause to exist in abundance
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, who is of many kinds of sound, upholds all peoples, is unobstructed and wealthy, being praised by us in many ways, bring about true fruits for us. O Indra, you who are lord of all beings that take birth, cause the fame endowed with greatness to be abundant in us, your praisers.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

The many-voiced Indra, the possessor of opulence, the supporter of men, the irresistible, bestows upon us, when praised by us, assured (rewards): you, (Indra), are the king of men : grant to us abundantly that great fame which (is due) to (your) worshipper.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 5-20) prescribes that in reciting the mantras of the Agnimāruta-śastra this Ṛk एवा न इंद्रः (evā na iṃdraḥ) be recited as the concluding mantra, by the sūtra एवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरप्यीति परिदध्यात् (evā na iṃdro maghavā virapyīti paridadhyāt). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa also says that this Ṛk is to be recited as the concluding mantra of the Agnimāruta-śastra mantras (Ai. Brā. 13-38) NOTE. What is there is explained here: एवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरप्सीत्युत्तमया परिदधातीयं ना इंद्रो मघवा विरप्सी करत्सत्या चर्षणीधृदनर्वेतीयं वै सत्या चर्षणीधृदनर्वा (evā na iṃdro maghavā virapsītyuttamayā paridadhātīyaṃ nā iṃdro maghavā virapsī karatsatyā carṣaṇīdhṛdanarvetīyaṃ vai satyā carṣaṇīdhṛdanarvā) (Ai. Brā. 13-38). This Indra is possessed of wealth, and is always engaged in activity. [The word विरप्ति (virapti) is derived from the root रभ राभस्ये (rabha rābhasye) and suggests one who, not being idle, is always engaged in some work.] With this Ṛk, which conveys these meanings on Indra's behalf, these Agnimāruta-śastra mantras are to be concluded. The words in this Ṛk, Indra and the rest,

p. 984

also convey a sense referring to the Earth. The word चर्षणी (carṣaṇī) means human beings. Because he upholds or nourishes human beings, Indra is called चर्षणीधृत् (carṣaṇīdhṛt). The intention expressed here is: may such an Indra, descending from his mount the horse, come and sit on this our sacrificial ground, and, protecting the true sacrificial work from obstacles and the like, make it fruitful. It is said here that by touching the earth while reciting this mantra, the Earth is, as it were, prayed to. त्वं राजा जनुषां धेह्यस्मे इतीयं वै राजा जनुषां अधि श्रवो माहिनं यज्जरित्र इतीयं वै माहिनं यज्ञश्रवो यजमानो जरिता यजमानाय्यैवैतामाशिषमाशास्ते॥ (tvaṃ rājā januṣāṃ dhehyasme itīyaṃ vai rājā januṣāṃ adhi śravo māhinaṃ yajjaritra itīyaṃ vai māhinaṃ yajñaśravo yajamāno jaritā yajamānāyyaivaitāmāśiṣamāśāste‖) (Ai. Brā. 13-38) O Indra (or O Earth), you are king of all of us who are born, that is, of all, beginning with the officiating priests and the sacrificer; and you provide all our desires. Procure great fame and food for the sacrificer who is praising. In this sacrifice the sacrificer praises you much. For such a sacrificer, make the sacrifice he is performing fruitful and bestow great fame: thus the priests pray. This is the main purport.

Ṛk 21

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

नू ष्टु॒त इं॑द्र॒ नू गृ॑णा॒न इषं॑ जरि॒त्रे न॒द्यो॒३॒॑३ न पी॑पेः ।
अका॑रि ते हरिवो॒ ब्रह्म॒ नव्यं॑ धि॒या स्या॑म र॒थ्यः॑ सदा॒साः ॥२१॥

nū ṣṭuta iṃdra nū gṛṇāna iṣaṃ jaritre nadyo3 na pīpeḥ |
akāri te harivo brahma navyaṃ dhiyā syāma rathyaḥ sadāsāḥ ‖21‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

नु । स्तुतः । इंद्र । नु । गृणानः । इषं । जरित्रे । नद्यः । न । पीपेरिति पीपेः ।
अकारि । ते । हरिऽवः । ब्रह्म । नव्यं । धिया । स्याम । रथ्यः । सदाऽसाः ॥ २१ ॥

nu | stutaḥ | iṃdra | nu | gṛṇānaḥ | iṣaṃ | jaritre | nadyaḥ | na | pīperiti pīpeḥ |
akāri | te | hari 'vaḥ | brahma | navyaṃ | dhiyā | syāma | rathyaḥ | sadā 'sāḥ ‖ 21 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र नु क्षिप्रं स्तुतः पूर्वैर्ऋषिभिः संस्तुतो नुक्षिप्रंगृणानोऽस्माभिः स्तूयमानश्च त्वमिषमन्नं जरित्रे स्तोत्रे मह्यं नद्यो न अद्भिन्नदीरिव सीपेः ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you were quickly (नु (nu)) praised by the earlier seers and are now praised by us. Fill (पीपेः (pīpeḥ), "make swell") food for me, the praiser, as rivers are filled with water.

p. 985

प्यायय । प्रवृद्धं कुरु । हे इंद्र हरिवो हरिवन् हरिसंज्ञकाश्वोपेतेंद्र ते तुभ्यं नव्यं नवतरं ब्रह्म स्तोत्रमकारि । अस्माभिः क्रियते । रथ्यो रथवंतो वयं धिया प्रज्ञारूपया स्तुत्या सदासास्त्वां सर्वदा भजमानास्त्वदर्थं हवीरूपस्यान्नस्य दातारो ना स्याम । भूयास्मै ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Make it abound. O Indra, lord of the horses called Hari, a newer hymn (navyaṃ brahma) has been made for you by us. We, possessed of chariots, with praise in the form of insight (धिया (dhiyā)), ever serving you (सदासाः (sadāsāḥ)), may become givers of oblation-food for you.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • नु (nu)—quickly (in eagerness to worship you)
  • स्तुतः (stutaḥ)—you who were praised by the seers of former times
  • नु (nu)—with the same eager faith
  • गृणानः (gṛṇānaḥ)—and praised by us
  • जरित्रे (jaritre)—to me, the praiser
  • नद्यो न (nadyo na)—as rivers are filled by their flood
  • इषं (iṣaṃ)—food
  • पीपेः (pīpeḥ)—fill up
  • हरिवः (harivaḥ)—O Indra, who have horses called Hari
  • ते (te)—addressed to you
  • नव्यं (navyaṃ)—new
  • ब्रह्म (brahma)—hymn
  • अकारि (akāri)—is made by us
  • रथ्यः (rathyaḥ)—we who have a chariot
  • धिया (dhiyā)—with our praise in the form of insight
  • सदासाः (sadāsāḥ)—offering oblations and the like to you
  • स्याम (syāma)—grant that we may be
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who were praised by the seers of former times eager to worship you alone, and are praised by us too with the same eager faith, fill up food for me, the praiser, as rivers are filled by their flood. O Indra, possessor of the horses called Hari, we make a new hymn addressed to you. Grant that we, possessors of an excellent chariot, may be, with our praise in the form of insight, offerers of oblations and the like to you.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Glorified ( in the past ), glorified, Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water): Lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you : may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in (your) praise.

Sūkta 18 (Maṇḍala 4)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अयं पंथा इति त्रयोदशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका। अयं पंथाः सप्तोना संवाद इंद्रादितिनामदेवानामिति । यस्य वाक्यं स ऋषि-

Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn अयं पंथा (ayaṃ paṃthā) has thirteen Ṛks and is the eighth sūkta, in the Triṣṭubh metre. The Anukramaṇikā says here: अयं पंथाः सप्तोना संवाद इंद्रादितिनामदेवानामिति (ayaṃ paṃthāḥ saptonā saṃvāda iṃdrāditināmadevānāmiti), and goes on to say that the seer is the one whose speech it is. NOTE

p. 986

र्या तेनोच्यते सा देवतेति परिभाषितत्वादृषिदेवते तत्र तत्र ज्ञातव्ये । अस्मिन् सूक्ते इंद्रादितिवामदेवसंवादरूपिणी काचिदाख्यायिका श्लोकरूपेण सूच्यते। गर्भस्थो ज्ञानसंपन्नो वामदेवो महामुनिः । मतिं चक्रे न जायेय योनिदेशात्तु मातृतः । किंतु पार्श्वादितश्चेति ज्ञात्वा नु जननी त्विदं । दध्यौ शांतै शचीं देवीमदितिं त्विंद्रमातरं ॥ अदितिस्त्विंद्रसहिता गर्भिणीमभ्यगाद्वने । अदितींद्रवामदेवाः संवादमथ चक्रिरे॥ संवाद इति सूत्रेण कथा सैषात्र सूच्यते। नोक्तो वक्तृविशेषोऽत्र ह्युपदेशेश्वन्नुक्तितः ॥ अर्थतस्ववगंतव्यो वक्तृभेद इति स्थितिः । इंद्रोदितिर्यषिश्चास्मिन्मिथः सूक्ते समूचिरे ॥ गर्भॆ शयानं सुचिरं मातुर्गर्भादनिर्गतं । वामदेवं प्रति ब्रूत आद्ययर्चा शतक्रतुः ॥ द्वितीयादिभिरर्धर्चैऋषिरत्राह पंचभिः । नही स्वस्येति सप्त स्युरर्धर्चा आदितेर्वचः ॥ ममच्चन त्वा युवतिरित्यचः पंच वै मुनेः । दौर्गत्यशांतिमत्राह वामदेवस्तथांत्यया ॥ एवमर्थाद्वक्तृभेद इति बह्वृचशासनं । अर्थो विवेकस्पष्टत्वादुपदेशेषु नेरितः । ऋषिदैवतसिद्ध्यर्थं विवेकादर्थ ईरित इति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the Anukramaṇikā statement. The seer is the one whose speech a ṛk is, and the deity is the one of whom it speaks. Since this is the established rule, the seers and deities are to be understood verse by verse. In this sūkta a certain narrative, a dialogue between Indra, Aditi and Vāmadeva, is indicated in the form of verses (ślokas). While still in the womb, the knowing great sage Vāmadeva made up his mind: "I will not be born from my mother's birth-passage, but from her side." His mother learned of this and meditated, for her protection, on the goddess Śacī and on Aditi, the mother of Indra. Aditi went with Indra to the pregnant woman in the forest, and Aditi, Indra and Vāmadeva then held a conversation. The sūtra "saṃvādaḥ" indicates this story. The speaker is not named in the teaching, and the difference of speakers must be understood from the sense. Indra, Aditi and the seer spoke to one another in this sūkta. With the first ṛk Indra addresses Vāmadeva, who has lain long in the womb and not yet come out of it. With five half-verses from the second onward the seer speaks. The seven half-verses beginning "nahī nvasya" are Aditi's speech. The five ṛks beginning "mamaccana tvā yuvatiḥ" belong to the sage NOTE. With the last ṛk Vāmadeva speaks the pacification of misfortune. The speakers are thus known from the sense, as the Bahvṛca teaching says; the sense is not stated in the teachings because it is clear from discernment, and it is given here to establish the seers and deities.

Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "ayaṃ panthāḥ" is the eighth sūkta of the second anuvāka. It has thirteen ṛks; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "ayaṃ panthāḥ saptonā saṃvāda indrāditivāmadevānām", that is, in this sūkta there is a dialogue of Indra, Aditi and the seer Vāmadeva. "Yasya vākyaṃ sa ṛṣiḥ, yā tenocyate sā devatā": the one whose speech is in a ṛk is the seer of that ṛk, and the one whose matter is spoken of in the ṛk is its deity. As this is the established rule, in this sūkta too the seers and deities of the several ṛks are to be inferred according to context. A narrative concerning the conversation of Indra, Aditi and Vāmadeva, spoken of in this sūkta, is given here in verse form:

गर्भस्थो ज्ञानसंपन्नो वामदेवो महामुनिः । मतिं चक्रे न जायेय योनिदेशात्तु मातृतः ॥ १ ॥ किंतु पार्श्वादितश्चति ज्ञात्वा नु जननी त्विदं ॥ दध्यौ शांतै शचीं देवीमदितिं त्विंद्रमातरं ॥ २ ॥ अदितिस्त्विंद्रसहिता गर्भिणीमभ्यगाद्वने । आदितींद्रवामदेवाः संवादमथ चक्रिरे ॥ ३ ॥ संवाद इति सूत्रेण कथा सैषात्र सूच्यते । नोक्तो वक्तृविशेषोऽत्र ह्युपदेशेष्वनुक्तितः ॥ ४ ॥

p. 987

अर्थतस्त्ववगंतव्यो वक्तृभेद इति स्थितिः । इंद्रोदितिऋषिश्चास्मिन्मिथः सूक्ते समूचिरे ॥ ५ ॥ गर्भॆ शयानं सुचिरं मातुर्गर्भादनिर्गतं । नामदेवं प्रति ब्रूत आद्ययर्च शतक्रतुः ॥ ६ ॥ द्वितीयादिभिरर्धर्चैर्यषिरत्राह पंचभिः नही न्वस्येति सप्त स्युरर्धर्चा अदितेर्वचः ॥ ७ ॥ ममच्चन त्वा युवतिरित्यृचः पंच वै मुनेः । दौर्गत्यशांतिमत्राह नामदेवस्तथांत्यया ॥ ८ ॥ एवमर्थाद्वक्तृभेद इति बह्वृचशासनात् । अर्थो विवेकस्पष्टत्वादुपदेशेषु नेरितः ॥ ९ ॥ ऋषिदैवतसिध्यर्थं विवेकादर्थ ईरितः । (अनु. भा. ४-१८).

NOTE

The great-souled seer Vāmadeva, while in his mother's womb, thought thus: "If I were now to be born as ordinary people are, coming out through my mother's birth-passage, that would not befit the greatness of one who knows as I do. Therefore, when I come out of the womb, I shall not come by the birth-passage but by cleaving my mother's side." So he resolved. Vāmadeva's mother learned of this and feared that if the child split her flank and came out, death would befall her. To remove this fear she meditated on the goddess Śacī, Indra's wife, and on the goddess Aditi, Indra's mother. Hearing her cry of distress, Aditi came with Indra to the place in the forest where the pregnant woman (Vāmadeva's mother) was. Then a conversation took place between the goddess Aditi, Indra and the seer Vāmadeva in the womb. That very conversation is set forth in this sūkta. It cannot be said precisely who composed the dialogue of this sūkta in sūkta form, but the matter has come down by tradition. Who spoke which words, as stated in the sūkta, is to be understood according to the sense. This sūkta contains the dialogue held among the three, Indra, Aditi and the seer Vāmadeva. In the first ṛk of this sūkta is Indra's speech addressed to the seer Vāmadeva, who has been in his mother's womb for a very long time and has not yet come out (as an infant?). From the second ṛk up to the first half of the fourth is the speech of the seer Vāmadeva; from the latter half of the fourth up to the seventh ṛk is Aditi's speech; in the five ṛks from the eighth to the twelfth is the speech of the pregnant mother of the seer Vāmadeva. In the last ṛk, the thirteenth, is the pacifying mantra spoken by the seer Vāmadeva for the removal of misfortune.

p. 988

Therefore who the seers and deities are of each ṛk is to be learned from the sense of the respective ṛks. Since the sense stated in the ṛks is clear, it is not repeated here; this explanation had to be given here in order to make the seers and deities clear.

Sūkta 18. Maṇḍala 4; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 18. Aṣṭaka 3; Adhyāya 5; Vargas 25, 26. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 13. Seer: Vāmadeva Gautama (1: Indra; 2, 3 and, in 4, the first half, and 13: Vāmadeva; in 4, the latter half, 5, 6, 7: Aditi; 8, 9, 10, 11, 12: the pregnant mother of Vāmadeva). Deity: (1: Vāmadeva; 2, 3 and, in 4, the first half: Indra; in 4, the latter half, 5, 6, 7: Vāmadeva; 8, 9, 10, 11, 12: Indra; 13: आत्मशंसा इंद्रो ना (ātmaśaṃsā iṃdro nā) NOTE.) Metre: Triṣṭup.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒यं पंथा॒ अनु॑वित्तः पुरा॒णो यतो॑ दे॒वा उ॒दजा॑यंत॒ ॑ विश्वे ।
अत॑श्चि॒दा ज॑निषीष्ट॒ प्रवृ॑द्धो॒ मा मा॒तर॑ममु॒या पत्त॑वे कः॥

ayaṃ paṃthā anuvittaḥ purāṇo yato devā udajāyaṃta
viśve |
ataścidā janiṣīṣṭa pravṛddho mā mātaramamuyā pattave kaḥ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अयं । पंथाः । अनुवित्तः । पुराणः । यतः । देवाः । उत् अजायंत । विश्वे ।
अतः । चित् । आ । जनिषीष्ट । प्रवृद्धः । मा । मातरं । अमुया । पत्तवे। करिति कः॥

ayaṃ | paṃthāḥ | anuvittaḥ | purāṇaḥ | yataḥ | devāḥ | ut ajāyaṃta | viśve |
ataḥ | cit | ā | janiṣīṣṭa | pravṛddhaḥ | mā | mātaraṃ | amuyā | pattave| kariti kaḥ‖

p. 989

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

इंद्रवाक्यं । पुराणोऽनादिरयु प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानः पंथा योनिर्निगमनरूपो मार्गोऽनु आनुपूर्व्येण वित्तः । सर्वैर्जायमानैर्लब्धः । यतो यस्माद्योनिमार्गाद्विश्वे सर्वॆ देवा उदजायंत । उत्कर्षेणोत्पन्ना भवंति । तस्माद्योनिमार्गान्मनुष्या उत्पन्ना भवंतीति किमु वक्तव्यं । अतश्चिदस्माद्योनिमार्गादेव प्रवृद्यो गर्भे प्रकर्षेण वृद्धिं गतो वामदेव आ जनिषीष्ट । आ समंताच्चायतां । अमुयानूं मातरं पत्तवे पतनाय । मरणायेत्यर्थः । मा कः । मा करोतु ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra's speech. This path, beginningless, perceived directly, namely the birth-passage, the way of exit, has been found in due succession by all who are born. Since all the gods are born excellently from that very birth-passage, what need is there to say that men are born from it? Therefore from this very path let Vāmadeva, who has grown forth in the womb, be born; "ā" means completely, let him be born. As for this mother, "pattave" means for falling, that is, for death; "mā kaḥ": let him not bring it about.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यतः (yataḥ)—by which path in the form of the womb
  • विश्वे देवाः (viśve devāḥ)—all the gods also
  • उदजायंत (udajāyaṃta)—were born; (by such a path)
  • अयं पंथाः (ayaṃ paṃthāḥ)—this path of emergence from the womb, in the form of the birth-passage
  • पुराणः (purāṇaḥ)—as beginningless
  • अनु (anu)—from of old
  • वित्तः (vittaḥ)—is a matter known to all
  • अतश्वित् (ataśvit)—therefore indeed
  • प्रवृद्धः (pravṛddhaḥ)—Vāmadeva, fully grown in the womb itself
  • आ जनिषीष्ट (ā janiṣīṣṭa)—let him, obtaining worldly birth, come out of the womb
  • अमुया मातरं (amuyā mātaraṃ)—this his mother
  • सत्तवे (sattave)—so as to be subject to death NOTE
  • मा कः (mā kaḥ)—let him not do
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra's speech: this path of emergence from the womb, in the form of the birth-passage, by which all the gods also were born, is known to all as the beginningless place of birth for gods, men and the rest. Therefore let Vāmadeva, who has grown fully in the womb itself, obtain worldly birth and come out of the womb, and let him not bring about the death of this his mother.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Indra speaks.—This is the old and recognized path by which all the gods are born ; so, when full-grown, let him be born in the same manner ; let him not cause the loss of this his mother.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This sūkta contains the history of the birth of the seer Vāmadeva. Because Vāmadeva was already a great knower while in his mother's womb, he did not wish to come out through the birth-passage as ordinary people are born, but desired to come out by cleaving the side of his mother's body. His mother, who was pregnant and knew this, in fear that death would befall her, meditated on Indra's wife and on the goddess Aditi, Indra's mother, and took refuge in them. Then Aditi came with Indra to Vāmadeva's mother in the hermitage in the forest, pacified Vāmadeva in the womb, and spoke words of good counsel that he should give up his unnatural desire. First Indra speaks, addressing Vāmadeva.

p. 990

Indra (addressing Vāmadeva in the womb): "O Vāmadeva, all gods and men, when they are born, that is, when they come out of the mother's womb, come only by the mother's birth-passage. The woman's birth-passage is the place of origin of the whole class of living beings. This is the path ordained by nature. If you leave this order and come by cleaving your mother's side, your mother will die. Therefore do not do so."

Vāmadeva (in the womb): "O Indra, I will not come out by this most painful passage of a woman. I will make a way through my mother's side and come out. For I am not like ordinary people; my greatness is surpassing. Many great deeds have to be done by me. Without anyone else's help I can fight an enemy alone. I alone can debate with an adversary. Indra (you, Indra) has just said that if I do not come out by the mother's birth-passage but by another way, my mother will die. But what value can be put on Indra's word? Has that Indra not done many improper acts? Did he not go uninvited to Tvaṣṭṛ's house and forcibly drink the soma juice that had been bought at great cost? Indra's mother Aditi bore Indra in her womb for thousands of months and gave birth to him with great hardship. Yet all the deeds that Indra has done are against the world. Therefore I need not bow to Indra's word. I will come out of my mother's womb as I please."

Aditi: "O Vāmadeva, you should not speak slightingly of Indra. Among all the gods who have so far been born in the world and who will be born hereafter, none is equal to Indra. Thinking that it would not befit his dignity to bear Indra like an ordinary infant in the lying-in chamber, Aditi gave Indra surpassing power. By that power Indra stood forth manifest by his own radiance, and by his surpassing power he pervaded heaven and earth completely. All the rivers that flow on the earth, beginning with the sound अलला (alalā) and making a joyous noise, flow on, upholding and proclaiming Indra's greatness.

p. 991

O seer Vāmadeva, question those rivers and ask. Without Indra's help, how would the waters have come to those rivers from the clouds? Moreover, the nivid-utterances all concern Indra and are purely laudatory. The waters bear Indra's sin of brahmin-slaying in the form of foam. My son Indra slew Vṛtra with the thunderbolt and caused the waters that he had held back to fall on the earth as rain and flow as rivers. Can you reject the word of an Indra of such great nature?"

Vāmadeva (ironically, addressing Indra): "O Indra, did not your young mother (Aditi) bear you with joy? Was it not with joy that the demoness Kuṣavā swallowed you? You broke through that demoness with joy and came out. Through you joy came to the waters too. Was it not from excess of joy as well that the demon Vyaṃsa struck you, slapping you on the cheek? But you, struck by him, grew greater than he, smote his head with the thunderbolt and crushed it to bits. All these are your valorous deeds. Even so your greatness cannot be thought small. As a well-nourished cow obtains an excellent calf NOTE, your mother Aditi obtained you (Indra): of surpassing strength, unconquered by enemies, fulfiller of all wishes, impeller of all, able to protect yourself, moving at will. Then, when Aditi asked you, 'O Indra, my son, have Agni and the other gods abandoned your friendship?', you said to Viṣṇu, who was there: 'O friend Viṣṇu, you are all-pervading and my friend; show great valour to slay the asura Vṛtra.' Did you not say so? Besides, you seized your father by the foot, dragged him and killed him, and made your mother a widow. Can anyone else do this deed? Whether lying down or moving about, no one can kill you. Which other gods have strength and power equal to yours, or greater than yours?"

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

नाहमतो॒ निर॑या दु॒र्गहै॒तत्ति॑र॒श्चता॑ पा॒र्श्वान्निर्ग॑माणि ।
ब॒हूनि॑ मे॒ अकृ॑ता॒ कर्त्वा॑नि॒ युध्यै॑ त्वेन॒ सं त्वे॑न पृच्छै ॥२॥

nāhamato nirayā durgahaitattiraścatā pārśvānnirgamāṇi |
bahūni me akṛtā kartvāni yudhyai tvena saṃ tvena pṛcchai ‖2‖

p. 992

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

न । अहं । अतः । निः । अय । दुःगहा । एतत् । तिरश्चता । पार्श्वात् । निः । गमानि ।
बहूनि । मे । अकृता । कर्त्वानि । युध्यै । त्वेन । सं । त्वेन । पृच्छै ॥ २ ॥

na | ahaṃ | ataḥ | niḥ | aya | duḥgahā | etat | tiraścatā | pārśvāt | niḥ | gamāni |
bahūni | me | akṛtā | kartvāni | yudhyai | tvena | saṃ | tvena | pṛcchai ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

वामदेव एवमुक्तवंतमिंद्रं प्रत्याह । अहमतो योनिमार्गान्न निरया। न निरयाणि । न निर्गच्छानि । एतद्योनिनिगमरूपं वर्त्म दुर्गहा । दुर्ग्रहं । दुःखेन ग्राह्यं । न प्राप्यं भवतीत्यर्थः । किंतु तिरश्चता तिरश्चीनात्पार्श्वान्निर्गमानि । निर्गच्छानि । योनिदेशादनिर्गतोऽहं पार्श्वं भित्त्वा निर्गच्छानीत्यर्थः । अन्न्यैरकृतमिदमेव न केवलं मया क्रियते किंत्वनैरकृतानि बहूनि कर्माणि मे कर्त्वानि कर्तव्यानि संति । त्वेनैकेन सपत्नेन विवदमानेन सह युध्यॆ । युद्धं करवाणि । त्वेनैकेन बुभुत्तुना सं पृच्छै । सम्यक् पृच्छानि ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Vāmadeva replies to Indra, who has spoken in this way. "From this path of the womb I shall not go out (निरया (nirayā) means I shall not go out, I shall not depart). This path of leaving the womb is दुर्गहा (durgahā): hard to grasp, hard to take hold of, that is, not to be attained. Rather I shall go out from the slanting side." He means that he will not leave through the place of birth but will split the side and come out. "Not only this is done by me, which others have not done: many deeds are to be done by me which others have not done. I shall fight with one rival who disputes with me. I shall question thoroughly (सं पृच्छै (saṃ pṛcchai), 'may I question well') with one who wishes to know (बुभुत्तुना (bubhuttunā))." NOTE

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अहं (ahaṃ)—I
  • अतः (ataḥ)—from this path in the form of the womb
  • न निरया (na nirayā)—I shall not come out
  • एतत् (etat)—this path
  • दुर्गहा (durgahā)—is exceedingly painful
  • तिरश्चता (tiraścatā)—slanting
  • पार्श्वत् (pārśvat)—by the side path
  • निर्गमानि (nirgamāni)—I shall come out
  • अकृत (akṛta)—not done by others
  • बहूनि (bahūni)—many deeds
  • कर्त्वानि (kartvāni)—are to be done by me
  • तैन (taina)—with a single enemy
  • युध्यॆ (yudhyè)—I can fight
  • तैन (taina)—with a single opponent
  • संप्रच्छै (saṃpracchai)—I can debate
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The words of the sage Vāmadeva, who is in the womb: "I shall not come out by this path in the form of the womb. This path is exceedingly painful. I shall come out by the slanting side path. Many deeds not done by others are to be done by me. I can fight with a single enemy. I can debate with a single opponent."

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Vamadeva speaks—Let me not come forth by this path, for it is difficult (of issue): let me come forth obliquely from the side : many acts unperformed by others are to be accomplished by me : let me contend (in war) with one (enemy), in controversy with one opponent.

p. 993

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

प॒रा॒य॒तीं मा॒तर॒मन्व॑ चष्ट॒ न नानु॑ गा॒न्यनु॒ नू ग॑मानि ।
त्वष्टु॑गृ॒हे अ॑पिब॒त्तोम॒मिंद्रः॑ शतध॒न्यं॑ च॒न्वोः॑ सु॒तस्य॑ ॥३॥

parāyatīṃ mātaramanva caṣṭa na nānu gānyanu nū gamāni |
tvaṣṭugṛhe apibattomamiṃdraḥ śatadhanyaṃ canvoḥ sutasya ‖3‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

परायतीं । मातरं । अनु । अचष्ट । न । न । अनु । गानि । अनु । नु । गमानि ।
त्वष्टुः । गृहे । अपिबत् । सोमं । इंद्रः । शतधन्यं । चव्वोः । सुतस्य ॥ ३ ॥

parāyatīṃ | mātaraṃ | anu | acaṣṭa | na | na | anu | gāni | anu | nu | gamāni |
tvaṣṭuḥ | gṛhe | apibat | somaṃ | iṃdraḥ | śatadhanyaṃ | cavvoḥ | sutasya ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

मयि गर्भस्थिते सतींद्रो मदीयां मातरं परायतीं परेतां म्रियमाणामन्वचष्ट । अन्वब्रवीत् । एवमपीदानीं गर्भे स्थितोऽहं पुराणं पंथानं न नानु गानि । नानुगच्छानीति न । किंतु नु क्षिप्रमनु गमानि । अनुगच्छान्येव । वामदेवः स्वकीयमकृत्यकारित्वं परिहृत्येंद्रस्याकृत्यकारित्वमुत्तरार्धर्चेन प्रतिपादयति । इंद्रश्चन्वोः सोमाभिषवफलकयोः सुतस्य सोमं सुतवतोऽभिसुतवतस्त्वष्टुः संबंधिनि गृहेऽनुपहूतः सन् शतधन्यं बहुधनेन क्रीतं सोममपिबत् । बलात्कारेण सोमस्य पानं कृतवान् । अयमर्थस्तृत्तरीयैस्त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रं सोममाहरदित्यनुवाके । तै. सं. २-४-१२ । महता प्रबंधेन प्रपंचितः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

While I am in the womb, Indra spoke to my mother, who was departing (परायतीं (parāyatīṃ)), that is, dying. Even now, though I am in the womb, he says I shall not follow the old path: न नानु गानि (na nānu gāni), meaning "I would not follow", and yet नु (nu), quickly, अनु गमानि (anu gamāni), "I shall indeed follow". NOTE Setting aside his own improper acting, Vāmadeva shows Indra's improper acting in the latter half of the verse. In the house of Tvaṣṭṛ, who had pressed Soma at the two pressing-boards (चन्वोः (canvoḥ)), Indra, uninvited, drank the Soma bought with much wealth (शतधन्यं (śatadhanyaṃ)). He drank the Soma by force. This matter is set out at length in the anuvāka beginning त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रं सोममाहरदित्यनुवाके (tvaṣṭā hataputro vīṃdraṃ somamāharadityanuvāke) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मातरं (mātaraṃ)—my mother
  • परायतीं (parāyatīṃ)—that she is about to die
  • अन्वचष्ट (anvacaṣṭa)—(Indra) has said
  • न नानु गानि (na nānu gāni)—I shall not follow the ancient path (but)
  • नु (nu)—very soon
  • अनु गमानि (anu gamāni)—I shall come out just as I wish
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • चन्वोs (canvos)—in the Soma vessels
  • सुतस्य (sutasya)—which had been pressed
  • शतधन्वं (śatadhanvaṃ)—bought with much wealth
  • सोमं (somaṃ)—the Soma
  • त्वष्टुः (tvaṣṭuḥ)—of Tvaṣṭṛ
  • गृहे (gṛhe)—in the house
  • अपिबत् (apibat)—(went there uninvited and) drank
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra has told me that if I do not follow the ancient path, in the form of the womb, for coming out of the womb, my mother will die. But I shall not follow that path

p. 994

but shall come out quickly, just as I wish. In the house of Tvaṣṭṛ, Indra went uninvited and drank by force the Soma that had been pressed in the Soma vessels and bought with much wealth. (That too was an improper act.)

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

He, (Indra), has asserted that it will) cause the death of my mother : let me not proceed by the usual way, but proceed quickly, according (to my will): in the dwelling of Twashtri, Indra drank the costly Soma from the vessels of the offerers.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

We have already described at length earlier how Indra forcibly drank Soma in the house of Tvaṣṭṛ.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

किं स ऋध॑क्कृणव॒द्यं स॒हस्रं॑ मा॒सो ज॒भार॑ श॒रद॑श्च पू॒र्वीः ।
न॒ ही न्व॑स्य प्रति॒मान॒मस्त्यं॒तर्जा॒तेषू॒त ये जिनि॑त्वाः ॥ ४ ॥

kiṃ sa ṛdhakkṛṇavadyaṃ sahasraṃ māso jabhāra śaradaśca pūrvīḥ |
na hī nvasya pratimānamastyaṃtarjāteṣūta ye jinitvāḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

किं । सः । ऋधक् । कृणवत् । यं । सहस्रं । मासः । जभार । शरदः । च । पूर्वीः ।
नहि । नु । अस्य । प्रतिमानं । अस्ति । अंतः । जातेषु । उत । ये । जिनित्वाः ॥ ४ ॥

kiṃ | saḥ | ṛdhak | kṛṇavat | yaṃ | sahasraṃ | māsaḥ | jabhāra | śaradaḥ | ca | pūrvīḥ |
nahi | nu | asya | pratimānaṃ | asti | aṃtaḥ | jāteṣu | uta | ye | jinitvāḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अदितिर्यमिंद्रं सहस्रं बहून्मासो मासान्नूर्विर्बह्वीः शरदश्च संवत्सरांश्च जभार । बभार ॥ बिभर्तेरिदं रूपं ॥ गर्भे स्थित इंद्रो बहुषु संवत्सरेष्पदितिं क्लेशितवानित्यर्थः । एवंभूतः स इंद्रः किं यत्किमपि । सर्वमपीत्यर्थः । ऋधक् विरुद्धं कर्म कृणवत् । अकरोत् । इंद्रस्याक्षेपमसहमानादितिरिंद्रमाताप्येनं प्रति ब्रूते । हे वामदेव जातेषूत्पन्नेषु देवादिष्टंतर्मध्यॆ:-

Gist of the bhāṣya

Aditi bore Indra for a thousand (that is, many) months (मासः (māsaḥ)) and many autumns, that is, years: जभार (jabhāra) is the same as बभार (babhāra), a form of the root bhṛ. The meaning is that Indra, while in the womb, distressed Aditi for many years. Such an Indra, whatever (किं (kiṃ), meaning everything) ऋधक् (ṛdhak), contrary action he did, कृणवत् (kṛṇavat), he performed. Aditi, Indra's mother, cannot bear the reproach against Indra and answers Vāmadeva: "O Vāmadeva, among those who are born, gods and others, within them (the bhāṣya continues on the next page)

p. 995

Ṛk 4 (continued)

स्येंद्रस्य प्रतिमानं न ह्यस्ति । न विद्यते खलु । नु इति पादपूरणार्थः । उतापि च ये देवादयो जनित्वा जनयितव्या जनयिष्यमाणास्तेषु मध्येऽसेंद्रस्य प्रतिमानं नास्ति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

there is indeed no match for Indra. नु (nu) is a mere metrical filler. And among those, gods and others, who are to be born or will be born, there is no match for Indra."

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यं (yaṃ)—whom (Indra) (Aditi)
  • सहस्रं मासः (sahasraṃ māsaḥ)—for thousands of months
  • पूर्विः शरदः (pūrviḥ śaradaḥ)—for many years
  • जुभार (jubhāra)—she bore in the womb
  • सः (saḥ)—that Indra
  • किं (kiṃ)—whatever act
  • कृणवत् (kṛṇavat)—he did
  • ऋधक् (ṛdhak)—that is wholly and altogether contrary to the world
  • जातेषु (jāteṣu)—(O Vāmadeva) among those who have been born
  • उत (uta)—and
  • ये (ye)—who
  • जनित्वाः (janitvāḥ)—will be born in future, among all such gods
  • अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—in the midst
  • अस्य (asya)—for this Indra
  • प्रतिमानं (pratimānaṃ)—a comparison (those equal to him)
  • नहि अस्ति (nahi asti)—there is none at all
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Whatever deeds are done by Indra, whom his mother carried in the womb for thousands of months and many years, are all contrary to the world. Aditi's words: "O Vāmadeva, among all the gods who have been born and will be born, there is no one equal to Indra."

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Aditi speaks.—What irregular act has he committed whom (I, his mother,) bore for a thousand months and for many years? there is no analogy between him and those who have been or will be born.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒व॒द्यमि॑व॒ मन्य॑माना॒ गुहा॑क॒रिंद्रं॑ मा॒ता वी॒र्ये॑णा॒ ॑ नृष्टं ।
अथोद॑स्थात्त्व॒यमत्कं॒ वसा॑न॒ आ रोद॑सी अपृणा॒ज्जाय॑मानः॥

avadyamiva manyamānā guhākariṃdraṃ mātā vīryeṇā
nṛṣṭaṃ |
athodasthāttvayamatkaṃ vasāna ā rodasī apṛṇājjāyamānaḥ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

दद्यं इव । मन्यमाना । गुहा । अकः । इंद्रं । माता । वीर्येण । निऋष्टं ।

dadyaṃ iva | manyamānā | guhā | akaḥ | iṃdraṃ | mātā | vīryeṇa | niṛṣṭaṃ |

p. 996

अथ । उत् । अस्थात् । स्वयं । अत्यं । वसानः । आ । रोदसी इति । अपृणात् ।
जायमानः ॥

atha | ut | asthāt | svayaṃ | atyaṃ | vasānaḥ | ā | rodasī iti | apṛṇāt |
jāyamānaḥ ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

गुहा गुहायां गह्वररूपे सूतिकागृहे जातमिंद्रमवद्यमिव गर्हमिव मन्यमाना जानती मातेंद्रजनन्यदितिर्वीर्येण सामर्थ्येन नृष्टं नितरां प्राप्तमकः । अकरोत् । अथानंतरं जायमान उत्पद्यमान इंद्रः स्वयमेवात्कं तेजो वसान आच्छादकः सन् । दधान इत्यर्थः । उदस्थात् । उत्कर्षेणातिष्ठत् । किंच रोदसी द्यानापृथिव्यावापृणात् । समंतात्पूरयामास ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra was born in the cave-like lying-in room (गुहा (guhā)). His mother Aditi, considering it blameworthy (अवद्यमिव (avadyamiva)), made him नृष्टं (nṛṣṭaṃ), that is, fully endowed, with strength (वीर्येण (vīryeṇa)). Thereafter, Indra, being born, rose up by himself, clothed in अत्कं (atkaṃ), that is, splendour, and covering himself with it. Further, he filled रोदसी (rodasī), heaven and earth, on all sides.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—Indra
  • गुहा (guhā)—to give birth in the concealment of the lying-in room
  • अवद्यं इव (avadyaṃ iva)—(befitting his greatness) is not a praiseworthy act
  • मन्यमाना (manyamānā)—having thought
  • माता (mātā)—Aditi, Indra's mother
  • वीर्येण (vīryeṇa)—with extraordinary strength
  • नृष्टं (nṛṣṭaṃ)—as one endowed
  • अकः (akaḥ)—she made
  • अथ (atha)—afterwards
  • जायमानः (jāyamānaḥ)—Indra, who was born
  • स्वयं (svayaṃ)—his own
  • अत्कं (atkaṃ)—splendour
  • वसानः (vasānaḥ)—having put on
  • उदस्थात् (udasthāt)—rose up mightily
  • रोदसी (rodasī)—in both heaven and earth
  • आ अपृणात् (ā apṛṇāt)—pervaded completely
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Aditi, Indra's mother, considered that to give birth to Indra in the concealment of the lying-in room was not an act befitting his dignity, and made him endowed with extraordinary strength. Thereafter Indra, who was born, rose up clothed in his own splendour, and at once pervaded heaven and earth completely.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Deeming it disreputable (that he should be brought forth) in secret. his mother endowed (Indra) with (extraordinary) vigour : therefore, as soon as born he sprung up of his own accord, invested with splendour, and filled both heaven and earth.

p. 997

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

ए॒ता अ॑र्षंत्यलला॒ भवं॑तीऋ॒ताव॑रीरिव सं॒क्रोश॑मानाः ।
ए॒ता वि पृ॑च्छ॒ किमि॒दं भ॑नंति॒ कमापो॒ अद्रिं॑ परि॒धिं रु॑जंति ॥

etā arṣaṃtyalalā bhavaṃtīṛtāvarīriva saṃkrośamānāḥ |
etā vi pṛccha kimidaṃ bhanaṃti kamāpo adriṃ paridhiṃ rujaṃti ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

एताः । अर्षंति । अललाभवंतीः । ऋतवरीःइव । संक्रोषमानाः ।
एताः । वि । पृच्छ । किं । इदं । भनंति । कं । आपः । अद्रिं । परिधिं । रुजंति ॥ ६ ॥

etāḥ | arṣaṃti | alalābhavaṃtīḥ | ṛtavarīḥiva | saṃkroṣamānāḥ |
etāḥ | vi | pṛccha | kiṃ | idaṃ | bhanaṃti | kaṃ | āpaḥ | adriṃ | paridhiṃ | rujaṃti ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अललाभवंतीरललेत्येवंरूपं शब्दं कुर्वत्य ऋतावरीरिवोदकवत्य एवैता नद्यः संक्रोशमाना इंद्रमहत्त्वप्रतिपादकोद्भूतेन हर्षण बहुविधं शब्दायमानाः सत्योऽर्षंति । गच्छंति । एवंभूता नद्य इदं किं भनंति शोत्रग्राह्यं शब्दायमानं किं वदंतीमनुर्थं हे ऋषे त्वमेता नदीर्वि पृच्छ । विशेषेण पृष्टवान् भव । एवं संपृच्छ । विचारिते सत्येतच्छब्दायमानमिंद्रमाहात्मस्यैव वचनं भवतीत्यर्थः । किंच आप उदकानि परिधिमावरकं कमद्रिं कं मेघं रुजंति । भंजंति । आपः कमपि मेघं न भंजंति किंतु इंद्रो मम पुत्र एवोदकावरकं मेघं भक्त्वापः प्रवर्तयतीत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

अललाभवंतीः (alalābhavaṃtīḥ) means making a sound of the form "alala". Like ऋतावरीः (ṛtāvarīḥ), that is, full of water, these very rivers, संक्रोशमानाः (saṃkrośamānāḥ), resounding in many ways with the joy that has arisen from proclaiming Indra's greatness, flow (अर्षंति (arṣaṃti)). "What do these rivers say (भनंति (bhanaṃti)), what is this audible sound? O sage, question these rivers closely (वि पृच्छ (vi pṛccha))." The meaning is that, when asked, this sound proves to be a statement of Indra's greatness itself. Further, the waters break (रुजंति (rujaṃti)) which cloud (कमद्रिं कं मेघं (kamadriṃ kaṃ meghaṃ)), the encloser (परिधिं (paridhiṃ))? The waters do not break any cloud. Rather, my son Indra himself breaks the cloud that encloses the waters and sets the waters in motion.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अललाभवंतीः (alalābhavaṃtīḥ)—making the sound अलला (alalā) and the like
  • ऋतावरीः इव (ṛtāvarīḥ iva)—as if full of water
  • एताः (etāḥ)—these rivers
  • संक्रोशमानाः (saṃkrośamānāḥ)—accompanied by sounds of joy (proclaiming Indra's greatness)
  • अर्षंति (arṣaṃti)—flow
  • इदं किं भनंति (idaṃ kiṃ bhanaṃti)—(O sage) what is the meaning of this audible sound of theirs
  • एताः (etāḥ)—these rivers
  • वि पृच्छ (vi pṛccha)—ask, questioning
  • आपः (āpaḥ)—the waters
  • परिधिं (paridhiṃ)—the encloser
  • कं अद्रिं (kaṃ adriṃ)—which cloud
  • रुजंति (rujaṃti)—can they break?
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All these rivers flow, making sounds of joy such as "alala", as if proclaiming Indra's greatness. O sage, ask these rivers themselves what the meaning of this audible sound of theirs is. (Without Indra's help) which enclosing cloud could the waters break?

p. 998

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

These (rivers) flew murmuring as if, being filled with water, they were uttering sounds ( of joy ) : ask them what is this they say ; what is the encompassing cloud that the waters break through ?

किमु॑ ष्टिदस्मै नि॒विदो॑ भनं॒तेंद्र॑स्याव॒द्यं दि॑धिषंत॒ आपः॑ ।

mamaitānnutro mahatā vadhīna vṛtraṃ jaghanvā āsṛjadvi
siṃdhūn ‖ 7 ‖

किं । ऊं इति । स्वित् । अस्मै । निविदः । भनंत । इंद्रस्य । अवद्यं । दिधिषंते । आपः।
मम । एतान् । पुत्रः । महता । वधेन । वृत्रं । जघन्वान् । असृजत् । वि ।
सिंधून् ॥ ७ ॥

kiṃ | ūṃ iti | svit | asmai | nividaḥ | bhanaṃta | iṃdrasya | avadyaṃ | didhiṣaṃte | āpaḥ|
mama | etān | putraḥ | mahatā | vadhena | vṛtraṃ | jaghanvān | asṛjat | vi |
siṃdhūn ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यदेंद्रो वृत्रासुरं हतवान् तदा शाश्वतीं ब्रह्महत्यां प्राप्तवानिति वामदेवस्याभिप्रायमुन्नीयादितिराह । निविदः । मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रे प्रयुज्यमानानि मरुत्सोत्रो मरुद्धण इत्यादीनींद्रस्तुतिप्रतिपादकानि कानिचित्पदानि निविच्छब्देनोच्यंते । ता निविदोऽस्मा इदुं वृत्रवधनिमित्तं ब्रह्महत्यारूपं पापं प्राप्पुवंतमिंद्रं किमु ष्ट्वित् भनंत । भनंति । किं वदंतीति चेत् । तर्हि । पापरहितमिंद्रं मत्वा निविदः स्तुवंति। कथमिंद्रस्य पापरहितत्वं । उच्यते । आपः फेनरूपेणास्येंद्रस्यावद्यं ब्रह्महत्यादिरूपं पापं दिधिषंते । धारयंति । मम पुत्रो मदीयः पुत्र इंद्रो महता प्रभूतेन वधेन । वध इति वज्रनामैतत् । वज्रेण वृत्रं जघन्वान् । हतवान् । तत एतान् सिंधूनुदकानि व्यसृजत् । विशेषेण स्वैरत्वेन सर्तुं सृष्टवान् । इंद्रेणोत्सृष्टा अपस्तस्य पापं जगृहुरित्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that Vāmadeva speaks inferring that when Indra killed the demon Vṛtra he incurred the eternal sin of brahmin-slaying. निविदः (nividaḥ): certain phrases used in the Marutvatīya recitation, such as "Marut-stotra, Marud-gaṇa", which express praise of Indra, are called nivid. What do these nivids say of this Indra, who has incurred the sin of brahmin-slaying through the killing of Vṛtra? If it is asked what they say: they praise Indra as one free of sin. How is Indra free of sin? It is answered: the waters, in the form of foam, bear this blemish of Indra, the sin of brahmin-slaying and the like. "My son", that is, Indra, my own son, with a great, abundant वध (vadha) (vadha is a name of the thunderbolt) slew Vṛtra. Then he released these rivers, the waters, letting them flow freely and as they please. The meaning is that the waters released by Indra took his sin upon themselves.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • निविदः (nividaḥ)—these mantras in the form of 'nivid'
  • अस्मै (asmai)—concerning this Indra
  • किमु स्वित् (kimu svit)—what indeed
  • भनंत (bhanaṃta)—they say (they merely praise him)
  • आपः (āpaḥ)—the waters

p. 999

  • इंद्रस्य (iṃdrasya)—of Indra
  • अवद्यं (avadyaṃ)—the sin in the form of brahmin-slaying and the like
  • दिधिषंते (didhiṣaṃte)—they bear (in the form of foam)
  • मम (mama)—my
  • पुत्रः (putraḥ)—son, Indra
  • महता (mahatā)—with the great
  • वधेन (vadhena)—thunderbolt weapon
  • वृत्रं (vṛtraṃ)—Vṛtra
  • जघन्वान् (jaghanvān)—killed
  • एतान् सिंधून् (etān siṃdhūn)—these waters
  • वि असृजत् (vi asṛjat)—caused to be released to flow freely
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The mantras in the form of 'nivid' are merely laudatory with regard to Indra. The waters bear Indra's sin of brahmin-slaying and the like in the form of foam. My son Indra killed Vṛtra with the great thunderbolt, and released these waters so that they flow freely.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

What do the sacred expiatory strains declare to me? the waters receive the reproach of Indra : my son has slain Vritra with the mighty thunderbolt : he has set those rivers free.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For a detailed account of Indra's slaying of the demon Vṛtra, the consequent incurring of the fault of brahmin-slaying by Indra, and the course of action Indra undertook to remove that fault, see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 12, p. 627.

मम॑च्च॒न त्वा॑ युव॒तिः प॒रास॒ मम॑च्च॒न त्वा॑ कु॒षवा॑ ज॒गार॑ ।
मम॑च्चि॒दापः॒ शिश॑वे ममृड्यु॒र्मम॑च्च॒दिंद्रः॒ सह॒सोद॑तिष्ठत् ॥

mamaccana tvā yuvatiḥ parāsa mamaccana tvā kuṣavā jagāra |
mamaccidāpaḥ śiśave mamṛḍyurmamaccadiṃdraḥ sahasodatiṣṭhat ‖

vamat | cit | āpaḥ | śiśave | mamṛḍyuḥ | mamat | cit | iṃdraḥ | sahasā | ut |
atiṣṭhat ‖ 8 ‖

p. 1000

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

सूक्तशेषेण ऋषिरिंद्रं स्तौति । हे इंद्र ममच्चन माद्यंत्येव । प्रमत्तैवेत्यर्थः । युवतिस्त्वदीया मातादितिस्ता त्वां परास । पराचिक्षेक । किंच कुषनानाम्मी काचिद्राक्षसी सा ममच्चन प्रमत्तैव त्वा त्वां जगार । गिरति स्म । हे इंद्र ममच्चित्प्रमद्यंत एवापः शिशवे जाताय तुभ्यं ममृड्युः । सुखयांचक्रुः । ममच्चित् माद्यन्नेवेंद्रः सहसा स्वेन वीर्येणोदतिष्ठत् । सूतिकाग्रहाद्राक्षसीं बाधमानः सन् उत्कर्षेण तस्थौ ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

With the rest of the sūkta the seer praises Indra. O Indra, "exulting", that is, in joy alone, the youthful mother, your mother Aditi, "cast you forth" (परास (parāsa)). Moreover, there is a certain demoness named Kuṣanā; exulting, in her joy, she swallowed you. O Indra, exulting indeed, the waters gave delight to you, the newborn child. Exulting, Indra rose up by his own strength, resisting the demoness who seized the newborn, and stood up in triumph.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • ममच्चन (mamaccana)—exultingly
  • युवतिः (yuvatiḥ)—your mother Aditi
  • त्वा (tvā)—you
  • परास (parāsa)—bore
  • ममच्चन (mamaccana)—exultingly
  • कुषवा (kuṣavā)—the demoness named Kuṣavā
  • त्वा (tvā)—you
  • जगार (jagāra)—swallowed
  • ममच्चित् (mamaccit)—from that very excess of joy
  • आपः (āpaḥ)—the waters
  • शिशवे (śiśave)—as soon as Indra was born
  • ममृड्युः (mamṛḍyuḥ)—became givers of comfort
  • ममच्चित् (mamaccit)—from joy
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • सहसा (sahasā)—by his own power
  • उवतिष्ठत् (uvatiṣṭhat)—came out (breaking through the demoness)
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The words of the mother of the seer Vāmadeva: O Indra, your youthful mother (Aditi) bore you in joy. In joy the demoness named Kuṣanā swallowed you. From that same excess of joy the waters became comfort-giving as soon as Indra was born. Indra too, joyful, broke through the demoness by his own power and came out.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Vamadeva speaks.—Exulting, the youthful mother brought you forth : exulting, Kushava swallowed you : exulting, the waters gave delight to the infant : Indra, exulting, rose up by his strength

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अथा॒ निवि॑द्द॒ उत्त॑रो बभू॒वाञ्छिरो॑ दा॒सस्य॒ सं पि॑णग्व॒धेन॑ ॥

manuccana te maghavanvaṃso nivividhvā apa hanū jaghāna |

अध । निविद्दः । उत्तरः । बभूवान् । शिरः । दासस्य । सं । पिणक् । वधेन ॥ ९ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे मघवन्थनवन्निंद्र ममच्चिन प्रमाद्यन्नेव व्यंसो नाम राक्षसो निविविध्वान् प्रविध्यन् ते हनू त्वदीये हनू मुखपार्श्वे अप जघान । अपहतवान् । अध अथानंतरं हे इंद्र निविद्दो राक्षसेन ताडितस्त्वमुत्तरो व्यंसादधिकबलो बभूवान्‌भूतः सन् दासस्य क्षीणस्य व्यंसस्य शिरो वधेन वज्रेण सं पिणक् । पिष्टवानसि ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O wealthy Indra, exulting indeed, the demon named Vyaṃsa, striking, struck away your two jaws, the sides of your mouth. Then, O Indra, struck by the demon, you became superior, stronger than Vyaṃsa, and with the वध (vadha), the thunderbolt, you crushed the head of the exhausted दास (dāsa) Vyaṃsa.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मघवन् (maghavan)—O wealthy Indra
  • ममच्चन (mamaccana)—from excess of joy
  • व्यंसः (vyaṃsaḥ)—the demon named Vyaṃsa
  • निविविध्वान् (nivividhvān)—striking you
  • ते (te)—your
  • हनू (hanū)—on the cheeks
  • अप जघान (apa jaghāna)—struck, dashing against
  • अध (adha)—thereafter
  • निविद्दः (nividdaḥ)—you, struck by him
  • उत्तरः (uttaraḥ)—possessing greater strength than he
  • बभूवान् (babhūvān)—having grown
  • दासस्य (dāsasya)—of the asura Vyaṃsa
  • शिरः (śiraḥ)—the head
  • वधेन (vadhena)—with the thunderbolt, the instrument of slaying
  • सं पिणक् (saṃ piṇak)—crushed to powder
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, from excess of joy (from pride) the demon Vyaṃsa tried to strike you and dashed against your cheeks. Thereafter, struck by him, you grew stronger than he, and crushed the head of the asura Vyaṃsa with the thunderbolt, the instrument of slaying.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Vyansa, exulting and striking (hard blows) smote you, Maghavan, upon the jaw ; whereupon, being so smitten, you proved the stronger, and did crush the head of the slave with the thunderbolt.

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

गृ॒ष्टिः स॑सूव॒स्थवि॑रं तवा॒गाम॑नाधृ॒ष्यं वृ॑ष॒भं तुम्र॒मिंद्रं॑।
अरी॑ळ्हं व॒त्सं च॒रथा॑य मा॒ता स्व॒यं गा॒तुं त॒न्न॑ इ॒च्छमा॑नं॥

gṛṣṭiḥ sasūvasthaviraṃ tavāgāmanādhṛṣyaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ tumramiṃdraṃ|
arīḷhaṃ vatsaṃ carathāya mātā svayaṃ gātuṃ tanna icchamānaṃ‖

p. 1002

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

गृष्टिः । ससूव । स्थविरं । तवागां । अनाधृष्य । वृषभं । तुम्रं । इंद्रं ।
अरीळ्हं । वत्सं । चरथाय । माता । स्वयं । गातुं । तन्वे । इच्छमानं ॥ १० ॥

gṛṣṭiḥ | sasūva | sthaviraṃ | tavāgāṃ | anādhṛṣya | vṛṣabhaṃ | tumraṃ | iṃdraṃ |
arīḷhaṃ | vatsaṃ | carathāya | mātā | svayaṃ | gātuṃ | tanve | icchamānaṃ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

गृष्टिः काचिद्गौर्वत्सं यथा ससूव । सुषुवे । तथा मातेंद्रजनन्यदितिश्चरथाय स्वेच्छया संचरणायेंद्रं ससूव । सुषुवे । कीदृशमिंद्रं । स्थविरं वयसा प्रवृद्धं तवागां प्रवृद्धबलमनाधृष्ट्यं शत्रुभिरनभिभाव्यं वृषभं सेचनसमर्थं तुम्रं प्रेरकमरीळ्हं शत्रुभिरनभिभूतं स्वयं गातुमन्यनिरपेक्षगमनं तन्ने स्वशरीरायेच्छमानमिच्छंतं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

As a heifer bears a calf, so the mother, Aditi, Indra's mother, bore Indra for roaming at will. What sort of Indra? स्थविरं (sthaviraṃ): grown mature in age; तवागां (tavāgāṃ): of grown strength; अनाधृष्यं (anādhṛṣyaṃ): not to be overcome by enemies; वृषभं (vṛṣabhaṃ): able to shower; तुम्रं (tumraṃ): impelling; अरीळ्हं (arīḷhaṃ): not overcome by enemies; स्वयं गातुं (svayaṃ gātuṃ): going of himself, independent of others; and wishing it for his own body.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • गृष्टिः (gṛṣṭiḥ)—a well-nourished heifer
  • वत्सं (vatsaṃ)—a calf
  • ससूव (sasūva)—as having borne
  • माता (mātā)—Indra's mother Aditi
  • स्थविरं (sthaviraṃ)—one grown in age
  • तवागां (tavāgāṃ)—one of great strength
  • अनाधृष्यं (anādhṛṣyaṃ)—one not defeated by enemies
  • वृषभं (vṛṣabhaṃ)—the fulfiller of desires
  • तुम्रं (tumraṃ)—the impeller of all
  • अरीळ्हं (arīḷhaṃ)—the unobstructed
  • स्वयं गातुं (svayaṃ gātuṃ)—one who roams at will
  • तन्ने इच्छमानं (tanne icchamānaṃ)—one intent on protecting his own body
  • इंद्रं (iṃdraṃ)—Indra
  • चरथाय (carathāya)—for roaming at will
  • ससूव (sasūva)—bore
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a well-nourished heifer bears her calf, Aditi, Indra's mother, bore for roaming at will Indra, who is mature in age, of great strength, undefeated by enemies, the fulfiller of desires, the impeller of all, unobstructed, a roamer at will, and intent on protecting his own body.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

As a heifer bears a calf, his mother, (Aditi) bore Indra, mature (in years) strong. irresistible, vigorous, energetic, invincible, (destined) to follow his own course, heedful in his person.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

उ॒त मा॒ता म॑हि॒षमन्व॑वेनद॒मी त्वा॑ जहति पुत्र दे॒वाः ।
अथा॑ब्रवीद्वृ॒त्रमिंद्रो॑ हनि॒ष्यन्त्सखे॑ विष्णो वित॒रं विक्र॑मस्व॥

uta mātā mahiṣamanvavenadamī tvā jahati putra devāḥ |
athābravīdvṛtramiṃdro haniṣyantsakhe viṣṇo vitaraṃ vikramasva‖

अथ । अब्रवीत् । वृत्रं । इंद्रः । हनिष्यत् । सखे । विष्णो इति । वितरं । वि ।
क्रमस्व ॥ ११ ॥

uta | mātā | mahiṣaṃ | anu | avenat | amī iti | tvā | jahati | putra | devāḥ |
atha | abravīt | vṛtraṃ | iṃdraḥ | haniṣyat | sakhe | viṣṇo iti | vitaraṃ | vi |
kramasva ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

उतापि च हे मदीय पुत्रेंद्र अमी वह्नादयो देवास्ता त्वां जहति । त्यजंति । इत्युक्तवतींद्रस्य मातादितिरिंद्रं महिषं महांतं । महिष इति महन्नामैतत् । अन्ववेनत् । अयाचत । अथानंतरं हे विष्णो व्यापनशील हे सखे मित्रभूत हरे त्वं वृत्रं हनिष्यन् हंतुमिच्छन् वितरं वि क्रमस्व । अतिपराक्रमा भवेतींद्रो विष्णुमब्रवीत् । उवाच ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"And, O my son Indra, these gods, Agni and the rest, forsake you": having said this, Indra's mother Aditi implored Indra, the महिष (mahiṣa), the great one (mahiṣa is a name meaning "great"); अन्ववेनत् (anvavenat) means "she begged". Thereafter Indra said to Viṣṇu: "O Viṣṇu, the all-pervading, O friend, O Hari who are a companion, wishing to slay Vṛtra, stride out beyond (all others); be exceedingly valiant."

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • उत (uta)—and
  • पुत्र (putra)—O Indra
  • अमिः देवाः (amiḥ devāḥ)—these gods, Agni and the rest
  • त्वा (tvā)—you
  • जहति (jahati)—if they abandon (leave)
  • माता (mātā)—the mother Aditi
  • महिषं (mahiṣaṃ)—the great Indra
  • अन्ववेनत् (anvavenat)—asked
  • अथ (atha)—thereafter
  • इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra
  • विष्णुं (viṣṇuṃ)—to Viṣṇu
  • सखे (sakhe)—O friend
  • विष्णो (viṣṇo)—O Viṣṇu, the all-pervading
  • वृत्रं (vṛtraṃ)—Vṛtra the asura
  • हनिष्यन् (haniṣyan)—wishing to kill
  • वितरं (vitaraṃ)—exceedingly
  • वि क्रमस्व (vi kramasva)—"become valiant," said
  • अब्रवीत् (abravīt)—he said NOTE
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Aditi asked: "O Indra, my son, have the gods, Agni and the rest, abandoned your friendship?" Immediately Indra said to Viṣṇu: "O friend Viṣṇu, you are all-pervading and a well-wisher to me. Wishing to slay the asura Vṛtra, gain exceeding valour."

p. 1004

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

कस्ते॑ मा॒तरं॑ वि॒धवा॑मचक्रच्छ॒युं कस्माम॑जिघांस॒च्चरं॑तं ।
कस्ते॑ दे॒वो अधि॑ मार्डी॒क आ॑सी॒द्यत्पाक्षि॑णाः पि॒तरं॑ पाद॒गृह्य॑ ॥

kaste mātaraṃ vidhavāmacakracchayuṃ kasmāmajighāṃsaccaraṃtaṃ |
kaste devo adhi mārḍīka āsīdyatpākṣiṇāḥ pitaraṃ pādagṛhya ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

कः । ते । मातरं । विधवां । अचक्रत् । शयुं । कः । त्वां । अजिघांसत् । चरंतं ।
कः । ते । देवः । अधि । मार्डीके । आसीत् । यत् । प्र । अक्षिणाः । पितरं । पादगृह्य ॥ १२ ॥

kaḥ | te | mātaraṃ | vidhavāṃ | acakrat | śayuṃ | kaḥ | tvāṃ | ajighāṃsat | caraṃtaṃ |
kaḥ | te | devaḥ | adhi | mārḍīke | āsīt | yat | pra | akṣiṇāḥ | pitaraṃ | pādagṛhya ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र यद्यस्मात्कारणात्पितुः सकाशाज्जनिष्यमाणाद्भीतस्वं त्वदीयं पितरं पादगृह्य पादेषु गृहीत्वा प्राक्षिणाः । प्रकर्षणावधीः । तस्मात्कारणात्ते त्वत्तोऽन्यः को देवो मातरं स्वकीयजननीं विधवां पितृवधेन पतिरहितामकच्रत् । अकरोत् । कस्त्वत्तोऽन्यः शयुं शयानं चरंतं जागृतं ना त्वामजिघांसत् । हंतुमैच्छत् । ते त्वत्तोऽन्यः को देवो मार्डीके प्रजानां सुखकरणेऽधि अधिक आसीत् । अयमर्थ ऋक्सामे वै देवेभ्य इत्यनुवाके यज्ञो दक्षिणामभ्यध्यायदित्यादिब्राह्मणेन । तै. सं. ६-१-३-६ । तैत्तिरीयकैर्बहुधा प्रपंचितः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, because you, afraid of the one who was about to be born from your father's side, seized your father by the feet and struck him down (प्राक्षिणाः (prākṣiṇāḥ), "you killed by crushing"), for that reason what god other than you made his own mother a widow, bereft of her husband through the killing of the father? Who other than you wished to kill you, whether lying down or walking about, that is, awake? What god other than you was greater in making the creatures happy (मार्डीके (mārḍīke))? This meaning is elaborated in many ways by the Taittirīyas in the Brāhmaṇa beginning ऋक्सामे वै देवेभ्य (ṛksāme vai devebhya), in the anuvāka and in the passage yajño dakṣiṇāmabhyadhyāyat and so on (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-3-6).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यत् (yat)—for which reason
  • पितरं (pitaraṃ)—your father
  • पादगृह्य (pādagṛhya)—seizing and dragging by the leg
  • प्राक्षिणाः (prākṣiṇāḥ)—you felled and killed (therefore)
  • ते (te)—other than you
  • कः (kaḥ)—which deity indeed
  • मातरं (mātaraṃ)—his mother
  • विधवां (vidhavāṃ)—as a widow
  • अचक्रत् (acakrat)—could make
  • कः (kaḥ)—who other than you
  • शयुं (śayuṃ)—lying asleep
  • चरंतं (caraṃtaṃ)—and moving about
  • त्वां (tvāṃ)—you
  • अजिघांसत् (ajighāṃsat)—would wish to kill?
  • ते (te)—other than you
  • कः देवः (kaḥ devaḥ)—which deity indeed
  • मार्डिके (mārḍike)—as a bringer of happiness to the creatures
  • अधि आसीत् (adhi āsīt)—surpasses you

p. 1005

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, since you yourself seized your father by the leg, dragged and thrust him down and killed him, no one but you is capable of such a deed. Therefore no one except you can make his own mother a widow. Who indeed could kill you, whether you are lying asleep or moving about? Which god other than you could have greater power than you to be the giver of happiness to the creatures?

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

Who has made your mother a widow? who has sought to slay the sleeping and the waking? what deity has been more gracious than you, since you have slain the father, having seized him by the foot ? #### Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अव॑र्त्या॒ शुन॑ आं॒त्राणि॑ पेचे॒ न दे॒वेषु॑ विविदे मर्डि॒तारं॑ ।
अप॑श्यं जा॒यामम॑हीयमाना॒मधा॑ मे श्वे॒नो मध्वा ॑ जभार ॥ १३ ॥

avartyā śuna āṃtrāṇi pece na deveṣu vivide marḍitāraṃ |
apaśyaṃ jāyāmamahīyamānāmadhā me śveno madhvā
jabhāra ‖ 13 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अवर्त्या । शुनः । आंत्राणि । पेचे । न । देवेषु । विविदे । मर्डितारं ।
अपश्यं । जायां । अमहीयमानां । अध । मे । श्वेनः । मधु । आ । जभार ॥ १३॥

avartyā | śunaḥ | āṃtrāṇi | pece | na | deveṣu | vivide | marḍitāraṃ |
apaśyaṃ | jāyāṃ | amahīyamānāṃ | adha | me | śvenaḥ | madhu | ā | jabhāra ‖ 13‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अनया वामदेवः स्वकीयं दारिद्र्यं सूचयन्निंद्रस्योत्कर्षमाह । वामदेवोऽहमवर्त्या जीवनोपायराहित्येन शुनः शुनकसंबंधीन्यांत्राणि पुरीतंति

Gist of the bhāṣya

With this verse Vāmadeva, indicating his own poverty, proclaims Indra's pre-eminence. "I, Vāmadeva, for lack of any means of livelihood, cooked (पेचे (pece)) the entrails of a dog, the intestines (पुरीतंति (purītaṃti)) belonging to a dog."

p. 1006

पेचे । अपचं । देवेषु द्योतमानेषु वह्न्यादिषु मध्य इंद्रादन्यं मर्डितारं सुखयितारं न विविदे । न लेभे । किंच जायां स्वकीयां भार्याममहीयमानामश्लाघनीयामपश्यं । अद्राक्षं । अध अथानंतरं श्येनः श्येनवच्छीफुगामींद्रो मे मह्यं मधु मधुरोपेतमुदकमा जभार । आजहार ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"I cooked (अपचं (apacaṃ)). Among the shining gods, Agni and the rest, I found no comforter, no giver of happiness, other than Indra. Moreover I saw my own wife disrespected, not praised. Then Indra, swift-going like a falcon, brought to me sweet water, water endowed with sweetness."

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अवर्त्या (avartyā)—by reason of poverty
  • शुनः (śunaḥ)—of a dog
  • आंत्राणि (āṃtrāṇi)—the entrails
  • पेचे (pece)—I cooked
  • देवेषु (deveṣu)—among the shining gods
  • मर्डितारं (marḍitāraṃ)—any deity who gives happiness
  • न विविदे (na vivide)—I did not obtain
  • जायां (jāyāṃ)—my wife
  • अमहीयमानां (amahīyamānāṃ)—as disregarded
  • अपश्यं (apaśyaṃ)—I saw
  • अध (adha)—afterwards
  • श्येनं (śyenaṃ)—Indra, swift-going like a falcon
  • मे (me)—to me
  • मधु (madhu)—water full of sweetness
  • आ जभार (ā jabhāra)—brought and gave
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The words of the seer Vāmadeva: By reason of poverty I cooked the entrails of a dog. Among the shining gods I found no deity who gives happiness. And for that same reason I saw my wife disrespected. Afterwards Indra, swift-going like a falcon, brought me water full of sweetness.

English translation (H. H. Wilson)

In extreme destitution I have cooked the entrails of a dog, I have not found a comforter among the gods. I have beheld my wife disrespected : then the falcon (Indra) has brought to me sweet water.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Having spoken thus, he told of the hardship he had suffered. Living in extreme poverty and finding no food to eat, I had to cook and eat the entrails of a dog (entrails of a dog), that is, its flesh, which no one eats, that is, which is forbidden. Because of this poverty of mine I had to see the loss of honour of my wife. Then Indra, looking on me with a gracious eye, gave me water full of sweetness and consoled me, so he says.

p. 1007

This last Ṛk does not relate to the birth of the seer Vāmadeva. It is a statement made when Vāmadeva had grown up, matured, and was experiencing hardships and pleasures. Therefore how this Ṛk came to be included in this sūkta cannot be said.

Closing verses: वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । प्रमथांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pramathāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖)

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये तृतीयाष्टके पंचमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye tṛtīyāṣṭake paṃcamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖) ॥ ओं तत्स्यत् ॥ (‖ oṃ tatsyat ‖)

Here ends the fifth chapter in the third Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with Śrī Sāyaṇa's commentary and a Kannada translation.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं त. यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ ta. yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖)

शुभं शुभयात् (śubhaṃ śubhayāt) मंगळं (maṃgaḷaṃ)
